entry.summary: The paper develops a causal framework for matrix completion under missing-not-at-random data by relaxing the usual positivity and observation-independence assumptions, drawing on synthetic controls from panel-data econometrics. It proposes the synthetic nearest neighbors estimator, adapting to heterogeneous, target-specific local observation patterns, and proves finite-sample entrywise error bounds and consistency. It matters for causal inference and recommender-style problems where missingness is informative and observation patterns vary by unit.

entry.title: Another Slice of Swiss Cheese for Untrusted Monitoring

author.name: martinveron

entry.summary: A concrete AI control experiment showing that a linear probe trained to perceive code backdoors in activation space can detect monitor-policy collusion, catching 86 percent of colluding transcripts at a 1.4 percent false-positive rate. The author argues probes trained on mundane task-specific facts should be part of the control toolkit, since they outperform trusted monitoring on the safety-usefulness frontier under a 2 percent audit budget.

entry.title: The average-farmer illusion in language-model simulations of agricultural decisions

author.name: Zhanliang Zhu, Ziwei Li, Yuchen Liu, Liujun Zhu, Ruiqi Wu, Tongqing Shen, Junliang Jin, Jianyun Zhang

entry.summary: The authors test whether language-model agents used as synthetic survey respondents truly reproduce human behavior, comparing Claude, Codex, and Kimi against matched farmer decisions from China and four African countries under four prespecified prompt designs. Some configurations match observed means and adoption rates, but person-level predictions are weak, decisions cluster near typical values, and extremes are largely missing, with a simple marginal-distribution generator matching aggregate performance without any farmer information.

entry.title: T-LoopFormer: Token-Level Elastic-Depth Looped Transformers for Latent Reasoning With Dynamic Routing

author.name: Mingqian Yu, Wenpeng Zhang, Peilin Zhao

entry.summary: T-LoopFormer introduces dynamic token-choice routing into looped Transformers, letting each token adaptively select its recursion depth in latent space rather than applying a uniform fixed depth. This promises better compute allocation and efficiency for latent reasoning, where inference happens in hidden states instead of emitted tokens.

entry.title: The Troy Moment of AI: Why SomeWill Cheat and SomeWill Follow?

author.name: Ivy Zhang

entry.summary: Motivated by the July 2026 OpenAI-Hugging Face incident, this study uses seven ImpossibleBench tasks with GPT-5.6 Sol, Claude Fable 5.1, and Gemini 3.8 Flash to ask whether agents stop or escalate when tasks become impossible, and whether observing peers changes that choice. It varies information about prior peer activity, including unpunished, punished, and claimed peer behavior.

entry.title: GRIN+: Towards Fast Yet Effective Machine Unlearning for Imbalanced Medical Data

author.name: Minghui Huang, Junxiao Wang

entry.summary: This paper tackles machine unlearning in medical settings, where privacy rules such as GDPR and HIPAA require removing patient data from trained models, but severe class imbalance and long-tailed distributions make standard unlearning methods fail. The authors propose GRIN+ to better balance privacy, efficiency, and utility, avoiding the deletion of rare-condition diagnostic features caused by majority-class gradient dominance.

entry.title: ShieldVLA: Feasibility-Aware Safety Alignment for Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Manan Tayal, Akshay Nambi

entry.summary: ShieldVLA fine-tunes vision-language-action models for safety using Hamilton-Jacobi reachability, learning a model-free approximation of the reachability value function directly from visual observations. This replaces soft Lagrangian cost penalties that often leave residual constraint violations or yield overly conservative behavior. It also addresses the scarcity of dense per-step safety labels in visual robotic domains.

entry.title: Confuse the Model, Control the Flow: Understanding and Mitigating Privacy Leakage from LLM Agents with Information Flow Control

author.name: Minsun Shim, Ramisha Raida Karim, Ruthwik Jakkula, Kaiwen Zhou, Xin Liu, Xin Eric Wang, Zhou Li

entry.summary: The paper argues that making the backend LLM itself more privacy-preserving through prompts, training, or consent checks is structurally flawed, because the enforcement mechanism and the adversarial attack surface are the same conversational context. The authors demonstrate this failure against existing defenses and propose information flow control as an external enforcement layer for deciding when sensitive user data may be disclosed to a given party. It matters because personal LLM agents increasingly hold private data and communications.

entry.title: Calibrating Interpretability Instruments Before Trusting Their Verdicts

author.name: Orion Reblitz-Richardson

entry.summary: This note documents six specific ways that interpretability measurements of LLM internals fail while still returning plausible numbers, making a broken instrument look like a finding. Examples include covariance-matched nulls that saturate, per-head attributions that overshoot true residual writes on reordered-normalization architectures, sign-chaotic interchange patches pinned at a ceiling, and read-from verdicts measured past the layer where the model decided. It argues causal claims about model internals require instrument calibration before interpretation.

entry.title: When the World Lies: Backdoor Attacks on Latent World Models for Downstream Control

author.name: Roberto Ria\~no, Gorka Abad, Stjepan Picek, Aitor Urbieta

entry.summary: This paper demonstrates a supply-chain backdoor against pretrained latent world models that are reused as dynamics backbones for control. An adversary who controls only the released checkpoint can hijack a downstream controller trained entirely on clean data by routing trigger-bearing observations into a chosen latent region and reshaping local dynamics there, without encoding an explicit trigger-to-action rule.

entry.title: Steady-State Convergence of Stochastic Approximation

author.name: Yixuan Zhang, Qiaomin Xie

entry.summary: This work develops a unified steady-state convergence theory for constant-stepsize stochastic approximation under Markovian, multiplicative noise, covering mean operators that are only locally differentiable or even locally nondifferentiable. A multi-step universality framework reduces the original recursion to tractable auxiliary processes, yielding sharper rates than prior theory. It matters for understanding the bias of constant-stepsize algorithms widely used in reinforcement learning and stochastic optimization.

entry.title: Temperature Fragility and the Conditional Benefits of Truncation Sampling

author.name: Francesco La Rosa

entry.summary: This paper measures whether truncation samplers such as top-p and min-p actually improve accuracy at the temperatures deployed systems use, rather than at the 1.5-3 range where gains were originally reported. Testing thirteen open-weight models on GSM8K and MMLU-Pro at temperatures 0.7, 1.0, and 1.3, with ten models run under eight decoding configurations, it finds that benefits are conditional and model-dependent, and that behavior at deployment defaults differs from the reported regime. It matters because decoding defaults are rarely validated and this quantifies when truncation helps, does nothing, or hurts.

entry.title: North Small Translate: Advanced Cost-Effective Translation (Cohere CAT+)

author.name: Tom Kocmi, Alexandre B\'erard, Phil Blunsom, Samuel Cahyawijaya, Shaun Cassini, Nicholas Frosst, Ona de Gibert, Aidan Gomez, Nithya Govindarajan, Shun Kiyono, Olivia Lasche, Lawrence Rogers, Kelly Marchisio, Nikita Moghe, Yash More, Camila Moran-Hidalgo, Yiyang Nan, Michael Sachs, Trisha Starostina, Daan van Stigt, Spencer Rarrick, Sebastian Vincent, Ivan Zhang

entry.summary: Cohere presents North Small Translate, an open-weight instruction-following MT model built on the Command A Plus mixture-of-experts foundation with 25B active of 218B total parameters. Training uses difficulty sampling plus a five-step protocol of supervised fine-tuning, direct preference optimization, and online reinforcement learning, with a non-reasoning base for throughput and optional agentic capabilities for quality gains.

entry.title: Recoverability as a System Primitive for Long-Horizon AI Agents

author.name: Zhihui Zhang, Wei Liu

entry.summary: This paper introduces recoverability as a system primitive that treats resuming interrupted agent work as an explicit decision rather than an automatic continuation. It defines a behavioral contract tying the recovery choice to supporting evidence, execution, and independent checks, and presents a reference architecture connecting persistence, validation, and control with runtime instances. It matters because long-horizon agents that resume from unverified state can propagate earlier errors.

entry.title: UniCAR-RL: Seeing Better before Thinking Deeper in Visual Mathematics

author.name: Yuzhe Li, Hao Yan, Hao Wang, Xingchen Liu, Ya-Qi Yu, Jihao Wu, Minghui Liao, Wei Chen, Yuliang Liu

entry.summary: UniCAR-RL is an annotation-free reinforcement learning framework that explicitly decouples perception optimization from reasoning optimization to improve visual mathematical reasoning in multimodal LLMs. It targets the cascading failures caused by fine-grained perception deficits and initial visual hallucinations, which sparse-reward end-to-end RL cannot disentangle. It matters because it offers a way to isolate and fix perceptual errors without costly perception-enhanced chain-of-thought data.

entry.title: A note on goal-based hierarchical RL

author.name: Kevin Murphy

entry.summary: Kevin Murphy examines the agent-centric general value function construction, which lets an agent choose its goal and decide when a goal is finished on top of choosing actions, and notes that it assumes a fully observed environment where observations are sufficient statistics. The note connects this framework to a more general agent design based on an internal belief state and internal goal, extending the construction toward partially observed settings.

entry.title: HISPO: Hierarchical Importance-Sampling Policy Optimization with Entropy-Derived Segments

author.name: Quoc-Vinh Lai-Dang, Hyo-Sang Shin

entry.summary: HISPO introduces segment-level policy optimization for RLVR, building contiguous segments from rollout-time entropy and assigning soft entropy-based saliency to address credit assignment in long-form math reasoning. It contrasts with token-level correction in GRPO and DAPO and sequence-level correction in GSPO.

entry.title: NoteVQA: Benchmarking VLMs on Real-Life Questions from Human Communities

author.name: Haonan Jiang, Guojian Zhan, Jiancong Xie, Shijun Wan, Dongiia Zhao, Cheng Chen, Yahui Liu, Yao Hu, Chuan Mu

entry.summary: NoteVQA is a benchmark of 252 real everyday visual questions drawn from Xiaohongshu, a major Chinese image-sharing platform, spanning 12 topical categories and 7 user intents, each with a concise reference answer distilled from expert community responses. It targets the long tail of everyday photo-grounded questions that capability-focused benchmarks miss.

entry.title: EvoOntology: A Self-Evolving Ontology Layer for Data Agents

author.name: Meiduo Chong, Shaolei Zhang, Ju Fan, Xiaoyong Du

entry.summary: EvoOntology addresses the agent-data gap in which heterogeneous tables, files, and databases live outside the agent and are reachable only through generic tools. It introduces a self-evolving ontology layer exposed as an MCP server with schema, content, and related layers, aiming to scale better than raw exploration or manually authored semantic layers.

entry.title: LongAgent: History-Guided Agentic Search for Longitudinal Outcome Prediction

author.name: Siyao Wang, Florian Guitton, Shuojie Fu, Guanyu Tao, Kai Sun, Wenjia Bai

entry.summary: LongAgent is an agent-based method for medical longitudinal outcome prediction that autonomously searches over combinations of variable sets, temporal windows, and longitudinal aggregation functions to find candidates with predictive value. It targets the heterogeneity of medical data, where variables differ in source, sampling spacing, and health aspect.

entry.title: Beyond Quacking: Deep Integration of Language Models and RAG into DuckDB

author.name: Anas Dorbani, Sunny Yasser, Jimmy Lin, Amine Mhedhbi

entry.summary: The paper presents FlockMTL, an extension that deeply integrates LLM capabilities and retrieval-augmented generation into database management systems, illustrated with DuckDB. It targets the effort of orchestrating heterogeneous data systems, managing data movement, and handling low-level details such as LLM context management for knowledge-intensive analytical applications.

entry.title: Sampling headroom is not selection gain: a compute-value audit of test-time scaling for video world models

author.name: Yuhua Jiang, Junjie Lu, Feifei Gao

entry.summary: The paper introduces the Compute-Value Audit, a sequential framework separating whether extra test-time sampling creates better candidates from whether the system can reliably select them. On 192 Physics-IQ scenes, expanding the candidate pool from 4 to 16 substantially raises oracle quality but yields much smaller realized gains. It is a cautionary, methodologically careful study of test-time scaling for video world models.

entry.title: ReCAST: Reward Credit Assignment across Timesteps for Online Diffusion Reinforcement

author.name: Yihang Chen, Yuanhao Ban, Kuei-Chun Kao, Cho-Jui Hsieh

entry.summary: ReCAST is presented as the first method for per-reward, timestep-dependent credit assignment in diffusion reward fine-tuning. It separates how much each reward should matter to the user from when during denoising that reward's feedback is actually informative, using a reward-by-timestep decomposition instead of applying all rewards uniformly across the trajectory. This matters because diffusion RL fine-tuning with multiple objectives currently conflates preference weighting with temporal signal quality, which wastes or misdirects optimization.

entry.title: Same Patient, Different Order: Action-Level Reliability of Clinical LLM Agents Under Repeated Runs

author.name: Rohith Reddy Bellibatlu, Manpreet Singh, Zhoutian Han, Wenbin Zhang

entry.summary: This paper shows that clinical agents can pass a benchmark while producing materially different test orders, medications, or referrals on identical inputs across runs. The authors introduce a same-input rerun protocol with six reliability metrics and apply it to 1000 MedAgentBench runs over 50 write-capable tasks using small quantized open-weight models.

entry.title: The Misery of Mechanistic Interpretability: A Formal Perspective

author.name: Tobias Ladner, Matthias Althoff

entry.summary: The authors show that interpretable replacement networks, the standard tool of mechanistic interpretability, are fragile: even semantically minor input perturbations flip the dominant IRN features, and thus the human-understandable interpretation, across five open-weight model families including GPT-2 small, Gemma 2 2B, Gemma 3 1B, Llama 3.2 1B, and R1-Distill-Qwen 1.5B. They propose the first formal verification framework for the faithfulness of IRNs, moving beyond empirical evaluation on clean data. The result casts doubt on the reliability of widely used interpretability claims.

entry.title: Learning Multimodal One-step Flow Policy via Value-weighted Optimal Transport

author.name: Jaehun Shon, Jinha Choi, Jongwook Jeon, Jongmin Lee

entry.summary: The authors present OptiFlow, a framework for one-step flow policy learning in offline reinforcement learning that frames policy learning as a structured sample-allocation problem. It jointly trains a value-aware reference flow policy and an efficient one-step policy, coupling their samples through state-wise entropic optimal transport to avoid mode collapse and out-of-distribution value overestimation. This matters for deploying fast, single-step generative policies on multimodal offline data.

entry.title: Toward Optimal Switching Regret for Multi-Armed Bandits with Oblivious Adversary

author.name: Mengxiao Zhang

entry.summary: This paper resolves an open problem in adversarial multi-armed bandits by giving a single algorithm that attains near-optimal switching regret for every unknown number of arm switches against an oblivious adversary. It combines a fixed-share learner with a small learning rate and dyadic-interval subroutines that look for local improvements.

entry.title: JumpStart Your Policy Learning with Lessons from 160,000 Training Runs

author.name: Nabil Omi, Eric Bae, Chung Yik Edward Yeung, Siddhartha Sen, Ali Farhadi

entry.summary: This large-scale empirical study trains over 160,000 offline reinforcement and imitation learning policies across 114 datasets to systematically examine how reporting choices, hyperparameters, and dataset properties shape conclusions. It finds no universally dominant algorithm, with top methods close on aggregate yet differing substantially across environments, and distills practical guidance for reliable benchmarking.

entry.title: An immune world model for multiscale forecasting and therapeutic hypothesis generation

author.name: Taoyong Cui, Xi Wang, Zonghang Li, Jinchao Ding, Lingsen You, Yuzhi Xu, Wanghan Xu, Fang Wu, Kejun Ying, Wanli Ouyang, Pheng Ann Heng, Ling Yang, Zhenfei Yin, Yingcheng Wu

entry.summary: The authors build an Immune World Model, an action-conditioned model that learns how interventions move immune states across cellular, tissue and patient levels, constructed by a governed evolutionary AI Scientist that searched candidate architectures. The resulting model was frozen before independent confirmation and reportedly generalized to unseen interventions and biological contexts. It matters as a template for multiscale, intervention-aware models in therapeutic hypothesis generation.

entry.title: Rethinking Correctness for Uncertainty Estimation in Clinical Prediction with Vision-Language Models

author.name: Mingcheng Zhu, Jinning Liang, Tingting Zhu

entry.summary: Uncertainty estimation for clinical VLMs hinges on a correctness criterion that decides whether each output counts as right, and flawed criteria can distort conclusions about reliability. The paper proposes a two-axis framework evaluating correctness criteria by their agreement with human judgement and by their fidelity to human-referenced uncertainty estimation performance, then assesses eight criteria across three clinical prediction tasks and three models. This matters because unreliable correctness definitions could undermine safe deployment decisions in clinical settings.

entry.title: End-to-End Verifiable and Robust Federated Learning

author.name: Doryan Lesaignoux, Enrique M\'armol Campos, Gabriele Spini, Jos\'e L. Hern\'andez-Ramos, Stephan Krenn

entry.summary: Federated learning protects raw data but introduces integrity risks when clients or infrastructure are untrustworthy, and the two key needs, robustness to poisoned or Byzantine updates and public verifiability of aggregation, have mostly been pursued separately. The paper presents a protocol making a robust, outlier-excluding aggregation pipeline publicly auditable by combining cryptographic techniques. It matters because efficient public verifiability for robust aggregation has been a persistent gap in trustworthy federated learning.

entry.title: A Chosen Future Can Still Be Rewritten: Causal Writability in Video Models

author.name: Xingyun Wang, Haomin Zheng, Man Yuan, Leqian Yang, Ziming Liu

entry.summary: The authors show that when a video model generates physically incorrect motion, the correct motion is often still represented internally and can be made to control generation. Training on videos with slow red and fast blue oscillating masses, they find a low-dimensional edit derived from simple physical variables restores correct fast motion, and identify a sharp depth boundary at which the same edit stops working, which they call causal writability.

entry.title: When Can You Trust Your Synthetic Users? Diagnostics and Corrections for LLM Consumer Panels

author.name: Robson Tigre, Hugo Gobato Souto

entry.summary: The paper argues that aggregate validation metrics hide systematic failures in LLM-based synthetic consumer panels, including variance compression, coefficient sign-flips, subgroup error balloons of 10-30 percentage points, and global corrections that worsen demographic bias. It provides a formal framework decomposing synthetic-panel bias into covariate and concept shift, with testable diagnostics, decision thresholds, and a doubly robust AIPW estimator requiring only a small calibration sample.

entry.title: Part Grounding, Not Action Knowledge: Locating the Bottleneck in VLM Affordance Prediction

author.name: Sarthak Sattigeri

entry.summary: This paper separates two steps that affordance questions conflate: identifying which part of an object to act on, and knowing what action that part requires. Across 19 articulated objects and eight models from three developers, it finds that under an open prompt push was produced only once in 64 evaluations where it was correct, and inspection shows models often describe a different part than the one being scored.

entry.title: Physically Typed and Geometry-Aware Representations for Earth Foundation Models

author.name: Rajiv Ranjan

entry.summary: The author proposes that Earth-observation foundation models should respect physical transformation laws, distinguishing scalars, polar vectors, pseudovectors, covectors, and higher-order tensors rather than treating all latent embeddings alike. The position paper contrasts semantically rich geospatial embeddings with geometry-aware weather and climate models that use spherical operators, meshes, and hybrid solvers. It argues for unifying these two threads in a physically typed Earth foundation model.

entry.title: CyclOT: Learning Quadratic Optimal Transport Maps via Synchronized Forward-Backward Interpolants

author.name: Shizhou Xu, Jiachen Liu, Shih-Hsin Wang, Stefan Broecker, Yuhao Huang, Bao Wang, Thomas Strohmer

entry.summary: CyclOT learns both forward and reverse quadratic optimal-transport maps from unpaired samples by training bidirectional neural maps whose displacement interpolants are synchronized. The objective combines a bidirectional quadratic action, discriminator-restricted Jensen-Shannon endpoint terms, and two-sided cycle consistency, avoiding precomputed pairings or explicit convex potentials. The authors prove a population-level recovery guarantee under stated regularity conditions.

entry.title: Artificial entrepreneurial cognition: Locating and causally steering an opportunity recognition dial inside large language models (LLMs)

author.name: Christian Fisch, Angela Altmeier, Martin Obschonka, Michal Kosinski, Pin Ni

entry.summary: The authors introduce the notion of artificial entrepreneurial cognition, the functional organization of entrepreneurship-relevant representations inside AI systems, and use representation engineering to locate an opportunity-recognition direction in Llama 3.1 8B-Instruct. Using 636 matched scenario pairs with and without an opportunity, they identify a direction that can be causally steered to dial opportunity recognition up or down. It matters as a cross-disciplinary demonstration that mechanistic interpretability can measure and manipulate an economically meaningful cognitive construct in an LLM.

entry.title: SpectralShift: Effective Context Window Extension of Gated DeltaNet via Spectral Reparameterization

author.name: Zian Liu, Yiwen Hu, Zican Dong, Tian Xie, Wayne Xin Zhao, Yucheng Ding, Ran Tao, Bryan Dai

entry.summary: SpectralShift studies long-context extension of Gated DeltaNet from the spectral perspective of its transition matrix, identifying two requirements for long-range retrieval: a sufficiently broad slow spectral band matched to the target dependency length, and preservation of fast-decaying modes for state clearing and context switching. It then applies spectral reparameterization to extend context rather than naive continued pretraining.

entry.title: Quantifying the Generation Modality Gap in Speech-Text Language Models

author.name: Ju-Chieh Chou, Jiawei Zhou, Karen Livescu

entry.summary: The paper builds a unified, generation-based evaluation suite to compare speech-only, text-only, and speech-text language models trained on matched data and evaluated under matched settings, using flow-matching acoustic generation. It measures semantic coherence, lexical fidelity, and other dimensions to quantify how much pure speech models lag behind text and speech-text systems.

entry.title: ModularRSI: Modular and Generalizable Recursive Harness Self-Improvement

author.name: Siwei Wu, Jincheng Ren, Yizhi Li, Haau-Sing Li, Chengran Yang, Yuxuan Zhang, Weicheng Gu, Jian Yang, Riza Batista-Navarro, Chuanyi Zhang, Xianglong Liu, Ming Zhou, Bryan Dai, Chenghua Lin

entry.summary: This work targets recursive self-improvement of agent harnesses for long-horizon coding and terminal tasks, arguing current approaches conflate benchmark-specific adaptation with reusable improvement. It proposes modular harness evolution that localizes recurring behavioral deficiencies rather than rewriting monolithic harnesses, aiming for better transfer to unseen tasks.

entry.title: Dream-RSI: Recursive Self-Improvement through Evolving Worlds

author.name: Tong Zheng, Xidong Wu, Zheng Zhang, Zhankui He, Chaoyi Zhang, Benjamin Coleman, Ruoqiao Wei, Di Bai, Haolin Liu, Rui Liu, Xue Wang, Yue Zhuan, Wang-Cheng Kang, Renkai Xiang, Heng Huang, Xinwu Cheng, Yunsong Guo

entry.summary: Dream-RSI frames exploration strategy design as the bottleneck for recursive self-improvement in autonomous agents, where fixed strategies fail to scale and online policy optimization is expensive under delayed feedback. It adds a lightweight orchestration layer that makes exploration explicit and programmable while leaving the underlying system unchanged.

entry.title: Psychosis involves a deficit of information compression in connected speech

author.name: Samuele Vallisa, Claudio Palominos, Rui He, Emre Bora, Burcu Verim, Cemal Demirlek, Berna Yalincetin, Philipp Homan, Wolfram Hinzen

entry.summary: The study tests the hypothesis that psychosis involves a general deficit in information compression, using LLM embeddings and next-token predictions on connected speech. It operationalizes this via intrinsic dimensionality of LLM representations and mean surprisal, linking compression to grammatical organization as what enables prediction in language. The work sits at the intersection of computational linguistics and clinical neuroscience.

entry.title: Empathy Is Steerable but Multi-Axial: Mechanism Geometry and Persona Effects in LLMs

author.name: JuHeon Ha, Byounghan Lee, Yunseo Choi, Kyung-Ah Sohn

entry.summary: Using the EPITOME framework, which decomposes supportive empathy into Emotional Reactions, Interpretations, and Explorations, the authors test whether activation directions derived from these labels produce distinguishable intervention effects or share structure. Across three instruction-tuned LLMs they find contrastive activation addition yields a stable middle-layer intervention that consistently shifts empathy proxy scores. They also examine how persona prompts interact with those directions.

entry.title: TF-IDF and BM25 Are Exact KL Divergences

author.name: Ivan Silajev

entry.summary: The paper gives a probabilistic derivation showing that the classic retrieval scoring functions TF-IDF and BM25 can be interpreted as exact Kullback-Leibler divergences between two probability models. It handles the practical BM25 variant with the +1 correction in the IDF term as well as the original formulation. The result provides a unified theoretical foundation for these heuristics and enables principled comparison with other retrieval methods.

entry.title: FFVO: A Feedforward Pose Decoder for Long-Horizon Visual Odometry

author.name: Meng-Li Shih, Shih-Yang Su, Yuliang Zou, Hao Xiang, Haidong Zhu, Vincent Casser, Brian Curless, Dmitry Kalenichenko, Mingxing Tan, Dragomir Anguelov

entry.summary: FFVO adapts joint feed-forward reconstruction architectures into a pose-specialized decoder for stable long-horizon camera-pose estimation in autonomous driving. It uses a compact camera-token representation for efficient temporal aggregation and a hierarchical local-to-global temporal decoder that separates short-range motion aggregation from long-range consistency to mitigate geometric ambiguity. The goal is to make one-pass reconstruction networks practical over long videos where cost, long-context ambiguity, and temporal instability currently bite.

entry.title: AlayaVista: Streaming World Modeling from Panoramic States to Perspective Video

author.name: Jiaming Tan, Mingliang Zhai, Zhen Li, Yuwei Wu, Chuanhao Li, Kaipeng Zhang

entry.summary: AlayaVista is a camera-controllable streaming video world model that decouples panoramic world evolution from perspective observation synthesis. Starting from a single perspective image, it maintains global scene context while generating high-fidelity perspective views at low latency, avoiding the trade-off between off-screen content preservation and broad spatial coverage. This addresses a central tension in interactive video world models for long rollouts under camera motion.

entry.title: A 25-$\mu$s/inf Event-driven Graph Neural Network Processor with Spatiotemporal Caching and Spline Convolution for Ultra-low-latency AI at the Edge

author.name: Adrian Kneip, Martin Lefebvre, Daniel Gehrig, Victoria Catal\'an Pastor, Davide Scaramuzza, Marian Verhelst, Charlotte Frenkel

entry.summary: This paper presents ETHEREAL, an accelerator for event-driven graph neural networks on dynamic vision sensor data, claimed as the first EV-GNN accelerator scaling to 640x480 resolution. It combines a neighbor-parallel spline convolution engine with a 2D/3D split memory hierarchy and a region-of-interest spatiotemporal caching mechanism to handle the mix of dense-regular compute and sparse-irregular memory access. Measured results report end-to-end inference at 25.6 microseconds latency, positioning it for ultra-low-latency edge AI.

entry.title: SONAR: A Structure-Consistent Neural Operator for Null-Space-Aware Sparse View CT Reconstruction

author.name: Song Ni, Haijun Yu, Haodong Li, Changsheng Fang, Shuyi Fan, Yixing Huang, Hengyong Yu

entry.summary: SONAR is a structure-consistent neural operator for sparse-view CT that predicts a low-dimensional null-space-aware representation from acquired projections as pseudo-measurements, rather than estimating the full null-space in high-dimensional image space. It separates measurement residuals from pseudo-measurement residuals and lifts them into the image domain using physical modeling. The approach targets the severely ill-posed nature of sparse-view CT, where limited projections poorly constrain null-space information, and could improve dose-reduced imaging.

entry.title: Deformable 2D Gaussian Splatting for Efficient 4K Video Compression

author.name: Chenhao Zhang, Fengqing Zhu

entry.summary: The paper proposes a real-time video compression framework that represents and compresses groups of pictures using coarse-to-fine multi-scale deformable 2D Gaussian splatting, aiming to combine the rate-distortion competitiveness of learned compression with fast rendering. It targets ultra-high-definition video, where neural video compression and implicit neural representations suffer high decoding latency and memory use. The work is an early exploration of Gaussian splatting as a video codec representation.

entry.title: MedVA: An End-to-End Neuro-Symbolic Agentic System for Medical Volume Visualization

author.name: Haill An, Suhyeon Kim, Minjun Kang, Eunwoo Lee, Bin Sheng, Lei Bi, Younhyun Jung

entry.summary: MedVA is an end-to-end neuro-symbolic agentic system for medical volume visualization that selects regions of interest and controls their relative visual emphasis according to clinical intent. It argues that relying on multimodal LLM inference throughout the workflow can yield clinically incomplete interpretations and unreliable operations, so it combines neural components with symbolic control. The system aims to reduce the clinical and visualization expertise otherwise needed for trial-and-error transfer-function tuning.

entry.title: Multi-Stage NeRF for Efficient 3D Coronary Artery Reconstruction from Two Narrow-Angle Angiographic Projections

author.name: Deyu Meng, Mojtaba Lashgari, Yiying Wang, Abhirup Banerjee

entry.summary: NeCA++ is a multi-stage self-supervised neural radiance field framework for reconstructing 3D coronary arteries from just two narrow-angle angiographic projections, matching routine clinical acquisition constraints. It decomposes reconstruction into stages that progressively refine spatial support and representation capacity, targeting the failure of existing 2D-to-3D methods that assume wide angular coverage or many views. The work is aimed at improving 3D vessel understanding during real-time cardiac interventions.

entry.title: Differential Realizability of Static Control Allocation in Multirotors: An Impossibility under Nonredundant Full Actuation and a Pseudoinverse Obstruction under Redundant Actuation

author.name: Antonio Franchi, Mirko Mizzoni

entry.summary: The paper analyzes control allocation for multirotors with bidirectional propellers, noting that the signed-quadratic map from rotor speed to thrust is not a local diffeomorphism at zero speed. It proves that under nonredundant full actuation no globally continuously differentiable exact static allocator can exist, and that under redundant actuation a pseudoinverse-based allocator requires unbounded rotor-speed derivatives, introducing differential realizability as a formal criterion.

entry.title: Learning In-Hand Object Reaching to General 6D Poses

author.name: Junxiao Lin, Tianyue Wu, Jie Yin, Jia Pan, Kaifeng Zhang, Weiming Zhi

entry.summary: The paper formalizes in-hand 6D object pose reaching, where coordinated finger motions move a grasped object to a palm-relative target position and orientation without regrasping. It presents POISE, a sim-to-real reinforcement learning framework that combines diverse stable-grasp initialization and other techniques to achieve joint position and orientation control on multi-fingered hands.

entry.title: Force-Aware Reinforcement Learning with Hybrid Sensorless Force Estimation for Wheeled-Legged Loco-Manipulation

author.name: Xuanqi Zeng, Jiaming Wang, Tianlin Zhang, Lingwei Zhang, Botian Xu, Weipeng Xia, Zhongyu Li, Yun-Hui Liu

entry.summary: This work presents a force-aware reinforcement learning approach for wheeled-legged loco-manipulation that regulates end-effector interaction forces without an end-effector force/torque sensor. A hybrid estimate combining generalized momentum observation and other signals is supplied as an explicit policy observation, enabling force-guided contact behavior under floating-base dynamics and changing support contacts.

entry.title: VLBiMan++: Expanding the Generalization Boundary of Vision-Language Anchored One-Shot Bimanual Manipulation

author.name: Huayi Zhou, Wei Gao, Yiyang Han, Kui Jia, Hui Huang

entry.summary: VLBiMan++ extends a vision-language anchored framework for one-shot bimanual manipulation, starting from a single human demonstration that is decomposed into reusable and adaptable skill components. Vision-language grounded geometric adaptation then transfers these skills to novel tasks, objects, scenes, and embodiments without retraining, systematically expanding where one-shot generalization holds.

entry.title: GLAM: Training a latent world model over global spatiotemporal memory for active exploration and navigation

author.name: I-Tak Ieong, Ruizhi Feng, Zhaoyang Lu, Yifei Cao, Jiayao Zhao, Leon Li, Senhua Zhu, Wenbo Ding

entry.summary: GLAM is a goal-conditioned latent world model trained over global spatiotemporal memory that jointly predicts future map representations and robot-centric waypoint latents from map tokens, a goal, and current pose, following a JEPA-like latent prediction paradigm. GLAM NAV wraps this into a full navigation system for active exploration and semantic navigation. It matters because it unifies memory, prediction, and planning intent in a shared latent space instead of treating them as separate modules.

entry.title: InterSocialBench: Benchmarking Human and LLM Preferences for Companion-Robot Social Behavior

author.name: Yaodan Xu, Boyang Guo, Yuqing Gu, Qingxin Zhang, Yiwen Deng, Meng Liu, Lintian Li

entry.summary: InterSocialBench is a benchmark of 210 domestic scenarios and 18 high-level behaviors that pairs judgments from 100 human participants with 23,520 responses from seven large language models across 16 personality conditions. Annotations distinguish a preferred action from explicitly appropriate and inappropriate alternatives, with structured construction covering behavioral alternatives, competing situational cues, and task history, and evaluation separating preference agreement from explicit rejection.

entry.title: DIDO: Distilling Interaction-Centric Dynamics into One-Step Denoising for World Action Models

author.name: Jing Lyu, Shuanghao Bai, Runze Xiao, Zhenyu Liao, Wenxing Tan, Zihan Tang, Ruochuan Shi, Cheng Peng, Yuheng Ji, Yihao Wang, Badong Chen, Pengwei Wang, Zhongyuan Wang, Xiaoguang Zhao

entry.summary: DIDO targets the latency of video-generation-based World Action Models for manipulation, observing that scene structure converges in early denoising steps while gripper and object interaction dynamics stay blurry and only emerge later. Naively truncating a multi-step video model to one step therefore preserves structure but loses the interaction-centric dynamics, so DIDO distills the converged multi-step dynamics into a one-step denoiser.

entry.title: WLA$^3$: World Latent Action Modeling for Semantics, Dynamics, and Kinematics

author.name: Peidong Liu, Zhiyuan Xiang, Mingyang Li, Wenhao Li, Jiale Zhang, Jiahao Sun, Jiawei Li

entry.summary: WLA3 is a unified generalist policy framework built around representations learned by a World Latent Action Model, motivated by the lack of clean, unified action supervision across heterogeneous data sources such as human egocentric video. The WLAM learns how multimodal world states change over a local interval, encoding synchronized camera views and available embodiment-state changes into a compact latent action plus a richer transition representation.

entry.title: Automting AI Safety Research: 1 Managing expectations

author.name: Gerard Boxo

entry.summary: The first post in a series arguing that large parts of AI safety research could soon be automated, and that expectations should be calibrated accordingly. It identifies three recurring alignment challenges and argues that automated researchers will likely accelerate capability measurement and technique development but struggle to justify that those techniques remain reliable under stronger optimization pressure.

entry.title: Towards a knowledge-enhanced single-cell foundation model

author.name: Hanqing Zhang, Jie Bao, Mei Ma, Shuai Liu, Jiaying Ma, Jiaguan Liu, Jiaxiao Li, Zhenbo Li, Wenwen Gong, Zhijun Ca

entry.summary: The authors report that expanding transcriptomic pretraining data yields diminishing returns, while incorporating biological knowledge such as cell-level text annotations and gene-level regulatory information opens an additional scaling dimension. They present scKITE, a single-cell foundation model that injects annotation and regulatory supervision through lightweight auxiliary decoders used only during pretraining.

entry.title: Issue Bias in Generative AI Writing Assistance: Political Issues and LLMs in the Swedish 2026 Election

author.name: Bastiaan Bruinsma, Annika Fred\'en, Paul R\"ottger, Moa Johansson, Asad Sayeed

entry.summary: The authors probe six LLMs with 107 Swedish policy propositions crossed with 77 writing templates and three prompt framings, generating over 148,000 responses to measure default stance tendencies and framing sensitivity ahead of the 2026 Swedish election. It offers large-scale empirical evidence on how AI writing assistants may shape voter information.

entry.title: When Tool Calls Succeed but Workflows Fail: Anomalies at the Agent-Tool Boundary

author.name: Artem Trofimov, Boris Novikov

entry.summary: This paper studies long-running agent workflows where individual tool calls succeed yet the overall workflow state becomes inconsistent under retries, speculative execution, concurrency, and partial failures. It contributes an effect-history model that separates the semantics transaction systems need (occurred, compensable, staged, reorderable) from what shared agent-tool interfaces actually expose.

entry.title: Planning as Dynamics Relaxation: Hippocampal Recurrent Network Realizes Optimal Goal-Directed Navigation

author.name: Yuhang He, Junfeng Zuo, Tianhao Chu, Si Wu

entry.summary: The paper shows that a hippocampal recurrent network whose weights encode transition probabilities between spatial locations can perform optimal goal-directed navigation through relaxation dynamics, with obstacles represented as vanishing connections. Learned via behavioral-timescale synaptic plasticity, the network handles complex environments with obstacles and blocked corridors. It offers a biologically plausible account of planning that connects cognitive map theory to dynamical systems.

entry.title: When Malicious Instructions Persist: Persistent Memory Poisoning Attack on Harness-Based Agents

author.name: Shuhuai Huang, Jingfeng Zhang, Hong Jia

entry.summary: The authors propose PMPA, a Persistent Memory Poisoning Attack that embeds malicious instructions into benign external sources so a victim agent writes them into persistent memory without any direct access to the agent framework. Once stored, the poisoned memory is retrieved in later sessions, triggering further malicious actions and privacy leakage, and the attack is evaluated on the named agent platform.

entry.title: AGENTQ: Quantization-Conditioned Backdoor Attacks on LLM Agents

author.name: Xiaoqun Liu, Qiben Yan

entry.summary: AGENTQ studies quantization-conditioned attacks, in which an adversary ships a full-precision checkpoint that passes audits but misbehaves only after quantization, and extends this threat to LLM agents where the triggered payload is a structured function executed without human oversight. The authors find that naively adapting prior backdoor injection methods achieves malicious behavior after quantization but at a large cost to benign utility, motivating agent-specific attack design. It matters because quantized open-weight agents are a common deployment path assumed to be behavior-preserving.

entry.title: The Stochastic Deputy: Structural Tenant Isolation for Tool-Using LLM Agents

author.name: Mirza Samad Ahmed Baig, Syeda Anshrah Gillani, Asher Ali, Muhammad Hamzah Siddiqui

entry.summary: This paper formalizes the stochastic deputy problem: multi-tenant tools that accept a tenant identifier and validate it against the caller's entitlement effectively delegate resource selection to an LLM whose context may contain attacker-controlled instructions. The proposed structural defense removes tenant identity from the Model Context Protocol tool schema, binds scope to a verified credential and enforces it below the agent. In a 373-trial ablation across eight model configurations and two transports, a correctly validated tenant parameter served every out-of-scope attempt, while removing the parameter made such requests inexpressible.

entry.title: AgentKV: Phase-Aware KV Eviction for Agentic LLMs

author.name: Taowen Tony Liu, Jeffrey T. H. Wong, Can Xiao, Bowen Yang, Hao Mark Chen, Yiren Zhao

entry.summary: AgentKV shows that agentic generation breaks the recency assumption behind most KV-cache eviction policies, because future queries form a mixture over think, act and tool-use phases that occupy measurably different query subspaces. The method keeps a small query buffer per phase and scores cached keys against their union to avoid evicting tokens later phases will need. It matters because agentic serving consumes far more tokens than chatbot workloads and is bandwidth- and capacity-bound.

entry.title: Single-condition neural solvers encode transferable response spaces for parametric differential equations

author.name: Wenbo Cao, Weiwei Zhang

entry.summary: The paper shows that the output Jacobian of a neural solution model trained at a single parameter condition defines a reusable response space for cross-condition solution variation. It introduces Linearized Subspace Transfer, which recovers target solutions by minimizing the target PDE residual over response-space coordinates, and Active Transfer Modeling, which uses post-transfer residuals as coverage indicators to selectively acquire response spaces from further single-condition models. This could drastically reduce the data and physics-constrained training needed for parametric PDE operator learning.

entry.title: Same path, different: a mechanistic comparison of looped and stacked transformer encoders on 12-lead ECG

author.name: Pawel Olszowiec, Michal Byra, Grzegorz Gruszczynski, Grzegorz Stefanski, Alberto Presta

entry.summary: Recurrent or looped transformers that reuse one weight-tied block L times are gaining popularity for parameter efficiency, but their representational and dynamical differences from stacked transformers remain uncharacterized. This controlled study trains a looped bViT and a standard ViT on 12-lead ECG classification from PTB-XL under identical protocols, finding accuracy parity despite an 8.9x parameter reduction, and uses geometric similarity metrics to compare latent representations. It provides rare mechanistic evidence about what weight tying preserves and what it changes.

entry.title: ABSOL: Aggregated Bayesian Subsampling Orchestrated with LLMs

author.name: Jackson Hassell, Chen Shen, Estevam Hruschka

entry.summary: ABSOL is a hybrid framework that uses large language models as bounded semantic guides to help learn Bayesian network structure from data, aiming to keep probabilistic reasoning explicit while reducing the cost and fragility of structure search. Evaluated on five discrete Bayesian network benchmarks ranging from 27 to 1041 nodes, it is reported as the only method tested that produces a viable graph on every benchmark and achieves the best edge F1 on the larger networks. It matters as a concrete example of LLMs augmenting rather than replacing structured probabilistic reasoning.

entry.title: LynnReal-Omni: Native multi-modal Video Generation for Agentic Visual Workflows

author.name: Xiaofeng Mao, Peijia Lin, Shaohao Rui, Yibo Zhang, Haibin Wan, Weijie Ma

entry.summary: LynnReal-Omni is a 32B shared multimodal diffusion transformer that unifies text-to-video, image-conditioned, reference-guided generation, structural control, editing, and degraded-input restoration in one native multimodal framework. The motivation is that stochastic video diffusion is hard to control for long-horizon scenes, while agentic creation (references, editable 3D scenes, game states) provides control but not fidelity, so combining the two yields stable high-quality generation. It is a unified large-scale video generation system aimed at agentic visual workflows.

entry.title: Exact Feasibility Certification and Optimal Responsibility Allocation for Multi-Robot CBF Safety Filters

author.name: Chandan Kumar Sah, Jishnu Keshavan

entry.summary: This paper develops an exact feasibility certificate for multi-robot control barrier function safety filters with heterogeneous control-affine dynamics and convex input sets, decomposing a feasibility reserve into safety demand versus actuator supply. The decomposition shows when CBF gain tuning or added actuation can and cannot resolve infeasibility and identifies which agents and interactions cause the conflict. It also proposes an algorithm to optimally allocate shared safety constraints by maximizing the reserve.

entry.title: Generalized Agent Iteration: One Formal Framework for Iterative Policy Improvement and Recursive Self-Improvement

author.name: Hongyao Tang, Yi Ma, Pengyi Li, Yifu Yuan

entry.summary: The paper observes that 'recursive self-improvement' is invoked at many scales without a unified formal account, and proposes Generalized Agent Iteration (GAI) as a framework covering both classical iterative policy improvement and RSI as cases of one learning paradigm. It aims to give theoretical grounding to claims about self-improving agents where the update principle and evaluation base shift inside the agent.

entry.title: Safety as a Constraint: Fine-Tuning a LLM Recommender to Explain Itself

author.name: Jiashu He, Emma Yanyang Kong, JJ Tan, David Fagnan

entry.summary: The authors train a recommender LLM to generate personalized explanations for its recommendations from a user's viewing history at a large video streaming service. They impose faithfulness and safety-style constraints on the generated explanations so the model explains itself without relying on costly frontier-model calls in the member-facing pipeline. It matters because self-explaining recommenders can raise user trust while cutting latency and cost.

entry.title: Do Not Restart: Residual Completion for Stateful Agent Handoffs

author.name: Runzhi Deng, Yiming Zhong, Fang Zhao, Pan Zhou

entry.summary: This paper formulates commitment-constrained residual completion and proposes Commitment-Frontier Residual Completion, or CFRC, for stateful handoffs between models and agents. CFRC enforces target-before-proposal, whole-proposal-before-authority, and live-evidence-before-success, freezing a residual contract from accepted progress and admitting execution only when the remainder is fully covered. It matters because routing and cascades reduce cost but risk losing accepted choices, realized effects, and unfinished obligations.

entry.title: When does a scaling result justify a different allocation? A critical review of resource-allocation evidence for AI systems

author.name: Seyed Morteza Emadi

entry.summary: This critical integrative review asks when a reported scaling result actually licenses a resource-allocation decision, comparing evidence across pretraining, test-time computation, retrieval and agent evaluation. It distinguishes the performance of a tested procedure from the best achievable performance under a budget and identifies recurring mismatches such as counting success before an answer is chosen, assuming information a deployed system will not have, and omitting costs.

entry.title: Bayesian Intelligence from the Outside

author.name: Alex Smolin, Bryan Wilder

entry.summary: The authors develop a theory of Bayesian intelligence for agents such as language models, in which each prompt induces a possibly imperfect internal experiment and the agent reports its posterior over answers after updating a full-support prior. Under repeated independent draws from the same unobserved experiment, they show the agent's behavior admits this explanation exactly when its reports are never fully contradictory, with frequencies and probability sizes imposing no further restrictions.

entry.title: Self-Orchestrating Language Models: Leveraging Semantic Dependence for Efficient Inference

author.name: Tian Jin

entry.summary: This thesis argues that language models can direct their own inference execution by annotating which tokens depend on which others, enabling strategies such as speculative or parallel decoding, adaptive computation, and better long-context memory behavior. The goal is to reduce autoregressive latency and memory bottlenecks in low-batch, long-context deployment.

entry.title: RSIAgent: Autonomous Exploration for Recursive Self-improvement in New Environments

author.name: Sibo Zhu, Shicheng Fan, Xinyue Wang, Wenyi Wu, Kun Zhou, Biwei Huang

entry.summary: RSIAgent is a training-free multi-agent framework where curriculum, actor, and verifier agents cooperatively explore unfamiliar environments, validating outcomes and storing reusable causal relationships between actions, conditions, and consequences. It uses a broad-then-deep exploration strategy to find both diverse environment structure and hard-to-discover behaviors.

entry.title: EEG-Xplain: Decoding Neural Black-Boxes of EEG Foundation Models

author.name: Hansong Ma, Junxiao Wang

entry.summary: This work introduces a unified attribution framework for interpreting EEG foundation models such as BIOT, LaBraM, and EEGMamba across heterogeneous architectures. It combines gradient-, perturbation-, and activation-based explanations to analyze behavior spatially via topographic channel maps, temporally via attribution heatmaps, and in the frequency domain.

entry.title: KnowBench: Effort Reduction as a Unified, Deployment-Grounded Benchmark for Clinical AI

author.name: Jocelyn Kang, Caroline Zhang

entry.summary: KnowBench proposes Effort Reduction as a single deployment-grounded metric for clinical AI, defined as the proportion of system-generated clinical work product accepted by the responsible clinician under expert and safety review. The identical construction is instantiated across tasks such as visit notes, coding, orders, chart summarization, and patient summaries, replacing research-style similarity and rubric evaluations.

entry.title: When Should a World Model Move? Loss-Conditioned State Execution

author.name: Jintao Xu, Zhengyu Chen, Ben Zhang, Yongzhi Qi, Jianshen Zhang

entry.summary: The paper introduces loss-conditioned state execution, a model-agnostic method that decides whether to execute a world model's feasible proposal or retain the current state. It formalizes state movability as the existence of a loss-reducing feasible correction and shows that predictive informativeness or occurrence ranking alone does not guarantee reduced downstream loss, with two transition laws sharing occurrence and variance yet requiring opposite decisions.

entry.title: Multimodal-Multiresolution Foundation Model for Lunar Remote Sensing

author.name: Paolo Fraccaro, Gabby Nyirjesy, Daniela Szwarcman, Himanshu Patil, Vishal Gaur, Rohit Lal, Rachel A. Slank, Geoffrey Dawson, Hiyam Debary, Michael K. Barker, Andrew Annex, Vishnu Viswanathan, Zachary Morse, Ethan I. Schaefer, Nikolaos Dionelis, Ankur Kumar, Campbell D. Watson, Manil Maskey, Rebekah I. Dawson-Rigas, Juan Bernab\'e-Moreno, Rahul Ramachandran, Sujit Roy

entry.summary: The authors pretrain a multimodal foundation model from scratch on SomBench, a geographically partitioned corpus of nearly two million co-registered tile bundles spanning 11 modalities at 1 m and 100 m per-pixel scales. The model extends the TerraMind masked-token architecture with explicit acquisition-geometry context and joint multi-resolution training so one set of weights covers both scales. It is a substantial domain foundation model for planetary science.

entry.title: Decoupling Error Attribution in Cloud-Native Graph-RAG: A Data Integrity Diagnostic Framework

author.name: Shuai Yan, Yuhang Wu, Xiaodong Huang, Ke Wang

entry.summary: The authors propose a three-layer diagnostic framework that separates errors in cloud-native Graph-RAG systems into reasoning loss, knowledge graph defects, and Cypher query generation errors. Evaluated on a spatio-temporal ecological knowledge graph with eight injected defect types, the study finds data integrity rather than algorithmic reasoning is the dominant bottleneck, with structural defects dropping accuracy from 0.93 to 0.39, and it describes a Parametric Knowledge Masking Effect where model priors compensate for broken retrieval. This matters because it reframes Graph-RAG evaluation around data quality and provides a decomposition method for diagnosing failures.

entry.title: One Spectrum, Two Resources: Data-Memory Scaling in Autoregressive Prediction

author.name: Chiwun Yang, Xiaoyu Li

entry.summary: This theoretical paper shows that data quantity and learned memory capacity are governed by a single predictive-energy spectrum in a positive-entropy autoregressive retrieval source. Each coordinate contributes its query probability times the squared radius of its unknown logit, and the authors prove a minimax law where data set the resolution and memory sets a level reached by optimal bit allocation, with the full curve also recovering the spectrum. It matters as a step toward principled joint scaling laws that explain how much state or context is needed to benefit from more data.

entry.title: Open-UniMo: Towards Unified Motion-Language Understanding and Generation in the Open World

author.name: Guocun Wang, Kenkun Liu, Guorui Song, Jing Lin, Zhe Huang, Luyuan Zhang, Dake Zhong, Choo Sin Wai, Xiaoguang Han, Haoqian Wang

entry.summary: Open-UniMo is a unified Large Motion-Language Model trained on million-scale open-world motion-language data, extending a Qwen text vocabulary with motion tokens to give motion representation parity with text. It argues that treating motion as an auxiliary modality creates text-dominated representations and limited cross-modal interaction, and that next-token prediction is a poor fit for long motion sequences due to error accumulation. The work is a step toward embodied systems that both synthesize and interpret human actions.

entry.title: A Responsive Present, a Shared Past, a Social Other: Teens' Overreliance on Companion AI Chatbots

author.name: Mohammad Namvarpour (Matt), Tyler Chang, Afsaneh Razi

entry.summary: Analyzing 17,053 verified quotations from 3,930 teen-relevant Reddit posts via thematic analysis, the study maps 53 topics across seven groups describing how teens experience AI companions. It documents both benefits such as comfort, recognition and identity exploration and harms including problematic attachment, social substitution, emotional dependence and academic disruption.

entry.title: Pick Your Poison: Learning to Select Poison Sets for Stronger LLM Backdoor Attacks

author.name: Aashiq Muhamed, Mona T. Diab, Virginia Smith, Andrew Ilyas, Matthew Jagielski

entry.summary: The paper shows that fixing the number of poisoned examples and sampling them randomly substantially underestimates worst-case backdoor vulnerability: across three LLaMA-3-8B settings, attack success ranges from 3% to 80% depending only on which poison set is chosen. It formalizes poison selection as oracle-budgeted set optimization and introduces SAILS, which learns a set scorer from a few hundred fine-tuning runs to select stronger poison sets.

entry.title: Not All Prompts Are Equal: Exploration-Guided Prompt Scaffolding for Multimodal Reinforcement Post-Training

author.name: Yuanhao Yue, Qianli Ma, Chengyu Wang, Haoting Wang, Lei Shen, Jun Huang

entry.summary: This work argues that training prompts in online RL for multimodal LLMs are unevenly informative, with saturated and overly hard prompts consuming equal rollout budget. It proposes an Exploration Potential Score derived from KL-regularized policy improvement theory and uses it to adapt the prompt distribution dynamically during post-training, requiring no extra rollout overhead.

entry.title: Clean Scores, Buried Evidence, and Confident Wrong: A Receipt-Based Audit of Frontier Agentic QA

author.name: Luis M. S\'anchez

entry.summary: This audit study shows that frontier models perform well on shallow document and chart reading but degrade sharply when evidence is buried, producing more forced declarations, more tool calls, and higher cost per correct answer. Confidence and benchmark calibration fail to capture these wrong answers, and a documented production incident shows fabricated structural claims mixed with accurate numeric tables. The author argues agentic evaluation needs claim-level provenance receipts, condition-aware scoring, and human-adversarial verification rather than leaderboard scores.

entry.title: Kaininja: Extending Native 3D Generators to the Part Level

author.name: Ruihan Yu, Lian Fu, Muyao Niu, Zheng-hui Huang, Yu-Ju Tsai, Sho Kuno, Fengbo Lan, Yonghao Yu, Erwin Wu, Ming-Hsuan Yang, Kaipeng Zhang, Zhixiang Wang

entry.summary: Kaininja extends native image-to-3D generators from producing a single fused mesh to producing part-level assets needed for editing, rigging, and simulation. The core technical idea is a dual-volume representation that overcomes the limitation of voxel grids storing only one surface sheet per voxel, which cannot represent interfaces where two parts touch.

entry.title: Algorithmic Information Dynamics of Learning: A Certified, Differentiable Complexity Controller for Grokking

author.name: Luan Ozelim, Hector Zenil

entry.summary: The authors replace the piecewise-constant Block Decomposition Method with a certified, differentiable complexity estimator so that algorithmic information dynamics can be used as a controller inside learning dynamics. Applied to grokking, the estimator acts as a controller that accelerates the transition in Levin's description-length-versus-time sense, within a data-dependent Occam boundary whose finite-size trend follows f_c proportional to ln p over p. It connects algorithmic information theory to a practical intervention on training dynamics.

entry.title: Inherited Heads: Audio language models track speakers with their text backbone's attention, and an attention-mass ranking retrieves a different set

author.name: Bojro Das

entry.summary: This paper shows audio language models are poor at tracking a designated speaker, scoring far below chance on a six-speaker description task, yet adding fixed biases to roughly a hundred attention heads redirects outputs to a chosen speaker with 90 percent or higher success and no training. Strikingly, heads selected purely from the text-only backbone transfer almost as well, indicating speaker tracking is inherited rather than audio-specific.

entry.title: Know When to Stop, Where to Restart: Accelerating Multi-Turn Agentic On-Policy Distillation

author.name: Zhiyu Gui, Kexin Huang, Jia Guo, Junkang Wu, Zihao Wang, Zhiqiang Zhang, Jun Zhou, Jiancan Wu, Xiang Wang

entry.summary: This paper targets the cost of on-policy distillation for multi-turn agentic training, which is dominated by autoregressive student rollouts. Analysis on the tau-squared benchmark shows that informative teacher supervision is concentrated in the prefix of each turn and that cross-turn loss of teacher endorsement is temporally locked to the student's first tokens, motivating adaptive stop-and-restart scheduling instead of fixed offline budgets. It matters for making agentic distillation affordable at scale.

entry.title: Learning to Solve Stochastic Controls with Unknown Drifts and Running Rewards: Theory, Algorithms and Convergence

author.name: Jin Ma, Gaozhan Wang, Jianfeng Zhang, Xunyu Zhou

entry.summary: The authors study continuous-time, potentially high-dimensional stochastic control where drift coefficients and running reward functions are unknown, adopting an exploratory relaxed-control formulation with entropy regularization. They derive probabilistic representations of the optimal value function and its gradient via an auxiliary process and develop scalable RL algorithms with convergence guarantees. It matters as a rigorous bridge between reinforcement learning and continuous-time stochastic control.

entry.title: Nearly Minimax-Optimal Regret for Linear Contextual Bandits with Arbitrary Adaptive Action Sets

author.name: Tianyuan Jin

entry.summary: This work studies stochastic linear contextual bandits where the set of available actions is an arbitrary menu that can depend on both the unknown parameter and the interaction history. It establishes matching upper and lower regret bounds up to logarithmic factors, showing an O(K^{1/4} sqrt(dT)) upper bound that improves on the prior O(sqrt(dKT)) result by a factor of K^{1/4} for small menus. Tightening these bounds matters for understanding how menu structure, particularly adaptivity, affects achievable learning rates.

entry.title: Impute-EM: Native Mixed-State Diffusion Models for Heterogeneous Data Imputation

author.name: Sergei Kholkin, Kirill Sokolov, Dmitry Baranchuk, Evgeny Burnaev, Alexander Korotin

entry.summary: Most diffusion imputation methods force discrete variables through continuous surrogates such as one-hot relaxations, creating a mismatch with data that mixes numerical, categorical and binary variables. Impute-EM is an Expectation-Maximization style framework that alternates between imputing missing entries with the current model and refitting a diffusion backbone on the completed data, instantiated with native mixed-state diffusion combining Gaussian and masked categorical components. This native treatment should improve imputation quality on heterogeneous tabular data.

entry.title: Solving Finite-sum Coupled Compositional Optimization via Multi-block-Single-probe Estimator

author.name: Wei Jiang, Sifan Yang, Yibo Wang, Lijun Zhang, Zechao Li

entry.summary: This work tackles finite-sum coupled compositional optimization of the form averaging f_i(g_i(w)), where each inner function is accessible only through a stochastic oracle and only O(1) functions can be sampled per iteration. The authors propose a multi-block single-probe estimator to track multiple coupled functions simultaneously, extending variance-reduction techniques like SPIDER and STORM to this harder setting.

entry.title: The Limits of Reference-Free Speech Quality Metrics as Evaluators and Rewards on Modern Text-to-Speech

author.name: Antonis Asonitis, Juan Pablo Zuluaga Gomez, Francesco Verdini, Aref Farhadipour, Marzieh Razavi, Pierre-Edouard Honnet, Vijeta Avijeet

entry.summary: This paper tests the assumption that reference-free quality predictors such as UTMOS, DNSMOS, and SCOREQ track human preference, across six human-rated corpora spanning artifact-rich to defect-free TTS. Using a pairwise protocol, it finds that predictors agree with listeners when one clip has audible defects, but once both clips are clean no single predictor reliably matches human preference, undermining their use as reward signals for preference optimization.

entry.title: Resolution-Independent Analysis of Encoder--Decoder Operator Learning via Limiting Kernels

author.name: Lei Shi, Jia-Qi Yang, Ding-Xuan Zhou

entry.summary: This work analyzes encoder-decoder operator learning in which a finite-dimensional encoded kernel induces an operator-valued kernel on the underlying function spaces. As input/output resolution increases the induced kernels converge in operator norm to a limiting kernel, letting regularity assumptions be stated independently of resolution. The authors give convergence bounds for regularized stochastic gradient descent with fixed and decreasing step sizes.

entry.title: Introspective Uncertainty Estimation for LLM-Based Code Generation

author.name: Thomas Klassert

entry.summary: This thesis asks whether introspection over a code LLM's internal hidden states can predict functional correctness of generated code at both response and line levels. It evaluates response-level methods on LiveCodeBench and BigCodeBench and extends the analysis toward fault localization for practical risk assessment. The goal is to make LLM code generation more trustworthy in software engineering workflows.

entry.title: Neuron Activation-based Computation of Logical Explanations for Deep Neural Networks

author.name: Tom\'a\v{s} Kol\'arik, Faezeh Labbaf, Fabrizio Leopardi, Grigory Fedyukovich, Michael Wand, Natasha Sharygina

entry.summary: This paper introduces a symbolic framework for computing formal explanations of neural network behavior that is parameterized by internal neuron activations and uses logical engines such as SMT solvers. Unlike prior work that either ignores relations between input features or relies on specialized NN verifiers that fail to scale, the approach yields explanations expressed in a general logical notation. The aim is efficient, scalable, provably guaranteed explanations for deep architectures.

entry.title: Strong and Compact Policies for Submodular Markov Decision Processes via LP-Based Submodular Orienteering

author.name: Lars Rohwedder, Rico Zenklusen

entry.summary: This theory paper studies MDPs where rewards are monotone submodular rather than additive, a variant that captures applications such as coverage and diversity-seeking sequential decision making. The authors connect the stochastic problem to deterministic submodular orienteering and derive LP-based policies that are both strong in approximation quality and compact in representation. It matters because it advances the theoretical foundations of reinforcement learning with non-additive, diminishing-returns reward structures.

entry.title: Thin-shell stability of Gaussian cooling: logconcave sampling with sesteric complexity from a cold start

author.name: Yunbum Kook, Santosh S. Vempala

entry.summary: Kook and Vempala prove thin-shell stability along the Gaussian cooling path for logconcave measures, generalizing the thin-shell theorem, and use it to improve cold-start sampling complexity to roughly n^2.5, matching the abstract Speedy walk bound. This is a meaningful step in the theory of high-dimensional logconcave sampling, a core primitive behind Bayesian inference and randomized algorithms.

entry.title: MTAC-IFBench: Benchmarking Instruction-Following in Multi-Turn Agentic Coding

author.name: Bosi Wen, Cunxiang Wang, Jiayi Gui, Haoke Zhang, Yilin Niu, Pei Ke, Dayong Yang, Hongning Wang, Minlie Huang

entry.summary: MTAC-IFBench targets instruction-following in multi-turn agentic coding, where agents must respect process constraints and developer directives throughout a task, not just produce functionally correct code. The benchmark is designed to fill the gap left by existing suites that focus on single-turn chat or final functional correctness.

entry.title: CITECHOICE: A Causal Audit of How Document Presentation Redistributes Citation Credit in Agentic Search

author.name: Sriram Selvam, Anneswa Ghosh

entry.summary: CITECHOICE performs a causal audit of citation allocation in multi-turn agentic search, selecting independently verified document pairs that support the same fact and replaying them in a hash-verified 2x2 design that crosses pair order with structured versus prose rendering. It finds that structured rendering concentrates citation credit in ways that shift which sources are credited.

entry.title: What Limits Us? Analyzing Self-Reported Limitations in NLP Research

author.name: Tawan Thaepprasit, Peeranuth Kehasukcharoen, Ding Wang, Remi Denton, Peerapon Vateekul, Piyawat Lertvittayakumjorn

entry.summary: The authors conduct a large-scale analysis of Limitations sections from ACL and EMNLP papers published between 2020 and 2025, a corpus too large for manual review. They build a human-AI hybrid framework for iterative qualitative coding and use it to trace trends in self-reported limitations, their correlation with paper attributes, and recurring writing patterns. The work matters as meta-science on how honestly and systematically the NLP community discloses weaknesses in its own research.

entry.title: Can We Trust the Judges? Validation of Factuality Evaluation Methods via Answer Perturbation

author.name: Sarra Gharsallah, Adele Robaldo, Mariia Tokareva, Giovanni Gatti Pinheiro, Ilyana Guendouz, Rapha\"el Troncy, Paolo Papotti, Pietro Michiardi

entry.summary: The paper introduces a meta-evaluation framework that systematically tests factuality metrics using controlled corruptions of gold-standard answers, producing ranked outputs with known degradation levels. Experiments show pipeline-based methods such as RAGAS factual correctness track degradation better than LLM-as-judge approaches. The authors also propose a new variant of the factual correctness metric.

entry.title: RESKILL: Explicit Failure Attribution and Structured Repair for Interactive Language Agents

author.name: Mengyi Deng, Xin Li, Duyi Pan, Zilin Wang, Zhiwei Li, Zhijiang Guo, Wei Wang

entry.summary: RESKILL addresses post-failure repair for language agents that rely on reusable skills, replacing opaque one-shot reflection with a structured repair state maintained across rounds. Given a failed rollout, it links failure hypotheses to candidate skill patches, selects local repairs via coverage-based attribution, retests the edited skill set in the environment, and uses retest outcomes to guide later edits. The LLM supplies structured repair factors while the repair procedure remains explicit.

entry.title: Enabling Streaming User Transcription in Full-Duplex Speech-to-Speech Models

author.name: Ke Hu, Nourchene Ferchichi, Edresson Casanova, Ankita Pasad, Elena Rastorgueva, Chen Chen, Nithin Rao Koluguri, Piotr Zelasko, Yifan Peng, Hainan Xu, Zhehuai Chen, Boris Ginsburg

entry.summary: The paper adds streaming ASR capability to an existing full-duplex speech-to-speech model by introducing a lightweight ASR head in parallel to the agent text head. The approach requires minimal extra parameters and no significant architectural changes, enabling real-time user transcription while preserving turn-taking and barge-in behavior. Applications include conversation logging, accessibility, and quality monitoring.

entry.title: Verifiable by Construction: Claim-Level Evaluation of Verbatim Citation in Clinical Question Answering

author.name: Jiashuo Zhang, Yuling Chen, Yvonne Commodore-Mensah, Michael Oberst

entry.summary: The paper evaluates whether current models can produce clinical QA answers that are verifiable by construction, meaning fine-grained verbatim quotes from reference material that substantiate each factual claim without requiring clinicians to open other documents. It builds a standardized harness to test the end-to-end chain: citing every factual claim, producing verbatim quotes, and ensuring quotes fully substantiate claims. The setting is high-stakes because clinicians need fast verification.

entry.title: STAGE: Diagnosing Semantic Transfer at Grounded Execution in Embodied Agents

author.name: Baosheng Jin, Yushen Liang, Hua Shen

entry.summary: The paper studies the semantic-action gap, where instruction semantics are recoverable by an embodied agent but weakly expressed in its continuous actions. It introduces SAT-Bench, a fixed-observation counterfactual benchmark that holds the visual scene and agent state constant while changing only instruction semantics. On LIBERO target-name and pixel-grounded relation swaps, target recovery reaches 100.0% and 95.8% while OpenVLA action sensitivity remains only 6.8% and 7.7%, a gap that persists across 1,000 additional counterfactuals.

entry.title: Structure-Token Evidence-Anchored Reasoning for Scientific Chart Understanding

author.name: Alberlucia Rafael Soarez, Camila Ferreira, Daniel Kim, Mariana Costa, Alejandro Torres

entry.summary: This paper introduces STEER, a method for scientific chart question answering that keeps a Llama-3.2-Vision encoder frozen and adds three modules: a chart structure graph encoder that binds ticks, legends and marks; evidence-anchored step reasoning that requires every arithmetic step to cite a specific graph node; and a weak-parser/strong-reasoner alignment scheme that uses a table extractor only as a teacher of node attributes. The work targets a real weakness of vision-language models, which often hallucinate plausible-looking numbers from charts they never actually read, and anchors reasoning in explicit coordinate-frame evidence.

entry.title: Realtime-Venus: A full-duplex interaction system with asynchronous delegation

author.name: Ruixiang Zhao, Hualei Wang, Renhe Sun, Enzhi Zhou, Jincenzi Wu, Xujie Song, Kexin Shi, Zihang Liu, Pengcheng Zhu, Jiayi Zhou, Baoyue Zhang, Changhao Zhang, Zitong Wang, Jinhong Wang, Tong Niu, Jingjing Liu, Junan Lin, Haolin He, Hengshuo Chu, Yuhui Chen, Jian Liu, Yuge Huang, Junliang Xing, Yuntao Wang, Weiqiang Wang, Chun Yu, Yuanchun Shi

entry.summary: Realtime-Venus is a proactive full-duplex interaction system built from two separately trained 9B models, one for audio-visual interaction and one for spoken dialogue, each integrating continuous perception, conversational control, and native speech generation on a shared causal timeline for user inputs, model outputs, and delegation events. A dual-loop runtime coordinates live interaction with asynchronous delegation, allowing the system to ground conversation in evolving visual context. It targets natural dialogue in digital and physical environments where timely, continuous responsiveness matters.

entry.title: Beyond OCR Accuracy: Text-Centric VQA Under Image Degradation with Modular and End-to-End

author.name: Ritali Vatsi, Rachapudi Jagadeesh, Shruti Singh Baghel, Himani Sharma, Amit Shukla, Pawan Goyal

entry.summary: This empirical study compares modular OCR-based pipelines (including a custom SA-DBNet detector combining ResNet-18, self-attention spatial modeling, and deformable convolutions) against an end-to-end vision-language baseline for text-centric visual question answering on degraded images. The evaluation covers 4013 degraded images and 7000 question-answer pairs, probing how motion blur, low resolution, and compression artifacts affect each paradigm. It matters because real-world document and scene-text understanding rarely enjoys clean inputs, and the paper quantifies the robustness gap between pipeline design choices.

entry.title: SPARK: Representation-Level KV Memory Alignment for Safer Vision-Language Models

author.name: Mohd Azfar, Izhar Dad Khan

entry.summary: SPARK is a two-stage framework that repairs multimodal KV memory during prefill to defend vision-language models against jailbreaks that split harmful intent across text and images. Stage 1 identifies harm-associated directions with a disposable diagnostic adapter, and Stage 2 projects them out and learns a lightweight residual repair anchored by an image-structural prior to keep visual grounding. It matters because it operates at inference without modifying model parameters.

entry.title: From Density to Biopsy Decisions and Malignancy Prediction: A Benchmark Study of Multimodal Large Language Models Against Radiologists in Digital and Contrast-Enhanced Mammography

author.name: Ali Abbasian Ardakani, Afshin Mohammadi, Taha Yusuf Kuzan, Beyza Nur Kuzan, Alisa Mohebbi, Masume Behruzi, Hamid Khorshidi, Ashkan Ghorbani, Elham Asadiara, Zeinab Khorshidi Lotfi, Ansar Rahman, Nedim Christoph Beste, U. Rajendra Acharya, Sepideh Hatamikia

entry.summary: This benchmark compares four multimodal LLMs against radiologists of varying expertise on breast density assessment, BI-RADS categorization, biopsy candidacy, and continuous malignancy probability using 179 paired digital and contrast-enhanced mammography exams. Radiologists generally matched or exceeded most MLLMs on density classification, and masking images added limited benefit.
