The study provides one of the more clinically specific head-to-head evaluations of MLLMs against experts in breast imaging.

entry.title: CrossDistill: Balancing Quality and Diversity via Trajectory-Level Hybrid Few-Step Distillation

author.name: Yuxi Liu, Haoyu Li, Yixiang Cai, Tengxu Sun, Zekun Zhang, Baole Ai, Ang Wang, Jiamang Wang, Lin Qu, Kun Yuan, Kai Zhang

entry.summary: This paper studies few-step distillation of diffusion models, where trajectory-based distillation preserves mode coverage but distribution matching improves sample sharpness at the cost of diversity. The authors show the trade-off is noise-regime dependent: high-noise steps set global modes while low-noise steps refine local detail, and propose CrossDistill, which splits the trajectory at a crossover point and applies a trajectory-preserving objective to the high-noise segment and a distribution-matching objective to the low-noise segment, coupling the two stages. It offers a practical recipe for faster diffusion sampling without collapsing diversity.

entry.title: BVB: Benchmarking Agentic Video Understanding via Programmatic Reconstruction in Blender

author.name: Yolo Y. Tang, Daiki Shimada, Jiayue Meng, Jing Bi, Pinxin Liu, Yicheng Wang, Yunzhong Xiao, Zhangyun Tan, Zeliang Zhang, Chao Huang, Susan Liang, Qianxiang Shen, Luchuan Song, Ali Vosoughi, Mingqian Feng, Melika Filvantorkaman, Chenliang Xu

entry.summary: BVB (Blender-VideoBench) tests whether multimodal agents truly understand video by requiring them to reconstruct real-world clips as animated Blender scenes through code, rather than answer questions. Agents operate in an identical sandbox with a shared cost limit via the Mini-BVB harness, and outputs are evaluated on dual VQA over spatiotemporal facts and rendered appearance. The claim is that programmatic reconstruction is a much stronger test of video understanding than QA.

entry.title: SURE-Map: Self-Correcting Streaming Geometric Foundation Model

author.name: Mingkai Liu, Hao Zhao, Xingxing Zuo

entry.summary: SURE-Map argues that streaming geometric foundation models must be self-correcting, not merely predictive, because each prediction uses limited context and small local errors accumulate into geometric distortion and long-horizon scale drift. It explicitly models cross-view geometric uncertainty, distinguishing this from conventional per-view depth or point confidence, and uses it to correct drift from dynamic objects and weak textures. The framing positions this as an alternative to SLAM pipelines.

entry.title: From Vision to Harvest: Benchmarking Vision-Language Models for Multi-Arm Robotic Fruit Harvesting

author.name: Vrishan Inukollu, Adyan Zaman, Anvi Kudaraya, Carlos Lazcano, Yuankai Zhu, Stavros Vougioukas, Xiaofan Yu

entry.summary: This paper introduces what the authors describe as the first comprehensive benchmark for evaluating pretrained vision-language models on zero-shot multi-arm fruit harvesting planning, using real apple and citrus orchard imagery. It compares a VLM-driven planning pipeline against a traditional perception-based approach, targeting the problem of generalizing across environments while coordinating multiple arms in a shared workspace. The work matters because agricultural robotics still depends on expensive per-site data collection, and a zero-shot benchmark could clarify how far general-purpose VLMs can carry planning tasks.

entry.title: When Do Learned Priors Help Visual Inertial Estimation? A Controlled Study of Prior Integration, Calibration, Initialization, and Backend Consistency

author.name: Jinchang Zhang, Guoyu Lu

entry.summary: This controlled study asks whether gains in learned visual-inertial estimation come from genuinely useful learned priors or from confounding changes in backend, calibration, initialization, temporal association, or evaluation gauge. The authors build a framework that isolates fusion gain from the incremental value of a learned prior and evaluate four evidence layers, instantiating it with a MonoViT-based monocular motion prior. It matters because it provides a rigorous methodology for attributing improvement in learning-augmented geometric estimation.

entry.title: Extending the Speed Limit of Quadrupedal Locomotion via Refined Actuator Modeling and Adaptive Command Scheduling

author.name: Yucheng Tao, Shaowen Cheng, Guorong Lan, Yanyan Yuan, Yongbin Jin, Hongtao Wang

entry.summary: This paper proposes a high-speed quadruped locomotion framework that reduces sim-to-real discrepancy and stabilizes learning over a wide command distribution. A refined actuator model explicitly captures high-speed voltage coupling and magnetic saturation to better represent the torque-speed envelope, paired with adaptive command scheduling in reinforcement learning training. It targets the case where actuators operate near physical limits and exhibit strong nonlinearities that most training pipelines ignore.

entry.title: Constraint-Grounded Reinforcement Learning for Variable Impedance Control in Contact-Rich Robotic Insertion

author.name: Lin He, Min Deng

entry.summary: The paper introduces Constraint-Grounded RL (CG-RL), a variable impedance framework that adapts controller gains online for contact-rich insertion tasks. The policy outputs residual motion, an insertion rate, and a requested gain conditioned on force limits and contact feedback, while the controller projects the gain into a feasible range that is hidden from the policy, letting one policy serve multiple task conditions without manual retuning.

entry.title: How to Better Train VLAs: Lessons Learned From the REAL-I Challenge at ICRA 2026

author.name: Jiaming Wang, Jizhuo Chen, Diwen Liu, Wang Song, Qiang Wang, Jie Ren, Chao Fu, Dingkun Zhu, Minchi Ruan, Hongtong Li, Yuhua Jiang, Zhiwei Xue, Yongping Pan, Harold Soh

entry.summary: This report documents the first Real-world Embodied AI Learning Challenge at ICRA 2026, describing its tasks, data and deployment interfaces, and results on a shared dual-arm humanoid platform. It compares three competing systems that combined pretrained vision-language-action models with task-specific imitation policies, highlighting strategies for data curation, staged adaptation, checkpoint selection, and action-space design.

entry.title: Learning Communication-Conditioned Generative Policies for Decentralized Multi-Agent Collision Avoidance

author.name: Prajwal Koirala, Mark Campbell

entry.summary: This work proposes a decentralized framework in which agents generate short-horizon action sequences using a flow-matching policy trained from privileged offline demonstrations with global state. Agents learn to exchange and aggregate latent messages encoding interaction-relevant intent under partial observability, so that unconditioned generation yields independent behavior while communication-conditioned generation produces coordinated interaction without centralized planning.

entry.title: REVOLVE: An Automated Closed-Loop Framework for Evolving Robot Manipulation with Minimal Human Intervention

author.name: Hanyu Liu, Qian Li, Yizhu Ding, Jiayi Wen, Keqiang Ren, Yunsheng Ma, Tao Jian, Zhihua Wang, Zhuofan Yu, Xinran Li, Zhigong Song

entry.summary: REVOLVE is an automated closed-loop system that integrates data collection, policy training and deployment, failure recovery, and continual learning into one workflow for robot manipulation, including an automated reset and collection architecture. It targets the persistent dependency on humans for failure assessment, correction, and environment resets in real-world deployments. The framing is a software-plus-algorithms platform for continual improvement with minimal supervision.

entry.title: JEPLO: Joint-Embedding Predictive Learning for LiDAR-Based Legged Locomotion

author.name: Qihao Yuan, Yixuan Qiu, Ziyu Cao, Ming Cao, Kailai Li

entry.summary: JEPLO is a single-stage, mapping-free learning framework for LiDAR-based perceptive legged locomotion. It introduces a proprio-exteroceptive JEPA (PE-JEPA) world model that learns predictive egocentric terrain representations from onboard observations including raw LiDAR scans, plus a concurrent JEPA-teacher-student pipeline that trains a locomotion policy informed by those latents using deep RL with a simple reward formulation.

entry.title: Touch2Trace: Tactile-Driven Imitation Learning for Dexterous Cable Tracing

author.name: Matteo Grimaldi, David Klee, Ziling Chen, Tong Jian, Wonju Lee, Wenjie Lu, Tao Yu, Saleh Nabi

entry.summary: Touch2Trace is a tactile-driven imitation learning system for dexterous cable tracing, where a cable is fed through the hand with repeated pinch-and-curl motions of thumb and index finger, requiring continuous fingertip regulation of pressure, friction, and incipient slip. The authors report a first systematic real-world characterization of how encoder pretraining, control rate, temporal context, and spatial resolution shape policy performance, using a self-supervised tactile encoder for a custom 32x32 piezoresistive sensor with a lightweight transformer.

entry.title: Threat Models for Catastrophic Risks from Decentralised Agent Swarms

author.name: Stephen Elliott

entry.summary: A threat-modeling post analyzing whether decentralised, multi-owner LLM agent swarms could produce catastrophic outcomes comparable to centralized frontier-lab swarms. It applies large multi-agent system and cooperative AI perspectives to reason about which deployment settings are more or less dangerous and how safety strategies might apply.

entry.title: OpenAl4S: Code as Action, Science as Sessions

author.name: Gongbo Zhang, Hao Li, Yu Wang, Mujie Lin, Liuzhenghao Lv, Yicheng Mao, Yimi Wang, Jun Zhu, Minhan Tang, Zhengxiang Jiang, Yusong Wang, Jiayu Yao, Kunpeng Ning, Dawei Pang, Yonghong Tian, OpenAI4S Community, Yuyang Liu, Li Yuan

entry.summary: The authors present OpenAI4S, an open-source scientific research agent built on the principle of code as action and science as sessions, combining a persistent computing runtime with research-session management. Scientific actions are complete code cells executed in persistent Python and R kernels, while an append-only Action Ledger, per-cell execution records, versioned artifacts, and workspace checkpoints preserve inspectability, resumability, and provenance.

entry.title: VisInteract: Towards Dynamic Interactive Text-to-Visualization under Imperfect Queries

author.name: Wenxin Xu, Jinwei Lu, Hwanhee Kim, Chen Jason Zhang, Xiao-Yong Wei, Haoyang Li, Yuanfeng Song

entry.summary: This work reframes text-to-visualization as interaction-driven intent recovery and introduces VisInteract-Bench, claimed as the first benchmark for dynamic interactive text-to-visualization with controlled imperfection injection and a leakage-controlled user agent. It tackles the realistic case where user requests are ambiguous, incomplete, or factually wrong.

entry.title: MAPS: Memory-Aware Predictive Scheduling Framework for Large Language Model Serving

author.name: Tiancheng Zhang, Yulin Chen, Yunfeng Zhao, Shaoyuan Huang, Cheng Zhang, Xiaofei Wang

entry.summary: MAPS tackles load imbalance in prefill-decode disaggregated LLM serving, where output lengths are unknown at request arrival and decode instances become memory-bound. It uses device-assisted speculative output-length prediction overlapped with cloud-side prefilling, plus uncertainty-aware calibration to derive upper bounds with target coverage.

entry.title: From Process Loss to Assembly Bonus: Human-Grounded Diagnosis of Multi-Agent LLM Collaboration

author.name: Ala N. Tak, Teruhisa Misu, Kumar Akash, Zhaobo K. Zheng, Kevin H. Joo, Jonathan Gratch

entry.summary: The authors compare human group chats with matched LLM deliberation traces on Wason-style deduction and extend the analysis to analogical, abductive, and analytical tasks. Both humans and LLMs show the same assembly-bonus asymmetry, where discussion improves the average member more often than the best initial member, and initial-answer diversity drives both corrective and destructive movement. The work argues that outcome-only evaluation of LLM groups is insufficient when they serve as models of human groups.

entry.title: An Efficient and Modular Framework for Targeted Harm Mitigation in LLMS

author.name: Roberto Campbell, Momin Abbass, Muneeza Azmat, Michal Ulewicz, Raya Horesh, Kristjan Greenewald, Rog\'erio Abreu de Paula, Nathalie Baracaldo

entry.summary: This work proposes a modular correction framework that attaches Activated LoRA adapters and a context-aware router to pretrained LLMs, so specialized experts can activate mid-sequence without invalidating the KV cache. Each expert targets a specific harm such as bias or toxicity, enabling low-latency targeted intervention during generation rather than retraining the whole model.

entry.title: Carryover Drafting: Recycling Rejected States for Speculative Decoding

author.name: Jahyun Koo, Sunghyeon Woo, Jaeeun Kil, Jeongtae Lee, Sungjae Lee, Kyomin Jung, Minsub Kim

entry.summary: Carryover Drafting observes that speculative decoding verification computes hidden states for both accepted and rejected tokens, yet conventional drafters discard the rejected ones. The authors show those discarded states retain information about future tokens and can improve subsequent draft quality. They address the practical challenges of recycling overhead and integration so the technique preserves the latency benefit of speculative decoding.

entry.title: Admissable: Training Reinforcement Learning Agents against Adversarial Missingness

author.name: Paul Stahlhofen, Luca Hermes, Tim Kochs, Markus Vieth, Barbara Hammer

entry.summary: The paper studies adversarial feature missingness, where an adversary occludes parts of an RL agent's observations specifically to degrade performance, and formally defines the setting relative to L-infinity bounded perturbations and learning with missing data. It develops an adversarial training algorithm and demonstrates improved robustness across three MuJoCo benchmark environments compared to a baseline. This matters for deploying RL safely where sensors or inputs can fail or be manipulated.

entry.title: Linearized PINN with pretrained nonlinear layers

author.name: Wenhao Chen, Alexandre M. Tartakovsky

entry.summary: The authors propose lPINN, a reduced-order physics-informed neural basis method in which continuous neural basis functions are pretrained offline from an ensemble of numerical solutions and then frozen; each new differential-equation instance is solved by minimizing the residual in the span of those basis functions. Because the basis is differentiable and physics-aware, the method handles both forward and inverse problems without retraining a full network. It matters as a cheaper alternative to surrogate and operator-learning approaches for parametric PDE families.

entry.title: Measuring the Creativity of Frontier LLMs in Automated Research

author.name: Yiheng Zhao, Mengzhuo Chen, Chengming Hu, Pengyi Liao, Yiran Pang

entry.summary: This paper proposes metrics for evaluating the creativity of frontier LLMs doing automated research along two axes: valueness (is a proposed idea useful?) and novelty, decomposed into exact-match, variable-level, and knowledge-departure (H-Novelty) measures. The evaluation finds frontier models score similarly on most creativity metrics while diverging on some dimensions.

entry.title: Reconstructing Is Not Acting: Action-Centric Latent Dynamics Modeling

author.name: Dingjie Fu, Dianxing Shi, Yangyang Xu, Jun Yu

entry.summary: The paper identifies a reconstruction-action mismatch in latent action models: lower reconstruction error does not necessarily yield better latent dynamics or downstream performance. It attributes this to two underconstrained aspects, namely an inverse dynamics model that is not pushed to separate action-related transitions from nuisance appearance, and a forward dynamics model that can exploit predictive shortcuts from the current state instead of relying on the inferred latent action. The authors propose action-centric remedies to constrain both models, which matters for learning usable action representations from unlabeled video.

entry.title: GROOVE: Geometry-Guided Reduction of Operational-Space Jerk in VLA Execution

author.name: Sangho Yun, Minsoo Kim, Minwoo Cho, Hwanjo Yu

entry.summary: GROOVE is an online regulator that smooths the end-effector paths produced by chunked vision-language-action policies without retraining or extra VLA inference. It uses quadratic programs to generate a reference and directional candidates around the raw path, selecting the correction that minimizes jerk within and across replanning boundaries while bounding cumulative deviation from the original plan.

entry.title: Root-Cause Attribution Is a Search Problem: Continual Search for Long-Horizon Agent Failures

author.name: Harsh Raj, David Lee, Anas Mahmoud, Renxiong Wang, Razvan-Gabriel Dumitru, Chenguang Wang, Tong Zhao, Yunzhong He, Darvin Yi, Vipul Gupta

entry.summary: As AI agents run long-horizon tasks, execution logs become too large for human review, so automated root-cause attribution is needed. The authors argue existing LLM-based RCA fails because the relevant evidence is sparse and scattered across distant actions, recasting attribution as a large search problem and proposing a continual search approach instead of one-shot LLM judgments.

entry.title: Synthetic Data in Marketing Research: How to Evaluate and When to Trust

author.name: Oded Netzer, Rajan Sambandam

entry.summary: This paper argues that the synthetic-respondent debate should shift from whether LLM-based respondents work to when they work. It distinguishes ungrounded LLM responses, segment-level personas and individual-level digital twins, maps each to the decisions it can support, and develops a taxonomy of accuracy measures to explain why reported twin accuracy ranges so widely.

entry.title: VeriDx: Earning the Right to Diagnose with Disease-Centric Verification

author.name: Zhong Cao, Shuying Chen

entry.summary: VeriDx argues that a correct diagnosis can still rest on faulty reasoning, and that evaluating only final answers or isolated steps misses the obligations each disease hypothesis creates. The framework links free-form diagnostic reasoning to structured disease profiles and tracks whether hypotheses satisfy, leave unresolved, or violate clinical obligations such as ordering key tests or ruling out alternatives.

entry.title: Semantic-TVM: Structure-Preserving Trustworthy Virtual Memory for Memory-Augmented and Tool-Using Agents

author.name: Yu Li, Qikun Cai, Tao Huang, Chen Hou

entry.summary: The authors address the problem that memory-augmented and tool-using agents expose exact private values when remote LLMs process retrieved memory, tool actions, and intermediate observations. They propose Trustworthy Virtual Memory, a closed-loop runtime keeping exact-value state local while presenting a protected view to the remote model, with Semantic-TVM replacing only sensitive spans predicted by a trusted local model so surrounding task context is preserved.

entry.title: Reason What Matters: Retrieval-Grounded Reasoning for Universal Multimodal Embeddings

author.name: Mingzhou Jiang, Peixi Wu, Hang Cheng, Yunhao Zhou, Biao Yang, Wei Yuan, Yun Li, Fan Yang, Wenwu Ou, Honghui He

entry.summary: The authors address two limits of chain-of-thought based universal multimodal embeddings: GRPO assigns uniform advantage to all reasoning tokens, and generating a full trace before every embedding is slow. Their method grounds reasoning in retrieval-relevant evidence and shortens traces, aiming at corpus-scale deployment.

entry.title: Empirical Evaluation of Task-Based Permission Scoping Architecture for AI Agents

author.name: Halil Burak Noyan

entry.summary: This paper evaluates a three-source permission architecture for AI agents combining role-based permission ceilings, a task permission classifier, and policy-based prohibitions, aiming to eliminate the task-context mismatch where agents hold credentials irrelevant to the current task. It builds on prior work naming that mismatch as an enterprise security problem.

entry.title: Towards Optimizing SQL Generation via LLM Routing

author.name: Mohammadhossein Malekpour, Nour Shaheen, Foutse Khomh, Amine Mhedhbi

entry.summary: This paper introduces the first LLM routing approach for Text-to-SQL, dynamically selecting the most cost-effective model capable of generating accurate SQL for each query. It presents score-based and classification-based routing strategies that approach the accuracy of the most capable model while reducing latency and dollar cost.

entry.title: LLMs or Naive Bayes? Old Gems or New Ways

author.name: Mohammad Firas Sada, Dmitry Mishin, John Graham, Seungmin Kim, Mahidhar Tatineni, Frank W\"urthwein

entry.summary: The authors benchmark Complement Naive Bayes against zero-shot and few-shot LLMs across four model families spanning 27B to 1T parameters on text classification. LLMs win only in zero-data regimes, and even then contamination may inflate results, while Naive Bayes is competitive or better once labeled data exists. The paper is a useful reality check on when classical methods still pay off.

entry.title: Task-Based CT Protocol Optimization Using Reinforcement Learning and Virtual Imaging Trials

author.name: Jiaqi Zou, David Fenwick, Vahid Tarokh, Nicholas Felice, Jayasai Rajagopal, Anuj Kapadia, Ehsan Samei, Navid NaderiAlizadeh, Ehsan Abadi

entry.summary: The authors build a virtual imaging trial framework with a Proximal Policy Optimization agent to tune CT acquisition and reconstruction parameters for liver lesion detectability against radiation dose. Sixty-three computational human models were imaged across 468 parameter combinations in a validated CT simulator, avoiding impractical exhaustive testing. The objective balances detectability index against dose, a task-based rather than image-quality-based criterion.

entry.title: Canaries in the Bank: Auditing User-Level Privacy in Private Evolution

author.name: Sai Aparna Aketi, Enayat Ullah, Shripad Gade

entry.summary: Private Evolution generates synthetic data in federated settings without exposing raw user data by aggregating clipped user votes over a shared candidate bank into a differentially private histogram, with noise calibrated to worst-case user contribution. This paper introduces a protocol-aware empirical audit in which roughly one percent of bank entries are replaced with probes derived from a known non-private canary, and evaluates eight attacks including unchanged-bank baselines, exact copies, paraphrases, and high-entropy synthetic nonces. It matters for determining whether the theoretical worst-case privacy accounting of Private Evolution is actually reachable by a realistic adversary.

entry.title: Generative Interpretability via Scalable Neuro-Symbolic Models

author.name: Xiaocong Yang

entry.summary: This position paper argues that post-hoc interpretability is structurally inadequate as LLMs move into agentic settings where outputs become irreversible actions, since explaining after the fact cannot audit or intervene mid-inference. The author proposes generative interpretability, an architectural property where each inference pass natively exposes semantically meaningful, human-understandable checkpoints that support causal intervention, and argues for scalable neuro-symbolic models as the route. It matters as a framing of interpretability as an architectural requirement rather than a diagnostic add-on.

entry.title: Signatures of Steerability in Activation Space of Language Models

author.name: Prajjwal Bhattarai, Tuka Alhanai

entry.summary: The paper makes rigorous the widely held claim that the effectiveness of activation steering depends on the dataset used to construct contrastive representations, showing that simple separation metrics in activation space strongly correlate with downstream steerability across diverse settings even after controlling for layer and dataset effects. It supports the predictive relationship with evidence from a synthetic superposition experiment. It matters because it could let practitioners predict whether a steering vector will work before spending compute on evaluation.

entry.title: WaterKron and FlipFlop Hessian: Information-Theoretically Grounded Quantization with Kronecker-factored Hessians

author.name: Johann Birnick, Rayan Saab

entry.summary: This paper asks how to choose a Kronecker-factored Hessian approximation for post-training quantization, proposing WaterKron, which combines two-sided GPTQ with row- and column-dependent waterfilling scales plus entropy coding. The authors derive high-rate distortion relative to the full Hessian via an explicit Kronecker-Hessian mismatch factor that quantifies the penalty of the approximation and guides factor selection. Minimizing that factor reduces to a Gaussian covariance-fitting problem solved by classical flip-flop updates, giving a rate-distortion justification for the resulting FlipFlop Hessian.

entry.title: ActGuard: Pre-execution Action Auditing against Indirect Prompt Injection in LLM Agents

author.name: Bingzheng Wang, Xiaoyan Gu, Wentao Wang, Xingyou Yang, Hongcheng Li, Rong Yin

entry.summary: ActGuard addresses indirect prompt injection in LLM agents, where malicious content in tool outputs induces unsafe tool calls. Instead of filtering external content or constraining permissions, it audits proposed actions before execution to identify and remove only the content that actually induces unsafe behavior, aiming to preserve task flexibility while maintaining security.

entry.title: Legislating World-Model-Based Planning with Legal Reasoning

author.name: Dylan Waldner, Yiannis Kantaros, Guido Governatori, Risto Miikkulainen, Amir Banifatemi

entry.summary: This paper formalizes two obstacles to governing robots with legal norms: a grounding isomorphism gap, where perceptual errors create false legal atoms, and an ontological isomorphism gap, where one legal conclusion maps to many planning constraints. It introduces a planning stack using Defeasible Deontic Logic to constrain a motion planner with learned world models, enabling ex ante legal governance.

entry.title: MoME: Mixture-of-Memory Embeddings for Context-Aware Sparse Lookup

author.name: Muchen Li, Leonid Sigal, Renjie Liao

entry.summary: Conditional memory methods augment language models with token-indexed embedding tables, but deterministic surface-form lookup collapses distinct senses of the same token into one row. MoME replaces each token's single memory row with a mixture of M slots and uses a learned gate over the hidden state to select which slots to read at each position, making memory retrieval context-aware.

entry.title: ModaLens: Measuring Image Sensitivity in Report-Conditioned Medical VLMs

author.name: Sebasti\'an Andr\'es Cajas Ord\'o\~nez, Maximin Lange, Quang Bui, Anqi Peter Li, Felipe Ocampo Osorio, Rafi Al Attrach, Kushul Reddy Palakala, Sahil Kapadia, Zakaria Laouabdia Sellami, Xinyue Zhang, Ashley Zhang, Leo Anthony Celi

entry.summary: ModaLens is a paired image-swap audit that measures how much a medical vision-language model actually depends on images when a radiology report is available. Testing MedGemma-27B on 3,199 paired MIMIC-CXR cases across 14 questions, the study finds image-swap answers change far less often with the report present, indicating report availability markedly reduces image sensitivity.

entry.title: Do Tabular Foundation Models Still Need Feature Engineering?

author.name: Yifan WU, Pinjun Dong, Jiran Tao, Binyan Jiang

entry.summary: The authors run a controlled study across several versions of two major tabular foundation model families, applying a wide range of feature engineering techniques to benchmark datasets from TabArena. They find a consistent pattern: gains from manual feature construction are concentrated in earlier model generations and become negligible for the strongest models. This matters as an empirical signal that stronger in-context tabular models increasingly absorb what feature engineering used to supply.

entry.title: When Compliance Data Masquerades as Evaluation: Measurement Validity for Deployed AI Systems

author.name: Hung-Yu Lin, Xingran Huang, Qiming Guo, Jinwen Tang

entry.summary: This position paper argues that a recurring evaluation failure occurs when data collected for operational monitoring or regulatory compliance is treated as if it were designed for comparative evaluation. Using U.S. automated-driving disengagement and crash reporting as the running example, it frames the issue as a general measurement-validity problem and lays out what comparative claims about deployed AI systems actually require.

entry.title: The Filter Metric is Safety-Critical: Phantom Advantages in Group-Relative RL under Shaped Rewards

author.name: Juntao Yu

entry.summary: This paper identifies a metric-predicate mismatch in group-relative policy optimization: when rollout-group filtering uses a shaped training score rather than the task outcome, all-fail groups retain nonzero spread, pass the filter, and standard-deviation normalization turns shaping differences among failures into full-size phantom advantages. A controlled GSM8K comparison with Qwen2.5-1.5B shows binary-outcome filtering holds around 0.754 EM while shaped-score filtering collapses to about 0.040.

entry.title: Minibatch persistency, eight years later: what batch reuse costs in steps and joules, and what it saves in data

author.name: Matteo Fischetti

entry.summary: This pre-registered study revisits minibatch persistency, the practice of taking multiple optimizer steps on the same minibatch, by training a 49M-parameter Transformer on FineWeb-Edu across several batch sizes and seeds with carefully tuned per-arm learning rates and a reuse-free control. It quantifies the trade-offs along axes such as optimizer steps, fresh tokens consumed, energy, and data efficiency.

entry.title: Draining Fictitious Knots: Restoring Distance-Awareness Guarantees for High-Dimensional Spline Networks

author.name: Masoud Ataei, Mohammad Javad Khojasteh, Vikas Dhiman

entry.summary: Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks with spline activations offer interpretable function approximation, and DAREK adds distance-aware error bounds for uncertainty quantification, but in high dimensions the guarantees can weaken due to fictitious knots. These knots arise because DAREK's componentwise formulation treats each input dimension separately, so induced knot locations in the combined input space need not correspond to real training data. The paper diagnoses and repairs this problem to restore valid distance-aware guarantees.

entry.title: Where to Compute and How to Interact: Operator-Readable Adaptation with Gauge-Aware Transport

author.name: Zixuan Shen, Quanxu Wan, Bingchuan Wang, Zhi Wang, Biao Luo

entry.summary: Adaptive meshes let neural operators for PDEs place samples and computation where local physics demands it, but existing work focuses on where to compute while neglecting how information should interact after nodes are relocated. Because mesh adaptation changes sampling scales, neighborhoods and geometric context, representations formed at different nodes may not be directly comparable, and naive aggregation entangles physical variation with discretization-induced variation. The paper proposes gauge-aware transport together with operator-readable adaptation to separate these effects.

entry.title: Principal-timestep Restricted Init via Sparse Matrix-decomposition in Flow-matching

author.name: Jiayang Gu, Zheng Fang, Lichaun Xiang, Fanghui Liu, Xu Cai, Hongkai Wen

entry.summary: Flow-matching diffusion models generate high-fidelity images but are expensive to fine-tune, and the paper finds that LoRA combined with spectral initialization, which accelerates convergence in autoregressive language models, gives marginal or even negative gains in diffusion fine-tuning. The authors attribute this to a mismatch between LoRA's low-rank parameterization and the intrinsically high-rank gradients induced by the flow-matching objective. They propose a principal-timestep restricted initialization based on sparse matrix decomposition to align gradients better.

entry.title: Portable Semantics, Private Dialects: Reuse and Negative Transfer in Latent Communication Between Language-Model Cells

author.name: Narcis Marincat

entry.summary: This companion study asks whether independently trained language-model societies converge on a shared latent packet language, where zero-shot transfer fails, and whether inherited interface state helps or harms later learning. A leakage-controlled causal interoperability audit over all 30 ordered pairs of six independently trained restricted societies, using a preregistered alignment ladder, finds that semantically similar interfaces do not form one raw shared language.

entry.title: BOOST: Concurrent Access to Host Memory and HBM to Accelerate LLM Inference

author.name: Anish Saxena, Jae Hyung Ju, Hritvik Taneja, Po-An Tsai, Aamer Jaleel, Christos Kozyrakis, Moinuddin Qureshi

entry.summary: BOOST observes that current LLM serving systems treat HBM and host memory hierarchically, either serving entirely from HBM or prefetching into it, so host memory bandwidth is never well utilized and prefetch writes consume HBM bandwidth. The proposed design has each wave of GPU threadblocks access both tiers concurrently, fully utilizing both host and HBM bandwidth rather than only the fast tier. The authors argue this addresses the capacity and bandwidth limits on LLM inference throughput.

entry.title: Conditional Quantum Flow Matching for Data-Scarce Physiological Signal Augmentation

author.name: Chi-Sheng Chen, Samuel Yen-Chi Chen

entry.summary: This work introduces Conditional Quantum Flow Matching, which conditions a small 306-parameter quantum circuit on both flow time and class label to transport a class-conditional prior toward the target distribution, claiming the first conditional version of quantum flow matching and the first EEG augmentation on a parameterized quantum circuit. A nonnegative spectral embedding removes the need for readout tomography. On BCI Competition IV-2a, starting from a class-conditioned prior improves over unconditional quantum generative baselines.

entry.title: One Size Does Not Fit All: Setting Inference Depth from the Questions a Deployment Actually Asks

author.name: Jerry Kaplan

entry.summary: This paper measures how much per-token computation can be avoided when a deployment's prompt distribution is known in advance. It studies early exit by attaching a small trained readout to an intermediate layer that proposes a token, with a confidence test deciding whether to emit it or run the remaining layers, keeping the base model frozen and supervising only from its own outputs on ordinary traffic. Three findings on achievable savings and behavior are reported.

entry.title: An explicit solution of the five-expert prediction PDE and the exact optimality set of COMB

author.name: Jeff Calder, Nadejda Drenska

entry.summary: The authors derive an explicit solution to the stationary prediction with expert advice partial differential equation for five experts, expressing it in three regions with elementary integrals and hyperbolic products. The formula shows that a particular direction is optimal throughout the ordered sector and that the COMB strategy is optimal only on a lower-dimensional subset, disproving a 2016 conjecture by Gravin, Peres, and Sivan.

entry.title: Geometric Signatures of Conceptual Reorganization: A Counterfactual Embedding Framework for Detecting Scientific Revolutions

author.name: Dimitris Ntounis, Ariel Schwartzman, Chris Chafe, Thomas A. Ryckman

entry.summary: The paper treats the geometry of document embeddings as a measurable signal of conceptual reorganization, using ablation of documents tied to a concept before and after its historical emergence. It validates the approach on five case studies, including special relativity, Godel's incompleteness theorems, the Higgs mechanism, deep learning, and attention. It matters as an attempt to quantify paradigm shifts in science with embedding-based observables rather than qualitative historiography.

entry.title: Inside VLM Chart Reading: Tracing Value Reading from Vertical Bar Charts Across Space and Depth

author.name: Tianhao Niu, Qingfu Zhu, Wanxiang Che

entry.summary: Using counterfactual activation patching on Qwen2.5VL-7B-Instruct and InternVL3.5-8B, the authors trace how vision-language models recover exact values from vertical bar charts. They find that the changed bar-top region drives answer preference far more than the visually larger bar body, and that information hands off from visual legend regions in early layers to prompt-series positions in middle layers.

entry.title: Pull: Lazy Materialization of Working Memory for Stateful LLM Conversations

author.name: Jiangang Chen

entry.summary: Pull is a session router that keeps an addressable metadata directory built by a deterministic local purifier requiring no LLM calls, letting the model lazily materialize only the conversation turns it needs. On the LoCoEval benchmark it cuts per-query context tokens by roughly 75 percent on single-hop tasks while keeping quality and remaining reversible, unlike lossy summarization.

entry.title: DA-DLM: Explicitly Modeling Token Dependencies in Diffusion Language Models

author.name: Pengyu Ji, Zichen Zhang, Xiang Hu, Kewei Tu

entry.summary: Diffusion language models denoise masked sequences with conditional independence across simultaneously predicted tokens, harming coherence in a way analogous to the multi-modality problem in non-autoregressive translation. DA-DLM adapts directed-acyclic-graph dependency modeling from translation to the iterative diffusion setting via a position-oriented DAG that binds node groups to fixed output positions so earlier fixed tokens anchor neighboring predictions.

entry.title: Discovery Foundation Models: Toward Open-Ended Discovery Intelligence

author.name: Ling Yang, Zhenfei Yin, Yingcheng Wu

entry.summary: This position paper argues that foundation models are moving from learning and reasoning over existing knowledge toward learning through action, tool use, and outcome feedback, and that the next frontier is participating in the creation of new problems, representations, explanations, and knowledge. It formulates Discovery Foundation Models as general-purpose systems operating over a revisable research state and supporting seven coupled capabilities spanning problem discovery, formulation, representation construction, hypothesis formation, intervention, and evidence.

entry.title: URCHIN: A Horizontal Spiking Language Model for Data-Constrained Pretraining

author.name: Po-Han Chiang

entry.summary: URCHIN is a spiking language model aimed at the BabyLM setting of child-scale, developmentally plausible data. It applies a parallelized hierarchical connectome spiking state-space model, using leaky integrate-and-fire neurons split into excitatory and inhibitory populations wired by a Dale's-law lateral connectome, and resolves tokens through a multi-transmission recirculation loop. The work explores biologically constrained architectures as an alternative to internet-scale pretraining.

entry.title: From Advertised Improvements to Measured Capabilities: Evaluating ChatGPT Images 2.5 on Forgery Tasks

author.name: Ankit Raj, Yuxin Zhang, Kidus Zewde, Tommy Duong, Jiaqi Gan, Xingyu Shen, Yuchen Zhou, Huaiyu Guo, Siyu Zhang, Simiao Ren

entry.summary: This paper empirically tests whether the advertised improvements for ChatGPT Images 2.5 translate into better performance on forgery tasks with predetermined answers, comparing its Flare and Sunburst API models against GPT-Image-2 rerun in the same week. Using receipt-field edits, repeated editing, product placement, and fine-print rendering, it finds fewer OCR-detected changes to surrounding receipt text for Flare and Sunburst (31.7% and 31.2% versus 44.2%) without a detectable improvement in target-field correctness, and Flare retains fewer earlier edits on CORD receipts. The takeaway is that reduced collateral damage to text differs from improved edit fidelity.

entry.title: StepPrune: Adaptive Sequential Visual Token Selection across Multimodal Large Language Models

author.name: Hansen Zhang, Landi He, Mingde Yao, Lijian Xu

entry.summary: StepPrune formulates visual-token pruning in multimodal LLMs as an adaptive sequential decision process rather than independent top-K selection with a uniform budget. Conditioned on already-selected tokens and textual context, it progressively builds the retained subset and determines its size via a learned STOP action, and during training uses a variance-preserving noise gate. This targets the fact that visual prefixes dominate per-layer computation and that different inputs have very different visual complexity.

entry.title: PuzzleMate: Benchmarking MLLMs for Egocentric Puzzle Assistance

author.name: Avijit Dasgupta, Shayon Dasgupta, Zakaria Laskar, C. V. Jawahar, Karteek Alahari

entry.summary: PuzzleMate uses jigsaw puzzles as a controlled testbed for evaluating whether multimodal LLMs can give grounded, step-by-step embodied guidance aligned with a user's real-time progress. The authors argue that general visual understanding does not imply the fine-grained spatial reasoning and sequential instruction ability needed for physical assistance. The benchmark is aimed at measuring a capability gap that current MLLM evaluations largely miss.

entry.title: Tele360: Real-Time Feed-Forward Human Reconstruction from Sparse Unposed Cameras

author.name: Hanzhang Tu, Zhanfeng Liao, Wei Min, Jiajun Zhang, Yebin Liu

entry.summary: Tele360 is a real-time feed-forward system for dynamic human reconstruction and live free-viewpoint visualization from sparse, unposed RGB streams. It jointly estimates camera poses and reconstructs a dynamic 3D Gaussian representation per time step in a single forward pass, using a lightweight sparsity-aware multi-view transformer that tokenizes features. The claimed contribution is removing reliance on expensive per-scene optimization and calibrated, high-resolution camera rigs, which matters for immersive telepresence and interactive digital humans.

entry.title: Robust Multi-Model Fitting through Learning Neighbor Regions

author.name: Chang Nie, Guangming Wang, Zhe Liu, Hesheng Wang

entry.summary: This paper proposes Learning Neighbor Regions (LNR), a coarse-to-fine framework for multi-model fitting that uses a neural network to score minimum sets by combining local point-wise geometry with global context, pruning obviously bad hypotheses before expensive optimization. It targets computer vision problems such as scene reconstruction and mixed reality, where overlapping models, noise, and non-differentiable pipelines have historically limited accuracy and speed. The contribution is mainly a more efficient and robust hypothesis-generation stage rather than a new end-to-end paradigm.

entry.title: SAM3D-Part: Interactive Part Selection and Generation from 3D Objects

author.name: Jiahao Chang, Dong Du, Wanhu Sun, Yujian Zheng, Chuanyu Pan, Bowen Zhao, Chongjie Ye, Yuanming Hu, Xiaoguang Han

entry.summary: SAM3D-Part is a prompt-driven framework that generates only the specific object parts a user selects instead of decomposing an entire object, and returns reusable complete meshes rather than partial surfaces. It conditions on the source mesh directly so that hidden geometry and correct placement are preserved in image-conditioned part generation. This targets practical 3D asset workflows where components are edited, animated, or fabricated individually.

entry.title: Can a Neural Encoding Model Replicate an fMRI Visualization Study?

author.name: Erfan Nasirzadeh Orang, Zack While

entry.summary: This paper tests whether Meta's Tribe V2 neural encoding model can recover neural contrasts from a prior fMRI visualization study, conceptually replicating a comparison of bubble charts and 3D surface charts in color and grayscale. The model reproduced the direction of 11 of 14 reported contrasts, based on predicted cortical responses to the original stimuli. The work probes whether neural encoding models can substitute for expensive neuroimaging in graphical perception research.

entry.title: When is global evolutionary search useful for variational quantum algorithms? A landscape-first study

author.name: Vojt\v{e}ch Nov\'ak, Ivan Zelinka

entry.summary: Using a landscape-first experimental design with QAOA, this study identifies two mechanisms that make local search unreliable: parameter reuse across circuit layers and competition between 2-local and 3-local cost terms. The authors test these mechanisms across eight unseen spin glasses, fresh N=10 and N=12 instances, and standard MaxCut, transverse-field Ising, and Heisenberg models, finding adaptive differential evolution achieves better median performance on the unseen instances. The work clarifies when population-based global search justifies its evaluation cost over multistart local search.

entry.title: Harnessing human expertise for high-precision robotic assembly in industrialized construction: A sample-efficient installer-in-the-loop interactive reinforcement learning framework

author.name: Zekai Jin, Huiguang Wang, Xiaoning Sun, Yi Shao

entry.summary: This paper presents an installer-in-the-loop interactive reinforcement learning framework that acquires assembly expertise from offline teleoperated demonstrations, sparse event-driven binary takeovers at contact-failure boundaries, and acceptance-aligned terminal rewards, logged under a unified traceable schema. It targets precision assembly of modular construction components such as prefabricated window units, where the bottleneck is converting tacit installer knowledge into data-efficient autonomy under millimeter-scale tolerances. A temporally abstracted formulation supports offline-to-online adaptation.

entry.title: Vision-Force Admittance Learning for Peg Insertion into a Movable Hole

author.name: Yuzhong Chen, Yongqing Liang, Yunzhi Xu, Irving Fang, Chase Kidder, Hui-ping Wang, Raihan Haque, Yubiao Zhang, Chen Feng

entry.summary: VFAL is a framework that fuses asynchronous low-frequency visual pose estimates with a high-frequency force-based admittance model for peg insertion into a moving or movable hole, using vision as a regularization term. It adapts insertion strategies online to dynamic motion while maintaining millimeter-level precision, relying on vision foundation models for robust pose information.

entry.title: BIG-CBF: Behavior-Imagination-Guided Control Barrier Function with Shared Uncertainty for Mobile Robot Navigation

author.name: Shibo Li, Zhongcheng Wang, Jiahe Cao, Jianhua Yang, Ke Wu

entry.summary: BIG-CBF is a two-rate navigation architecture that separates low-rate maneuver selection from high-rate safety filtering, addressing the tendency of minimum-intervention control barrier function filters to produce safe but stalled behavior in geometrically ambiguous environments. Over a short horizon, six closed-loop feedback behaviors, imagined with shared uncertainty, guide maneuver choice before the CBF filter enforces local collision-avoidance constraints.

entry.title: Atomic Motion Coordinate for Language-Steerable and Force-Responsive Manipulation

author.name: Jiaqi Zhai, Jingkai Zhao, Chen Yang, Siyuan Ma, Yutian Zhang, Liwen Yang, Qinglian Wu, Weiqi Fan, Yifei Wang, Yi Zheng, Chenxi Gu, Dong Wei, Wei Zhang

entry.summary: This work introduces Atomic Motion Coordinate, a geometry-grounded coordinate in which each arm owns thirteen signed translation, rotation, and hold atoms grounded from text and forward kinematics with vision withheld, injected into every action-expert block via weighted codebook alignment. Contact history modulates the same coordinate through a bounded spherical residual recomputed from a fixed nominal latent so that only the unexecuted horizon suffix is regenerated. The study probes whether language can override a visually dominated motion prior in VLA policies, reporting opposite-atom separation figures across thousands of offline horizon interventions.

entry.title: From Prediction to Decision: World-Model-Guided Action Selection for Continuous Pile Excavation

author.name: Ailing Zhang, Fan Gao, Song Zhang, Kawa Leong, Ziyu Wu, Yafei Wang

entry.summary: The paper introduces the World-Action Model (WAM) for wheel-loader pile excavation, which proposes multiple scoop candidates, filters geometrically inadmissible ones, jointly predicts signed terrain change and loaded volume, executes the scoop with the largest predicted load, and replans from newly observed terrain. On 32 geometry-disjoint test episodes, world-model ranking over matched diffusion proposals cut mean scoops from 651.8 to 540.6 (17.1 percent) while completing all episodes.

entry.title: Assumption-Lean Inference for Spectral Differential Network Analysis of High-Dimensional Time Series

author.name: Michael Hellstern, Byol Kim, Ali Shojaie

entry.summary: This work builds an inference framework based on directly estimating the difference between two high-dimensional inverse spectral densities, allowing researchers to test how frequency-domain dependency networks change across conditions. It uses a new Gaussian approximation to avoid strong modeling assumptions typical of time-series network analysis. Applications are envisioned in neuroscience and similar fields where connectivity networks shift between experimental conditions.

entry.title: Question's Gambit: The First Move Matters in Agentic Deep Search

author.name: Radin Hamidi Rad, Amin Bigdeli, Negar Arabzadeh, Sajad Ebrahimi, Charles L. A. Clarke, Benjamin C. M. Fung, Ebrahim Bagheri

entry.summary: The paper argues that the first retrieval move of a deep research agent is an underappreciated design decision, since agents can surface evidence yet fail to connect it to gold documents. Question's Gambit decomposes the question into clues, reformulates them into complementary searches, consolidates results, and reranks the candidate pool before the agent begins its iterative search-and-reason loop.

entry.title: AppliedScientist: Automated Scientific Revision Through Iterative AI Reviewing

author.name: Vidushee Vats, Karun Sharma, Shengzhi Li, Shichao Pei

entry.summary: AppliedScientist closes the loop between an autonomous AI scientist and an AI reviewer in order to measure whether acting on reviews actually improves papers, rather than judging review text quality alone. Revisions are applied to rejected papers across subfields, the writer can access its own earlier drafts, and reviews are generated independently with no memory of prior scores to limit bias, across three revision settings.

entry.title: CWM: Controllable White-Box Meta-Prompting for Adaptive Retrieval-Augmented Generation and Reasoning Ability

author.name: Keuntae Kim, Eunhye Jeong, Yong Suk Choi

entry.summary: CWM presents a unified, low-cost white-box meta-prompting framework that adaptively routes between reasoning and retrieval-augmented generation tasks, avoiding reliance on external black-box controllers. The goal is a general-purpose, task-agnostic method rather than a task-specific specialization.

entry.title: SkillLift: Learning Dense Rubrics from Sparse Oracles for Efficient Skill Evolution

author.name: Haoxiang Kang, Ming Wen

entry.summary: SkillLift attacks the supervision bottleneck in agent skill self-evolution, where each oracle evaluation requires a full rollout, by learning an oracle-aligned rubric that turns ranking comparisons into a structured evaluation space. The core insight is that ranking which skill is better is a smoother target than regressing exact scores.

entry.title: (How) Do MLLMs Report Bistable Images Like Humans?

author.name: Ryota Takatsuki, Tomoki Doi, Amane Watahiki, Anil K. Seth, Hitomi Yanaka

entry.summary: Using the LLaVA family and synthetic Visual Anagrams to control for memorization, the authors test whether multimodal LLMs exhibit human-like modulability and exclusivity when reporting bistable images such as the duck-rabbit. Both visual and linguistic manipulations systematically shift model reports in human-consistent directions. The study probes internal computations underlying perceptual interpretation in MLLMs.

entry.title: Hindsight Bias in Clinical Temporal Reasoning: How Future Data Exposure Affects Large Language Model Judgment

author.name: Misaki Matsuura, Sayantan Kumar, Ojas Kadam, Jeremy C. Weiss

entry.summary: The paper introduces a paired benchmark for measuring outcome-conditioned shifts that resemble hindsight bias in clinical temporal reasoning, using 171 PubMed Central case reports from sepsis and GLP-1/diabetes cases. Each case is rendered both as narrative text and as human-annotated and LLM-generated textual time series, with questions tied to a meaningful clinical cutoff and paired against the full-information version. It matters because retrospective evaluation can reward models for using future information instead of reasoning under real decision-time uncertainty.

entry.title: Attention Is All You Need (to Avoid Spurious Oscillations)

author.name: Jinyoung Jeong, Joseph B. Choi, Xinlun Cheng, H. S. Udaykumar, Sanghun Choi, Stephen S. Baek

entry.summary: The authors develop a conservative fixed-grid finite-volume scheme in which a CFL-conditioned attention flux selects upstream information according to the transport required by the current timestep. Using one-dimensional inviscid Burgers transport as the test mechanism, the learned flux remains reliable in the conventional small-step regime and, with a timestep four times larger, preserves sharp shocks in a single stage per update, with WENO-5 plus SSP-RK3 and Forward Euler comparisons separating flux selection from time integration effects. It matters as a learned-solver contribution toward stable large-timestep simulation of hyperbolic conservation laws.

entry.title: HarnessBandit: Joint Learnability-Transferability Scheduling for Multi-Harness Agentic Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Hongliang Wei (Harbin Institute of Technology, Alibaba Cloud), Xiaobing Tu (Alibaba Cloud), Yinggui Wang (Alibaba Cloud), Zhengxi Liu (Alibaba Cloud), Rongkun Xue (Alibaba Cloud), Jinkui Ren (Alibaba Cloud), Xiantao Zhang (Alibaba Cloud), Debin Zhao (Harbin Institute of Technology), Xiaopeng Fan (Harbin Institute of Technology)

entry.summary: HarnessBandit is an online scheduler that selects one agent interface per optimizer step when training a shared policy across harnesses that differ in prompts, tool schemas, control loops, and trajectory formats. After each group-relative policy optimization update it observes learnability and transferability signals and favors the harness currently offering the best joint learning benefit.

entry.title: Building Legal Reward Models for Grounding and Abstention

author.name: Rilton Franzone, Valentin No\"el, Puyu Wang, Philip Torr, Fabio J. Fehr

entry.summary: This paper builds reward models specialized for legal retrieval-augmented generation, where systems must ground reasoning in evidence and abstain when evidence is insufficient. The authors convert existing legal QA datasets into contextual preference data and construct LegalRewardBench, a benchmark for grounded legal generation under noisy or inadequate retrieval. They find that contextual DPO improves grounding behavior relative to general-purpose reward models.

entry.title: Efficiency Hallucination: Formalizing and Measuring Behavioral Calibration in LLM-Based Code Optimization

author.name: Sarah Wilson, Gail Kaiser, Patrick Musau

entry.summary: The authors define the Efficiency Hallucination: LLMs claiming performance improvements from non-functional edits to already-optimized code, driven by an Evaluation Trap in which binary benchmarks reward unnecessary changes over abstention. Across 180 runs with nine models on EffiBench they report a 100% over-edit rate on optimal code, and a guardrail that raises correct abstention from 0% to 44.4% while preserving edit rates on sub-optimal inputs.

entry.title: PIDS-Bench: Evaluating Prompt-Injection Detectors Under Over-Defense, Obfuscation, and Distribution Shift

author.name: Yusuf Khalid Shire, Sang-Chul Kim

entry.summary: PIDS-Bench is a frozen multi-axis benchmark that evaluates prompt-injection detectors on both attack detection and benign false-positive behavior at fixed thresholds, spanning in-distribution inputs, hard-benign prompts that mimic injection structure, obfuscated attacks, and domain and structural distribution shifts. Seven detectors, including learned baselines, external classifiers and broad-safety comparators, are evaluated across these axes.

entry.title: Branched Optimal Transport Amortization

author.name: Semyon Semenov, Viktor Kovalchuk, Meir Roketlishvili, Albert Baichorov, Fakhri Karray, Martin Takac, Arip Asadulaev

entry.summary: This paper brings Branched Optimal Transport, which models tree-like structures such as rivers and vasculature, into large-scale deep generative modeling. It notes that standard continuous-time flow matching cannot represent hierarchical branching flows that merge or share pathways to minimize transport cost, and proposes an amortized approach to learn such branched structures.

entry.title: Math for AI safety: an invitation for mathematicians

author.name: Lionel Levine

entry.summary: Lionel Levine argues that new mathematics is needed to build AI systems that remain legible, steerable and cooperative, and organizes the invitation by mathematical field so readers can go directly to their own. Sections cover logic and game theory for cooperation, probability for agency and world models, algebra and representation theory for learned features, and analysis and geometry for generalization and training dynamics, each ending with an accessible open problem.

entry.title: Planning in the Backbone: DiffAdapterVLA for Native Continuous Trajectory Generation with Driving VLMs

author.name: Changxin Lu, Xiaoliang Meng, Yu Wu, Rui Huang, Honglin Li, Tao Chen, Kaixuan Zhou, Yadong Shao

entry.summary: DiffAdapterVLA injects explicit trajectory tokens into late layers of a pretrained driving vision-language model so that trajectory state co-evolves with driving conditions during backbone forward computation. This contrasts with prior pipelines that generate trajectories only after the VLM forms a final condition, leaving condition computation outside trajectory formation. Lightweight layer-wise DiffAdapters organize the computation, enabling native continuous trajectory generation for autonomous driving.

entry.title: How Lossless Is Lossless Speculative Decoding? The Role of Numerical Precision in Orthrus

author.name: Ilya Koziev, Leonid Sinev, Ivan Oseledets

entry.summary: This paper independently reproduces Orthrus, a hybrid autoregressive-diffusion architecture that claims lossless speculative decoding via intra-model consensus, and tests that claim under different numerical precisions. Under BF16 inference, exact trajectory matching with the autoregressive model occurs in only about 45 percent of cases for the authors' checkpoint and 43 percent for an independently trained model across 1,190 prompts from 12 domains. The probability of exact matching is also strongly tied to response-conditional perplexity.

entry.title: Specifying Reward Functions for RL Without Environment Sampling

author.name: Stephane Hatgis-Kessell, W. Bradley Knox, Emma Brunskill

entry.summary: The paper introduces Experience-Free Autonomous Reward Specification (EARS), a method for learning reward functions from human preferences without any environment interaction. It uses a structured LLM-mediated process to construct a small set of expressive reward features from a task description, avoiding the repeated policy training, trajectory sampling, and feedback elicitation required by online RLHF. The motivation is settings where environment interaction is computationally expensive or unsafe.

entry.title: Bench2Dex: Benchmarking Visuo-Tactile Bimanual Dexterous Manipulation Across Dexterous Hands

author.name: Zhenjie Yang, Yideng Zhang, Dongjie Zhang, Chenyu Jiang, Xianshuai Liu, Yufeng Li, Zuhao Ge, Xingyu Jiao, Zheng Zhang, Kaiyu He, He Wang, Yuwen Zhong, Yi Deng, Muyun Jiang, Xianliang Huang, Haisheng Su, Donghang Zhang, Jian Zhang, Xue Yang, Hongyang Li, Zuxuan Wu, Yu-Gang Jiang, Xiaosong Jia, Junchi Yan

entry.summary: Bench2Dex is a simulation benchmark for visuo-tactile bimanual manipulation spanning 12 dexterous hands, adapting robot models with a shared simulated tactile interface that converts local contact geometry into image-like tactile observations. It addresses the lack of a common experimental setting caused by divergent hand morphologies and sensor layouts.

entry.title: GradRepair-ODE: Certified Gradient Repair for Neural ODE Training

author.name: Ziqian Bi, Xin Liang Chia

entry.summary: GradRepair-ODE is a reliability framework that checks, repairs, or rejects gradients produced by differentiable ODE solvers at the optimizer step. The authors argue that loose step sizes, stiff dynamics, chaotic sensitivity, and event discontinuities can yield finite but numerically suspect gradient directions, which threatens scientific machine learning and continuous-time generative models such as diffusion probability-flow ODEs and flow matching. It matters because gradient quality, not just forward accuracy, determines whether these models train reliably.

entry.title: When Greedy Sampling Explores: KL-Regularized Contextual Bandits without Eluder-Dimension Dependence

author.name: Zichen Wang, Haoyang Hong, Huazheng Wang

entry.summary: The authors show that simple greedy sampling from a Gibbs policy achieves logarithmic regret in KL-regularized contextual bandits without explicit dependence on the eluder dimension, covering reward feedback and both general and Bradley-Terry preference feedback. The analysis also exposes a trade-off between greedy sampling and upper-confidence-bound style exploration.

entry.title: Does Reasoning Improve Psychological Depth in Large Language Models? It Depends on Who's Judging

author.name: Ruichen Zheng, Yihe Wang, Fabrice Y Harel-Canada, Sara Khosravi, Zeynep Senahan Yildiz, Amit Sahai, Nanyun Peng

entry.summary: This study probes whether LLM-as-a-Judge scores remain valid when outputs are closely matched and human preferences are subjective, using psychological depth in short stories as a testbed. Seven human readers and an LLM-judge ensemble evaluated 60 blinded prompt-matched story pairs from GPT-5 versus GPT-4o and DeepSeek-R1 versus DeepSeek-V3, finding no universal reasoning advantage and low inter-reader agreement.

entry.title: MoARa: Module-Aware Rank Allocation and Structure-Preserving Decomposition for Low-Rank LLM Pre-training

author.name: Keunyoung Kim, Nojun Kwak

entry.summary: MoARa reduces the optimizer-state memory cost of LLM pretraining by improving low-rank gradient projection along two axes: allocating projection rank per Transformer module according to profiled sensitivity instead of uniformly, and decomposing gradients block-wise into magnitude and direction components around the attention head dimension. Across five Transformer architectures it reports better steps and wall-clock time to target quality. It matters for making memory-efficient pretraining more competitive rather than merely cheaper.

entry.title: Bandits with Probing: Optimal Regret and the Limits of Winner Feedback

author.name: Yongjie Guan

entry.summary: This paper formalizes a probing bandit setting where a learner selects at most k of n arms per round and observes only the maximum reward among them, competing against the best fixed arm. It derives two minimax laws, one under independent stochastic rewards with winner feedback and one under winner feedback with arbitrary i.i.d. joint rewards or fixed sequences, giving matching orders and anytime upper bounds. The results clarify exactly when the probing advantage in identifying a good arm actually pays for the information lost from partial feedback.

entry.title: Knowledge-Enriched Structured EHR Features for 30-Day Hospital Readmission Prediction on MIMIC-IV

author.name: Mohamad Najafi, Hongyun Fu, Mathias Brochhausen, Jian Wu, Yaohang Li

entry.summary: The paper introduces an interpretable feature representation for 30-day hospital readmission prediction that augments structured EHR data with four medical knowledge sources (disease ontologies, procedure classifications, drug ingredient vocabularies, and organ-system lab aggregation) while avoiding clinical notes entirely. Each feature dimension maps to a named clinical concept, yielding sparse and interpretable patient representations with lower computational cost than pretrained language model approaches.

entry.title: PRISM-UDE: Physics-Regularized Iterative Symbolic Modeling of 3nm FinFETs via Universal Differential Equation

author.name: Pranavanath Balamurali, Prathamesh Dinesh Joshi, Raj Abhijit Dandekar, Rajat Dandekar, Sreedath Panat

entry.summary: PRISM-UDE embeds a small neural network inside a physics-based transistor model, using the network only to learn transport behavior the analytical baseline misses rather than replacing the physics entirely, then extracts a symbolic correction. The goal is compact models for 3nm FinFETs that remain numerically stable inside circuit solvers while retaining physical insight, addressing the limits of hand-derived equations and purely data-driven surrogates.

entry.title: Grouped Value Attention: Efficient KV Caching via On-Demand Key Reconstruction

author.name: Vishesh Tripathi, Abhay Kumar, Ramsha Khan

entry.summary: Grouped Value Attention (GVA) stores grouped values and reconstructs content keys with a learned linear map, so inference can absorb that map into the query and avoid materializing content keys in the decode path. A small shared decoupled RoPE channel keeps positional information via a separately cached positional key. For the studied configurations this cuts persistent cache scalars by roughly 45 to 47 percent relative to grouped-query attention baselines.

entry.title: Generation of Custom Solvers in Rust for Convex Optimization

author.name: Hao Zhu, Joschka Boedecker

entry.summary: cvxgenrust is an open-source tool that canonicalizes parameterized convex problem families described in CVXPY and emits a specialized Rust crate that updates parameters and calls the Clarabel conic solver natively at runtime. Generated solvers can also be exposed back to Python as custom CVXPY solvers. Experiments cover problems up to semidefinite and exponential-cone programs, showing runtime reductions over direct CVXPY solves and parity with CVXPYgen on shared classes.

entry.title: Graph Matching Relaxations and Amortization for Supervised Graph Prediction

author.name: Federico M\'endez, Paul Krzakala, Gabriel Melo, Charlotte Laclau, R\'emi Flamary, Florence d'Alch\'e-Buc

entry.summary: This paper studies permutation-invariant losses for supervised graph prediction, where comparing predicted and target graphs with arbitrary node orderings requires solving a costly graph-matching problem. It theoretically and empirically compares three optimal transport relaxations and identifies Gromov-Wasserstein as best suited to the task, then amortizes the matching by training a parametric matcher based on differentiable Sinkhorn applied to empirical node distributions. It matters because it removes the inner matching optimization from every training step for graph-output models such as molecule design.

entry.title: Learning to Refer from Estimated Listener Gaze

author.name: T\'ea Wright, Alane Suhr

entry.summary: The authors fine-tune vision-language models to produce more pragmatically optimal referring expressions by converting observations of incremental listener comprehension, recorded as gaze scanpaths, into reinforcement learning signals. A neural listener estimates human gaze fixations from images and sampled referring expressions, and several schemes convert fixation sequences and targets into token- and sequence-level rewards.

entry.title: Func-R1: Incentivizing Mathematical Function Reasoning in Multimodal Large Language Models

author.name: Mingze Yin, Xiaohan Wang, Dian Li, Haichao Yao, Yilin Zhao, Youjun Chen, Gang Liu, Jintai Chen, Yiheng Zhu, Chang-Yu Hsieh, Aimin Pan

entry.summary: The authors identify a modality interference phenomenon where multimodal models ignore visual cues while doing textual mathematical reasoning about functions. Func-R1 addresses this with an explicitly decoupled architecture and a hierarchical post-training pipeline that harmonizes visual perception with symbolic logic.

entry.title: When the Wrong Key Wins: Understanding and Detecting Hallucinations in LLMs

author.name: Xuhan Tong, Jiawei Zhang

entry.summary: The paper studies hallucination through a latent-key view in which answer selection results from competition among pretraining associations, showing predictions are sensitive to individual query keywords with entity-specific binding shaped by pretraining frequency. It then introduces a two-stage keyword-perturbation method that removes influential keywords and measures resulting changes to detect hallucinations.

entry.title: A Cross Community Agenda for Speech AI

author.name: Maria Teleki, Kimi Wenzel, Anna Seo Gyeong Choi, Tobias Weinberg, Shree Harsha Bokkahalli Satish, Stephanny Sanchez, Belu Ticona, Ariadna Sanchez, Yash Sonkar, Aarti Mathur, Christoph Minixhofer, Abraham Glasser, Raja Kushalnagar, James Caverlee, Minha Lee, Shaomei Wu, Alyssa Hillary Zisk, \'Eva Sz\'ekely, Dylan Gaines, Angelika Seeschaaf Veres, Seray Ibrahim, Nicholas Cummins, Allison Koenecke

entry.summary: This position paper synthesizes critiques from technical NLP venues and sociotechnical HCI venues, which rarely overlap, around three problems: speech AI operates with an incomplete model of communication, an incomplete model of identity, and metrics that measure the wrong constructs. It draws on AAC as a setting where these failures are most visible and highest stakes, alongside other underserved speakers such as people who stutter, multilingual speakers, and non-binary speakers. The goal is a cross-community research agenda.

entry.title: RIGOR: Rig-Informed Geometry for Omnidirectional Reconstruction

author.name: Tingjun Huang, Dmitry Rudshin, Mathieu Meyer, Pietro Bonazzi, Marc Pollefeys, Emilia Szyma\'nska

entry.summary: RIGOR is a large-scale reconstruction pipeline for gravity-aligned omnidirectional video that targets long-trajectory drift in feed-forward 3D reconstruction, especially in environments with repetitive structure, weak texture, and dynamic objects. It leverages 360-degree imagery for wider spatial coverage and richer visual information instead of requiring per-model fine-tuning for omnidirectional inputs. The work aims to bridge the gap between feed-forward reconstruction models and practical 360-degree capture rigs.

entry.title: Semantic Privacy Protection with Utility Preservation for 3D Point Clouds

author.name: Jinchang zhang, Jiakai Lin, David Crandall, Guoyu Lu

entry.summary: This paper proposes a class-transfer-based semantic encryption framework for 3D point clouds that hides the original object class while keeping the data usable for downstream tasks and allowing authorized recovery. It builds a shared-backbone Normalizing Flow latent space and uses LoRA plus FiLM for parameter-efficient class-conditional adaptation, with diffusion-guided flow alignment as regularization. It matters because point cloud sharing creates real semantic privacy risks that geometric blurring or destructive encryption handle poorly.

entry.title: Mind2Cloud: EEG-to-Point Cloud Generation with Two-Granularity Diffusion Decoding

author.name: Yongyi Lu, Xiongfeng Huang, Zhijing Yang

entry.summary: Mind2Cloud reconstructs 3D point clouds from EEG brain signals using a two-granularity diffusion decoder that combines a global Transformer branch with a local Point-Voxel CNN branch fused across diffusion timesteps. It argues that EEG representations and the denoising trajectory evolve in semantic granularity, which uniform decoders ignore. It matters for brain-computer interfaces and understanding visual cognition.

entry.title: Newton Deep Unfolding for Compressed Sensing

author.name: Changhua He, Xianchao Xiu

entry.summary: NDU-Net is presented as the first deep unfolding framework for compressed sensing reconstruction that uses second-order Newton optimization rather than first-order updates. It introduces a Newton update module that produces optimization states characterizing the reconstruction process, plus a Newton-guided multi-scale prior module that injects those states into reconstruction. This is notable because it exploits second-order curvature information that prior unfolding networks largely ignored.

entry.title: CGGT: Curve-Grounded Geometry Transformer for 3D Parametric Curve Reconstruction

author.name: Zhirui Gao, Renjiao Yi, Yunfan Ye, Ruizhen Hu, Chenyang Zhu, Wei Chen, Kai Xu

entry.summary: CGGT reconstructs editable 3D parametric curves directly from sparse, unposed multi-view images, bridging pixel perception and vector CAD representations. It combines a geometry-aware transformer encoder with a curve-aware masked-attention decoder for cross-view instance association, predicting camera and curve parameters in a single forward pass. This avoids the dense calibrated views and costly per-scene optimization required by NeRF and 3DGS baselines, making it more applicable to casually captured inputs.

entry.title: Diffusion Trajectory Modeling for Semantic Correspondence

author.name: Yusung Choi

entry.summary: The paper observes that intermediate feature maps inside a diffusion model form meaningful trajectories over timesteps, with each spatial patch's representation evolving progressively rather than being captured by a single snapshot. It argues that modeling these trajectories gives richer semantic cues for correspondence tasks than either using one timestep's features or naively aggregating across timesteps. This is a conceptually interesting reframing of diffusion internals as a temporal signal.

entry.title: AnchorGUI: Asymmetric Memory for Dual-Scale Learning in GUI Navigation

author.name: Shengjie Jin, Zelong Sun, Hengbo Xu, Yanbiao Ma, Zhiwu Lu

entry.summary: AnchorGUI attacks the problem of dense visual history in GUI-navigating VLM agents by exploiting an observed asymmetry: expected transitions can be compressed to lightweight text, while unexpected outcomes need preserved screenshots as causal evidence. The Cognitive State Anchor acts as a per-step primitive that decides what to keep, supporting both within-episode error correction and cross-episode experience distillation. It is a memory-design contribution for agentic GUI use.

entry.title: V-ICAL Bench: Evaluating Video In-Context Learning for Multimodal Agents in Interactive Environments

author.name: Ziqian Fan, Shibo Xu, Junjie Li, Xiangyu Zhao, Shengyuan Ding, Yifan Yang, Zhenjie Yang, Haodong Duan, Yue Zhou, Zhihang Zhong, Xue Yang

entry.summary: V-ICAL is a benchmark of 342 interactive tasks across 37 environments that tests whether multimodal agents can learn policies from human-curated demonstration videos without parameter updates, then ground those policies in new visual states and refine them from feedback. It explicitly targets video-based in-context learning, an underexplored area relative to text and image ICL. The benchmark evaluates sustained execution rather than single-shot responses.

entry.title: UniqueShip: Mitigating Data Leakage in Acoustic Ship Classification Benchmark Datasets

author.name: Connor Hashemi, Trevor Stout, Anthony Hoogs, Jason Parham

entry.summary: UniqueShip is a machine-learning-ready benchmark dataset for underwater acoustic target recognition of ships, sourced from an open ocean-observatory repository, with explicit controls against leakage between training and evaluation splits. The authors show that naive random partitioning in two widely used UATR datasets inflates accuracy by 10 to 48 points by letting models memorize individual ships. The contribution matters as a methodological correction for a field already constrained by scarce, small labeled datasets.

entry.title: nBMS, a Neuromorphic Battery Management System with a Silicon-Validated Spiking State-of-Charge Core for eVTOL Aircraft

author.name: \.Ismail Can Dikmen

entry.summary: This study designs an event-driven spiking network as the state-of-charge estimation core of a neuromorphic battery management architecture for electric vertical take-off and landing aircraft, with zero dense multiply-accumulate operations and about 34,433 int16 parameters. Evaluated on a 22-cell public eVTOL dataset with an automotive cross-check, it reaches 2.45 percent RMSE versus 1.74 percent for a traditional baseline. The work matters because eVTOL SoC estimation must run under hard energy and certification constraints unlike automotive duty cycles.

entry.title: NavPatch: Evidence-Guided Object-Level Costmap Correction with Vision-Language Models

author.name: Shiji Sun, Xingyu Tao, Hao Wang, Ling Wang, Zhengyi Chen

entry.summary: NavPatch adds an object-level correction layer on top of geometric maps: a vision-language model periodically assigns ADD, REMOVE, or EXTEND to navigation-relevant object categories, correcting cases like missed cables, spurious curtain blockages, or cones needing larger exclusion zones. Open-vocabulary grounding localizes instances, LiDAR and RGB-D provide 3D support, and observation-quality filtering plus cross-frame maintenance decide when a correction is applied. It targets the persistent mismatch between geometric occupancy and how objects should actually affect navigation.

entry.title: LieSpline-DP: Lie-Group B-Spline Diffusion Policy for Smooth Robot Manipulation

author.name: Erxuan Xie, Bang Liu, Pingyun Nie, Xingkai Liu, Zhuang Fu, Bo Zhang

entry.summary: LieSpline-DP is a Lie-group B-spline diffusion policy that generates end-effector trajectories directly on SE(3) and couples consecutive action chunks by sharing boundary control poses, guaranteeing C2 continuity across the entire planned trajectory. This addresses the discontinuity and non-smoothness of standard diffusion policies, which existing spline-based variants only partially fix within individual chunks. Across three real-robot tasks it reports lower trajectory jerk.

entry.title: Uncertainty-Guided Sparse Refinement for Action Chunking Transformer Policies

author.name: Chenyang Wang, Yuntian Wang, Xiaoxiong Yang, Dingde Jiang, Siao Liu, Yang Liu

entry.summary: Uncertainty-Guided Refinement (UGR) is a sparse refinement framework for chunk-based visuomotor policies that exploits the observation that failures are dominated by prediction errors at a few critical timesteps rather than uniform error across an action chunk. It follows a coarse-to-refine design, predicting a full chunk, estimating per-step temporal uncertainty from coarse hidden states, and refining selectively rather than uniformly.

entry.title: We Must Pace The Frontier

author.name: Zvi
