entry.summary: Zvi's analysis of Dario Amodei's essay calling for pacing frontier AI development, covering three proposals (embedded evaluators, democratic coordination, global coordination) and industry reactions from OpenAI, Musk, Hassabis, and Nadella. It frames the moment as meaningful progress while cautioning that serious disagreements remain about implementation.

entry.title: Asclepius: An Adaptive Harness for Long-Horizon Clinical Agents

author.name: Grace Chang Yuan, Xiaoman Zhang, Sung Eun Kim, Luyang Luo, Pranav Rajpurkar

entry.summary: Asclepius targets long-horizon agent failure in clinical settings, where agents run for hours under time and resource contention rather than on short single-task trajectories. Using the Clinical Environment Simulator, where an agent manages an entire emergency-department shift with multi-dimensional grading, it identifies an 'execution gap': agents reach correct diagnoses but fail to deliver complete, timely critical actions.

entry.title: How User-AI Mistreatment Occurs and Matters in Conversational Systems?

author.name: Fanqi Zeng, Sadid A. Hasan, Chaocheng He

entry.summary: This paper audits 777K English LMSYS-Chat-1M conversations to study hostility, coercion, and adversarial pressure directed by users at models, an under-studied counterpart to model-generated harm. Two independent detectors — an eight-category lexicon for hostility toward the assistant and the dataset's moderation signal — capture different, weakly overlapping phenomena, with the lexicon surfacing insults, threats, and jailbreak coercion that moderation labels miss.

entry.title: GeoSkill:Experience-Driven Hierarchical Skill Learning with Collaborative Revision forGeospatialAgents

author.name: Han Luo, Xian Xu, Yinhe Liu, Yanfei Zhong

entry.summary: GeoSkill is an experience-driven hierarchical skill learning framework for geospatial agents that distills prior execution experience into reusable procedural knowledge for planning and tool use. It addresses the failure of existing memory-augmented paradigms to capture both long-horizon tool-chain orchestration and tool-level invocation constraints, and it replaces unreliable LLM self-reflection with collaborative revision. It matters for building agents that improve on recurring geospatial analytical tasks.

entry.title: Positioning manuscripts in the scientific landscape with agentic AI

author.name: Jiawen Chen, Zichen Zhang, Bingxuan Li, Quan Sun, Yiyan Zhang, Edric Tam, Jinjie Lin, Didong Li, Yun Li, Bingxin Zhao

entry.summary: The paper introduces PASS, a Publication-oriented Agentic Scientific System that infers a manuscript's likely publication venue by positioning it within its domain-specific literature context. It asks whether agentic AI can help researchers navigate the publication process itself, which is time-consuming and uncertain. It matters as a concrete test of LLM agents on a meta-scientific task with measurable outcomes.

entry.title: Diversified and Perceptible Counterfactual Examples Leveraging Expert Knowledge

author.name: Akram Bensalem (IMT Atlantique - INFO), Fahima Djelil (Lab-STICC\_MOTEL, IMT Atlantique - INFO), Marie-Jeanne Lesot (IMT Atlantique - INFO, Lab-STICC, Lab-STICC\_MOTEL), Gr{\'e}gory Smits (IMT Atlantique - INFO, Lab-STICC, Lab-STICC\_MOTEL)

entry.summary: The paper proposes generating counterfactual explanations that incorporate a fuzzy linguistic vocabulary so that the resulting feature changes are semantically meaningful to human explainees, not just minimal. Because fuzzy-domain constraints make features dependent, gradient-based generators like DiCE do not apply directly, so the authors introduce a continuous embedding of the data to generate diversified, perceptible counterfactuals.

entry.title: From Semantic to Token Communication: The Next Paradigm for Large-Model-Driven 6G Intelligent Connectivity

author.name: Yu Ma, Zhen Gao, Li Qiao, Xiaoyuan Zhang, Mahdi Boloursaz Mashhadi, Yin Xu, Wenjun Xu, Xiaodong Xu, Kaibin Huang, Jiangzhou Wang, Rahim Tafazolli, Sheng Chen, Tony Q. S. Quek, Ping Zhang

entry.summary: This position paper argues that tokens, rather than task- or modality-specific semantic representations, should serve as the universal unit for meaning-aware communication in 6G networks driven by large models. It surveys the fragmentation of current semantic communication approaches and proposes a unifying token-based framework for interoperability and scalable design. The work is conceptual and forward-looking rather than empirical.

entry.title: Certifiably Interpretable Training of ReLU-MLPs for Boolean Tasks with Guaranteed Truth-Table Generalization

author.name: Hrad Ghoukasian, Anastasis Kratsios

entry.summary: The authors introduce MACCHIATO, a training algorithm that jointly constructs a structured ReLU multi-layer perceptron from partial truth-table observations and an explicit Boolean circuit over signed literals using AND, OR, and XOR gates. That circuit certifies what the network subnetworks compute and how they compose, by iteratively projecting residuals onto low-dimensional circuit classes and exactly compiling them. It matters as a route to models whose behavior is provably explainable rather than explained after the fact by approximate probes.

entry.title: Symmetry- and Property-Aware Crystal Generation with Reinforcement Learning for Inverse Materials Design

author.name: Ting-Wei Hsu, Arun Bansil, Qimin Yan

entry.summary: SPARC is a reinforcement learning framework for inverse crystal design that optimizes physical objectives while preserving the crystallographic symmetry conditions required for a response to be well defined. It is demonstrated on two tasks, including strong uniaxial dielectric anisotropy, a tensorial property meaningful only under appropriate symmetry constraints. The work matters because generating structures with good numerical property values but wrong symmetry yields responses that are accidental or unprotected, a common pitfall in materials generation.

entry.title: Domain-Specific Jargon in Large Language Models: A Comparative Analysis between General-Purpose and Specialist Models

author.name: Darin Keng, Zhewei Sun

entry.summary: The authors build two new medical-jargon evaluation benchmarks and compare a general-purpose Llama-3.1 against a version fine-tuned on medical text. Counterintuitively, the general model wins on both tasks, and mechanistic interpretability reveals systematic miscalibration in the fine-tuned model, which appears to have shifted its decision surfaces around domain terms rather than genuinely reorganizing parametric knowledge.

entry.title: Understanding the Limits of Agentic ICD Coding

author.name: Chong Yock Eng, Yushi Cao, Yiming Chen, Kezhi Mao, Hongchao Jiang

entry.summary: The authors evaluate neural, workflow, and agentic ICD-10-CM coding systems on a rarity-stratified subset of MIMIC-IV discharge summaries, exposing two orthogonal failure modes. Neural classifiers show a 0.43 micro-F1 rare-versus-common code gap, workflow systems fail on injury and external-cause codes requiring multi-step guideline following, while a tool-augmented agent with structured access to official reference materials recovers up to 0.34 micro-F1.

entry.title: Loop-Back Authority in LLM Agent Teams: A Paired Experiment on Flat and Hierarchical Coordination

author.name: Burak Agachan, Max van Duijn, Amirhossein Zohrehvand

entry.summary: This paper isolates one variable in multi-agent LLM coordination: whether a Manager agent may reject worker output and require a revision. Holding agents, roles, prompts, tools, models and data fixed across 43 paired runs, it tests the classical organizational prediction that authority speeds convergence against work on sycophancy and Degeneration-of-Thought predicting authoritative critique harms quality. The design tests the authority link directly on open-ended work, which prior framework-level comparisons left untested.

entry.title: Per-Matrix Optimality Is Not Enough: Three-Level Optimization for Low-Rank LLM Compression

author.name: Huicheng Zhang, Xiyao Feng, Ze-Tong Li, Chengkai Zhu, Xiao Shi, Xiwei Pan, Jinguo Liu, Ge Bai, Xin Wang

entry.summary: This work argues that independently optimal per-matrix SVD truncation is insufficient because compression errors compound through a block's nonlinear forward pass. It introduces a three-level optimization chain, whitened SVD, block-level joint optimization, and end-to-end language-modeling loss refinement, requiring only 256 calibration sequences with no instruction or recovery data, and reports large WikiText-2 perplexity reductions on LLaMA-7B at 60 percent compression.

entry.title: Specification Oracles

author.name: Atticus Cull, Justin McCarthy

entry.summary: The paper asks whether a language model can act as a compact, living specification oracle that learns facts about a target system and answers questions about it, comparing two storage strategies: external text notes versus changes to model weights. Across four families of 596-fact worlds and two Qwen2.5 sizes, weight-only oracles benefited far more from structure, with the 7B model gaining roughly 18.5 percentage points on structured versus unstructured worlds versus about 1.1 points for notes. It bears on how knowledge should be represented when a model is expected to answer arbitrary specification questions.

entry.title: Certifying Model Upgrades with Slice-Wise Non-Regression and Incumbent Fallback

author.name: Shengwei Zhang, Tao Wu, Fei Qian

entry.summary: The paper studies checkpoint selection when an updated model improves an aggregate metric but may regress on slices important to specific users. It proposes a release procedure that separates candidate search from independent paired evaluation and falls back to the incumbent when certification fails, with finite-sample guarantees derived from intersection-union and Learn-then-Test principles.

entry.title: High-Probability Nash Regret for Decentralized Learning in Markov $\alpha$-Potential Games: Episodic and Fully Online Asynchronous Algorithms with Applications to Markov Congestion Games

author.name: S. Rasoul Etesami

entry.summary: The paper studies decentralized learning of Nash equilibria in infinite-horizon discounted Markov potential games under bandit feedback, proposing KL-projected natural policy gradient algorithms for an episodic setting and a fully online asynchronous setting. It establishes finite-time high-probability Nash regret bounds of roughly T to the minus one quarter and T to the minus two fifteenths, removing a distribution-mismatch coefficient present in prior work. It matters for the theoretical foundations of multi-agent learning in Markov congestion-type environments.

entry.title: Learning CNF Formulas from Uniform Random Solutions: Near-Tight Sample Complexity for Valiant's Algorithm

author.name: Weiming Feng, Yixiao Yu, Yiyao Zhang

entry.summary: The paper revisits Valiant's classic algorithm for learning k-clause, degree-d CNF formulas from i.i.d. uniform random satisfying assignments in the local lemma regime. It shows that for fixed t at least one, under a mild condition on k relative to log d, the algorithm achieves total variation error epsilon with roughly n-to-the-ceiling-t over epsilon samples, proves a matching lower bound for t greater than one, and shows optimality up to log factors at t equal to one. This sharpens a forty-year-old result at the intersection of learning theory and satisfiability.

entry.title: Beyond Noise: Understanding and Overcoming Temperature Effects in Analog DNN Inference

author.name: Niklas Summ, Xiao Wang, Hendrik Borras, Bernhard Klein, Holger Fr\"oning

entry.summary: Analog accelerators promise high energy efficiency for machine learning on constrained platforms, but they suffer from noise and physical non-idealities that shift with environmental conditions such as temperature. This experimental study characterizes both stochastic and systematic non-idealities across a range of operating temperatures on representative analog hardware, then develops countermeasures. It provides much-needed empirical grounding for making analog DNN inference reliable in the field.

entry.title: Calibrating subgrid parametrizations of single-column ocean models via simulation-based inference

author.name: Luben M. C. Cabezas, Sacha Wendling, Aur\`ele Gallard, Gabriel Mouttapa, Julien Le Sommer, Pedro L. C. Rodrigues

entry.summary: This paper applies simulation-based inference to calibrate free coefficients in subgrid vertical-mixing parametrizations of ocean models, which cannot be measured directly and must be tuned against large-eddy simulations. Unlike existing point-estimate approaches, SBI approximates the full posterior over parameters, quantifying uncertainty when the inverse problem is ill-posed or multiple configurations fit comparably well.

entry.title: Aries: A Proprietary Medium-Range Weather Prediction Model for the Energy Industry

author.name: Lukas Hedegaard Morsing, Arian Bakhtiarnia, Jonas Lynge Olesen, T\'omas Bragi Bj\"ornsson Leth, Christian G{\o}bel Bach

entry.summary: Aries is a Swin Transformer based machine-learned weather prediction model developed at a commodities trading firm, trained on ERA5 reanalysis at 0.25 degree resolution to predict 74 prognostic and 11 diagnostic atmospheric variables. It is evaluated on 2025 ECMWF Analysis initializations so all comparisons sit in a strictly out-of-sample period, and on 10-metre wind speed it beats both ECMWF HRES and AIFS in RMSE.

entry.title: Diffusion-Based Multiple-Shooting Indirect Optimal Control for Fuel-Optimal Spacecraft Trajectory Generation

author.name: Saeid Tafazzol, Ehsan Taheri, Ryne Beeson

entry.summary: The authors aim to combine the exploratory strength of diffusion generative models with the optimality guarantees of indirect optimal control for fuel-optimal spacecraft trajectories. Because indirect methods are highly sensitive to initial costate estimates for the resulting Hamiltonian boundary-value problems, the work uses diffusion-based multiple shooting to enlarge the convergence domain. This targets long-horizon bang-bang solutions where naive diffusion control methods previously had no optimality guarantees.

entry.title: When Faster VLA Deployment Changes Closed-Loop Behavior: Task Success-Latency Analysis of SmolVLA Across PyTorch and ONNX Variants

author.name: Rafiqul Islam

entry.summary: The study evaluates SmolVLA on LIBERO Spatial and Object tasks, comparing PyTorch with AMP against ONNX Runtime CUDA execution across 100 and 300 episodes per suite. Faster ONNX variants cut p99 latency roughly in half but Spatial success dropped from 70 to around 40 percent, while Object performance stayed near 89 percent. A graph audit revealed that the requested FP16 and INT8 artifacts were byte-identical FP32 graphs, meaning the reported precision label did not reflect the actual operators executed.

entry.title: Shared KV Caching for Replicated 27B Inference: Correctness Failures and Performance Boundaries

author.name: Frank Li

entry.summary: This empirical systems paper studies two single-GPU 27B vLLM replicas sharing a host-memory LMCache pool so that prefill work can be reused across replicas. It isolates a raw-pointer fallback that drops a dependency on the current CUDA stream, showing with controlled byte tests that the transfer fails under imposed delay and passes once the dependency is restored, and characterizes when shared caching still pays off given lost prefix locality. It matters as a documented correctness pitfall and performance boundary for real multi-replica serving stacks.

entry.title: Zero-SNR Analyticity of the Scalar MMSE Is Equivalent to Gaussianity

author.name: Yixing Zhang

entry.summary: The paper proves that, under a square-exponential moment condition, the scalar minimum mean-square error in a Gaussian channel is analytic at zero SNR if and only if the input random variable is Gaussian (with constants as degenerate Gaussian cases). The proof reframes estimation as a backward heat flow acting on the moment-generating function, and shows any non-Gaussian input forces a nonzero complex zero whose cluster produces a localized singularity. It matters as a clean characterization result at the intersection of information theory, estimation, and random matrix style analysis.

entry.title: ForeSight: Enhancing Risk Monitoring via Early Safety Signal Distillation

author.name: Hanling Wang, Chenlong Wei, Ling Xu, Hanyan Niu, Qi Cao, Shizhou Huang, Yang Yang, Xiaohui Zhu, Yao Zhu

entry.summary: ForeSight forecasts whether an LLM response will be harmful from the very first generated token, distilling weak and redundant early hidden-state signals into a compact, more reliable safety representation. The work targets a real gap: prior early-risk detectors rely on surface tokens or logits with weak initial signal, or on dense internal representations that carry entangled, safety-irrelevant information.

entry.title: SlopShape: Identifying AI-Generated Commercial Web Content

author.name: Jochen Madler (Sitefire)

entry.summary: The paper asks whether AI-generated text can be identified from structural signatures rather than word-level cues, examining how information is presented, ordered, evidenced, and voiced. It replicates StoryScope on commercial content, comparing 2,250 pre-ChatGPT human blog posts from 268 company domains against 11,250 AI mirrors from five frontier models. A 214-feature instrument applied by an LLM is validated against human gold annotation.

entry.title: Merging the Knowledge of LLMs for Automatic Speech Recognition

author.name: Hayato Futami, Tatsuya Kawahara

entry.summary: The paper proposes incorporating external language models into LLM-based ASR by model merging rather than decoding-time fusion, avoiding the extra inference cost of shallow fusion and density-ratio methods. Domain extension and transfer are formulated as arithmetic operations on LoRA parameters. Experiments evaluate the approach against established LM fusion baselines.

entry.title: Restore What Matters: Lessons from Joint Restoration and Recognition

author.name: Lanqing Guo, Xijun Wang, Minchul Kim, Yu Yuan, Wes Robbins, Xingguang Zhang, Nicholas Chimitt, Stanley H. Chan, Zhangyang Wang, Xiaoming Liu

entry.summary: This paper argues that the conventional restore-then-recognize pipeline is misguided because visually pleasing restoration rarely improves downstream recognition, and proposes a Joint Restoration-for-Recognition paradigm in which task signals dictate where, how much, and whether restoration is applied at all. The framework rests on three pillars: optics-accurate turbulence simulation grounded in real image formation, neuroscience-inspired selective attention and neuroplasticity to focus capacity on identity-critical regions, and vision-side task alignment. It draws broad lessons from a joint restoration and recognition study.

entry.title: Selective Tool Use for Agentic Change Visual Question Answering in Remote Sensing

author.name: Yakoub Bazi, Mohamad M. Al Rahhal, Mohamed A. Mekhtiche, Mansour Zuair

entry.summary: This paper addresses the unreliability of vision-language models on change VQA questions requiring exact transition statistics, area measurements, or spatial information in bi-temporal remote sensing imagery. It proposes a selective tool use framework where a single VLM either answers directly or invokes a deterministic change-analysis tool over semantic maps and then composes the structured observation into its final answer. The construction of a supporting dataset accompanies the framework, illustrating the agentic tool-routing pattern for geospatial analysis.

entry.title: Reverse Spatio-Temporal Disease Progression Modelling

author.name: Ulugbek Shernazarov, Moucheng Xu, Inomjon Ramatov

entry.summary: The paper proposes reverse disease progression prediction: given later diseased anatomy, reconstruct the unobserved healthier baseline, motivated by the fact that imaging in diseases such as Alzheimer's typically begins only after pathology is suspected. Existing deep longitudinal models run forward from a baseline and cannot exploit the incubation period for early intervention. This inversion reframes progression modeling around reconstructing pre-symptomatic states rather than forecasting decline.

entry.title: What Makes a 3D Scene Editable? A Factorized Benchmark of Fidelity, Locality, Consistency, and Preservation

author.name: Sariah Patro, Arjun Mehra, Nikhil Bhatia

entry.summary: The authors introduce EditBench3D, a representation-agnostic benchmark that evaluates neural 3D scene editing across four properties: instruction fidelity, spatial locality, cross-view consistency, and preservation of non-target content. The protocol combines visibility-aware 3D target supports, paired descriptions, held-out cameras and five edit families, and is applied to eight NeRF, 3D Gaussian Splatting, hybrid and proxy-based editors over 240 scene-edit pairs. It matters because it exposes weaknesses that semantic-alignment-only metrics hide and gives the field a more rigorous evaluation standard.

entry.title: SyntheticDoc: A Large Synthetic Dataset for Document Unwarping and Illumination Correction

author.name: Daniel Woortmann, Tanguy Magne, Olga Sorkine-Hornung

entry.summary: SyntheticDoc is a procedurally generated dataset of one million high-resolution document images with pixel-perfect annotations including UV maps, normals, albedo, and shading, intended to replace the decade-old Doc3D benchmark for document unwarping and illumination correction. The authors argue that progress in document rectification is bottlenecked by training data scale and quality. Dataset releases of this size can shift the subfield's baseline.

entry.title: Physical Kernel: Structured Visual Latents for Dark Manipulation

author.name: Jinting Hang, Hong Li, Zhenhui Cai, Zhihao Zhao, Jian He

entry.summary: This work studies dark manipulation: after a brief lit Write phase encodes an RGB frame into a latent, a policy and open-loop dynamics complete contact-rich manipulation skills with no further pixel input. On ManiSkill StackCube, dark_f reaches 68.1 percent stacked versus 35.6 percent for per-step re-encoding and 0 percent for frozen or black-frame encodings, and it remains robust (82.5 percent lift) under occlusion that collapses lit re-encoding to 0 percent. Action shuffling inflates dynamics MSE roughly 9.4x, supporting that the dynamics model is genuinely action-conditioned.

entry.title: TopoRig: Topology-Agnostic Facial Rigging via Multi-Source Supervision

author.name: Andrew Fleet, Soroush Mehraban, Vida Adeli, Cole Clifford, Babak Taati

entry.summary: TopoRig is a topology-agnostic facial rigging framework that predicts FACS-conditioned deformations directly on input mesh vertices while preserving the original topology. It combines complementary supervision from template-biased common-topology rigs, topology-diverse but noisier transferred rigs, and targeted image-based cues for controls that geometric transfer captures poorly. The approach targets artifact and correspondence errors that arise when deformation transfer is applied to arbitrary meshes.

entry.title: Mobile Multi-Robot Navigation under Runtime Uncertainty via Koopman Operator Learning and Nonlinear Model Predictive Control

author.name: Xiaobin Zhang, Konstantinos Karydis

entry.summary: This work develops a nonlinear model predictive control framework for mobile multi-robot navigation that uses Koopman operator theory to learn lifted bilinear dynamics. Evaluated on target-reaching and formation-control problems with obstacles and randomized wheel slipping, the learned model is embedded in NMPC to handle runtime uncertainties in closed loop.

entry.title: DreamSat-Bench: Development and Initial Testing of a Testbed for AI-Based Pose Estimation from 3D Reconstruction

author.name: Alex Posadas-Nava, August Berne, Giovanni Lavezzi, Kareena Shah, Alejandro Carrasco, Josiane Uwumukiza, Giacomo Battaglia, Paolo Panicucci, Minduli C. Wijayatunga, Victor Rodriguez-Fernandez, Richard Linares

entry.summary: DreamSat-Bench is a modular rendezvous and proximity operations testbed for benchmarking AI-based relative navigation, integrating software- and hardware-in-the-loop robotics with MuJoCo, Isaac Lab, and LeRobot in one platform. Robotic arms trace 3D trajectories while orbital environments and lighting are customized to probe the simulation-to-reality gap, demonstrated with an end-to-end vision-based navigation evaluation.

entry.title: Real-World Reinforcement Learning with MPC Scaffolding for Dexterous Manipulation

author.name: Emek Bar{\i}\c{s} K\"u\c{c}\"uktabak, Karankumar Patel, Zhaodong Yang, Jinda Cui, Kazuhiro Sasabuchi, Jun Takamatsu

entry.summary: This framework uses sampling-based model predictive control as scaffolding for real-world dexterous reinforcement learning, populating an offline replay buffer and pretraining actor and critic without human demonstrations or corrective actions. During online learning, MPC intermittently guides data collection while an off-policy Soft Actor-Critic learner trains on both prior MPC experience and new interaction. It addresses the inefficient early exploration and costly failures that block real-world RL for manipulation.

entry.title: HarnessVLN: Unifying Training-Free Embodied Navigation through an Agent Harness

author.name: Yang Chen, Lirong Che, Zhenyu Huang, Wenbo Fu, Chuang Wang, Xu Cao, Daqi Liu, Yuzhe Yang, Jian Su, Lan-Zhe Guo

entry.summary: HarnessVLN is a zero-shot, training-free framework whose Agent Harness coordinates perception, retrieval, grounding, navigation, recovery, and termination through a unified tool interface. The harness validates planner proposals against spatial evidence, geometric feasibility, and subgoal consistency, adding structured verification that training-free MLLM navigation pipelines usually lack. It targets the generalization problems of trained navigation policies and the reliability problems of purely prompted MLLM agents.

entry.title: P-POSEMEM: Projective Semantic Memory for Consistent Language Grounding under Pose-Graph Rewrites

author.name: Ha Sier, Ali Salmasi, Mengya Xu, Haizhou Zhang, Jie Lu, Zhuo Zou, Xianjia Yu, Tomi Westerlund

entry.summary: P-POSEMEM addresses the problem that semantic memory committing detections to world coordinates breaks when SLAM optimizes, loop-closes, or marginalizes the underlying pose graph, causing queries to select different objects. It stores each observation as an immutable event at its birth keyframe, retains Bayes-tree elimination conditionals for marginalized keyframes, and integrates semantic likelihoods over the joint posterior of poses, anchors, and identities, with a total-variation defect metric (Dproj) quantifying inconsistency.

entry.title: StereoPatch: Patch-Aligned RGB-Depth Fusion for Spatial Perception in Robot Manipulation

author.name: Yanan Zhou, Zhaoyan Qian, James Zhao, Weiming Zhi

entry.summary: StereoPatch introduces a patch-aligned RGB-depth representation that binds registered metric geometry directly to the RGB patches used for action prediction, so policies do not have to learn RGB-depth correspondence from limited demonstrations. Depth is injected into the visual tokens on a shared 2-D patch grid via asymmetric cross-attention, targeting cases where visually similar scenes demand geometrically different actions.

entry.title: On Large-Scale Multiple Testing Over Networks: A Non-Asymptotic Approach

author.name: Mehrdad Pournaderi

entry.summary: The article diagnoses a finite-sample failure of an earlier greedy interval-aggregation algorithm for distributed false discovery rate control, tracing it to a winner's-curse bias of order Theta(m^{-1/4} sqrt(log m)) in selected density statistics. It proposes Cross-Fit Greedy Aggregation, which selects the nested rejection family on one half of each node's data and scores it on the other, achieving finite-sample FDR control under a tight communication budget. This matters for distributed scientific and sensor-network analyses where global FDR guarantees are required.

entry.title: TimeThink: Eliciting Compositional Reasoning in Timeseries Large Language Models

author.name: Sudarshan Regmi, Arvind Pillai, Yu Yvonne Wu, Yuliang Chen, Bibek Panthi, Tess Z. Griffin, Michael V. Heinz, Lisa Marsch, Nicholas C. Jacobson, Andrew Campbell

entry.summary: TimeThink tackles the failure of timeseries multimodal LLMs to capture dynamic temporal patterns, producing only implicit reasoning unsuited to high-stakes domains such as healthcare. It offers a synthetic framework built on core timeseries primitives to elicit explicit compositional reasoning, targeting the out-of-distribution compositional questions where RL-trained timeseries models currently fall short.

entry.title: JaxAHT: A JAX-Based Library for Ad Hoc Teamwork

author.name: Caroline Wang, Rolando Fernandez, Zelal Su Mustafaoglu, Montek Kundan, Jiaxun Cui, Lingyun Xiao, Zhihan Wang, Di Yang Shi, Aditya Madhan, Johnny Liu, Arrasy Rahman, Peter Stone

entry.summary: JaxAHT is an open-source JAX library that standardizes and accelerates the Ad Hoc Teamwork research lifecycle, covering teammate generation, ego agent training, and evaluation against unseen teammates. It leverages JAX hardware acceleration and parallelization to achieve large wall-clock speedups and provides a validated teammate suite. It matters because computational cost and lack of standardized benchmarks have slowed progress in coordinating with novel partners.

entry.title: ClinAgent: A ReAct-Based Agent for Conversational Access to Clinical Trial Information

author.name: Antonino Vaccarella, Riccardo Cantini, Domenico Talia, Paolo Trunfio, Marianna Talia, Rosamaria Lappano, Marcello Maggiolini

entry.summary: ClinAgent is a conversational agentic retrieval-augmented generation system based on the ReAct paradigm that lets clinicians and researchers query clinical trial registries in plain language across multi-turn interactions. The LLM agent iteratively reasons over queries, selects among integrated tools, and refines actions from intermediate outputs to produce grounded, up-to-date answers. It matters because registry querying is currently manual, error-prone, and lacking cross-source synthesis.

entry.title: MOSCOPT: Mixture-of-Skills Collective Optimization for LLM Agents

author.name: Zhenyu Zhang1, Jiudong Yang

entry.summary: MOSCOPT proposes a text-native, parameter-free method that jointly optimizes a pool of N prompt-based skills plus a gating skill that dynamically selects K skills per step, rather than optimizing a single monolithic template. Optimization uses a custom EditAdam with dual internal states across three interleaved update phases, and the authors report broad gains with ablations across five benchmarks.

entry.title: DynSTEER: Dynamic Stage-wise Trajectory Evaluation and Execution-time Review for Agents

author.name: Zhichao Shi, Wenjie Zhang, Xuhui Jiang, Xiaojun Wu, Cehao Yang, Chengjin Xu, Jian Guo, Yuanzhuo Wang

entry.summary: DynSTEER targets three weaknesses in long-horizon agent evaluation: terminal-only scoring that cannot localize errors, single-reference matching that penalizes valid alternative paths, and costly post-hoc judging that cannot halt failing runs. It segments rollouts into stages anchored on key completed actions, evaluates milestone progress with adequate context, and supports execution-time review and strategy adjustment.

entry.title: STHMoE: Hypergraph-Enhanced Heterogeneous Dependency Coordination for LLM-Based Urban Traffic Data Forecasting

author.name: Jiawen Chen, Qi Shao, Yongjian Chang, Mingtong Zhou, Duxin Chen, Wenwu Yu

entry.summary: STHMoE proposes a spatio-temporal hypergraph-enhanced mixture-of-experts framework that decouples urban traffic dynamics into frequency-domain and structural components to coordinate temporal, spectral, pairwise, and higher-order dependencies. It targets non-stationary sensor streams where existing LLM-based forecasting methods miss higher-order structure.

entry.title: ProIQA: A Process-Based Framework for Fine-Grained Math Item Quality Assessment

author.name: Junkai Tong, Mingjia Li, Haoran Chen, Yaoyu Jiang, Hanjie Ge, Yixuan Wang, Hong Qian

entry.summary: ProIQA moves math item quality assessment from shallow stem-based metrics to a process-aware formulation covering knowledge concepts, difficulty, and disciplinary competencies. It targets the bottleneck of validating automatically generated educational items without unscalable manual review.

entry.title: Are LLMs Good Financial User Simulators? A Preliminary Study

author.name: Jiajie He, Jiangyuan Hong, Dongling Ni, Wenjin Liu, Xintong Chen

entry.summary: This preliminary study tests whether LLMs can simulate individual financial decisions in a controlled paper-trading environment with 120 volunteers using non-redeemable virtual funds under real-time market conditions. Simulators predict the participant's next-trading-day action, security, and quantity, and results show that point-in-time market context improves action prediction.

entry.title: Diagnosing Faults in Reinforcement Learning Simulators and World Models with Canonical Polynomial Invariants

author.name: Tesfay Zemuy Gebrekidan, Hadush Hailu Gebrerufael

entry.summary: Using exactly recovered polynomial invariants canonicalized as reduced Groebner bases, the authors test whether embedding physical structure improves learned dynamics models. On Acrobot they find exactness adds little to rollout prediction, but canonical invariants are valuable for diagnosing which physical constraint a simulator violates. The result questions a common premise in physics-informed world modeling while offering a concrete diagnostic tool.

entry.title: Task-Aware Federated Fine-Tuning for MoE-based Large Language Models

author.name: Tingqi Wang, Hongyu Ke, Haoxin Wang, Rafal Angryk, Zhipeng Cai

entry.summary: FedTAR is a task-aware federated fine-tuning method for mixture-of-experts LLMs that tackles heterogeneity when clients have different task preferences. Because naive aggregation of client updates can weaken expert specialization and create conflicting directions on shared experts, the method establishes task-aware assignment to preserve specialist behavior while still pooling shared capacity. It matters for deploying capable MoE models in privacy-sensitive, resource-constrained distributed settings.

entry.title: A Three-Axis Stress Test of LLM vs Classical ML for Network Intrusion Detection under Distribution Shift and Adversarial Evasion

author.name: Muhammad Ebad Atif, Muhammad Haider Ali

entry.summary: The authors evaluate XGBoost and a RoBERTa-LoRA model for network intrusion detection across three axes: same-dataset performance, cross-dataset transfer, and adversarial evasion, using two independently collected NetFlow v2 networks. The models are statistically tied in the same-dataset setting, but XGBoost wins decisively under distribution shift by about 15 F1 points and 25 balanced-accuracy points, while the transformer's false positive rate on the target network reaches 0.78. It matters as a caution against the common same-dataset benchmarking protocol when comparing LLMs to classical ML for security.

entry.title: ReWeight: Leveraging Human Data for VLA Post-Training via Demonstration Retrieval and Sample Weighting

author.name: Chenwei Wang, Dianye Huang, Match W. L. Ko, Chenjia Bai, Zhongliang Jiang

entry.summary: ReWeight incorporates egocentric human demonstrations into vision-language-action post-training through demonstration-level retrieval and sample-level weighting. It learns a cross-embodiment visuomotor representation from visual observations and future actions to measure behavioral similarity between human and robot data, then uses optimal transport to retrieve and reweight useful human demonstrations while suppressing embodiment mismatch.

entry.title: Mizan: A National Benchmark for Evaluating Large Language Models on Iraqi Arabic and the Iraqi Civic Context

author.name: Nawar S. Alseelawi, Mustafa S. Aljumaily

entry.summary: Mizan is introduced as Iraq's national LLM benchmark covering Iraqi Arabic and Iraqi civic context, pairing an MSA baseline track with an Iraqi track across six axes including dialect comprehension and generation, bidirectional MSA-Iraqi translation, Iraq-specific knowledge, official document field extraction, and safety. It responds to the fact that Arabic LLM evaluation has matured around Modern Standard Arabic while dialectal Arabic, the language actually spoken, is nearly invisible in existing leaderboards. The benchmark matters for exposing coverage gaps in multilingual evaluation.

entry.title: A latent dimension of Condorcet's jury theorem for multiple AI advisers

author.name: Kazutoshi Sasahara, Aoi Naito, Ryo Fujie

entry.summary: The paper analyzes what happens when multiple AI advisers answer the same question, as in self-consistency and LLM-as-judge panels, showing that Condorcet-style reliability gains come with increasingly visible disagreement. A binomial model shows visible dissent approaches certainty faster than reliability below an adviser accuracy of 0.8, so more advisers can make disagreement more likely than correctness. It matters for how multi-sample and judge-panel inference should be configured and communicated to users.

entry.title: SeqMaestro: From nucleotide sequences to biological hypotheses through interpretable machine learning

author.name: Evgeny S. Saveliev, Krzysztof Kacprzyk, Charlotte Capitanchik, Neelanjan Mukherjee, Kate Matlin, Ryan Sheridan, Srinivas Ramachandran, Jernej Ule, David L. Bentley, Mihaela van der Schaar

entry.summary: SeqMaestro is a machine learning framework that operates directly on nucleotide sequences while producing human-understandable representations, bridging interpretable methods such as sparse linear models and decision trees with raw-sequence deep learning. It targets regulatory genomics, evolutionary biology and phenotype prediction, where classical motif and k-mer features lack flexibility and deep models lack inspectability.

entry.title: Refinement-based Flow Policy Optimization

author.name: Bumgeun Park, Hyukjun Yang, Donghwan Lee

entry.summary: Flow-based policies are expressive for online RL, but standard flow matching requires samples from the target distribution, which is unavailable when the action distribution is defined only implicitly by a Q-function. RFPO alternates between Q-guided stochastic refinement of actions sampled from noise and self-target flow matching, enabling flow policies to be trained in online RL settings.

entry.title: Dynamic Semantic Compression for Efficient Latent-Space Inference in Large Language Models

author.name: Peipei Li, Dongsen Zhang, Yuchen Liu, Wenjun Xu

entry.summary: The paper proposes DSEI, a framework that performs segment-level inference in latent space rather than token-by-token decoding. A Dynamic Semantic Autoencoder, trained self-supervised, compresses segment-level semantics into compact latent representations via adaptive weighting and gated fusion, and is then integrated into the LLM for dense latent-space inference. The claimed benefit is substantially reduced memory overhead and improved computational efficiency.

entry.title: A Language-Guided Multimodal Foundation Model for Zero-Shot and Multi-Task Brain Signal Analysis

author.name: Mingzhi Chen, Yiyu Gui, Guibo Luo, Yuchao Yang

entry.summary: METIS is a multimodal foundation model for brain signal analysis built on a unified language-signal alignment framework, pretrained on a large and diverse brain-signal corpus. It targets zero-shot and multi-task use, addressing the limitations of task-specific retraining and general-purpose multimodal models that fail to interpret neural signals due to representational misalignment.

entry.title: AttnFuse: A Composable DSL for Compiling Attentions to Fused GPU Kernels

author.name: Varun Kumar Dasoju, Tian Zhao

entry.summary: AttnFuse is a small domain-specific language for describing attention variants that compiles them to fused GPU kernels, extending beyond PyTorch's flex_attention by supporting transformations applied before the central matrix multiplication. Notably it can express Rotary Position Embedding, which most modern LLMs rely on but which the prior approach excluded.

entry.title: FlowTSFM: Turning Encoder Depth into Quantile Transport

author.name: Bahaeddine Abdessalem, Shifeng Xie, Zehao Xiao, Youssef Attia El Hili, Ambroise Odonnat, Jianfeng Zhang, Lujia Pan, Keli Zhang, Malik Tiomoko

entry.summary: FlowTSFM reformulates a time series foundation model so that encoder depth acts as a recurrent transport process: a single shared Transformer block is applied iteratively while a quantile-flow objective supervises intermediate states along a trajectory from a prior to the forecast. With only 38.8M parameters it reports competitive results on GIFT-Eval and TIME.

entry.title: Linear Ensemble Sampling with Smaller Ensembles

author.name: Taehyun Hwang, Min-hwan Oh

entry.summary: This theory paper studies how small an ensemble must be for ensemble sampling to retain strong regret guarantees in linear bandits. By refreshing the ensemble only when the regularized Gram matrix changes substantially, the authors reduce the sufficient ensemble size to Theta(d log d + d log log T), narrowing the gap to the intrinsic Omega(d) barrier.

entry.title: GRPO-QM: Target Preserving Exploration for Quantum Tomography

author.name: Yufeng Wang, Parivesh Priye, Lu Wei, Haibin Ling

entry.summary: GRPO-QM learns only an exploration strategy for a fixed quantum-tomography posterior, using a group-relative policy over reversible physical moves with an exact Metropolis correction that keeps the posterior stationary. Reconstruction comparisons suggest most of the gains come from physical proposal mechanisms and prior knowledge rather than from learning, and a closed-form counterexample shows a reward tied to accepted motion can rise even when a physical observable worsens. This is a valuable cautionary result about reward design in RL-for-inference.

entry.title: Structured Features Overfit Where Random Features Grok

author.name: Chon-Fai Kam, Miloud Bessafi, Frederic Cadet

entry.summary: Motivated by a recent proof that over-parameterized ridge regression over unstructured random Gaussian features groks with delay growing as one over weight decay, the authors show that a structured band-limited Fourier feature map over Z_p squared does not exhibit this delay. Enlarging the band at fixed positive weight decay drives peak held-out accuracy monotonically from near perfect down to very poor, with degradation setting in at a capacity ratio far below the interpolation threshold. It matters as a concrete theory counterexample showing that grokking behavior depends on feature structure.

entry.title: Ensemble-Conditioned Molecular Design

author.name: Ross Irwin, Alessandro Tibo, Jon Paul Janet, Simon Olsson

entry.summary: The authors reframe molecular design as optimization over both the modes of a molecule's conformational ensemble and aggregate properties computed over the whole distribution, rather than searching for a single bioactive conformer. They introduce ensemble-conditioned guidance, which conditions 3D molecular generative models simultaneously on ensemble modes (shapes, pharmacophore profiles, pockets) and distribution-level property targets. It matters for drug design where viability depends on conformational distributions.

entry.title: BioDCASE: Active Learning for Bioacoustics

author.name: Ben McEwen, Rupa Kurinchi-Vendhan, Shiqi Zhang, Lukas Rauch, Marek Herde, Sara Beery

entry.summary: Passive acoustic monitoring generates far more audio than can feasibly be annotated, making active learning a natural fit, but published sampling methods are hard to compare because they use different models, budgets, metrics and datasets. The paper presents the 2026 Active Learning for Bioacoustics BioDCASE challenge, a systematic evaluation of sampling strategies under a common protocol. It matters as infrastructure for reproducible benchmarking in an ecologically important, label-scarce domain.

entry.title: Bayesian Optimisation Using Product-of-Experts Gaussian Process Models with Uncertainty Calibration

author.name: Yean Hoon Ong

entry.summary: Bayesian optimization usually relies on a single global Gaussian process surrogate, whose cubic cost in the number of training points limits large-scale problems. The paper introduces BO-pro-c, which uses the product-of-experts Gaussian process with uncertainty calibration as its surrogate, combining local experts to reduce computation and improve uncertainty quantification while preserving global correlations. Adopting this calibrated expert model in the BO loop has not been thoroughly studied before.

entry.title: Privacy-Aligned Personalized Federated Learning with Compact Adaptation and Variable-Length Gaussian Communication

author.name: Yilin Xu, Chun Hei Michael Shiu, Chih Wei Ling, Linqi Song

entry.summary: The paper addresses a structural misalignment in personalized federated learning under record-level differential privacy, where client variation is low-dimensional but repeated training releases high-dimensional updates. It releases a private client context once, confines repeated adaptation to a fixed coefficient space, and realizes the Gaussian mechanism for coefficient updates through variable-length quantization to cut communication cost.

entry.title: Survey of Novel Deep Learning Architectures for Denoising Gravitational-wave Signals

author.name: Rohan Raha, Prayush Kumar

entry.summary: This survey provides the first controlled comparison of five neural network architectures for gravitational-wave denoising, trained identically across the full astrophysically motivated spinning, precessing binary-black-hole parameter space. It argues that current methods are developed on narrow parameter ranges that prevent principled comparison and reliable deployment as detector event rates rise. A unifying principle about the role of matched filtering emerges from the comparison.

entry.title: Harnessing Image Question Dependence for Better VLM Test-time Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Xinrui He, Ting-Wei Li, Junting Wang, Mengting Ai, Xinyu He, Hanghang Tong, Jingrui He

entry.summary: The paper analyzes test-time reinforcement learning for vision-language models and finds that consensus-based gains come mostly from answer normalization rather than genuine content correction. Many initial answers are wrong because the model fails to use image and question jointly, so consensus rewards can entrench grounding errors instead of fixing them. The authors propose exploiting image-question dependence to build more reliable self-generated learning signals.

entry.title: Bridging the Synthetic-to-Real Gap for Few-Shot Cryo-ET Classification

author.name: Siddhant Bharadwaj, Ashish Vashist, Rashi Singh, Pranav Vinodh, Nishanth Artham, Runmin Jiang, Xingjian Li, Min Xu

entry.summary: Subtomogram classification in cryo-electron tomography suffers from scarce labeled data, while simulators can generate unlimited synthetic subtomograms that differ substantially from real ones. The authors propose a synthetic-to-real adaptation framework with a learnable transformation module that bridges the domain gap at both input and feature levels. Experiments show consistent gains over existing transfer-learning baselines in few-shot settings.

entry.title: Riemannian ascent--descent for nonconvex nonconcave minimax landscapes: convergence to basin saddle points and applications to distributionally robust optimization

author.name: Rishabh Dixit, Pranav Upadrashta, Alex Cloninger

entry.summary: This paper studies distributionally robust optimization formulated as minimax problems over the product of a Euclidean space and a Riemannian manifold, where the landscape is generally nonconvex and nonconcave. Since no globally convergent first-order method is known for this setting, the authors define a basin saddle point, a locally defined Nash equilibrium over a delta basin and a geodesic ball. They develop an abstract convergence framework for a Riemannian gradient ascent with multistep descent under local conditions.

entry.title: VGFM: Expressive Robot Policies via Dense Value Guidance in Flow Matching

author.name: Prajwal Koirala, Mark Campbell

entry.summary: The authors propose Value-Guided Flow Matching, an offline reinforcement learning framework that injects dense value-based shaping directly into a flow-based generative policy, avoiding the need for backpropagation through time, auxiliary critics, or distillation. The goal is to get rich multimodal action representations for robot control while retaining tractable policy improvement.

entry.title: Improving the Last-Iterate Guarantees of Anytime Algorithms for Stochastic Monotone Variational Inequalities

author.name: Jun-Hyun Kim, Ahmet Alacaoglu

entry.summary: The paper analyzes a single-loop, single-call stochastic algorithm with Halpern anchoring for constrained convex-concave problems and monotone variational inequalities, using one unbiased gradient-operator sample per iteration. It proves an anytime last-iterate rate of order t to the minus one quarter for both gradient-mapping norm and restricted gap, improving on the previous best restricted-gap rate of t to the minus one fifth, and covers unbounded feasible sets and structured oracles without bounded variance. It matters for equilibrium computation in monotone games with noisy feedback.

entry.title: DenMark: Robust Semantic Watermarking for Diffusion Language Models

author.name: Tianhao Ma, Weihao Xuan, Dong-Dong Wu, Farshid Nooshi, Takashi Ishida, Gang Niu, Naoto Yokoya, Masashi Sugiyama

entry.summary: DenMark is a semantic watermarking framework for diffusion language models that injects key-dependent signals directly into the denoising process by partitioning output into fixed token regions and using temporally-aware scoring. This addresses the mismatch that existing semantic watermarking assumes autoregressive generation, where candidate units are complete before scoring, whereas DLM tokens remain incomplete and are updated in flexible orders.

entry.title: Don't Just Look, Intervene: Perturbation Based Region Labeling for VQA Images

author.name: Marko Jojic, Zhaonan Li, Ben Zhou

entry.summary: The paper introduces model-causal visual evidence as an annotation target, defined as the image regions whose counterfactual removal or perturbation changes a model's answer distribution for a given image-question pair. It proposes Counterfactual Search for Grounding Regions, a scalable pipeline that proposes candidate regions, perturbs them, measures answer sensitivity, and aggregates evidence across multiple judges. The aim is supervision for visual grounding without expensive manual annotation.

entry.title: Hyper-LLaVA: Hyperbolic Uncertainty-aware Modality-Balanced Routing for Multimodal Continual Instruction Tuning

author.name: Kunlun Xu, Yanqin Zhang, Wenwen Qiang, Jiahuan Zhou

entry.summary: Hyper-LLaVA targets multimodal continual instruction tuning, where parameter routing must handle incrementally accumulated tasks. It identifies two flaws in state-of-the-art routing based on sample-to-task-center similarity with equal-weight cross-modal fusion: intra-task diversity is underexploited, and modalities with differing reliability can misguide routing when fused uniformly. The proposed method uses hyperbolic uncertainty-aware representations and modality-balanced routing to correct both issues.

entry.title: DynEoMT: Learning Object Dynamicity from Online Segmentation Queries

author.name: Calvin Galagain, Martyna Poreba, Fran\c{c}ois Goulette

entry.summary: DynEoMT augments query-based online video segmentation with region-level dynamicity prediction, labeling each segmented region as dynamic or static relative to the camera. Crucially, it does so using only the current frame and propagated queries, without optical flow, depth, camera pose, or previous frames. The paper also introduces annotations because existing benchmarks do not label this attribute, making motion-awareness an explicit output rather than an implicit one.

entry.title: Direct Conditional Transition Sampling for Diffusion Inverse Problems

author.name: Qi Yu, Hanlin Wu, Xiaohui Sun

entry.summary: DCTS is a training-free diffusion inverse-problem solver that approximates an ideal clean-space posterior refresh using a direct stochastic-flow transport rather than explicit probability-flow ODE integration and clean-space MCMC. It estimates the measurement-conditioned clean mean along a short inner path and transports Gaussian source noise to the next noisy state, aided by a denoiser-compatible sufficient statistic. This targets the trade-off between cheap local guidance and costly global posterior correction.

entry.title: LIMODENet: Attention-Free Compact Encoders for Information-Preserving Onboard Satellite Image Restoration

author.name: Thanh-Dung Le, Vu Nguyen Ha, Ti Ti Nguyen, Symeon Chatzinotas

entry.summary: LIMODENet is a 0.69M-parameter, softmax- and QKV-free encoder designed for onboard satellite image restoration on neuromorphic accelerators that support neither attention nor softmax. Its residual stages are interpretable as ODE discretizations, and the authors show empirically that probe accuracy rises sharply from stem to head, evidence of information preservation. At matched parameter count it beats CNN autoencoders and skip-connection U-Nets on DVB-S2X-degraded EuroSAT.

entry.title: GRAVA: Grounded Reasoning-to-Action Representation and Learning for Autonomous Driving

author.name: Xiao Liu, Haoyu Li, Jianghao Leng, Lin Wang, Chao Sun

entry.summary: GRAVA targets driving vision-language-action models whose intermediate reasoning is often weakly grounded in scene evidence and loosely tied to executable behavior. Its Grounded Reasoning-to-Action component unifies grounding, reasoning and action generation in one autoregressive stream, linking action-relevant language to 2D visual regions and ego-centric physical states, organizing interactions in a trajectory-anchored typed graph, and serializing this into grounded reasoning that a single VLM decodes into an executable planner action. This addresses a central weakness of current VLA driving models.

entry.title: Learning Manipulation-Sufficient Representations via Outcome Bottlenecks

author.name: Md Selim Sarowar, Sungho Kim

entry.summary: This paper proposes learning stochastic visual representations through a policy-free, action-conditioned outcome bottleneck, where marginal outcome log-loss acts as a distortion term and a KL term regularizes rate, motivated by the minimal statistic preserving outcome distributions across admissible actions. The implemented finite model is evaluated as a rate-regularized mixture predictor, and the same encoder supports grasp selection, conformal filtering, active viewpoint selection, and latent test-time adaptation. It links networked manipulation, rate-distortion theory, and perception for control.

entry.title: A Memristive Synapse for Online STDP Learning and Inference in SNNs

author.name: Elia Mateu-Barriendos, \'Alvaro G\'omez-Pau, Daniel Arum\'i, Rosa Rodr\'iguez-Monta\~n\'es, Salvador Manich

entry.summary: This paper presents a fully analog memristive synaptic circuit that performs online spike-timing-dependent plasticity in spiking neural networks, generating gradual timing-dependent conductance updates directly from pre- and post-synaptic spikes without external digital control or synthesized STDP waveforms. Post-layout simulations in 130 nm CMOS show timing-dependent conductance adaptation, and a 2x2 network illustrates unsupervised neuron specialization. The work is a hardware-level contribution to on-chip learning in neuromorphic systems.

entry.title: Decentralized Multi-Robot Task Allocation Under Degraded Communication: A Benchmark of Performance, Reliability, and Computation

author.name: James Lott, Vahraz Honary

entry.summary: The authors benchmark six decentralized multi-robot task allocation algorithms (CBAA, ACBBA, PI, HIPC, DMCHBA, DGA) in a collaborative visit scenario under ideal and degraded communication conditions including Bernoulli loss, Gilbert-Elliott loss, and Rayleigh fading. The study characterizes tradeoffs across travel cost, communication robustness, allocation reliability, computational burden, and scale sensitivity using hundreds of paired instances.

entry.title: GIFT: Glove-Inferred Force Transfer: Force-Aware Human-to-Robot Skill Transfer from a Wearable Sensing Glove to a Robot Hand Without Tactile Sensors

author.name: Tzah Sarusi

entry.summary: GIFT transfers force-aware manipulation skills from a human demonstrator to a robot without shared tactile hardware, measuring fingertip force in newtons on the human side via a wearable glove and estimating it in newtons on the robot side from actuator-current residuals relative to a free-space baseline. Demonstrations are captured with a head-mounted camera and no robot present, decoupling data collection from the target platform.

entry.title: Novel Ex-vivo Calf Brain Model with Integrated Sub-Skull Force Sensors to Access Simulated Neurosurgical Procedures

author.name: Hamad Binhammad, Matheus Ballestero, Mohammed Babgi, Seana Shaka, Nima Hemati, Rothaina Saeedi, Aiden Mazidi, Bianca Giglio, Rukun Dou, Houssem-Eddine Gueziri, Amir Hooshiar, Rolando F. Del Maestro

entry.summary: The authors present and validate a portable ex-vivo force-sensing platform that quantifies tool-tissue interaction forces across the skull-brain interface, using fresh calf brain tissue in a 3D-printed human skull equipped with a six-degree-of-freedom force/torque sensor and real-time acquisition. Five validation protocols assess accuracy and dynamic fidelity against ground-truth measurement.

entry.title: EMoG: Emotion-Modulated Gait Generation for Expressive Humanoid Locomotion

author.name: Yi Lu, Tianhao Jiang, Honglong Tian, Yumeng Zhang, Qingrui Zhao, Zhengtao Wang, Xiao-Xiao Long, Qiu Shen, Xun Cao

entry.summary: EMoG introduces an emotional-style code with continuously adjustable intensity that conditions a lightweight MLP to generate expressive but command-consistent periodic gait trajectories in real time, tracked by a unified reinforcement learning policy. The authors collect a large-scale emotion-annotated gait dataset from professional performers and build an automated pipeline to extract physically consistent motions. It matters for humanoid robots that need to communicate affect and intent, not just walk stably.

entry.title: C$^2$Nav: Compare Before You Commit for Zero-Shot Vision-and-Language Navigation

author.name: Runtian Zheng, Congpeng Zhang, Ying Liu

entry.summary: C2Nav proposes a complementary model-robot interface for zero-shot vision-and-language navigation in continuous environments, where the VLM compares controller-constructed alternatives instead of emitting waypoints, pixels, headings, progress, or arrival decisions directly. Geometry, thresholds, action magnitude, and execution stay on the physical side, and the training-free framework coordinates ordinal gaze election over physically vetted candidate views with further faculties. It reduces the coupling between a generative response and irreversible commitment or geometric magnitude.

entry.title: Flow-Matched Motion Priors: Online Optimal-Transport Rewards for Imitation Learning

author.name: Yilin Zou, Chenghua Liu, Chenglong Wu, Fanghua Jiang

entry.summary: Flow-Matched Motion Priors (FMP) replaces the adversarial discriminator of Adversarial Motion Priors with an online scalar reward learned from paths connecting current rollout histories to an expert motion bank, using entropic optimal transport for the coupling. The authors argue naive optimal transport averaging produces barycentric targets that wash out joint motion across gait phases, and that flow matching on a learned potential avoids this.

entry.title: Goal-Oriented Communications for Physical AI: Design and Testbed

author.name: Shutong Chen, Wenkai Zhang, Adnan Aijaz, Miao Guo, Yansha Deng

entry.summary: This paper builds an end-to-end goal-oriented communication testbed for Physical AI, connecting a PiPER robot arm with an RGB-D camera and 5G modem to an NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin edge device, transmitting only task-relevant semantic representations to meet strict latency requirements that existing 5G networks struggle to support. The authors note that prior goal-oriented communication frameworks were mainly evaluated in simulation and had not been validated in a practical Physical AI deployment.

entry.title: $\tau$-Elicitation: Benchmarking multi-turn entity extraction in voice agents

author.name: Soham Ray, Victor Barres

entry.summary: The authors introduce a 200-task voice benchmark spanning ten entity types, controlled difficulty levels, caller realism, and three environments, to expose where exact entity capture fails in voice agents. A matched text agent passes all tasks while four voice configurations achieve robust exact success of only 0.14 to 0.41, and a scaffolding strategy prescribing spelling, read-back, correction, and confirmation raises robust pass rates by 14 to 31 points at added interaction cost.

entry.title: Identity Is More Than Recall: A Benchmark for Persistent Identity in Deployed AI Agents

author.name: Zhenyu Zhao, Roy Zhao

entry.summary: PAI-Bench is a provider-neutral benchmark measuring how well deployed agents honour a versioned, update-governed identity contract, separating recall, composition, behavioural enactment, resistance, persistence, lineage, and role-conditioned updates while keeping scoring oracles outside the target process. Two frozen campaigns cover sixteen synthetic profiles and thirty-two probes across three target configurations, and a judge-independent literal audit finds direct-parent identifiers in 48/48 atomic responses but only 1/48 implicit self-portraits.

entry.title: MANAS-2: Constrained Reconstruction for EEG Foundation Models

author.name: Arvasu Kulkarni, Aditya Ray Mishra, Mahir Jain, Parshva Runwal, Lakshya Saini, Siddharth Panwar, Sandeep Singh

entry.summary: MANAS-2 is an EEG foundation model combining a Raw-Band Hybrid masked autoencoder that reconstructs temporal waveform patches and compact spectral-band targets with Constrained Reconstruction, a physics-motivated regularizer on temporal decoder output. The regularizer penalizes RMS energy differences between adjacent short windows to bias the encoder toward oscillatory-envelope organization. It matters because masked reconstruction on low-SNR waveforms may not yield the most useful representations.

entry.title: SAILOR: Solver-Assisted Interactive LLM-based Optimization Recovery

author.name: Shaghayegh Sadeghi, Stephen L. Smith, David C. Del Rey Fern'andez

entry.summary: SAILOR targets a practical failure mode in LLM-driven optimization modeling: when a natural-language problem omits costs, capacities, demands or bounds, the model must either halt or invent values. The system detects unsupported numerical choices, asks targeted follow-up questions prioritized by uncertainty and solver-derived sensitivity estimates, and updates the model before returning a solution, evaluated on 1,723 instances across seven masked benchmarks.

entry.title: Safety Signals to Verify NetOps Agents with Action-Level Granularity

author.name: Tobias Labarta, Frederik Pahde, Novak Boskov, Maximilian Dreyer, David Birkenberger, Manzoor Ahmed Khan, Sebastian Lapuschkin, Wojciech Samek

entry.summary: The authors study agents that autonomously manage datacenter network operations, where long-horizon reliability and correct abstention from risky actions are essential. Because abstention requires knowing an action's impact before execution, they construct action-level ground truth for network repair tasks and derive safety signals that let a system verify agent actions at fine granularity.

entry.title: AI Deployment Accountability Engineering: A Vision for Accountable AI in Safety-Critical Socio-Technical Systems

author.name: Murat Kantarcioglu

entry.summary: This vision paper argues that pre-deployment, model-centric properties such as accuracy, robustness, fairness and interpretability are necessary but insufficient once an AI system operates inside a changing socio-technical environment. It proposes AI Deployment Accountability Engineering as a subdiscipline covering distribution shifts, institutional constraints, human feedback loops, privacy requirements and interactions among multiple AI agents.

entry.title: Moral Rebel Agents: Decision-Making Under Conflicting Obligations

author.name: Hector Munoz-Avila, David W. Aha, Paola Rizzo

entry.summary: The paper investigates moral rebellion, meaning an autonomous agent's ability to deviate from an assigned task when morally justified. It formalizes an amoral baseline plus four moral rebel architectures, including utilitarian agents, deontic agents enforcing normative constraints, utilitarian-deontic hybrids, and a further variant, to compare behavior under conflicting obligations.

entry.title: Crypto Accounting Bench: Evaluating Frontier and Open-Weight Models on Crypto-Asset Accounting Tasks

author.name: Kareem Khattab, Omar Khattab, Mohamed Ibrahem

entry.summary: The authors introduce CAB, a benchmark of 118 tasks drawn from seven pseudonymized organizations that asks language models to reconstruct the exact journal entry posted for a crypto-asset transaction, including accounts, sides, amounts, currencies, and full-precision quantities. Twelve proprietary and open-weight models are evaluated on this realistic accounting task.

entry.title: Medical Knowledge Simplification for Patients in the Era of LLMs: A Case Study on Diabetes

author.name: Pallika Kafle, Yipeng Zhou, Guanfeng Liu, Quan Z. Sheng, Cheng-Hsin Hsu

entry.summary: This paper presents MediClear, an LLM-based system augmented with retrieval-augmented generation that rewrites complex diabetes information into patient-friendly language, and evaluates it with human participants. It contributes one of the few human-centered evaluations of medical simplification, arguing that readability alone does not guarantee real-world patient comprehension or better health decisions.

entry.title: Potential of Artificial Intelligence Algorithms for Identification of Relevant Diagnostic and Prognostic Biomarkers of Early-Stage Liver Cancer

author.name: Ali Bou Nassif, Darko Castven, Manar Abu Talib, Jibran Sualeh Muhammad, Ahmed Ammar Kubba, Jens Marquardt, Abdalla Sayed Ali

entry.summary: This study applies deep learning and explainable AI to transcriptomic data in order to diagnose hepatocellular carcinoma and identify biomarkers across five disease stages. Using semi-supervised construction from three source datasets and feature selection such as SelectKBest, the best model reached about 90.7 percent accuracy with 15 genes, while a 20-gene model achieved the lowest loss.

entry.title: Physically Aware Radiomics Without Interpolation: Disentangling Voxel Geometry and Signal Modification in CT and MRI

author.name: David Corral Fontecha, Juan Miranda Bautista, Pablo Menendez Fern\'andez-Miranda, Sergio Rubio-Mart\'in, Lara Lloret Iglesias, Jose A. Vega

entry.summary: The authors modify PyRadiomics so texture features account for true voxel spacing without resampling the underlying image, isolating interpolation-induced signal change from genuine geometric effects. Comparing native, resampled, spacing-aware, and fake-isotropic configurations in CT and MRI, they show that conflating voxel geometry with interpolation artifacts can distort radiomic texture measurements. This matters for reproducibility of radiomics pipelines used in clinical imaging research.

entry.title: Pedestrian Crossing Intent Classification From Event-Based Vision Using Convolutional Spiking Neural Networks With Temporal Augmentation

author.name: Henok Teklu, Mustafa Sakhai, Maciej Wielgosz, Matej Mertik

entry.summary: This work builds an end-to-end pipeline for predicting whether a pedestrian will cross a road, converting JAAD driving footage into synthetic dynamic vision sensor event streams with the v2e simulator and augmenting training with CARLA-simulated DVS sequences under normal and adverse weather. It then classifies crossing intent with convolutional spiking neural networks, targeting the motion blur, high dynamic range, and class imbalance problems that hurt conventional frame-based RGB models. The contribution matters for energy-efficient, low-latency perception in autonomous driving safety systems.

entry.title: Chance-Constrained Belief-Space Maneuver Planning for Autonomous Collision Avoidance Under Uncertainty

author.name: Grace Ra Kim, Duncan Eddy, Mykel J. Kochenderfer

entry.summary: This work formulates the decision of whether a spacecraft should maneuver to avoid a conjunction as a belief-space planning problem, representing uncertain orbital states as Gaussian beliefs. The planner uses chance-constrained belief-space Monte Carlo tree search to reason about possible future tracking updates before time of closest approach, with a terminal chance constraint bounding collision probability. It matters for space situational awareness, where acting too early can be as costly as acting too late.

entry.title: PolicyMem: Geometric Policy Memory for LLM Governance

author.name: Yuanchen Bei, Zhengzhang Chen, Yanjun Zhao, Haoyu Wang, Hanghang Tong, Haifeng Chen

entry.summary: PolicyMem externalizes natural-language policies as reusable geometric memory objects so that policy evidence can be shared consistently across detection, intervention, and verification. It aims to bridge the gap between learned guards, which are strong semantically but coupled to a training taxonomy, and programmable frameworks, which are flexible but require heavy manual prompt engineering.

entry.title: LIMBO: Lifelong Inference-Time Memory and Budget Optimization for LLM Agents

author.name: Siddharth Sharma, Nilesh Prasad Pandey, Onat Gungor, Tajana Rosing

entry.summary: LIMBO addresses inference-time memory allocation for lifelong LLM agents that use experience replay, arguing that every replayed trajectory competes with retrieval, reasoning, tool use, and verification for the same limited prompt and compute budget. Existing methods use fixed replay policies regardless of whether replay helps the current task, and the authors propose adaptive allocation instead. It matters for making long-running agents both competent and cost-efficient.

entry.title: Towards Evolving Context Parameterization for Large Language Models

author.name: Xiaobing Shi, Zherui Li, Yiming Jiang, Kun Wang, Yufei Guo

entry.summary: The paper formalizes the Memory Updating with Sequential Evolution task and builds MUSE-bench to evaluate whether context parameterization methods can incorporate updates while preserving unaffected information. It observes that existing approaches assume static contexts and lack mechanisms to distinguish validity states under continual updates, and proposes PLUME, a training-free method that builds a global update representation. It matters for memory systems in LLMs that must evolve as facts change.

entry.title: Task-Specified Active Metrological Inspection with Measurement-Steered VLA Manipulation and Deterministic Evidence Gating

author.name: Zhiling Chen, Jingzhan Ge, Ruimin Chen, Matthew P. Castanier, David Gorsich, Farhad Imani

entry.summary: The paper formulates task-specified active metrological inspection for high-mix low-volume manufacturing and proposes FRAME, a hierarchical dual-arm framework that turns an inspection instruction plus structured specification into traceable conformance evidence. It couples learned manipulation with calibrated laser profilometry, using a task manager to ground requirements and deterministic gating to validate evidence. The work matters because it reframes robot inspection around completeness and validity of measurement evidence rather than task completion alone.

entry.title: ATTRICITE: Training an Open 4B Model for Citation Recovery toward Faithful Attribution

author.name: Yee Man Choi, Xuehang Guo, Songcheng Cai, Yimu Wang, Yi R. Fung, Qingyun Wang

entry.summary: The authors introduce ATTRICITE, an open 4B-parameter tool-using model trained to recover the paper originally cited from a citation-bearing passage, along with the CITEALIGN dataset of 7,607 computer-science instances and a 709-instance evaluation benchmark. Author citations serve as the human attribution signal, with target recovery standing in as a proxy for faithful attribution. It matters for verifiability of scientific claims and for building open, small-scale attribution tooling.

entry.title: NeuroActiSep: Detecting Factual Hallucinations from Feed-Forward Neurons in a Single Pass

author.name: Ali Derogar Odolou, Reza Nazari, Mostafa Salehi

entry.summary: The paper ranks feed-forward neurons at the final prompt token using a dedicated neuron-selection dataset, then transfers the selected neuron identities to train hallucination classifiers on other factual question answering datasets. It provides evidence that probes built on these neuron features match probes built on full internal states, and analyzes the distribution and effect of selected neurons. It matters for cheap, single-pass white-box hallucination detection.

entry.title: Compositional SVG Generation via VLM-Driven Hierarchical Semantic Parsing

author.name: Sehwan Park, Taehoon Kim, Geonhee Han, Dohyun Kim, Seung Wook Kim, Paul Hongsuck Seo

entry.summary: This paper introduces an agentic VLM pipeline that recursively decomposes visual scenes into semantic and geometric hierarchies to produce structured, editable SVG rather than flat collections of paths. It uses top-down decomposition, visual grounding and prompt-driven amodal occlusion recovery so each component is geometrically complete. The authors also release a Semantic SVG Benchmark with human-annotated semantic groupings to measure the capability.

entry.title: Route, Don't Fix: Regime-Dependent Decoding Correction and a Trajectory-Gated Router for Reliable Clinical LLM Answer Selection

author.name: Zeyu Dong, Benjamin Wang, Joyee W. Jin

entry.summary: The paper argues that fixed inference-time logit corrections are not universally useful: a corrector that gains roughly ten points on a truthfulness stress test barely helps on clinical multiple-choice tasks, where instruction tuning concentrates probability on one answer and terminal entropy is low. The authors propose ALTAS, which reads terminal entropy and late-layer signals to route between correction regimes, improving clinical answer selection without new infrastructure or extra model calls.

entry.title: Steering Generative Robot Policies with Lexicographic Preferences

author.name: Yixuan Jia, Jonathan P. How

entry.summary: The paper shows that a frozen generative robot policy based on diffusion or flow matching can be steered at inference time to respect lexicographically ordered deployment objectives, such as hard embodiment feasibility constraints ranked above user preferences. This lets operators impose priority-ordered requirements not represented during training without retraining the policy.

entry.title: SpliTEE: Improving LLM Inference on Trusted Hardware with Differentially Private GPU Outsourcing

author.name: Shashie Dilhara Batan Arachchige, Robin Carpentier, Hassan Jameel Asghar, Dali Kaafar

entry.summary: Noting that CPU-based trusted execution environments are much slower than GPUs for LLM inference, SpliTEE extends the Slalom split-inference idea of distributing work between a TEE and an untrusted GPU while protecting intermediate values, adding differential privacy for the outsourced computation. The goal is to preserve prompt privacy against a remote provider while recovering much of the GPU throughput advantage.

entry.title: Beyond Numerical Time Series: A Unified Benchmark for Multimodal Forecasting with Heterogeneous Context

author.name: Peng Chen, Zhihao Zhuang, Hongzhou Chen, Junhao Huang, Aiping Yang, Mengsen Wu, Yiding Liu, Xilin Dai, Zewei Dong

entry.summary: The authors introduce MUSE-Bench, a benchmark for multimodal time series forecasting that covers fourteen datasets across eight domains and six context types including metadata, events, holidays, news, images and numerical covariates. It evaluates statistical, foundation, multimodal and general-purpose LLM forecasters under a unified setting to address the fragmented, numerical-centric state of existing benchmarks.

entry.title: EMR: Self-Evolving Medical Multi-Agent System via Experience Mining and Reuse

author.name: Dongsheng Shi, Yue Li, Xin Yi, Linlin Wang

entry.summary: EMR is a self-evolving medical multi-agent system that addresses the static strategies and lack of persistent memory in existing clinical LLM agents. It builds a hierarchical clinical experience library spanning principles, diagnostic patterns and representative cases, then at inference emulates multidisciplinary consultation with a planner coordinating department-specific agents and a summary agent.

entry.title: When Correlations Mislead: Confounder-Aware Multi-View Urban Region Representation Learning

author.name: Sean Bin Yang, Ying Sun, Zongyi Xu, Tung Kieu, Jilin Hu, Bin Yang, Kristian Torp, Hua Lu, Torben Bach Pedersen

entry.summary: This paper proposes CURE, a confounder-aware framework for learning urban region embeddings from heterogeneous views such as mobility flows, points of interest, and land use. It argues that typical multi-view methods strengthen cross-view interactions and thereby propagate spurious correlations induced by shared latent confounders, destabilizing downstream predictions. CURE instead encodes each view on its own regional graph structure and explicitly accounts for confounding, aiming at more robust mobility, safety, and demand forecasting.

entry.title: Concept-Grounded Reasoning with Prompt-Driven Localization for Interpretable Structured Report Generation

author.name: Xinyue Xu, Hongbin Lin, Juangui Xu, Hualiang Wang, Lehan Wang, Lijie Hu, Weiyang Liu, Adrian Weller, Xiaomeng Li

entry.summary: CORAL is a multimodal framework that integrates spatial grounding and concept-level supervision into a unified reasoning process for medical report generation. It uses a prompt-driven segmentation model to localize lesions and grounds generation in clinically defined intermediate attributes, addressing the limited interpretability of end-to-end multimodal fusion in existing medical MLLMs. The goal is evidence-driven, standardized report generation for modalities such as ultrasound and X-ray.

entry.title: PIVOT: Physics-Grounded Verification for AI-Generated Audio-Video Detection

author.name: Bo Zheng, Kangran Zhao, Xiaoyu Zhang, Weinan Guan, Zhiheng Li, Yize Chen, Haizhou Li, Qingshan Liu, Siwei Lyu, Baoyuan Wu

entry.summary: PIVOT is a physics-grounded detector for AI-generated content that estimates physical quantities from video and audio, selects physical laws relevant to each clip, and verifies whether measurable constraints are satisfied.
