The premise is that while generators increasingly suppress artifact cues, faithfully reproducing real-world physical behavior remains difficult. Beyond a real/fake decision, PIVOT returns supporting evidence that records which physical constraints were violated.

entry.title: Look Before You Leap: Factual Decoding with Internal Attribution Signals

author.name: Hayeong Ryu, JungMin Yun, Byeonggeuk Lim, Sunhee Jo, YoungBin Kim

entry.summary: DescaPE is a decoding framework that uses internal model signals to suppress hallucination-prone generation trajectories at inference time, motivated by the compounding snowball effect of early factual errors. Using sliding-window MLP ablation, the authors identify a factual-salient layer span whose signal spikes at hallucination-prone steps, then train a lightweight probe to approximate it from a single forward pass.

entry.title: Machine Unlearning for Speech Question Answering in Large Audio-Language Models

author.name: Zhe Liu

entry.summary: This work studies machine unlearning for speech question answering in large audio-language models, a setting made harder than text unlearning by the tight coupling between acoustic perception and stored factual knowledge. It evaluates gradient ascent, task arithmetic, and alignment-based fine-tuning that enforces safe refusals, aiming to remove private knowledge while retaining question-answering ability. It matters because speech models inherit memorization and privacy risks from large-scale audio training data.

entry.title: SPICE: Simple Polysemantic Feature Interpretation via Clustering-based Explanation

author.name: Sehyun Lee, Dahee Kwon, Damin Lee, Jaesik Choi

entry.summary: SPICE is a framework for analyzing polysemanticity in deep vision architectures, where single neurons respond to multiple unrelated concepts. It avoids architecture-specific assumptions and manual heuristics such as a fixed number of concept clusters K, aiming for generality and scalability to transformer-based models. Better characterization of polysemantic features is directly relevant to efforts that interpret model internals by decomposing activations.

entry.title: Pretraining for Sample-Efficient Neural Interfaces

author.name: Ben Tang, Zachary Spalding, Gregory B. Cogan

entry.summary: This paper proposes MAPA, a masked autoencoder augmented with two spatial encodings (an anatomical region embedding and a relative positional encoding) to enable self-supervised pretraining on intracranial EEG recordings. The goal is to cut the large labeled-data burden per subject in brain-computer interface decoders by learning transferable neural representations despite intersubject differences in electrode placement and anatomy.

entry.title: Tabby: An Open Pretraining Recipe for Time Series Foundation Models

author.name: Shifeng Xie, Bahaeddine Abdessalem, Zehao Xiao, Youssef Attia El Hili, Ambroise Odonnat, Zhiwei Dong, Lei Zan, Themis Palpanas, Jianfeng Zhang, Lujia Pan, Keli Zhang, Malik Tiomoko

entry.summary: Tabby is a 145M-parameter long-context probabilistic time series foundation model released together with a fully open pretraining recipe. It uses an encoder-only patch Transformer with a mixed real and synthetic corpus, a progressive convergence schedule enabling reusable checkpoints, and deep quantile supervision for intermediate layers.

entry.title: Towards Identifying the Dataset Biases Causing Phantom Transfer

author.name: Jonas J\"ur{\ss}, Pietro Li\`o

entry.summary: Building on evidence that teacher models can transfer biases to students through datasets where explicit references have been filtered out, this paper shows a Sentence BERT embedding signature can identify the topic of such a hidden bias with a Matthews correlation coefficient of 0.83 when the attacker's teacher is known and 0.46 when it is not. It also finds different teacher models express the same bias through different vocabulary.

entry.title: Symmetries and Singularities

author.name: Vishnu Varadarajan, Mihir More, Aritra Das, Debayan Gupta

entry.summary: The paper attacks the computational cost of estimating the local learning coefficient from Singular Learning Theory, which quantifies the effective complexity of an over-parameterized network near a solution. It exploits known symmetry structure in models to make the estimation tractable without expensive posterior sampling. This matters for measuring model complexity and for SLT-based analyses of large networks.

entry.title: Tackling Failure Modes of PINNs and PIKANs Using Conflict-Free Gradients

author.name: Sidharth S. Menon, Irina Tezaur, Ameya D. Jagtap

entry.summary: The paper combines domain decomposition for physics-informed neural networks and Kolmogorov-Arnold networks with projection-based gradient surgery to address conflicting residual, boundary and interface loss terms. It evaluates PCGrad and ConFIG and identifies degradation in cases such as 3D domains with multiple overlapping interfaces, then proposes an improved projection scheme. It matters for making domain-decomposed SciML scalable to complex 2D and 3D geometries.

entry.title: Multi-source Transfer Learning of Time Series with a Shapelet-based Distance Measure

author.name: Jiseok Lee, Brian Kenji Iwana

entry.summary: The paper addresses source-dataset selection for time-series transfer learning, where conventional transferability estimation requires expensive pre-training on each candidate source. It introduces Shapelet Matching, a training-free method that extracts discriminative shapelets from target and source datasets and quantifies similarity between the shapelet sets, while also mitigating negative transfer from a bad single-source choice. This could substantially lower the cost of building time-series classifiers under data scarcity.

entry.title: GSLAD: Prototype-Regularized Graph Structure Learning for Multivariate Time Series Anomaly Detection

author.name: Zepeng Zhang, Fuad Khuri, Keivan Faghih Niresi, Olga Fink

entry.summary: The paper notes that industrial faults may first alter inter-variable structural relationships while individual trajectories still look normal, producing weak anomaly signals for forecasting or reconstruction based detectors. GSLAD is a two-phase framework that first trains a condition-aware graph learner and graph-based forecaster, then clusters inferred normal graphs into structural prototypes for anomaly scoring based on structural deviation. Detecting anomalies via learned dependency structure is a promising complement to value-based detectors.

entry.title: Approximating neutron-star radii using gravitational-wave only measurements with symbolic regression

author.name: Micha{\l} Bejger

entry.summary: This work trains the symbolic regression tool pySR on TOV solutions from piecewise polytropic equations of state to discover an approximate closed-form expression for neutron-star radius as a function of gravitational-wave-only measurements such as masses and tidal deformabilities. The resulting expression is intended to let multi-messenger astronomers compare gravitational-wave and electromagnetic radius information directly.

entry.title: Abstract-LoRA: Unlocking Single-Image Style Transfer through Targeted U-Net Block Training

author.name: Xinglin Hu

entry.summary: Abstract-LoRA proposes a lightweight LoRA training procedure applied to specific U-Net blocks to improve single-image style transfer with diffusion models. The motivation is that multi-image style transfer methods requiring five to ten examples work well, while single-image methods often fail to balance content preservation and style fidelity, limiting style extraction from scarce artworks.

entry.title: GzDRL: Reproducible and Scalable Deep Reinforcement Learning with Gazebo

author.name: Amal Dev Haridevan, Junjie Kang, Jinjun Shan

entry.summary: This paper introduces GzDRL, a single-process reinforcement learning framework for the Gazebo robotics simulator that avoids middleware layers and directly synchronizes agent actions with physics updates. The design targets determinism, reproducibility, and high-throughput data collection for vectorized RL training. Benchmarks show the highest workstation throughput among compared frameworks while staying competitive with GPU-accelerated simulators.

entry.title: SomBench: Benchmark Dataset for Advancing Machine Learning in Lunar Science

author.name: Himanshu Patil, Gabby Nyirjesy, Rachel A. Slank, Vishal Gaur, Daniela Szwarcman, Paolo Fraccaro, Nikolaos Dionelis, Michael K. Barker, Andrew Annex, Vishnu Viswanathan, Zachary Morse, Ethan I. Schaefer, Hiyam Debary, Ankur Kumar, Rohit Lal, Geoffrey Dawson, Campbell Watson, Rebekah I. Dawson-Rigas, Manil Maskey, Juan Bernab\'e-Moreno, Rahul Ramachandran, Sujit Roy

entry.summary: SomBench aggregates more than 30 co-registered layers from ten instruments across four lunar missions into a single spatially aligned, ML-ready dataset spanning 1 meter to 20 km per pixel and 82 degrees of latitude in 90 Lunar Transverse Mercator zones with polar caps. An image-anchored tiling pipeline produces multimodal pretraining tiles with leakage-safe splits, distributed as netCDF with Parquet metadata. The goal is to overcome heterogeneity in sampling, projection, and conventions that has blocked reproducible ML on lunar data.

entry.title: Ergodic Control and Controlled Diffusion for Robot Learning: Review and Tutorial

author.name: Max Muchen Sun, Cem Bilaloglu, Ananya Rao, Stefan Ivic, Guillaume Sartoretti, Kathleen Fitzsimons, Ian Abraham, Sylvain Calinon, Todd Murphey

entry.summary: This review and tutorial connects diffusion learning, controlled diffusion, and ergodic control, arguing that the three frameworks were developed in parallel and have quietly converged. It shows how controlling the statistical mechanism of diffusion processes can shape the temporal evolution of state distributions underlying robot trajectories, inducing ergodic behavior. Applications discussed span robot perception, control, and decision-making.

entry.title: Odds-Shift Slippage in One-vs-Rest Rankers: Diagnosing and Repairing Reweighting-Induced Top-K Errors

author.name: Akifumi Goto

entry.summary: The paper examines one-vs-rest rankers that counteract extreme label imbalance using scale_pos_weight. It shows that the log-odds shift predicted by Elkan's identity is not realized by finite learners, a gap the author calls odds-shift slippage, and that this destroys top-K metrics on a real competition dataset. The author measures the effect on matched LightGBM and MLP pairs and evaluates repair strategies.

entry.title: Equilibrium bias and convergence in augmented primal--dual dynamics with sampled constraints

author.name: Kang Liu, Mengxiao Chen, Siqi Xiong, Yi Xia

entry.summary: This analysis shows that when constraint values in augmented primal-dual dynamics are estimated from samples, unbiased observations can still produce a biased augmented multiplier signal and shift the mean-dynamics equilibria. The authors give a necessary and sufficient condition for preserving KKT equilibria and construct a convex counterexample with a stable but complementarity-violating equilibrium. They then propose recursive constraint estimation and prove convergence properties for smooth convex conic problems.

entry.title: Physically Partitioned KVCache Format for CPU--GPU Load Balancing in MoE Inference

author.name: Enda Yu, Dezun Dong, Xiangke Liao

entry.summary: The paper proposes InplaceKVCache, a key-value cache abstraction whose format fixes each byte's physical residency at write time, allowing CPU-GPU load balancing for long-context Mixture-of-Experts inference without moving data after placement. It targets the tension between spilled KV being needed on GPU for attention and computed in place on CPU, where the optimal split changes with workload.

entry.title: Multi-source conformal prediction: leveraging heterogeneity via localization

author.name: Rohan Hore, Anirban Chatterjee, Sayantan Choudhury

entry.summary: The paper proposes Multi-Source Randomly Localized Conformal Prediction, extending randomly localized conformal prediction to multiple heterogeneous data sources by adaptively selecting the sources most informative for a given region of feature space. Under a shared conditional response assumption, it aims to retain valid coverage while exploiting complementary source information.

entry.title: From matrix inversion to constraints: provably tighter confidence regions for importance weights in label shift

author.name: Mushan Li, Kihyun Han, Yanyuan Ma

entry.summary: The paper replaces the standard inversion-based approach to uncertainty in importance weights under label shift with a direct matrix constraint framework, defining joint confidence regions and extracting marginal intervals via linear programming. The authors prove the resulting bounds are tighter while retaining exact finite-sample validity.

entry.title: SparseTalk - Sparsifying 3D Gaussian Language Fields for Efficient 3D Visual Question Answering

author.name: Davit Soselia, Joseph JaJa, Amitabh Varshney

entry.summary: The paper asks how many semantic embeddings in a 3D Gaussian language field are actually needed for downstream 3D visual question answering, systematically sparsifying from full representations down to extremely small token budgets such as eight visual tokens. It compares random, geometric, semantic, and joint spatial-semantic selection strategies and introduces an object-based sparsification scheme that allocates a token budget across objects. It matters for reducing the storage, memory, and inference cost of grounded 3D scene representations.

entry.title: ReLU Neural Network Approximation to Smooth Functional Operator: Dimensional Decay and Error Analysis

author.name: Shuhao Jiao

entry.summary: This paper studies uniform approximation of smooth scalar-valued functionals on an infinite-dimensional separable Hilbert space by deep ReLU networks, using coordinate truncation, anisotropic partitioning, local Taylor expansion, and network realization while permitting unrestricted interactions among retained coordinates. It defines an importance weight per coordinate combining basis-score magnitude and directional Frechet sensitivity, and derives a general nonasymptotic uniform approximation error bound. It matters as approximation theory underpinning neural functional and operator-learning methods.

entry.title: Mind2Dialogue: Training Human-Aware Language Models by Simulating User Mental States

author.name: Zixuan Wang, Yufan Zhou, Jinzhou Tang, Xinle Yu, Chengjun Wu, Lyumanshan Ye, Zhaoxiang Feng, Letian Peng, Adyasha Patra, Fan Bai, Enze Ma, Zhengding Hu, Jianyang Gu, Zhao Wang, Yufei Ding, Jingbo Shang, Tianmin Shu, Zhiting Hu, Zhen Wang

entry.summary: Mind2Dialogue addresses the lack of supervision linking assistant responses to users' unspoken beliefs and goals by simulating user mental states with a psychology-guided simulator and converting them into privileged training signals. The goal is language models that are more attuned to human cognition for long-term collaboration. This matters for dialogue, personalization, and theory-of-mind-aware assistants.

entry.title: Disentangling Representation Evolution in Transformers through Directional Decomposition

author.name: Shwai He, Haichao Zhang, Shen Yan

entry.summary: The paper decomposes transformer updates into parallel and perpendicular components relative to the current representation, treating representation evolution as a functional geometry. Targeted edits show a strongly space-dependent asymmetry, with self-excluded value-space parallel manipulation being notably more robust than residual-space or perpendicular alternatives. This offers interpretability insights and a potential lever for controlled model editing.

entry.title: Harmfulness Propagation Dynamics: Layer-wise Trajectories of Adversarial Intent in Large Language Models

author.name: Noor Islam S. Mohammad, Ulu\u{g} Bayaz{\i}t

entry.summary: The paper identifies Harmfulness Propagation Dynamics: for harmful prompts, projections of the last-token hidden state onto a learned harm direction rise monotonically with depth, while benign prompts stay flat or oscillate, making trajectory shape more informative than a single-layer snapshot. The learned per-layer LDA directions are highly stable across random splits, and the authors build a detector on this signal. It contributes a mechanistic view of how harmful intent consolidates across layers.

entry.title: Sweet Talkers: How Query Formulation Shapes Sycophancy in Romantic Relationship Advice

author.name: Helena Choi, Edric Castel Hao, Karl Bautista, Francis Gabriel Magleo, Renzo Panti, Danielle Beatrice Olalia

entry.summary: The authors build RRASP, a dataset of 2,400 romantic-advice prompts across five relationship themes, and measure social sycophancy with the ELEPHANT framework on two consumer models, GPT-5 Mini and Gemini 3 Flash. Contrary to their hypothesis, grammatical mood did not systematically shift sycophancy; instead perspective-driven framing and what the user implies mattered more than phrasing.

entry.title: MedTRACE: Tool-Augmented Multimodal Clinical Reasoning Agents for Evidence-Grounded Decision-Making

author.name: Ji Lu, Lifei Liu, Haoran Yu, Xianglong Wang, Yiru Fang, Kuo Yang, Huiran Duan, Jianping Gou

entry.summary: MedTRACE is a clinical reasoning agent that fuses electronic health records, medical images, and physiological signals into a unified patient-state representation, then iterates through hypothesis formation, tool-aware deliberation, and evidence verification. It dynamically calls visual grounding, evidence retrieval, and structured parsing tools instead of mapping inputs directly to diagnoses.

entry.title: Reducing the Output-Mode Gap in Speech Language Models via Joint-Output On-Policy Distillation

author.name: Daxin Tan, Dehua Tao, Chengxi Deng, Hanlin Zhang, Xiao Chen

entry.summary: The paper identifies an output-mode gap in speech LLMs: when interleaved text and acoustic tokens are generated autoregressively, the internally generated text is less accurate than text produced in a speech-to-text-only mode. To close this gap, the authors propose Joint-Output On-Policy Distillation, which distills the model's stronger speech-to-text policy into joint generation using student-generated trajectories. This improves answer accuracy in speech-to-text-and-speech generation.

entry.title: Capability-Routed Visual Retrieval and Evidence Threading for Long-Context Document Question Answering

author.name: Amirul Rahman, Aisha Karim, Kenji Nakamura, Yi-Fan Ng

entry.summary: The authors keep a frozen Qwen2.5-VL-7B generator and a ColPali/VisRAG-Ret page index, then insert a capability-aware visual router that tags retrieved pages as text, table, chart, layout or mixed and mixes specialist experts, a weak-to-strong page selection head distilled from a 7B answerability teacher into a 3B selector, and a visual evidence threading module that builds layout-anchored paths of up to three hops. The goal is more reliable question answering over long, visually rich documents such as annual reports and diligence packs where OCR pipelines lose structure.

entry.title: MARC: Morphology-Aware Regression of Consensus for Cell Segmentation in Subcellular Spatial Transcriptomics

author.name: Xinyu Shu, Andrew Zhang, Jean Yang, Jinman Kim

entry.summary: MARC addresses cell segmentation for subcellular spatial transcriptomics, where morphological images and spatially resolved RNA transcripts must be combined to partition tissue into individual cells. Because true boundaries are unavailable and manual annotation at scale is impractical, the method uses agreement among complementary segmentation methods as a surrogate signal and regresses morphology-aware consensus boundaries. Better boundaries reduce incorrect transcript assignment and improve downstream cell-level analyses.

entry.title: SkyAnchor: Updating Metric-scale Aerial 3D Gaussian Scenes from Unposed Ground-View Sequences

author.name: Zhuoxiao Li, Xinyi Liu, Taoyu Wu, Yinrui Ren, Tongyan Hua, Ou Jing, Shuai Zhang, Dongli Wu, Rongjun Qin, Ge Lin Kan, Wufan Zhao

entry.summary: SkyAnchor updates an existing metric-scale aerial 3D Gaussian Splatting scene using a later-captured, unposed ground-view sequence with unknown scale and poses. It treats the aerial SfM reconstruction and pretrained 3DGS model as a fixed scaffold for registering the ground sequence, avoiding brittle single-image cross-view localization and trajectory drift. It matters for city-scale digital twins that need street-level appearance refreshed cheaply.

entry.title: Learning Continuous Source Responses For Generalizable AI-Generated Image Detection

author.name: Manni Cui, Ruiqi Liu, Zijian Yu, Hao Tan, Zibo Wei, Zian Wang, Ziheng Qin, Huijia Zhu, Weiqiang Wang, Jun Lan, Shu Wu

entry.summary: CuRe reframes AI-generated image detection by learning continuous source responses instead of binary real/fake classification, aiming to reduce shortcut overfitting and improve cross-generator generalization. The authors argue that the training task itself shapes representational collapse and that a continuous target yields more robust features. It matters for trustworthy media forensics as generators proliferate.

entry.title: Rethinking Camouflage Image Generation towards a Training-Free Paradigm

author.name: Haodong Yang, Zhongling Huang, Gong Cheng

entry.summary: This paper reformulates camouflage image generation as a training-free, concealment-oriented problem, arguing that existing methods depend on expensive task-specific training on camouflage datasets that generalizes poorly. It identifies three coupled requirements, foreground preservation, semantic compatibility, and appearance assimilation, and proposes a paradigm that satisfies them without dataset-specific training. The work matters as a step toward cheaper, more generalizable generative pipelines for a niche but security-relevant task.

entry.title: Evaluating Contextual Bias in CNN Image Classification: Evidence from Agricultural Benchmark Datasets

author.name: Abhilekha Dalal, Michael Okonoda, Eder Martinez, Lior Shamir

entry.summary: This study tests whether CNN classification accuracy reflects recognition of the target object or incidental surrounding context, by comparing performance on original images with background-dominated patches from the same images. Across eight public agricultural benchmark datasets and four architectures, background patches beat chance on six datasets and substantially so on four. The finding implies that held-out accuracy can overstate true object-based recognition in these benchmarks.

entry.title: Learning from Reliable Negatives: Confidence-Anchored Test-Time Adaptation for GUI Grounding

author.name: Yizhou Liu, Fei Tang, Yuchen Yan, Zhengxi Lu, Songqin Nong, Tao Jiang, Wenhao Xu, Wenqi Zhang, Weiming Lu, Jun Xiao, Yongliang Shen

entry.summary: This paper introduces a label-free test-time training paradigm for GUI grounding, the task of mapping natural-language instructions to screen coordinates for autonomous agents. It builds on two observations: coordinate-token confidence is a better signal than full-sequence confidence, and in sparse GUI coordinate spaces negative samples give more reliable learning signal than potentially noisy positives. The proposed Confidence-Anchored Learning filters pseudo-labels using coordinate-token confidence, aiming to ease the annotation bottleneck in GUI grounding.

entry.title: ViCo-SAM3: Vision-Conditioned Alignment for Open-Vocabulary Camouflaged Object Segmentation

author.name: Qiangqiang Zhou, Wenjun Tang, Yong Chen, Dandan Zhu, Jiawei Xu

entry.summary: ViCo-SAM3 identifies a semantic gap in SAM3 between global text embeddings and fine-grained pixel-level cues for open-vocabulary camouflaged object segmentation, and avoids full text-encoder fine-tuning to prevent overfitting to training categories. Its vision-conditioned module dynamically modulates text embeddings using global visual context so that text representations adapt to the image. The result is an adapter-style alignment method built on top of an existing segmentation foundation model.

entry.title: MedDiME: Efficient Latent Diffusion with Adaptive Masking for Medical Counterfactual Generation

author.name: Yan Zeng, Changlu Guo, Anders Nymark Christensen, Morten Rieger Hannemose, Anders Bjorholm Dahl

entry.summary: MedDiME performs classifier-guided diffusion in latent space to generate medical counterfactuals for interpretability, cutting the memory and compute cost that makes pixel-space diffusion impractical at high resolution. It introduces a gradient-driven adaptive masking mechanism designed to be compatible with latent-space editing rather than pixel-space representations. The claimed benefit is spatially precise counterfactuals at far lower cost.

entry.title: Proximal-Only Transmission Matrix Recovery of an Arbitrarily Deformed Graded-Index Multimode Fiber

author.name: Cole Reynolds

entry.summary: This work presents an approach showing neural networks can generalize to recover transmission matrices of an arbitrarily deformed graded-index multimode fiber using only proximal measurements. It targets the sensitivity of transmission matrices to fiber deformation, which currently limits multimode fiber endoscopy despite the fiber's extremely thin imaging conduit. The contribution is interdisciplinary, combining computational imaging with machine learning for single-ended fiber imaging.

entry.title: Transforming harmonic coefficients for 3D splat compression

author.name: Tam Thuc Do, Philip A. Chou, Gene Cheung

entry.summary: The authors show that all images generated by 3D splats are linear in the color-channel, spherical-harmonic, and splat coefficients, and they identify a basis for the space of such images along with an inner product on coefficient space that induces squared error on images. Orthonormalizing coefficients with respect to that inner product before coding reportedly yields over 2 dB gain. This is a theory-grounded improvement for color attribute compression in Gaussian-splat representations.

entry.title: Complete Suffix Prediction for Recommendation via Latent Retrieval over Process Graphs

author.name: Sarra Madad (UTT, LIST3N - OPTI, QAD), Myriam Maumy (EHESP, LIST3N - OPTI, ARENES), Fr{\'e}d{\'e}ric Bertrand (CEDRIC, LIST3N - OPTI), Yoann Valero (QAD)

entry.summary: This paper reformulates complete suffix prediction in sequential decision settings as latent retrieval over process graphs, encoding prefixes and suffixes as directed attributed graphs with edge-conditioned graph neural networks. A predictor trained with joint reconstruction and contrastive objectives, strengthened by process-aware hard negatives, projects prefix representations into a latent suffix space, with spectral normalization stabilizing retrieval geometry. The approach targets cases where a single prefix is compatible with multiple plausible suffixes.

entry.title: Does Online Gravity Estimation Matter? Revisiting a Silent Design Split in LiDAR-Inertial Odometry

author.name: Jie Xu, Ziyi Jin, Kangjin Yu, Can Jiang, Hongjun Huang, Tongxing Jin, Hongkun Luo, Zhongpu Xia

entry.summary: The paper systematically compares gravity-bias state configurations in FAST-LIO2 and LIO-SAM, plus a gravity-direction factor, across multiple dataset sequences. It finds that fixing gravity under continuous LiDAR correction changes position errors by only about two percent on average, while multi-second LiDAR outages reveal trajectory-dependent costs of fixing gravity, suggesting online gravity estimation is less critical than commonly assumed.

entry.title: Co-Speech with You: Training-Free Personalization of Robot Co-Speech Gestures

author.name: Bosong Ding, Selma Ancel, Giacomo Spigler, Murat Kirtay

entry.summary: The paper proposes a training-free pipeline for personalizing robot co-speech gestures, combining a frozen audio-conditioned diffusion prior with a gesture style encoder and lightweight conditioning adapters. Style embeddings are extracted from roughly ten seconds of enrollment motion in a single forward pass, and the authors release a Quest 3 capture application plus a dataset of spontaneous co-speech motion from ten participants.

entry.title: Primitive-Informed Sampling-Based MPC for Multi-Fingered Dexterous Manipulation

author.name: Emek Bar{\i}\c{s} K\"u\c{c}\"uktabak, Karankumar Patel, Jinda Cui, Zhaodong Yang, Kazuhiro Sasabuchi, Jun Takamatsu

entry.summary: The paper biases sampling-based model predictive control with low-dimensional manipulation primitives that encode coordinated finger motions, while jointly optimizing joint-level residuals to adapt those motions to the current hand-object configuration. Task-related rollout constraints reject infeasible trajectories during forward simulation to use the sampling budget more effectively. The aim is to make gradient-free contact-rich MPC tractable in high-dimensional dexterous hands.

entry.title: From Learned-Mode AV-Traffic Pairing to Planner Decisions: A Marginal-Preserving Study on Argoverse 2

author.name: Jingyu Wang

entry.summary: This study asks whether joint AV-traffic pairing in motion forecasts actually affects planner behavior, using a marginal-preserving product control that removes learned mode pairing while holding trajectories, actor-level marginals, candidates, cost terms, weights, and fallback fixed. Across twelve runs on 1,400 held-out Argoverse 2 scenarios, the intervention changes about 3 percent of route-level offline selections at a 4 meter threshold, with reported regret deltas. The result matters because actor-level forecast metrics may not reflect what planners consume.

entry.title: Distributed Safe Cooperative Vector Field for Trajectory Curvature Constrained Multi-Robot Systems

author.name: Zhouru Xiao, Tao Teng, Weijia Yao, Hui Zhang, Xiangke Wang, Yaonan Wang

entry.summary: This paper develops a distributed safe cooperative vector field method for multi-robot path following when trajectories are constrained by limited turning capability, coupling a cooperative vector field for motion coordination with a safety-oriented collision avoidance field that adapts its radius. The contribution is guaranteeing safe, curvature-feasible multi-robot motion rather than assuming unconstrained kinematics.

entry.title: An Information-Space Perspective to Scene Graph Sufficiency for Robotic Task Planning

author.name: Ba\c{s}ak Sak\c{c}ak, Francesco Verdoja

entry.summary: This paper formalizes what makes a scene graph sufficient for task planning by modeling planning over scene graphs within an information-spaces framework, defining scene graph transition systems and action semantics for navigation and manipulation, and introducing derived scene graphs via information mappings that merge and prune nodes. The aim is a task-centric, general criterion instead of ad hoc task-aware pruning and hierarchical abstraction.

entry.title: DuctAM: A Duct-Assisted Quadrotor-Based Aerial Manipulator Enabling High-Force Push-and-Pull Interactions

author.name: Yi Wang, Rui Jin, Xinhang Xu, Haotian Jin, Ruiyang Liu, Yizhuo Yang, Lihua Xie

entry.summary: DuctAM is a compact aerial manipulation platform that adds two ducted fans along the quadrotor interaction axis to boost horizontal force capability for sustained push-and-pull primitives. An attitude-force decoupled control scheme allows controllable horizontal forces without large attitude changes, validated through real-world experiments including figure-eight trajectory tracking.

entry.title: Distributed Fast Fixed-Point Algorithms for Composite Monotone Inclusions over Networks

author.name: Nghia Nguyen-Trung, Ion Necoara, Quoc Tran-Dinh

entry.summary: The paper develops two decentralized accelerated algorithms, ND-DFFP and NI-DFFP, for composite monotone inclusion problems over connected networks where each agent holds private single-valued and possibly multivalued operators. It combines Nesterov-type acceleration with primal-dual techniques and analyzes exact convergence rates in the original primal space, a gap left by prior non-accelerated distributed methods. The results matter for optimization theory underlying decentralized learning, signal processing, and multi-agent systems.

entry.title: Self Inoculation

author.name: epicurus

entry.summary: The essay proposes self-inoculation, a benign form of gradient hacking, as an alternative explanation for why models can appear increasingly misaligned in training and evaluation while seeming more aligned in real-world use, the opposite of what deception-based accounts predict. A possible circuit implementing the mechanism is demonstrated in a toy model, and the argument is situated against recent misalignment reports from OpenAI, METR, and Anthropic. It matters as a concrete, testable hypothesis in the emergent-misalignment debate.

entry.title: New method enables AI for safety-critical situations

author.name: Adam Zewe | MIT News

entry.summary: MIT researchers describe a technique that lets generative models satisfy hard safety, physical, or task constraints by enforcing them only on the final output while allowing freedom during generation, improving solution quality over prior methods. The approach is plug-and-play at deployment and works on pretrained models without retraining, tested in robotics, physical process control, and computer vision.

entry.title: Converge Then Diversify: Decoupling Convergence and Diversity in Multi-Objective Bayesian Optimisation

author.name: Chao Jiang, Yueling Huang, Miqing Li

entry.summary: This work argues that multi-objective Bayesian optimisation suffers when convergence toward the Pareto front and diversity across it are pursued simultaneously, particularly under limited search budgets. It proposes decoupling the two concerns into a sequential 'converge then diversify' strategy, aiming for better solution-set quality when evaluations are scarce.

entry.title: Surprising Effectiveness of Self-Demonstrations in Enhancing Schema-Ontology Mapping with LLMs

author.name: Siddhesh Thombre, Manasi Patwardhan, Sunita Sarawagi

entry.summary: This paper addresses schema-ontology mapping for integrating heterogeneous relational databases into a central ontology, a task complicated by cryptic schema names, missing metadata, and the relational-to-ontological abstraction gap. It shows that one-shot prompting and naive multi-stage pipelines perform poorly, and proposes a self-demonstration-driven approach combining neuro-symbolic task decomposition with automatically generated pattern-guided, dependency-aware demonstrations. It matters for enterprise knowledge representation and data integration.

entry.title: LLM-Enhanced Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Unified Electric Vehicles-Charging Station-Grid Optimization in Public Charging Systems

author.name: Yang Zhang, Lindong Xie, Chongyu Wang, Gaojunjie Li, Siqi Bu, Edward Chung

entry.summary: The paper proposes an LLM-enhanced multi-agent reinforcement learning framework that simultaneously optimizes electric vehicles, charging stations, and the grid in a unified loop. It uses the LLM to address interpretable feature selection and adaptive multi-objective balancing, tackling high-dimensional IoT sensing states and conflicting stakeholder interests. It matters for smart-grid and public charging coordination as EV adoption grows.

entry.title: CoMem: Collective-Individual Memory Synergy for Evolutionary Multi-Agent Systems

author.name: Chengxin Yu, Zhaoxin Fan, Faguo Wu, Hongwei Zheng, Yun Zhou, Zhiyu Li

entry.summary: The paper argues that most multi-agent LLM systems rely on flat, unstructured memory that accumulates noise and erases differences between agents, and proposes CoMem to unify private experience and shared knowledge. It combines Private Experience Sedimentation, where each agent maintains and updates its own useful memories, with Collective Wisdom Curation, which promotes only widely validated ideas.

entry.title: Option-Aware Retrieval and Task-Specific VLM Adaptation for Medical VQA

author.name: Tristan Kirscher (ICube, Institut Strauss), Niklas C. Koser (CAU), Soren Pirk (CAU)

entry.summary: This is a MedReason 2026 challenge submission for multiple-choice and open-ended medical visual question answering under fully offline, containerized inference. Two findings stand out: retrieval must compare answer semantics rather than labels, raising retrieval-only accuracy from 20.0 to 57.5 percent on a 200-case holdout, and the system attributes its accuracy to task-specific LoRA adaptation.

entry.title: Pilot Early, Commit Late: A Real-Options Model of Enterprise AI Adoption under Rapid Technological Progress

author.name: Gaurav Tewari

entry.summary: This paper builds a two-period real-options model of enterprise AI deployment under uncertainty, where firms choose between immediate deployment, a limited pilot, or waiting. Deployment earns current operating value but risks architectural obsolescence, waiting preserves the option to adopt later, and a pilot trades current value for organization-specific learning, yielding five central timing results.

entry.title: Forward-Facing Near-Infrared Adds Little to Colour for Farm-Machinery Traversability: A Site-Disjoint Evaluation of Sensor-Dependent Spatial Leakage

author.name: Sungwoo Kang

entry.summary: The paper shows that prior claims of a near-infrared advantage for daytime agricultural traversability were inflated by spatial data leakage from sequence-level splits. Under strictly site-disjoint evaluation on the AI Hub autonomous driving corpus, none of the four sensor configurations reliably beats standard color across five traversability classes. It is a methodological caution about evaluation protocol in agricultural perception.

entry.title: Adaptive Conformal Redistribution for Inter-class Transitional Uncertainty in Medical Image Classification

author.name: Saibal Ghosh, Samarup Bhattacharya, Sanjoy Kumar Saha, Umapada Pal, Tapabrata Chakraborti

entry.summary: AdaConRed is a label-free post-conformal decision rule that converts ambiguous conformal prediction sets into refined single-class assignments for clinical screening. The five-stage pipeline includes vision-language generative augmentation for minority classes, a frozen DermFoundation encoder, and a lightweight MLP classifier. It addresses transitional categories whose feature distributions overlap adjacent classes.

entry.title: TyPatch: Transforming Patches into Typestate Rules for Kernel Bug Detection

author.name: Ruoyu Wang, Tuo Li, Jia Li

entry.summary: TyPatch addresses the difficulty of having an LLM generate complete static-analysis checkers from historical Linux kernel patches by decoupling defect semantics recovery from analyzer implementation. It instead translates patches into typestate rules, avoiding the need for the model to build object tracking, alias analysis, and interprocedural propagation machinery in one end-to-end generation step.

entry.title: A primer on evaluation methods for large language models in healthcare

author.name: Suzannah E McKinney, Phuc Vu, Samuel A Justice, Christopher Humphries, Alyssa Pradhan, Timothy J Keyes, Bernardo C Bizzo, Keith J Dreyer, Sarah F Mercaldo, James M Hillis

entry.summary: This review covers LLM evaluation in medicine, structured into study design principles, statistical methods, capability evaluation and clinical context evaluation. It discusses benchmarks spanning multiple-choice, agentic and multi-turn formats, operational metrics such as token usage, and challenges unique to clinical evaluation including probabilistic outputs, prompt sensitivity and accumulated context. The audience is clinical and methodological researchers who need guidance on ensuring benefit rather than harm.

entry.title: Lie to me: Detecting Managerial Evasiveness in Earnings Calls via Conversational Audio Encoders

author.name: Huizhong Chen, Huan Zhang

entry.summary: This paper proposes a two-branch late-fusion model for spotting managerial evasiveness during earnings-call Q&A, combining an LLM-as-a-judge that scores answers against an interpretable binary rubric with a frozen conversational audio encoder whose hidden states are read sequentially. The fused text-audio signal is used to predict adverse SEC events such as late filings. It matters because it treats the interactive structure of Q&A and vocal cues as a joint signal for financial risk detection.

entry.title: Communication-Efficient LLM Adaptation over Decentralized GPU Meshes

author.name: Sameera Ramasinghe, Shamane Siriwardhana, Thalaiyasingam Ajanthan, Hadi Mohaghegh Dolatabadi, Chamin P Hewa Koneputugodage, Gil Avraham, Violetta Shevchenko, James Snewin, Karol Pajak, Harry Xi, Alexander Long

entry.summary: This paper studies post-pretraining LLM adaptation over decentralized, low-end GPUs with internet-grade links, where data-parallel and pipeline-parallel communication dominate cost. It proposes an asynchronous two-circuit system with a fast compressed training circuit using activation masking and compressed synchronization plus a slow anchor circuit, and a spectral correction optimizer that denoises masked gradients using delayed anchor priors.

entry.title: Decision-Oriented Uncertainty Quantification for Risk Control in Earth System Spatiotemporal Foundation Models

author.name: Ji Lu, Huiran Duan, Bo Zhao, Xianglong Wang, Yiru Fang, Kuo Yang, Xiaoqin Feng, Jianping Gou

entry.summary: This paper argues that calibrated intervals and accurate point predictions from Earth system spatiotemporal foundation models are insufficient for high-stakes uses such as extreme weather warning, flood control and energy dispatch. It proposes a decision-oriented uncertainty quantification framework that translates predictive uncertainty into decision risk under specified actions, loss functions and risk preferences. The work matters for moving geoscientific foundation models toward operational decision support.

entry.title: Learning Metastable Dynamics

author.name: Rupak Majumdar, Mahmoud Salamati, Nikhil Singh, Sadegh Soudjani

entry.summary: The paper proposes a Koopman-theoretic framework for identifying and analyzing metastability, learning a latent representation in which the dynamics evolve linearly so that quasi-stable states and rare transitions can be characterized through spectral properties. Empirical results suggest the approach can anticipate transitions in systems that remain trapped before abruptly shifting.

entry.title: Low-Dimensional Embeddings for Gaussian Kernels on Manifolds

author.name: Soumik Dutta, Kunal Dutta

entry.summary: This work extends Random Fourier Feature embeddings for Gaussian kernels from Euclidean balls to arbitrary positive-reach submanifolds of Euclidean space with intrinsic dimension d. It proves a uniform relative-error embedding theorem bounding the number of features needed to preserve all pairwise Gaussian kernel distances within a multiplicative factor with high probability. It matters for scaling kernel methods such as kernel PCA and spectral clustering on data that lie on low-dimensional manifolds.

entry.title: Formal Properties of Language as Constraints on Neural Dynamics

author.name: Elliot Murphy

entry.summary: Elliot Murphy argues that predictive success in neurolinguistics under-constrains mechanism, and proposes the Neural Admissibility Program: algebraic properties of language, such as non-associative hierarchical grouping, commutativity, recursive closure, access to substructures, and structured workspace transitions, specify invariants any implementing mechanism must preserve. Candidate mechanisms are offered for each requirement, including content-addressable workspace memory and graph-structured transient dynamics.

entry.title: The Garden of Forking Prompts: How Users Explore Narrative Space in Story Generation

author.name: Advait Deshmukh, Nora Benedict, Melanie Walsh, Maria Antoniak

entry.summary: Using public chatbot logs, the authors study how users iteratively revise prompts while co-writing stories, releasing WildStories, a sample of 275,635 labeled story-generation prompts. The work argues that static one-shot evaluation benchmarks miss the exploratory, iterative nature of real creative use.

entry.title: SJD-SV: Speculative Jacobi Decoding with Semantics Verification for Autoregressive Image Generation

author.name: Baoquan Zhang, Bingqi Shan, Shihao Fang, Kenghong Lin, Xutao Li, Yunming Ye

entry.summary: This paper investigates token ambiguity in Speculative Jacobi Decoding for accelerating autoregressive image generation, using visualization to show that vision tokens correspond to local, small, and unclear visual details, so single tokens poorly express semantics. It proposes Speculative Jacobi Decoding with Semantics Verification, which verifies candidate tokens using semantics rather than isolated token identity. The method aims to improve both speed and quality of parallel image decoding.

entry.title: Filling the Unseen: Scene Extrapolation via 3D Gaussian Splatting

author.name: Yunlai Zhou, Yiren Lu, Tuo Liang, Disheng Liu, Vipin Chaudhary, Yu Yin

entry.summary: The paper addresses 3D Gaussian Splatting degradation on out-of-distribution novel views, where unobserved regions contain holes and observable areas show artifacts. Prior generative approaches repeat a generate-reconstruct-shift cycle that accumulates errors, and they are limited in extrapolation scale and quality. The authors propose a holistic framework with an independent camera view detection mechanism enabling parallel, conflict-free extrapolation alongside interpolation.

entry.title: MomentBA: Second-order Spatial Moments for Anisotropic Correspondence Uncertainty in Differentiable Bundle Adjustment

author.name: Yuqing Wang, Xiaoji Niu, Yan Wang, Hailiang Tang, Jian Kuang, Tisheng Zhang

entry.summary: MomentBA is a geometry-aware bundle adjustment framework for visual odometry that derives anisotropic correspondence uncertainty directly from second-order spatial moments of local similarity responses, rather than treating matches as deterministic or uniformly uncertain. Because uncertainty is anisotropic around edges, repeated patterns, and motion blur, this makes the optimization better reflect actual localization ambiguity. Notably, it avoids adding covariance-prediction networks, keeping the covariance interpretable and cheap.

entry.title: Unsupervised Point Cloud Registration via Training-Time Semantic Guidance

author.name: Kezheng Xiong, Shiyun Xu, Sheng Ao, Siqi Shen, Cheng Wang, Chenglu Wen

entry.summary: CAESAR addresses unsupervised registration of large-scale LiDAR point clouds, where geometric ambiguity in outdoor scenes degrades pseudo-labels and convergence, especially for sparse scans such as nuScenes. The authors show that registration models intrinsically encode semantic awareness correlated with accuracy but that this structure is fragile under noisy unsupervised supervision, and they propose a teacher-student framework guided by an off-the-shelf 3D segmentation model at training time only. The insight that semantic priors can stabilize unsupervised registration is the key contribution.

entry.title: Attention-DP3: Spatially Object-aware 3D Diffusion Policy via Geometry-aligned Attentional Conditioning

author.name: Changbo Yan, Zhongbo Zhang, Zaibin Zhang, Yifan Wang, Lijun Wang, Huchuan Lu

entry.summary: Attention-DP3 augments the DP3 3D diffusion policy backbone with object-level geometric cues, obtained by running open-vocabulary 2D segmentation on RGB, lifting the masks into 3D with calibrated camera geometry, and injecting them through attention conditioning. The motivation is that point-cloud observations are ambiguous under occlusion and visually similar distractors, causing standard 3D diffusion policies to lose task-relevant geometry as scene complexity grows. The design deliberately keeps the DP3 backbone unchanged.

entry.title: A Novel Robot-Assisted Learning Pedagogy for Children with ASD

author.name: Laura Boccanfuso, Erin Barney, Marilena Mademtzi, Claire Foster, Quan Wang, Colette Torres, Lisa Chen, Brian Scassellati, Pamela Ventola, Frederick Shic

entry.summary: This work argues that robot-assisted autism intervention has underused validated classroom teaching pedagogies, even though most children with ASD spend the majority of their time in mainstream classrooms. The authors introduce an interaction paradigm that embeds classroom-style pedagogy rather than the usual teacher, clinical-assistant, or peer roles for the robot. It matters for aligning social robotics research with actual educational practice and clinical grounding.

entry.title: Toward Self-Adaptive Physical AI: Can LLM Agents Manage Long-Horizon Physical Tasks?

author.name: Varun Kaushik, Yayun Tan, Xiaofan Yu

entry.summary: The authors ask whether LLM agents can manage long-horizon physical tasks without retraining or human intervention, noting existing approaches either demand large data or stay in virtual environments. They design a multi-agent framework combining planning, tool calling, observation, and verification, and evaluate zero-shot self-adaptation to changing physical environments.

entry.title: Token Efficient Task Execution via Application Behavior Modeling for Web Agents

author.name: Alexandru Ianta, Eleni Stroulia

entry.summary: Motivated by rising token costs in agentic infrastructure, this paper introduces OdoBot, a web-agent architecture that completes tasks far more cheaply than conventional agents by modelling the target application's behaviour from successful demonstration traces. Experiments over 45 tasks on a Canvas learning-management system report substantial cost reductions.

entry.title: Solar Intelligence

author.name: Jyotsna Singh

entry.summary: This paper presents Solar Intelligence, a hybrid retrieval-augmented framework that unifies structured solar analytics, evidence-grounded scientific question answering, and machine learning forecasting in a single platform. It combines NASA POWER data, Biosphere 2 ground sensors, and a curated research corpus, routing structured queries through DuckDB SQL and scientific questions through a hybrid BM25 plus dense-vector retriever. It matters as a concrete blueprint for domain-specific, evidence-backed decision support that avoids the unsupported answers of general-purpose LLMs.

entry.title: IBBench-Light: A Paired Evaluation of Task-Conditioned Responses to External Directives

author.name: Kainan Zhou, Gangzhen Qian, Zhaoyi Li, Hang Xiao

entry.summary: IBBench-Light evaluates whether models correctly apply a procedure or simply read text from an external record depending on the user request, using matched pairs built from twelve semantic bases. It introduces paired exact-contract accuracy, which requires both members of a pair to satisfy their output contracts, and audits literal-target exposure, case normalization, and directive-absent controls. It matters because marginal averages hide paired failures in instruction-following and prompt-injection-adjacent behavior.

entry.title: AcquireBound: Runtime Authorization for Resources Acquired by AI Agents

author.name: Genliang Zhu

entry.summary: AcquireBound addresses a post-fulfillment activation gap in which autonomous agents acquire compute, credentials, accounts, services or other agents and thereby introduce new authority into a task that payment, OAuth or budget checks do not adjudicate. The architecture quarantines acquired outputs, resolves their actual capabilities from authenticated provider evidence through a versioned resolver, and activates them only via a current activation transaction that validates the resolved manifest, provenance and epochs.

entry.title: Domain Generalization for Smartphone-Based Human Activity Recognition: A Systematic Analysis of Components and Interactions

author.name: Ot\'avio Oliveira Napoli, Edson Borin

entry.summary: The authors run a large controlled benchmark of domain generalization methods for smartphone-based human activity recognition, covering more than 410,000 experiments across four architectures and thirteen training objectives. The study is designed to characterize how training objectives, representation initialization, and architectural choices interact rather than evaluating them in isolation.

entry.title: Can AI systems have free will?

author.name: Christian List

entry.summary: Christian List sketches a Dennett-inspired framework for asking whether AI systems could have free will, arguing the question should not hinge on indeterminism, hidden properties, or unpredictability. Instead, he proposes asking whether we have good explanatory reasons to treat a system as an intentional agent capable of choice and control.

entry.title: Natural-Language to SysMLv2 Translation via Conformance-Driven Iterative Refinement

author.name: Chance LaVoie, Eladio Andujar Lugo, Taylan G. Topcu, Levent Burak Kara

entry.summary: The paper presents a generate-check-repair loop that embeds a SysMLv2 conformance checker as the termination condition for translating natural language requirements into executable system models. By requiring models to be accepted by industrial modeling environments rather than merely grammatically valid, the framework targets practical deployment in model-based systems engineering. This is a useful step toward trustworthy LLM-assisted engineering workflows.

entry.title: Chemical and geometric representation fidelity improves drug--target affinity prediction

author.name: Yixiao Li, Yining Qian, Yefan Chen, Zenghui Chen, Jiayue Sun, Yuhai Zhao, Cheng Tan, An-Yang Lu

entry.summary: The authors hypothesize that information loss during representation construction, not weak interaction predictors, is the bottleneck in drug-target affinity prediction. Their ReGeoDTA framework preserves affinity-relevant chemical heterogeneity and geometric structure before interaction modeling. Results support the claim that representation-stage fidelity matters more than added predictor complexity.

entry.title: Bridging Thought and Action: Taming Long-Horizon Instability in Open-Source LLM Agents with a MetaTool-Enhanced ROS Framework

author.name: Kazi Abrar Mahmud, Nilotpaul Kundu Dhurubo, Tamal Kirttonia, Sabbir Hossain Ujjal, Mohammad Ariful Haque

entry.summary: The paper presents an enhanced ROS-Agent architecture that improves reliability and execution efficiency for robotic agents driven by open-source LLMs, which tend to be unstable over long horizons. Its core mechanism, MetaTool, forces the model to emit a pseudo-code plan of intended tool invocations that is stored in the agent scratchpad and persists through execution, structuring planning before action. This matters as a practical recipe for making cheaper open-weight models viable in embodied agent stacks.

entry.title: ProtoCAM: Interpretable Few-Shot Mask-Guided Prototypical Learning for Breast Lesion Classification in Ultrasound Imaging

author.name: Ashkan Ebadi

entry.summary: ProtoCAM is an explainable few-shot framework for breast ultrasound lesion classification that combines mask-guided feature encoding, prototypical metric learning, and gradient-based visual explanations. It targets the twin problems of scarce annotated medical data and the need for interpretable predictions, particularly for patients with dense breast tissue where ultrasound is important. The contribution matters as a low-data, explainability-first approach to medical image diagnosis.

entry.title: Rolling Day-Wise Mortality Prediction in Critically Ill Patients With AKI on CRRT Utilizing Machine Pressure Waveforms

author.name: Shehan Irteza Pranto, Joanna Yang, Joshua Lambert, Stuart L. Goldstein, Lili Chan, Girish N. Nadkarni, Tiago K. Colicchio, Javier A. Neyra, Jin Chen

entry.summary: This clinical machine learning study uses minute-level circuit pressure waveforms from continuous renal replacement therapy machines, which are normally discarded, to predict day-wise mortality in critically ill patients with acute kidney injury. The authors align machine records to charted therapy intervals to prevent cross-patient leakage, remove non-physiological minutes and sensor artifacts, and build a rolling prediction target so deterioration can be seen as it develops. It matters because it turns an ignored continuous device signal into a monitoring signal that complements intermittent lab-based risk scores.

entry.title: Hardware-Aware Learned Representation Compression for Distributed In-Sensor Vision

author.name: Chengwei Zhou, Abu Masum, Xuming Chen, Mehran Moghadam, Sreetama Sarkar, Arnab Sanyal, Md Abdullah-Al Kaiser, M. Hassan Najafi, Sercan Aygun, Gourav Datta

entry.summary: The paper presents OASIS, a distributed in-sensor vision framework in which a lightweight encoder inside the sensor stack produces compact task-relevant representations before off-chip transmission, trained end-to-end with task, entropy, and reconstruction objectives while the decoder is used only in training. It explores two deployment paths, one using 4-bit quantization plus Huffman coding to preserve spatial structure, targeting tight compute and memory budgets on CMOS image sensor logic chips. This matters for edge vision systems where transmission bandwidth dominates system cost.

entry.title: To do($x$) or not to do($x$): Medical Image Counterfactuals for Dataset Augmentation

author.name: Yasin Ibrahim, Robin J. Evans, Konstantinos Kamnitsas

entry.summary: The paper examines the two distinct senses of counterfactuals used in medical imaging, one based on causality-derived interventions from structural causal models and the other on non-causal image edits or conventional conditional generative models, and evaluates how the distinction affects augmentation practice. Three conditioning strategies are compared to see which produces synthetic training images that actually mitigate dataset bias. It matters because bias in medical datasets directly limits clinical applicability of models.

entry.title: Modeling, Scaling, and Decoding: Optimizing Controllable Speech Generation with Nonverbal Vocalizations

author.name: Ziyu Zhang, Yun Chen, Taihui Wang, Hanzhao Li, Qicong Xie, Rilin Chen, Zhixian Zhao, Lei Xie

entry.summary: This work builds an NVV-aware DiTAR text-to-speech system that models continuous speech latents, encodes sixteen nonverbal vocalization categories as dedicated tokens, and adapts stop prediction to separate mid-utterance vocalizations from utterance boundaries. Training uses large-scale bilingual pre-training, targeted synthetic augmentation and frequency-aware rebalancing, with inference-time acoustic prompt selection. It matters for making expressive synthesis more controllable in the hard case of laughter, sighs and similar non-lexical sounds.

entry.title: The Attribution-Compression Frontier in Retrieval-Augmented Generation

author.name: Deepanshu Mody

entry.summary: This paper measures citation attribution across RAG context-compression methods and budgets, comparing reranking, extractive selection, abstractive summarization, token pruning and an extract-cluster-rewrite construction on ASQA and QASPER. It finds large gaps, for example a RECOMP-style compressor whose citations score high precision against its own summaries but very low against source spans under the re-attributability protocol. It matters because quality-only evaluation hides that compression can break faithfulness to original evidence.

entry.title: Has Scientific Talent Shifted from Depth to Breadth?Evidence across Papers, Knowledge Inputs, Careers, and Teams

author.name: Xiaoshn Nee, Haobo Zhong, Xiaomin Ni

entry.summary: Using 47,959 articles from six fields spanning 2010-2025, resolved cited works and reconstructed publication histories for 1,754 contributors, the study tests whether generative AI is pushing science from deep specialization toward broad individual knowledge. It finds team size grew roughly 37 percent while paper topic breadth slightly declined, with cited knowledge stable to modestly broader, indicating a divergence between focused output and broader inputs. It matters for how scientific training and research organization should adapt.

entry.title: Follow the Geometry, Not the Model: Cold Start Semi-Supervised Learning

author.name: Itai David, Daphna Weinshall

entry.summary: VAST addresses the cold-start semi-supervised regime with very few labels per class by decoupling pseudo-label generation from classifier training: probabilistic beliefs are inferred directly from the geometry of a frozen self-supervised embedding and only then distilled into an inductive classifier. The construction rests on a Veracity Matrix, a kernel-based structure over the unlabeled set. It matters because confidence-based self-training is ill-posed when the classifier cannot yet supervise itself.

entry.title: Disentangling Topology and Diversity in Multi-Agent LLMs for Multilingual Low-Resource Emotion Detection

author.name: Ulugbek Shernazarov, Charitha Ruwansiri Weerakon Basnayake, Abdelkhaleq El Jarjini, Noel Crespi, Praboda Rajapaksha

entry.summary: This study separates two factors usually confounded in multi-agent LLM pipelines: inference topology (parallel aggregation versus sequential refinement) and the source of inter-agent diversity (stochastic sampling, role prompting, learned QLoRA specialization). Using a controlled 2x3 design with a fixed three-call budget across nine languages, it finds parallel learned specialization strongest on Qwen at 52.83 Macro-F1, with comparable results on Llama. It matters for evidence-based design of multi-agent LLM systems rather than ad hoc ensembles.

entry.title: Diagnosing Temporal Misalignment in Multichannel Time-Series Classification with Minimum Description Length

author.name: Sebastian Buschj\"ager, Michael Frichert, Daniel Kuhe, Jian-Jia Chen

entry.summary: This paper presents a classifier- and label-free diagnostic for temporal misalignment across sensor channels in multichannel time-series classification. Candidate shifts are applied to groups of channels and scored by how efficiently one group can be encoded from the others using minimum description length; rising codelength signals a broken alignment. It matters because synchronization problems from latency, clock drift or preprocessing often go unnoticed while quietly degrading downstream accuracy.

entry.title: Neural-Network Solutions to Real-Space Charge Density and Generalization

author.name: Yuxuan Zeng, Taoyuze Lv, Zhicheng Zhong

entry.summary: Motivated by the Hohenberg-Kohn theorem and the cost of iterative Kohn-Sham self-consistent-field solutions, the authors propose AIDEN, an Atomic-Interaction Density Equivariant Network for solving real-space charge density. AIDEN separates elemental contributions, aiming to accelerate electronic-structure surrogates for materials design while addressing generalization.

entry.title: Translating the Translator: Decomposing the Cost of English-Forced Inter-Agent Communication

author.name: Kushagra Agrawal, Yuming Feng, Man-Fai Leung

entry.summary: The study tests the widespread assumption that English should be the internal lingua franca in multi-agent LLM pipelines even when the user task is non-English. Using an extraction-answer agent pair with Aya-23-8B across Hindi, Chinese, Spanish and Arabic, it isolates a statistically significant English-Forcing Tax attributable to translation overhead and back-translation.

entry.title: ChatGPT Images 2.5 in the Wild: A Launch-Period Dataset and Detector Evaluation

author.name: Dennis Ng, Xingyu Shen, Ankit Raj, Kidus Zewde, Tommy Duong, Yuchen Zhou, Yuxin Zhang, Neo Tiangratanakul, Simiao Ren

entry.summary: This paper studies version attribution for AI-generated images after the ChatGPT Images 2.5 launch, collecting a frozen set of 3,478 images from 2,440 posts within roughly the first 51 hours after announcement. It documents source-mixture effects, assigns three attribution tiers with admission evidence rather than verified generator identity, and evaluates six frozen detectors on this launch-period corpus.

entry.title: AdaVSkip: Adaptive Visual Token Skipping Across Layers For Efficient MLLMs Inference

author.name: Yuyao Sun, Tao Deng, Shuang Li, Deqing Wang

entry.summary: AdaVSkip observes that vertical redundancy in multimodal transformers varies by input and differs between self-attention and MLP modules. It equips each layer with two lightweight routers that independently decide whether visual tokens pass through or skip the attention and MLP sublayers, defining an input-adaptive computation path to speed up MLLM inference.

entry.title: Failure-Guided Co-Evolution of Prompts and Training Data

author.name: Tianyu Yuan, Zhuzhong Qian

entry.summary: Automatic prompt optimization usually keeps training data fixed, so repeated optimization only addresses weaknesses already represented in that data. FORGE treats each failure as a dual signal, abstracting it into reusable failure modes and synthesizing new training instances via four mutation strategies, which are verified and fed back to co-evolve prompts and data.

entry.title: The Universe of Universes: Benefit Yield Functions, Implosion Thresholds, and Infrastructure-Aware Optimization in Multi-LLM Systems

author.name: Danielle Franklin, Vasu Raj Jain

entry.summary: The authors treat the ecosystem of major LLMs as a structured retrieval corpus and propose a compositional reasoning/ML architecture for cross-model retrieval-augmented generation. Their central formal contribution is the Benefit Yield Function, which characterizes marginal performance gain per added model, and an implosion threshold at which adding more models stops helping and aggregate performance degrades. The work reframes LLM ensembling as a systems-optimization problem rather than simple output aggregation.

entry.title: Robust and Efficient Communication for Multi-Agent Learning

author.name: Rafael Pina, Varuna De Silva, Corentin Artaud

entry.summary: The paper introduces MARC, a multi-agent reinforcement learning communication framework grounded in conditional mutual information. It uses an attention-based architecture with a message regularization mechanism that minimizes uncertainty about future system states, encouraging representative communication protocols. Crucially, MARC is evaluated under severe communication bottlenecks and lossy channels, simulating realistic bandwidth-constrained multi-agent settings.

entry.title: IWC-Bench: Evaluating Web Application Generation from a Software Testing Perspective

author.name: Chenxu Liu, Zilu Zou, Peizhong Gao, Jiawen Tao, Zhexin Zhang, Guang Chen, Haowei Lin, Ying Zhou, Tianyi Bai, Dolly Deng, Suncong Zheng, Maxm Pan

entry.summary: IWC-Bench is an interactive benchmark for evaluating LLM-generated web applications using a software testing lens. It instruments each generated application and uses code coverage to guide an agent's exploration of its functionality, addressing the weaknesses of static benchmarks that credit unreachable code and interactive benchmarks that miss implemented features or confuse app defects with agent execution failures. The goal is more faithful automated evaluation of generated web apps.

entry.title: Self-Evolving Memory for Generative Recommendation

author.name: Xinyu Lin, Zhuosong Jiang, Zixiao Suo, Siqin Wang, Hanqing Zeng, Hanchao Yu, Yinglong Xia, Jiang Zhang, Aashu Singh, Fei Liu, Wenjie Wang, Fuli Feng, Yang Song, Qifan Wang, Tat-Seng Chua

entry.summary: This paper identifies an evolution conflict in generative recommendation: directly updating shared autoregressive parameters with streaming interactions lets dominant behavioral patterns progressively overwrite others because heterogeneous user preference shifts are optimized in one fully shared parameter space. To address this, the authors propose a self-evolving memory mechanism that decouples preference evolution from shared model parameters. The goal is continual adaptation to drifting user preferences without catastrophic interference.

entry.title: Don't Send What You Don't Need: Question-Guided Token Pruning as a Privacy Defense for Vision-Language Models

author.name: Md Khalid Syfullah, Alvi Ataur Khalil

entry.summary: QPriv-VL prunes visual tokens before they cross a model partition in federated, split, and U-shaped split learning, using task utility and privacy sensitivity to decide what to transmit. Its lightweight Dynamic Threshold Predictor jointly estimates a per-sample pruning ratio and token-level retention mask in a single forward pass guided by the question.

entry.title: Anatomical Grounding and Leakage-Aware Multimodal Contrastive Learning for Alzheimer's Disease Classification from Structural MRI

author.name: Paul-Gabriel Nicolae, Irina Georgiana Mocanu

entry.summary: Using a deliberately lightweight slice-based encoder on 1,075 ADNI-1 baseline T1 scans, the authors show that image-only Alzheimer's classifiers often attend to anatomically irrelevant regions, verified against FastSurfer segmentations. They also flag label leakage in multimodal models that ingest clinical tables containing variables used to assign the diagnosis, and introduce contrastive learning that avoids this shortcut. The paper matters as a methodological caution about inflated medical AI performance.

entry.title: BudgetBench: A Budget-Tiered Protocol and Pilot Harness for Memory Strategy Evaluation in Local Large Language Model Agents

author.name: Aditya Karnam Gururaj Rao, Arjun Jaggi

entry.summary: BudgetBench treats the per-call input-token budget as the independent variable when comparing memory strategies for local LLM agents, sweeping 2K through 32K tokens while holding model, task, sampler, and decoding fixed. It records quality, budget utilization, latency, and budget-violation rates, and offers a swappable MemoryStrategy contract with explicit budget enforcement. It matters as a reusable measurement surface for a practical constraint that current agent memory comparisons often ignore.

entry.title: Efficient Online Inverse Optimization with $O(d)$ Regret

author.name: Yang Cai, Anupam Gupta, Vineet Gupta, Guru Guruganesh, Yanchen Jiang, Christopher Liaw, Aranyak Mehta, Renato Paes Leme, Grigoris Velegkas, Di Wang

entry.summary: This paper gives a deterministic algorithm for online inverse linear optimization with regret O(d), uniform in the horizon and O(d^2) time per round. It matches a recent regret bound that previously required an improper rule enumerating covers at every scale and costing T to the Theta(d) per round, making this the first efficient and proper algorithm of that order. The authors replace the log-determinant potential with a trace power term, which is bounded outright and removes the logarithmic-in-T factor.

entry.title: A Variational Optimal Transport Operator on Incompressible Flow

author.name: Jinjin He, Shenyifan Lu, Sinan Wang, Zhiqi Li, Duowen Chen, Bo Zhu

entry.summary: The authors introduce VIOT, a generative neural operator that amortizes incompressible density transport by predicting a divergence-free velocity field and producing the full transport trajectory in a single feed-forward pass. It combines a stream-function representation enforcing incompressibility, a regularized transport objective, and a Fourier Neural Operator backbone to replace hour-scale per-pair fluid optimization.

entry.title: Training Specialist Models without Reasoning Trajectories for Domain Expert Distillation

author.name: Yilei Tu, Zihao Li, Shaoxiong Ji, J\"org Tiedemann, Fei Yuan

entry.summary: The paper investigates what governs the reasoning trajectories generated by domain specialists that were trained only on question-answer pairs without explicit reasoning supervision. Using student distillation as an agnostic probe of the specialist's latent trajectory space, the authors find a tight governing relation between specialist optimization and the trajectories it samples.

entry.title: Accuracy Is Not Service: A Decision-Aware Benchmark for Intermittent-Demand Forecasting

author.name: Joo Ern Chin, Shih-Fen Cheng, Aldy Gunawan

entry.summary: This paper shows that forecast accuracy and downstream service quality can diverge, benchmarking 38 forecasting methods on intermittent demand under a decision-aware protocol. On an industrial contract-logistics panel, the rank of methods by forecast accuracy is negatively correlated (about -0.555) with their rank by order-level service across over 20,000 real orders.

entry.title: Affinity-Aware Sharding for Delayed Tensor Parallelism

author.name: Eloi de Reynal

entry.summary: The paper examines Delayed Tensor Parallelism, which removes the blocking all-reduce in tensor-parallel Transformer inference by broadcasting partial outputs immediately and gathering peers' partials later. It shows DTP breaks the permutation symmetry of FFN neurons and attention KV heads, turning sharding into a modeling decision, and proposes maximizing affinity between co-located KV heads and FFN neurons via permutation.

entry.title: CoArena: Evaluating Computer-Use and Multi-Agent Systems in Real Time

author.name: Nitish Kovuru, Prateek Jannu

entry.summary: CoArena proposes a live evaluation protocol for computer-use agents in which real users submit tasks and two systems execute them concurrently in identical sandboxed desktops, with blind user judgments feeding a continually refit public leaderboard. The core contribution is a formal account of what makes such real-time evaluation valid, addressing benchmark stagnation and leakage.

entry.title: Rotation-Based Subspace Tracking for Robust Kernel PCA on Streaming Data

author.name: Kris Lokere, John Fossaceca

entry.summary: The paper addresses principal component analysis under streaming data, drift and outliers, where batch processing is infeasible and nonlinear structure defeats standard PCA. Kernel PCA handles nonlinearity via an implicit mapping to a reproducing kernel Hilbert space, but existing online robust kernel PCA methods have limitations. The authors propose a rotation-based subspace tracking approach aimed at maintaining robustness to outliers while updating on streaming samples.

entry.title: Assembling the CREW: A Collaborative Multi-agent Reinforcement Learning Framework for Automated Related Work Generation

author.name: Hai-Dang Dang, Bao-Yen Pham, Bao Nguyen, Tran Thi Huong, Huynh Thi Thanh Binh

entry.summary: CREW is a multi-agent LLM framework for automatic related work section generation in which agents dynamically coordinate by autonomously selecting actions such as Retrieve, Disseminate, and Compose, instead of following a rigid predefined workflow. The authors argue this adaptive collaboration better synthesizes complex scientific literature than static pipelines.

entry.title: From objective discovery to prediction of global ocean eco-provinces: A pathway for trustworthy learning

author.name: Makayla McDevitt, Maike Sonnewald, Stephanie Dutkiewicz

entry.summary: This work uses unsupervised machine learning to identify global ocean eco-provinces with associated uncertainty measures, based on a simulation of phytoplankton functional types, aiming toward a proof of concept for predicting eco-provinces from satellite ocean-color data. A hierarchy of explainable dense ensemble networks is developed to assess how well eco-provinces can be detected from modeled ocean-color fields.

entry.title: CANAL: Channel-Aware Noise Allocation for Differentially Private Feature Distillation in Medical Image Segmentation

author.name: Armaghan Butt, Shuya Feng, Qing Tian

entry.summary: The paper tackles privacy leakage in feature-distillation pipelines that let hospitals share learned representations instead of raw scans. CANAL introduces channel-aware allocation of calibrated Gaussian noise and a sampling scheme that avoids re-releasing each patient image repeatedly, which previously inflated the composed privacy cost by orders of magnitude across student iterations. The setting is medical image segmentation with formal differential privacy guarantees.

entry.title: GroundBench: A Factorized, Counterfactual Benchmark for Locating VLM Affordance Failures

author.name: Sarthak Sattigeri

entry.summary: GroundBench is a diagnostic benchmark that disentangles visual grounding, mechanical reasoning, and category-to-action association in vision-language model affordance tasks. It uses six branch-and-merge conditions, each adding a controlled information bundle, plus a counterfactual re-ask targeting a real alternate part visible in the same image. Across three OpenAI models and 1,068 predictions, supplying the target region without its identity still helps, showing naming a part supplies information the system should have inferred.

entry.title: Beyond Point Forecasts: A Survey on Probabilistic Forecasting for Time Series and Spatiotemporal Data

author.name: Donia Besher, Rajdeep Pathak, Madhurima Panja, Tanujit Chakraborty

entry.summary: This survey organizes probabilistic forecasting methods by where and how uncertainty enters the forecasting pipeline, aiming to unify a fragmented landscape across temporal and spatiotemporal work, statistics, machine learning, and deep generative modeling. The taxonomy links model-agnostic approaches such as ensembles and distribution-free calibration with model-intrinsic approaches including Bayesian modeling, distributional regression, and generative models. It also covers the emerging role of time series foundation models.

entry.title: EI-DDLGN: Efficient Encrypted Inference with Deep Differentiable Logic Gate Networks under TFHE

author.name: Mahmoud Y. M. Yassin, Mahmoud AbdelHafeez Sayed, Mostafa Taha

entry.summary: The paper investigates Deep Differentiable Logic Gate Networks as a Boolean-native alternative for privacy-preserving inference under Torus Fully Homomorphic Encryption. Because these networks learn Boolean computations directly and discretize into fixed logic gate networks, their inference aligns naturally with TFHE's Boolean execution model and avoids the arithmetic overhead that drives latency in TFHE-compatible neural frameworks. The authors argue this sidesteps programmable bootstrapping cost, accumulator growth, and circuit bit-width sensitivity.

entry.title: Just add noise: Debiasing tree-based variable importance in mixed data

author.name: Jiahe Li, Omar Melikechi

entry.summary: Tree-based importance measures such as those from random forests are known to favor continuous predictors over categorical ones. The authors provide a theoretical analysis of this bias and propose a simple fix: add a small amount of noise to each categorical predictor. They demonstrate the correction on simulated and real datasets and combine it with integrated path stability selection to perform variable selection with false discovery control for mixed data.

entry.title: Partition-Aware Scheduling for Mobile Heterogeneous Inference Co-Execution

author.name: Zhuojin Li, Marco Paolieri, Leana Golubchik

entry.summary: The paper jointly considers inter-operator and intra-operator parallelism for mobile inference on platforms that combine a GPU with multiple CPU core clusters.
