It formalizes partition-aware DAG scheduling for heterogeneous mobile inference, showing that the best strategy depends on the structure of the operator DAG, which motivates a structure-adaptive scheduler. Target workloads include CNNs and vision transformers represented as static operator DAGs with fixed tensor shapes.

entry.title: Neural Modal Decomposition: Architectural Priors from Observables

author.name: Juho Park, Kaushik Sengupta

entry.summary: The paper presents a neural framework that learns the pole-residue modal decomposition of multi-port linear time-invariant responses end to end, so that a model can predict responses for arbitrary geometries and port configurations while also extracting the underlying eigenmode structure. The authors frame this as a shared design principle across RF cavities, photonic devices, and superconducting quantum chips.

entry.title: Theseus in the Graph: Towards Traceable Multi-Hop Graph Navigation

author.name: Eduin E. Hernandez, Luis F. Garcia, Nurassyl Askar, Sergio A. Diaz, Stefano Rini

entry.summary: The paper reframes multi-hop knowledge graph question answering as question-conditioned graph navigation, in which an agent traverses relations from a topic entity toward the answer so that intermediate hops are explicit and verifiable. This formulation, called THESEUS, aims to make it possible to check whether correct answers actually came from faithful multi-hop reasoning.

entry.title: MAST: Label-Efficient, Robust, and Generalizable Sound Detection for Biodiversity Monitoring via Masked Audio Pretraining and Self-Training

author.name: Tianyi Xu, Daniel Pimentel-Alarc\'on, Zuzana Bu\v{r}ivalov\'a, Claudia Sol\'is-Lemus

entry.summary: MAST targets passive acoustic biodiversity monitoring by combining masked audio pretraining of a ViT-based encoder with a lightweight mel-spectrogram detector, then iteratively self-training on unlabeled recordings. A box-level contrastive loss pulls matched event regions together and pushes confusable background negatives apart, improving separation of animal vocalizations from noise. It matters because time-frequency annotation of animal sounds is expensive and site-specific, so label-efficient, transferable detection is the key bottleneck for scaling bioacoustic monitoring.

entry.title: Bridging Control, Inference, Transport, and Thermodynamics: From Theory to Applications in Learning

author.name: Emmy Blumenthal, Nikolas Claussen, Benjamin Eysenbach, Catherine Ji, Gautam Reddy, Colin Scheibner, Benjamin Sorkin

entry.summary: This review synthesizes a conceptual thread linking control theory, optimal transport, probabilistic inference, non-equilibrium thermodynamics, and machine learning, centered on optimizing free-energy-like functionals under dynamical or statistical constraints. It surveys applications in reinforcement learning and related learning settings. As a synthesis, it provides a useful map of an active interdisciplinary research frontier.

entry.title: PhysMent: An Interactive Approach For LLM Reasoning In Physics Problems

author.name: Joseph Chan, Utkarsh Jha, Xiyin Yang, Abhinav Jarajapu, Anik Sahai, Eddie Hu, Robin Jeshua Deepak, Stefano Saravalle, Aditya Shah

entry.summary: PhysMent is a benchmark that tests LLM physical reasoning through iterative, tool-mediated interaction with a MuJoCo simulator, requiring models to probe object states, apply forces, advance time, and edit scenes rather than answering from static givens. It covers 105 classical-mechanics scenes across difficulty regimes and scene modalities. This pushes evaluation toward active experimentation, closer to how physical understanding is actually tested.

entry.title: Causal Analysis and Mitigation of Spurious Onsets in Full-Duplex Speech LLMs

author.name: Kento Nishi

entry.summary: This paper diagnoses why full-duplex speech LLMs such as Moshi and PersonaPlex start speaking during prolonged user silence, showing that onset probability spikes by over nine orders of magnitude in a single 80-ms frame, implicating conditioning on prior nonspeech output rather than repeated sampling. It then proposes mitigation of these spurious onsets. The work targets a concrete and annoying failure mode of real-time conversational speech models.

entry.title: Beyond Depth and Width: The Information-Slack Dilemma in Streaming Test-Time Compute

author.name: Xiaotian Zhang (Trooly.AI)

entry.summary: This paper conceptualizes a tradeoff in streaming reasoning where early computation has more time budget but rests on incomplete evidence, while waiting improves information but shrinks computational slack. It proposes treating evidence-dependent computational jobs as the unit of analysis and outlines a research agenda on when to start, support, and commit such results.

entry.title: MUSE: A Theory-Harnessed Story Engine for Vibe Narrativizing

author.name: Jianxiang Ma, Xiaocui Yang, Daling Wang, Yuesong Hou, Mingfu Zhang, Yichen Gao, Junzhao Huang

entry.summary: The paper frames Vibe Narrativizing as the task of turning natural-language writing requirements into a finished story, and proposes MUSE, an engine that organizes story knowledge into decision-specific guidance. It engineers Robert McKee's story theory through rule atomization, semantic consolidation, and mechanism abstraction, then carries those decisions through planning, drafting, and revision. The contribution targets the twin bottlenecks of guidance quality and sustained use of that guidance across a long creative pipeline.

entry.title: Exploring Multimodal Turn-Taking Cues in Face-to-Face Conversation using Voice Activity Projection

author.name: Willem Berner, Julio Cesar Cavalcanti, Kalle {\AA}str\"om, Gabriel Skantze

entry.summary: This work asks whether visual signals improve turn-taking prediction beyond audio alone by extending the Voice Activity Projection model with visual features such as gaze, head movement, body and hand pose, and facial action units. Features are drawn from the large-scale Meta Seamless Interaction dataset of dyadic face-to-face conversations. The paper studies how best to fuse these visual cues with the transformer-based self-supervised VAP backbone.

entry.title: MarKey: Marginal Utility Guided Greedy Keyframe Selection for Long Video Understanding

author.name: Hongchang Shi, Jinpeng Hu, Ao Wang, Wenzheng Zhou, Hui Ma, Feng Li, Zenglin Shi

entry.summary: MarKey is a training-free framework for selecting keyframes in long-video understanding with multimodal LLMs, formulating selection as subset-aware greedy optimization based on marginal utility. Unlike methods that score frames in isolation, it accounts for how each candidate frame complements the already-selected subset. This reduces redundant selections and improves evidence coverage under a limited visual encoding budget.

entry.title: Pixel-wise Planarity for High-Precision Monocular Plane Segmentation

author.name: Ahmetcan Yavuz, Alpay Ozkan, R\'emi Pautrat, Shaohui Liu, Marc Pollefeys

entry.summary: The paper proposes a pixel-wise planarity prediction framework for monocular plane segmentation, built on a pretrained geometric backbone that predicts depth and surface normals. A dedicated planarity head estimates per-pixel planarity confidence, and at inference depth, normals, and planarity are combined in a lightweight region-growing procedure enforcing geometric consistency. The authors also analyze existing plane ground-truth annotations and document substantial flaws in them.

entry.title: RxScribe Bench: A Multi-Axis Benchmark for Evaluating Vision-Language Models on Indian Outpatient Prescriptions

author.name: Somil, Vijay Saini, Vidit Verma, Riya, Aastha Batta, Vibhuti Malhotra, Chayan Khetan, Piyush Mittal, Puneet Poonia

entry.summary: RxScribe Bench evaluates vision-language models on handwritten Indian outpatient prescriptions, decomposing performance into four axes tied to clinical severity instead of a single blended accuracy number. Models receive only a prescription image and an output schema and must produce a structured record that is compared field-by-field against human ground truth. The central insight is that fabricating a drug and misreading a legible dose carry very different clinical risks and should not be scored as equivalent errors.

entry.title: VectorHarness: Recovering Editable, Relation-Preserving Structure from Scientific Graphics

author.name: Jiahao Tang, Yiren Song, Alex Jinpeng Wang

entry.summary: VectorHarness reframes scientific graphic reconstruction from visual replication to raster-to-authoring: recovering an editable representation that supports native, customized editing rather than a pixel-similar copy. The multi-agent framework reconstructs heterogeneous components and preserves relations among them, addressing the common copy-paste failure of prior reconstruction systems where complex regions remain practically uneditable. It matters for scientific publishing and diagram-reuse workflows.

entry.title: Multimodal Foundation Models Adaptation based on Domain-Aware Relaxed Orthogonal Subspace for Remote Sensing

author.name: Han Luo, Ruoyu Yang, Yinhe Liu, Yanfei Zhong

entry.summary: This paper diagnoses a subspace mismatch problem in parameter-efficient fine-tuning: LoRA-style updates constrain adaptation to a fixed low-rank subspace chosen without observing downstream activation distributions, which is a poor coordinate system under large domain shift such as remote sensing. It proposes Domain-aware Relaxed Orthogonal Subspace adaptation (DROS), a unified framework that reformulates low-rank adaptation to be domain-aware and less rigidly orthogonal. The aim is to keep PEFT cheap while recovering accuracy on heavily shifted multimodal tasks.

entry.title: TotalSynth: Robust Whole-Body Synthetic CT from MRI and CBCT

author.name: Valentin Boussot, Cedric Hemon, Anais Barateau, Caroline Lafond, Jean-Claude Nunes, Jean-Louis Dillenseger

entry.summary: TotalSynth is a reusable pretrained framework for generating whole-body synthetic CT from MRI and CBCT, evaluated on a large multi-cohort corpus assembled from SynthRAD, prostate datasets, and BIC-MAC. It compares three model families using image-domain, anatomy-aware, registration-based, and uncertainty metrics. It matters for radiotherapy planning workflows where CT acquisition can be avoided or supplemented.

entry.title: BLInD: Learning Driver Intent as a Distribution over Future Ego Trajectories

author.name: Flavian Pegado, Ronit Hire, Shreyas Rajesh, Soham Phade

entry.summary: BLInD is a compact network that maps recent vehicle-state history (speed, curvature, indicators, vehicle type) to a top-k multimodal distribution over future ego trajectories, using no camera, LiDAR, map, or object tracks. The authors compare autoregressive and flow-matching decoders and show the flow-matching variant generalizes across datasets without adaptation. It matters for low-latency, safety-critical intent prediction where rich sensing is unavailable.

entry.title: Adapting Open-Weight MLLMs to Generate Point Prompts for Electron Microscopy Segmentation

author.name: Samia Mohinta, Albert Cardona

entry.summary: The authors fine-tune LoRA adapters on open-weight multimodal LLMs to output centroid coordinates as point prompts for a frozen microSAM segmenter, automating prompt generation for electron microscopy images. Qwen3-VL reaches 0.736 AP50 after supervised fine-tuning and reward optimization, versus 0.247 unadapted. It matters for scaling connectomics and EM segmentation without human prompting.

entry.title: Two-Stage Mixture-of-LoRA for Multi-Task Medical Vision-Language Learning

author.name: Zhanghao Chen, Yuanyuan Li, Zhenyu Lu, Shuo Gao, Guangquan Zhou, Yikun Zhang

entry.summary: This paper presents a shared-specific Mixture-of-LoRA architecture built on MedGemma-1.5-4B, with one shared LoRA plus six task-specific expert LoRAs and a two-stage training procedure that first jointly trains all adapters and then refines individual experts with the rest frozen. It targets heterogeneous output formats, conflicting gradients, and imbalanced data in medical vision-language tasks. It matters for consolidating many clinical tasks into one adapted model.

entry.title: A Building as a Repository: KIR, a Typed Intermediate Representation for Agent-Authored Building Information Models

author.name: Dmitry Kuklev

entry.summary: KIR is a typed intermediate representation in which a building is authored as a program stored in a versioned repository and lowered to host BIM applications as build targets. It is structured around seven ways a generator writing into a stateful, partially observable host can silently go wrong, giving each a data-level representation, such as ambiguous selectors becoming typed refusals with candidates and defaults retaining provenance. The work generalizes lessons from compiler and agent-safety design to architectural authoring agents.

entry.title: SCOUT-SLAM: Structurally-Coupled Dual Uncertainty-Aware 3DGS SLAM in the Wild

author.name: Kumaran Karthik, Pramat Shastri Jois, Suresh Sundaram

entry.summary: SCOUT-SLAM addresses a circular dependency in 3D Gaussian Splatting SLAM where reconstruction instability degrades uncertainty modeling, which in turn harms tracking and static-scene reconstruction. It proposes a structurally-coupled dual-uncertainty framework estimating both camera-tracking and reconstruction uncertainties from a shared base network, with a low-rank adaptation for efficiency. The goal is robustness under rapid camera motion and cluttered dynamic environments in the wild.

entry.title: Long-to-Short Video Evidence Reasoning for Grounded Question Answering

author.name: Kaiyan Chen, Junbin Xiao, Xun Yang

entry.summary: LOVER is a reinforcement-learning video reasoning model for grounded question answering that introduces three elements: a long-to-short video evidence curriculum that adapts training from long-range grounding to short-term reasoning, GQA-specific rewards favoring an IoP-style measure over strict temporal IoU for evidence spotting, and adaptive timestamp rendering that overlays timestamps onto frames using background-aware positioning. The paper argues these choices improve both evidence localization and answer accuracy compared with prior RL-based video reasoning models.

entry.title: Assessing nnU-Net Generalization across Brain Tumor Populations in BraTS-GoAT 2026

author.name: Tristan Kirscher (ICube, Institut Strauss), Vivian Metzger (Institut Strauss), Philippe Meyer (Institut Strauss, ICube), Xavier Coubez (Institut Strauss, ICube)

entry.summary: This BraTS-GoAT 2026 challenge report trains a conventional 3D nnU-Net on 1,351 labeled cases with five-fold cross-validation and reports Dice of 0.7805 (enhancing tumor), 0.8288 (tumor core), and 0.8854 (whole tumor) on pooled validation. The key finding is a large generalization drop, roughly 0.075 mean Dice, between source out-of-fold cases and pooled validation across heterogeneous populations, with mirroring and a residual encoder giving only marginal changes. It is a useful negative-result style generalization analysis.

entry.title: MambaMPD: A Mamba-Driven Segmentation Framework for Marine Pollution Detection from Remote Sensing Imagery

author.name: Shuaiyu Chen, Wei Han, Peng Ren, Chunbo Luo, Zeyu Fu

entry.summary: MambaMPD applies Vision Mamba to marine pollution detection in remote sensing, targeting low signal-to-noise ratios, fragmented pollution patches, and indistinct boundaries where pollutants resemble surrounding water. It injects two structural priors: frequency-aware augmentation using wavelet decomposition and multi-scale edge-guided attention. The paper argues state-space models are underexplored for this task despite their long-range dependency advantages.

entry.title: POLARIS: Training-Free Audio Fingerprinting with Saliency-Based Landmarks and Delaunay Grouping

author.name: Jiheng Li

entry.summary: POLARIS is a training-free audio fingerprinting system that selects landmarks from a locally normalized saliency field and groups them into sparse fingerprints using Delaunay triangulation, adding two-hop neighborhood fingerprints only at query time for distorted queries. It is evaluated on synthetic distortions from a public benchmark, excluding pitch and tempo shifts, plus a new benchmark of real re-recorded music, where it reportedly leads among training-free methods. The contribution is a practical, low-cost fingerprinting pipeline that avoids learned components.

entry.title: How Well Do Pseudo-Rigid Body Models Capture Real Plants? In-Field Validation of Simulated Blueberry Canes

author.name: Hannah Kolano, Chelse VanAtter, Wei Yang, Cindy Grimm, Joseph R. Davidson

entry.summary: This study validates coupled spring-loaded beam models used to simulate deformable plant limbs by comparing them against real blueberry cane mechanical properties measured in the field. It assesses how faithfully pseudo-rigid-body approximations capture real plant behavior, a prerequisite for planning and control of agricultural robots that must physically bend and push vegetation.

entry.title: Multi-Task Visual Perception Network with LLM Conditioning for Autonomous Navigation

author.name: Praveen Kumar, K. R. Guruprasad, Tushar Sandhan

entry.summary: The paper proposes an interactive navigation framework that drops reliance on globally consistent maps, which accumulate drift over long deployments. It fuses multi-task visual perception with large language models to interpret text or voice commands and produces sequential action plans from local visual cues and egocentric geometric instructions, executed step by step by the robot.

entry.title: Comparing Trajectories from Positions Alone: Curvature-Based Time Alignment and Drift Error Metric

author.name: Effie Daum, Daniele De Martini, Claire Dune, Fran\c{c}ois Pomerleau

entry.summary: This paper proposes a trajectory-evaluation protocol that combines a curvature-signal-based temporal alignment method with an error metric normalized by travelled distance, addressing hidden assumptions in standard ATE and RPE tools. It argues that unreported evaluation parameters make field-robotics accuracy comparisons misleading, especially when independent reference trajectories are unavailable. The contribution is methodological infrastructure for state estimation, localization, and SLAM benchmarking.

entry.title: Dynamics-Informed Reinforcement Learning for Agile and Energy-Efficient Locomotion of a Monopedal Hopping Quadcopter

author.name: Ruigang Chen, Qi Zhang, Zhicheng Zhong, Zhuorui Yun, Yizhar Or, Mingyi Liu

entry.summary: This paper proposes a dynamics-informed RL framework for a monopedal hopping quadcopter that embeds a target specific energy in the reward, constraining optimization to a physically viable energy manifold to avoid the energy-inefficient reward hacking common in hopping policies. Phase-consistent rewards encourage bio-inspired stance-phase impulse and penalize electro-mechanical power waste.

entry.title: Continuous Manifold-Decomposed Impedance Retargeting for Contact-Rich Imitation Learning

author.name: Jiahao Liu, Kento Kawaharazuka, Tasuku Makabe, Kei Okada

entry.summary: CMDIR extends Manifold-Decomposed Impedance Retargeting to convert fixed-impedance demonstrations into continuous variable-impedance controllers, which can also serve as structured supervision for imitation learning. A Continuous Task-Manifold Impedance Representation pairs an evolving task frame with controller instructions, and Demo-relative Compromise dynamics handle moving-basis transport and control/physical metric mismatch, with a Quality-to-Fast compiler that certifies candidates by multi-resolution checks.

entry.title: What we have is not what we prepared for

author.name: PeacockOfJuno

entry.summary: An argument that many pre-LLM assumptions about superintelligent AI risk do not transfer to current agentic language model systems, catalogued as a numbered list of recurring fallacies. It contends that LLM agents differ fundamentally in persistence, memory, and agency structure from the RL-agent models that shaped earlier risk thinking.

entry.title: Vibe Patenting: Evaluating LLM Judges for Professional Patent-Drafting Agents

author.name: Toshiaki Koike-Akino, Vlad Blaykhman, Ye Wang, Jing Liu, Gene V. Vinokur

entry.summary: This study builds 'Vibe Patenting,' an end-to-end patent-drafting testbed, to test how reliable LLM judges are when evaluating complex professional work. It finds that judge-guided iterative revision steadily improves judged quality where unguided revision plateaus, letting a cheaper low-reasoning agent approach a much more expensive high-reasoning one, while stronger models and more reasoning generally help.

entry.title: Fraglingo: Molecular Design via Attachment-Aware Autoregressive Fragment Generation

author.name: Thao Nguyen, Jeonghwan Kim, Zhenhailong Wang, Heng Ji

entry.summary: Fraglingo is an autoregressive fragment-based molecular generator that jointly models fragment identity and attachment in a continuous space, instead of the common two-stage approach of selecting a fragment from a fixed vocabulary and then predicting how to connect it. This lets generation mirror chemist-like edits such as scaffold extension, substituent replacement, and site-specific decoration.

entry.title: Enhancing Event Candidate Acquisition for Event Linking

author.name: Ziyang Zhang, Yinan Liu, Boyi Xue, Yingxuan Huang, Bin Wang, Xiaochun Yang

entry.summary: The paper introduces MACE, a multi-agent candidate event acquisition method that refines event structure before linking text mentions to knowledge base entries. Evidence-specialized LLM agents acquire time, location, participant, and event-type evidence, expose intermediate queries to lookup tools, and a coordinator revises the evidence set before final candidate construction. It matters for improving event linking robustness against short ambiguous mentions and noisy arguments.

entry.title: Four Ledgers, Not One Score: Responsible Communication of LLM-Judge Calibration in Biomedical ML

author.name: Sidi Chang, Peiying Zhu

entry.summary: The authors argue that synthetic perturbations are not a substitute for ground truth when calibrating LLM judges, since a planted mutation key is neither a detector output nor human annotation. They formalize four distinct ledgers, spanning planted perturbations, independent detector outputs, source-linked human dispositions, and human-added discoveries, and audit the design, scoring code, read paths, and human records of a private Japanese care-handoff workflow.

entry.title: Empirical Evaluation of Open-Source Large Language Models for Retrieval-Augmented Generation in ESG Domain

author.name: Motaz Saad, Anna Borrelli, Ivan Gentile, Kianna Kazemi, Francesco Piccialli, Antonella Longo

entry.summary: This study benchmarks seven open-source models from 2B to 30B parameters on ESG KPI extraction using 100 persona-based synthetic QA pairs derived from 498 real EU corporate ESG reports spanning 2010 to 2024. It provides a structured evaluation resource for a domain where open-model performance was previously unclear.

entry.title: Data storytelling meets interpretable machine learning: Decoding AI decisions for non-experts without revealing sensitive data and model details

author.name: Lemen Chao, Zixuan Yang, Anran Fang, Mingran Sun, Ming Lei

entry.summary: This work integrates data storytelling with interpretable machine learning to make AI decisions understandable to non-experts while avoiding disclosure of sensitive data or model internals. Following a design science paradigm, it proposes a formal definition, the DIST Pyramid for aligning storytelling with IML, and an I-P-O model plus architecture for explaining decisions.

entry.title: BEACON: Behavior and Appearance Control for Subject-Specific Video Generation

author.name: Pokrzywa Baptiste, Nabyl Quignon, Yara Bahram, Muhammad Osama Zeeshan, Antitza Dantcheva, Eric Granger

entry.summary: BEACON is a lightweight framework for person-specific video generation that disentangles visual identity from subject-specific expressive behavior, addressing the limitation that single-reference-image conditioning carries no temporal dynamics. This yields more expressive, subject-specific facial behavior while preserving identity. The approach targets human-centric generative video.

entry.title: ECAS: An Edge-Controlled Agentic System for Validation-Gated Scientific Application Execution

author.name: Baixi Sun, Mingze Xia, Huihuo Zheng

entry.summary: ECAS is an edge-controlled agentic system that closes the loop on scientific computing campaigns on HPC resources with limited human intervention, separating the cloud-hosted model from direct credential and execution authority. It addresses two obstacles: giving a cloud model direct HPC access exposes credentials and execution authority, while withholding it requires continuous human supervision, and one-shot generation cannot adapt when artifacts fail in a site-specific HPC environment. It matters as a security-conscious design pattern for agents operating high-stakes scientific infrastructure.

entry.title: Pathwise Individual Rationality in Federated Learning: A Mechanism-Architecture Co-Design

author.name: Amin Meghrazi, Srinivasan Parthasarathy, Andrew Perrault

entry.summary: This work studies federated learning through the lens of individual rationality, the requirement that participating in a federation be no worse for a client than training locally. It shows that clients can remain below their local-training baseline for hundreds of rounds and proposes a mechanism-architecture co-design that bounds per-round cumulative surplus along the training path rather than only asymptotically. This matters for realistic incentive design in cross-silo and cross-device federated deployments.

entry.title: Certification cost of quantum models: measurement correlation, not parameter count

author.name: Pavel Sulimov, Claude Lehmann

entry.summary: The paper quantifies the number of circuit executions needed to certify an empirical Fisher matrix of a trained variational quantum model to a given relative error, deriving a cost scaling in readout variance and squared gradient norm. It shows a single constant reproduces costs across circuit families with different parameter exponents, arguing that measurement correlation rather than parameter count governs certification cost.

entry.title: Online local learning for generative thermodynamic computing

author.name: Huilin Wang, Weibing Deng

entry.summary: This work proposes training generative thermodynamic computers, which convert thermal noise into structured data via Langevin dynamics, with a local parameter update applied immediately at each integration step. The reverse-path Onsager-Machlup objective yields a coupling gradient that is a symmetric sum of local residual-state correlations, so no trajectory-wide accumulation is needed; in MNIST-scale digital simulations, online training matches trajectory-batch validation loss while releasing less heat on average across five seeded pairs. It matters as a step toward physically realized, energy-efficient learning hardware.

entry.title: HyperProve: Answer-Guided Hypergraph Expansion for Multi-Hop Question Answering

author.name: An Nguyen Phu, Dung Nguyen Quang, Luu Hieu An, Linh Ngo Van, Trung Le, Thien Huu Nguyen

entry.summary: HyperProve is a retrieval-augmented QA framework that couples question decomposition with answer-conditioned expansion over a hypergraph of atomic facts, carrying intermediate answers and supporting hyperedges as retrieval state that biases the next expansion. This lets the system build coherent multi-hop evidence chains instead of treating each retrieval as an isolated match to the original question.

entry.title: Perceive, Refine, Reason: A Calibrated Pipeline for Measuring Indicators in Strategic Visual Communication on Social Media

author.name: Weihong Qi, Chen Ling

entry.summary: The PRR pipeline turns flexible vision-language detectors into auditable measurement instruments for computational social science, addressing the gap between coarse image-level labels and measurement of which specific objects appear, how prominently, and where. It combines natural-language category prompting with pixel-level refinement using Segment Anything and a multimodal LLM arbiter. The work targets scale-appropriate, validated measurement of visual content that shapes social media opinion.

entry.title: Closed-form Bayesian homography estimation from noisy point correspondences

author.name: Hanne Beuter, Sebastian Dorn

entry.summary: This paper presents a fast Bayesian formulation for homography estimation from point correspondences that explicitly incorporates measurement uncertainty and prior knowledge and yields a posterior distribution over homography parameters, including a closed-form posterior mean. The motivation is that conventional estimators give only point estimates while uncertainty propagates into downstream steps like calibration and 3D reconstruction, which matters in safety-critical settings such as medical imaging, autonomous driving and defense. It offers a principled probabilistic alternative to standard methods.

entry.title: Fault Diagnosis for Underwater Vehicles using Moving Horizon Estimation and Gaussian Processes

author.name: Fotis Panetsos, Kostas J. Kyriakopoulos

entry.summary: This work proposes model-based fault detection and diagnosis for underwater vehicles with actuator faults, explicitly accounting for unmodeled dynamics. A moving horizon estimator produces a lumped disturbance estimate, Gaussian processes approximate the unmodeled dynamics with uncertainty, and a generalized likelihood ratio test on the residual isolates faults. It matters because it separates fault effects from model error, a common failure mode in marine fault diagnosis.

entry.title: OrchSLM: Probing the Dynamics of Small Language Model Orchestration

author.name: Chengxi Zhang, Yu Yao

entry.summary: OrchSLM studies replacing cloud-scale LLMs with small language models in agentic pipelines, where latency, privacy, connectivity, and cost make monolithic LLMs problematic. Because SLM context windows and capacity limit long-horizon reasoning and interaction-heavy strategies like debate and iterative verification, the work motivates a complementary non-interactive paradigm using heterogeneous SLMs.

entry.title: AutoTailor: Automatic, User-Aligned Capability Selection and Adaptation for Web Agents

author.name: Xinyun Cao, Adriana Szekeres, Fazle Elahi Faisal

entry.summary: AutoTailor is a meta-agentic framework that builds and maintains a compact set of trajectory-derived MCP APIs for web agents, whose automatically discovered tool collections are often large, redundant, and misaligned with user demand. It filters for unsuitable granularity and redundancy offline, prioritizes broadly useful capabilities while preserving semantic coverage, and reselects APIs online based on task outcomes and usage.

entry.title: Toward a Decision-Assurance Layer for AI-Assisted Flight Planning in Air Traffic Management

author.name: Alexandre Barreto (George Mason University), Shou Matsumoto (George Mason University), Jorge Valverde-Rebaza (Tecnol\'ogico de Monterrey), Cleiton Ataide (DECEA: Department of Airspace Control), Paulo Costa (George Mason University)

entry.summary: Generative AI is already being used informally in air traffic management for flight-plan generation, trajectory interpretation, and constraint checking, but non-deterministic outputs create safety risks in human-in-the-loop settings. The paper proposes the AI Trust and Assurance Layer (ATAL), a model-agnostic architecture combining semantic stability under prompt variation, operational consistency of structured outputs, and normative constraint validation against domain rules.

entry.title: Carbon-Aware Routing for Function Calling in Edge-Cloud LLM Systems

author.name: Aikaterini Maria Panteleaki, Varatheepan Paramanayakam, Spyros Tragoudas, Iraklis Anagnostopoulos

entry.summary: This work addresses the energy and carbon footprint of routing function-calling queries to powerful cloud LLMs by distributing them across a three-tier edge-cloud architecture with heterogeneous hardware. A lightweight k-NN predictor in a unified semantic-lexical embedding space estimates per-tier accuracy, delay, and power, which are combined with real-time grid carbon intensity to route queries.

entry.title: Partition Scores Are Not System Scores: Deployment-Fidelity Gaps in Decomposed Algorithm Selection

author.name: Jiachen Zhang, Yu Tang, Li Zhu

entry.summary: The paper defines a deployment-fidelity gap G(R) as the difference between partition-level utility, which grants an oracle choice inside a selected algorithm family, and the deployable end-to-end utility a real learned within-family selector achieves. It derives accounting consequences including a per-instance margin-regret stability condition for when partition-time family choices transfer to deployment. It matters because oracle-style summaries are commonly reported as upper bounds on what deployable selectors can actually reach.

entry.title: Externalizing Requirement-to-Repair Artifacts as Observable Traces for LLM-Based Program Repair

author.name: Zewen Tao, Shin-nosuke Ishikawa

entry.summary: The authors propose THEMIS, a stage-aware repair workflow that makes the requirement-to-repair process inspectable by producing semantic interpretations, a runtime requirement-code graph, graph-derived developer guidance, retained repair rationale, and post-edit audit records. A retrospective audit of 300 SWE-bench Lite cases shows complete developer rationale is available for 288 cases and a full audited field set for 214 cases.

entry.title: BusMA: A Bus Communication Substrate for Multi-Agent Systems

author.name: Yanwen Peng, Delvin Ce Zhang, Xi Wang, Nikolaos Aletras

entry.summary: Observing that hierarchical manager-worker and router-based message passing restrict agent autonomy and propagate misrouted errors, the authors propose BusMA, a communication framework borrowed from bus architectures in computer systems. It lets any agent address peers through a shared channel and comprises agent registration, message routing, and shared memory management.

entry.title: Parameter-Efficient Adaptation of Pretrained Language Models for Time-Series Forecasting

author.name: Tamanna Kumavat, Georg Brunner, Kyriakos Flouris

entry.summary: This work studies how to adapt a pretrained GPT-2 backbone to univariate time-series forecasting by projecting fixed-length numeric patches directly into the embedding space, bypassing tokenization. Controlled ablations across seven datasets in energy, weather, traffic, and finance identify which design choices drive effective cross-modal transfer.

entry.title: TryOnReward: Learning Foveated Consistency for Reinforcement Fine-Tuning of Virtual Try-On

author.name: Xueheng Li, Yong Liu, Xiaolong Fu, Wen Xue, Chengjun Xie, Yipeng Sun, Yan Li, Simiu Gu

entry.summary: TryOnReward is a fine-grained reward model for virtual try-on built on a vision-language backbone and designed to align with human preferences rather than weak classic fidelity metrics. The authors use it for reinforcement fine-tuning, arguing that generic VLMs lack the discriminative granularity needed and cause reward hacking. The method targets detail preservation of garment and person attributes.

entry.title: IMM-based Multiple Object Tracking using a State Prediction Neural Network

author.name: Chan-Bin Lim, Dong-Hee Paek, Seung-Hyun Kong

entry.summary: PR-IMM augments an Interacting Multiple Model tracker with a transformer-based state predictor that uses radar Doppler measurements to estimate object displacement, adding a learned mode alongside constant-velocity, constant-acceleration, and constant-turn models. The design aims to capture nonlinear motion while retaining the stability and interpretability of physics-based models. It targets autonomous driving perception in adverse weather.

entry.title: The Agentic Company OS: Substrate Inversion for Sustained Enterprise Agent Deployment

author.name: Oliver Aleksander Larsen, Mahyar T. Moghaddam

entry.summary: This position paper argues that enterprise AI agents typically succeed in demos but stall in sustained production because they reason over data structured for human operators rather than for language models. The authors propose rebuilding the cognitive substrate, the shared working context agents read, around representations matched to how models read and act, and they connect failure modes such as loss of feedback and unreliable repetition to this architectural root cause. It matters as a framing piece for why enterprise agent reliability is an infrastructure problem rather than purely a model problem.

entry.title: Building a Production Greek-English Speech Recognizer

author.name: Christos Petrocheilos, Cleopatra Papadopoulou, Chris Porikis, Ioakeim Perros, Ayoub Kirouane, Themistoklis Nikolis

entry.summary: The authors report a multi-month engineering program producing Sophea, a bilingual Greek-English production ASR system, evaluated against nine deployment gates covering Greek and English word error rate, language identification, and hallucinations on non-speech audio. Across 23 training iterations and two architectures, no single training-data composition passed all nine gates, and the paper details the tradeoff where dense Greek domain exposure improved noisy-environment Greek accuracy but degraded English language identification unless a rebalanced mix was used at some accuracy cost. It matters as a candid account of multilingual production ASR tradeoffs and data pipeline engineering.

entry.title: Predictive audio representations for early detection and tracking of hidden dynamic objects

author.name: Katerina Vinciguerra, Moritz Brandes, Danilo Hollosi, Letizia Marchegiani

entry.summary: The paper extends audio-based perception of occluded traffic agents from single-vehicle scenarios to richer multi-agent settings, using predictive audio representations to detect and track hidden dynamic objects before they become visible. It targets the safety gap where camera and lidar systems cannot see around occlusions in time for robust planning.

entry.title: On the Equivalence of Stochastic Control and Path Space Formulations for Schr\"odinger Bridges over Compact Connected Lie Groups

author.name: Hamza Mahmood, Georgiy A. Bondar, Abhishek Halder, Adeel Akhtar

entry.summary: This paper proves equivalence between the stochastic optimal control and path-space formulations of the Schrodinger bridge problem for kinematic equations on compact connected Lie groups. Using horizontal lifts and stochastic anti-development, the authors derive a Girsanov-type change of measure and show expected control energy equals relative entropy to the reference Wiener measure, with implications for existence, uniqueness, and computation.

entry.title: LePlanner: An Iterative Amortized Controller For World Models

author.name: Saksham Bansal, Om Naphade, Chayan Aggarwal, Vrishin M

entry.summary: LePlanner is an amortized iterative controller that learns to construct and refine latent action sequences using a frozen world-model predictor, targeting the tradeoff between expensive search-based planners like CEM and MPPI and fast but brittle policies on contact-rich multimodal tasks. It aims to retain search-like quality while amortizing inference cost.

entry.title: DiTAR+: Dual Optimization for Robust Autoregressive Diffusion Speech Synthesis

author.name: Ziyu Zhang, Tianlun Zuo, Hanzhao Li, Haoyu Zhang, Lei Xie

entry.summary: This paper tackles decoding instability in continuous-latent autoregressive diffusion transformer models for zero-shot speech synthesis, where long utterances and complex linguistic structures cause the diffusion decoder to lean on acoustic inertia and ignore semantic conditioning. The authors propose DiTAR+, a dual-optimization framework combining Dilated Context Sampling, which widens the historical receptive field while respecting temporal continuity to limit cumulative error, with a second optimization aimed at the acoustic dependency problem. It matters because zero-shot TTS stability on long-form speech is a practical bottleneck for deployment.

entry.title: Rethinking the Implications of Human Feedback for Preference Learning in Human-Robot Collaboration

author.name: Qiping Zhang, Kate Candon, Debasmita Ghose, Marynel V\'azquez

entry.summary: The paper revisits the standard three-step pipeline for learning reward models from human feedback in human-robot interaction, where fixed implication rules derive accepted or rejected labels for unchosen actions. Through a user study in two collaborative simulation environments, the authors find human-provided implication labels frequently diverge from the standard fixed rule, and using the human labels substantially improves preference learning. It argues that label derivation should itself be learned or elicited rather than assumed.

entry.title: GraMRAG: Orchestrating Multi-Agent Multi-Step Reasoning via Graph Memory with Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Zhongyu Wang

entry.summary: GraMRAG proposes a graph-memory-guided multi-agent RAG framework built around a dynamic multimodal memory graph, combined with a vision-text bridged reasoning paradigm that unifies multi-scale entity cropping and a ReAct-style visual toolchain. The goal is to overcome shallow reasoning depth and state blindness in existing multi-agent RAG systems on knowledge-intensive multimodal questions. It matters as a step toward longer-horizon cross-modal retrieval and reasoning.

entry.title: Graph-Transformer Fraud Detection with Self-Supervised Pretraining and Conformal Risk Control

author.name: Sergei, Komarov

entry.summary: The paper introduces GTFD, a graph-transformer detector that fuses structural evidence from a corporate payment graph with temporal transaction sequences via a cross-modal gating layer. A conformal risk-control head converts the fused representation into threshold-free anomaly scores with finite-sample coverage guarantees, and the model is pretrained with self-supervised link masking. It matters for combining relational and temporal fraud signals while giving statistical guarantees on alert rates.

entry.title: AURA: Unified Multimodal Framework for Conversational Music Editing

author.name: Quoc-Huy Trinh, Minh-Van Nguyen, Debesh Jha

entry.summary: AURA is a conversational music editing framework where a multimodal LLM reads the full dialogue history plus optional image and reference audio, distilling intent into compact concept tokens injected into a frozen MusicGen backbone. Only about 91M parameters are trained while 1.9B backbone parameters stay frozen, and it is evaluated on Slakh2100 and MoisesDB. It matters for multi-turn, progressively refined creative audio workflows rather than one-shot edit commands.

entry.title: Bridging the Modality Gap in Long-Form Clinical Audio: A Comparative Study of Lightweight and Heavyweight End-to-End SOAP Generation

author.name: Ziyu Zhang, Mingchen Shao, Wenjie Tian, Tianlun Zuo, Longhao Li, Lei Xie

entry.summary: For the BeTraC 2026 challenge the ASLP team builds a fully end-to-end multimodal system that generates structured SOAP notes directly from long-form doctor-patient audio, bypassing intermediate transcripts. Using a 1.41-million-sample multi-task corpus, training proceeds through domain pre-training, supervised fine-tuning and reward optimization, compared at 3B and 30B scale. It matters because cascaded ASR pipelines lose or hallucinate information on extended clinical audio, and E2E alternatives are still rare.

entry.title: Sharing standardized image-derived data in computational pathology using DICOM

author.name: Daniela P. Schacherer (Fraunhofer Institute for Digital Medicine MEVIS, Bremen, Germany), Christopher P. Bridge (Athinoula A. Martinos Center for Biomedical Imaging, Massachusetts General Hospital, Boston, USA), David Clunie (PixelMed Publishing, Bangor, USA), Igor Octaviano (Radical Imaging LLC, USA), Andr\'e Homeyer (Fraunhofer Institute for Digital Medicine MEVIS, Bremen, Germany), Markus D. Herrmann (Harvard Medical School, Boston, USA), Olivier Gevaert (Stanford University, Stanford, USA), Tabita Ghete (University Hospital Erlangen, Erlangen, Germany), Markus Metzler (University Hospital Erlangen, Erlangen, Germany), Henning Hoefener (Fraunhofer Institute for Digital Medicine MEVIS, Bremen, Germany), Tahsin Kurc (Stony Brook University, Stony Brook, USA), Curtis Lisle (National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases, Bethesda, USA), Kenneth Philbrick (Google Research, Mountain View, USA), Joel Saltz (Stony Brook University, Stony Brook, USA), Yuanning Zheng (Stanford University, Stanford, USA), Andrey Fedorov (Harvard Medical School, Boston, USA)

entry.summary: This paper describes how image-derived pathology data such as region-of-interest delineations and segmentation masks can be encoded and shared in a standardized way within the NCI Imaging Data Commons, which relies on the DICOM standard for hosting de-identified radiology and pathology data. It addresses the fact that sharing of derived annotations lags far behind sharing of the underlying images. It matters because computational pathology progress depends on access to large, diverse, interoperable annotation datasets.

entry.title: SENTINEL: A Multi-Pathway Architecture for Detecting Living-Off-the-Land APT Attacks on Windows Command Lines

author.name: Ahad Bin Islam Shoeb, Kamrul Hasan, Jamal Uddin Tanvin, Liang Hong, Imtiaz Ahmed, Md Arif Billah, Al Amin

entry.summary: SENTINEL proposes a multi-pathway detection architecture combining BERT-based semantic encoding with character-level CNNs to catch living-off-the-land APT activity in Windows command-line telemetry. It targets a real evasion gap highlighted by campaigns such as Volt Typhoon, where only signed, legitimate Windows utilities are abused for long-term persistence. The work is relevant to defenders handling obfuscated, multi-stage command sequences that defeat single-model detectors.

entry.title: CompCQR: Compositional Query Generation for Training-Free Conversational Search

author.name: Yunah Jang, Kang-il Lee, Joongbo Shin, Kyomin Jung

entry.summary: CompCQR tackles conversational query reformulation by generating several complementary stand-alone queries instead of repeatedly invoking an LLM to produce one rewrite. The authors observe that retrievers are highly sensitive to content ordering, so reordering the same information changes retrieval coverage and effectiveness. Their training-free compositional approach aims to remove costly repeated LLM calls while better aligning reformulations with the downstream retriever.

entry.title: Skill Composition for Legged Robot Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Daniel Gigliotti, Flavio Maiorana, Fabio Patrizi, Luca Iocchi

entry.summary: This position-style paper argues that composing independently trained legged-robot sub-policies should be treated as a first-class research problem rather than an implementation detail. It notes that specialized controllers train quickly and validate reliably, while end-to-end policies covering everything do not, leaving transitions between skills fragile. Reliable composition is framed as what converts separate skills into a reusable, extensible repertoire.

entry.title: OCT-FedSIR: Toward Trustworthy Federated Ophthalmic Learning under Annotation Noise

author.name: Sina Gholami, Abdulmoneam Ali, Tania Haghighi, Rashadul H. Badhon, Behafarin Emam, Sally S. Y. Ong, Atalie C. Thompson, Theodore Leng, Ahmed Arafa, Jennifer I. Lim, Minhaj Nur Alam

entry.summary: OCT-FedSIR is a reliability-aware spectral framework for federated OCT classification when participating institutions differ in annotation quality and data distribution. It combines class-balanced spectral estimation, logit adjustment, complementary spectral descriptors, selective spectral relabeling and noise-aware federated optimization. The authors evaluate it across multiple real ophthalmic datasets (Kermany, University of Illinois Chicago and others), aiming to distinguish genuine class imbalance from corrupted supervision.

entry.title: Semantic Fibers and Cross-Gram Interference: A Calculus of Safety Drift in Overcomplete Representations

author.name: Mohammed Ahnouch, Lotfi Elaachack

entry.summary: The paper formalizes cross-lingual safety failures in which a model refuses a harmful English request but complies with a faithful translation. For a declared equivalence relation, representation, metric, dictionary, scoring head, threshold and contrast model, it shows safety drift admits an exact linear-algebraic characterization as a cross-Gram functional of within-fiber contrast, with worst-case values given by a support function and margin invariance by an annihilator condition.

entry.title: Mirror, Mirror on the Wall: Prompt Echoing in Small Instruct Language Models

author.name: Inez Okulska, Bartosz Naskr\k{e}cki, Jan Piotrowski, Tomasz Steifer

entry.summary: The paper investigates prompt echoing, where instruct models mirror the prompt instead of answering it, asking whether this reflects training-data leakage or a misbehaving induction/copying mechanism. Studying small models from the Gemma, Llama, Qwen, SmolLM and OLMo families, the authors find echoed prompts often partially overlap training data but conclude the behavior is primarily driven by induction heads.

entry.title: Rethinking Procedural Audio Pre-training: Source Scaling and Objective Adaptation

author.name: Jiajun Peng, Fengrui Liu, Xinyu Liu, Feng Liu

entry.summary: The authors dissect procedural audio as a pre-training source, separating formula-class coverage from within-class rendering diversity and showing the two scales benefit different learning formulations and tasks. Matching experiments also show procedural audio prefers low mask ratios (10-25%) while natural AudioSet data favors 50-75%, implying pre-training recipes do not transfer unchanged between domains.

entry.title: Augmenting Large Audio-Language Models with Frame-Level Grounding for Fine-Grained Temporal Perception

author.name: Yanfeng Shi, Yan Song, Junhui Li, Tinggan Huang, Wu Guo, Haoyu Song, Ian McLoughlin

entry.summary: Large audio-language models struggle with precise acoustic event localization because generative timestamp-token prediction lacks explicit correspondence to fine-grained audio evidence. The authors keep the LALM frozen to encode the event query with audio as context and attach a dedicated frame-level grounding model, improving temporal precision and reliability of localization.

entry.title: ProtoGuide: Prototype-Driven Guidance for Class-Conditional Graph Generation

author.name: Salvatore Romano, Marco Grassia, Pietro Li\`o, Giuseppe Mangioni

entry.summary: Class-conditional discrete diffusion for graphs normally embeds the class signal in the denoiser during training, coupling conditioning to the trained model, while classifier guidance cannot be used directly because gradients do not flow through sampled discrete edges. ProtoGuide relaxes the denoiser output into a differentiable soft adjacency, embeds it with a frozen Siamese GNN, and scores it against target-class prototypes at each reverse step, enabling post-hoc guidance.

entry.title: End-to-End Cell Detection via Instance-aware Graph Modeling

author.name: Ruochen Liu, Yalin Zheng, Jingxin Liu, Jianfeng Zhang, Shoujun Huang, Dexing Kong, Haofeng Li, Wei Lou

entry.summary: This work proposes an end-to-end framework for cell detection and classification that jointly models visual appearance and relational structure among cell nuclei, rather than using the common two-stage pipeline of visual extraction followed by graph-based relational modeling. By unifying both stages, it avoids separate per-stage tuning and enables joint optimization. The motivation is capturing complex cellular interactions in the tumor microenvironment for more accurate pathological analysis.

entry.title: CodeTS: Verifiable Text-to-Time Series Generation via Executable Code

author.name: Xudong Yuan, Shunyu Liu, Tongya Zheng, Huiping Zhuang, Mingli Song, Kaixuan Chen

entry.summary: CodeTS reformulates text-to-time-series generation as a text-to-code-to-time-series process, using executable code as an explicit intermediate interface that specifies how textual requirements shape target temporal patterns. This provides a verifiable mechanism for deriving generation logic from natural language, which prior methods lacked. The approach targets scenario-specific synthesis when real observations are scarce or expensive.

entry.title: Automating Attack Graph Construction for Agentic Pentesting. Towards Neuro-Symbolic Vulnerability Hunting

author.name: Oliver Stevanovic, Jasmin Wachter

entry.summary: This paper presents a semi-automated pipeline that bridges symbolic attack-graph reasoning and LLM-based agents for security testing. It parses findings from Trivy, Semgrep, and Nmap into MulVAL predicates and uses an LLM-assisted process to construct domain-specific Datalog rules linking scanner evidence to attack techniques, after which MulVAL/XSB performs symbolic inference to generate auditable attack paths. A web-security case study demonstrates feasibility.

entry.title: A Unified Vision-Language Model for PSMA PET/CT Report Generation, Visual Question Answering, and Lesion Segmentation

author.name: Yang Xing, Jiong Wu, Savas Ozdemir, Yang Zhou, Boxiao Yu, Ying Zhang, Zheren Zhu, Chenyu You, Wei Shao, Yang Lu, Kang Wang, Tinsu Pan, Yang Yang, Kuang Gong

entry.summary: The authors propose a unified PSMA PET/CT vision-language model handling report generation, visual question answering, and lesion segmentation within one framework. It uses a LLaVA-style architecture with a PET/CT vision encoder, an MLP-Mixer projection module, a LoRA-tuned language model, and a 3D segmentation branch, trained in four stages from encoder pretraining through multitask tuning. Language tasks used 5,747 PSMA PET/CT studies with paired reports, while segmentation used the PSMA subset of AutoPET, and the model outperformed a prior PET report baseline.

entry.title: Before You Poll with LLMs: A Deliberative Diagnostic Framework

author.name: Ahmed Wali, Hassaan Tayyab

entry.summary: This paper introduces a Deliberative Polling Diagnostic Framework that compares how human and LLM persona beliefs shift after identical informational interventions, testing whether models reason through new information or merely retrieve cached opinions. The authors argue current silicon-sampling evaluations only capture a static snapshot of opinions and miss dynamic fidelity.

entry.title: SlipSense: Multimodal Tactile Learning for Low-Latency and Generalized Slip Detection

author.name: Tong Jian, Aditya Thurvas Senthil Kumar, Xinyi Li, Ziling Chen, Tianyu Dai, Ali Sengul, Matteo Grimaldi, Wenjie Lu, Saleh Nabi, Tao Yu

entry.summary: SlipSense is a tactile slip-detection framework built on a custom sensor, TacV5, pairing a 32x32 piezoresistive array at 240 Hz with a 3-axis accelerometer at 8 kHz. It uses modality-specific encoding, intra-sensor fusion, and cross-modal attention with causal temporal prediction to detect slip with low latency and across platforms, evaluated on 1.4 million frames. Reliable, fast slip detection is a prerequisite for dexterous robotic manipulation.

entry.title: Operational Range Bounding in Spectroscopy: A Safety Cage Framework for Machine Learning Models

author.name: Nikki Grens, Lu\'is F. Sim\~oes, Kai Hou Yip, Theresa Lueftinger

entry.summary: The authors evaluate a modular safety-cage layer that runs alongside a black-box ML model to judge whether a prediction is trustworthy without altering the estimator, using indicators such as uncertainty and out-of-distribution signals. The setting is exoplanet transmission spectroscopy, where ground truth is unavailable and instrument anomalies or domain shift can quietly invalidate outputs.

entry.title: Online Bayesian Node Classification on Inductive Graphs under Distribution Shift

author.name: Jinwen Xu, Gonzalo Mateos Buckstein, Qin Lu

entry.summary: This work adapts a Bayesian last-layer approach by placing random parameters atop a deterministic GNN encoder to give inductive node classifiers calibrated uncertainty under distribution shift. Because the categorical softmax likelihood breaks Gaussian conjugacy, the authors introduce a variational Bayesian last-layer objective that jointly handles training and streaming test-time updates.

entry.title: Benchmarking Optimizers to Solve Inverse Problems with Differentiable Physics Simulators

author.name: Xiang Chen, Huanhuan Xia

entry.summary: This paper benchmarks optimizers for solving inverse problems through differentiable physics simulators, a paradigm valued for combining physical correctness with gradient-based efficiency. It builds 12 differentiable simulators spanning discrete and continuous mechanics, atomistic simulation, rendering, and semi-empirical models, then compares optimizer performance across them.

entry.title: Pre-training with Graph Transformers

author.name: Jiaming Wang, Thomas Laurent, Xavier Bresson

entry.summary: This article surveys pre-training strategies for graph transformers in biochemistry, running experiments to compare objectives. It reports that supervised pre-training using computed molecular properties as labels yields the largest downstream gains, and highlights the importance of constraining model capacity to avoid overfitting in graph transformers.

entry.title: Representing Clinical Conditions on Vital Signs from Healthy Individuals using Latent Modeling

author.name: Rafael Pina, Varuna De Silva, Mindula Illeperuma

entry.summary: The paper proposes a conditional variational autoencoder that augments vital-sign data from healthy individuals so it mimics patterns of a given clinical condition, addressing the scarcity of representative clinical datasets. The model is trained on a public ICU dataset and evaluated against vital-sign data collected from healthy participants. Success here would enable synthetic generation of condition-specific physiological signals without needing large patient cohorts.

entry.title: Data-driven Prediction of Satellite-observed Avalanche Activity from Snowpack Simulations

author.name: Jakob Grah, Filippo Maria Bianchi, Bert Kruyt, Karsten M\"uller

entry.summary: Avalanche forecasting needs snowpack information and recent activity records, but field observations are sparse across large mountain regions. The study compiles five winters of Sentinel-1 SAR avalanche detections across Norway and part of Sweden alongside SNOWPACK simulations forced by numerical weather prediction on a 20 by 20 km grid at several elevations and slope angles, then trains a transformer on five days of snowpack output to predict the next day's SAR-based Avalanche Activity Index. It tests whether physically grounded snowpack simulations can substitute for scarce direct observations.

category.term: AI for Science and Earth Observation

entry.title: Task-Directed Residual AddUNet:Perfect-Reconstruction Routing for Full-Rate Representations

author.name: Vikram R. Lakkavalli

entry.summary: This paper gives a perfect-reconstruction interpretation of AddUNet, showing that the survivor-skip structure of a constrained additive U-Net is exactly equivalent to a critically sampled multirate PR filter bank. It then introduces a residual full-rate PR architecture that routes task-irrelevant or redundant structure away from the task-facing representation while retaining it explicitly, guaranteeing exact reconstruction.

entry.title: QSTAR: Quantum Selective Transfer with Adaptive Routing

author.name: Saim Rehman, Nouhaila Innan, Muhammad Shafique

entry.summary: QSTAR is a selective quantum transfer learning framework that keeps high-confidence classical predictions and routes only low-confidence samples to a fallback quantum branch, using a frozen ResNet18 backbone on Fashion-MNIST. The authors compare manually designed quantum heads, KetGPT-designed quantum heads, and parameter-matched classical baselines, reporting that standard quantum heads reach at most 57.0% accuracy while the strongest KetGPT head reaches 78.5%.

entry.title: Exploring new directions in enhancing the ACTS parameter optimization suite

author.name: Chance LaVoie, Qi Bin Lei, Rocky Bala Garg, Lauren Tompkins

entry.summary: This paper examines the ACTS track-seeding parameter auto-tuner, which currently uses an Optuna Tree-structured Parzen Estimator, and investigates whether Bayesian optimization can overcome its expensive evaluations, restricted search space, and scalarized objective. Using the Open Data Detector under identical search ranges and a 100-trial budget, the authors compare Expected Improvement and Upper Confidence Bound against TPE and random search.

entry.title: From Masking to Merging: Rethinking SpecAugment for Efficient Audio Spectrogram Transformer

author.name: Minhee Park, Hyowon Ahn, Chanwoo Kim

entry.summary: The authors propose SpecAugment-Patch Merging, which masks spectrogram patches and then merges selected pairs of masked patches after positional embeddings, shrinking the token count the transformer must process. Increasing merged pairs from 0 to 100 leaves AudioSet mAP essentially flat (34.07 to 34.08) while raising throughput about 13.9 percent, with similar trends on ESC-50 and Speech Commands V2.

entry.title: Stochastic Gradient Descent over P2

author.name: Maria Oprea, Qin Li, Yunan Yang

entry.summary: The paper asks whether the classical diffusion approximation of stochastic gradient descent, which replaces stochastic gradient noise with Gaussian noise, extends to optimization over probability measures in the Wasserstein space P2. Because that space is nonlinear and infinite dimensional, the authors use Lions differentiability to lift the problem to a linear Hilbert space where higher-order calculus is available. They then construct a Gaussian random-field approximation with controlled velocity fields.

entry.title: Privacy-Preserving Deep Joint Source-Channel Coding with In-Loop Concept Erasure

author.name: Rami Eid, Maria Slim, Mariette Awad, Hadi Sarieddeen

entry.summary: The paper proposes LEAPSC, which integrates in-loop least-squares concept erasure inside a variational information bottleneck encoder for deep joint source-channel coding. Periodically refitting the projection operator couples encoder dynamics to the erasure mechanism, driving attribute-conditional mean differences toward zero within each task-label group. Additional components include conditional value-at-risk tail-sensitive privacy and feature-wise linear modulation for semantic communication.

entry.title: Runtime-Incremental Transformer for Reinforcement-Learning-Based Adaptive Control

author.name: Giansalvo Cirrincione, Adriano Fagiolini

entry.summary: The paper addresses attention-based meta-controllers for adaptive control of robotic manipulators with non-observable friction memory, where head counts are fixed before training and tuned via costly offline search, causing catastrophic failures at long memory horizons. It introduces a runtime mechanism that grows and prunes attention heads during reinforcement learning, triggered by the effective rank of the on-policy context distribution and per-head output magnitude. This lets representational capacity adapt online rather than being fixed in advance.

entry.title: Joint Optimization for Federated Learning and Transmission over Unreliable Wireless Networks with Heterogeneous Data

author.name: Changheng Wang, Xianchao Zhang, Zhiqing Wei, Lingzhu Zhao, Zhongming Yang, Zhiyong Feng

entry.summary: The authors propose federated random walk averaging, a FedAvg variant that mitigates client drift from heterogeneous data by updating models along random-walk paths and aggregating them at the server. Parameters are transmitted in packets with retransmission support to reduce the impact of wireless errors along those paths, and a joint optimization formulation accounts for transmission delays that otherwise hinder exploration. The goal is improved convergence under both data and channel heterogeneity.

entry.title: What Input Resolution Is Required for Bird Species Identification, and What Is Its Latency Cost on an Edge Device? A Study of 14 Input Resolutions and Six Architectures with On-Device Measurements

author.name: Takeshi Nishikawa

entry.summary: This factorial study varies input resolution across 14 side lengths from 16 to 224, six architectures, two training and evaluation regimes, and 30 random seeds, totaling 2,520 checkpoints and 5,040 evaluations, with latency measured on an NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano. The motivating application is identifying distant birds spanning only tens of pixels for wind-farm bird-strike mitigation. Key findings include that required resolution depends on the accuracy target and that changing architecture buys more accuracy than raising resolution.

entry.title: Towards Anticipatory Databases Through Shared Data and Workload Semantics

author.name: Farzaneh Zirak, Kasper Overgaard Mortensen, Farhana Choudhury, Renata Borovica-Gajic

entry.summary: The paper argues that database management systems should use workload semantics, rather than only low-level signals like recency and frequency, as a first-class control signal for anticipatory decisions. It introduces the notions of semantic locality and semantic trajectories to capture relationships among nearby queries and how analytical focus evolves over a session, and sketches a framework representing semantic context at data, query, and session levels.

entry.title: S3-Tracker: Self-Supervised Surgical Tissue Tracking With Contrastive Random Walks

author.name: Jiaming Zhang, Zijian Wu, Mehran Armand, Septimiu Salcudean

entry.summary: The paper introduces a self-supervised Track-Any-Point method that learns point correspondences in endoscopic video by contrastive random walks over unlabeled surgical footage, avoiding the need for annotated trajectories. The method reportedly matches semi-supervised baselines while implicitly handling soft tissue deformation, supporting intraoperative registration.

entry.title: Learning Multi-Agent Task Assignment and Navigation in the Factory: from Simulation to Real Robots

author.name: Abdalwhab Bakheet Mohamed Abdalwhab, Giovanni Beltrame, David St-Onge

entry.summary: The paper investigates decentralized multi-agent reinforcement learning for multi-robot multi-machine tending in industrial settings, introducing Feature-fusion Multi-Agent PPO that combines 2D LiDAR measurements with task-specific state. A full simulation-to-reality pipeline built on high-fidelity robotics simulation and ROS2 is deployed on physical mobile manipulators.

entry.title: CCMAN: Cognitive Instability-Aware Cross-Modal Attention Network for Interpretable Temporal Biomarkers of Verbal Fluency Speech

author.name: Madhurananda Pahar, Caitlin Illingworth, Dorota Braun, Daniel Blackburn, Heidi Christensen

entry.summary: The paper proposes a transfer learning framework that learns task-agnostic cognitive speech representations from multiple memory-probing tasks and finetunes them on a minute-long verbal fluency task. CCMAN fuses semantic, acoustic, and linguistic signals via bidirectional cross-attention, gated fusion, and transformer temporal modeling to detect early cognitive decline non-invasively.

entry.title: Eigenvalue-Decomposition Cost Denoising as an Alternative to Predict-then-Optimize for Shortest-Path Problems

author.name: Henry Aldridge-Krawciw, Irene Aldridge

entry.summary: The authors propose denoising observed cost vectors via eigenvalue decomposition as a structurally different remedy when predict-then-optimize methods such as SPO+ are misspecified, i.e. when true costs are nonlinear in features but the predictor is linear. The setting is where a decision-maker sees many noisy realizations of the same underlying cost process, allowing the realized costs themselves to serve as a noisy signal. It matters as a decision-focused learning alternative that sidesteps predictor misspecification.

entry.title: Projection-Free Multi-level Algorithms for Stochastic Constrained Compositional Optimization

author.name: Wei Jiang, Sifan Yang, Wenhao Yang, Yibo Wang, Yuanyu Wan, Zechao Li, Lijun Zhang

entry.summary: The paper develops projection-free algorithms for stochastic constrained multi-level compositional optimization, where objectives are nested compositions of smooth functions and the feasible set is convex, using linear minimization oracles instead of costly projections. It provides variance-reduced and momentum-based methods with complexity guarantees under Frank-Wolfe gap and gradient mapping criteria, including weaker smoothness assumptions. This is relevant to scalable training of nested objectives such as those in meta-learning and distributionally robust models.

entry.title: From Token Probabilities to Semantic Constraints: Towards Declarative Probabilistic Evaluation of Language Models

author.name: Kyle Richardson, Cullen Anderson, Pranav Balakrishnan, Takuto Ban, Daksha Ladia, Ankita Gupta, Marisa Hudspeth

entry.summary: ModelLog is a declarative probabilistic framework for pretraining evaluation that expresses evaluation targets as symbolic constraints over token-level predictions and measures how strongly a model's distribution satisfies them. The authors demonstrate it on tasks probing negation, mutual exclusivity, and consistency, connecting evaluation to learning signals. This aims to make evaluation more interpretable and theoretically grounded than aggregate benchmark scores.

entry.title: DARE: Dialectical Agentic Reasoning for Structured Knowledge Fact Checking

author.name: Yifei Li, Xiaohan Zheng, Wentao Qian, Liansheng Zhuang

entry.summary: DARE reframes structured knowledge fact checking as an iterative retrieve-reason-reflect loop in a multi-agent framework, aiming to fix the failure modes of LLM-generated graph reasoning programs: invalid relation generation, single-path reasoning without self-correction, and biased evidence assessment that over-weights supporting signals. It integrates relation-grounded evidence and dialectical critique between agents.

entry.title: Measuring the Cost of Variety Conflation in Multilingual MT Evaluation: Adding Mozambican Xichangana, Nyanja and Sena to FLORES+

author.name: Felermino D. M. A. Ali, Delfina L\'azaro Mateus, Manuel Valente Mangue

entry.summary: This paper extends FLORES+ with Portuguese-source evaluation sets for three Mozambican Bantu varieties and shows that conflating language varieties with related reference languages badly distorts MT evaluation. Swapping only the reference from Tsonga to Xichangana drops spBLEU by 13.10 points for NLLB-200 and 15.30 for Google, while variant-aware fine-tuning reverses the penalty on the intended variety.

entry.title: When Tools Get in the Way: The Effect of Unnecessary Tool Availability on LLM Answering

author.name: Saanvi Paturi, Arsen Kenzhebayev, Arham Sethi, Vyas Raina, Ivaxi Sheth, Vatsal Raina

entry.summary: Using 500 query pairs across 10 knowledge domains, this study asks whether merely making a related but unnecessary tool available degrades a model's ability to answer from its own knowledge, and whether a preceding tool interaction changes that behavior. It shifts attention from appropriate tool selection to the collateral cost of tool presence on questions that do not need tools.

entry.title: Typhoon ASR Streaming: Steerable Low-Latency Thai Speech Recognition with Real-Time Shallow Fusion

author.name: Warit Sirichotedumrong, Tanawin Samutsin, Shah Faisal Wani, Sittipong Sripaisarnmongkol, Kunat Pipatanakul

entry.summary: The paper presents a deployable streaming Thai ASR system that restores streaming behavior in a full-context open model using a cache-aware encoder, and adds shallow fusion with an n-gram language model plus phrase boosting for decode-time vocabulary steering without retraining. It reports results across two Thai benchmarks and two model sizes.

entry.title: SALUTE: Benchmarking and Adapting LLMs for the Defense Domain

author.name: Hyeongcheol Park, Sumin In, Suyeon Myeong, Hogun Park, Sangmin Kim, Moonhyun Lee, Daekyeong Park, Sangpil Kim

entry.summary: SALUTE is an end-to-end framework for evaluating and adapting LLMs to the defense domain, combining a curated corpus of open-access U.S. military doctrine and government documents, a grounded instruction dataset from doctrinal sources and defense news, and associated evaluation tasks. It aims to consolidate fragmented, task-specific prior work in military language technology.

entry.title: Sequential Adapter Stacking for Cross-Lingual Low-Resource ASR

author.name: Thai Thi Thanh Thao Dang, Mengjie Qian, Kate Knill

entry.summary: The paper investigates parameter-efficient transfer from high-resource source languages to low-resource target languages on Whisper, motivated by the sharp degradation of multilingual ASR for languages with little labeled data. Alongside warm initialization and attention-based fusion, it proposes Sequential Adapter Stacking, which places a trainable target-language adapter atop a frozen source-language adapter. Evaluation covers three target languages unsupported by Whisper.

entry.title: ScorePrompts: Natural-Language Exploration of Symbolic Music Scores through Analysis

author.name: Emmanouil Karystinaios, Gerhard Widmer

entry.summary: ScorePrompts is an interactive system where users upload a symbolic score, receive natural-language descriptions of its musical structure, ask questions about specific passages, and inspect the corresponding analysis in staff notation. Specialist MIR components first estimate harmony, tonality, cadences, formal boundaries, texture, and note-level roles at note, beat, measure, and piece levels; a schema-constrained language model then converts these results into descriptions rather than inferring structure from raw MusicXML. A deterministic router selects relevant measures and analytical levels for questions.

entry.title: CALICO: A Human-Centered, Codebook-Aligned System for Annotation

author.name: Boqin Yuan, Xiaoyi Gu, Fiona Li, Chang Wan, Angel Hsing-Chi Hwang, Jieyu Zhao

entry.summary: CALICO is a human-centered workflow for codebook-based annotation with LLMs that treats prompts as editable, versioned, and optimizable artifacts rather than hidden fixed instructions. It integrates codebook parsing, prompt generation, result inspection, prompt versioning, natural-language human feedback, and label-support tooling so non-technical domain experts can diagnose and correct model behavior. The goal is more reliable, revisable, and auditable LLM-assisted annotation in scientific research.

entry.title: Language-Guided Representation Learning for Robust Cross-Sensor Material Recognition

author.name: Mashood M. Mohsan, Muhayy Ud Din, Binzhao Xu, Ahmad Abubakar, Irfan Hussain

entry.summary: The paper proposes a language-guided distillation framework for learning tactile representations that generalize across different vision-based tactile sensors. Natural-language touch descriptors such as rough, soft, or slippery serve as a sensor-agnostic supervisory signal because they encode high-level material properties invariant to optics, elastomer, and illumination differences. The authors build a 39K-sample touch-language dataset to support this training.

entry.title: What Does the Encoder Actually Decide? A Controlled Comparison of Vision Backbones on Joint Tree Segmentation and Stereo Depth

author.name: Yida Lin, Bing Xue, Mengjie Zhang, Sam Schofield, Richard Green

entry.summary: This study holds dataset, decoders, losses, schedule, and evaluation fixed to measure how much the encoder choice alone affects joint semantic segmentation and stereo depth on thin vegetation, a robot tree-pruning setting. It builds a hard parameter-sharing network with one encoder feeding both task branches and swaps encoders across CNN, transformer, hybrid, MLP-mixer, and state-space families near a 25M budget, trained from scratch. Depth is evaluated only on tree pixels.

entry.title: GaugeDefect: Detecting Surface Anomalies by Curvature of Feature Transport

author.name: Yefan Wang

entry.summary: GaugeDefect proposes a geometric cue for industrial surface anomaly localization: rather than asking whether each local patch looks unusual, it measures how features vary and connect across the surface, capturing curvature of feature transport. This targets defects such as thin scratches, small dents, and disrupted repeated patterns that leave locally plausible appearance but disturb the global relational structure. The work complements appearance-based, reconstruction-based, and distillation-based anomaly detectors.

entry.title: Global-Local Contextual Progressive Expansion Network for Martian Landslide Segmentation in Multimodal Remote Sensing Imagery

author.name: Leo Thomas Ramos, Sidike Paheding, Abel A. Reyes-Angulo, Rajaneesh A., Sajinkumar K. S., Angel D. Sappa, Thomas Oommen

entry.summary: This paper provides what it describes as the first comprehensive assessment of modern neural segmentation models for Martian landslide segmentation, a task complicated by highly variable morphology, sparse irregular foregrounds, and heterogeneous spectral plus topographic cues. It also proposes TransCPLES, a U-shaped network that progressively expands global-local context to handle these challenges. The results aim to support understanding of Martian surface processes and future space exploration.

entry.title: Zero-Shot Cross-Material Ptychographic Phase Reconstruction Using Deep Learning

author.name: Wen-Chun Lin, Yu-Chee Tseng, Jen-Jee Chen, Nan-You Chen

entry.summary: The paper presents a local-to-global deep learning framework that reconstructs full-field ptychographic phase maps directly from diffraction patterns without iterative refinement at inference. Local wrapped-phase patches are predicted in a sine-cosine representation and stitched using calibrated scan positions and Gaussian weighting, and the model is tested zero-shot on a different material. It matters for speeding up large-scale 4D-STEM characterization.

entry.title: SignMimic: Robust High-Quality Sign Language Motion Generation via Human-Shape-Oblivious Pose Transfer Guidance

author.name: Zhewen He (New York University Abu Dhabi), Junyi Yu (New York University Abu Dhabi), Haomian Huang (New York University Abu Dhabi), Zhenhua Li (ChatSign Technology), Yi Fang (New York University Abu Dhabi, ChatSign Technology)

entry.summary: SignMimic tackles sign language video mimicking by separating rigid canonicalization (TNet-based SE(3) alignment), non-rigid adaptation in canonical space to preserve hand and face articulators, and Pose-MAE-style completion before conditional video diffusion. The decomposition aims to eliminate handshape drift and spatio-temporal instability in prior monolithic pipelines. It matters for accessibility tooling and linguistically faithful sign synthesis.

entry.title: Beyond Natural Images: Rethinking AI-Generated Image Detection in Documents
