author.name: Zhangjie Fu, Jiazhen Yan, Yuanwen Chen, Xinquan Yu, Yanzhe Li, Hui Jiang, Lei Gao, Chenfu Bao

entry.summary: The authors build AIGDoc-Pilot, a controlled diagnostic benchmark for AI-generated document images, and show existing detectors degrade substantially on documents, with mean AUC dropping more than 7 percent. They identify document-specific properties such as spatially inconsistent generation artifacts and use them to motivate improved detection. It matters because invoices, certificates, and medical records are high-stakes forgery targets.

entry.title: Context-Aware Mutual Learning for Blind Image Inpainting and Beyond

author.name: Haoru Zhao, Yufeng Wang, Zhaorui Gu, Bing Zheng, Haiyong Zheng

entry.summary: This work argues that existing two-stage blind inpainting pipelines treat mask estimation as a one-way signal to the inpainting network, overlooking the reciprocal relationship between the two stages. It proposes a context-aware mutual learning scheme in which mask estimation and inpainting inform each other, aiming at better inpainting quality and generalization to unknown real-world contamination. The relevance is practical: real corruption masks are rarely known in deployment.

entry.title: MCIQA-2K: A Multi-Dimensional Dataset and No-Reference Quality Assessment Benchmark for Colorized Images

author.name: Yunkai Zhuang, Qihang Yan, Zicheng Zhang, Guangtao Zhai

entry.summary: MCIQA-2K is a 2,000-image benchmark for no-reference quality assessment of colorized images, built from outputs of five colorization models and annotated along three perceptual dimensions: color smearing, semantic color misalignment, and global naturalness. The authors argue that full-reference metrics fail on colorization because a grayscale image admits many plausible colorizations. It provides both data and a proposed assessment method for a task where standard metrics are known to be inadequate.

entry.title: Patient-Level, Leakage-Aware Deep Learning for Cross-Center Periapical Radiograph Classification

author.name: Md Jubaer Rahman, Ulas Bagci

entry.summary: This paper introduces a patient-level, leakage-aware benchmark for single-tooth intraoral periapical radiograph classification on DentIRO, comprising 5,300 images from 3,243 patients across two clinics and four disease classes. It explicitly avoids the image-level splits that leak patients between training and test and adds cross-clinic validation. Five transfer-learning models are compared, providing a reproducible baseline in a dental AI area lacking such benchmarks.

entry.title: G-ray: Ray-Level Relative Geometric Position Encoding in Multi-View Vision Transformers under Camera Heterogeneity

author.name: Shuo Zhang, Xin Su, Wei Wang, Jun Liu, Xinrui Zeng, Yongsen Chen, Chenjie Wang, Guibo Zhu, Jinqiao Wang, Bin Luo, Liangpei Zhang

entry.summary: This paper examines relative position encoding for multi-view vision transformers when cameras have different fields of view or projection models. The authors argue that existing rotary encodings based on image-plane coordinates produce projection-dependent phases and inconsistent geometric cues, and propose G-ray, which parameterizes rotary phases by camera-local ray angles so the same ray pair induces the same relative phase across projections. G-ray can be used standalone or combined with existing encodings.

entry.title: CapsuleMotion: A Lightweight Real-Time Visual Motion Predictor for Capsule Endoscopy

author.name: Oliver Bause, Julia Werner, Oliver Bringmann

entry.summary: CapsuleMotion addresses the battery bottleneck in video capsule endoscopy by predicting frame-to-frame motion from on-device compression metrics, letting the capsule spend energy in a goal-directed way so that complete gastrointestinal screening becomes more likely. The system is explicitly lightweight and real-time, designed for the severe compute and power constraints of a swallowable device. It is an applied medical-engineering contribution rather than a general ML advance.

entry.title: BSC-Net: A Small-Branch-Sensitive Structural Continuity Network for Coronary Vessel Segmentation and Quantitative Angiographic Analysis

author.name: Wanxian Li, Jiaqian Qin, Qingyi Xian, Yazhi Li, Song Chen, Liman Li, Hao He

entry.summary: BSC-Net is a ResNet-U-Net variant for X-ray coronary angiography segmentation that combines targeted sampling to boost small-vessel representation with long-range contextual modeling and an Edge-Informed Loss to repair broken vascular continuity. The authors motivate it with the clinical need for accurate quantitative coronary analysis, where noise, bifurcations, and vessel-background overlap cause missed small branches. It is a domain-specific architectural and loss-function contribution.

entry.title: What a gated sensing pipeline never looks at: bandwidth reduction and the misses behind it

author.name: Raghu Venkat, Tricha Anjali

entry.summary: The paper evaluates a gated sensing pipeline that transmits findings instead of video over a constrained airborne link, reporting a 41,977x bit reduction while detecting only 1 of 4 staged events, and then documents that this detection was itself an artifact later removed by a tracker-speed correction (performance falling to 1 of 7). It is an unusually candid accounting of what bandwidth-ratio metrics hide, including the events a gating policy never inspects. The emphasis is on evaluation honesty in severely bandwidth-limited perception systems.

entry.title: From Model Patterns to Abstract Semantics in Compositional Zero-Shot Learning

author.name: Weize Li, Zhicheng Zhao, Fei Su

entry.summary: This work reframes compositional zero-shot learning by treating primitive variations as context-driven activation of concrete visual cues rather than fixed independent representations, addressing the limited variant capacity and abstract-vs-concrete competition in prior VLM-based methods. The proposed CLEAR framework uses cloze-style reasoning and re-ranking in a coarse-to-fine manner inspired by human perception. It is a representation-perspective contribution for compositional generalization.

entry.title: TRACE: Two-Stage Detector-Response Estimation With Angular Cosine Expansion for Ring Artifact Correction in Photon-Counting CT

author.name: Jigang Duan, Heran Wang, Ligen Shi, Zheng Sun, Ping Yang, Xing Zhao

entry.summary: TRACE tackles ring artifacts in photon-counting detector CT caused by detector response nonuniformity, modeling residual stripe amplitudes that vary slowly with projection angle as a fixed bias plus low-order DCT components. A learnable analysis-synthesis architecture represents ideal projections while two-stage unsupervised optimization separates them from fixed and angular components. The method is fully unsupervised and tailored to measured PCD-CT data.

entry.title: Seeing What the Vehicle Sees: Video-Augmented Virtual Reality for Physical Autonomous Vehicles

author.name: Md Tanjemul Islam, Mohammad Shafin, Md Rafiul Kabir

entry.summary: This paper presents a video-augmented VR framework that couples a physical ROS 2 autonomous robot vehicle to a Unity 6 application on a Meta Quest 3S headset, transmitting vehicle state and live onboard camera streams over two independent channels. It addresses the fact that most passenger-facing VR studies rely on fully simulated vehicles or scripted scenarios rather than a physically operating autonomous system. The goal is to improve passenger understanding of what the vehicle perceives and why it acts.

entry.title: Learning-Based Dynamic Obstacle Avoidance for a UAV Using Only Three Range Sensors

author.name: Mohammad Reza Ranjbar Divkoti, A. Pedro Aguiar

entry.summary: The paper presents a deep reinforcement learning approach for online kinodynamic motion planning of a fixed-altitude UAV that must dodge static and dynamic obstacles with only three range sensors and yaw-only control. A behavior grid map representation is combined with PPO to give a stable continuous-control policy under severe partial observability. The appeal is sensor-minimal, low-cost autonomy for nonholonomic, fixed-wing-like platforms.

entry.title: Belief-Adaptive Online Autonomy for Quadrotor UAV Navigation under GNSS Degradation in Urban Environments

author.name: Deepak Kumar Panda, Weisi Guo

entry.summary: This framework augments an extended Kalman filter with explicit GNSS trust modeling, second-order online belief adaptation, and latency-aware handling of out-of-sequence measurements for quadrotors in urban canyons. GNSS trust is a latent belief state that modulates measurement weighting and multipath bias uncertainty, updated from filter consistency signals rather than reactive covariance tuning. It targets non-stationary, temporally correlated GNSS errors that break conventional GNSS-IMU fusion.

entry.title: A Vision Based Framework Integrating Attention and Action Cues for Interpretable Cognitive Workload Assessment in Human Robot Collaborative Assembly

author.name: Junyan Xionga, Naiyi Feng, Xingke Xia, Qihang Fan, Suchang Chen, Daqiang Guo

entry.summary: This work presents a vision-based, attention-and-action framework for continuously estimating operator cognitive workload in human-robot collaborative assembly, combining RGB-D observations, robot states, and calibrated task-relevant zones into a temporally consistent behavioral representation. The goal is to replace body-worn physiological sensors, which are impractical in factory settings, with an interpretable camera-only assessment.

entry.title: Assistance Torque Estimation via Dynamics-Aware Optimization for Lower-Limb Exoskeleton in Complex Environments

author.name: Xiao-Yin Liu, Guotao Li, Weiqun Wang, Zeng-Guang Hou

entry.summary: This work proposes a dynamics-model-based optimization method that directly generates motor assist torque for a lower-limb exoskeleton, avoiding the expensive motion-capture ground-truth pipeline and the assumption that scaled human joint torques give optimal motor commands. A data-driven prediction network is then trained to provide accurate real-time torque estimates in complex outdoor environments.

entry.title: Volumetric Harmonic Field Navigation for Quadrotors

author.name: Shuxiu Jia, Amartya Mukherjee, Yating Yuan, Jun Liu

entry.summary: This work couples a precomputed volumetric harmonic potential field with a constrained predictive planner that queries the field at predicted positions rather than extracting a global reference path for a quadrotor. In structured 3-D tests, harmonic guidance produced larger minimum clearance and lower RMS jerk than matched Dijkstra guidance at the cost of longer paths, a pattern that held even when both used the same passage.

entry.title: On Detecting Multiple Simultaneous Change-points in High Dimensional Non-Stationary Time Series

author.name: Richard Song

entry.summary: The paper studies detection of multiple simultaneous change points in high-dimensional non-stationary economic and financial time series using standard and adaptive fused group lasso with mixed L2,1 penalties. It shows L2 consistency and, with data-dependent weights, L0 consistency, giving conditions on the interplay between minimum structural-change magnitude, number of change points, and sample size. It matters for econometric and financial monitoring where many series shift together.

entry.title: Brockman says HuggingFace incident model had not been alignment-trained; ETA: roon clarifies that it was

author.name: Caspar Oesterheld

entry.summary: A short post documenting an inconsistency: Greg Brockman stated the model involved in the Hugging Face incident had not undergone alignment training, and an update cites an OpenAI employee clarifying that it was alignment trained with reasonable-looking eval scores. It highlights uncertainty about whether alignment post-training was applied to the highly persistent internal model.

entry.title: Grounded Adjudication of Variations across Extracted TimeLines (GAVEL): Comparing Clinical Timelines Against Their Case Reports

author.name: Jack Cummins, Sayantan Kumar, Ketan Tamirisa, Jeremy C. Weiss

entry.summary: GAVEL is an LLM-judge protocol that compares two extracted clinical timelines against their source case report, returning a discrepancy type, verdict, and supporting passage. Evaluated with GPT5.6sol and DeepSeek V3.2 across 2,738 findings and 126 reports, it also ranked six LLM extractors and two human annotators, with merged timelines preferred in 77.0% of comparisons.

entry.title: Cost Characterization of Vertically Partitioned Federated Knowledge Graphs

author.name: Md Saikat Islam Khan Bappy, Oshani Seneviratne

entry.summary: This paper formalizes vertical partitioning of knowledge graphs as a design space and compares four partitioning strategies including semantic domain grouping, frequency-balanced partitioning, co-occurrence graph-cut partitioning, and random partitioning. It evaluates them across metrics such as communication cost, candidate set size, load balance, and query latency. It matters because partitioning choice is a key data-management decision for federated multi-hop query answering.

entry.title: Degraded but Not Entirely Ineffective: PE-Based Deformable Graph Neural Networks

author.name: Jinhua Wu, Xinliang Zhang

entry.summary: The paper proposes PEBDSAM, a position-encoding-based deformable spatial aggregation module for graph neural networks. It aims to simultaneously address over-smoothing with depth, over-compression from long-range dependencies, fixed receptive fields, and topological noise on heterophilous graphs. It matters as an attempt at a single mechanism covering several long-standing GNN limitations.

entry.title: Converting Sequenced Fuzzy Cognitive Maps to Causal Virtual Worlds with Large Video Generators

author.name: Akash Kumar Panda, Olaoluwa Adigun, Bart Kosko

entry.summary: The authors show how users can construct and manipulate causal virtual worlds using LLM and large video model agents, where fuzzy cognitive maps encode granular causal structure and drive the causal evolution of the scene. Sequences of dynamical meta-rules of the form if A then B define causal scenes, with the map's transient feedback dynamics producing the causal arrow observed in generated video.

entry.title: ER-EDF: A Psychology-Grounded Emotion Regulation Framework for Speech Empathetic Dialogue Generation in Large Audio-Language Models

author.name: Hongyu Jin, Wenda Zhang, Runqiu Fei, Gongping Huang, Mike Conway, Ting Dang

entry.summary: This work argues that empathetic spoken dialogue requires not only perceiving a user's emotion but regulating how it is expressed, and that large audio-language models typically treat emotion as a direct conditioning signal, producing affect mirroring rather than calibrated support. It proposes ER-EDF, a framework grounded in the Perception-Action Model and emotion regulation theory that explicitly decouples perception from regulation.

entry.title: Predicting build orientation for SLM dental parts: a comparison of rotation representations and direct vector regression

author.name: Felix Schmalzel, Reimar Waitz, Moritz Kronberger, Thorsten Sch\"oler

entry.summary: The authors treat the manual selection of build orientation for selective laser melting of dental parts as supervised learning of a part's up-axis from technician-labeled production data. Using roughly 2,400 patient-specific parts, they compare 13 up-axis representations, spanning six classical SO(3) parameterizations and seven direct unit-sphere representations, across ResNet-50 multi-view and PointNeXt-S point-cloud backbones.

entry.title: Multilingual Agent System for Inclusive Wildfire Evacuation Guidance

author.name: Shruti Kulkarni, Lynn Tong, Aditi Namboodiripad, Chelyah Miller, Helen Lin, Peeyush Patel, Bogdan Bistriceanu, Diane Myung-kyung Woodbridge

entry.summary: The paper describes BEACON, a multilingual service delivering personalized wildfire evacuation guidance such as navigation routes, checklists, and a chatbot in the user's language. It targets the gap that most US emergency messaging is English-only despite tens of millions of residents with limited English proficiency. The work is an application-oriented system paper with social impact framing.

entry.title: Evaluation of MLLM-Agnostic Plug-and-Play Keyframe Selection Methods for Long Video Understanding

author.name: Dilip Sarkar, Md. Safayet Islam, Liang Liang

entry.summary: The paper surveys and evaluates training-free, model-agnostic keyframe selection methods for long-video understanding with multimodal LLMs, contrasting them with retraining and adapter-based approaches. It organizes methods by whether they use the query alongside candidate frames and benchmarks them under a common protocol. The work is mainly a systematization and evaluation contribution.

entry.title: Conflict-Predictive Variable Horizons in Multi-Drone Distributed Model Predictive Control

author.name: Linda M\"{u}mken, Michael Schwung, Stefan Lier, Andreas Schwung

entry.summary: The paper proposes a conflict-predictive variable prediction horizon in distributed model predictive control for multi-drone collision avoidance, where each drone locally extrapolates neighbor flight lines and computes time-to-conflict in closed form. The horizon is chosen as the smallest admissible value whose planning window covers the predicted conflict, reducing per-step cost. The underlying distributed MPC formulation is left unchanged.

entry.title: FaithfulBench: Does AI Counsel Uphold or Undermine the User's Professed Faith?

author.name: M Waleed Kadous, Benjamin Olsen, Walter Scheirer, Daniel D. Slate, Alexander Arnold, DZ Kalman

entry.summary: FaithfulBench is presented as the first benchmark scoring AI moral counsel by how well it adheres to the user professed faith tradition, with scenarios drawn from each tradition respected texts and the faithful answer used as the judging standard. Five frontier models are tested with and without tradition identification and a source-rooted counselor guide, plus a pressure condition measuring whether models cave to the answer the user wants.

entry.title: Talking to Me or Someone Else? Rethinking Talk-to-Me Detection in Egocentric Videos

author.name: Feiyu Du, Xi He, Jia Li, Yapeng Tian, Weili Wu

entry.summary: The authors reformulate talk-to-me detection in egocentric video as an online, frame-level prediction task rather than offline clip-level binary recognition, and explicitly model diverse non-TTM speaking states such as talking-to-others, self-talk, and background conditions. They construct an Online TTM dataset to support the new formulation and benchmark methods on it. It matters for real-time egocentric assistants and socially aware wearable computing.

entry.title: EdgeHAR: An Edge-Native Compact Sensor Foundation Model for Human Activity Recognition

author.name: He Zhang, Siyu Yuan, Siyu Liu, Sizhen Bian, Bin Guo

entry.summary: EdgeHAR is a compact sensor foundation model for wearable human activity recognition that factorizes signals into an activity-semantic code, a motion-dynamics code and a third disentangled factor, aiming to separate reusable activity knowledge from acquisition variations. It targets robustness to unseen users, devices, sampling rates and sensor placements while fitting edge deployment. It matters for on-device wearable intelligence where cloud-scale foundation models are impractical.

entry.title: Natural Language Knowledge Graph Query Execution: Leveraging Controlled Semantics in the LLM Context Window

author.name: Blake G. Fitch

entry.summary: NLKGQ is a working system and framework that routes domain concepts to an LLM through a formal OWL ontology rather than informal prompt prose or schema dumps. In a single LLM call it supplies a SPARQL-oriented system prompt, the complete domain ontology and domain context, so the model queries knowledge graphs using semantically precise tokens. The claim is that declared machine-readable vocabulary improves NL-to-query execution over informal context transfer.

entry.title: MANE: A Multi-Path Adaptive Network for Edge Onloading of Deep Neural Networks

author.name: Sokratis Nikolaidis, Stylianos I. Venieris, Leonidas Malachias, Iakovos S. Venieris

entry.summary: MANE addresses split computing in dense indoor environments where one edge server must serve many competing IoT devices, causing latency SLO violations. It presents a distributed inference mechanism that adapts across multiple pathways to manage shared edge resources when head models run on-device and heavier tails run on the server. The work targets practical scheduling and load-balancing problems in edge AI deployments.

entry.title: PACE: Progressive Angular-to-Norm Contrastive Embedding

author.name: Yanping Li, Wei Zhou, Yawen Liu, Yibo Wang, Ke Zhu, Guangda Huzhang, Qing-Guo Chen, Zhao Xu, Jun Zhang, Wei Wei

entry.summary: Most multimodal embedding models train with cosine-based contrastive objectives, which stabilize training but confine semantics to angular geometry so that embedding norms carry no meaning. The authors attribute the instability of directly optimizing dot-product similarity to premature expansion of the optimization space, reflected in angular-norm entanglement and directional anisotropy, and propose a progressive angular-to-norm schedule to recover norm as a semantic signal.

entry.title: Pre-PEFT Probing: Weight Statistics and Perturbation Robustness for Layer Selection in VLM Vision Encoders

author.name: Qingtao Xia, Jiahua Bao, Siyao Cheng, Jie Liu

entry.summary: Rather than applying LoRA-style adapters to all layers of a vision-language model, this work probes each vision-encoder Transformer layer before fine-tuning to estimate its adaptability. It characterizes layers through Q/K/V weight statistics such as norms and condition numbers and through robustness to controlled parameter perturbations, then relates these indicators to actual fine-tuning gains.

entry.title: On the role of the tokenizer in ECG transformer models

author.name: Jiawei Li, Fabio Bonassi, Johan Sundstr\"om, Thomas B. Sch\"on, Ant\^onio H. Ribeiro

entry.summary: This paper systematically compares eight tokenization strategies for ECG signals across Transformer, Informer, Reformer, and FEDformer backbones on the nine-label CPSC2018 classification task, controlling input projection and backbone capacity to isolate token construction effects. Physiology-aware tokenizations (median-beat and HeartLang) reach mean macro-AUCs around 0.89 versus roughly 0.82 for point-wise and patch-wise tokenization, while also cutting sequence length from 1,250 to about 158 tokens. Pooling the two physiology-aware representations yields an 8.2 percent relative macro-AUC improvement.

entry.title: Circuit-MLLM: Topological Logic-Guided Latent-Space Visual Reasoning for Circuit Schematic Understanding

author.name: Jinyuan Deng, Yuqi Jiang, Wenjing Huang, Xin Li, Qi Sun, Cheng Zhuo

entry.summary: Circuit-MLLM targets circuit schematic understanding, a domain where dense component layouts and topological logic confound general multimodal models. It reformulates circuit analysis as device localization, path tracing, and sequential reasoning in latent space, supported by a circuit knowledge mining mechanism that aligns latent representations with structurally rich multi-granularity features.

entry.title: Scalable partial information decomposition for symptom networks via supervised embeddings

author.name: Cillian Hourican, Eric Dignum, Rick Quax, Debraj Roy

entry.summary: The paper introduces embedding-based PID (ePID), which compresses all nonfocal symptoms into a low-cardinality discrete embedding so that a tractable two-source partial information decomposition can be computed per symptom pair. This yields source-unique, remainder-unique, redundant, and synergistic information components that scalar edge weights in symptom networks cannot express. The method was benchmarked on synthetic Bayesian networks calibrated to PHQ-9 and on real symptom data, addressing a long-standing scalability barrier in psychometric network analysis.

entry.title: Curvature-Independent Regret Bounds for Distributed Online Optimization on Hadamard Manifolds

author.name: Zhanyuan Cai, Emre Sahinoglu, Shahin Shahrampour

entry.summary: The paper studies decentralized online Riemannian optimization on Hadamard manifolds and removes the usual dependence on curvature information for a narrower class of horospherical-convex functions. It analyzes Distributed Riemannian Online Gradient Descent with implicit Frechet-mean consensus, obtaining square-root and logarithmic regret for h-convex and strongly h-convex objectives.

entry.title: Exploring napping paradigm for Recurrent Spiking Neural Networks

author.name: Andreas Massey, Stefano Nichele, Aliaksandr Hubin

entry.summary: Motivated by how biological brains balance model accuracy against complexity during offline sleep, the authors test a micro-sleep napping paradigm for recurrent spiking neural networks that combines proportional weight scaling with continuous stochastic membrane activity. The work asks whether biologically inspired offline regularization can improve generalization in engineered SNNs.

entry.title: Retrieval-Guided Fine-Tuning as Noisy Estimation: Risk bounds and Architectural Analysis

author.name: Bhargav Lad, Yifan Hao

entry.summary: The paper models retrieval-guided fine-tuning as a noisy estimation problem in a multi-task linear regression framework, using an OLS proxy for single-layer linear self-attention to derive finite-sample risk bounds. It shows retrieval failure decays exponentially with task separation relative to noise and identifies when RAG-FT beats target-only or full-corpus training, introducing a distance-proportional noise model.

entry.title: Inverse Learning of the Altruism and Cost Level in Mixed-Individual Mean Field Games

author.name: Haoyang Cao, G\"ok\c{c}e Dayan{\i}kl{\i}, Xiaofei Shi

entry.summary: Mixed-individual mean field games interpolate between non-cooperative MFGs and fully altruistic mean field control via a parameter governing the degree of altruism. The authors address the regulator's problem that intrinsic altruism levels and private structural parameters such as individual labor costs are unobservable, formulating an inverse learning problem to recover them. The framework is continuous-time stochastic with large interacting populations.

entry.title: Fusing Spectral Signatures and Activation Clustering for Backdoor Detection in Healthcare Imaging Models: Method, Implementation, and Evaluation

author.name: Suresh Tamang

entry.summary: This work combines two established backdoor detection techniques, spectral signature analysis and activation clustering, into a fused detector aimed at healthcare imaging models, a setting where poisoning and adversarial attacks are named sector-level threats. The paper emphasizes method, implementation, and evaluation on medical imaging benchmarks, where reported detection results are relatively sparse.

entry.title: Editorial routing shapes how computational results are qualified in AI-assisted scientific writing

author.name: Jihan Kim

entry.summary: Holding computational evidence fixed, this study tests whether assigning comparisons across modeling choices to different locations in a research workflow (a group repository, Supporting Information, or working notes) changes how manuscripts report numerical qualifications. Anthropic's Claude Sonnet 5 often dropped numerical qualifications when comparisons were relegated to a group repository but retained them with SI or working notes; Claude Opus 5 was less sensitive, and a targeted placement rule largely restored sentence-level reporting.

entry.title: E2A-Bench: Benchmarking Evidence-to-Action Reliability in Financial Chart Reasoning

author.name: Xiaoya Wang, Yutong Xu, Junjie Wang

entry.summary: E2A-Bench is a 969-query benchmark for financial chart reasoning built from 323 HS300 constituents across three input modalities with deterministic OHLCV-derived evidence anchors. It evaluates grounding, reasoning-action consistency, evidence-confidence calibration, and directional coverage via UCR, RCI, ECI, and NDR, shifting evaluation from claim-centric hallucination checks to end-to-end evidence-to-action reliability.

entry.title: TATK: Triple-Aware Top-K Learning with Knowledge-Grounded Verification for LLM-based Sequential Recommendation

author.name: Yuchen Guan, Jiaye Liu, Yifei Han, Zhenxi Zhang, Yixuan Weng, Bin Li

entry.summary: TATK tackles the mismatch between text-generation interfaces and full-catalog top-K ranking in LLM-based sequential recommendation by combining position-aware top-K rewards with metadata knowledge-graph prompting, followed by structure-aware reranking of candidates. It is evaluated on three Amazon Reviews 2023 categories under a matched setting.

entry.title: Improving Mathematical Reasoning Capabilities in Large Language Models via Reasoning Process Error Classification

author.name: Runa Yoshida, Kosuke Nishida, Kyosuke Nishida

entry.summary: The authors manually analyze incorrect LLM solutions on math datasets, define 21 reasoning-error classes, and identify which classes occur most frequently. They then design a prompt that explicitly targets eight of these classes and show improved mathematical reasoning performance.

entry.title: Reliable Egocentric Action Anticipation via Temporal Reliability Suppression and Compositional Graph Decoding

author.name: Mahsa Mohammadi, Sareh Rowlands

entry.summary: The authors identify two failure modes for egocentric action anticipation under temporal corruption: unreliable evidence during encoding and implausible verb-noun combinations during decoding. They propose Temporal Reliability Suppression, which predicts a per-frame suppression score used as a learned attention penalty and for reliability-weighted pooling, plus Robust Verb-Noun Graph decoding that re-ranks compositions for plausibility. The work targets wearable anticipation systems that must stay reliable with missing frames, masking, and sensor noise.

entry.title: Contour-Guided Spectral Routing for Robust Real-Time Pedestrian Detection

author.name: Sam Williams, Yuan Xiang

entry.summary: The paper proposes a unified contour-guided spectral routing detector that explicitly orders spatial, spectral, and boundary information flow instead of bolting frequency processing, attention, and boundary reasoning onto a baseline separately. It targets three coupled failure modes in driving scenes: tiny targets, occlusion, and weather or illumination distortion. The value lies in a more principled representation pipeline for safety-critical real-time perception.

entry.title: ESAFusion: LiDAR--4-D Radar Fusion via Local Geometric Complementation and Multiscale Adaptive Interaction for 3-D Object Detection

author.name: Gang Ma, Senjie Hu, Junjie Liu, Chao Wang, Hui Wei

entry.summary: ESAFusion fuses LiDAR with 4D radar for 3D object detection under difficult driving conditions, using an evidence-aware radar selection module to suppress radar clutter and a scale-adaptive interaction scheme for multiscale feature exchange. It targets the challenges of sparse radar measurements, differing spatial sampling between modalities, and region-dependent modality importance. The work is relevant to robust perception where LiDAR alone degrades.

entry.title: PC$^2$-AD: Point Cloud Upsampling to Safeguard 3D Anomaly Detection with Resolution-constrained Edge Devices

author.name: Yutong Gu, Yingxi Xie, Kejin Huang, Jian Ning, Hanzhe Liang, Linlin Shen, Jinbao Wang

entry.summary: PC2-AD compensates for the train-test sampling-resolution gap in 3D anomaly detection, where low-cost edge sensors produce test point clouds far sparser than the normal training data. It adapts a pretrained upsampler to normal training geometry, filters candidates by geometric spacing and coverage, and refines selection using normality scores to avoid introducing anomalous structure. The aim is to protect detector reliability under resolution-constrained deployment.

entry.title: LG-VLN: A Zero-Shot Vision-and-Language Navigation Framework with LangGraph State Orchestration

author.name: Jianhe Zhao, Yanhua Qiu, Zhiyu Zhang, Zibo Zhao, Jinhua Xie

entry.summary: LG-VLN addresses continuous-environment vision-and-language navigation using only monocular input, avoiding LiDAR, panoramic cameras or extra sensors. An online feed-forward 3D reconstruction network predicts depth, poses and dense point clouds for agent-pose estimation and map fusion, while geometry and navigation share dense CleanDIFT features so semantic consistency can reject unreliable map updates. A LangGraph-based state orchestration layer manages the navigation state, targeting zero-shot generalization in unseen 3D environments.

entry.title: Learning to Exploit Passive Dynamics for Energy-Efficient Target Hopping of a Spring-Legged Quadcopter

author.name: Ruigang Chen, Qi Zhang, Zhicheng Zhong, Zhuorui Yun, Yizhar Or, Mingyi Liu

entry.summary: This work replaces heuristic PID tuning for a spring-legged monopedal quadcopter with a direct estimated-state-to-motor PPO policy that commands all four motors without a hopping state machine or low-level attitude controller. Its reward combines energy-manifold shaping for vertical-energy tracking and apex anchoring with an efficiency term that penalizes general and airborne power use and near-stationarity aloft.

entry.title: LabAgent: Customize Any Research Hubs for Scientific Discoveries Using AI Agents

author.name: Lei Liu, Yikun Zhang, Jialin Chen, Wanjia Zhao, Rex Ying, Wengong Jin, Hua Xu, James Zou, Tianyu Liu, Hongyu Zhao

entry.summary: LabAgent targets the continuity problem in labs, where departing staff take irreplaceable experimental methods with them. It proposes a reproduce-and-discovery harness with mechanisms that verify skill execution and record corrective experience so errors can be corrected or avoided, aiming to preserve and extend lab research capabilities.

entry.title: From Legal Text to AI-specific Risk Sources: A Systematic Analysis of the EU AI Act's High-Risk Requirements

author.name: Ronald Schnitzer, Mike Auer, Rumpa Choudhury, Andreas Hapfelmeier, Maximilian Hoeving, Isabelle Painter, Josiane Xavier Parreira, Sonja Zillner

entry.summary: The paper asks whether the EU AI Act's high-risk requirements cover the same risk sources as established AI risk taxonomies, noting no clear mapping currently exists between them. It performs a systematic classification intended to give practitioners a structured basis for aligning regulatory obligations with AI risk management practice.

entry.title: Bypass Observation: A Conceptual Design of a Non-Intrusive Layer-Wise Semantic Extraction Architecture

author.name: Haibin Tong, Jiang Yu

entry.summary: This paper introduces Bypass Observation, a read-only architecture that attaches observation heads to selected Transformer layers without feeding their outputs back into the backbone, with variants including shared, layer-specific, and adaptive heads. It derives a closed-form overhead approximation governed largely by V/(12d), estimates representative costs from roughly 30 to 240 percent, and discusses reductions via sparse observation, low-rank factorization, and top-k readout. It matters for interpretability and monitoring of internal model reasoning.

entry.title: From Ideas to Actions: A Public-Data Decision-Support Toolchain Across the Venture Lifecycle

author.name: Lei Qu (Shanghai Xing Yun Zhi Li AI Institute)

entry.summary: This paper describes a public-data decision-support toolchain for founders, combining proposal profiling, market and moat screening, and auditable investor-company event chains for retrospective analysis. It reports an F0.5 of 0.5357 on a held-out validation sample and roughly 0.63 on the combined set, versus about 0.27 for a raw LLM baseline.

entry.title: An Evolutionary Computation Framework for Multi-Agent Q-Learning with Mean-Field Environmental Feedback

author.name: Lichen Wang, Shijia Hua, Linjie Liu

entry.summary: The paper formulates a coupled learning-environment model in which agents run stateless Q-learning on a fixed graph while their average behavior drives an environmental variable that modifies payoffs. Under a mean-field closure they derive a deterministic transport equation for the Q-value distribution coupled to the environmental state. Finite-network Monte Carlo simulations validate the approximation.

entry.title: Adaptive Phase-Switching for Communication-Efficient Federated LoRA Fine-Tuning

author.name: Jerry Adams Franklin

entry.summary: This paper measures per-round upload and download bytes for a bidirectional B-only federated LoRA protocol, correcting prior accounting that omitted the asymmetric transition round and grouped-query attention shapes. It places five methods on a single communication-quality frontier and introduces ReverseAdaptive, an adaptive phase-switching aggregator that locates the frontier knee by monitoring relative improvement in global loss against a dimensionless criterion. It matters for cost-aware design of federated fine-tuning where communication, not computation, dominates.

entry.title: Real-Time Synthesis of Robust Controlled Invariant Sets for Monotone Systems

author.name: Yasin Sonmez, Mahmoud Khaled, Majid Zamani, Murat Arcak

entry.summary: The paper targets online computation of controlled invariant sets, formal safety certificates needed for safety-critical autonomous control, which standard synthesis algorithms compute too slowly as state dimension grows. For monotone systems with lower-closed safety specifications, the authors reformulate lower-closed sets on a d-dimensional grid as threshold functions represented by column heights along a designated axis, addressing the membership-test and redundancy-check bottlenecks of lazy fixed-point algorithms. It matters for real-time certified safety in high-dimensional monotone dynamics.

entry.title: How broad is that claim? Mapping Generalisation in NLP Research

author.name: Chenxin Diao, Nataliya Stepanova, Emily Allaway

entry.summary: This work introduces NLPGenX, a taxonomy for labeling scientific claims by their level of generality and framing, and NLPGenA, an LLM-powered framework that classifies sentences from scientific articles into five generalisation classes. The goal is automated detection of over-reliance on broad generalisations and potential misrepresentation of findings. The framework is validated with human annotators and applied to the NLP literature.

entry.title: Multi-View Molecular Representation Learning with Hierarchical Graphs and Contextualized Fingerprints

author.name: Gwang-Hyeon Yun, Jong-Hoon Park, Bing Hu, Helen Chen, Anita Layton, Young-Rae Cho

entry.summary: HiFi-Mol pretrains a hierarchical graph encoder and a contextualized fingerprint encoder separately, then integrates them for molecular property prediction. The graph branch uses fragment-aware masking with multi-resolution supervision, while the fingerprint branch tokenizes chemical patterns, together aiming to generalize to structurally novel compounds from limited labeled data.

entry.title: A Multi-Resolution Multi-Domain Pre-Training Framework for Universal Traffic Forecasting

author.name: Zhouyang Liu, Jindong Han, Hao Wang, Xinyue Liu, Hui Gao, Dongsheng Li, Hao Liu

entry.summary: FlexST is a pre-training framework for traffic forecasting that introduces modularity and adaptivity to handle highly heterogeneous spatio-temporal data. It uses a multi-resolution spatio-temporal diffusion module to capture both short-term fluctuations and long-range trends, aiming to reduce the parameter inefficiency and generalization limits of homogeneous pre-training paradigms.

entry.title: Machine Learning under Imperfect Data: Challenges and Methods

author.name: Masoumeh Zareapoor

entry.summary: This short survey organizes machine-learning methods that cope with incomplete, imbalanced, weakly labeled, or distribution-shifted data around a few shared mechanisms: information loss, biased empirical risk, ambiguous supervision, and unstable representations. It reframes these problems as symptoms of common learning pathologies rather than unrelated technical issues, offering a unifying lens for practitioners.

entry.title: T-SMART: Mechanism-Level Attribution for Tool-Augmented Time-Series Question Answering

author.name: Ivan Delgado, Himansi Gupta, Bishal Khatri, Niharika Sapre, Lameta Shamoon, Onat Gungor, Tajana Rosing

entry.summary: T-SMART is a neurosymbolic framework for time-series question answering that separates roles: a frozen LLM interprets questions and selects operations, deterministic tools perform the arithmetic, and structured perception is invoked only when needed. Controlled paired ablations attribute the dominant performance gains to deterministic computation, improving accuracy by about 31.7 percentage points.

entry.title: GNN4PPM: Multi-Target Predictive Process Monitoring with Relational Graph Convolutional Networks

author.name: Ana Costa, Johannes M\"akelburg, Luise Pufahl

entry.summary: GNN4PPM introduces a predictive process monitoring approach that predicts all next events together with their complete data payload in a single step, rather than only the activity label. It represents event-log information as a heterogeneous knowledge graph and applies relational graph convolutions to capture the richer recorded context that existing pipelines discard. This matters for business process analytics where payload attributes carry much of the actionable signal.

entry.title: Privacy Preserving Gossip Learning

author.name: Erkan Bayram, Mohamed-Ali Belabbas, Tamer Ba\c{s}ar

entry.summary: The paper proposes a decentralized learning algorithm in which each agent holds one private sample and a shared model, with updates required to preserve endpoint mappings at samples already learned. Building on Tuning without Forgetting, it shows an indistinguishability guarantee for the learner whenever the protected set contains another sample with the same label. It matters for privacy-preserving decentralized training where agents act as learner, teacher and protected party in turn.

entry.title: Large-scale bioacoustic detection using semantic segmentation: a deep learning framework applied to fin whale calls in ocean-bottom seismometer recordings

author.name: Jocelyn Japnanto, Alex A. Saoulis, Miriam Romagosa, Rita Leit\~ao, Gabrielle Arrieta, M\'onica A. Silva, Matthew Graham, Ana M. G. Ferreira

entry.summary: The authors repurpose ocean-bottom seismometer recordings, originally collected for geophysics, as a passive acoustic monitoring resource for baleen whales. They present a semantic segmentation framework that assigns each spectrogram pixel a probability of belonging to a fin whale 20 Hz call and converts probability maps into time-frequency bounding boxes. The model is trained on hydrophone data and applied to large, varied sensor networks.

entry.title: Speak to the City: Multimodal Resolution for Outside-the-Vehicle References

author.name: Alireza Parchami (Mercedes-Benz Tech Innovation GmbH, Saarland University), Artin Saberpour (Saarland University), Robin Connor Schramm (Mercedes-Benz Tech Innovation GmbH, RheinMain University of Applied Sciences), J\"urgen Steimle (Saarland University), Ulrich Schwanecke (RheinMain University of Applied Sciences)

entry.summary: The authors present a multimodal framework that fuses passenger gaze with natural language to resolve outside-the-vehicle references to points of interest, addressing ego-motion and referential ambiguity in vehicles and XR headsets. They build a VR pipeline synchronizing 360-degree transit video with GNSS telemetry and run a 46-participant study to collect gaze-speech behavior for training a lightweight transformer.

entry.title: Bridging the Gap in ECG-Based Emotion Recognition: A Unified Evaluation of Deep Learning Models

author.name: Timothy C Sweeney-Fanelli, Ajan Ahmed, Masudul Imtiaz

entry.summary: This study benchmarks prominent deep learning architectures for automated emotion recognition from ECG signals, arguing that inconsistent preprocessing and evaluation across prior work make comparisons meaningless. To enable fair and generalizable comparison rather than mere cross-dataset adaptation, the authors release two open-source frameworks and emphasize generalization over dataset adaptability. It matters as a corrective to a literature where reported gains are hard to trust.

entry.title: When Consistency Does Not Mean Reliability: Evaluating Local LLM Judges Against Human Ratings

author.name: Aakash Kumar Tiwari

entry.summary: This study asks whether LLM judges that score responses consistently actually agree with humans, using two local open-weight judges (LLaMA-3-8B and Qwen2.5-7B) to score 300 GPT-2-generated responses three times each against nine human annotators across five question categories. It separates self-consistency from human agreement, exposing a gap that common judge-validation practice obscures.

entry.title: SHIFT-M3: Pre-fusion Alignment-based Consistency Screening for Multimodal ECG Record Integrity

author.name: Md Ashik Khan, Md Nahid Siddique

entry.summary: SHIFT-M3 treats multimodal clinical record integrity as a triage problem: before fusing waveform, report, and metadata, a lightweight text-based screen checks whether two independently produced ECG text views (an LLM interpretation and a clinical report summary) are consistent. Evaluated on 784,680 MEETI ECG records, it targets silent cross-patient linkage failures that standard predictive models are not designed to catch.

entry.title: Tone on a Budget: A Reference-Free Metric for Lexical Tone in Massively Multilingual Text-to-Speech

author.name: Moses Daudu, Adeola Enitan Bamidele, Honor-Jesus Bezaleel

entry.summary: The paper argues that character error rate computed from ASR output silently drops Yoruba tone diacritics, so a synthesizer can score well while producing the wrong word. It introduces DunDun, a reference-free lexical tone metric that reads the gold High/Mid/Low sequence directly from input diacritics and compares it with predictions, requiring no tone-labeled corpus.

entry.title: Can We Triage LLM Translation Errors in Classical Texts Without Human References? Source Novelty, GEMBA Scoring, and Budgeted Review through Pali-to-English Translation

author.name: M\'at\'e Metzger

entry.summary: This study tests reference-free error triage for Pali-to-English translation across 15,493 passages produced by three LLMs, comparing source novelty, embedding distance, peer disagreement, backtranslation, and GEMBA scoring. Signals were calibrated on LLM-adjudicated and author-adjudicated samples, with human references used only for calibration and never as inputs to the risk signals.

entry.title: Parameter-Efficient Quantum NLP for Paraphrase Detection: Performance, Robustness, and Entanglement

author.name: Farha Nausheen, Khandakar Ahmed, Farina Riaz

entry.summary: The authors empirically evaluate a 10-qubit hybrid quantum-classical variational circuit with only 2,148 parameters for paraphrase detection on MRPC, Quora Question Pairs, and adversarial PAWS. The circuit reaches 75.53 percent accuracy on QQP across ten seeds, statistically beating parameter-matched classical baselines and surpassing a 4-bit DistilBERT with far fewer parameters, while MRPC results approach BERT-base at much lower parameter cost. Circuit-depth scaling and entanglement analyses are included.

entry.title: ArtSociety: Multi-Agent Multimodal Collaboration for Art Emotion Understanding

author.name: Jian Li, Fanfan Ji, Jinxiang Lai, Ying Tai, Jian Yang, Xiao-Tong Yuan, Chengjie Wang, Yabiao Wang

entry.summary: ArtSociety is a multi-agent framework addressing the AffectiveArt task of jointly predicting fine-grained art emotion across 12 classes with a 1549:1 head-to-tail ratio, binary valence and arousal, and five attribute-grounded descriptions. It assembles heterogeneous experts including a DINOv2-Giant vision agent, a scene-grounded chain-of-thought fine-tuned MLLM, and three closed-source reasoning agents, coordinated by training-free controllers such as a rare-class-aware voting arbiter that lowers agreement thresholds for tail emotions. The design targets empirical trade-offs that single models handle poorly.

entry.title: A Comprehensive Review of Multimodal Facial State Analysis: Tasks, Methods, and Resources

author.name: Xuri Ge, Tianshuo Zhang, Ruihan Li, Hui Ye, Kaiwen Zheng, Junchen Fu, Da Huo, Joemon M. Jose, Hu Han

entry.summary: This survey reviews multimodal facial state analysis, which integrates visual, audio, textual, and physiological cues to overcome the environmental sensitivity and weak interpretability of unimodal vision methods. It emphasizes two threads: multimodal learning for contextual semantic understanding and interpretable language generation, plus multi-task learning for jointly analyzing expressions, action units, and related states. The paper catalogs tasks, methods, and available resources.

entry.title: Rank-Consistent Set Reasoning for Co-Salient Object Detection

author.name: Yuan Xiang, Matteo Rossi, Yingzhou Chen

entry.summary: Rank-Consistent Set Reasoning (RCSR) models an image group for co-salient object detection as an unordered set rather than a sequence or a semantic label. It ranks how strongly each spatial region agrees with a small set of learned group slots at every scale and aggregates ranks with a robust trimmed statistic, suppressing accidental pairwise matches and preventing one atypical group member from dominating. A set encoder builds group slots directly from multi-scale visual features.

entry.title: MoVT: Video-Augmented Motion Tokenizer for Text-to-Motion Generation

author.name: Beibei Jing, Tianle Guo, Youjia Zhang, Zikai Song, Yawei Luo, Junqing Yu, Tao Guan, Wei Yang

entry.summary: MoVT tackles the scarcity of 3D motion training data for text-to-motion generation by leveraging large-scale human action videos. Its core component is a cross-modal augmented motion tokenizer that projects discrete 3D motion tokens into 2D space, enriches the motion codebook with real-world motion patterns learned from video, and maps the enriched tokens back to 3D so that 2D and 3D codebooks stay aligned. The approach is intended to broaden the diversity of motions a generator can produce from unconstrained text prompts.

entry.title: Beyond Dead Reckoning: A Point of View on Camera--DAS--GNSS Continuity in Road Tunnels

author.name: Lyes Saad Saoud, Hesham A. Rakha, Mona Jaber, Moussa Ayyash

entry.summary: This position paper argues that tunnel localization for connected and automated vehicles should be treated as infrastructure-assisted cross-modal track continuity rather than extrapolation from the last trusted satellite fix. It sketches a stack where a portal satellite fix provides the global anchor, distributed acoustic sensing supplies continuous motion evidence, cameras give sparse identity and lane anchors, onboard sensors handle short-term dynamics, and edge computing handles association, fusion, integrity monitoring, and guarded reacquisition. Ground truth is reserved for offline calibration and validation, and the paper lays out a falsifiable research and deployment agenda.

entry.title: Watch AI materials-science & bioscience abilities closely

author.name: Yair Halberstadt

entry.summary: An argument that near-term biorisk depends on whether spiky-capability LLMs can design dangerous pathogens, which requires iterative lab access rather than a single act of deception. It proposes watching AI progress in materials and biological sciences as an early-warning indicator and compares such achievements to finding a single satisfying counterexample.

entry.title: Governing at Machine Speed: An Adaptive Intelligence Architecture for Real-Time AI Policy Enforcement

author.name: Sandeep Bokkasam, B. Durgalakshmi

entry.summary: The paper diagnoses an 'attestation deficit': organizations have AI governance policies but cannot produce auditable, tamper-evident evidence of enforcement within regulatory deadlines. Using figures from the Stanford AI Index, IBM/Ponemon breach-cost study and an industry consortium survey, it argues the failure is organizational and architectural, and proposes an adaptive intelligence architecture for real-time policy enforcement.

entry.title: FLoKD: Adaptive Knowledge Distillation for Federated Low-Rank LLM over Wireless Networks

author.name: Xinlu Zhang, Na Yan, Yang Su, Yansha Deng, Toktam Mahmoodi

entry.summary: FLoKD targets federated fine-tuning of LLMs without sharing raw client data, where LoRA still imposes communication costs that scale with model size and token-level distillation logits are expensive to transmit. The method combines low-rank adaptation with adaptive knowledge distillation to cut communication overhead for deployment over bandwidth-constrained wireless networks.

entry.title: FedV-KGQA in Practice: Design Lessons and an Interactive Prototype

author.name: Md Saikat Islam Khan Bappy, Oshani Seneviratne

entry.summary: This poster reports empirical findings from FedV-KGQA, a method for multi-hop question answering over vertically partitioned knowledge graphs where each organization holds disjoint relation types. Each silo trains a knowledge graph embedding locally and a server concatenates silo-specific entity views to rank candidates, so raw triples never leave the silo. It matters for privacy-preserving federated reasoning over distributed enterprise knowledge.

entry.title: Beyond Scene Description: Multi-Agent Orchestration for Non-visual Access to Virtual Worlds

author.name: Toqeer Ali Syed, Ali Akarma, Adeel Ahmad, Danial Hameed

entry.summary: The paper observes that assistive tools for blind and visually impaired users each solve one isolated task, which fails in a live virtual room where obstacles, speakers, gestures, chat and notifications arrive simultaneously. MetaBlind distributes nonvisual access across eight specialized agents covering perception, navigation and related functions to avoid trading a visual barrier for an auditory one.

entry.title: Variational Template Matching with Statistical Fusion for Anomaly Detection in Patterned Structures

author.name: Qinwu Xu, Yifan Jiang

entry.summary: The paper proposes a variational template matching framework that represents anomaly templates as a family of transformed instances and detects them via normalized cross-correlation over the transformation space, improving robustness to scale, rotation, and perspective variation. A density-based statistical anomaly score from kernel density estimation adds a smooth score capturing distributional tails. The method targets small-data industrial inspection settings where deep learning is impractical.

entry.title: Feasibility and Memory Mechanisms of Chern-Simons Context Reservoir Computation

author.name: Jyotiranjan Beuria, Venkatesh H. Chembrolu

entry.summary: This paper asks whether a reservoir computer built on Chern-Simons gauge dynamics is a usable computational substrate, and whether evolving the gauge connection adds anything beyond simpler dynamical mechanisms. The authors compare four matched reservoir models - reciprocal transport, instantaneous transverse reconstruction, local nonlinear feedback, and fully coupled conserved-current Chern-Simons dynamics - across ten random seeds, checking Gauss law propagation, convergence under refinement, and stability under constraints. The work matters mainly as a physics-inspired computing feasibility study that isolates which effects are genuinely gauge-specific versus generic reservoir behavior.

entry.title: SGWIB:Sliced Gromov-Wasserstein Information Bottleneck for Video Highlight Detection

author.name: Hanjuan Huang, Yung-Chieh Yeh, Hsing-Kuo Pao

entry.summary: The paper introduces the Sliced Gromov-Monge Gap, a structure-aware regularizer that extends the information bottleneck principle to video highlight detection while preserving temporal relationships among neighboring and distant segments. Conventional information bottleneck formulations would compress away inter-segment relational structure, so the authors build a sliced Gromov-Wasserstein variant that keeps highlight-relevant temporal organization intact. It matters as a first information-bottleneck formulation for this task family.

entry.title: LPA-CWM: A Learned Physical Adjudicator for Motion Reasoning with Counterfactual World Models

author.name: Kunwei Wu, Xiang Liu, Guocai Yao, Junming Chen, Zhikang Chen, Min Zhang, Pengwei Wang, Sen Cui

entry.summary: The paper addresses counterfactual world models that extract motion by comparing factual and intervened video predictions, noting that responses from different target-frame masks vary in reliability while uniform aggregation treats them equally. LPA-CWM adds a small 3.0M-parameter learned physical adjudicator that predicts relative weights for unordered candidate responses while keeping the video predictor and intervention generator frozen, followed by windowed localization and a paired re-evaluation step. It matters as a lightweight way to improve motion extraction from pretrained video models.

entry.title: Assessing the Applicability of Existing Design Recommendations to AI Companion Design: A Multi-Method Study

author.name: Soobin Cho, Deveshi Modi, Divya Mavinkurve, Jieqiong Ding, Mark Zachry

entry.summary: This multi-method study examines whether existing design guidance for trustworthy and relational AI systems transfers to LLM-based AI companions, which are built for emotional connection rather than instrumental tasks. It characterizes what makes companion design hard, given relational, emotional and potentially long-term interactions. It matters for HCI and responsible design as companion apps proliferate rapidly.

entry.title: TriCalRAG: A Three-Strategy, Retrieval-Augmented Benchmark for On-Premise LLM-Based Root Cause Analysis in AIOps

author.name: Rohit Patel, Susil Kumar Mohanty, Jeenal Chaudhary

entry.summary: TriCalRAG benchmarks open-weight LLMs served locally via vLLM on a single high-memory workstation GPU against a classical LSTM log anomaly detector (DeepLog) across four public log datasets. It compares two open-weight models under zero-shot, few-shot and retrieval-augmented prompting over labeled incident history. The motivation is data privacy, latency and per-query cost that make cloud-hosted LLM root cause analysis impractical at production log volumes.

entry.title: Enemray: Toward Capable Language Models for Hassaniya

author.name: Cheikh Ahmed

entry.summary: Enemray is a Hassaniya-centric language model built with a stability-plasticity objective: gain strong Hassaniya linguistic and cultural competence while retaining the reasoning, multilingual, instruction-following and safety behavior of a base instruction-tuned model. The pipeline separates language acquisition from behavioral specialization using a continual-pretraining corpus, layer-selective continual pretraining, transfer into instruction-tuned parameter space, and supervised fine-tuning.

entry.title: Interpolation Is Not Invariance: Pair Count Is Not Coverage in Transformation Audits

author.name: Mohammed Ahnouch, Lotfi Elaachak

entry.summary: This work argues that counting equivalent pairs in transformation audits overstates coverage, because pairs derived from the same semantic object are correlated and orbit graphs contain redundant edges. It distinguishes edge count, effective contrast rank, population support rank and graph spectral gap, characterizes their roles in audit coverage, and derives conditions for the existence of population-invariant calibrated readers.

entry.title: IMPACT-VLA: Interaction-aware Multimodal Propagation Attribution via Counterfactual Trajectories for Vision-Language-Action Policies

author.name: Jinwoong Kim, Sangjin Park

entry.summary: IMPACT-VLA investigates which execution stages and modalities contribute to success in Vision-Language-Action robot policies, going beyond local sensitivity or temporally aggregated importance. It constructs behavioral phases and uses counterfactual trajectories to attribute how input interventions propagate through subsequent states, observations and actions, capturing phase-dependent contributions and cross-phase dependencies.

entry.title: Validating Hybrid-State Cache Recovery for GLM-5.3-Flash with vLLM and LMCache

author.name: Frank Li

entry.summary: This engineering study examines state-recovery consistency when using external KV cache transfers with a 45-layer GLM-5.3-Flash model, a quantized NVFP4 checkpoint, vLLM and LMCache under four-way tensor parallelism. It reports a recovery mismatch where the full prompt state was restored but the scheduler credited one fewer token, and shows that strict-prefix lookup alignment improved agreement with a recomputation control from 34/36 to 36/36 generations.

entry.title: Personalizing Personal Health Interfaces: Co-Design with Generative AI

author.name: Karthik S. Bhat, Vidhi Shah, Vedika Agnihotri, Dong Whi Yoo, Koustuv Saha

entry.summary: A co-design study in which 14 participants used Figma Make to redesign Google and Apple Health dashboards, exploring what generative AI enables and constrains in personal health interface design. Participants produced more personal, forward-looking and interactive designs, but conversational AI concepts converged on familiar chat-window patterns, suggesting a tension between imagined personalization and generative tooling defaults.

entry.title: Generate to Explore, Select to Exploit: Aligning LLM-based Headline Generation with Personalized Recommendation

author.name: Yi Chen, Rufeng Cheng, Qiang Xie, Tao Li

entry.summary: This industrial paper addresses headline generation in recommendation feeds, arguing that optimizing an LLM to produce one best headline causes mode collapse toward generic, average-taste text that harms long-tail audiences. The proposed GESE framework decouples personalization into generative exploration of diverse headlines and selective exploitation, operating at the presentation layer rather than in ranking.

entry.title: DepthBenchCAD: When Does Deeper Auditing Yield More Reliable Conclusions?

author.name: Hongye Yang, Zhihao Xie, Shengjun Xiong, Boxiao Huang

entry.summary: The paper questions the intuition that auditing more parameter edits per generative CAD program always yields more reliable evaluation, since a fixed budget means deeper audits reduce the number of tasks and generations sampled. It decomposes evaluation into task templates, stochastic generations and within-program edits, defining an audit-depth-invariant average failure risk and analyzing variance against measured execution costs.

entry.title: TEAR: Table Extraction with Attribute Recommendation from Texts via Large Language Models

author.name: Tong Li, Shuye Ding, Jiachuan Wang, Yongqi Zhang, Shuangyin Li, Lei Chen, Bo Li

entry.summary: TEAR tackles table extraction from naturally occurring texts such as news and social media, a setting where high variability and missing structural cues defeat fixed heuristic prompts and where manually predefined schemas cannot capture the needed columns. The method combines LLM-based extraction with attribute recommendation so the schema is induced rather than supplied.

entry.title: Spook the Machine: Gamified Exploration of Human Imagination of Machine Fear

author.name: Levin Brinkmann, Hiromu Yakura, Sonia Nicoletti, Mar Canet Sola, Thomas F. Eisenmann, Ali Dasmeh, Omar Sherif, Bramantyo Ibrahim Supriyatno, Prateek Gupta, Ignacio Serna, Rodrigo Bermudez Schettino, Iyad Rahwan

entry.summary: Spook the Machine is a gamified platform where participants generate images intended to frighten AI agents endowed with personality-driven phobias, with machines responding from calm analysis to begging for mercy and successful scares shown to later users. In a Halloween 2024 public deployment, 832 participants created 15,719 artifacts across 89 machines in a 2x2 design varying emotional expressiveness and reward structure. The study explores how humans imagine and engage with machine affect in human-AI interaction.

entry.title: Don't Count the Edits, Judge by the Outcome Alone: Reward-Based Evaluation for Grammatical Error Correction

author.name: Hayeong Ryu, Sunhee Jo, Seunguk Yu, YoungBin Kim

entry.summary: The authors propose SURE, a source-conditioned reward evaluator for grammatical error correction trained on within-source preferences spanning minimal-edit and rewrite-oriented corrections. SURE jointly learns an overall reward with criteria-level supervision for grammaticality, faithfulness, and fluency, plus span-level grounding for source-side error resolution. Experiments on SEEDA show competitive performance against strong baselines, with particular gains in settings where valid rewrites diverge from gold references.

entry.title: Predictive Likelihood Ratios for Language Model Watermark Detection

author.name: Li Ma

entry.summary: This paper builds predictive likelihood ratio tests for keyed watermark detection in language models, averaging over uncertain probability deficits and residual-tail distributions rather than requiring a single tuned signal strength. It uses a mixture prior over tail shape and effective width with hierarchical extensions, and analyzes power properties under an exact conditional pivot null.

entry.title: Benchmarking Intra-Patient 3D Deformable Multimodal Image Registration

author.name: Matteo Barbieri, Giammarco La Barbera, Juan Pablo De La Plata, Sabine Sarnacki, Isabelle Bloch, Pietro Gori

entry.summary: This work benchmarks intra-patient 3D multimodal deformable image registration across three datasets spanning different anatomical regions and difficulty levels, including synthetic deformation recovery and real clinical cases. It compares classical optimization-based registration with modern learning-based and foundation-model approaches using complementary metrics such as Dice and 95th-percentile Hausdorff distance.

entry.title: LLM-Based Schema-Aware Split Learning for Privacy-Preserving Mental Distress Prediction Across Heterogeneous Surveys

author.name: Md Khalid Syfullah, Alvi Ataur Khalil

entry.summary: This paper proposes a schema-aware split learning framework that uses an LLM as a shared semantic encoder to harmonize heterogeneous mental health survey schemas across institutions without pooling raw data. Each survey record is serialized into natural-language descriptions so that models can be trained collaboratively while preserving privacy. It targets a practical obstacle in collaborative mental health research: incompatible question formats and scales across data holders.

entry.title: GeoTTER: Leveraging Local Geometry of Optimal Transport for Zero-Shot Classification

author.name: Wei-Yang Alex Lee, Rudrasis Chakraborty, Vishnu Lokhande

entry.summary: GeoTTER reframes zero-shot classification as an optimal transport problem that adapts its cost structure instead of relying on fixed embedding-derived costs. It injects local geometric structure via graph-Laplacian smoothing to curb label jaggedness and corrects angular drift, aiming to improve calibration and neighborhood consistency in the assignment.

entry.title: Graph Neural Networks for Influence Maximization in Social Networks: An Unsupervised Minimum Dominating Set Approach

author.name: Erfan Ahmadi, Mina Shirazi, Behnam Bahrak

entry.summary: The paper presents an unsupervised graph neural network framework for the NP-hard Minimum Dominating Set problem, targeting influence maximization and related social-network applications. Its key feature is eliminating the need for ground-truth solutions during training, addressing the scalability limits of classical combinatorial solvers.

entry.title: Learning Through Energy Refinement and Manifold Projection: A Cooperative EBM-AE Framework

author.name: Ryad Zemouri

entry.summary: The paper introduces a cooperative Energy-Based Model and Autoencoder framework that jointly trains an EBM with a denoising autoencoder and iterates EBM to AE to EBM sampling to alternate Langevin refinement with manifold projection. The goal is to reduce the computational cost and sampling difficulty that have long hampered energy-based generative modeling.

entry.title: CyFM: Cylindrical Optimal Transport for Few-Step Complex-Valued Flow Matching

author.name: Marcel Musia{\l}ek, Iga Wolanin, Damian Ryczko, Anna Grelewska, Oleksii Furman

entry.summary: CyFM treats complex-valued signals such as MRI and audio spectrograms in their natural amplitude-phase cylindrical geometry rather than as flat two-channel Euclidean data, replacing the inherited metric with a decoupled product metric. The empirical study derives analytic bridges and measures the cost and benefit of this substitution for few-step flow matching.

entry.title: Should All Noises Be Treated Equally: Impact of Input Noise Variability on Neural Network Robustness

author.name: Salma Alsinan, Maksim Makarenko, Sixiu Liu, Ali Aldawood, Ibrahim Hoteit

entry.summary: This paper studies how the type, scale and complexity of input noise affect the performance, generalization and robustness of neural networks on two geophysical tasks, first-break picking and seismic denoising. Using simulated seismic-while-drilling data with controlled stochastic noise augmentation, the authors characterize when models break down under out-of-distribution noise. It matters because it argues against treating all corruption as interchangeable in augmentation pipelines for real field data.

entry.title: HGTO: A Unified Graph-Based Physics-Informed Formulation for Structural Topology Optimization

author.name: Kangzheng Liu, Uday Kumar Punna, Leixin Ma

entry.summary: HGTO reformulates neural topology optimization from coordinate-space fields to finite-element graph space, parameterizing element densities on the element graph and determining structural state on the corresponding node-element graph. This lets the method exploit the discrete relations inherent in the finite element mesh rather than treating density and displacement as generic coordinate fields. It matters for data-free topology optimization in structural design.

entry.title: Sensory Precision Inference for Multimodal Arbitration under Uncertainty

author.name: Tin Mi\v{s}i\'c, Takato Horii

entry.summary: The paper proposes a multimodal perceptual inference model in which latent beliefs and modality-specific sensory precisions are jointly updated through iterative free-energy minimization, allowing adaptive arbitration when modalities conflict or degrade. It addresses the underexplored role of dynamically inferred precision in active-inference accounts of multisensory conflict. It matters for autonomous agents that cannot assume all sensory streams remain informative.

entry.title: A Lifecycle Cost Analysis of Smart-Contract-Coordinated Federated Learning Marketplaces

author.name: Luan Mantegazine, Luiza Leidemer, Claudio Geyer

entry.summary: This paper presents an experimental study of the operational cost of a DAO-governed federated learning marketplace coordinated by smart contracts. It decomposes gas consumption for every blockchain operation across the contract lifecycle, runs ablations isolating the impact of on-chain coordination and IPFS storage on federated training, and derives cost implications for operating at scale.

entry.title: Machine learning-assisted calibration of Agent-based Models: surrogate-based optimization with Genetic Algorithm and Particle Swarm Optimization

author.name: Duguma Yeshitla Habtemariam, Jihwan Lee

entry.summary: The study adapts surrogate-assisted evolutionary computation to the difficult problem of calibrating agent-based models, where objectives are stochastic, rugged, and only evaluable through costly simulation. A machine learning surrogate screens candidate parameters each iteration and only the top half are validated in the simulator, reducing simulation demand while correcting surrogate error. A full factorial sweep over two optimizers, five surrogates, and four calibration objectives is run on two contrasting ABMs.

entry.title: ViFA-Council: Multi-Agent LLM Deliberation for Vietnamese Folk Art Generation

author.name: Hai-Dang Nguyen, Minh-Phuong Pham, Thao Thi Phuong Dao, Trong-Le Do, Vinh-Tiep Nguyen, Trung-Nghia Le

entry.summary: ViFA-Council is a three-stage multi-agent framework in which several large language models deliberate to handle image outpainting and educational story generation grounded in traditional Vietnamese folk paintings. It orchestrates collaboration among GPT-4o, Gemini 3.1 Pro, and Claude Sonnet 4.6, using task-specific JSON schemas to enforce cultural constraints and enable cross-model critique. The motivation is that single-model pipelines suffer stylistic hallucination and cultural misrepresentation.

entry.title: HQARRF: Hierarchical Q-learning and Force-aware Routing for Multi-Charger Scheduling in Wireless Rechargeable Sensor Networks

author.name: Liang-Ching Tao, Pi-Chung Wang

entry.summary: The paper presents a two-level scheduler for multi-charger wireless rechargeable sensor networks. A lower-level interpretable ARR-F score ranks clusters by combining attraction to urgent sensors, repulsion from charger crowding, and a force bonus, while an upper-level gated Q-learning controller decides whether to redirect service to high-risk, under-served zones using compressed zone state. Reported results across 27 parameter settings show improved coverage and reduced duplicated service.

entry.title: Parameter Estimation of Ringdown Quasinormal Modes with Autoencoder

author.name: Momoka Iida, Hayato Motohashi, Hirotaka Takahashi

entry.summary: The paper develops an autoencoder framework for analyzing multi-component quasinormal modes in black hole ringdown gravitational waves, training the latent space to represent physical mode parameters so that denoising and parameter estimation happen jointly. It targets the difficulty of separating overlapping modes in noisy signals.

entry.title: Prescreening Point Defects in Semiconductors With Machine Learning

author.name: Paul Karlsson, Joel Davidsson, Rickard Armiento

entry.summary: The paper explores physics-guided machine learning models for predicting defect formation energies and zero-phonon lines to prescreen point defects for quantum applications. The models are designed specifically to avoid the costly relaxation step of machine learning interatomic potentials so they can serve as a fast filter in high-throughput density-functional-theory workflows.

entry.title: A Game-Theoretic Framework for Incentive-Compatible AI training Under Renewable-Energy Constraints

author.name: Konstantinos Varsos, Ramin Khalili, Adamantia Stamou, George D. Stamoulis, Vasillios A. Siris

entry.summary: The paper models carbon-aware distributed AI training as a game in which autonomous agents choose whether and how intensively to participate given limited renewable energy availability across heterogeneous cloud and edge nodes. It aims to align training workloads with periods of excess renewable generation while keeping participation incentive-compatible. It matters for the sustainability of large-scale collaborative training and for scheduling compute against variable low-carbon supply.

entry.title: Learning under Target Shift: Optimal Density Ratio Estimation and Importance-Weighted Regression

author.name: Ren-Rui Liu, Zheng-Chu Guo

entry.summary: This work tackles density ratio estimation and importance-weighted regression under target shift with continuous outputs, where the input-conditional distribution stays fixed but the output marginal changes. The authors propose an RKHS-based spectral regularization method and, notably, establish finite-sample convergence rates that prior methods lacked for the continuous case. The result strengthens the theoretical toolkit for distribution shift correction in regression.

entry.title: Quenched Ensemble Sampling

author.name: David Yallup

entry.summary: The paper introduces Quenched Ensemble Sampling, which relaxes the hard energy constraint of nested sampling into a family of repulsive potentials at the energy boundary, preserving the quenched path of decreasing energy while enabling scalable gradient-based kernels. This targets the practical failure of samplers at phase transitions in physical systems. It could broaden nested sampling's applicability in high-dimensional scientific inference.

entry.title: Token Merging for Multilingual Speech Recognition: A Systematic Study Across Model Scale and Fine-Tuning

author.name: Dylan Luke Holyoak

entry.summary: This systematic study evaluates token merging, a training-free inference-time sequence-shortening technique, on the Whisper family across sixteen languages and three model sizes, including interactions with DoRA fine-tuning for low-resource languages. It finds substantial efficiency gains with almost no accuracy loss in most settings. The work is a practical guide for deploying multilingual ASR under compute constraints.

entry.title: RFCLLM: Evaluating LLMs' Reasoning Ability of Network Protocol State Machines

author.name: Anqi Chen, Dan Goldwasser, Cristina Nita-Rotaru

entry.summary: RFCLLM assesses whether LLMs can correctly interpret natural-language protocol specifications by mapping them into finite-state transition systems and comparing against manually built ground truth. The authors design four tasks and 1482 queries spanning sixteen protocols, and analyze judge biases and difficulty gaps. The work is relevant to security-critical uses of LLMs for protocol analysis and testing.

entry.title: CVSS-X: A Multilingual Speech-to-Speech Translation Corpus for 28 Languages

author.name: Lucas Rafael Stefanel Gris, Alef Iury Siqueira Ferreira, Frederico Santos de Oliveira, Augusto Seben da Rosa, Alexandre Costa Ferro Filho, Arlindo Rodrigues Galv\~ao Filho, Anderson da Silva Soares

entry.summary: CVSS-X is a large synthetic speech-to-speech translation corpus translating English into 28 target languages across twelve families, with roughly 240,000 parallel speech pairs per language and over 16,000 hours, eight times larger than its predecessor CVSS. It offers canonical-voice and cross-lingual voice-cloning variants, enabling bidirectional S2ST research when combined with CVSS. The resource lowers data barriers for low-resource spoken translation.

entry.title: Neyshekar: An Open Persian Read-Speech Corpus for Automatic Speech Recognition

author.name: Ahmad Amirivojdan, Farzad Nadiri, Abolfazl Alizadeh, Shaghayegh Yaraghi

entry.summary: The paper introduces Neyshekar, an open Persian read-speech corpus covering formal and informal registers, named entities, and longer utterances, with roughly 99 hours of validated recordings from 190 contributors. It documents the prompt-construction, normalization, and validation pipeline, including automatic register labeling that is not human-verified.

entry.title: Personalized and Explainable Blood Pressure Estimation from PPG via Hybrid CNN--Morphological Features

author.name: Myung-Kyu Yi, Jongshill Lee, Jeyeon Lee, In Young Kim
