entry.summary: This work proposes a physiology-guided hybrid framework for cuffless blood pressure estimation from photoplethysmography that couples a CNN branch capturing waveform dynamics with a morphology-prior branch encoding person-specific vascular characteristics. The design targets two weaknesses of prior work: the fragility of handcrafted fiducial-point methods and the black-box nature of deep models. Personalization and physiological interpretability are emphasized for continuous monitoring.

entry.title: Preserving Subject-Clarity in Image Outpainting with Multiscale Wavelet Supervision

author.name: Abhilash Neog, Taewan Kim, Yi Wu, Xu Chen, Jian Jiao

entry.summary: This work targets image outpainting for commercial imagery, where poor framing and truncated subjects or text degrade subject clarity, defined as an image's ability to communicate its primary subject. The proposed framework combines vision-language-model-guided semantic conditioning with multiscale wavelet supervision to improve structural consistency and fine-detail fidelity beyond typical diffusion outpainting. The goal is to extend image boundaries without the semantic drift and detail loss common in prior methods.

entry.title: The MODA General Attribute Suite: A Four-Track Evaluation Benchmark for Fashion Attribute Extraction

author.name: Arkid Mitra (Hopit AI)

entry.summary: This paper releases a four-track benchmark for fashion attribute extraction that deliberately separates garment crops, catalogue product images, applicability-aware full-body photos, and product text, each with its own frozen test set, input contract, metric and leakage unit. The protocol adds label-blind prediction and SHA-256 commitment of predictions to make results auditable, addressing the common practice of collapsing heterogeneous settings into one aggregate score. It matters as measurement infrastructure for an applied commercial domain.

entry.title: Target-Checked Reliability Score Refinement for Video Question Answering

author.name: Guoxiang Ren, Rohitash Chandra

entry.summary: This paper studies whether answer-level reliability scores from video-language models can be improved under target shift without retraining models or changing their answers. It collects option-probability lists from three fixed video-language models across four deterministic video samplings, represents cross-view changes and cross-model agreement as a response graph, and compares the raw chosen-answer probability against a boosted-tree score and a logistic-regression score calibrated on a labeled target pilot. The contribution is a cheap post-hoc calibration recipe for high-confidence errors.

entry.title: Accelerating HKTex without Mesh Eigensystems: Local Unfolding and Randomized Thermal Features

author.name: Zhewen He, Junyi Hu, Yi Fang

entry.summary: This paper removes the global Laplace-Beltrami eigendecomposition bottleneck in Heat Kernel Texture evaluation by replacing spectral evaluation with radius-bounded local unfolding and an analytic log-map kernel, plus randomized thermal features. It reports modest PSNR improvements on Objaverse meshes while cutting initialization cost roughly 40x and scaling to large proxy meshes. It matters for practical intrinsic appearance rendering.

entry.title: Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning of Foundation Models for Liver Tumor Segmentation in CT

author.name: Ramtin Mojtahedi, Mohammad Hamghalam, Jacob J. Peoples, Richard K. G. Do, Amber L. Simpson

entry.summary: This study benchmarks PEFT strategies for adapting a frozen SAM backbone to liver tumor segmentation in abdominal CT, comparing LoRA, QLoRA, a convolutional adapter, and a proposed Directional Spectral Top-K adapter (DiSCo). DiSCo uses SVD-derived spectral bases with rank-gated coefficients and about 0.14M trainable parameters, evaluated across five prompting regimes. It matters for cheaply adapting foundation segmentation models to clinical tasks.

entry.title: MorphoStyle: Motion Style Transfer with Morphology Control

author.name: Xin Feng, Eleonora D'Arnese, Mohan Sridharan

entry.summary: MorphoStyle performs shape-aware motion style transfer on top of a shape-conditioned Finite-Scalar-Quantization VAE, jointly controlling action content, style, and body morphology. It targets the failure mode where naive combinations of style transfer and shape-aware generators leak action content from the style reference and break shape-consistent kinematics. It matters for character animation across non-canonical body shapes.

entry.title: Sparsity-Adaptive Sharpness-Aware Minimization

author.name: Shiryu Ueno, Yoshikazu Hayashi, Kunihito Kato

entry.summary: SA-SAM derives a sparsity-dependent perturbation radius for sharpness-aware minimization by keeping mean absolute perturbation approximately invariant as sparsity increases, addressing the loss of corruption robustness in heavily pruned networks. It also evaluates a Magnitude-Weighted Hessian importance measure derived from second-order removal-path analysis. It matters for deploying compact, robust models.

entry.title: PRI-Net: A Lightweight Multimodal Framework for 3D UAV Localization

author.name: Zhixuan Chen, Jialiang Lu, Zhong Ye, Yinghui He, Guanding Yu

entry.summary: PRI-Net tackles 3D UAV localization by combining point cloud splatting, residual attention fusion, and an information bottleneck to handle sparse LiDAR, modality imbalance, and bandwidth-constrained edge-to-server links. A splatting strategy converts sparse LiDAR into dense depth maps and a residual attention module reduces modal bias, with the bottleneck limiting redundant transmission. It targets practical drone-traffic and counter-UAV deployment constraints.

entry.title: TTDF: A Two-Stage Framework for Reliable Surgical Phase Transition Detection

author.name: Yushi Guo, Pietro Valdastri, Duygu Sarikaya

entry.summary: TTDF reframes surgical workflow transition detection as an event-level task evaluated on the outputs of a frozen online phase recognizer, rather than optimizing frame-wise accuracy and temporal consistency. It addresses false and duplicate transition events caused by temporal jitter and workflow-illegal switches, as well as persistent but incorrect candidates. The approach is causal and matters for context-aware surgical assistance and decision support.

entry.title: Floquet Fibre Geometry and Higher-Order Reduced Coordinates for Off-Manifold Transients near Nonlinear Aeroelastic Flutter

author.name: Puxue Tan

entry.summary: This theoretical paper proves that reduced coordinates near an attracting limit cycle require invariant-fibre geometry: the classical first-order phase-isostable chart from adjoint Floquet modes leaves only O(delta^2) invariance residual, while projection along a non-invariant metric-orthogonal complement generically leaves an O(delta) error. It demonstrates for a nonlinear aeroelastic limit cycle that metric-normal and strong-stable directions differ by tens of degrees. The results bear on model reduction for transient dynamics near flutter.

entry.title: Does Attention-Guided Masking Really Help Object Discovery in Object-Centric Learning?

author.name: Youliang Tao, Yanhua Han, Bin Zhao, Juho Kannala, Joni Pajarinen, Rongzhen Zhao

entry.summary: This paper interrogates a common assumption in object-centric learning: that slot attention already encodes object-discovery ability and can therefore be used to design better masked-reconstruction self-supervision. The authors compare Attention-Guided Masking against the simple Random Masking used by DIAS across six datasets and find that AGM does not always outperform random masking. It is a useful negative/sobering result warning that intuition-driven masking strategies may not deliver consistent gains.

entry.title: Integrating Multi-view Multi-light Surface Reconstruction into Cultural Heritage Workflows

author.name: Baptiste Brument, Robin Bruneau, Benjamin Coupry, Vincent Demoulin, Jean M\'elou, Antoine Laurent, Fabien Castan, Jean-Denis Durou, Lilian Calvet

entry.summary: This paper connects multi-view, multi-light surface reconstruction methods with established cultural heritage documentation practices, where RTI domes already capture illumination-varying image sets but standard photogrammetry software does not exploit them. The goal is fine-scale surface detail capture in a form usable by archaeologists, conservators, and heritage technicians. It is a translational workflow paper bridging acquisition hardware and recent CV methods.

entry.title: Refracted Light Interaction in Turbulent Bubbling Water (RLITBW): A Macroscopic Fluid-Optic Entropy Source

author.name: Nirjhar Debnath, Dwaipayan Datta, Kousik Dasgupta

entry.summary: The paper introduces a low-cost macroscopic true random number generator based on refracted light interaction in turbulent bubbling water, exploiting compound classical chaos from multiphase fluid dynamics and time-varying optical refraction. It develops a physical-mathematical model and contrasts this approach with expensive quantum or tightly controlled electronic entropy sources used in cryptography and stochastic simulation. The work targets cheap, physically grounded randomness for security-critical and simulation applications.

entry.title: Language-Grounded Semantic Target Navigation for Autonomous Surface Vehicles

author.name: Yuqing Lin, Youngroung Kim

entry.summary: SGNav lets an autonomous surface vehicle find and approach a maritime target specified by an operator in natural language rather than coordinates. It combines text-guided semantic grounding, harbour-aware candidate filtering, CLIP-based semantic verification, and grounded target control for port and harbour settings. The contribution is bringing language-conditioned target specification to the maritime autonomy domain, where it has been largely absent.

entry.title: Two-Stage Personalized Gait Phase Estimation in Stroke Survivors During Exoskeleton-Assisted Walking: An Offline Feasibility Study

author.name: Hyungseok Ryu, Pilwon Hur

entry.summary: This study evaluates personalized gait phase estimation for stroke survivors using functional IMU alignment and two-stage sequential adaptation of models pretrained on healthy gait, from a single thigh-mounted IMU. Stage 1 builds a distillation-regularized participant-specific model, and Stage 2 refines it conditionally with low-rank adaptation. LSTM, TCN, and Transformer backbones are compared across five stroke survivors walking with a powered knee exoskeleton.

entry.title: Understanding User Preferences of a Slope-Aware Variable-Admittance Filter for a Robot Guide Dog

author.name: Federico Esposito, Mario Selvaggio, Aaron Link, Fabio Ruggiero

entry.summary: This letter studies how stiffness and damping parameters of a slope-aware variable-admittance filter affect user preference when a quadruped robot guide dog physically pulls a handle for a visually impaired user. The system combines path following, momentum-based interaction-wrench estimation, and depth-camera slope extraction, evaluated through high-fidelity simulation and a human-subject study with blindfolded sighted participants using a Taguchi L9 design.

entry.title: Tracking the Ground: Online Lidar Identification of Robot-Induced Soil Deformation in Agricultural Environments

author.name: Tom Montagnon, Johann Laconte, Benoit Thuilot, Wonjae Cho, Roland Lenain

entry.summary: This paper proposes a framework to quantify traffic-induced soil deformation in agricultural settings and estimate its evolution online from lidar observations, using a reduced-order parametric model that represents soil behavior through physical parameters. The motivating claim is that soil health is degraded by vehicle traffic but soil state is rarely treated as a variable in agricultural robotics.

entry.title: Op-Ed: I Worked at Google DeepMind. You Should Listen to the Warnings About AI

author.name: TurnTrout

entry.summary: A Guardian op-ed by a former Google DeepMind researcher arguing that AI labs are racing toward superintelligence without adequate safeguards, and citing the Hugging Face agent incident as evidence of misalignment risk. It calls on governments to regulate and on the public to demand protection.

entry.title: Planning or Learning: Reliability and Cost in Multi-Asset Maintenance

author.name: Xian Yeow Lee, Chandrasekar Venkatraman, Ahmed Farahat

entry.summary: This empirical study compares planning and reinforcement learning for multi-asset bearing maintenance using run-to-failure data, under identical settings and across a range of failure-penalty scenarios. It finds a consistent behavioural difference driven by objective formulation: planning enforces reliability as a hard constraint whereas the learning approach balances it against cost within the objective.

entry.title: Windowed A-K-MDP

author.name: Xiangwen Yang, Frankie Cho, Iadine Chades

entry.summary: The paper shows that the A-K-MDP algorithm for building interpretable abstract MDPs with at most K states can skip better abstract states because it selects a discretization divisor via binary search. It proposes Windowed A-K-MDP, which enumerates every distinct feasible partition inside a declared divisor window and evaluates candidates until ideal value loss or exhaustion. It matters for making conservation decision policies more interpretable to managers.

entry.title: ViperQ: Order Flow Pattern Recognition via Auction Market Theory for Reinforcement Learning Trading

author.name: Asser Moustafa, Rares-Mihail Neagu, Jugal Kalita

entry.summary: ViperQ is a reinforcement learning trading system whose state representation is built explicitly from Auction Market Theory primitives such as Volume Point of Control, Value Area position, Low Volume Node flags, Cumulative Volume Delta divergence, and tape-velocity signatures, assembled into a 20-dimensional normalized vector. Two proximal policy optimization agents are trained with a proprietary or specified objective on this representation. It matters because practitioner microstructure theories had lacked a peer-reviewed computational instantiation in RL trading.

entry.title: ANASSA: An Agentic AI Orchestration Framework for Spatial Intelligence

author.name: Constantinos Papantoniou, Brian Hilton

entry.summary: This work surveys and synthesizes agentic frameworks that combine LLMs and large multimodal models with geospatial tooling, identifying where reasoning, execution, and evaluation remain poorly integrated for real-world GIS workflows. It proposes ANASSA as an orchestration framework aimed at making spatial analysis semi-autonomous and more robust.

entry.title: Enabling Creative Exploration for Vibe Design Agents

author.name: Yifan Zhang, Nghi D. Q. Bui, Georgios Evangelopoulos, Arnaud Benard

entry.summary: The authors note that vibe design agents should help users explore coherent design alternatives rather than emit one valid page, and that raising token temperature is a blunt lever because it perturbs aesthetics and syntax-sensitive code together. Their inference architecture makes design direction an explicit intermediate decision, using a structured specification pre-pass with typicality scores, an external selector, and a downstream generator.

entry.title: New Conditions for Philosophers to Catch the Wave of Citizen Deliberation in the Age of Artificial Intelligence in advance

author.name: Bernard Reber (CEVIPOF)

entry.summary: This conceptual paper examines how large language models might support citizen deliberation, for example through moderation, translation, facilitation, summarization, and writing assistance, while warning about insufficient epistemic caution around AI-labeled technologies. It describes the Democratic Commons project, which evaluates LLMs against five proposed democratic principles.

entry.title: Design of a Deep Learning Credit Risk Early Warning System Integrating Multi-source Heterogeneous Data

author.name: LiYang Wang (Washington University in St. Louis), Zhen Zhong (Georgetown University), Zhen Tian (University of Glasgow), Keyu Chen (Wuyi University), Keyu Chen (Wuyi University)

entry.summary: The paper proposes a credit risk early warning system that fuses multi-source heterogeneous data such as transaction behaviors and social networks using deep neural networks with attention mechanisms. Testing reportedly shows improved accuracy and timeliness of early identification of corporate and individual credit risks.

entry.title: Exploring Automated Vulnerability Identification in JavaScript Code Using Large Language Models

author.name: Manit Kaushik, Ishir Bhardwaj, Pranav Gupta, Pankaj Jalote, Arun Balaji Buduru

entry.summary: This empirical study evaluates three LLM families, Gemini 1.5 Flash, GPT-4o Mini, and DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-8B, across zero-shot, chain-of-thought, few-shot, and fine-tuning settings for detecting JavaScript vulnerabilities. The dataset contains 1,125 snippets spanning five CWE categories, motivated by the observation that SAST tools often miss real-world flaws in isolated code snippets.

entry.title: CRAF: Cross-View Residual-Aware Fusion for Deepfake Speech Detection

author.name: Minh-Xuan Phan, Khalid Zaman, Candy Olivia Mawalim, Masashi Unoki

entry.summary: CRAF fuses complementary representations from self-supervised speech models, which capture low-level acoustic detail, with auditory large language models, which provide higher-level contextual information, for detecting deepfake speech. A residual-aware fusion explicitly separates information shared between the two views from view-specific signal to improve generalization to unseen spoofing attacks.

entry.title: Finite-Time Node Separation in Recurrent Graph Neural Networks with Persistent Gaussian Perturbations

author.name: Mostafa Haghir Chehreghani

entry.summary: The paper provides a finite-time theoretical analysis of recurrent GNNs augmented with persistent Gaussian noise, showing that although such noise prevents asymptotic oversmoothing globally, individual node representations can still be indistinguishable at finite depth. It proves an exact second-moment decomposition of the expected squared distance between node representations, yielding a universal lower bound proportional to noise variance times dimension, without contraction or stationarity assumptions. This sharpens the theoretical picture of noise-based remedies for oversmoothing.

entry.title: RA-CoA: Training-free Fashion Image Captioning via Retrieval-Augmented Chain-of-Attributes

author.name: Abhirama Subramanyam Penamakuri, Shreya Shukla, Anand Mishra

entry.summary: RA-CoA proposes a training-free fashion image captioning approach that uses retrieval-augmented chain-of-attributes reasoning on top of instruction-tuned vision-language models, targeting fine-grained domain terms such as neckline, closure type, graphic pattern, and silhouette. The motivation is that fashion inventories change rapidly, so retraining is impractical and zero-shot adaptability is essential for e-commerce product search. It matters as a practical, scalable alternative to fine-tuned captioners in a fast-moving domain.

entry.title: CIDERS: Cloud-Edge LLM Collaborative Learning via Accelerating Personalized Bilevel Optimization

author.name: Victor H. Chen, Hairui Yu, Stella K. Chung, Hong Yan

entry.summary: CIDERS frames cloud-edge LLM collaboration as a personalized bilevel optimization problem, where the upper level optimizes edge-side personalization and the lower level governs cloud-side knowledge transfer. The goal is to simultaneously preserve a shared cloud knowledge foundation and enable domain-specific adaptation at the edge.

entry.title: Event-Native Symbolic-Temporal Spike Encoding Framework for Heterogeneous Cyber Streams

author.name: Dalton Diez, Peyton Andras, Max Shroyer, James Ghawaly Jr

entry.summary: This paper proposes a symbolic-temporal spike encoding framework that lets spiking neural networks consume heterogeneous cyber security streams containing categorical identifiers, irregular timing, and local behavioral context. The motivation is that standard rate- and population-based encodings do not match the mixed semantics of intrusion detection data.

entry.title: ReH-FUSE: Reliability-Aware Hierarchical Fusion of Experts for Multimodal Emotion Recognition in Conversation

author.name: Guan-Hua Wen, Hou-Chiang Tseng, Kuan-Yu Chen

entry.summary: ReH-FUSE addresses multimodal emotion recognition in conversation by adapting to the instance-dependent reliability of text, audio, and cross-modal evidence rather than using fixed fusion. A decision-level router first models text-versus-audio preference and then balances that unimodal mixture against a cross-modal expert, evaluated across three runs on IEMOCAP.

entry.title: Nonparametric Variance-Penalized Actor-Critic: Statistical Inference for Risk-Sensitive Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Saunak Kumar Panda, Tong Li, Yisha Xiang, Ruiqi Liu

entry.summary: This work proposes a nonparametric variance-penalized actor-critic that replaces the usual dedicated variance critic with online estimators based on bootstrapping and random scaling from the stochastic-approximation statistics literature. The approach keeps a single-critic architecture and yields bounded variance penalties while reducing estimation error.

entry.title: SH-WRNN: Implicit Spherical Harmonics Weight Field Routing Neural Networks for Asymmetric Edge Intelligence

author.name: Zhibin Jiao, Xiangjing An

entry.summary: SH-WRNN replaces static discrete synapse weight matrices with a differentiable continuous field parameterized by spherical harmonics, retrieving per-layer connections by mapping latitude and longitude onto a plane. The stated goal is more compact, flexible representations suited to asymmetric edge intelligence settings. It is an unusual challenge to the fully-connected layer as a foundational primitive.

entry.title: A pullback-corrected scalar auxiliary variable optimizer with momentum and adaptive mobility

author.name: Jiahao Zhang, Shiheng Zhang, Guang Lin

entry.summary: Scientific machine learning objectives are often sums of terms such as residual, boundary, initial, and data losses, and the pullback-corrected scalar auxiliary variable method tracks the shifted objective with a scalar while component gradients form a low-rank curvature correction. The authors carry that correction into an optimizer with momentum and adaptive mobility, applied to both gradient and stored momentum in a single implicit solve. A mobility nonincreasing in the Loewner order yields an exact modified energy law covering Euclidean and AMSGrad-type choices.

entry.title: 3D Gait-Based Autism Classification Using Attention-Enhanced Deep Learning with Cross-Fold Statistical Stability Analysis

author.name: Md Nadim Mahamood, Md Arif Shahriar, Md Parvej Sikder, Md Rasul Islam, Md Shafi Ud Doula, Md Ashraful Alam, Kamrul Hasan

entry.summary: This work proposes an attention-enhanced Transformer for autism spectrum disorder screening from 3D gait features, evaluated on two structurally different representations: precomputed statistical gait descriptors and learned feature sequences. It targets gaps in prior work such as single-dataset evaluation, reliance on convolutional architectures, and merely descriptive cross-validation reporting. A formal cross-fold stability analysis is added to assess how robust the reported performance is.

entry.title: Parameter isolation with domain-specific experts for incremental audio classification

author.name: Jongyeon Park, Do-Hyeon Lim, Sang-won Park, Hong Kook Kim, Kyungdeuk Ko, Hyeongcheol Geum, Jeong Eun Lim

entry.summary: The paper addresses domain-incremental learning for audio classification by isolating parameters into domain-specific experts instead of relying on domain-invariant features and weight regularization, which tend to overwrite prior knowledge. The proposed scheme aims to adapt to new domains while preserving earlier ones without access to their data.

entry.title: SyRHM: Symbolic-Language-Enhanced Reasoning with Associative Retrieval for Zero-shot Harmful Meme Detection

author.name: Hanling Wang, Chenlong Wei, Yingjuan Li, Di Wu, Yuchao Zhang, Xiaohui Zhu, Yao Zhu

entry.summary: SyRHM decomposes harmful meme detection into meaning-grounded retrieval plus symbolic-language-enhanced multi-stage reasoning, converting multimodal inputs into symbolic intermediate representations and planning over retrieved, semantically related memes. The goal is to capture implicit harmful intent arising from visual-textual incongruity and cultural stereotypes that surface-level multimodal detectors miss.

entry.title: Corpus Characterization and Inverse Constitutional Fine-Tuning for Style-Aware Radiology Reports

author.name: Sarah Y. Li, Elijah Renner, Rayan Ansari, Alaa Youssef

entry.summary: This paper characterizes stylistic variation in 2,000 CheXpert Plus radiology reports using Bio-ClinicalBERT embeddings, UMAP, and HDBSCAN, finding five distinct reporting patterns differing in pathology focus, structure, and lexicon. It then adapts inverse constitutional AI to derive a style-focused constitution from radiologist writing and fine-tune models toward those conventions, targeting the style gap that undermines clinician trust.

entry.title: EMCStereo: Attention-Enhanced Stereo Matching for Thin-Structure Depth Estimation with a Synthetic Tree-Branch Benchmark

author.name: Yida Lin, Bing Xue, Mengjie Zhang, Sam Schofield, Richard Green

entry.summary: EMCStereo augments a PSMNet-style cost-volume backbone with three lightweight attention modules for stereo matching of thin structures such as tree branches, where objects are only a few pixels wide against cluttered backgrounds. The modules include Efficient Multi-scale Attention on deep features, a Multi-Scale Fusion block learning spatial pyramid weights, and Coordinate Attention on final matching features, together leaving the network slightly smaller and adding modest inference overhead. The work also contributes a synthetic tree-branch benchmark for evaluation.

entry.title: HGSQ: Heatmap-Guided Sparse Query Detector for Real-Time Aerial Small Object Detection

author.name: Yangchen Zeng

entry.summary: HGSQ is a heatmap-guided sparse query detector for real-time aerial small object detection, aiming to preserve fine-grained localization while avoiding redundant computation on large background regions. It targets the inefficiency of Transformer detectors that initialize dense queries and run multi-layer decoders over mostly background tokens, which is wasteful when small objects occupy sparse image regions. The framing is explicitly deployment-oriented for aerial and UAV settings rather than claiming universal detection superiority.

entry.title: Query-Conditioned Spherical Centroid Aggregation for Multimodal Retrieval

author.name: Ambuj Mehrish, Anindya Nag, Sebastiano Vascon

entry.summary: This paper observes that recent geometric aggregators for multimodal retrieval (Gramian volumes, hyperbolic volumes, spectral objectives) treat all modalities symmetrically and, under a unified protocol, often underperform the strongest single-modality pathway by a wide R@1 margin. It attributes this to uniform modality influence and proposes SCALAR, a query-conditioned aggregator that assigns relevance-based weights to each modality before computing a spherical centroid, accommodating arbitrary modality subsets and trained on masked reduced-arity views. The result is a more adaptive aggregation scheme.

entry.title: An Adaptive Fixed-Time Line-of-Sight Guidance Scheme for 3D Path Following of Underwater Vehicles: Theory and Experiment

author.name: Hanzhi Yang, Jalil Chavez-Galaviz, Nina Mahmoudian

entry.summary: This paper proposes a robust fixed-time adaptive line-of-sight guidance framework for 3D path tracking by autonomous underwater vehicles, guaranteeing convergence within a preset time independent of initial conditions. A key selling point is that it requires no modification to the underlying vehicle controller, making it applicable to commercial AUV platforms. Theory is paired with experimental validation.

entry.title: Alignment Problem Redux

author.name: Mateusz Bagiński

entry.summary: This essay offers a conceptual account of what generates alignment-problem intuitions, starting from the premise that generally capable minds cannot pre-plan for every situation and must adapt and learn continuously, changing themselves in the process. The author positions the model as tentative, explicitly not original, and assembled from ideas present in others' writing, aiming to give a clearer exposition of the underlying generator of these concerns. It matters as a synthesis/framing piece rather than new empirical alignment research.

entry.title: Not all Negation Cues are Equal: Affixal Negations Yield Better Negation Understanding

author.name: Tian Tan, Eduardo Blanco

entry.summary: The authors build NegCue, a dataset of over 1.8M samples covering single-word, multi-word, and affixal negation across more than 200 cues, then continue pretraining encoder-only LMs and LLMs on it. Results on five downstream benchmarks show that negation types contribute unevenly to gains, with affixal negation proving especially beneficial for negation understanding.

entry.title: Bi-Level Routing and Sparse Spatial Attention based Multi-View BEV 3D Object Detection for Autonomous Driving

author.name: Jing Zhang, Jiaqi Liu, Zibo Wang

entry.summary: Sparse-BEVNet improves Bird's Eye View multi-view 3D object detection by introducing bi-level routing attention in the image backbone to cut computation, cascaded group attention in the fusion module to strengthen cross-level interaction without extra cost, and a sparse spatial cross-attention mechanism for the 2D-to-BEV transformation. The design targets the computational complexity and dense-view-transformation inefficiency of existing BEV detectors. It matters for making autonomous-driving perception cheaper without sacrificing accuracy.

entry.title: Online Language Adaptive Sampling for Better Distributed Cross-lingual Gains

author.name: Quang Phuoc Nguyen, F\'elix Gaschi, David Anugraha, Santiago Mart\'inez Novoa, En-Shiun Annie Lee

entry.summary: Realignment improves cross-lingual transfer for extremely low-resource languages, but existing methods sample parallel sentences uniformly and randomly, which can be suboptimal at limited batch sizes. The authors propose an adaptive sampling strategy with trainable per-language sampling probabilities, up-weighting languages that contribute more to the realignment loss so the distribution evolves during training.

entry.title: ZAPS: Zero-Cost Active Proxy Search for Neural Architecture Search

author.name: Hassan Touayouch, Rabie Najem, Mohammed Benjelloun

entry.summary: ZAPS is a four-stage pipeline for neural architecture search that combines zero-cost proxy signals with architectural topology inside a single active-learning framework. It first selects a compact, non-redundant proxy subset offline because proxies are strongly correlated and naive aggregation compounds shared errors.

entry.title: HiGFRL: Hierarchical Graph Fusion-Driven Reinforcement Learning for Dependency-Aware Task Scheduling in Heterogeneous Cloud

author.name: Tiangang Li, Shi Ying, Xiangbo Tian

entry.summary: HiGFRL proposes a three-level state representation for dependency-aware scheduling in heterogeneous cloud clusters, combining a static hypergraph, a dynamic global graph and a local bipartite graph to model high-order task dependencies and task-resource coupling. A hierarchical graph fusion reinforcement learning framework then produces scheduling decisions intended to avoid myopia. It matters for online scheduling where DAG topology and multi-dimensional resources interact.

entry.title: Channel-Adaptive Region Adjacency Graph Carriers for Semantic Image Communication

author.name: Karim Abdallah, Maria Slim, Mariette Awad, Hadi Sarieddeen

entry.summary: The paper introduces a segmentation-derived region adjacency graph carrier for semantic image communication, where nodes hold interpretable region attributes and edges preserve adjacency. Channel-adaptive graph simplification controls the node budget and semantic belief propagation denoises graph embeddings before diffusion-based reconstruction.

entry.title: Human-Grounded Calibration for Long-Text Image-Text Congruence in Vision-Language Models

author.name: Alessandro Gambetti, Qiwei Han

entry.summary: This paper proposes Congruency Score, a lightweight calibration layer that maps image-text similarity evidence from dual-encoder vision-language models into a bounded, interpretable congruence score. Using DOCCI and Urban1k with four frozen backbones, the authors show that reducing post-projection centroid distance does not uniformly improve retrieval performance. Human-grounded evaluations on DOCCI support the calibration approach's interpretability.

entry.title: YOLO12-MambaScan: An Efficient Object Detector with High-Frequency Enhancement and State-Space Modeling

author.name: Hao Wang

entry.summary: YOLO12-MambaScan is an aerial-image detector built on YOLO12 that adds a triple-path high-frequency enhancement convolution, receptive-field coordinate-attention convolution, and a Mamba-based global-context module. The motivation is that small objects in UAV imagery occupy few pixels, high-frequency edge and texture cues are easily lost, and global context is hard to model in cluttered scenes. It targets monitoring, traffic management, and disaster-response applications.

entry.title: Weakly Supervised Spatial Grounding for Discriminative Attention-Based Ultrasound-Histopathology Alignment in Prostate Cancer Grading

author.name: Obed Korshie Dzikunu, Emma Willis, Mohammad Mahdi Abootorabi, Mohamed Harmanani, Zhuoxin Guo, Ferdinand Luger, Adam Kinnaird, Brian Wodlinger, Parvin Mousavi, Purang Abolmaesumi

entry.summary: This work studies unpaired cross-modal distillation that transfers prostate cancer grade structure from histopathology into a micro-ultrasound encoder by aligning pooled needle-region embeddings to a frozen histopathology teacher. The authors decouple two functions that a single objective usually conflates, adding weak spatial supervision derived from routine percentage-involvement records to constrain the predicted malignant tissue proportion within each core, with the alignment loss then operating on the resulting discriminative features. The goal is better ultrasound-based grading without needing paired pathology.

entry.title: HydroMap: Probabilistic Water Surface Elevation Mapping for Semantic Scene Representation in Inland Waterways

author.name: Zhongbi Luo, Yunjia Wang, Herman Bruyninckx, Peter Slaets

entry.summary: HydroMap reconstructs water surface elevation from stereo observations in an odometry-decoupled framework and fuses it with a structural map, since LiDAR SLAM often returns sparse or missing water points. Per-frame water points form joint cell observations with propagated stereo and pose uncertainty, which are fused into a persistent probabilistic elevation map and converted into a unified semantic representation. It matters for autonomous surface vehicles that need the water surface itself to be represented, not just surrounding structures.

entry.title: A Hybrid Agentic AI Framework for Intelligent Supply Chain Analytics

author.name: Xian Yeow Lee, Teppei Inoue, Haiyan Wang, Chetan Gupta

entry.summary: The paper proposes an agentic system for supply chain analytics in which a coordinator agent interprets user intent and delegates sub-tasks to specialized agents covering database querying, KPI analysis, demand forecasting, and performance diagnosis. The system supports both exploratory analysis and deterministic workflows, letting planners move between ad hoc questions and structured processes.

entry.title: Map Users and Mapmakers: The Scope of Cognitive Attribution from Acquired Representations

author.name: Yiling Wu

entry.summary: This conceptual paper asks what it actually means when a system acquires a representation, such as a map, and argues that possessing a representation does not automatically transfer the capacities used to build it. The author proposes a five-part attribution table separating effective tracking, application of acquired structures, acquisition from explicit specification, acquisition from identifying observations, and retention and reuse, with each entry carrying both a positive capacity claim and a further claim needing extra support.

entry.title: OptoAgent: A Trustworthy Multi-Agent Framework for Opportunistic Vision Micro-Screening in Classroom Environments

author.name: Toqeer Ali Syed, Ali Akarma, Adeel Ahmad, Hammad Muneer

entry.summary: The paper addresses children with reduced distance vision who rarely report difficulties, arguing that scheduled school screening misses in-classroom moments. SightSentinel turns an existing wall display into a recurring screening site by embedding short calibrated optotype probes in ordinary educational content, with eight specialized agents splitting perception and related work.

entry.title: GEAR: From Dynamic Encoding to Dynamic Activation in Social Trajectory Prediction

author.name: Jiaheng Chen, Jiaxing Li, Leixia Wang, Jianan Ju, Tinghe Zhang

entry.summary: GEAR argues that dynamically encoding social context does not automatically mean dynamically activating it during trajectory generation. The method modulates how strongly social cues influence predictions across different future horizons and scene densities, strengthening social signals when interactions matter more.

entry.title: Biquaternionic Space with Complex-valued Attention for Temporal Knowledge Graph Completion

author.name: Rushan Geng, Cuicui Luo

entry.summary: The paper proposes BSCA, a temporal knowledge graph embedding model that combines circular and hyperbolic rotations inside a unified biquaternionic space and uses complex-valued attention to adaptively fuse time-conditioned and relation-conditioned entity representations. Experiments across five benchmarks show competitive performance with the largest gain on one dataset. It matters as an attempt to broaden the geometric expressiveness available to temporal knowledge graph reasoning.

entry.title: A Hybrid Dependency-Aware Framework for Task Decomposition and Dynamic Agent Generation in Oracle-to-PostgreSQL Migration

author.name: Oleg Grynets, Oleg Kaskun, Alona Seletska, Daryna Tukalo, Vasyl Lyashkevych

entry.summary: This paper treats enterprise Oracle-to-PostgreSQL migration as a dependency-aware planning problem rather than direct code translation, building a cross-file dependency graph, condensing cyclic dependencies, and generating specialized migration agents at runtime from task specifications. A deterministic ANTLR-based parsing path handles most units, with an LLM fallback only when parsing fails. It matters for reliable, auditable large-scale database migration with coverage guarantees.

entry.title: Lightweight Generalized DeepFake Face Detection with WAVIE: Wavelet Augmented Vision Intermediate Embeddings

author.name: Arya Pulkit, Aditya Ruhela, Akarshan Kapoor, Arnav Bhavsar

entry.summary: WAVIE is a lightweight deepfake face detector that combines spatial and frequency cues on top of a frozen CLIP backbone by projecting intermediate transformer embeddings through a learnable wavelet-augmented path. The design targets generalization to unseen manipulation methods, a known weakness of detectors trained on specific forgery pipelines. It matters for misinformation mitigation and digital forensics where cross-method robustness is essential.

entry.title: AlgoRAG: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Theoretical Computer Science Education -- A Comprehensive Evaluation Framework for Algorithm Analysis and Complexity Theory

author.name: Sushan Adhikari

entry.summary: This paper introduces AlgoRAG, a domain-specific retrieval-augmented generation system aimed at teaching theoretical computer science topics such as algorithm analysis and complexity theory. It pairs an LLM with a curated knowledge base of textbooks, hundreds of lecture slides, practice problems, proof templates and complexity worksheets, adding math-aware entity recognition and notation-aware retrieval. The contribution matters as a case study in grounding LLM tutoring in authoritative, notation-heavy material rather than free-form generation.

entry.title: A property-registry contract for retrieve-or-refuse thermal-mechanical lattice search

author.name: Shaoliang Yang, Henry Chu, Zu Yashengjiang, Jun Wang

entry.summary: This work applies conflict diagnosis to a catalogue of homogenized thermal-mechanical lattice properties, covering 1,397 unit cells and 19 base materials (over 26,000 combinations). Rather than returning the nearest match when requirements are jointly unsatisfiable, the system refuses and returns inclusion-minimal unsatisfiable subsets for feasible sets of up to eight constraints, indicating which requirement to relax. It contrasts this with generative models that will emit a candidate even when no library entry satisfies the specification.

entry.title: RAIN: Region-Aware Inversion Network for Semantic Watermark Extraction

author.name: Zilai Li

entry.summary: RAIN studies semantic watermark extraction for diffusion models, where Gaussian Shading normally requires costly multi-step diffusion inversion to recover the initial noise. Using extended flow matching and conditional regression, the authors argue that near the high-SNR image endpoint only a first-step output statistic is needed, since Gaussian Shading requires the recovered latent merely to land in the correct watermark decision region.

entry.title: LiftGCN: Efficient Energy-Preserving Graph Learning via Joukowski Spectral Lifting for Finite Element Stress Prediction

author.name: Chen Zeng, Qiao Wang

entry.summary: Finite element stress fields have sharp local gradients near holes, notches and loading regions that conventional message passing smooths away. LiftGCN uses Joukowski spectral lifting to map the real spectrum of a normalized graph operator into a spectrally stable, energy-preserving propagation scheme, aiming to preserve high-frequency components at lower cost than unitary propagation with high-order approximations.

entry.title: Interpreting hierarchical organisation of speaker embeddings

author.name: Yanze Xu, Wenwu Wang, Mark D. Plumbley

entry.summary: This work applies Single-Linkage Clustering to speaker embeddings to test whether they naturally form hierarchical clusters, framing the analysis explicitly within explainable AI rather than as pure representation description. The goal is to interpret the internal organization of speaker recognition networks whose mechanisms remain largely opaque.

entry.title: FedLTLib: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Federated Long-Tail Learning

author.name: Changkun Lin, Junxiao Wang

entry.summary: FedLTLib is a benchmark for federated learning under long-tail data distributions, formalizing the combination of client heterogeneity and severe class imbalance as double heterogeneity. It targets realistic mobile edge scenarios where head classes dominate and rare but important tail classes are extremely scarce.

entry.title: More Than Just Access: Generative AI as Communication Intermediary for Blind and Low-Vision Users

author.name: Protik Dey, Mohd Saifuzzaman, Taslima Akter

entry.summary: Drawing on semi-structured interviews with 19 blind and low-vision participants, this study examines generative AI tools such as ChatGPT, Gemini, Be My AI, and Seeing AI as communication intermediaries. It analyzes where these tools succeed and fail in reading, describing, and substituting for interpersonal requests for help, and what users gain and risk as the tools take on that role.

entry.title: Transfer Learning for Socioeconomic Estimation in Forced-Displacement Settings

author.name: Steven Ndung'u, Adel Daoud, Ismael Yacoubou Djima, Hai-Anh H. Dang, Patrick Michael Brock

entry.summary: This work studies transfer learning for estimating socioeconomic conditions of forcibly displaced populations by combining earth observation data with machine learning. It responds to the fact that household surveys for displaced groups are infrequent and costly, leaving gaps precisely in fragile and conflict-affected settings where conditions change quickly.

entry.title: A derivative-fidelity failure mode in physics-informed neural networks: strengthened benchmark evidence from function-value training

author.name: Koji Koyamada

entry.summary: This paper formalizes derivative fidelity as a distinct PINN failure mode, showing that models trained only on function values can approximate sin and exp visually well while automatic-differentiation derivatives are substantially wrong. It probes training-point density, activation choice, endpoint-dense evaluation, and both L2 and maximum-error diagnostics on one-dimensional benchmarks. The result matters because downstream uses of PINNs, such as solving or discovering differential equations, depend on accurate derivatives rather than values alone.

entry.title: PPDL: A Real-world Industrial User Retention Ratio Forecasting Framework Integrating Physical Priors with Deep Learning

author.name: Zibo Zhao, Zhengxiong Guan, Chaoli Zhang, Linyuan Geng, Xuanbing Zhu, Zhonglong Zheng, Fan Wu

entry.summary: PPDL is an industrial forecasting framework for channel-level user retention ratios in multi-channel paid user acquisition, aimed at improving budget allocation. It handles channel heterogeneity, the decay-then-saturation trend, and seasonality by combining physical priors with deep time-series modeling for large short-video platforms.

entry.title: An Uncertainty-Aware Hybrid Mathematical-Machine-Learning Model for Smart Irrigation Decision Support

author.name: Andrea Scariolo

entry.summary: This study couples a four-parameter water-balance model with a Random Forest that learns only the physical residual, then adds conformal prediction for 90%-nominal intervals and a risk-aware rule that converts forecasts into irrigation decisions. The aim is to combine the transparency of physical models with data-driven accuracy while carrying uncertainty through to the decision.

entry.title: Optimal Transport for Efficient, Unsupervised Anomaly Detection on Industrial Data

author.name: Abigail Langbridge, Fearghal O'Donncha, James T Rayfield, Bradley Eck

entry.summary: The authors propose an optimal-transport framework for unsupervised anomaly detection in industrial time-series sensor data. It requires minimal user input, adapts in real time without labels, tolerates noise and data gaps, and provides counterfactual explanations to support auditability in Industry 4.0 deployments.

entry.title: Selecting k Paths with the Minimum Longest Path Length in the Stochastic Semi-Bandit Setting

author.name: Shunsuke Aoki, Atsuyoshi Nakamura

entry.summary: The paper formulates an online problem where k origin-to-destination paths must be selected each round to minimize the maximum stochastic traversal time, subject to per-edge capacity limits on parallel transmissions. It casts this as a semi-bandit problem and proposes an algorithm for it. The work is relevant to network routing and load balancing where worst-case latency, not average latency, is the objective.

entry.title: Cloud Workflow Scheduling Based on Graph Attention-Driven Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Zongjin Li, Shaohan Feng, Chunxi Yang, Wenbo Wang

entry.summary: This paper presents a hierarchical reinforcement learning framework for dynamic cloud workflow scheduling that balances deadline satisfaction, container utilization and energy consumption under stochastic task speeds and placement-dependent communication. It assigns predicted sub-deadlines to tasks and uses multi-head graph attention over evolving DAGs to capture dependency topology. It matters for data-center scheduling where workflow structure is central.

entry.title: Frame-Synchronous Hand Gesture Detection by Projected Winding Order

author.name: Amey Thakur

entry.summary: Rather than classifying gestures per frame, this work treats hand rotation about its long axis as a synchronization problem and shows an exact, training-free solution. A normalized 2D cross product of palm edges at the wrist and outer knuckles, under the camera projection, factorizes into a form that yields frame-accurate gesture timing without a classifier or calibration data.

entry.title: Early-Stopping Thresholds for ES-HyperNEAT: A Data-Driven Approach from Fitness Dynamics

author.name: Romain Claret, Arthur Gygax, Michael O'Neill, Paul Cotofrei, Pascal Felber

entry.summary: Most Evolvable-Substrate HyperNEAT configurations stagnate at random-guessing performance and waste compute, so the authors frame early stopping as binary classification over early fitness trajectories. They compute a cumulative median of best-per-generation fitness and compare it to a threshold tuned by maximizing F1 on an initial 90-trial dataset. The resulting rule achieves F1 of 0.872 on 180 independent validation trials, retaining over 90 percent of successful runs while cutting cost by 41.6 percent.

entry.title: Real-World Deployment and Performance Characterisation of Fog-Based Deep Learning for Cold-Chain Temperature Prediction over LoRaWAN

author.name: Jeremiah Taguta, Jean Frederic Isingizwe Nturambirwe, Clement Nthambazale Nyirenda

entry.summary: The paper reports what the authors describe as the first real-world fog deployment of deep learning for fresh-produce cold-chain temperature prediction. An LSTM-GRU model runs entirely on a Raspberry Pi 4 with no cloud dependency, consuming LoRaWAN sensor data from a South African apple cold-storage facility where cold-chain breaks were induced. The system produces verifiable conditional hashes alongside predictions, addressing latency and data-loss concerns of cloud inference.

entry.title: A Functional SVD Framework for Regularized Multivariate Functional PCA with Dual Penalization

author.name: Yue Zhao, Hossein Haghbin, Rebecca Sanders, Mehdi Maadooliat

entry.summary: The paper develops a regularized multivariate functional principal component analysis method based on a generalized functional singular value decomposition within a Hilbert space framework. It simultaneously regularizes principal components and their scores, adding a sparsity penalty on scores to filter out irrelevant subject-specific variation and improve interpretability.

entry.title: TestHallVQA: Exploring LVLMs' Document-Level Reasoning under Redundant Contexts from Scientific Exams

author.name: Yongqi Yu, Yu Zhang

entry.summary: TestHallVQA is a multi-image VQA benchmark combining document-level scale with multi-page, redundant, noisy context drawn from scientific exams. The authors theoretically analyze how irrelevant visual tokens degrade performance and then quantify this systematically. It matters for evaluating vision-language models in realistic, clutter-heavy document understanding settings.

entry.title: In the Blind: Building Pseudo-References for MT Evaluation

author.name: Diptesh Kanojia, Chi-kiu Lo, Archchana Sindhujan, Samuel Larkin, Greg Hanneman, Alon Lavie

entry.summary: This system description explains how the authors constructed pseudo-references for ten WMT26 general MT language pairs that lack human references, by generating candidates from seven models under multiple prompt conditions, scoring with reference-free quality estimation, selecting per document, and post-editing with GPT-5.5 (an existing model released earlier in 2026). It documents a notable failure mode where QE-guided selection can favor fluent output in the wrong language. The paper is valuable as an honest account of evaluation under reference scarcity.

entry.title: When Edit Localization Amplifies Relative Selection Bias: Gradient Geometry, Target Mismatch, and Importance Weighting

author.name: Shengwei Zhang, Haoda Dai, Yifei Li, Yuheng Song

entry.summary: The paper analyzes how localizing human corrections to editable spans interacts with selective feedback, decomposing localized gradients into edited and retained components and deriving when squared relative selection bias increases or decreases. It shows that oracle importance weighting recovers the population mean for each fixed localization objective, but those objectives differ in target, and it quantifies finite-sample error against a common full-gradient target. The result warns that common localization practice can amplify selection bias.

entry.title: Semiotic Relations and Proof Methods: A Cross-Genre Study of Argument Structure with Large Language Models

author.name: Edirlei Soares de Lima, Marco A. Casanova, Antonio L. Furtado

entry.summary: The paper reviews four semiotic relations inspired by the master tropes (metonymy, metaphor, irony, synecdoche) and maps them onto options for moving from a hard-to-prove statement to a related statement that enables proof. These correspond to proof by inference, analogy, contradiction, and case analysis. LLMs are used in a cross-genre study of argument structure to examine how these relations manifest.

entry.title: Interpretable Temporal Video Reasoning with EventGraph and EventField

author.name: Durgendra Narayan Singh

entry.summary: The paper presents a structured temporal video reasoning pipeline built around a discrete EventGraph, a continuous EventField, and a human-readable EventGlyph view. On a calibrated EPIC-KITCHENS subset of 10 videos and 50 temporal reasoning questions, EventField plus Glyph reaches 0.98 overall accuracy, beating the caption baseline by 0.40 and direct VLM-only QA by 0.20. It also evaluates manual, heuristic, and heuristic-plus-Gemini annotation pipelines and includes cross-video pair benchmarking.

entry.title: IROH: Insightful Ranking Of Humor using Multi-Stage Hybrid Retrieval with Rationale-Distilled LLM Judges for JOKER 2026 Track Task 1 English

author.name: Ana-Maria Luisa Mocanu, Sebastian Mocanu, Ciprian-Octavian Truic\u{a}, Elena-Simona Apostol

entry.summary: The VANGUARD team presents IROH, a three-stage retrieval system for JOKER Task 1 English at CLEF 2026 that placed first with 0.6347 MAP. The pipeline combines hybrid sparse-dense retrieval, cross-encoder reranking, and a LoRA-adapted LLM judge ensemble, with query-aware rationales generated by Gemma 4 and structured hard negatives for training. Ablations across cross-encoders, dense embedders, and judge configurations identify the rationale-distilled judge as the primary driver of ranking quality.

entry.title: Synthetic Leprosy Image Generation Using Mask-Conditioned Latent Diffusion and Transfer Learning from Large Chronic Wound Datasets

author.name: Yusuf Abdulkadir

entry.summary: This paper builds a three-stage pipeline to generate synthetic leprosy imagery in a low-data regime, starting with a DeepLabV3-ResNet50 segmentation network that supplies lesion masks for two wound datasets lacking them. It then assembles a mask-conditioned latent diffusion model from Stable Diffusion 1.5 components, trained on 3,280 region-of-interest wound crops, widening the UNet input convolution from 4 to 11 channels to accept mask features. The central question is whether abundant chronic-wound photography transfers to neglected tropical disease data scarcity.

entry.title: Multi-View Structure-from-Motion Enables Oriented Projective Shape Analysis in Three Dimensions

author.name: Musab Alamoudi, Robert L. Paige, Vic Patrangenaru

entry.summary: This statistics paper extends projective shape analysis, a geometric framework for studying landmark configurations from pinhole-camera images, to oriented projective shape in three dimensions. Classical two-view reconstructions are identified only up to a 3D projective transformation that may reverse orientation, which previously forced sign-blind summaries. The work shows that multi-view structure-from-motion enables oriented analysis and develops corresponding methodology.

entry.title: DTI-Guided Volumetric Spherical Harmonics Regression for Single-to-Multi-Shell dMRI Synthesis

author.name: Binghua Li, Christina Andica, Tong Liang, Ziqing Chang, Chao Li, Wataru Uchida, Kaito Takabayashi, Qibin Zhao, Toshihisa Tanaka, Zhe Sun, Shigeki Aoki

entry.summary: DTI-SHNet synthesizes unobserved diffusion MRI shells from a single-shell input by operating in the real symmetric spherical harmonics coefficient domain with DTI-derived, direction-agnostic parametric maps as conditions. The design handles protocol mismatch where source and target gradient direction sets do not align. It matters for enabling richer microstructural modeling without long multi-shell acquisitions.

entry.title: Small Object Detection in Drone Aerial Imagery with LAF-YOLOv10

author.name: Quratulain Nayeem, Fahmina Taranum, Mohammed Mudassir Uddin

entry.summary: LAF-YOLOv10 integrates four independently validated techniques into YOLOv10n, namely a partial convolution C2f block, an attention-guided feature pyramid, a P2 detection head replacing P5, and Wise-IoU v3 regression, then stress-tests whether the combined gains match their sum of parts. Training is repeated across three random seeds on VisDrone-DET2019 with comparison against the unmodified baseline. The paper's contribution is as much methodological skepticism about stacked tricks as it is a detector.

entry.title: Zero-shot video highlight detection based on text descriptions and synthetic images

author.name: Michal Byra, Alberto Presta, Grzegorz Stefanski, Krzysztof Arendt

entry.summary: The paper proposes a zero-shot video highlight detection framework that uses an LLM to generate textual descriptions of probable highlight events from lightweight metadata such as titles or categories, converts those descriptions into synthetic visual prototypes with a diffusion model, and matches both text and image representations to frames via CLIP. This removes the need for highlight annotations or dataset-specific training, and the authors report strong zero-shot results on TVSum and SumMe. It is a straightforward but useful pipeline combining several off-the-shelf models for annotation-free video summarization.

entry.title: CatchMonitor: a machine learning system for automated fish discard quantification

author.name: Geoff French, Michal Mackiewicz, Mark Fisher, Helen Holah, Rebecca Lamb

entry.summary: CatchMonitor is a prototype computer vision system that quantifies discarded fish automatically from Remote Electronic Monitoring video captured on trawlers, using semi-supervised learning to improve species identification and simple robust tracking for counting. The authors also measure variability across human expert analysts to contextualize achievable accuracy. It is a deployment-oriented fisheries compliance tool.

entry.title: Translation-Invariant Tile-Based Phase Unwrapping with Residual-Weighted Multipath Averaging

author.name: Antoine Moevus, Max Mignotte

entry.summary: This paper proposes a semi-global phase unwrapping strategy that unwraps each tile in the frequency domain via DCT least squares, then merges tiles spatially with a translation-invariant scheme and residual-weighted multipath averaging. It targets interferometric and coherent imaging, where the hard part is distinguishing wrapping jumps from noise, true discontinuities, undersampling, and decorrelation. The contribution is a hybrid spatial-frequency scheme, a combination the authors note remains scarce.

entry.title: Robotic Servo Tracking of Moving Targets with Dynamic Imitation Constraints

author.name: Yazhe Luo, Sipu Ruan, Yifei Li, Diansheng Chen

entry.summary: The paper proposes a visual servo tracking method for moving targets that imposes imitation-based trajectory constraints, addressing the trajectory discontinuity and oscillation typical of residual-to-velocity mapping approaches. It formulates and analyzes convergence of a dynamic model for a robot approaching a moving target, and introduces time-scalable deformation plus shape and amplitude modulation to generate trajectory families. The goal is constrained, non-conservative tracking rather than purely reactive servoing.

entry.title: Mind Which Bird You Favour: Parameterizing Adequacy-Fluency Balance in Meta-Evaluation of Machine Translation

author.name: Behzad Shayegh, Niloofar Kazemi

entry.summary: This paper argues that machine translation meta-evaluation hides a tunable tradeoff between prioritizing adequacy versus fluency, and that the balance depends on the arbitrary mix of systems in the meta-evaluation set. Because that system set is a small filtered sample that shifts across years and language pairs, the resulting balance is unrepresentative and unstable. The authors expose the tradeoff as an explicit, tunable choice by reweighting existing systems to hit a target balance while minimizing distortion.

entry.title: CiteGuard-RAG: A Validation-Centered AI System for Evidence-Grounded Question Answering

author.name: Sumit Barua, Guan Hong, Halil Dursunoglu, Charles Rodgers, Alvis Fong

entry.summary: CiteGuard-RAG combines hybrid semantic-lexical retrieval, citation-constrained generation, sentence-level grounding validation, and single-pass regeneration so that validation at runtime decides whether a candidate answer is accepted, refused, or regenerated. It is evaluated on 400 questions spanning a controlled housing-law dataset, PrivacyQA, and CUAD.

entry.title: Multi-Modal Tumor Survival Prediction via Graph-Guided Mixture of Experts

author.name: H Mathavan, H Liu

entry.summary: The paper addresses multimodal tumor survival prediction by combining clinical data, cell slides, and genomics, a setting complicated by missing modalities and heterogeneous integration needs. It proposes a graph-guided mixture-of-experts approach to fuse all modalities simultaneously while handling missing or varying inputs.

entry.title: A Personalized Dynamic Balance Evaluation Paradigm for Hip Exoskeleton-Assisted Walking under Unexpected Ground Perturbations

author.name: Yun Chen, Oluwasegun T. Akinniyi, Qiang Zhang

entry.summary: The paper introduces a participant-specific composite balance cost that integrates seven biomechanical sub-metrics spanning margin of stability, center-of-mass dynamics, and whole-body angular momentum. Nonnegative fusion weights are learned on the simplex and combined with an empirical-Bayes hierarchical model to estimate the posterior probability that a given assistance condition is best.

entry.title: A Multi-Stage Agentic Framework for Effective Counter-Narrative Generation and Refinement

author.name: Carmel Kronfeld, Sharva Gogawale, Tetsuro Kobayashi, Irad Ben-Gal

entry.summary: This work presents a multi-stage agentic pipeline for generating, refining, and evaluating counter-narratives against pro-Russian hate and misinformation narratives about the war in Ukraine, designed to be adaptable to other domains. A pilot human evaluation identifies effective technique-style pairings, such as repetition combined with emotional framing.

entry.title: Hypergraph-Regularized Gramian Volumes for Multimodal Retrieval

author.name: Anindya Nag, Ambuj Mehrish, Sebastiano Vascon

entry.summary: HyVol is a training-time module for volume-based multimodal retrieval, where a text query is jointly scored against a candidate's video, audio and subtitle embeddings. Because the volume score is candidate-local, semantically related training samples usually serve only as contrastive negatives; HyVol adds document hyperedges connecting a candidate's observed modalities and semantic hyperedges linking candidates whose captions are mutual top-k neighbors, applying residual corrections to modality embeddings through a shallow gated hypergraph network. The aim is to inject cross-candidate semantic structure into the learned geometry.

entry.title: Homeostatic Continual Learning

author.name: Yue Jin

entry.summary: This single-author paper formulates a continual learning problem and proposes Homeostatic Continual Learning, in which an agent detects outliers in environment data when it produces an outlier output and gradually completes its model and policy. The author also sketches how the method could support a world model that factorizes objects into features, abstracts them into comparable concept instances, and maps concepts to intents. It matters as an attempt at avoidance of catastrophic forgetting in changing environments.

entry.title: Semantic Knowledge Technologies: what the Semantic Web lost sight of, and what it never had

author.name: Achille Zappa

entry.summary: The paper revisits the Semantic Web project, noting that its standards became knowledge infrastructure while the promised machine competence never materialized, and that language models now answer questions over scientific knowledge without any inspectable account of what they know. It diagnoses three omissions in formalizing truth and proposes an extended programme called Semantic Knowledge Technologies.

entry.title: Diffusion-Based Generation of Gait Trajectories

author.name: Damian Benasco, Juan Carballeira-Lopez, Jaime Ramos-Rojas, Julio S. Lora-Millan, Antonio J. Del-Ama, David Rodriguez-Cianca, Pablo Lanillos

entry.summary: The paper explores conditional diffusion models for generating lower-limb joint-angle trajectories conditioned on gait parameters such as step length, motivated by the need for patient-specific reference trajectories in exoskeletons and rehabilitation robotics. It compares a baseline transformer diffusion model with a controllable diffusion transformer variant that incorporates conditioning for greater controllability.

entry.title: Geometric Flow enhanced Graph Coarsening

author.name: Chaoqun Fei, Guoxuan Li, Tinglve Zhou, Chuanqing Wang, Yangyang Li

entry.summary: This work proposes a graph pooling and coarsening method that augments clustering-based pooling with geometric flow, aiming to capture higher-order connectivity among neighboring nodes that rough topology alone misses. The motivation is that edge-level message-passing ease reflects node closeness and depends on neighbor interconnectivity.

entry.title: Oops, Not Now: PEARL, a RAG-Based Support Agent for Gameplay and What Players Want from AI Help

author.name: Jiahong Li, Sai Siddartha Maram, Atieh Kashani, Ulia Zaman, Zhiyu Lin, Cameron Marano, Roger Azevedo, Jichen Zhu, Magy Seif El-Nasr

entry.summary: PEARL is a dual-component retrieval-augmented generation system for a puzzle game that teaches parallel programming, combining semantic knowledge retrieval with structural board-state matching to deliver contextualized hints. The paper also reports player expectations for AI assistance, arguing that grounding generative models in structured game data yields capabilities a plain LLM with game state access lacks.

entry.title: Trustworthy, Explainable, and Sustainable Decentralized Intelligence for 6G Networks

author.name: Giovanni Perin, Michele Rossi, Enrique Tom\'as Mart\'inez Beltr\'an, Fernando Torres-Vega, Jos\'e Mar\'ia Jorquera Valero, Manuel Gil P\'erez, Eunjeong Jeong, Nikolaos Pappas, Farah Abed Zadeh, Chamara Sandeepa, Bartlomiej Siniarski, Madhusanka Liyanage, Bet\"ul G\"uven\c{c} Paltun, Leyli Kara\c{c}ay, Ioannis Pitsiorlas, Marios Kountouris

entry.summary: This multi-institution paper argues that AI in 6G shifts from an add-on optimization tool to a distributed structural layer spanning an edge-cloud continuum, where centralizing heterogeneous data creates latency, bandwidth, failure-point, and governance problems. It surveys decentralized intelligence approaches while emphasizing trustworthiness, explainability, and sustainability requirements.

entry.title: A New Transformer-Based Approach for Audio-Based Kinship Verification and a New Uncontrolled Mandarin Kinship Speech Dataset

author.name: Qiyang Sun, Langqing Zhang, Yupei Li, Bj\"orn Schuller

entry.summary: The paper proposes CONVTRAP-TN, which the authors describe as the first application of transformer architectures to audio-based kinship verification, and conducts an ablation study on the model. It also introduces ARKIN, a Mandarin kinship speech dataset collected to reflect everyday recording conditions, since existing kinship-labeled speech datasets are either extremely noisy internet data or recordings made in specified environments. It matters for biometric and speaker-attribute research under realistic acoustics.

entry.title: LLaTSA: Large Language Model-Aligned General-Purpose Transient Stability Analysis

author.name: Chao Shen, Hongwei Zhen, Junyan Shao, Zhenghao Yang, Yifan Zhang, Mingyang Sun

entry.summary: LLaTSA extends general-purpose LLM-based transient stability analysis by addressing short-observation ambiguity, mismatch between numerical trajectories and LLM embeddings, neglected coupling among state variables, and the inference cost of dense backbones. It aligns numerical power-grid trajectories with LLM representations to predict dynamic trajectories across heterogeneous systems. It matters for reducing the need to retrain grid stability predictors when network configuration or generation mix changes.

entry.title: Surrogate-Assisted Genetic Programming with Phenotypic Characterisation in Dynamic Multi-Mode Project Scheduling

author.name: Yuan Tian, Yi Mei, Mengjie Zhang

entry.summary: The study investigates how phenotypic characterization (PC) can improve surrogate-assisted genetic programming for evolving scheduling heuristics in dynamic multi-mode resource-constrained project scheduling, where simulation-based fitness is expensive. It compares three PC encoding schemes under a fixed budget of full fitness evaluations. It matters for making evolutionary heuristic discovery tractable under tight computational budgets.

entry.title: A Generative AI Integrated Multimodal Framework for Low-Latency Multi-Camera Person Re-Identification

author.name: Leon Fernando, C Dombawala, P. Hettigoda, Vanodhya G. Warnasooriya, Ishara Neranjana, Rashmika Nawaratne

entry.summary: This framework for multi-camera person re-identification combines global visual embeddings, VLM-generated fine-grained semantic attributes and optional facial cues, orchestrated by a cost-aware early-exit cascade that spends expensive modalities only on ambiguous cases. It targets robustness to occlusion, viewpoint and illumination change plus low-latency deployment. It matters for practical surveillance and tracking where latency and missing cues are the binding constraints.

entry.title: From Visual Attribution to Clinical Reasoning: Explainable Parkinson's Disease Screening from Hand-Drawn Patterns

author.name: Aritra Dey, Utsav Kumar Nareti, Chandranath Adak, Soumi Chattopadhyay, Krishna Gopal Sasmal, Saeed Anwar

entry.summary: This work presents an explainable framework for Parkinson's disease screening from offline hand-drawn spirals and meanders, modeling tremor oscillations, stroke irregularity and curvature instability with subject-disjoint evaluation. A multi-stage explainability pipeline maps visual attributions toward clinically grounded reasoning rather than black-box scores. It matters for trustworthy, low-cost early neuromotor screening.

entry.title: From Visual Feedback to Textual Reviews: A Multi-Agent Vision-Language Framework for Image-Grounded Review Assistance

author.name: Utsav Kumar Nareti, Ayush Bansal, Kumari Priya, Chandranath Adak, Soumi Chattopadhyay, Muhammad Saqib, Saeed Anwar

entry.summary: This paper defines image-grounded review assistance, a new task that generates editable review drafts from user-uploaded product images, going beyond objective captioning toward opinionated, context-rich text. The authors propose a multi-agent vision-language framework to produce these drafts, motivated by e-commerce platforms where visual feedback is abundant but detailed written reviews are scarce. The work sits at the intersection of multimodal generation and applied user assistance.

entry.title: PeerPen: AI-Assisted Writing for Online Mental Health Peer Support

author.name: Jiwon Kim, Sherry Gong, Maya Ajit, Soorya Ram Shimgekar, Yunhao Yuan, Dong Whi Yoo, Eshwar Chandrasekharan, Koustuv Saha

entry.summary: PeerPen is a writing-assistance tool embedded in a Reddit-like interface that offers draft generation and revision of user-written responses for online mental health peer support. Interviews with 15 participants found the tool reduced the burden of composing supportive replies and increased confidence, while raising concerns about authorship, ownership and preserving the personal nature of peer support.

entry.title: CAL-MOS: Bridging Layers with Adapters for Robust MOS Prediction Across Speech Foundation Models

author.name: Alef Iury Siqueira Ferreira, Pedro Lustosa Rege Botelho, Fernanda Silva, Daniel Casanova, Rafael Faustino, Frederico Oliveira, Arlindo Galv\~ao Filho, Anderson da Silva Soares

entry.summary: The study benchmarks ten speech foundation models on four MOS datasets under full fine-tuning, frozen last-layer probing, and naive cross-layer weighted aggregation, finding the best layer is strongly backbone- and dataset-dependent and that naive fusion is unstable. It evaluates a layer-calibrated aggregation approach with adapters to improve robustness of speech quality prediction.

entry.title: Physics Informed Neural Network model for the dynamical study of Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm

author.name: Adri\'an Robles Arques, Mart\'in Ruiz Fernandez, Javier Sanchis, Miguel A. Teruel, Juan Trujillo

entry.summary: The authors develop a three-dimensional physics-informed neural network framework to simulate pulsatile blood flow in the human aorta over a two-minute interval, extracting pressure and velocity fields and estimating wall stress via Laplace's law. The approach avoids mesh generation and conventional CFD overhead by leveraging automatic differentiation.

entry.title: Turkish MMLU Pro: Traceable Option Augmentation and Its Validity Limits in Turkish Multiple-Choice Evaluation

author.name: M. Ali Bayram

entry.summary: Turkish MMLU Pro examines whether adding distractor answer options lowers multiple-choice scores without improving assessment validity, using 12,000 Turkish-source questions across 58 sections. Each question keeps its stem, five original options, and source key, and receives five additional options copied from other questions in the same section, with candidates proposed by sentence embeddings and selected by a language model, then deterministically verified. A 25-model calibration shows source-key accuracies spanning 34.8 to 81.4 percent, and one API model drops from 93.7 to 83.1 percent when going from five to ten choices.

entry.title: Big Brains and Changing Environments: Cause or Consequence?

author.name: Sian Heesom-Green, Jonathan Shock, Geoff Nitschke

entry.summary: Using neuro-evolution in an artificial seasonal foraging task, this paper tests the Cognitive Buffer Hypothesis, which predicts large brains evolve in response to changing environments. Comparing agents evolved exclusively in changing environments against agents first evolved in static environments and then transitioned, the authors find larger neural networks in dynamic environments arise mainly from prior static evolution and perform better under unpredictable change. The results challenge strict CBH predictions and support a colonization-order interpretation.

entry.title: Beyond AI Literacy: A Structured Review and Exploratory Meta-Analysis of Measures for Competent Generative-AI Use

author.name: Daniele Veri'

entry.summary: This structured review examines 24 focal empirical publications on how researchers measure competent generative-AI use at work, grouping measures into knowledge and use, epistemic oversight, reliance calibration, and operational control of tool-using agents. An exploratory meta-analysis pools three subjective-objective correlations, finding a very small pooled effect that the author could not fully reconcile with the largest study's reported value.

entry.title: Sylvas: Synergistic Learning Value based Device Scheduling in Federated Continual Learning

author.name: Yuxuan Sun, Yuxuan Bai, Tan Chen, Sheng Zhou, Zhisheng Niu

entry.summary: Sylvas is a device scheduling framework for federated continual learning at the wireless edge that quantifies each device's contribution to global learning and schedules the most valuable participants under resource constraints. It evaluates learning value from distributional and other perspectives to handle spatio-temporal drift and label scarcity in IoT-style deployments.

entry.title: Criticality in Dissimilar Decomposition and Undersampling of Random Datasets with Anomalies

author.name: Ghurumuruhan Ganesan

entry.summary: This theory paper models AI-generated content in future LLM training corpora as anomalies linked to main data points and studies decomposition and undersampling properties of the resulting random datasets. Using redundancy graphs and iterative techniques, the authors bound the minimum size of a strongly dissimilar decomposition and demonstrate a phase transition: the minimum size is governed by main data points when anomalies are rare, and shifts as anomalies grow. It offers a formal lens on training-data composition as synthetic data accumulates.

entry.title: Data-Efficient Agentic Graph Domain Adaptation via Reliability-Aware Prototype Learning

author.name: Yingxu Wang, Kunyu Zhang, Siyang Gao

entry.summary: This work tackles graph domain adaptation in data-efficient agentic settings where only limited labeled source evidence is available, which makes source anchoring unstable and target calibration fragile. It proposes reliability-aware prototype learning to stabilize knowledge transfer from labeled source graphs to unlabeled target graphs under distribution shift.

entry.title: Learning Source Acquisition Policies by Offline Planning

author.name: Ziqi Zhao, Run Xu, Qingjian Ni

entry.summary: O-MPAC learns policies for selecting feature groups whose value depends on later queries under an acquisition budget, transferring finite-horizon risk-cost targets from complete training records into a shared source-action scorer. At inference the scorer re-scores after each query and applies a hard cost mask, with analysis of how tied teacher targets and planning horizon affect decisions.

entry.title: A family of spectral conjugate gradient algorithms derived by least-squares approximations based on a modified quasi--Newton update with application to a revised robust binary classification model

author.name: Saman Babaie-Kafaki, Maryam Khoshsimaye-Bargard, Ahmad Mousavi

entry.summary: The authors develop a spectral three-term modification of the Hestenes-Stiefel conjugate gradient algorithm that retains its anti-jamming property while enforcing sufficient descent. A modified secant equation yields a memoryless BFGS update, and the spectral parameter is chosen by steering the search direction toward the BFGS direction in a least-squares sense. Convergence is analyzed without convexity assumptions and the method is tested on a robust binary classification problem.

entry.title: Domain-specific Pretraining Profile and Transformer Performance: Evidence from Modeling Digital Pragmatics in Arabic-English Code-switching

author.name: Fahad Al Hussen, King Saud University, Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, Mohammed Q. Shormani, Ibb University, Ibb, Yemen
