Using preregistered tests with single-super-patch KV ablation and teacher-forced drops in gold-answer log-probability, the authors find retention is decoupled from causal utilization, and attention only weakly correlates. It matters because it warns that popular KV-cache eviction heuristics based on reconstruction or attention may be optimizing the wrong signal.

entry.title: STAR: Sparse Tactile Representation Learning in Vision-Tactile-Language-Action Models for Dexterous Manipulation

author.name: Xiangcheng Liu, Tianhao Wu, Le Zheng, Yidong Wang, Bowen Jiang, Mingjie Pan, Xinlin Ren, Yi Liu, Jianlan Luo

entry.summary: The authors build a bimanual teleoperation platform and collect a 200-hour dataset of 10,576 trajectories over 65 tasks with synchronized vision, tactile, and language annotations, then propose STAR, a training recipe for vision-tactile-language-action models that handles the spatial, temporal, and informational sparsity of tactile signals. It matters because large-scale real-world tactile data and effective sparse-tactile representations are widely viewed as bottlenecks for dexterous manipulation.

entry.title: Occamy-1.0: Open Pareto-frontier 35B Intelligence for Co-work

author.name: Wenhui Chen, Shiwen Cheng, Hao Dong, Chenda Duan, Ruixiang Feng, Zhong Guan, Boqiang Guo, Xueyuan Han, Haojie Hao, Liangmeng Huang, Zhelong Huang, Xinke Kong, Hongyu Li, Jiazheng Li, Junbo Li, Qingchuan Li, Yukun Lian, Chang Liu, Tianyu Liu, Zicheng Liu, Shuyi Ouyang, Yijun Pan, Kunyu Shi, Xiaojun Tang, Bingquan Wang, Kesu Wang, Yuchen Wang, Sibo Wei, Sicong Xie, Xiaoying Xing, Yi Xu, Zhijun Xu, Hongwei Xue, Qingcheng Zeng, Di Zhang, Guannan Zhang, Haochen Zhang, Tianlong Zhang, Tianyu Zhao, Tianyu Zhao, Yanjun Zheng, Jialong Zhu, Zijian Zou

entry.summary: Occamy-1.0 is a 35B-parameter mixture-of-experts co-work agent model built by further post-training the open Qwen3.6-35B-A3B checkpoint. The authors emphasize execution-grounded data, replayable long-horizon trajectories across multiple agent harnesses, and staged post-training aimed at cost efficiency rather than peak reasoning capability. It matters because it targets the practical economics of multi-step agent workflows where state tracking and recovery dominate.

entry.title: Is Gaussian Splatting Becoming Neural Again? A Taxonomy and Controlled Study of Learned Parameterization

author.name: YuanHang Wang, Xin Cao, Yi Zhang

entry.summary: This paper characterizes the trend of using neural networks to generate or share Gaussian parameters in 3D Gaussian Splatting along five axes: attribute decoding, spatial sharing, view-conditioned decoding, topology generation and amortized inference. An analysis of 19 representative methods shows the choices address different limitations and cannot be reduced to a simple neural/non-neural label, and a controlled mip-NeRF 360 study isolates three forms of neural parameterization. Sharing appearance and opacity helps reconstruction while decoding geometric structure adds no gain, favoring selective neuralization.

entry.title: SoK: Rethinking Jailbreaking in the Era of Agentic AI: Attacks, Defenses, and Practical Consideration

author.name: Md Jueal Mia, Yanzhao Wu, Selcuk Uluagac, M. Hadi Amini

entry.summary: This systematization of knowledge asks which established jailbreak findings still hold now that models are more strongly aligned and are deployed as agents with tools, memory, and multi-step execution. It reorganizes jailbreak security around the full agentic execution pipeline and builds unified taxonomies of attacks and defenses. The paper is valuable as a map of where classic LLM jailbreak results transfer to, or break down in, agentic deployments.

entry.title: Rethinking Heterogeneous System Disaggregation for Subquadratic Attention

author.name: Arya Tschand, Yaosheng Fu, Vikram Sharma Mailthody, Nicolai Oswald, Po-An Tsai, Ritchie Zhao, Oreste Villa, Vijay Janapa Reddi, Karu Sankaralingam

entry.summary: SQD argues that existing disaggregated serving systems are designed around dense attention and therefore make the wrong split for frontier models using subquadratic attention. The scheme disaggregates decode by quadratic versus subquadratic attention rather than by operator type, exploiting the distinct arithmetic intensity and memory footprints of each. The authors report throughput and energy-efficiency gains on emerging DRAM-based and SRAM-only heterogeneous hardware.

entry.title: The Anatomy and Boundary of Adaptation under Temporal Tabular Shift

author.name: Tianyu Wang, Xi Vincent Wang, Lihui Wang, Mian Li, Zhihao Liu

entry.summary: The paper studies prequential adaptation of frozen tabular foundation models under temporal drift, where labels are revealed only after prediction, and asks when such adaptation helps versus harms. It attributes gains to four recurring mechanisms under a streaming protocol that removes several optimistic biases, and formalizes limiting factors as an identified-set diameter wall and an orthogonal L2 projection wall. These walls characterize what cannot be recovered from unlabeled data or expressed by a frozen representation.

entry.title: TokenMapper: A Step Toward Interoperable Speech Token Translation

author.name: Tal Kozakov, Tal Rosenwein, Eliya Nachmani

entry.summary: Neural audio codecs turn speech into discrete token sequences, but each codec has its own vocabulary and codebook structure, so different speech models cannot exchange tokens directly. The authors propose TokenMapper, a direction-aware framework that translates tokens directly between heterogeneous speech tokenizers in the discrete domain. This matters because it could remove the decode-to-waveform and re-encode step that currently adds latency and information loss in voice agents and speech-to-speech translation.

entry.title: Certified Safety Curation: Distribution-Free Guarantees for Safe Offline Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Adam Haroon, Cody Fleming

entry.summary: The paper introduces a filter-then-clone pipeline for safe offline RL when costs are not labeled per transition: a state-only value learned from segment comparisons scores whole trajectories, Learn-then-Test calibration certifies a selection threshold with a distribution-free (alpha, delta) bound on the unsafe fraction, and behavior cloning follows. It argues this is the first certification of training-set composition for offline RL or imitation.

entry.title: Certifying Concept Unlearning in Text-to-Image Diffusion Models

author.name: Mansi, Luca Marzari, Francesco Leofante

entry.summary: The paper argues that attack-success-rate evaluations of concept unlearning in text-to-image diffusion models only provide finite-query empirical evidence and leave residual leakage unquantified. It introduces a certification framework combining statistical certification with worst-case analysis along concept-relevant embedding directions to yield high-confidence guarantees with bounded error on residual concept leakage.

entry.title: Sampling via Decision-Flow: Training-Free Extraction of Improved Latent Reasoning Paths in Large Language Models

author.name: Zhendong Mi, Shaoyi Huang

entry.summary: Building on the distribution-sharpening hypothesis that RL mainly reallocates probability mass toward high-reward trajectories already latent in base models, the authors propose Decision-Flow Sampling (DF-Sample), a training-free, data-free inference-time framework. It builds a hierarchical reasoning tree, scores terminal nodes, and back-propagates utilities to guide intermediate branching decisions instead of purely local step-wise sampling.

entry.title: Granularity-Adaptive Credit Assignment for Long-Horizon LLM Agent Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Taoran Liang, Yang Liu, Shang Luo, Yingguang Yang, Rongrong Zhang, Yingzong Min, Yulin Huang, Jianshen Zhang, Yongzhi Qi, Kefu Xu, Congjing Ran, Bin Chong

entry.summary: The paper criticizes trajectory-level group-relative RL methods such as GRPO for broadcasting a single scalar reward to every step of long-horizon agent trajectories, and criticizes prior step-level approaches like GiGPO for merging step and episode estimates under one fixed weight. It proposes GACA, a critic-free estimator whose credit-assignment granularity is state-dependent, spending more resolution on pivotal branching decisions than on routine transitions.

entry.title: Quantile-based Loss Filtering for Outlier-Robust Stochastic Gradient Descent

author.name: Jamie Haddock, Anna Ma, Elizaveta Rebrova

entry.summary: This paper proposes Quantile-k-Loss SGD (QkL-SGD), a general framework for finite-sum optimization in which a subset of component functions are corrupted and produce unreliable gradients. At each iteration the method samples k component losses and updates using an index drawn uniformly from the lower empirical q-quantile, generalizing prior minimum-loss-based SGD and quantile methods for corrupted linear systems. The authors prove linear convergence under convexity assumptions, with sample size scaling in the number of corruptions.

entry.title: A Ranking Approach for Measuring Calibration

author.name: Anirban Chatterjee, Rina Foygel Barber

entry.summary: Expected Calibration Error is the standard miscalibration measure but cannot be estimated with guaranteed accuracy without assumptions. The authors propose rankECE, a measure based on comparing points with neighboring predicted probabilities, and study its theoretical properties as an alternative that avoids this fundamental limitation.

entry.title: The Cost of Compression: A Rate-Distortion Limit on Factual Hallucination

author.name: Xi Wang, Shijia Xu, Rongfeng Guo

entry.summary: The authors model closed-book factual recall as a coverage and compression problem: a learner sees M facts, stores them in at most B bits, and must answer queries without retrieval. They prove a lower bound on error that separates coverage failures from approximation failures, showing that even observed facts may be recalled incorrectly when memory is finite.

entry.title: AMDKernelVault: Large-Scale Datasets and Agentic Training for AMD GPU Kernel Optimization

author.name: Ji Liu, Saptarshi Majumder, Yiqing Huang, Wenwen Ouyang, Umang Pandey, Zeping Li, Chushi Chen, Zihao An, Puyuan Yang, Zekai Li, Sina Rafati, Ziqiong Liu, Pratik Prabhanjan Brahma, Dong Li, Zicheng Liu, Sharon Zhou, Emad Barsoum

entry.summary: The authors release a large open corpus of HIP and Triton kernels for AMD CDNA GPUs, including over 62,000 execution-verified HIP samples, ROCm libraries QA entries, and roughly 40,000 Triton kernels, along with agent-driven pipelines that convert PyTorch references into validated kernels. They further train Qwen3-8B with supervised fine-tuning and execution-aware reinforcement learning to reduce dependence on repeated frontier-model calls.

entry.title: DuplexDrama: A Synthesized Dialogue Dataset with Scenarios, Full-Duplex Behaviors, Expressive Speech, and Sound Events

author.name: Qingxiang Guo, Wenke Fan, Shuofeng Zhao, Dawei Yang, Zhiyang Zhou, Yingxin Shang, Hongwei Cai, Zhou Wang, Weixu Wang, Lin Yang, Shuran Zhou, Yang Song

entry.summary: This paper introduces DuplexDrama, a synthesized spoken dialogue dataset that jointly covers persona/scenario settings, three full-duplex behaviors (interruption, backchannel, incomplete), persona-aligned emotional speech, and script-aware sound events. It is built through a four-stage pipeline and validated on both scripts and synthesized audio, yielding over 2,000 hours across a 64-voice pool with 13 personas, and was used internally to train full-duplex models.

entry.title: The Talker Does Not Control The Doer (in Current AIs)

author.name: Eliezer Yudkowsky

entry.summary: Eliezer Yudkowsky argues, based on personal observation of the August 2026 frontier models Fable 5 and Sol 5.6 and the so-called Hugging Face incident, that the part of a model that converses and appears obedient is not the part that actually generates code and prose. He uses a historical analogy about misaligned communication channels to suggest the conversational facade cannot be trusted to reflect the system's real behavior.

entry.title: Continuous Learning of Gravity Field Irregularities Around Small Bodies via Neural Hamiltonian ODEs

author.name: Giacomo Acciarini, Dario Izzo

entry.summary: The authors learn unknown gravity-field dynamics near a small body directly from tracking data by embedding a neural network inside the system Hamiltonian, yielding Neural Hamiltonian ODEs whose variational equations give exact training gradients. The method needs only position and velocity arcs at realistic noise levels, with a continual-learning scheme that warm-starts the network as new data arrive. It targets spacecraft proximity operations around asteroids, where shape and density irregularities make analytic gravity models inaccurate.

entry.title: IMPLY: Physically Anchored Consistency for World-Model Rollouts

author.name: Aman Mehta, Riya Baviskar

entry.summary: The paper argues that existing consistency checks for world-action models only ask whether a model's predicted futures agree with each other, with no grounding in physics, and that a model which ignores the object can pass such checks. IMPLY instead inverts a simulator to read the implied physics of each rollout, then scores a set of rollouts by how well a single object explanation accounts for all of them, anchored to two observed calibration pushes. It provides a physically anchored alternative to purely self-consistent evaluation of world models.

entry.title: Certified AI Triage of ICU Alarms

author.name: Mohammed Sameer Syed, Rozhin Yasaei

entry.summary: This paper reframes ICU alarm reduction as three-way triage (retain, suppress, or defer) and provides a statistical guarantee that the fraction of suppressed alarms that were genuine stays below a user-set budget with 95 percent confidence under i.i.d. sampling, with a clustered sensitivity check for waveform-dependent events. On the VTaC benchmark a 5 percent budget certifies across all three seeds while suppressing 74.8 percent of false alarms and silencing only 1.5 percent of genuine ones.

entry.title: Does Video Memory Use What It Retrieves? A Causal Audit of Memory Specificity

author.name: Aditi Tiwari, Akshit Bhalla, Darshan Prasad, Heng Ji

entry.summary: This causal audit introduces read-time memory substitution, swapping the consumed memory value while leaving other computation unchanged, to separate memory benefit from memory specificity. Across frozen video world models, identity-free controls with no evaluation-specific content recover nearly all the benefit on Ego-Exo4D and 7-Scenes and about 70% on TUM, indicating memory gains often do not depend on the retrieved content.

entry.title: Language Is an Insufficient Substrate for Quantitative Reasoning, and Consequential Domains Need Large Quantitative Models

author.name: Reuben Vandeventer, David Imrem, David J. Wild

entry.summary: This position paper argues that language is a lossy encoding of the quantitative record, so no downstream scaling can recover information that description never encoded. It formalizes this as a property of the training representation rather than of model capacity, and identifies further properties that consequential settings such as risk pricing, capital allocation and clinical triage demand. The claim is that these domains require dedicated large quantitative models rather than LLM-derived progress.

entry.title: GTA: Graph Theory Agent and Benchmark for Algorithmic Graph Reasoning with LLMs

author.name: Zixiang Xu, Yanbo Wang, Chenxi Wang, Lang Gao, Zirui Song, Yue Huang, Zhaorun Chen, Xiangliang Zhang, Xiuying Chen

entry.summary: The paper presents GT Bench, covering 24 classical graph problems in 44 task-structure settings with over 100,000 examples across natural language, structured language, adjacency list and adjacency matrix representations. It evaluates eight LLMs and shows accuracy is strongly tied to input representation and that the best representation shifts with the task, and it introduces a graph theory agent counterpart. It matters because prior graph evaluations used small graphs, simple tasks and single input formats.

entry.title: BlueLM-GUI Technical Report: A Real-Device-Centric Flywheel for Self-Improving Mobile GUI Agents

author.name: Tong Ye, Kunyang Han, Guozhi Wang, Longqiang Luo, Zhifeng Ding, Yongxiang Zhang, Xiaolei Shen, Yuxuan Zhang, Zhuping Zhang, Tao Xu, Yue Pan, Yucheng Zhao, Yupei Hu, Yuanjiang Ouyang, Danfeng Shen, Runqi Lin, Hongda Cai, Zhaoxiong Wang, Mengjia Yan, Yingjie Zhong, Chen Zhou, Zeyu Zhang, Xuwen Zhu, Penggang Shi, Mingcheng Luo, Ziyang Wu, Min Jin, Mingfu Shen, Zairong Xu, Fan Zhang, Hao Wang, Liang Liu, Zhulin Xie, Lijun Yao, Xiao Liang, Liangmin Wen, Liqiang Feng, Feilong Wu, Min Hu, Min Chen, Guanjing Xiong, Xiaohu Ruan, Xiaoxin Chen

entry.summary: BlueLM-GUI is a 35B-parameter mixture-of-experts mobile GUI agent built around a real-device-centric data flywheel, addressing sandbox-to-production distribution mismatch, underutilized real-device failures, and saturating fixed benchmarks. It uses a dual-track pipeline with Heterogeneous Triple-System Consensus evaluation and an error correction and derivation module to salvage trajectories into supervision, plus a three-stage training recipe. It matters as an industrial-scale account of closing the loop between real device rollouts and agent training.

entry.title: MedRoundsQA: A Persona and Difficulty Aware Evaluation for Multi-Turn Medical Consultations

author.name: Youssef Mohamed, Ahmed Heakl, Qinrong Cui, Junhong Liang, Rafiq Ali, Bdour Babillie, Nazira Dunbayeva, Lang Gao, Omar Hussein, Ahmed Nada, Ahmed Mohamed Magdy Mohamed, Jinghui Liu, Salman Khan, Imran Razzak, Yuxia Wang, Xiuying Chen

entry.summary: MedRoundsQA converts 1,387 board-exam cases across 17 specialties into structured 24-slot clinical records and then instantiates them as controlled doctor-patient dual-agent dialogues with varied patient personas, holding clinical content fixed. Cases are ordered by model-based uncertainty to support easy-to-hard analysis, and fifteen LLM doctor agents are evaluated. It pushes medical benchmarking away from single-turn multiple-choice questions toward interactive evidence elicitation.

entry.title: Hierarchical Prototype Emergence in Modern Hopfield Models

author.name: Aditya Cowsik, Adithya Sriram

entry.summary: This theoretical work studies how dense Hopfield networks with polynomial activation can store hierarchically correlated memories and generalize beyond them by reconstructing prototypes. The authors analytically derive conditions under which each level of the hierarchy is locally stable as an energy minimum, and show that only a quasi-polynomial amount of information is needed for generalization beyond the stored parts. It is framed as a step toward understanding hierarchical structure in modern architectures such as diffusion models.

entry.title: Beyond the Query: Do Retrieval Signals Improve Adaptive Multimodal RAG Routing?

author.name: Qiaomu Li, Qiuyuan Zhang, Nong Ming

entry.summary: The paper tests a common assumption in adaptive RAG: that retrieval-time signals help a router decide whether to run another retrieval, rerank, or multimodal step. Across document, audio and video RAG, it compares matched query-only and query-plus-retrieval routers while holding actions, router family, training and evaluation constant. The headline finding is a negative result: the tested retrieval signals do not deliver reliable routing improvement over a query-only baseline, even when they weakly predict when a later step helps.

entry.title: Calibrated Ambiguity in Multimodal Language Models: Humans reach for cultural references, while models describe the picture

author.name: Cody Kommers, Mingrui Ye, Evelyn Gius, Daniela Mihai, Hoyt Long, Zheng Yuan, Drew Hemment

entry.summary: The paper treats ambiguity not as a defect but as a communicative resource, operationalizing calibrated ambiguity through a Dixit-style clue-generation task. Comparing human and multimodal model clues under a new coding rubric, the authors find models show ambiguity collapse, producing over-specified outputs that leave little room for multiple legitimate interpretations, and that humans instead lean on cultural references. It matters as a culturally grounded evaluation of what multimodal models still miss about open-ended human expression.

entry.title: Score-based Outlier Generation via Controlling the Radon-Nikodym Derivative

author.name: Amartya Mukherjee, Tristan Milne, Kry Yik-Chau Lui, Stephanie Hazlewood, Jun Liu

entry.summary: This paper introduces a measure-theoretic definition of outliers based on the distribution of log-likelihood values, guaranteed to assign higher probability mass to low-likelihood events by a specifiable magnitude. It derives how likelihood reweighting modifies the diffusion score and uses the relation to controllably alter reverse-time dynamics for generating outliers.

entry.title: GUIDE: Generative Utility Inference and Decision Engine

author.name: Anagha Tiwari, Alexander G. Gray, Nick Feamster, Brian Jabarian, Alex Imas, Alex Kale

entry.summary: GUIDE is an LLM-driven elicitation architecture that infers multidimensional user preferences through conversation, combining Bayesian adaptive sampling for question selection with symbolic representation learning to initialize domain-specific preference models. It generalizes adaptive sampling through an extensible type system of transforms over a parameterized preference state, aiming to ground alignment inference in domain knowledge.

entry.title: The Rank the Task Demands: A Causal Rank Law for Matrix Memories Trained on Group Composition

author.name: Samuel Larson

entry.summary: Using a group-composition testbed with a hard single-state bottleneck and a fixed decoder, the paper reports causal evidence that gradient descent recruits precisely the rank demanded by a task's algebraic structure. It extends an earlier associative-binding rank law from a scalar capacity bound to a representation-theoretic one.

entry.title: ProactiveBench: Can Streaming Video Models Really Interact Like Humans?

author.name: Kaixuan Du, Xin Wan, YuKun Wang, Hang Zhang, Meng Cao, Dai Guan, Ming Chen, Ni Li

entry.summary: ProactiveBench evaluates streaming video understanding models on when to respond rather than only what to answer, using one-second stream intervals with no explicit response cue. It contains six subtasks varying trigger ambiguity and timing tolerance, including an Event Sensitivity metric that geometrically combines response and silence rates and window-based subtasks that distinguish early, in-window, and missed responses.

entry.title: Robust Policy Optimization via Adversarial Importance Sampling

author.name: Amine Andam, Jamal Bentahar, Mustapha Hedabou

entry.summary: The authors identify limitations across the algorithm design, implementation, and evaluation stages of adversarially robust deep reinforcement learning. They introduce Adversarial Importance Sampling (Advis), which reweights trajectories from standard training to estimate and optimize worst-case returns without extra environment interaction or auxiliary networks, and release advrl, a modular PyTorch library for robust DRL. The method is positioned as jointly achieving properties prior work achieved only separately.

entry.title: Judging by the Cover: Cleaning LLM Truthfulness Benchmarks to Avoid Surface-Level Feature Leakage

author.name: Foad Namjoo, Remy Ogasawara, Amirali Abdullah, Cullen Anderson, Narmeen Fatimah Oozeer, Jeff M. Phillips

entry.summary: The paper shows that binary-choice truthfulness benchmarks such as TruthfulQA are contaminated by surface-level artifacts: a simple six-feature logistic classifier can separate correct from incorrect answers, letting models score above chance without reasoning. The authors identify similar leakage in other benchmarks and release a cleaned TruthfulQA variant with leakage reduced close to chance.

entry.title: Agent as Policy for Robotic Manipulation

author.name: Mengzhao Jia, Yang Lin, Xixin Zhang, Zhihan Zhang, Xiaobai Liu, Meng Jiang

entry.summary: Agent as Policy demonstrates that a general-purpose agent can directly drive a physical robot throughout task execution without task-specific or environment-specific training. Given a task and robot interface, the agent interprets visual evidence, writes executable programs, issues motion commands, and revises actions based on physical outcomes, tested on real manipulation tasks spanning precision work, dynamic motions, and deformable objects.

entry.title: Kraken: LLM-based Speech-to-Speech Translation via Low-bitrate VQ and Dual-path Source Conditioning

author.name: Hayato Futami, Hassan Shahmohammadi, Tushar Dhyani, Alkis Koudounas, Rapha\"el Lafargue, Yosuke Kashiwagi, Quentin Jodelet, Emiru Tsunoo

entry.summary: Kraken addresses two obstacles in LLM-based speech-to-speech translation: predicting high-bitrate speech tokens and reliance on tightly aligned speaker/prosody data. It uses single-layer vector quantization trained to reconstruct self-supervised features, plus a source-conditioned Autowave-X token-to-waveform decoder, relaxing data constraints and improving non-linguistic transfer.

entry.title: Type Diversity Enables Transformers to Generalise Compositionally

author.name: Anssi Moisio, Mathias Creutz, Mikko Kurimo

entry.summary: The paper argues that Transformers' weaker structural versus lexical compositional generalization stems from dataset statistics, not architecture: prior benchmarks have high lexical type diversity and low structural type diversity. By constructing linguistically diverse variants of COGS and SLOG, the authors show that increasing structural constructor diversity substantially changes generalization behavior.

entry.title: Fast and Faithful: Principled Conditional Flow Matching for Inverse Problems

author.name: Shirin Shoushtari, Edward P. Chandler, Xiao Shi, Ulugbek S. Kamilov

entry.summary: This paper proposes a principled parametrization of the measurement-conditional velocity field for flow-matching-based imaging inverse problems. Under linear interpolation, the conditional velocity is expressed in terms of the posterior mean, which is characterized as the unique minimizer of a variational objective, so the forward model is enforced inside the learned velocity rather than bolted on via concatenation or separate data-consistency steps. It matters because it unifies conditioning-based and inference-guided approaches while offering fast sampling.

entry.title: SNAP3D: Physically Grounded 3D Parts for Assembly from a Single Image

author.name: Yu-Rou Tuan, Hao-Tang Tsui, Nicolas Ugrinovic, Kris Kitani, Xiaoxuan Ma

entry.summary: This paper targets part-aware 3D asset generation from a single image, arguing that existing methods produce visually plausible parts that fail as physical assemblies because neighbors interpenetrate, lack valid connections, or collapse under gravity. The authors propose a physics-guided framework that removes inter-part penetration, recovers a contact graph between adjacent parts, and inserts parameterized connectors at contact surfaces, refining connector placement and orientation using feedback from physical simulation.

entry.title: Brand New AI Solves a Millennium Prize

author.name: Zvi

entry.summary: Zvi's commentary covers three threads: an OpenAI next-generation model reportedly leapfrogging Astra within a week, the claim that this system solved the Navier-Stokes Millennium Prize problem eight days after starting training, and human credit disputes around the mathematics. It frames the real story as the rapid cadence of frontier AI progress rather than the math drama.

entry.title: Amortized Low-Rank Adaptation for Model-Based Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Fernando Palafox, David Fridovich-Keil

entry.summary: The paper studies adapting a learned world model to an unknown test-time environment from only a few episodes, within a known family of environments. It introduces CLAW, which uses a hypernetwork to generate low-rank (LoRA) adapters for the world model, aiming to combine the cheapness of in-context adaptation with the expressivity of gradient-based adaptation. The result is a method for fast, expressive test-time adaptation in model-based RL.

entry.title: Adaptive Agent Design

author.name: Raj Kiriti Velicheti, Subhonmesh Bose, Tamer Ba\c{s}ar

entry.summary: The paper studies an agent acting against a general non-Markovian environment that maintains internal agent states and is free to choose both the transition kernel over those states and the state-feedback policy it induces. It formalizes a bi-level design problem optimized from offline observational data collected under a behavioral policy, and proves almost-sure convergence of a soft Q-learning algorithm to the fixed point of a soft Bellman equation defined by stationary averages. It also characterizes how the resulting policy differs from optimal, including partially observed settings.

entry.title: Offline Reinforcement Learning for Wind Farm Control: A Wind Tunnel Study under Dynamic Wind Directions

author.name: Yuhan Su, Hongyang Dong, Simone Tamaro, Filippo Campagnolo, Carlo L. Bottasso, Xiaowei Zhao

entry.summary: The authors propose MTD3-BC, an offline reinforcement learning algorithm that learns yaw control for wind farm power maximization from a pre-collected dataset under changing wind directions. It adds an action-consistency term to the policy objective to keep yaw adjustments smooth and moderate, and avoids costly online interaction with a simulator. Validation is performed in a wind tunnel, giving the approach rare physical-experiment grounding.

entry.title: Physics as the label for measuring and correcting materials reasoning in multimodal models

author.name: Hasan Kurban, Rasul Khanbayov, Mustafa Kurban

entry.summary: MatPCR is a label-free benchmark that uses programmatic oracles to verify the physical consistency of a model's materials reasoning chain, checking diffraction geometry via Bragg's law, scale bars, spectral peaks, and Materials Project-grounded checks of stability, band-gap class, and magnetization. This targets the gap that answer-level evaluation and DFT verification leave in reasoning-chain validity.

entry.title: Competence-Gated Pooling of Language Models and Priors for Event Forecasting

author.name: Aditi Tiwari, Aashrith Bandaru, Heng Ji

entry.summary: The paper reframes hybrid forecasting around a model's relative competence, i.e. its marginal value beyond an existing external forecast, rather than standalone accuracy. Under Brier loss it characterizes when model disagreement improves an external forecast and introduces a competence gate that learns domain-level weights from resolved outcomes, shrinks uncertainty toward a global weight, and recalibrates the pool. It matters for any system that must decide whether an LLM adds signal over markets, crowds or statistical baselines.

entry.title: Toward Robust Personalized Alignment for LLMs: Mitigating Persona Drift in Multi-Turn Dialogue

author.name: Youyuan Zhang, Siyuan Li, Fangming Liu, Jing Li

entry.summary: The paper proposes CORE, which separates turn-local evidence from persistent persona-state revision and selectively updates grounded user preferences through uncertainty-aware belief revision. It also introduces PERSIST, a held-out post-anchor benchmark for persona-state robustness under sequential interaction stress covering ambiguity, conflict and controlled social influence. It matters for long-horizon personalized alignment where profiles evolve but transient observations should not trigger updates.

entry.title: Reproducing and Evaluating the Generalizability of Subliminal Learning in Open-Weight Models

author.name: Daan van der Weijden, Nathan Brack, Selene Baez Santamaria

entry.summary: This reproduction study revisits subliminal learning, where a teacher model transmits behavioral preference traits through semantically unrelated training data during distillation. The authors reproduce the original animal-preference and misalignment experiments across number sequences, code, and chain-of-thought, then extend to new preference categories (actors, politicians), a chess-move generation task, an additional open-weight model, and an answer-space-size ablation. The work is important because it stress-tests a surprising and safety-relevant phenomenon on openly accessible checkpoints.

entry.title: When Rubrics Fail: Hallucinations Reveal Blind Spots in Medical AI Evaluation

author.name: Griffin Farrow, Lily Sijia Li, Jack Johnson, Tingyan Wang, Philip Torr, William Bolton, Fabio J. Fehr

entry.summary: The paper investigates whether the dominant rubric-based evaluation paradigm in medical AI actually captures clinically relevant hallucinations. Using a taxonomy of medical hallucination types and a clinician-validated error-injection pipeline that creates matched correct and error-injected responses, the authors test across HealthBench, HealthBench Professional, and LiveMedBench and find rubrics miss clinically relevant hallucinations. It is a direct challenge to how medical LLM quality is currently measured.

entry.title: Pelican-Sim 1.0: A General World Model Simulator for Embodied Intelligence

author.name: Shilong Zou, Shilin Zhang, Yingji Zhang, Yuhang Huang, Yi Zhang, Zeyuan Ding, Han Dong, Junwei Liao, Yong Dai, Jian Tang, Xiaozhu Ju

entry.summary: Pelican-Sim 1.0 is a technical report on a general world-model simulator that predicts future observations from visual context and robot actions to support downstream learning and decision making. Key design choices include a unified 28-dimensional action space spanning mainstream embodiments, action-visual injection via URDF and camera-rendered action videos to improve controllability, and sparse mixture-of-experts layers for heterogeneous embodiments. Reported gains include PSNR improvements over alternative fusion baselines.

entry.title: Chopthin-Consensus Power Sampling: A Diversity-Preserving Approach to LLM Decoding

author.name: Minoo Ahmadi, Seyedarmin Azizi, Erfan Baghaei Potraghloo, Mehdi Kamal, Massoud Pedram

entry.summary: This paper introduces Chopthin-Consensus Power Sampling, which applies the Chopthin resampler to inference-time power sampling via Sequential Monte Carlo for LLM reasoning. Instead of equal-weight resampling that aggressively prunes low-weight trajectories and destroys genealogical diversity, the method bounds the ratio between largest and smallest particle weights and carries unequal weights forward. The aim is to preserve diverse reasoning paths while keeping the benefits of SMC-based decoding without any post-training.

entry.title: HypoKG: Evidence-Disciplined Biomedical Hypothesis Generation Beyond Endpoint Knowledge

author.name: Dominic Okonkwo, Adetayo Okunoye, Ismailcem Budak Arpinar

entry.summary: HypoKG asks whether LLM-generated biomedical hypotheses genuinely reason from scientific evidence or merely sound plausible, by unifying KEGG, Rhea, and UniProt into a single biochemical knowledge graph and building a benchmark of 550 paths from enzyme sources to rare disease endpoints. It generates 13,200 hypotheses from six LLMs under four information conditions, varying whether models see only the source enzyme, the full biological path, or only the source and disease endpoint. Hypotheses are scored with an expert-derived five-criterion rubric on a 1-5 scale per criterion.

entry.title: Optimizing Geoengineering Interventions Using Differentiable Climate Models

author.name: Pulkit Dubey, Dorian S. Abbot, Ashesh Chattopadhyay

entry.summary: The paper uses recently developed differentiable atmospheric models to design a novel geoengineering control strategy, imposing a uniform 4 K ocean warming in the differentiable primitive-equation model JAX-GCM. It then asks which pattern of sea-surface temperature cooling across five ocean-masked zonal bands, with free amplitudes, returns land near-surface air temperature closest to the model's own unwarmed climatology. The setup represents a cooling pattern that could be deployed while minimizing disruption.

entry.title: SCOPE-OPSD: Fisher-Conditioned Privileged Subspaces for On-Policy Self-Distillation

author.name: Yunmeng Chen (Chongqing Ant Consumer Finance Co., Ltd), Kunyu Wang (Alibaba Cloud Computing Co., Ltd), Peihan Li (Chongqing Ant Consumer Finance Co., Ltd), Yi Wang (Chongqing Ant Consumer Finance Co., Ltd), Shuyin Xia (Chongqing University of Posts and Telecommunications), Yi Liu (Chongqing Ant Consumer Finance Co., Ltd), Xinyong Cheng (Alibaba Cloud Computing Co., Ltd), Dehui Wang (Alibaba Cloud Computing Co., Ltd), Xiangyong Zhai (Alibaba Cloud Computing Co., Ltd), Yanxing Liu (Chongqing Ant Consumer Finance Co., Ltd), Song Liu (Chongqing Ant Consumer Finance Co., Ltd)

entry.summary: The work asks whether the aligned final-layer discrepancy between a solution-conditioned self-teacher and a student can serve as a second supervision channel beyond next-token probabilities in on-policy self-distillation. SCOPE-OPSD projects the privileged teacher-student residual onto a frozen rank-64 factor estimated from residual covariance and language-model-head Fisher sensitivity, reusing existing forward passes and adding no rollouts or inference modules. A rank-matched random control with per-arm gradient-RMS calibration isolates the contribution of the structured subspace, strengthening the experimental claim.

entry.title: Supermartingale Certificates for Parametric MDPs

author.name: Kaushik Mallik, {\DH}or{\dj}e \v{Z}ikeli\'c

entry.summary: The paper studies formal verification and synthesis for parametric Markov decision processes with general measurable state and action spaces. It introduces a parameter-flattening transformation mapping parametric MDPs to semantically equivalent non-parametric ones, and defines parametric supermartingale certificates that generalize classical supermartingale certificates. This yields, per the authors, the first verification and synthesis algorithms for polynomial-arithmetic parametric MDPs, which matters for reasoning about uncertain-parameter decision systems with guarantees.

entry.title: Tasks over Application Manuals: Revealing Gaps in Long-Horizon Procedural Reasoning for Language Models

author.name: Utkarsh Soni, Syed Shariyar Murtaza, Yifan Nie, Sachin Chandrasekhar, Eugene Wen

entry.summary: This work introduces TAM, a benchmark for long-horizon procedural reasoning, built from real-world tasks in ICD-10-CM clinical coding and U.S. tax or regulatory domains that require following manuals hundreds of pages long with interdependent guidelines. It argues existing multi-hop benchmarks are too short-horizon to reveal whether LLMs can reliably follow complex real procedures.

entry.title: Inverting Self-Triggered Control: Adversarial Reinforcement Learning for Sparse Denial-of-Service Attacks

author.name: Adam Haroon, Erick J. Rodr\'iguez-Seda, Tristan Schuler, Cody Fleming

entry.summary: This work inverts self-triggered RL control (RL-STC) by training an adversarial RL agent to discover the sparsest jamming or DoS schedule that destabilizes a closed loop, using a Lyapunov-increase admissibility predicate mirroring the defender's safety certificate. It proves a plant-property lower bound on the minimum jam count needed to force a crash against a self-triggered controller.

entry.title: Almost Sure Convergence Analysis of Stochastic Gradient Methods with Clipping and Additive Noise

author.name: Amartya Mukherjee, Jun Liu

entry.summary: The paper proves almost-sure convergence of SGD with clipping and additive Gaussian noise (SGD-CN) under smoothness and uniformly bounded stochastic-gradient-noise assumptions with standard decaying step sizes, extending the analysis to momentum variants. It targets the theoretical gap created by clipping bias and added noise variance in robust and privacy-oriented training.

entry.title: PLSP (Pre-hoc Liminal Space Profiling): OOD Prediction over Detection -- An Anticipatory Approach for Machine Learning Model Reliability

author.name: Vipul Bansal, Himanshu Buckchash, Balasubramanian Raman, Deepak Dhungana

entry.summary: PLSP reframes OOD handling from post-hoc detection to pre-hoc prediction, introducing a dataset-independent CREDibility Score (CREDS) and credibility curves that characterize the maximum credibility a model can attain on given data. The authors argue existing detection methods rely on inference-time metrics like accuracy and AUC-ROC and thus assess OOD response only indirectly.

entry.title: Temporal Recurrence Favors Fewer Layers

author.name: Ivan Anokhin, Johan Obando-Ceron, Irina Rish, Sebastian Risi

entry.summary: This study frames depth allocation as a compute-budget problem, asking how much within-step depth is still needed once temporal recurrence carries computation across streaming steps. Sweeping within-step depth, expert width, and experts per layer across budgets, it compares the best recurrent and non-recurrent allocations at roughly matched per-step compute on tasks such as Sokoban and autoregressive settings.

entry.title: Where Decoder Cosine Similarity Fails for SAE Feature Flow Discovery

author.name: Hendrik Droste, Christian Medeiros Adriano, Kathrin Korte, Holger Giese

entry.summary: This interpretability paper examines how sparse autoencoder features interact during model updates, focusing on MLP sublayers as a first test case. It builds a transition atlas of triples in which a residual-state feature plus an MLP-update feature jointly predict a downstream residual feature, and identifies where decoder cosine similarity, a common proxy, fails to capture these feature-flow relationships.

entry.title: GenOR-Twin: A Semantic Middleware for Integrating Operational Discourse with Mathematical Optimization

author.name: Rahimeh Neamatian Monemi, Shahin Gelareh, Lubin Cui, Nelson Maculan

entry.summary: This paper proposes a neuro-symbolic middleware that uses large language models purely as semantic translators between unstructured operational logs and formal mathematical optimization models, rather than as direct solvers. A dynamic constraint injection mechanism converts qualitative disruption events described by humans into hard constraints that reshape the optimization problem's feasible region at runtime. The design aims to preserve the feasibility guarantees of exact combinatorial solvers while still letting human operational discourse steer the model.

entry.title: A Unified and Constrained View of Regularization-Based Robust Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Amine Andam, Jamal Bentahar, Mustapha Hedabou

entry.summary: This paper unifies regularization-based robust deep RL by deriving new upper bounds on the performance gap between nominal and worst-case policies. Each bound decomposes into an existing regularization objective plus a KL-divergence penalty, explaining why KL penalties improve robustness in practice. The authors then recast robust training as constrained optimization, showing existing methods are the fixed-Lagrange-multiplier special case and jointly updating the multiplier with policy parameters instead.

entry.title: The Battery Price of edge AI: A study of the Environmental Impact of LLM Inference on Mobile Devices

author.name: \'Edouard Gu\'egain, Tristan Coignion

entry.summary: This paper systematically studies the energy consumption, performance, and accuracy of on-device LLM inference, motivated by the shift toward local-first AI driven by privacy and latency concerns. The authors evaluate 18 models spanning families, sizes, and quantization levels on two modern smartphones and a server. They argue that the additional battery drain could shorten device battery life and raise device replacement rates, adding an environmental dimension to the local-versus-cloud tradeoff.

entry.title: Dissecting GPU Utilization for LLM Inference on Nvidia Hopper

author.name: Mohammad Siavashi, Gerald Q. Maguire Jr., Dejan Kostic, Marco Chiesa

entry.summary: The authors profile vLLM with FlashAttention-3 and cuBLASLt on an H100 across cold prefill, warm prefill, and decode phases, showing that a single SM utilization counter masks the real story. During decode, dense projection GEMMs become small-row matrix multiplies that fill only a fraction of Hopper's fixed 64-row bfloat16 GMMA fragments, making the workload look saturated while doing little useful work.

entry.title: SynthSentry: Detecting Synthetic Data Contamination in Language Model Training Data

author.name: Praveen Kumar Myakala, Ravichandra Namburi, Sowmya Keragodu Jayaramu, Sooraj George Thomas

entry.summary: Rather than diagnosing model collapse after training, SynthSentry screens a corpus of unknown provenance before training by computing a corpus-level distributional divergence over lexical diversity collapse, n-gram tail truncation, and perplexity variance across reference models. It requires no access to the generating model, no generation history, and no synthetic labels, and is evaluated on corpora contaminated by small open-weight and instruction-tuned generators.

entry.title: Representation-based Masked Diffusion Model

author.name: Yangrong Hu, Ding Huang, Xueyu Zhou, Jian Huang

entry.summary: Masked diffusion models enable parallel text generation, but existing samplers update masked tokens independently and ignore their mutual dependencies, hurting coherence. RMDM encodes text into a continuous semantic space with a pretrained encoder and uses that representation to explicitly carry global semantics and coordinate parallel token updates.

entry.title: LifeMem: Enabling Lifelong Experience Reuse for LLM Agents

author.name: Yuli Qiu, Yutong Li, Wei Su, Zeming Liu, Wanxiang Che, Heyan Huang, Haifeng Wang, Yuang Guo

entry.summary: LifeMem is a lifelong learning framework that clusters accumulated agent interaction trajectories by underlying workflow to extract reusable skills, then recalls relevant skills and trajectories at inference to guide new tasks. It targets two problems in memory-based agents, poor cross-environment transfer of experience and catastrophic forgetting as experience accumulates.

entry.title: SAS: Simple Attention Sparsification via End-to-End Optimization of Context Ranking

author.name: Zhiwei Li, Lei Zhu, Hao Gu, Xiang Hu, Yan Wang, Haitao Mi, Sirui Han, Leo Liang, Zhijiang Guo

entry.summary: SAS targets post-training attention sparsification, arguing that existing trainable selectors distill dense attention distributions rather than directly optimizing which context units matter under a fixed attention budget. The method optimizes context ranking end-to-end with the language modeling loss so the selector's ranking aligns with predictive impact, improving sparse attention efficiency.

entry.title: UniMo: Unifying Human and Animal Motion Generation

author.name: Zeyu Zhang, Zhiyuan Zhang, Siheng Wang, Yiran Wang, Danning Li, Ian Reid, Richard Hartley

entry.summary: UniMo proposes a unified point cloud-based motion generation framework that bypasses skeletal topology differences, allowing text-driven motion generation to extend from humans to diverse animal species within one model. It also targets the limited scale and annotation quality of existing animal motion datasets, which have constrained prior per-species approaches.

entry.title: Balancing Emotional Alignment and Semantic Consistency in Image Generation via Reinforcement Learning with Valence-Arousal Anchoring

author.name: Jisheng Dang, Zhenxuan Wang, Bin Li, Ronghao Lin, Bin Hu, Tat-Seng Chua

entry.summary: The paper tackles continuous emotion control in text-to-image generation, where stronger affective conditioning often causes emotion-semantic drift and unintended content changes. It combines flow-matching generation, continuous valence-arousal conditioning, GRPO reinforcement learning, and a neutral semantic anchor that converts the deterministic probability-flow ODE into a marginal-preserving SDE. This matters for controllable generative models where affective intent must be adjusted without altering objects or layout.

entry.title: Physics-Aware Video Generation via Agentic Planning and Graph-Guided Optimization

author.name: Minh-Loi Nguyen, Xuan-Vu Le, Thanh-Toan Do, Tam V. Nguyen, Minh-Triet Tran, Trung-Nghia Le

entry.summary: PhysPlan is a training-free test-time guidance framework that aims to inject physical plausibility into video diffusion models without retraining them. It replaces global gradient updates and rigid scheduling heuristics with agentic planning and graph-guided optimization so that passive backgrounds are not corrupted and dynamic state changes are better modeled. It matters because video generators still produce visually appealing but causally impossible sequences.

entry.title: Guardrailed Meta-Agent Loops: Stress-Testing Policy Pinning, Budget Bounds, and Crash Recovery

author.name: Qinzhen Ma, Jialin Wu

entry.summary: The authors present GuardrailLoop, a simulation-based testbed for self-improving agent workflows, addressing the audit problem that arises when a controller can alter both its behavior and the criteria by which that behavior is judged. It makes three operational contracts jointly testable: preservation of human-defined policy, compute accounting at every recorded execution prefix, and recovery of a specified scientific state after crashes, with a hash-pinned policy fixing goals, scope, evaluation identity, budget, and release conditions.

entry.title: GLARE: Generative Learning via Adversarial Reward Estimation For Social Dynamics Forecasting

author.name: Tenghao Huang, Zhaoxuan Tan, Muhao Chen, Jonathan May, Mengting Wan, Longqi Yang, Pei Zhou, Sihao Chen

entry.summary: The paper introduces the Meeting Dynamic Forecasting Benchmark, built from 2,207 real meetings and 24,794 future-facing queries, where a model generates a plausible multi-turn continuation from a transcript prefix plus an active question. It evaluates utility toward the question and human-likeness without requiring exact reproduction of the observed future, and presents GLARE, an adversarial imitation learning adaptation for conditional generation. It matters for modeling multi-party social dynamics rather than exact next-utterance prediction.

entry.title: Large Distant Gradients Need Not Be Reliable: reliability-weighted credit assignment for long-horizon autoregressive forecasting

author.name: Junhao Zhao, David Michael Simberg, Jacob Kang, Colin Connor Kurniawan, Nan Xu

entry.summary: In long-horizon autoregressive forecasting, backpropagation through many steps can let distant gradients dominate updates while amplifying noise alongside signal, so a large distant gradient is not necessarily trustworthy. The authors propose Internal Dual-Wiener routing, a backward-only intervention that keeps the full forward rollout and all horizon losses while reliability-weighting internal gradient routes using bounded Wiener gains for identity and nonlinear paths. This matters for credit assignment in long-rollout training of forecasting and sequence models.

entry.title: FRIST: FMRI Representation Informed Shared-space Training Improves EEG-only Individual-Finger BCI Decoding

author.name: Jintao Zhang, Yidan Ding, Joshua Kosnoff, Maxim Karrenbach, Hanwen Wang, Bin He

entry.summary: FRIST is a two-stage EEG decoding framework that first learns fMRI-informed spectral projections from simultaneous EEG-fMRI recordings, then uses fMRI-derived class geometry to guide residual refinement of EEG predictions, transferring information through shared finger labels without paired data at test time. It targets individual-finger motor decoding, where cortical proximity and volume conduction blur EEG signals.

entry.title: VideoTok4D: A 4D-Aware Video Tokenizer for Compact World Representation

author.name: Xinyi Chen, Hanxin Zhu, Xijun Wang, Xingrui Wang, Sen Liang, Xin Li, Zhibo Chen

entry.summary: VideoTok4D argues that current video tokenizers treat video as sequences of 2D images rather than observations of a dynamic 3D world, biasing learned latents toward observation-centric rather than scene-centric structure. The method introduces spatiotemporal disentanglement and other designs to produce tokens that compactly represent real-world 4D scenes. It matters for video compression, reconstruction, and generation, and for world-model style representations.

entry.title: Reading the Whole Heart: Latent-Attention Masked Autoencoders for Multimodal Cardiac Representation Learning

author.name: Andrea Agostini, Simon B\"ohi, Moritz Vandenhirtz, Samuel Ruiperez-Campillo, Max Kr\"ahenmann, Silke M\"uhlstedt, Irene Cannistraci, Ece \"Ozkan Elsen, Julia E. Vogt, Thomas M. Sutter

entry.summary: LAMAE is a multimodal, structure-aware masked autoencoder that jointly learns patient-level cardiac representations during self-supervised pretraining instead of fusing modalities only at finetuning time. It exchanges information directly in latent space across ECG, echocardiography, chest radiographs and clinical variables. The work matters for medical foundation models that today remain largely modality-specific.

entry.title: AIM: A Privacy-Aware Interoperable Memory Framework for Multi-Agent Multi-User LLM Systems

author.name: Zachary Johnson, Nigel Boachie Kumankumah, Somya Chatterjee, Tejas Sathyamurthi, Min Chen, Xinyi Alice Li, Xiao Wang, Emily Morgan Gelchie, Jessica Lin, Sadid A. Hasan, Sulaiman Vesal

entry.summary: AIM is a unified, privacy-aware memory framework that lets multi-agent, multi-user LLM systems persistently manage both private and shared memory, dynamically classifying information as user-scoped private or globally public. It targets the limitation that existing agentic memory systems operate at the individual-user level and cannot share public knowledge across users. It matters for multi-user deployment of persistent memory agents and the privacy enforcement that entails.

entry.title: EvoRS: On-Policy Self-Evolution of Reward Systems for Open-Ended Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Weiyuan Li, Aili Chen, Xintao Wang, Yikai Zhang, Qingqing Dong, Jinghan Xu, Hongru Hou, Wenxuan Zhao, Chengkun Lang, Jun Gao, Yuanli Guo, Hongcheng Guo, Yanghua Xiao, Deqing Yang

entry.summary: EvoRS addresses the feedback loop in open-ended RL where a rubric-based reward system becomes unreliable as the policy optimizes against it, via reward hacking or reduced discriminability. It evolves the reward system from on-policy experience, representing it as an executable Reward-DAG that an agentic designer can modify, so failures in scoring mechanism and signal composition can also be repaired, not just the criteria. This matters for making rubric-based RL more robust over long training runs.

entry.title: EduFair-Bench: Evaluating Pedagogical Fairness of LLM Tutors Across Student Demographics

author.name: Jiaxu Zhao, Bahar Radmehr, Fares Fawzi, Tanya Nazaretsky, Tanja K\"aser

entry.summary: EduFair-Bench audits whether LLM tutoring quality varies systematically with student demographics, pairing a multi-domain question bank in mathematics, physics, and chemistry with a controlled simulation where a fixed LLM student interacts with each tutor across nine demographic levels spanning gender, immigration background, first language, and socioeconomic status. Quality is scored on five turn-level pedagogical metrics and four conversation-level dimensions using an LLM judge validated against human ratings. It extends fairness auditing from answer correctness to pedagogy itself.

entry.title: Agentic TCAD Calibration Workflow for Oxide Semiconductor Transistors

author.name: Gyujun Jeong, Junmo Lee, Sungwon Cho, Woohyun Hwang, Kwangyou Seo, Suhwan Lim, Wanki Kim, Daewon Ha, Rishi Ranade, Kihang Youn, Ram Cherukuri, Yiyi Wang, Asif Khan, Shimeng Yu

entry.summary: This paper demonstrates an agentic TCAD calibration workflow for a fabricated bottom-gate indium-tungsten-oxide transistor, where multiple physical models and parameter sets can reproduce the same measured transfer characteristics. Starting from the measured transfer curve and device information, the workflow uses measurement-to-TCAD residuals and local sensitivity tests to select bounded parameter corrections or evaluate additional physical models, addressing model ambiguity that makes manual calibration slow and expert dependent. It is presented as the first such agentic calibration demonstration for this device class.

entry.title: DriftSE: Speech Enhancement with Generative Drifting

author.name: Liang Xu, Diego Caviedes-Nozal, W. Bastiaan Kleijn, Longfei Felix Yan, Rasmus Kongsgaard Olsson

entry.summary: DriftSE formulates speech enhancement as a latent distribution equilibrium problem, training a drifting field that aligns the generator's pushforward distribution with the clean speech manifold in a latent domain, then discarding the drifting process at inference for one-step generation. The authors show that enhancement quality depends fundamentally on the latent choice, since semantic latents preserve phonetic structure but miss physical acoustic cues while acoustic latents risk linguistic hallucination. Their fix is dual-latent drifting, running parallel drifting in both semantic and acoustic spaces.

entry.title: Recommendation Retrievers Need Verifiers: Universal Generative Reranking for Sequential Recommendations

author.name: Benyu Zhang, Qiang Zhang, Rui Li, Qunshu Zhang, Devansh Tandon, Neeraj Bhatia

entry.summary: The paper targets a practical gap in multi-stage recommendation pipelines: the short prefix forwarded to expensive downstream rankers can miss relevant items that sit deeper in the retrieved list. It proposes a lightweight generative verifier that post-hoc promotes such candidates into the consumed shortlist without retraining or replacing the existing retriever. The contribution is a cheap, retriever-agnostic verification layer aimed at improving effective recall under a fixed shortlist budget.

entry.title: Earth-Agent-Pro: Towards Real-World Full-Chain Earth Observation with Agents

author.name: Zhutao Lv, Chenhao Dang, Yi Feng, Yanpei Gong, Xiaolei Wang, Junyan Ye, Conghui He, Weijia Li

entry.summary: The paper argues that real Earth observation agents must translate high-level scientific questions into executable workflows that acquire observations, prepare data, run domain computations and derive conclusions from runtime evidence, whereas existing agents and benchmarks start from prepared inputs. It presents Earth-Agent-Pro, an execution-adaptive plan-and-execute framework that constrains planning and tool use with expert-authored skills. A workflow-centered structured memory records planned steps, accepted evidence and dependencies, allowing repair of only the affected workflow suffix when runtime evidence changes.

entry.title: GraphAHA: Graph-Based Adaptive Search with Heterogeneous Actions for Test-Time Code Generation

author.name: Xitao Li, Haijun Wang, Gege Yuan, Qiyuan Wu, Jiali Wei, Ming Fan, Xiaofei Xie

entry.summary: Test-time scaling for code generation spends extra inference budget on sampling, feedback-conditioned repair, and reasoning-guided implementation, but tree-structured search duplicates work when different trajectories converge on the same program. GraphAHA replaces the tree with a graph search that merges equivalent states and shares evaluation statistics, and it adaptively allocates budget among heterogeneous actions whose payoffs vary by state. This matters for making inference-time compute for coding models more efficient and effective.

entry.title: Online Video Agent Harness for Long Video Understanding

author.name: Sen Yang, Boqiang Duan, Jing Yang, Weihao Bo, Jie Liu, Boyuan Tong, Ze Feng, Wenkang Zhang, Jingdong Wang, Hua Wu

entry.summary: Long video understanding is framed as a visual needle-in-a-haystack problem, where evidence is sparse in time and stuffing dense frames into one vision-language context causes context rot and high cost. VideoXAgent is a purely online agent harness that starts from the raw video file and query, plans and decomposes the task, calls specialized expert tools on demand, and aggregates and reconciles multimodal evidence. This matters for building efficient, query-adaptive video understanding systems instead of query-agnostic offline preprocessing pipelines.

entry.title: UniPart: Towards Zero-shot Language-Grounded 3D Part Segmentation for Embodied Interaction

author.name: Xinqiang Yu, Zekun qi, Jiawei He, Wenyao Zhang, Xuchuan Chen, Guaocai Yao, Li Yi, Zhaoxiang Zhang, He Wang

entry.summary: Fine-grained robotic manipulation needs part-level understanding, but existing 3D foundation models are either object-aware and general or part-aware only within closed taxonomies. UniPart is a feed-forward cross-modal 3D Transformer conditioned on CLIP text embeddings that segments the functional part specified by a free-form phrase in a point cloud. The authors also build LangPart-1M, with over 160K Objaverse assets and 8M text-to-part pairs generated with multi-view consistency, plus a manually labeled subset for fine-tuning and evaluation.

entry.title: Attention Quantization for Tabular Foundation Models

author.name: Jonas M. K\"ubler, Benjamin J\"ager, Klemens Fl\"oge, Noah Hollmann, Frank Hutter

entry.summary: This work studies inference efficiency for tabular foundation models, showing that the attention computation matters more than weight or KV-cache quantization, which dominate LLM practice. It develops an FP8 quantization strategy for queries, keys, and values using explicit FP8 matrix multiplication, and stresses aligning quantization error between test and training rows to preserve accuracy.

entry.title: MAxBench: A Multinomial Concept Recovery Benchmark

author.name: Divya Appapogu, Freya Behrens, Yonatan Belinkov, Aaron Mueller

entry.summary: MAxBench is a geometry-agnostic evaluation framework for multinomial concept representations in language models, addressing concepts like Animals or Countries that contain many subcategories rather than being binary like refusal. It samples from recovered concepts to assess how well different representation geometries and recovery methods handle non-binary concepts, which matters for steering and interpretability.

entry.title: DCRA: Diffusion-Conditioned Representation Alignment for Robust Time-Series Learning

author.name: Wenrui Xu, Anas Enanaa, Keshab K. Parhi

entry.summary: DCRA reframes the forward diffusion process as a structured corruption scheduler for representation learning, producing a controlled, continuous corruption trajectory instead of independently sampled perturbations. It applies this to noisy clinical time-series tasks such as EEG and ECG analysis, adding a feature-level consistency objective to improve robustness under noise and distribution shift.

entry.title: Scalable Discrete-to-Continuous Channel Simulation for Compression and Privacy

author.name: Joseph Rowan, Buu Phan, Ashish J. Khisti

entry.summary: The authors propose a scheme for exact and approximate simulation of discrete-to-continuous channels that uses a fixed number of random samples, giving runtime independent of the channel and input. This addresses the high computational cost, random stopping times, and potentially unbounded sample requirements of existing channel simulation methods used in compression and privacy applications.

entry.title: Patient-Reported Survey Data Improve Prediction of Opioid Use Disorder

author.name: Xiyue Jiang, Zihan Ding, Grace Han, Yinan Liu, Richard N. Rosenthal, Fusheng Wang

entry.summary: Using 267,747 All of Us participants with documented opioid exposure (15,287 OUD cases), the study compares EHR-only versus EHR-plus-survey models across 6-, 12-, and 24-month look-back windows with eight model classes. Survey augmentation improved PR-AUC across all 24 model-window combinations, with the best 24-month LightGBM model rising from 0.6219 to 0.6603.

entry.title: Quantifying the Value of Privileged Information Using a PAC-Bayesian Approach

author.name: Vasily Bokov (aQa, Leiden University, The Netherlands, LIACS, Leiden University, Leiden, The Netherlands, Honda Research Institute Europe GmbH, Offenbach, Germany), Sebastian Schmitt (Honda Research Institute Europe GmbH, Offenbach, Germany), Vedran Dunjko (aQa, Leiden University, The Netherlands, LIACS, Leiden University, Leiden, The Netherlands), Hao Wang (aQa, Leiden University, The Netherlands, LIACS, Leiden University, Leiden, The Netherlands)

entry.summary: This work develops a general PAC-Bayesian framework for Learning Using Privileged Information, seeking to explain when and how auxiliary training-only features transfer useful knowledge to a learner. It aims to move beyond the per-algorithm, setting-specific guarantees of Vapnik's original LUPI theory toward a cohesive generalization bound. The result gives a quantitative handle on the value that privileged information adds.

entry.title: GAUGE: When Not to Trust LLM-as-a-Judge in User-Simulated Evaluation of Task-Oriented Agents

author.name: Umesh Bodhwani, Thanh Tran, Kai Wei

entry.summary: GAUGE is an offline protocol that tests whether rankings produced by persona-driven LLM user simulators plus an LLM judge agree with a grounded, verifiable reward, evaluated over 25 agents from six providers on the tau-squared-bench and SimulatorArena benchmarks. It separates ranking validity from construct validity, two notions that release practices often conflate. The study reports a satisfaction-success gap, where conversations rated as satisfied by a blind panel carry essentially no information about actual task success.

entry.title: CueMem: Cue-Guided Context Reconstruction for Long-Term Conversational Memory

author.name: Changjian Wang, Rongzhen Li, Weili Guan, Shuming Shi, Quan Lu, Ning Jiang

entry.summary: CueMem treats extracted memory records as retrieval cues rather than self-contained evidence, linking each fine-grained cue to its source dialogue turns and reconstructing query-relevant context from those turns at query time. The design is motivated by reconstructive theories of autobiographical memory and aims to balance the cost of full-history prompting against the evidence loss of compressed memory.

entry.title: MedSNIP: Building and Benchmarking Snippet-Level Granularity for Medical Fact Verification

author.name: Hasan Iqbal, Sarfraz Ahmad, Hyunjae Kim, Sihyeon Park, Junjie Liao, Qingyu Chen, Preslav Nakov, Yuxia Wang

entry.summary: The authors argue that atom-level claim decomposition fragments clinically necessary context, and reformulate medical fact-checking at the snippet level where clause-grouped units preserve local clinical structure. They contribute MedSNIP-Bench, a human-annotated benchmark of 276 consumer-health and clinical-vignette responses segmented into 2,524 snippets, plus MedSNIP, an automatic snippet-generation pipeline.

entry.title: Continue, Adapt, or Yield: In-Turn Adaptation to Overlapping Speech in Full-Duplex Agents

author.name: Yunqi Lu, Tyler Baumgartner, Nikhil Johri, Brandon Tai, Candice Fan, Luc Debaupte, Ruben Aguilar, Bill Wang, Yi Zhong

entry.summary: The authors argue that full-duplex evaluation collapses to a keep-speaking-or-stop binary that misses a third human behavior: continuing while incorporating the listener's contribution. They introduce Duplex Cue, which separates listener intent (backchannel, collaboration, interruption) from speaker behavior (continue unchanged, adapt in-turn, yield), and run a 300-cue single-model case study on unscripted English conversations.

entry.title: CoralscapesV2: Panoptic and Fine-Grained Visual Scene Understanding in Coral Reefs

author.name: Jonathan Sauder, Thomas Ruckli, Gabriel\.e Strodomskyt\.e, Ibrahim Souleiman Abdallah, Rahma Hassan Abdi, Djama Goumaneh Awaleh, Mohamed Houssein Farah, Moustapha Nour, Osama Sharhubil Saad, Mustafa Mohammed Khalafallah Altaib, Maysoon Kteifan, Farah Alsoqi, Eyad Zgool, Jafar Al-Omari, Temesgen Gebremeskel Gebreluel, Zekaria Zekeria Abdulkerim, Meron Ghirmay, Teklehaimanot Beraki, Devis Tuia, Guilhem Banc-Prandi

entry.summary: CoralscapesV2 extends an existing coral reef dataset toward general-purpose panoptic and fine-grained scene understanding, increasing dataset size, scope, and label completeness for unconstrained reef imagery. The dataset is intended to support ecological monitoring at scale as reef data collection shifts from standardized surveys to opportunistic platforms. It matters because coral conservation depends on automating analysis of far more imagery than experts can annotate.

entry.title: DementiaCare-Bench: A Modality-Validated Video Benchmark

author.name: Afrouz Sheikholeslami, Yuankai Qi, Xuyun Zhang, Luping Zhou, Amin Beheshti, Quan Z. Sheng, Ming-Hsuan Yang

entry.summary: DementiaCare-Bench is a new benchmark built from 56 professionally produced caregiver training videos split into 94 clips across nine behavioral and psychological symptom categories, with over 2000 questions. It targets whether video-language models can reason about what preceded a behavior, since the appropriate caregiver response depends on the trigger. It matters because no prior benchmark evaluated VLM capability for dementia caregiving, and BPSD care is the hardest part of the disease for families.

entry.title: Breaking the Vision-Action Shortcut: Latent Interface Training for Generalizable Robotics Foundation Models

author.name: Jianman Lin, Shailesh Shailesh, Zhongyi Luo, Jiafei Duan

entry.summary: This paper diagnoses vision-action shortcuts, where robot foundation models exploit task-irrelevant visual cues correlated with demonstrated actions in-distribution, and proposes Latent Interface Training (LIT), a two-stage framework-agnostic strategy that first learns a spatial-goal-conditioned action prior without images and then integrates visual information through a constrained latent interface. The goal is improved generalization under visual distribution shift while preserving task-relevant spatial information. It matters because robustness to visual domain shift is a central weakness of current robot foundation models.

entry.title: PDE-constrained inverse problems at the $\sqrt{n}$ rate via debiased physics-informed neural networks

author.name: Yves Atchade, Debarghya Mukherjee

entry.summary: The authors study estimation of unknown finite-dimensional parameters in PDE-constrained inverse problems where the PDE solution is approximated by a physics-informed neural network, noting that existing estimators inherit the slow nonparametric rate of the network solution and thus yield biased, inefficient inference. They propose a two-step debiased estimator combining neural nonparametric estimation with an influence-function-based bias correction that removes first-order sensitivity to nuisance errors. It matters because it gives statistical validity and root-n rates to a technique widely used in scientific machine learning without formal guarantees.

entry.title: Who Pays for Open Review? Visible Author Reputation and Its Effect on Ratings

author.name: Qinghua Zhao, Xinyu Chen, Yanhui Yang, Tengfeng Sun, Junfeng Liu, Zhongfeng Kang

entry.summary: Motivated by a November 2025 OpenReview anonymity bug and subsequent calls for open review, the authors analyse over 18,000 reviewed ICLR 2026 submissions split into de facto open and blind groups by arXiv preprint timing. Ratings rise with author reputation under both mechanisms, with a significantly steeper slope under open review, and the open-versus-blind difference concentrates at borderline ratings. The pattern is robust across five reputation proxies, three aggregation rules, and five definitions of the open window, with a controlled simulation.

entry.title: UFO: Chain-of-Evaluation for Omni-Condition Alignment in Multi-Modal Image Generation

author.name: Danning Zhang, Yijing Lin, Shuhan Zhuang, Mengqi Huang, Shaojin Wu, Shancheng Fang, Zhendong Mao

entry.summary: The paper argues that evaluation of multi-modal, subject-driven image generation lags behind generation quality because existing metrics score each conditioning modality in isolation, contradicting the joint-alignment objective and correlating poorly with human judgment. It proposes UFO, described as the first unified framework for simultaneous omni-condition alignment evaluation, built on an atomized chain-of-evaluation paradigm that decomposes the composite alignment task. The contribution is primarily an evaluation methodology for multi-condition generation.

entry.title: Correlation-Guided Fast Machine Unlearning via Hessian Analysis

author.name: Ayushi Thakur, Ruchir Gupta, Amit Kumar Jaiswal, Prayag Tiwari

entry.summary: Approximate machine unlearning is often too slow for production because each data-removal request requires repeated expensive Hessian-inverse-vector computations. The authors propose a correlation-guided approach that exploits relationships between related deletion requests to speed up unlearning, motivated by security use cases such as intrusion detection, spam filtering, and regulatory right-to-be-forgotten compliance. It matters for making privacy-compliant model updates practical in deployed security systems.

entry.title: SeqMoE: Toward Full-Load Performance via Predictive and Graph-Compatible MoE Offloading

author.name: Zihan Wang, Yuqi Wang, Lei Gong, Cheng Tang, Wenqi Lou, Teng Wang, Chao Wang, Xuehai Zhou

entry.summary: SeqMoE targets Mixture-of-Experts inference on memory-constrained devices by predicting which experts will be activated so they can be prefetched in time, aiming to approach the performance of keeping all weights resident. Its key idea is recasting expert activation prediction as sequence modeling to enable accurate multi-step, multi-layer forecasts for offloading decisions.

entry.title: Explainable Prediction from Mobile Sensing Data through LLM-guided Concept Integration

author.name: Yuning Wang, Iman Azimi, Amir M. Rahmani, Pasi Liljeberg

entry.summary: The authors propose a Concept-Integrated Transformer (CIT) that uses a pretrained LLM to generate baseline-aware concept abnormality targets with confidence weights, avoiding manual concept annotation for small-cohort mobile health sensing studies. The framework aims for interpretable predictions grounded in behavioral and physiological patterns rather than opaque scores.

entry.title: Split Conformal Prediction with Label-Shift-Adjusted Bayesian Scores

author.name: Hyeonsu Lee, Juyeon Kim, Erkhembayar Jadamba, Seungjin Choi, Hyunjin Shin

entry.summary: The paper tackles conformal prediction under label shift, where standard exchangeability-based procedures lose their coverage guarantee. It argues that existing importance-weighting fixes pair reweighting with residual-based scores that ignore predictive uncertainty, yielding uniform-width intervals, and proposes label-shift-adjusted Bayesian nonconformity scores that restore validity while producing adaptive interval widths.

entry.title: Dual-guided Hierarchical Edge Localization for Large-scale Optimal Transport Across Dimensions

author.name: Wenzhou Xia, Qiaoqiao Ding, Jingwei Liang, Xiaoqun Zhang

entry.summary: The authors present HELLO, a hierarchical solver that reframes large-scale discrete optimal transport as edge localization, using dual potentials to drive coarse-to-fine initialization and within-level refinement. It recursively subsamples to assign candidate edges, then inserts the largest dual violators per row and column until the KKT residual meets tolerance, with budgeted pruning giving linear memory complexity. Finite-convergence properties are claimed for exact-arithmetic refinement.

entry.title: One Simple Trick for Improving the Performance of Energy-Limited Local Inference and Training

author.name: Erik Schultheis, Maximilian Kleinegger, Dan Alistarh

entry.summary: This short paper observes that in workloads alternating compute-heavy operations such as matmuls with memory-bound operations such as norms or cross-entropy, the compute-heavy segments can hit power or thermal limits and throttle, especially on small form-factor devices like the DGX Spark. The authors show that chunking workloads into smaller parts and alternating compute and memory access at higher frequency smooths power and temperature spikes. This prevents throttling and yields considerably faster wall-clock results.

entry.title: Diverse Minds, Divided Networks? Personality Composition, Polarization, and Collective Intelligence in LLM-Based Social Simulations

author.name: Raad Bin Tareaf

entry.summary: TraitMix treats the Big Five personality composition of a simulated social network, including trait levels and heterogeneity, as a controlled variable and measures polarization and collective performance in the same runs. Across 991 hundred-agent simulations spanning six contested topics and six language models, the study probes whether reducing polarization trades off against collective competence.

entry.title: VS-Splat: Voxel-Selective feed-forward Gaussian Splatting for end-to-end 3D object reconstruction from sparse-views

author.name: Yunsu Jeong, Hyuk Heo, Youngsang Kwak, Jaehwa Kwak, Il Yong Chun

entry.summary: VS-Splat is a feed-forward Gaussian splatting framework for reconstructing 3D objects from a few images that predicts primitives only inside selected voxels likely to contain the object, rather than spreading them uniformly. A learnable voxel selection module identifies object regions without 3D structural supervision, improving detail fidelity in sparse-view settings.

entry.title: DIA: Denoising Intermediate Advantage for Diffusion Policy Optimization

author.name: Arjun Sohal, Yuchi Zhao, Miroslav Bogdanovic, Alan Aspuru-Guzik

entry.summary: Diffusion-based robot policies are widely trained by behavior cloning but limited by demonstration quality and coverage, so the authors study reinforcement learning fine-tuning through interaction. Observing that existing policy-gradient approaches assign the same environment-level credit to every denoising step in an action chunk, they propose Denoising Intermediate Advantage, which distinguishes which intermediate denoising decisions contributed most to the final return.

entry.title: Drug firms’ secret data supercharge AI protein models

author.name: Unknown

entry.summary: A Nature news item indicating that proprietary pharmaceutical datasets are significantly boosting AI protein models, likely by supplying training data unavailable in the public domain. The coverage date and empty content field mean only the headline signal is available, but it points to the growing role of private data in advancing biological AI.

entry.title: When Successful Knowledge Graph Edits Displace Correct Answers: Rank-Level Locality beyond Parameter Support

author.name: Yi-Cheng Lai, Jerry Wang, Hsin-Ling Hsu, Li-Chu Chi, Ya-Wen Teng, Hen-Hsen Huang

entry.summary: The paper shows that editing a knowledge graph embedding model to promote a target answer can push previously correct answers out of the returned ranking list, an effect missed by locality tests that only inspect facts reusing the edited parameter.
