It introduces a rank-displacement audit at three scopes and derives dimensional and geometric conditions for updates that improve the target while preserving selected scores. On FB15k-237 with DistMult and ComplEx, direct promotion succeeds but causes no collateral damage in only about 23% of edits.

entry.title: Soft Symbol Grounding for Prototypical Concepts

author.name: Marcos Galv\'an-L\'opez, Nijesh Upreti, Hiram Calvo, Carlos Aguilar-Ib\'a\~nez, Vaishak Belle

entry.summary: Soft-PNet reframes concept grounding in neuro-symbolic models as a Metropolis walk over a precomputed cache of feasible symbolic solutions guided by a prototype distribution, eliminating the hand-crafted task-specific differentiable loss used by prior prototypical networks. The goal is to avoid reasoning shortcuts where models predict labels correctly while recovering the wrong intermediate concepts. It matters for interpretable, concept-based neuro-symbolic learning.

entry.title: SCQ: Stabilizing Conservative Q-Learning with Sigmoid-Bounded Entropy

author.name: Xiefeng Wu, Shu Zhang, Zhaojie Chu, Mingyu Hu

entry.summary: SCQ identifies an overlooked instability source in offline-to-online reinforcement learning: the standard log-entropy term can go negative and destabilise policy updates. The method replaces it with a sigmoid-bounded entropy formulation that stays strictly positive while retaining conservative Q regularization and return-based lower-bound calibration. This offers a simple, targeted fix for value-estimation instability in real-world robot learning pipelines.

entry.title: Diffusion Models and Concept Formation

author.name: Zekun Wang, Karthik Singaravadivelan, Christopher J. MacLellan

entry.summary: The authors argue that diffusion models implicitly perform the same computation as Cobweb, a classic incremental cognitive learner that builds a probabilistic concept hierarchy by maximising category utility. They draw a parallel between the Gaussian-smoothed marginals of a diffusion model, whose modes form a hierarchy, and a Cobweb tree of probabilistic prototypes. This is a theory paper linking generative image models to human concept formation and basic-level categorisation.

entry.title: A decision-basis contract for auditable LLM-assisted medical billing verification: deterministic rules, verbatim evidence, and fail-closed abstention

author.name: Jan H\"olter, Kevin Geis, Benjamin Raab, Boris Bauke

entry.summary: This proof of concept proposes a decision-basis contract for LLM-assisted medical billing verification that separates deterministic checks of versioned fee-catalog rules from LLM assessment of free-text documentation. The semantic layer labels each claimed item as supported, contradicted, or missing required information, requiring a verbatim evidence span for support or contradiction, and abstains fail-closed when rule context, assessment, or evidence is unavailable. Four locally run open-weight models were evaluated on a synthetic corpus.

entry.title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Scientific Code Understanding

author.name: Aaron Nobile, Andreas Adelmann, Mohsen Sadr

entry.summary: This paper investigates whether a useful fully local coding agent can be built from small open-source models by moving computation from inference to an offline ingestion stage. The RAG system parses code, constructs structural graphs, generates LLM entity explanations, and builds embeddings offline, while the online answering stage stays lightweight, avoiding the cost and data-privacy implications of large cloud-hosted coding assistants. It is evaluated on a 100-question benchmark for scientific code understanding.

entry.title: Bridging Vision Foundation Model Priors with CLIP for Spatial-aware Few-shot Anomaly Detection in Medical Images

author.name: Juzheng Miao, Yuchen Yuan, Cheng Chen, Pheng-Ann Heng

entry.summary: The paper observes that CLIP-based few-shot medical anomaly detection localizes lesions poorly because globally contrastive pretraining lacks explicit spatial supervision, while vision foundation models such as DINO learn spatially coherent patch representations through self-distillation and local-to-global consistency. It proposes Spatial-FAD, which injects a structural affinity prior from a VFM into CLIP via an adapter to improve lesion localization. The work combines complementary strengths of two foundation-model families for few-shot medical AD.

entry.title: Cognition on Graph: Navigating Massive Knowledge Space via Cognitive Cycles and Bidirectional Graph-Text Synergy

author.name: Gengxian Zhou, Jian Xu, Zichen Tang, Shiming Xiang, Haihong E, Cheng-Lin Liu

entry.summary: CoG is a training-free framework for retrieval-augmented generation over large heterogeneous knowledge bases combining knowledge graphs and text. It replaces reactive, topology-driven exploration with cognitive plan-explore-reflection cycles and deep bidirectional graph-text synergy. This matters because complex reasoning over global, structured knowledge remains a weak point of current RAG systems.

entry.title: MP-Bench: Evaluating Voice Agents as a Multiparty Conversation Participant

author.name: Yi-Jen Shih, Shih-Yun Shan Kuan, Guan-Ting Lin, Kai-Wei Chang, Siddhant Arora, Shu-wen Yang, Abdelrahman Mohamed, Shinji Watanabe, Hung-yi Lee, David Harwath

entry.summary: MP-Bench targets a gap in voice agent evaluation: existing benchmarks cover dyadic interaction and passive audio comprehension but not multi-party conversations, which are more complex due to open turn-taking and group dynamics. The benchmark tests whether agents produce contextually appropriate responses and navigate turn-taking in multi-speaker settings.

entry.title: FINESSE: An Agent-Based Simulator and Benchmark Dataset for Multimodal Financial Event Sequences

author.name: Tyler Farnan, Benjamin Eng, Adam Abate, Xirui Hou, Rizal Fathony, Nam H. Nguyen, Senthil Kumar

entry.summary: FINESSE is an agent-based simulation framework that generates synthetic, structured datasets of multiple interdependent financial event streams, such as transactions, payments, account status changes, and policy interventions, each with distinct schemas and action spaces. It targets the scarcity of representative open financial datasets that capture multimodal, dynamic structure, providing a benchmark environment for financial ML research.

entry.title: Quality-Constrained Routing over a Fixed Pool of Quantized Mixture-of-Experts Instances

author.name: Zhenghong Huang, Hongfan Wu, Jiheng Zhang

entry.summary: This paper studies request routing within a fixed resident pool of quantized mixture-of-experts model instances, treating instance materialization and replica counts as upstream provisioning decisions. It routes each request to maximize modeled throughput subject to a class-level expected quality-degradation budget, using Fragility-Weighted Perplexity computed from prompt tokens to predict request-specific quantization risk.

entry.title: Convergence of Stochastic Gradient Methods under Heavy-Tailed Noise and H\"{o}lder Smoothness

author.name: Misbah Uz Zaman, Anirbit Mukherjee

entry.summary: This paper relaxes two standard assumptions in stochastic optimization simultaneously, replacing Lipschitz smoothness with Holder-continuous gradients and finite-variance noise with a bounded alpha-th moment condition, with alpha between one and two. It proves SGD converges at rate T to the minus s over one plus s when alpha is at least one plus s, and analyzes regularized gradient clipping under the same relaxed regime.

entry.title: Beyond Argmax: A Mechanistic Study of Semantic Retention in Frozen Foundation-Model Composition for Generalized Few-Shot 3D Segmentation

author.name: Silas Kwabla Gah, Ebenezer Owusu

entry.summary: Motivated by the classical distinction between score-level fusion and hard decision-level voting, this paper asks how much semantic information is lost when heterogeneous frozen foundation models are collapsed to a single class before interacting. A same-input top-k retention ladder on 156 held-out ScanNet200 scenes varies only the number of semantic alternatives kept before interaction, with all weights, masks, and fusion rules frozen.

entry.title: Recurrent Dynamic Range Extension

author.name: Sebastian Dille, Keru Fu, S. Mahdi H. Miangoleh, Ya\u{g}{\i}z Aksoy

entry.summary: This paper reformulates HDR reconstruction as progressive dynamic range extension, learning to extend an input image by a single exposure value and then applying the network recurrently to reach the full high dynamic range of the scene. Because the formulation targets a bounded output domain, the authors can train on widely available RAW images and adapt adversarial losses for realism, using memory replay for recurrent backpropagation. It matters as a simpler, more data-efficient alternative to direct full-range HDR reconstruction.

entry.title: Pneumatic neurons for soft robots enable inflate-and-fire networks for rhythmic motion

author.name: Dongting Li, Michael Tolley, Nick Gravish

entry.summary: Inspired by leaky integrate-and-fire models of biological neural circuits, the authors introduce a pneumatic neuron (Pneu-ron), a soft actuator that unifies energy conversion, logic, and actuation in a single self-excitable module combining a low-boiling-point fluid, a heater, and a mechanical switch. Boiling the fluid inflates the module and triggers switching, allowing networks of these components to produce rhythmic motion without centralized electronics.

entry.title: DATAFARM: Distribution-Aligned Task and Motion Planning for Fine-Tuning Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Samrat Sahoo, Yixuan Huang, Tom Silver

entry.summary: The paper observes that raw task-and-motion-planning demonstrations, despite solving target tasks, provide surprisingly little benefit when fine-tuning pretrained vision-language-action models. The authors attribute this to a behavioral distribution mismatch between planner trajectories and pretraining data, and introduce DATAFARM, which incorporates the pretraining distribution directly when generating TAMP data for fine-tuning robot foundation models.

entry.title: Size Doesn't Matter: Material-State Reinforcement Learning for Excavator Transferable Soil Manipulation

author.name: Lennart Werner, Pol Eyschen, Sean Costello, Pierluigi Micarelli, Andrei Cramariuc, Marco Hutter

entry.summary: The authors learn excavation and soil-manipulation controllers with reinforcement learning inside a GPU-parallelized Material Point Method particle simulation, conditioning policies on material state such as shape and compactness so the tool can use multiple contact faces and move material both inside and outside the shovel. Policies operate in a normalized formulation so the same learned weights transfer across machine sizes. It matters because earthmoving autonomy has lagged behind heuristic-only approaches that ignore soil mechanics.

entry.title: DU-NO: A Parameter-Efficient Double U-Shaped Neural Operator for Phase-Resolving Wave Modeling

author.name: Enrique Hernandez Noguera, Md Meftahul Ferdaus, Nathan Cooper, Elias Ioup, Mahdi Abdelguerfi

entry.summary: DU-NO is a multiscale, double U-shaped spectral neural operator that attaches lightweight convolutional U-Net branches to approximate expensive phase-resolving wave models like FUNWAVE-TVD. It targets the accuracy of solver-level simulation at a fraction of the parameter count of hybrid spectral-convolutional baselines such as U-FNO. This matters for operational forecasting, uncertainty quantification and real-time coastal warning where full solvers are too costly.

entry.title: Learning Symbolic Constraint Representations from Examples: A Neuro-Symbolic Approach

author.name: Nassim Belmecheri, Arnaud Gotlieb, Nadjib Lazaar, Helge Spieker

entry.summary: This paper proposes a neuro-symbolic framework for constraint acquisition that replaces costly human-oracle interaction with neural Oracle Transformer models trained to emulate user responses and generalize conceptual knowledge. The learned oracle interacts with the FastCA constraint acquisition engine to refine responses into a sound, consistent and interpretable constraint network. It matters for reducing the query burden in learning user-defined concepts as constraint networks.

entry.title: LoRA-RC: Reservoir Computing with Low-Rank Adaptation

author.name: Wenbin Wan

entry.summary: LoRA-RC adapts a reservoir computing recurrent matrix through a low-rank correction driven by streaming prediction errors, with fixed base reservoir and adaptation bases and online adaptation of only a small core matrix. The update is projected onto a spectral-norm ball and low-pass filtered each step, which preserves echo-state and incremental stability properties. It matters for online prediction under system drift where readout-only adaptation fails but unconstrained adaptation destroys reservoir guarantees.

entry.title: What Drives Recovery in Agentic Text-to-Cypher? LAST-CQ: An LLM Agent Self-Refinement Framework

author.name: Ioannis Prokopiou, Athanasios Aidinis, Panagiotis-Christos Kyrmpatsos, Pantelis Vikatos

entry.summary: This paper uses the LAST-CQ five-agent, training-free Text-to-Cypher pipeline as an instrumented testbed to isolate which part of an agentic loop actually produces gains. Running counterfactual ablations over 2,471 live-database queries and six backbone models, the authors find that removing the correction step is the single largest contributor, and that replacing schema-grounded LLM-synthesised feedback with raw database error strings costs almost nothing end-to-end. It matters because it turns vague claims about agentic self-refinement into measured attribution of where the benefit lives.

entry.title: Autonomous Research for Open-Ended Problems: A Case Study on Telecom Ticket Retrieval

author.name: Junghyun Min, Huseyin Uzunalioglu, Mohamed Trabelsi

entry.summary: The authors examine whether fully autonomous LLM-driven ML research can handle open-ended, industry-grade problems rather than narrow search spaces like language modelling or biomedical benchmarks. They use telecom ticket retrieval as a case study, a task with freedom in representation, architecture, and training-data generation. The paper reports where autonomous research succeeds and where it degrades on this more open-ended industrial problem.

entry.title: Robust Trust

author.name: Piotr Dworczak, Alex Smolin

entry.summary: This theory paper studies an agent who acts on private information plus a recommendation from an informed but potentially misaligned adviser who is truthful with known probability and otherwise free to send any message. The authors characterise optimal robust decision rules maximising the agent's worst-case payoff, showing every optimum is equivalent to a trust-region policy in belief space where reports inside the region are taken at face value and outside ones are clipped to the boundary. They derive alignment thresholds above which advice is strictly valuable and fully solve binary-state and binary-action cases.

entry.title: Explanations-Driven Active Feature Acquisition for Algorithmic Recourse

author.name: Vinura Galwaduge, Jagath Samarabandu

entry.summary: This work joins algorithmic recourse with active feature acquisition, arguing that prior acquisition methods are explanation-agnostic and provide explanations only after features are bought. It uses Markov Blanket theory to unify counterfactual, semifactual, and alterfactual explanations and to characterize how available recourse grows as features are acquired, then builds an acquisition strategy on that framework. The setting reflects real decision systems that operate with partial, costly information.

entry.title: QuPAINT: Physics-Aware Multimodal Reasoning for Quantum Material Characterization

author.name: Sankalp Pandey, Xuan-Bac Nguyen, Hoang-Quan Nguyen, Tim Faltermeier, Nicholas Borys, Hugh Churchill, Khoa Luu

entry.summary: QuPAINT is a physics-aware multimodal framework for identifying and measuring exfoliated two-dimensional quantum material flakes from optical microscopy, a task requiring interpretation of subtle optical contrast and interference color. To handle synthetic-to-real domain shift and variation across materials, substrates, laboratories, and imaging conditions, the authors introduce the Synthia synthetic materials framework and build QMat-Instruct, a multimodal instruction dataset with image-specific reasoning traces. The goal is transferable flake characterization for device fabrication.

entry.title: ESTS at WMT26: Routing-Informed Expert Pruning for Model Compression

author.name: Liu O. Martin, Lucas Bandarkar, Nanyun Peng

entry.summary: This system description covers six submissions to the WMT26 Model Compression shared task for English-Chinese and English-Arabic translation, all derived from the open GPT-OSS-20B mixture-of-experts model. The authors rank experts using task-specific routing mass and cross-lingual routing divergence to decide how much capacity to keep per layer, physically prune low-importance experts, recovery-tune on synthetic translation data generated by GPT-5.1, and apply MXFP4 quantization to retained expert weights. It is a concrete recipe for MoE compression specialized to translation.

entry.title: Linear Exponential Quadratic Gaussian Covariance Steering

author.name: Chiran B. Cherian, Yasemin Isik, Abhishek Halder

entry.summary: The paper formulates and analyzes the linear exponential quadratic Gaussian covariance steering problem in continuous time over a finite horizon, interpretable as a risk-sensitive Schrodinger bridge between Gaussian endpoints in the linear-quadratic setting. Unlike the risk-neutral case, the optimal controller remains linear state feedback but no longer admits a closed form, instead being parameterized by a symmetric matrix solving an algebraic equation tied to the risk-sensitivity parameter. The result generalizes existing risk-neutral covariance steering theory.

entry.title: SIMS: Scale-Invariant Merit-Function-Based Scalarization for Multi-Task Learning

author.name: Zebin Chen, Fei Xing, Yang Chen, Hua Liu, Andy HF Chow, Yuhua Qian, Yu Zhang

entry.summary: The authors observe that merit-function scalarization for multi-objective multi-task learning is sensitive to the relative magnitudes of task losses, so optimization favors large-scale objectives even though Pareto-optimal solutions are invariant to positive rescaling. SIMS introduces a scale-invariant formulation to fix this pathology. It matters for making multi-task training and Pareto-front approximation stable when task losses differ by orders of magnitude.

entry.title: Behavior Quotient Learning for Low-Rank Adaptation of LLM Agents

author.name: Pengyang Zhou, Xiaobin Tu, Zhengxi Liu, Rongkun Xue, Haochen Li, Miancan Liu, Ziyuan Chen, Yinggui Wang, Jinkui Ren, Xiantao Zhang

entry.summary: Agent capabilities are often split across many LoRA adapters, which increases storage and adds routing overhead at inference. This work learns a single adapter under a fixed rank budget, addressing two issues: diverse trajectories causing equivalent decision-distribution changes that yield redundant updates, and aggregated updates exceeding the rank budget in ways that distort decisions when approximated in weight space. The behavioral-quotient framing matters for compact, single-adapter agent specialization.

entry.title: $\text{GSF-}\chi$: Global Stereochemical Fields for Chiral Graph Transformers

author.name: Jiaqing Xie, Yuxin Wang, Xipeng Qiu

entry.summary: GSF-chi is a graph transformer for molecular data in which stereogenic units modulate all pairwise interactions rather than designating a single special atom. Central and axial stereogenic units create reflection-even phase fields over all atoms, a handedness pseudoscalar sets the direction of a relative rotation on latent query-key blocks (a Chiral-RoPE), and a C2 projection separates mirror-even from mirror-odd spectral signatures.

entry.title: A Full Adam Theorem for Spectral Heavy-Tail Onset

author.name: Zongmin Liu

entry.summary: This paper proves a rigorous theorem characterizing spectral heavy-tail onset under full-batch Adam training within a closed Gaussian Stein-Hermite teacher-student state-evolution model. It starts from the actual Adam update recurrences, derives population gradients via Stein-Hermite calculus, proves finite-width covariance concentration, and converts Adam momentum into an exact Gaussian sign kernel, ultimately yielding matching upper and lower hitting bounds. The final scaling law is Theta of the inverse first spectral gap raised to an exponent.

entry.title: Transfer Learning for Evolving Domains

author.name: Ricardo Ribeiro Pereira, Jacopo Bono, Hugo Ferreira, Pedro Ribeiro, Pedro Saleiro, Pedro Bizarro, Carlos Soares

entry.summary: This position-style paper argues that classic transfer learning subfields (domain generalization, domain adaptation, multi-domain learning) each capture only a snapshot of a trajectory that deployed systems actually traverse as data and labels from a new domain accumulate over time. It proposes framing transfer learning for evolving domains as a unified problem where target data availability is dynamic rather than fixed. The authors come from a research group with applied ML deployment experience.

entry.title: R2VC: Modular Fact-Checking with Retrieval, Verification, and Confidence Calibration

author.name: Dhruv Dixit, Paritosh Pandey

entry.summary: The paper presents R2VC, a modular fact-checking pipeline that separates evidence retrieval, structured verdict generation, verification, and confidence calibration instead of entangling them in one end-to-end prompt. It combines hybrid sparse-plus-dense retrieval over Wikipedia, a supervised fine-tuned and DPO-aligned generator, an external NLI cross-encoder for candidate selection, and a lightweight sequence-level calibrator that supports selective abstention. The work matters because modularity makes failures diagnosable and reported confidence more trustworthy in automated fact-checking.

entry.title: GraphProfiler: Source-Linked Sensitive Attribute Inference via Personal Knowledge Graphs

author.name: Ahmed Sohair Khan, Estrid He, Chenglong Ma, Monica Wachowicz, Elham Naghizade

entry.summary: GraphProfiler is an auditable LLM-based profiler that represents a user's post history as a source-linked personal knowledge graph, enabling inference of sensitive attributes such as age, income, and occupation while exposing which posts and relationships drove each inference. This auditability supports targeted mitigation, redacting only the few posts that actually leak an attribute instead of perturbing entire histories.

entry.title: Parameter-Efficient Retrievers for Polish and European Languages

author.name: S{\l}awomir Dadas, Rafa{\l} Po\'swiata, Ma{\l}gorzata Gr\k{e}bowiec, Micha{\l} Pere{\l}kiewicz

entry.summary: This work presents a three-stage training pipeline (cross-lingual alignment, relational knowledge distillation, contrastive fine-tuning) for compact dense retrievers that stay competitive with much larger embedding models without any ground-truth relevance labels. The resulting PolDense and EuroDense models handle contexts up to 8,192 tokens and target Polish and broader European language retrieval.

entry.title: Single-Query Person-Centric Bimanual Hand-Object Interaction Detection

author.name: Jonghyun Kim, Junho Roh, Yubin Yoon, Hyotae Lee, Jongkuk Park, Taehwan Hwang, Jaechul Kim, Jungho Lee

entry.summary: The authors propose a person-centric formulation for bimanual hand-object interaction detection in which one query predicts a structured output for an entire person: body box, pose, hand boxes and states, and interaction targets. Part-aware deformable attention allocates attention across human, hand, and pose reference regions, resolving the hand-ownership ambiguity of hand-centric methods in multi-person scenes.

entry.title: Self-supervised Pre-training Helps Retinal Disease Progression Modelling Most When Data Is Scarce

author.name: Ifeoma Veronica Nwabufo, Julius Gervelmeyer, Sarah M\"uller, Philipp Berens

entry.summary: This study examines which self-supervised pre-training strategy best supports longitudinal disease progression modeling for age-related macular degeneration. Encoders are pre-trained on the large cross-sectional NAKO cohort and evaluated on time-to-late-AMD prediction using the longitudinal AREDS dataset, comparing in-house encoders against general-purpose DINOv2 and domain-specific RETFound foundation models. It matters because longitudinal cohorts are scarce, and the work quantifies when pre-training transfers most.

entry.title: RodForesight: A World Model Enhanced Diffusion Policy for Slender and Material Agnostic Rod Insertion

author.name: Chuanbo Yu, Mingyu Yue, Yan Lyu, Chuhan Song, Peng Wang

entry.summary: RodForesight tackles slender rod insertion in precision manufacturing, where high aspect-ratio parts bend during manipulation so the tip pose is not fixed relative to the gripper, invalidating standard peg-in-hole assumptions. The framework factorizes the task into a coarse visual-servoing approach stage that funnels diverse initial configurations into a compact hand-off region, followed by a predictive insertion stage that uses a world model and diffusion policy for fine alignment.

entry.title: WinSyn: An Automated Pipeline for Realistic Enterprise Question-Answering Evaluation

author.name: Amey Varhade, Ananya Sutradhar, Ravishankar Krishnaswamy, Navin Goyal

entry.summary: WinSyn is an automated pipeline that generates synthetic workplace email datasets with realistic scenarios, plus long- and short-form questions and gold answers, to evaluate enterprise QA agents using RAG and deep research techniques. It targets the complexity of enterprise data, where information is spread across evolving and conflicting emails, chats and documents. The work matters because existing benchmarks lack that complexity and rely on unnatural queries and short answers.

entry.title: Affective Agent: On-Device Personalized Intervention Reasoning for Wearable Systems

author.name: Reina Mun, Zishen Wan, Vijay Janapa Reddi

entry.summary: Affective Agent is a three-layer reference architecture (perception, personalization, reasoning) for deciding whether, when and how to intervene under uncertainty on wearable-class hardware, using a compact sub-billion-parameter language model combined with physiological evidence, context and user history. Personalization is achieved through host-managed structured memory evolution rather than per-user weight updates, and no cloud dependency is required. It matters for on-device affective computing and timely mental-health or wellbeing interventions.

entry.title: From Collaboration to Capability: Internalizing Routed LLM Experts into Compact Reasoners

author.name: Frank Nie, Shuyao Wang, Ethan B. Liu

entry.summary: The paper asks whether a compact controller that routes to stronger experts can absorb their reasoning and code so it still performs well after the experts are removed. Rivet combines expert-augmented reinforcement learning, which applies a shared outcome signal to controller decisions and returned expert spans, with verified trajectory internalization via format-aware supervised training. The deployed controller generates reasoning and code with local Python execution and no external LLM.

entry.title: Implicit Personality Representations in Humans and LLMs

author.name: Yilin Geng, Omri Abend, Eduard Hovy, Lea Frermann

entry.summary: The authors compare the relational structure of trait words in human implicit personality judgments, built from millions of crowd-sourced ratings of fictional characters, against the internal trait geometry of Qwen 2.5-7B-Instruct derived from contrastive activations. The two structures align strongly (Mantel r = 0.77), with agreement holding both trait by trait and in aggregate, and two dominant axes emerging in the model's trait representation. It is an interpretability result connecting LLM internal geometry to a century of personality psychology.

entry.title: When Agent Metrics Measure Different Things: An Evidence-Grounded Audit of the Praxa AI Pipeline

author.name: Stefan G. Creadore, Peyton Woakz

entry.summary: This is a retrospective measurement audit of an agent evaluation pipeline, showing how metrics can be numerically valid yet measure a different construct than their labels imply. It documents a routing report with 112 passes and 27 failures but zero gating failures because known gaps are exempted, and 8,843 tool-attempt rows where many durations are clamped to the signed 32-bit maximum, inflating reported percentiles. The paper is a concrete case study in construct validity and instrumentation artifacts in agent evaluation.

entry.title: Neural Multichannel Distant Speaker Diarization with Heavy-tailed Source Separation Model

author.name: Sicheng Mao, Baihan Li, Mathieu Fontaine, Anthony Larcher, Roland Badeau

entry.summary: This paper generalizes neural FCASA, a model that jointly learns blind source separation and diarization over speech mixtures, by replacing the Gaussian variance model used in source separation with two families of heavy-tailed distributions, the leptokurtic generalized Gaussian and Student's t. The motivation is that speech signals exhibit heavy-tailed statistics that Gaussian assumptions capture poorly, particularly in distant, multichannel, overlapping-speaker conditions. The approach exploits multichannel speech source features to improve diarization.

entry.title: Predicting Collision Cross Sections with GRACE: Geometric Residual Adduct Conditioning via Early-fusion

author.name: Parthasarathy Suryanarayanan, Susanta Das, Shreyans Sethi, Kenneth M. Merz, Jr., Joseph A. Morrone

entry.summary: GRACE is a 3D collision cross section predictor that adapts a pretrained molecular geometry encoder using geometric residual adduct conditioning through early fusion. The authors argue most predictors ignore explicit 3D structure or treat adduct identity as a late categorical feature, limiting capture of adduct-dependent geometric effects, since collision cross sections reflect size, shape, and ionization state of gas-phase ions. GRACE combines a residual objective relative to an adduct-aware physics baseline with an early-fusion conditioning scheme.

entry.title: Learning to adapt GR(1) specifications through degradation

author.name: Tiberiu-Andrei Georgescu, Dalal Alrajeh, Sebastian Uchitel

entry.summary: This work addresses the limitation of reactive-synthesis controllers built from GR(1) assume-guarantee specifications: when the environment violates unspecified assumptions, the synthesized system guarantees no longer hold. The authors propose an oracle-guided inductive synthesis approach that adapts the specification to be consistent with the observed assumption violation while degrading system guarantees as little as possible to preserve realisability. The method discovers multiple candidate adaptations using oracle-guided search.

entry.title: ORQA: An Occupation-Realistic Question and Answer Framework for LLM Professional Knowledge

author.name: Shreyas Krishnan, Serina Chang, Abhishek Nagaraj

entry.summary: ORQA is a method for evaluating occupation-level knowledge in LLMs by linking O*NET occupations to trusted occupation-specific sources, such as regulators, licensing bodies, professional organizations and government publications, and converting them into source-traceable question-answer pairs. A hybrid automated pipeline plus human review yields high-quality questions spanning 116 occupations across all 21 SOC major groups. It offers a more grounded alternative to mapping abstract skills onto jobs or relying on scarce expert annotation.

entry.title: Clustering-Based Balanced Sampling and Allocation with Data Parallelism for High-Performance Fine-Tuning

author.name: Hyunjin Kim, Youngeun Nam, Jaemin Han, Wonhyeok Choi, Jae-Gil Lee

entry.summary: Instruction-tuning corpora are large, redundant, and imbalanced, so naive large-batch fine-tuning over repeats overrepresented groups while under-covering informative rare ones, especially under multi-GPU data parallelism. The authors introduce CluSTER, which curates a representative reduced dataset via gradient-space clustering plus DP-aware balanced allocation, preserving the original distribution through weighted updates. It matters for lowering compute cost of LLM fine-tuning while keeping coverage across clusters and workers.

entry.title: Direct Preference Density Alignment for Conversational Audio Equalization

author.name: Ioannis Stylianou, Sven Ewan Shepstone, Jon Francombe, Pablo Martinez Nuevo, Zheng-Hua Tan

entry.summary: The paper proposes a preference-alignment framework for conversational audio equalization that avoids a learned proxy reward model while retaining online exploration, since offline DPO-style methods can suffer format collapse in bounded continuous spaces. It leverages roughly 90,000 user preference samples to construct a direct preference density objective. This matters for applying alignment techniques outside text, in real-time audio processing settings where reward proxies are unstable or memory-heavy.

entry.title: Explaining Time Series Forecasting with Horizon-Resolved Attribution

author.name: Seunghan Lee, Jun Seo, Jaehoon Lee, Junhyeok Kang, Sangjun Han, Sungdong Yoo, Minjae Kim, Tae Yoon Lim, Dongwan Kang, Hwanil Choi, Soonyoung Lee, Wonbin Ahn

entry.summary: Existing time-series explanation methods return a single importance vector, implicitly assuming every forecast step depends on the same past values, which the authors show is false. They propose Horizon-Resolved eXplanation (HRX), a plug-in framework that adds a horizon axis so each predicted step gets its own importance map, using an estimator that works with any differentiable forecaster without altering the backbone. This matters for diagnosing and trusting multi-step forecasting models used in planning and operations.

entry.title: Dynin-Robotics: Omnimodal Unified Diffusion Vision-Language-Action Model

author.name: Hoeun Lee, Jaeik Kim, Jusang Oh, Jinhyeok Kim, Geon Choi, Hyeonggeun Kim, Jaeyoung Do

entry.summary: Dynin-Robotics builds a vision-language-action model on Dynin-Omni, an omnimodal masked-diffusion backbone that represents language, visual observations, goals, and actions as discrete tokens. By varying conditioning and target spans, one model learns action prediction, action-conditioned next-observation prediction, terminal goal prediction, and trajectory-to-instruction reconstruction, enabling test-time scaling via goal prediction and action-candidate evaluation.

entry.title: Physics-Informed Conformal Prediction: Embedding PDE Consistency into Distribution-Free Uncertainty Quantification for Neural Operators

author.name: Michael Chin

entry.summary: PI-CP embeds PDE residuals into the nonconformity score of split conformal prediction for neural operators like the Fourier Neural Operator, yielding prediction intervals with distribution-free coverage guarantees that adapt spatially, tightening where physics is satisfied and widening where it is violated. It also proves that FNO translation equivariance creates a fundamental approximation barrier for certain PDE settings.

entry.title: On-Device Language Models for Privacy-Preserving Stress Prediction: A Multimodal Evaluation on Mobile Health

author.name: Ibukunoluwa Soyebo, Alyssa Donawa, Rodrigo Aguilar Barrios, Brice Patchou, Corey E. Baker

entry.summary: This paper evaluates on-device language models (ODLMs) for multimodal stress prediction using zero-shot prompting, comparing objective sensor features against subjective self-reports while measuring latency and throughput under mobile resource constraints. It finds that sensor features marginally outperform self-reports and that sub-2B models offer low latency with predictable resource use, highlighting both feasibility and practical limits of on-device mental health inference.

entry.title: Adaptive Chemotherapy Control under Tumor Heterogeneity via Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Bereket Sitotaw Kidane, Md Samiul Haque Motayed, Shuo Wang

entry.summary: The paper develops and compares closed-loop deep RL dosing policies with continuous (TD3) and discrete (DQN) action spaces trained on a high-dimensional heterogeneous tumor model, benchmarking against an open-loop Pontryagin Maximum Principle solution. Generalization is assessed on a 100-patient virtual cohort with plus or minus 10 percent perturbations in growth and drug-sensitivity parameters, with TD3 achieving better average tumor outcomes.

entry.title: Theoretical Guarantees for One-Shot Magnitude Pruning and Compute-Adaptive Early Exit

author.name: Erdem Koyuncu

entry.summary: This paper develops a unified theoretical treatment of compute reduction via one-shot magnitude pruning (static regime) and early exit (adaptive regime). Under an asymptotic single-neuron model it proves a concentration theorem for pruning with explicit rates, introduces a conditional perceptron for early exit whose excess generalization error decays as a power of the compute gap, and extends the analysis to deep networks by characterizing how pruning distortion accumulates with depth.

entry.title: Physical-State-Guided Diffusion Sampling for Full-Waveform Inversion

author.name: Chen Min, Haowen Jiang, Zheng Ma, Xiongbin Yan

entry.summary: The paper introduces Physical-State-Guided Diffusion Sampling (PSG), a method for seismic full-waveform inversion that couples a persistent physical velocity state to a learned diffusion prior through a Gaussian bridge. Waveform fitting regularizes the physical state, which in turn guides the reverse diffusion process, separating the wave-equation gradients from denoiser gradients. This targets the ill-posedness and initialization sensitivity that plague conventional FWI.

entry.title: Evidence-Aligned Local Composition of Discrete Experts for Sequence Restoration

author.name: Mohammad Panahazari, Usman A. Khan, Shuchin Aeron

entry.summary: The paper treats documents as compositions of text from different domains, such as prose, code, and configuration, and asks how to restore a corrupted document when only frozen domain experts are available. The authors introduce evidence-aligned local composition, which infers position-wise soft weights over experts from the marginal evidence of the corrupted observation under a corruption model, estimating evidence from the experts own denoising losses and smoothing weights across positions. This avoids needing region labels or a trained router at test time.

entry.title: Physics-enriched neural solvers for transient ice-flow simulation

author.name: Thomas Gregov, Sebastian Rosier, Brandon Finley, Andreas Vieli, Guillaume Jouvet

entry.summary: This work improves an online neural solver for transient glacier ice-flow simulation by feeding the network inexpensive input fields derived from low-order ice-flow balances instead of adding physics penalties to the loss. The approach leaves the governing energy objective untouched and adds physical structure purely through network inputs, tested across three real-world glaciers.

entry.title: Local Edits, Global Ripples: Replay-Informed Policy Adaptation for Workflow Synthesis

author.name: Manqing Mao, Hong Wang, Samson Koelle, Jie Yuan, Zhuoer Wang, James Feng, Yanjun Lin, Daniel Edmiston, Nikki Lijing Kuang, Zhecheng Sheng, Wei Niu

entry.summary: The paper studies persistent prompt-policy editing for agents that synthesize executable workflows, observing that edit locality does not imply effect locality and that composed edits can interfere destructively. It frames adaptation as two decisions, where to change the policy from execution feedback and whether a resulting edit remains safe to persist, and proposes a replay-informed approach for both.

entry.title: I Am No One: Style-Aware Paraphrasing for Text Anonymization

author.name: Ahmed Sohair Khan, Estrid He, Monica Wachowicz, Elham Naghizade

entry.summary: The authors address authorship re-identification, in which stable stylistic fingerprints let models link users to supposedly anonymized text, including speech-derived transcripts. They propose a prompt-driven anonymization method that builds compact stylistic profiles from small samples and uses a pretrained LLM to rewrite text to suppress identifiable style markers while preserving meaning and utility.

entry.title: Zipbench: Low-Cost Framework for Compressing Comprehensive Benchmarks of Large Language Models

author.name: Zhongzhan Huang, Junxin Li, Guoming Ling, Yupei Lin, Shanshan Zhong, Hefeng Wu

entry.summary: ZipBench is a benchmark compression method that avoids the expensive requirement of per-sample evaluation results from many LLMs, which prior compression approaches depend on. It evaluates only a small set of anchor models, synthesizes pseudo evaluation results, and comes with theoretical guarantees on error and rank consistency, making compression feasible for newly released benchmarks.

entry.title: SWARM: A Multilingual Human-Annotated Dataset for Russian Propaganda Detection in Search Engine Results

author.name: Manuel Tonneau, Abhinav Dubey, Farhan Shaikh, Ilaria Vitulano, Martha Stolze, Hale Dedeoglu, Clara Riechert, Ella Kuka, Maryna Sydorova, Mykola Makhortykh, Elizaveta Kuznetsova

entry.summary: SWARM is a dataset of 2,183 search engine results across nine languages and diverse web domains, with each document human-annotated for whether it supports a recurring Russian propaganda narrative. Benchmarking shows a source-based blocklist misses most propaganda-supporting documents because such content is not confined to flagged sites, and it compares supervised classifiers and zero-shot LLMs against the labels.

entry.title: Feature Recovery for Object Understanding After Irreversible Fire Damage

author.name: Aditi Tiwari, Sofia Stoica, Savya Khosla, David Forsyth, Heng Ji

entry.summary: The paper introduces TRACE, a transformation-aware benchmark for post-fire object understanding containing 21.4K real-image-grounded synthetic scenes with paired pristine-to-degraded object progressions across 499 identities. Five tasks target localization and pre-degradation understanding, addressing degradations that alter physical structure rather than merely adding image corruption.

entry.title: A Dual Cross-Attention Framework for Colposcopic CIN Grading and Swede Score Prediction Using a New Multi-Center Dataset

author.name: Dania Khan, Nuzhat Aisha Shaikh, Asfina Hassan Juicy, Raiyun Kabir, S M Shahida, Taufiq Hasan

entry.summary: This work presents a dual-stream cross-attention architecture that fuses paired cervigrams to grade cervical intraepithelial neoplasia and predict clinical Swede scores. The authors also release a new multi-center colposcopy dataset from BUET, designed to reduce reliance on scarce specialist interpretation in low- and middle-income settings. It matters because cervical cancer screening quality depends heavily on subjective colposcopic assessment.

entry.title: Pre-Trained Low-Rank Tensor Decomposition for Multi-Dimensional Image Recovery

author.name: Bing-Zhang Fu, Zhi-Long Han, Ting-Zhu Huang, Xi-Le Zhao, Deyu Meng

entry.summary: This paper proposes PLTD, described as the first pre-trained low-rank tensor decomposition framework that integrates a pre-trained large vision model into classical tensor decomposition. The goal is to capture structure shared across images rather than learning instance-specific decompositions from scratch, improving recovery fidelity while reducing learnable parameters and compute. It matters for multi-dimensional image recovery tasks such as denoising, inpainting, and completion.

entry.title: Adaptive AI: Energy Efficient Multi-exit TinyML on Intelligent Vision Systems at the Edge

author.name: Luca Crupi, Lorenzo Lamberti, Alessandro Giusti, Daniele Palossi

entry.summary: This work designs and deploys a multi-exit neural network on an ultra-low-power GWT GAP9 system-on-chip, so computation adapts to input difficulty instead of always running a fixed-depth model. Multi-exit execution is common on GPUs but rarely exploited on microcontroller-class edge devices with strict memory and compute limits. It matters for battery-powered IoT vision, where constant MAC counts waste energy and limit real-time responsiveness.

entry.title: AnchorVLN: Geometry-Anchored Vision-Language Grounding Reasoning for Open-Vocabulary Navigation

author.name: Long Giang Vu, Chengkai Yao, Yuxin Liu, FNU Aryan, Rajath Chandrashekar Aralikatti

entry.summary: AnchorVLN is an open-vocabulary vision-language navigation system that anchors metric quantities such as range, bearing, and comparative spatial relations in geometry rather than asking a VLM to emit them directly from images. This avoids hand-engineered geometric pipelines and waypoint-output requirements that force control-stack changes per robot, task, or vocabulary. It matters for deploying instruction-following navigation agents in unseen indoor environments without pre-built maps.

entry.title: DWMP: Leveraging Dual World Models for Humanoid Obstacle Traversal

author.name: Rongjun Jin, Jianming Ma, Yue Gao

entry.summary: DWMP addresses humanoid obstacle traversal by noting that proprioceptive and egocentric visual observations have fundamentally different characteristics: proprioception is low-dimensional but governed by highly nonlinear dynamics, while vision is high-dimensional, noisy, and redundant. The framework gives the actor separate but complementary world-model representations, including a Koopman-based dynamics model that lifts proprioceptive observations into a latent space where temporal evolution is approximately linear.

entry.title: Semiparametric Inference for Conditional Shapley Feature Importance

author.name: Agostino Gnasso

entry.summary: This paper studies conditional Shapley feature importance, where out-of-coalition features are integrated under their true conditional distribution rather than the marginal distribution used by popular implementations that misattribute importance under feature dependence. It proposes a one-step estimator with K-fold cross-fitting and a U-statistic correction of the squared loss that removes the Monte Carlo bias of the naive plug-in, yielding a root-n consistent, uncertainty-quantified global loss-based importance measure. It matters for trustworthy post-hoc interpretability when features are correlated.

entry.title: Alignment & Succession: The Two Bars of Alignment

author.name: L Rudolf L

entry.summary: This conceptual essay argues that discussions of AI alignment conflate two distinct success thresholds: a low bar where the AI simply obeys instructions and does not go rogue, and a much higher bar where the AI has fully internalized human values and could responsibly run society. It uses the framing of corrigibility, non-deceptiveness, and intent alignment for the first bar versus value alignment and coherent extrapolated volition for the second.

entry.title: MPT: Missing Prototype Tracking via Barycentric Reconstruction in Vehicular Federated Learning

author.name: Hanju Jang (Yonsei University), Gyeongmin Han (Yonsei University), Sungmin Lee (Yonsei University), Kichang Lee (Yonsei University), Chunghan Lee (Toyota Motor Corporation), JeongGil Ko (Yonsei University)

entry.summary: MPT addresses a concrete failure mode in cross-vehicle federated learning: a vehicle holding most samples of a class departs before convergence, making that class rare and silently degrading its recognition as the shared backbone keeps training. Because privacy rules block raw data and per-sample feature access, the method reconstructs and tracks the missing class prototype via barycentric reconstruction. The industrial co-authorship from Yonsei and Toyota signals a deployment-oriented framing.

entry.title: Anchoring Clinical Events in Time: UID-Preserving Multimodal Reconstruction and Source-Grounded Adjudication

author.name: Sayantan Kumar, Nicolas Grimaldi, Jack Cummins, Jeremy C. Weiss

entry.summary: This paper presents a UID-preserving framework that links each narrative clinical event occurrence to its source span and carries that identity through text-only estimation, structured-evidence retrieval, timestamped source-row grounding, and joint revision. It also introduces GAVEL, an LLM judge that compares two UID-aligned timelines against the narrative and structured record to supplement prior matching and temporal assessments. Experiments span six open-weight models over 40 mixed-critical-care summaries, including a comparison of GLM 5.2's multimodal and text-only variants.

entry.title: Simulating Disengaged Students to Evaluate LLM-based Tutors

author.name: Xianghui Meng, Jionghao Lin

entry.summary: The paper presents Disengagement-Aware Student Simulators (DAS2), a reproducible pre-deployment protocol that models five learner-engagement states - engaged, gaming, wheel-spinning, off-task, and mixed - to evaluate AI tutor performance. Two coders independently labeled 100 sampled tutoring sessions from ASSISTments09 based on anonymized interaction-log summaries to ground the simulators.

entry.title: Geometric-to-Semantic Spherical Transfer Learning for Cortical Sulci Labeling

author.name: Saeb Tounsi, Jo\"el Chavas, Pietro Gori, Vincent Frouin, Denis Rivi\`ere, Jean-Fran\c{c}ois Mangin

entry.summary: The paper tackles deep learning on cortical surfaces, where labeling more than 60 nomenclature-dependent sulci per hemisphere demands high capacity but expert annotations exist for only 62 subjects. It pretrains a spherical encoder on roughly 30,000 unlabeled UK Biobank subjects using a locally optimized strategy on continuous surface features like curvature and depth, then transfers to the scarce-label sulcus labeling task.

entry.title: Context-Aware Causal Gaze Forecasting for Human-Vehicle Interaction During In-Cabin Tracking Dropouts

author.name: Shabnam Shabani, Ghazal Farhani

entry.summary: This paper formulates causal gaze recovery, forecasting a driver's unavailable gaze at time t without using tracker data at or after t, unlike offline gap-filling that peeks at future observations. The Causal Context-Gated Forecaster encodes 60 frames of pre-dropout gaze and head pose history and combines it with DINOv3 scene features to handle dropouts during shoulder checks and mirror glances.

entry.title: MoPA: Coordinated Mobile Manipulation via Subsystem-Specific Perception Alignment

author.name: Guangyu Chen, Qiwei Liang, Shaolong Zhu, Tianxing Chen, Zikuan Xiao, Yifan Xie, Lingfeng Zhang, Ping Luo, Renjing Xu, Wenbo Ding

entry.summary: MoPA addresses mobile manipulation, where base motion and arm control need perceptual evidence at different spatial scales even though the two action modalities are kinematically coupled. It uses dual perceptual streams with mutually masked query banks to extract separate representations from a shared vision-language context, then adapts them jointly to their respective action branches. It matters because prior policies conditioned heterogeneous action heads on a single shared perception, leaving the perception-action correspondence implicit.

entry.title: ArtManip: Category-Level Articulated In-Hand Manipulation

author.name: Yang Yang, Tengyu Liu, Puhao Li, Zeyuan Chen, Yuyang Li, Xingwan Wang, Yingying Wu, Zhaopeng Cui, Siyuan Huang

entry.summary: ArtManip targets category-level in-hand manipulation of articulated objects with dexterous hands, a hard and underexplored problem with two bottlenecks: controlling an object's internal degrees of freedom while maintaining grasp stability on a free-floating base, and the labor-intensive acquisition of diverse object models and functional grasps needed for generalization. The authors report the first category-level method in this setting, generalizing across instances and diverse initial grasps, supported by an automated pipeline for constructing initial configurations.

entry.title: OneLA: Scaling Linear-Attention Decoding to Large Beams in Generative Recommendation

author.name: Xiangrui Yang, Cheng Peng, Yunfeng Zhao, Liang Zeng, Ao Hu, Jiawei Yang, Shengzhe Wang, Jingshan Lv, Xiao Liang, Chen Yang, Jiaqiang Liu, Yiming Qiu

entry.summary: The paper targets a serving bottleneck in generative recommendation, where large beam search over hundreds of candidate items makes recurrent linear attention expensive because each beam normally keeps its own state or replays shared history. OneLA instead represents all beam states with a single shared prompt-derived state plus compact append-only records of divergent transitions, computing only the state needed at each decoding step. It matters as a practical systems contribution for deploying linear-attention recommenders at realistic beam widths.

entry.title: SteerDuplex: Steerable Duplex Speech Dialogue Models

author.name: Utkarsh Tyagi, Ramaneswaran Selvakumar, Advait Gosai, Sonal Kumar, Nikhil Barhate, Isabell Sagar, Steven Li, Miheer Bavare, Daniel Quigley, Fabiola Tapia Carrillo, Jose M Patron E, Diego Mac\'ias Guti\'errez, Paul Song, Ramani Duraiswami, Dinesh Manocha, Yunzhong He

entry.summary: SteerDuplex targets steerability, the ability to shift conversational behavior along attributes like tone, persona, speaking rate, and voice style on instruction, which the authors find lacking in current full-duplex speech models. They first propose a taxonomy of text- and audio-based steerability, then build a Moshi-based full-duplex model fine-tuned on natural and synthetic dialogues for instruction following, vocal delivery, reasoning, and duplex interaction, with two-stage hybrid RL. It advances the under-explored controllability dimension of low-latency spoken dialogue systems.

entry.title: Skill Issue: Lessons from Optimizing Repository SKILLs for Coding Agents

author.name: Mykhailo Kozyrev, Andrei Kozyrev, Anton Podkopaev

entry.summary: The paper studies repository SKILL documents, markdown files versioned with code that coding agents read for knowledge, and notes that fully automated synthesis from synthetic benchmarks fails because capable agents saturate those tasks even with no document. Instead, the authors mine harder tasks from merged pull requests reverted at a frozen base commit and score candidate documents by whether the same agent performs better with than without them. On three Kotlin repositories, documents found by GEPA raise this score by about 4.9 percentage points while a competing optimizer leaves it essentially unchanged.

entry.title: Tracing and Coordinating Cross-Layer Influence for Multimodal Model Merging

author.name: Pengyang Zhou, Xiaobin Tu, Zhengxi Liu, Rongkun Xue, Haochen Li, Miancan Liu, Ziyuan Chen, Yinggui Wang, Jinkui Ren, Xiantao Zhang

entry.summary: This paper observes that most model-merging methods combine expert updates layer by layer, ignoring the fact that a visual or language expert update changes representations passed to later layers and thereby propagates across depth. When vision and language updates are merged, later updates act on inputs already modified by earlier ones, coupling their effects. The authors propose tracing and coordinating this cross-layer influence to better combine multimodal experts.

entry.title: Embodied-BenchForge: A Closed-Loop Agentic Workflow for Embodied Benchmark Construction

author.name: Baoyang Jiang, Fengchun Zhang, Leyuan Wang, Haotian Li, Yida Wang, Zhe Ji, Jinshan Lai, Xi Ren, Danyang Li, Zheng Yang, Jianwei Hu, Qiang Ma

entry.summary: Embodied-BenchForge is an agentic framework that turns user-specified evaluation intents into complete embodied benchmark artifacts. Its key idea is Closed-Loop Benchmark Synthesis, combining forward artifact synthesis with backward verification and repair, so that dependent intermediate artifacts are checked rather than passed downstream unchecked. This targets the propagation of local defects into final benchmarks that plagues staged construction pipelines.

entry.title: NDT Factory: Synthesizing Verified Network Digital Twins from Semantic Models via Multi-Agent LLM

author.name: Sudipta Acharya, Petar Djukic, Burak Kantarci

entry.summary: The NDT Factory is a multi-agent LLM system that synthesizes executable behavioral network digital twins on demand from semantic models, rather than relying on predefined analytical logic. It targets autonomous network management envisioned in TM Forum Level 4 autonomy, where Network Service Intents must be evaluated under varying conditions without hand-coded analysis. The system is validated on a Call Admission Control case study using deterministic what-if analysis as the admission decision process.

entry.title: Computing at Sea: Floating and Offshore Data Centres as a Pathway to Sustainable AI Infrastructure

author.name: Cheng Siong Chin, Jianhua Zhang, M. Venkateshkumar

entry.summary: This article examines floating and offshore data centres as an alternative model for AI infrastructure as land-based facilities hit limits in energy availability, cooling capacity, land use, freshwater consumption and carbon management. It argues conventional sites face urban land competition, grid congestion, environmental pressure and slow permitting, raising the question of where future compute can sustainably live. The piece is a positioning and survey contribution on physical infrastructure for AI scaling.

entry.title: Meddies-PII: A Multilingual Framework for Personally Identifiable Information Extraction in Clinical De-identification

author.name: Linh Uyen Le, Christian Hoang, Huy Hoang Ha

entry.summary: The paper introduces Meddies-PII-Dataset, one million synthetic clinical documents spanning seventeen languages and nine PII labels, generated with attribute-conditioned prompts and filtered through thirteen deterministic gates enforcing structural and annotation consistency. It then trains Meddies-PII-Model, a BIOES token classifier, and compares it against existing PII extraction baselines. The work responds to the cost of manual annotation and the limited transparency of prior synthetic alternatives.

entry.title: InRTL: Effective Intra-Inter Interaction Learning for Relational Tables

author.name: Weichen Li, Ken Zhong, Zheng Wang, Li Pan, Jianhua Li

entry.summary: Relational table learning models multiple tables linked by primary key-foreign key relationships, but lacks a principled unified framework. InRTL formalizes two complementary interaction patterns, within-table row associations and cross-table dependencies through PK-FK links, and develops a column-aware architecture to capture both. This matters for predictive tasks over enterprise databases and other multi-table data where naive flattening loses structure.

entry.title: Evaluating Context Segmentation in Locally Deployable SLMs for Cybersecurity CTF Tasks

author.name: Sebastiano Nordio, Michele Lotto

entry.summary: The paper notes that capable open-weight small language models can be run locally and bypass proprietary API guardrails, raising cybersecurity risk. It introduces context segmentation, a two-level agentic framework that breaks long exploratory exploitation tasks into contextually isolated sub-problems to counter context bloat and cognitive degradation from accumulated tool outputs. Evaluation is on the picoCTF dataset with memory-constrained local models, making the work both a capability assessment and a dual-use risk analysis.

entry.title: Comfort by Construction: Adaptive, Comfort-Bounded Action Spaces for Learned Driving Policies

author.name: Anna Rothenh\"ausler, Daniel Jost, Raghu Rajan, Faris Janjos, Oliver Scheel, Andreas Look, Joschka Boedecker

entry.summary: The paper shows that data-driven driving simulators with fixed action grids let reinforcement learning policies exploit unrealistic, abrupt maneuvers that inflate safety metrics without being human-comfortable. It proposes an adaptive action parameterization that rediscretizes the grid at every step to exactly span the feasible comfort region, avoiding the saturation and loss of fine control that naive clamping causes.

entry.title: Look Before You Leap: Pre-Action Verification for LLM Agents

author.name: Asaad Althoubi

entry.summary: This paper argues that cheap deterministic checks run before an agent action takes effect are an underused form of oversight, especially for silent failures where a wrong action produces a plausible but incorrect result. Across shell commands and code edits, a static verifier over 9,930 commands and 482 tools catches 95.8% of invalid commands at a 10.0% false-positive rate, with the option to abstain rather than guess.

entry.title: RiPPLE: Cross-Space Performance Prediction from Early Training for Neural Architecture Search

author.name: Yifan Yang, Zhaoyan Wang, Zheng Gao, Xiaoyu Li, Jiaojiao Jiang

entry.summary: RiPPLE addresses the cost of neural architecture search (NAS) by using partial, prefix-stage training as a source of labels for a small set of anchor architectures, then extrapolating those labels to rank the entire search space. The approach aims to combine the low cost of zero-cost proxies with the reliability of learned performance predictors, while avoiding the need to fully train candidates or rely on per-candidate partial-training features. It targets cross-space generalization, a known weakness of initialization-based proxies that vary in ranking quality across different search spaces.

entry.title: PinDCO: Whole-Page Aware Dynamic Creative Optimization at Scale

author.name: Yu Hao, Yuchun Li, Peimeng Sui, Meilin Liu, Tianyuan Cui, Hao Li, Zicong Zhou, Akanksha Baid

entry.summary: As generative AI multiplies the number of candidate ad creatives per campaign, Pinterest needs scalable dynamic creative optimization that matches creatives to audiences under tight latency and cost budgets. The paper presents PinDCO, a production system built around a Creative Component Fusion Network that scores creatives by modeling each component such as image, title, and layout with a dedicated tower using component-specific hyperparameters. The system handles whole-page aware retrieval and selection at billion scale.

entry.title: Efficient Vision-Language-Action Management and Serving for Robot Factories

author.name: Dionysios Adamopoulos, Nattapol Chanpaisit, Basel Fakhri, Christina Giannoula

entry.summary: The paper addresses serving Vision-Language-Action models for fleets of robots, where two-stage VLM plus action diffusion transformer inference is latency-critical and cannot run on-robot due to weight, cost, and power limits. It proposes a multi-request, multi-model serving and management system for multi-GPU edge servers that meets service-level objectives, since existing serving systems are optimized for throughput and stage disaggregation rather than latency SLOs. This matters for making robot-factory deployments feasible at scale.

entry.title: EAR: Entity-Aware Partitioning Approach for Retrieval-Augmented Generation Development

author.name: Cenab Batu Bora, Oylum Alatl{\i}, Sebnem Bora, Oguz Dikenelli

entry.summary: The paper argues that how a corpus is partitioned into retrievable units is an under-examined first design choice in retrieval-augmented generation. EAR extracts normalized surface anchors from questions, answer options, and corpora, retrieves local windows around matching anchors, and optionally attaches a larger parent passage via extractive summarization, evaluated on a cleaned 153-question MMLU-style set.

entry.title: SCDM: Spatial-Contextual Disentanglement Mamba via Differential Inference for Efficient Image Classification

author.name: Mustafa Bora \c{C}elik, Hayriye Akta\c{s} Din\c{c}er, Ayse Keles

entry.summary: SCDM proposes an asymmetric dual-branch state space model for medical image classification, with a positive branch extracting discriminative pathology features and a negative branch explicitly modeling normal anatomy to suppress it. This differential disentanglement aims to help Mamba-style models separate subtle disease signals from visually similar healthy tissue. It matters for medical AI where class boundaries are subtle and entangled representations hurt accuracy.

entry.title: MGAvatar: Mesh-Bound Gaussians for Head Avatar Geometry and Appearance Modeling

author.name: Lei Shi, Sen Peng, Zhiyang Deng, Zhonggui Chen, Xiaohu Guo, Baorong Yang, Xiao Dong

entry.summary: MGAvatar introduces a hybrid Gaussian-mesh representation for head avatars, binding Gaussians to mesh vertices in two modes so that progressive mesh deformation carries complex geometry. A pose-dependent offset module handles non-rigid deformation, and geometry and appearance are modeled jointly rather than relying on parametric templates such as FLAME. It matters for avatar reconstruction where hair and clothing are poorly captured by template-based priors.

entry.title: SV-Cine: Diagnosis-Conditioned Segmentation of Single Ventricle Physiology via Generative Data Augmentation

author.name: Lila Cunge, Yuehong Liu, Hang Xu, Thomas Coudert, Pierangelo Renella, J Paul Finn, William Hsu, Kim-Lien Nguyen

entry.summary: SV-Cine tackles cardiac MRI segmentation for single ventricle physiology, a rare congenital condition with atypical anatomy and very scarce clinical data. The framework generates synthetic 3D cardiac meshes with SDF4CHD and corresponding synthetic cardiac MRI through generative modeling, then uses diagnosis conditioning to guide segmentation of chambers and myocardium. It matters because rare-disease imaging lacks the data volumes that standard segmentation pipelines require.

entry.title: READ: Learning Risk-Informed Fields for End-to-End Autonomous Driving

author.name: Zhiyuan Liu, Yuanxin Tian, Zehong Ke, Jinhao Li, Hao Cheng, Zhenhua Xu, Wenhao Yu, Jianqiang Wang

entry.summary: READ argues that while learned planners implicitly capture how road structure, agents, and motion states influence maneuvers, the link between environmental factors and candidate actions stays opaque, and classical safety fields are explicit but use fixed risk shapes and weights that do not adapt per scene. The method learns risk-informed fields so that scene context influences predicted-trajectory safety in an inspectable way.

entry.title: The Iterative Equivariant Filter

author.name: Pieter van Goor, James Richard Forbes

entry.summary: The paper introduces the Iterative Equivariant Filter, which replaces the standard equivariant filter correction step with an iterative Gauss-Newton correction analogous to the iterated extended Kalman filter, combining symmetry-respecting estimation on Lie groups and homogeneous spaces with iterative nonlinear least-squares refinement. The derivation covers the iteration procedure and how intrinsic nonlinearity is handled. It matters for high-performance state estimation in navigation and robotics where symmetry structure and strong nonlinearity coexist.

entry.title: Consider how your global governance proposal is different from the EU Code of Practice

author.name: David Matolcsi

entry.summary: Written by an EU AI Office employee in a personal capacity, this post compares recent global AI governance proposals (e.g., Dario Amodei's coordination plan, Demis Hassabis's FINRA-style body) against the existing EU Code of Practice. It pushes proponents of new international regimes to specify concretely how their proposals differ from and improve upon existing European mechanisms.

entry.title: Legal Maximums on Context Windows

author.name: Julian Bradshaw

entry.summary: This policy proposal suggests capping frontier model context windows at a temporary legal maximum (e.g., around 5M tokens) as a legible, enforceable way to slow capability growth and force AIs to create monitorable external memory artifacts. It argues context length is a key constraint on continual learning and potentially recursive self-improvement, while noting context windows have effectively stalled around 1M tokens.

entry.title: T-GADE: Thermodynamical Generative-AI-Driven Evolution of LLM Artifacts

author.name: Kyoko Ogawa, Naoki Mori

entry.summary: T-GADE evolves structured LLM artifacts, such as a description paired with code, by extending thermodynamical genetic algorithms with LLM-based genetic operators and artifact-level diversity evaluation. A common free-energy objective supports both generational and steady-state updates, with Fermi-type occupancy excluding repeated genotypes and Bose-type occupancy permitting them. The authors establish exact one-member removal and conditions for recovering the zero-temperature survival rule of prior evolutionary methods.

entry.title: Interpreting the predictions of neural network classification based on a Taylor Coefficient Analysis (TCA)

author.name: Markus Klute, Artur Monsch, Lars Sowa, Roger Wolf

entry.summary: The authors introduce Taylor Coefficient Analysis, a taxonomy and paradigm for attributing a neural network's prediction to properties of the input feature space via a Taylor expansion of the output. They validate the approach on two simple benchmark tasks before applying it to a setup representative of a CERN LHC event-classification problem. It is a physics-driven contribution to neural network interpretability.

entry.title: Repair Before Reinforce: Context-Augmented Knowledge Graph Reasoning for Multi-Hop Question Answering

author.name: Tharaka D. Fonseka, Niraj K. Jha

entry.summary: This paper proposes a context-augmented training framework for multi-hop question answering over knowledge graphs, arguing that training LLMs only on isolated head-relation-tail triples limits the surrounding context needed for multi-hop reasoning. For each primary KG triple, supporting triples extracted from the graph are attached as context before reinforcement-style training; the KG extraction uses a framework called GraphMERT. The approach is validated on disease-specific KGs for Gastroparesis and Diabetes.

entry.title: Observation-Anchored Selective Assimilation for Longitudinal Tumor-State Proxy Forecasting in Post-Treatment Glioma

author.name: Yeonjae Jung, Minwoo Shin

entry.summary: The paper frames post-treatment glioma MRI forecasting as an observation-aware digital-twin update, where an intermediate observation anchors a patient-specific tumor-state proxy. Using 203 patients and 594 follow-up time points with a predefined no-new-treatment criterion, it builds continuous voxel-wise tumor-state proxy maps from lesion labels and uses a SegMamba-based single-step forecaster to generate update proposals. The selective assimilation design is meant to handle variable appearances and trajectories in serial imaging.

entry.title: LatentVerse: A Framework for Understanding Shared and Modality-Specific Information in Multimodal Latent Representations

author.name: Majd Alafrange, Samuel Friedman, John Kitonyo, Sana Tonekaboni, Mahnaz Maddah

entry.summary: LatentVerse is a representation-analysis resource combining a web-based visual analytics platform with report-driven exploration for dissecting multimodal latent embeddings, motivated by biomedical foundation models that encode clinical text, images, omics, and physiological signals. It targets the fragmentation of current representation-evaluation workflows, which lack multimodal analysis and reproducibility.

entry.title: SAGE-Loop: Reliable Closed-Loop LLM-Driven AutoML with Trial-and-Correction and Adaptive Ensembling

author.name: Junquan Gu, Shibo Cui, Xiangfeng Luo, Hang Yu

entry.summary: SAGE-Loop proposes a closed-loop, LLM-driven AutoML system that adds process-level correction and adaptive ensembling to overcome the one-way pipeline problem, where intermediate failures are terminated or bypassed and ensemble decisions stay static. It targets reliability, not just automation efficiency, by using trial-and-correction feedback during execution and structural diversity in ensembling.

entry.title: Information-Induced Training Geometry: Exact Reduction, Canonical Completion, and Structured Expressivity

author.name: Zavier Li

entry.summary: This theoretical paper studies how partial information from training data determines the geometry that an optimizer perceives, formalizing full-column-rank positive-definite metric compression under affine-invariant Riemannian geometry. It proves an explicit unique canonical completion realizing a visible target, yielding exact full-to-visible variational reduction, and shows that moving information channels produce a gauge-invariant rank stratification of the positive-definite cone. The framing connects information channels to structured expressivity of training dynamics.

entry.title: FoldNet++: a Large-Scale Synthetic Dataset for Robotic T-Shirt Folding and Unfolding

author.name: Yuxing Chen, Zhiyuan Wei, Bowen Xiao, Zhizheng Zhang, He Wang

entry.summary: FoldNet++ presents a large-scale synthetic dataset for robotic T-shirt folding and unfolding, spanning six robotic embodiments, one thousand T-shirts, one thousand environmental assets, and 120 thousand annotated episodes usable for training a range of manipulation policies. The authors follow the FoldNet pipeline to generate physically simulatable garments with diverse appearances and semantic keypoints, then produce demonstrations for each embodiment through a unified rule-based framework.

entry.title: Hybrid Physics-AI Framework of Body Center of Mass Dynamics from Wrist-Worn Sensors

author.name: Shuhao Que, Valentina Breschi, Ying Wang

entry.summary: This work builds a simplified kinematic model that maps wrist IMU measurements to body center-of-mass acceleration under reductive assumptions, then combines it with neural networks in several hybrid human-kinematic-model configurations (serial and parallel learning variants). The goal is to recover whole-body dynamics, for which center of mass is the physiological reference, from a wrist-worn device. It matters for daily-life health monitoring with wearables.

entry.title: VRL-Bench: Benchmarking agents on computer control tasks under finite trial budgets

author.name: Yu Bai, Yukai Miao, Dawei Wang, Li Chen, Yanyu Ren, Yuqian Shi, Dan Li, Ying Xiong, Chengqiu Tan, Run Zhou, Li Li

entry.summary: VRL-Bench is a harness for fairly comparing trial-and-error learning methods for computer-control agents under bounded trial budgets, spanning Reflexion and later verbal-memory approaches. Testing several models on MiniWoB and WebShop, the authors find that verbal reflection helps in some settings but hurts in others, and replay experiments show reflection can actually lower success rates. This is a useful negative-result contribution to the popular verbal reinforcement learning narrative.

entry.title: When Does AI Augment Work? A Workflow-Level Framework for Human-Agent Collaboration

author.name: AI Collaboration, Jiaying Wu, Caleb Ziems, Raymond Chan, Nancy F. Chen, Corlyss Chua, Gerard Chung, Jungpil Hahn, Wee Sun Lee, Zhengyuan Liu, Jamie Ng, Desmond C. Ong, Jeryl Ong, Da Ren Soon, Tianqi Song, Zhi-Xuan Tan, Sixing Tao, Emily Yang, Yajing Yang, Stella Xin Yin, Min-Yen Kan, Diyi Yang

entry.summary: The authors argue that measuring AI's workplace value through today's automation capability and adoption rates misses how human-agent collaboration can reshape work at the workflow level. They define AI augmentation through six conditions covering durable net value, meaningful human control, accountability and recovery, and long-term human development via learning, career pathways, and job purpose. The framework is a conceptual scaffold for evaluating augmentation claims rather than a new system.

entry.title: Residual Vector-based Reconstruction as Long-Context Recall Regardless of Context Window Size

author.name: MyungHoon Ryu, XinYu Piao, Jong-Kook Kim

entry.summary: The paper proposes retrieving facts from long documents by reconstructing them from parameter activations in the LLM's feed-forward layers, which are argued to store residual vectors representing source facts. This keeps GPU memory near-constant as context length grows and requires no additional training, addressing long-context recall beyond the pretrained context window. It offers an interesting activation-space alternative to prompt compression and context extension.

entry.title: PRISMA-LLM: An Empirical Reporting Framework for AI-Assisted Systematic Reviews

author.name: Miguel Zabaleta, Baihan Lin

entry.summary: The authors analyse SciLitBench, a corpus of 888 review-automation papers with 14,726 annotations, to characterise how methods, review-stage use, evaluation, and reported limitations have changed. They find automation shifting toward LLM and software-facing workflows including stages that can alter the evidence base, and that since 2023 38.0 percent of software and product papers reported no evaluation versus 9.3 percent of LLM papers, with 52 percent of positive-only LLM evaluations leaving a reliability requirement unmet. The paper proposes reporting guidance for auditable AI-assisted reviews.

entry.title: Extracting Dataset Mentions in Forced Displacement and FCV Documents: A Weakly Supervised Framework with LLM-Based Label Refinement

author.name: Rafael Macalaba, Aivin V. Solatorio, Patrick Michael Brock, Olivier Dupriez

entry.summary: This paper presents a weakly supervised framework for extracting references to datasets within forced displacement and Fragile, Conflict, and Violence documents, avoiding the need for a large manually labeled corpus. A lightweight model trained on general data is adapted, with LLM-based refinement of labels, to identify dataset mentions scattered across research papers, project documents, and humanitarian reports. The goal is better tracing of data use and identification of gaps in data availability and dissemination.

entry.title: A Graph-Based Approach for Mapping Kernel-Level Telemetry to MITRE ATT&CK

author.name: Matteo Lupinacci, Luigi Arena, Francesco Blefari, Angelo Furfaro

entry.summary: Mapping observed behavior to frameworks like MITRE ATT&CK is largely manual, and existing automation depends on retrospective threat-intelligence reports. This work instead collects kernel-level events via eBPF, correlates attacker commands into a provenance graph, and derives compact graph representations for LLM-based reasoning, comparing pure prompting with other mapping strategies. It matters for building evidence-based, real-time threat detection rather than report-driven attribution.

entry.title: 3D CT-to-PET Translation via Latent Brownian Bridge Diffusion

author.name: Sarita Mourya, Francesco Di Feola, Pierangelo Veltri, Paolo Soda

entry.summary: PET imaging provides functional information complementary to CT but is limited by radiation exposure, cost, and availability, motivating synthesis of PET-like images from CT. The authors propose a two-stage 3D framework that first trains a variational autoencoder on paired CT-PET data and then performs latent Brownian Bridge diffusion for cross-modal translation. This matters as a step toward reducing reliance on PET acquisition in cancer diagnosis and treatment planning.

entry.title: Generative Retrieval for Unsupervised Text-Based Person Search

author.name: Mang Ye, Yucheng Ji, Yang Bai, Min Cao, Siyuan Chai, Bo Du, Min Zhang
