entry.summary: The paper presents GTR+, a two-stage generation-then-retrieval framework for unsupervised text-based person search that learns from unlabeled images only. A tiered description generation process uses automated question-and-answer mechanisms and finer-grained enhancement to produce diverse, detailed pseudo-text descriptions that support later retrieval.

entry.title: Groupoid-Based Internal State Representations for Reinforcement Learning with Local Symmetries

author.name: Ben Opperman, Eduardo Alonso, Esther Mondrag\'on

entry.summary: This paper proposes a reinforcement learning framework that uses groupoids, rather than fixed groups, to capture local and state-dependent symmetries that standard MDP assumptions miss. The agent maintains orbit representatives and transporters to dynamically discover equivalence structures during interaction, exploiting modularity in realistic environments.

entry.title: Performance, Efficiency and Collapse -- Advantages and Challenges in Offline Post-training of Code LLMs

author.name: Abhinav Anand, Sanjana Reddy Pachika, Shweta Verma, Mira Mezini

entry.summary: This study asks whether reinforcement learning post-training for code LLMs can be done entirely offline using existing datasets instead of costly online sample generation and verification. It reports that zero-shot code generation can improve substantially within a few hours of training without online sampling, while also documenting collapse phenomena that limit the approach.

entry.title: Poisson-Corrector Complexity Bounds for Moreau--Yosida Unadjusted Langevin Sampling

author.name: Yuchen Xin, Zhihua Zhang

entry.summary: This work establishes convergence bounds for the Moreau-Yosida unadjusted Langevin algorithm sampling from a target whose negative log-density splits into a strongly convex smooth part and a convex Lipschitz part. It proves Wasserstein-2 error bounds between the Moreau-smoothed target and the MYULA invariant law with only logarithmic dependence on the smoothing parameter, yielding an iteration complexity of order epsilon to the minus four thirds.

entry.title: Optimizing for the decision not the prediction: an exploration of Smooth Net Benefit as a training objective

author.name: Koen M. F. Gorgels, Lasai Barre\~nada, Maarten van Smeden, Ben Van Calster, Ewout W. Steyerberg, Wouter A. C. van Amsterdam

entry.summary: The paper introduces Smooth Net Benefit, a differentiable approximation of Net Benefit designed to align model training with threshold-specific clinical utility instead of pure likelihood. It evaluates this objective across logistic regression, generalized additive models, and XGBoost with three Hessian implementations on the Framingham cardiovascular dataset and 44 TabZilla datasets covering 72 dataset-threshold combinations.

entry.title: Dimension-Corrected Hitting Times for Heavy-Tailed Spectral Emergence in Neural Optimizer Dynamics

author.name: Zongmin Liu

entry.summary: The author reformulates the emergence of heavy-tailed weight-matrix spectra in neural network training as a right-censored hitting-time estimation problem rather than discarding censored runs. In controlled full-batch teacher-student dynamics, the first-step spike-bulk gap alone does not predict onset time; instead a dimension-corrected spectral-gap scaling law fits the data well. The empirical exponents hint that width and initial spectral gap jointly govern how quickly heavy tails appear.

entry.title: MCRL2: Multi-resource Cross-attention-based Representation Learning-augmented Reinforcement Learning for Cloud Microservice Scheduling

author.name: Tiangang Li, Shi Ying, Xiangbo Tian, Chuan Shi, Ding Xiao

entry.summary: This work addresses cloud microservice scheduling under fluctuating workloads, where heterogeneous resource demands create nonlinear coupling across CPU, memory, and other dimensions. The authors propose MCRL2, an RL approach augmented with multi-resource cross-attention representation learning, arguing that prior RL schedulers neglect informative system representations and interdependencies among resource types. The method targets better load balancing and quality of service in data centers.

entry.title: Scenario-Independent Criticality Assessment and Prediction for Vulnerable Road Users in Autonomous Driving

author.name: J\"org Gamerdinger, Victor Schwarzenberger, Philipp Schmid, Sven Teufel, Oliver Bringmann

entry.summary: The paper argues that existing criticality metrics for automated vehicles are scenario-specific and focus mainly on vehicle-to-vehicle interaction, leaving vulnerable road users like pedestrians and cyclists poorly served given their less predictable motion. The authors propose a novel criticality metric tailored to vulnerable road users that incorporates factors such as object type, velocity, and criticality. A key aim is to distinguish critical from non-critical objects without the complexity of scenario-specific designs.

entry.title: Learning the Geometry of Collider Events with Metric-Aware Deep Sets

author.name: Lauren Hay, Rishabh Jain, Matt LeBlanc, Jennifer Roloff

entry.summary: The paper develops a Deep Sets surrogate for optimal transport between variable-size weighted point clouds that enforces non-negativity, exchange symmetry, and zero self-distance, while leaving the triangle inequality unconstrained. Applied to the Energy Mover's Distance between collider events, the Metric-Aware Particle Flow Network reaches percent-level mean absolute percentage error and much faster inference than exact and approximate alternatives. It shows architecture-aware metric constraints can give accurate, fast geometric surrogates for high-energy physics analysis.

entry.title: Membership Inference via Pairwise Likelihood Ratios

author.name: Shengjie Niu, Zebin Yun, Yeheng Ge, Jian Huang

entry.summary: The paper proposes Pairwise Likelihood MIA, a unified membership inference method that combines a Gaussian likelihood-ratio statistic with population calibration and the Cauchy combination test. It is designed to efficiently summarize and combine the statistical signals exposed by model outputs, such as confidence scores, logits, and intermediate features. The authors characterize theoretically how the likelihood-ratio statistic behaves, aiming to make privacy auditing more reliable.

entry.title: What Did the MLLM Hear? Token-Level Spectro-Temporal Grounding for Audio MLLM Explainability

author.name: Lucia Cascone, Valeria Fraenza, Michele Nappi, Fabio Narducci, Benedetto Simone

entry.summary: The paper introduces STAG, described as the first post-hoc framework for token-level spectro-temporal grounding of captions generated by audio-based multimodal large language models. STAG estimates the temporal support of each generated token using target-token-specific vocabulary projections of encoded audio representations, and measures relevance across frequency bands. This matters because acoustic evidence is spread over time and frequency and overlapping sounds complicate attribution, making interpretability of audio MLLMs genuinely difficult.

entry.title: High-Probability Convergence of SGD via Batched Updates

author.name: Feng Zhu, Robert W. Heath Jr., Aritra Mitra

entry.summary: The paper proposes Batched SGD, which partitions online samples into epochs and performs a single update per epoch using a refined low-variance gradient estimate. The authors show that this simple batching mechanism yields high-probability guarantees for the last iterate without restrictive assumptions such as bounded domains or bounded gradients, and without complex auxiliary-sequence proofs. This matters because mean-squared bounds are well understood but high-probability last-iterate guarantees for SGD have been comparatively difficult.

entry.title: Beyond Accuracy: Uncertainty-Guided Boundary Refinement for Reliable Biomedical Image Segmentation

author.name: Anima Kujur

entry.summary: The paper proposes RABR-Net, a two-stage framework that combines a strong UNet++ with an EfficientNet-B4 backbone and an uncertainty-guided refinement stage to improve boundary delineation in blood-smear microscopy images. It aggregates several uncertainty signals, such as predictive entropy, test-time augmentation variance, margin uncertainty, and probability gradients, to target clinically meaningful contour regions where global overlap scores hide errors.

entry.title: PA-CDM: Position-Aware Character Detection Matching for Evaluating Handwritten Mathematical Expression Recognition

author.name: Shiliang Luo (East China Normal University)

entry.summary: The paper argues that exact-match and string-similarity metrics for handwritten math recognition are blind to where errors occur, giving identical scores to subscript misplacements and fraction operand swaps. It introduces PA-CDM, a position-aware character detection matching metric that outperforms render-based and tree-edit alternatives on controlled error cases.

entry.title: Doc2FRC: Length-Consistent Document-Level Machine Translation via Fixed-Range Chunking

author.name: Xiaotian Wang, Youyuan Lin, Zhan Shen, Hitomi Yanaka

entry.summary: The paper tackles degeneracies in document-level machine translation with long-context LLMs, where direct document-to-document translation produces n-gram repetition and progressive quality decay. Fixed-Range Chunking uses dynamic programming to partition documents into chunks within a predefined length interval and applies the same chunking at training and inference to remove the length-distribution mismatch of rule-based chunking.

entry.title: Fewer Words, Not Fewer Tokens: Measuring the Sanskrit Tokenization Penalty per Proposition

author.name: Devansh Sharma

entry.summary: This study measures how subword tokenizers handle Sanskrit on identical FLORES-200 content, finding Sanskrit costs roughly 1.77-2.19 times English tokens but far less relative to Hindi. Against a matched English control, the apparent per-proposition advantage of Sanskrit-trained BPE disappears, suggesting the effect is about word-level density rather than inherent token efficiency.

entry.title: Revisiting Multi-Object Tracking Baselines: Hyperparameter Optimization with Multi-Fidelity Greedy Coordinate Search

author.name: Momir Ad\v{z}emovi\'c

entry.summary: This paper systematically applies hyperparameter optimization to multi-object tracking, an area where parameters are still largely tuned by hand and reported procedures are often undocumented. It evaluates across two datasets and four tracking-by-detection methods and proposes Multi-Fidelity Greedy Coordinate Search, which optimizes one parameter at a time under fidelity budgets.

entry.title: RelateAnything: Real-Time Open-Vocabulary Relation Prediction From Any Inputs

author.name: Ma\"elic Neau

entry.summary: RelateAnything argues that relation prediction has lagged behind open-vocabulary detection and promptable segmentation, which moved the taxonomy out of the model and into the input. The authors identify three obstacles, lack of a free-text verified relation corpus, label-conditioned architectures that cannot accept unseen vocabularies, and metrics that penalize larger vocabularies, and present a 53-million-parameter model plus a corpus and metric to address them. It matters for making scene-graph-style reasoning as flexible as modern open-vocabulary perception.

entry.title: DRS-VPT: Directly Relocalizing in a Scan with Vision Point Transformers

author.name: Lanke Frank Tarimo Fu, Maurice Fallon

entry.summary: DRS-VPT is a feed-forward transformer for image-to-scan registration that, given query images and a reference 3D point cloud, predicts the scan pose and point map along with each camera's pose and point map in the first camera frame, plus a coarse-to-fine pyramid of per-point and per-pixel features for direct reprojective alignment. This unifies tasks like camera-LiDAR calibration and indoor relocalization across driving and indoor settings. It matters for robust, generalizable 3D perception and localization without per-domain retraining.

entry.title: HemaHier: Chain-Conditioned Ordinal Hierarchies for Lineage-Aware Bone-Marrow Cytology

author.name: Afshin Bozorgpour, Peter Sch\"uffler, Edgar Jost, Dorit Merhof

entry.summary: HemaHier adds an ordinal-hierarchical prediction head to cytology foundation models, using a chain-conditioned maturity score that reads a single maturity value per lineage query. Supervision is restricted to biologically valid healthy maturation chains, while dysplastic and off-chain cell types stay as classes but are excluded from maturity supervision. It matters because flat classifiers ignore hematopoietic lineage structure and treat mild and severe mistakes as equally costly.

entry.title: Chain-SLAM: Globally Consistent Backend for Multi-Session LiDAR SLAM via Chained Loop Closure

author.name: Zhiheng Li, Xinhao Liu, Juexiao Zhang, Yongqing Liang, Chen Feng

entry.summary: Chain-SLAM is a LiDAR SLAM backend for large-scale multi-session mapping that maintains global consistency when merging maps collected at different times. It propagates geometric constraints across inter-session keyframes through an adjacency graph using chained loop closure, initializes alignment with GNSS-proximity place recognition, and then performs on-the-fly loop detection with joint optimization of loaded maps.

entry.title: Autonomous Precision Milling of Biological Structures via Generic Anatomical Priors and Active Boundary Perception

author.name: Enduo Zhao, Xiaofeng Lin, Yifan Wang, Yuhan Song, Weihan Li, Saul Alexis Heredia Perez, Kanako Harada

entry.summary: This paper proposes an uncertainty-aware framework for autonomous precision milling of biological structures such as bone, combining generic anatomical priors for conservative global guidance with active on-the-fly boundary perception. Semantic-guided registration and hybrid vision-force calibration turn the prior into robot-executable instructions, while sensing during execution decides boundary status. It matters because it targets surgical/robotic machining tasks where subject-specific preoperative models are expensive and static models cannot verify critical internal boundaries in real time.

entry.title: Distributed Stochastic Optimal Control for Pattern-Oriented Swarms

author.name: Qingrui Zhang, Chenghao Yu, Feng Xue, Xintong Wang

entry.summary: The paper proposes a Gaussian Random Field-based stochastic optimal control framework that extends the GRF into the temporal domain, casting collective coordination of pattern-oriented swarms as Bayesian inference so swarms can handle environmental uncertainty, non-convex constraints, and heterogeneous platform dynamics. It includes an uncertainty- and safety-aware collision avoidance module for navigation with stochastic obstacles. It matters for scalable, unified control of diverse swarm platforms under uncertainty.

entry.title: Exact Community Recovery in Bipartite Networks

author.name: Huan Qing

entry.summary: This paper proves that a simple spectral clustering procedure achieves exact community recovery in bipartite stochastic co-blockmodels, covering regimes where the number of communities grows, community sizes are unbalanced, and node degrees are heterogeneous. It matters for recommendation systems, biological networks, and social network analysis, where bipartite structure and unbalanced, heterogeneous degrees are the norm rather than the exception and prior guarantees were limited.

entry.title: Anthropic and OpenAI haven’t published a plan for aligning superintelligence

author.name: Zephaniah Roe

entry.summary: The author argues that neither OpenAI nor Anthropic has published a concrete, detailed technical plan for aligning superintelligence comparable in rigor to AI 2040, and that this gap reflects negligence and limited openness to external critique. It notes OpenAI's 2023 superalignment strategy as the closest attempt, which it found unconvincing and whose team no longer exists.

entry.title: LifeFuse-Mem: Lifecycle-Aware State Fusion Against Temporary Overwriting for Long-Term Memory

author.name: Hanyu Zhao, Yuqian Feng, Zhenyu Song, Yuanchao Cheng, Yance Jiao, Tengfei Pan, Li Du

entry.summary: The paper studies a lifecycle-labeled memory setting where the system must distinguish durable knowledge from information that should only affect the current context. It introduces LifeFuse-Mem, a neural memory framework that separates information by temporal lifecycle so short-lived writes do not overwrite durable states, which otherwise causes behavioral drift in persistent agents. The framing is relevant to the broader problem of long-running agent memory hygiene.

entry.title: Assisted Spatial Cognition Through Vision-Language Models

author.name: H. Riaz, J. B. Fernandez, I. Mills, D. Hickey, F. Cleary, M. I. Ali

entry.summary: The authors propose an end-to-end framework combining LLMs, vision-language models, and digital twin technology to give visually impaired and neuro-divergent users richer spatial understanding for indoor and outdoor navigation. It targets the 43 million-plus people worldwide who currently rely on route-constrained aids that lack full 3D scene comprehension. The work sits at the intersection of assistive technology, multimodal perception, and accessibility.

entry.title: Self-Verifying Anomaly Detection using Explainable AI for Cybersecurity of DER Networks

author.name: Damilola Popoola, Souradeep Bhattacharya, Manimaran Govindarasu

entry.summary: The paper presents ExCYDER, an explainable anomaly detection framework for Distributed Energy Resource networks, where growing attack surfaces demand both accuracy and operator trust. It combines ML detection with XAI so that Security Operations Center analysts can interpret alerts, and adds a self-verification element to make detections more reliable. The work is a domain application of interpretability to critical infrastructure security.

entry.title: When Connected Does Not Mean Similar: Charting the Homophily Boundary of SNAP-KG for Streaming Entity Integration

author.name: Jui-Chien Lin, Oshani Seneviratne

entry.summary: This work probes the operating limits of SNAP-KG, a framework that assigns newly arriving entities to semantic communities in a growing knowledge graph using only raw features and no graph access at inference. Extending evaluation to three heterophilous graphs, it measures per-view edge homophily and shows clustering quality collapses when no homophilous view exists, for both SNAP-KG and a transductive baseline.

entry.title: Curriculum-Based Adversarial Heterogeneous Agent Reinforcement Learning for Autonomous Quad-Copter Landing in Maritime Settings

author.name: Allan Minh-Tam Nguyen, Sree Showrya Kotala, Stefan Banioi-Crijman, Kurt Driessens, Rico M\"ockel

entry.summary: This paper studies simulated mid-air capture of quadrotor UAVs by a ship-mounted robotic arm, learning cooperative control policies with heterogeneous-agent proximal policy optimization. Training combines a curriculum and an adversarial wind agent inside NVIDIA Isaac Lab, and the resulting policies are compared against curriculum-based domain randomization and a single-sea-state baseline.

entry.title: LG-PF: Lightweight Confidence-Guided Polarization Image Fusion

author.name: Zhuangfan Huang, Zhenyu Kuang, Gao Wang, Yang Liu, Haishu Tan, Xiaosong Li

entry.summary: This paper introduces LG-PF, a lightweight framework for fusing total-intensity images with degree-of-linear-polarization (DoLP) images. Rather than transferring polarization detail everywhere, it estimates a spatial polarization confidence prior and uses a mask-guided multi-scale module to transfer only reliable polarization residuals. It matters because it addresses a known failure mode of polarization fusion, where noisy or unreliable DoLP responses degrade structural fidelity.

entry.title: When2Talk: When Should a Proactive In-Car Agent Talk?

author.name: Kaiser Hamid, Peihang Li, Nade Liang

entry.summary: This mixed-methods within-subject study placed 41 participants as passengers in a VR simulated fully automated vehicle to test when an in-cabin agent should speak. It compared an event-triggered policy that communicates immediately at every event against a context-sensitive policy that chooses immediate, delayed, or silent communication. The context-sensitive policy improved perceived communication appropriateness and reduced perceived interruption, with no significant trust difference.

entry.title: Online Material Estimation for Conditioned Diffusion Policy in Shaping Deformable Linear Objects

author.name: Ryunosuke Yamada, Tomohiro Motoda, Yukiyasu Domae, Tokuo Tsuji

entry.summary: The authors propose a diffusion policy conditioned on material labels estimated online during manipulation, using a recurrent network that predicts material properties (such as stiffness) from multi-view images and joint states, with the label conditioning every inference step. They validate with 480 real-robot demonstrations across four deformable linear object materials and three groove-placement tasks. It matters because a single visuomotor policy otherwise cannot produce correct action sequences when the same goal shape requires different deformation behavior per material.

entry.title: Mined from Scientific Literature: Process Schemas for Atomic Layer Deposition and Etching in Materials Science

author.name: Sameer Sadruddin, Eleni Poupaki, Alex Watkins, Bora Karasulu, Adriaan J. M. Mackus, Erwin Kessels, S\"oren Auer, Jennifer D'Souza

entry.summary: The authors present four domain-expert-reviewed JSON Schemas for atomic layer deposition and etching experiments and simulations, curated with schema-mining tools and grounded in the QUDT units ontology. The schemas structure materials, process conditions, configurations and measured or predicted results, and are demonstrated for schema-guided literature extraction and publication through ORKG templates. It matters as infrastructure for making materials science literature machine-actionable.

entry.title: CMA-OT: Hierarchical Expert Supervision for Dance-to-Music Generation

author.name: Jinting Wang, Chenxing Li, Dong Yu, Li Liu

entry.summary: CMA-OT tackles dance-to-music generation, where sparse dance cues such as rhythm and style must be mapped to dense musical content including structure, instrumentation, and dynamics. The proposed Curriculum-guided Multi-scale representation Alignment with scale-aware Optimal Transport leverages an external music expert to supervise intermediate representations rather than only the final audio. This aims to improve musicality and structural coherence in generated music.

entry.title: Creating an Atomic User Model for Personality-Aware Large Language Model Interaction

author.name: B. Sankar, Deepthika S, Pawni Yadav, Amogh A S

entry.summary: The paper argues that dominant personalization approaches store preferences as summaries reinserted into context, which inverts inference because preferences are only a task-dependent surface of a more stable personality structure. It characterizes personality seepage, where a prompt's linguistic surface carries a personality fingerprint the assistant mirrors, and proposes the Atomic User Model, a human-readable representation with a stable identity nucleus. The goal is assistant writing that transfers across tasks rather than being relearned per task.

entry.title: Not All Speech Is Intent: Adaptive Self-Correcting Inference Layer for Post-ASR False Wake-Up

author.name: Preeti Saraswat, Divya Neelagiri, Anil Yadav

entry.summary: The paper addresses false wake-up activations in conversational AI, where speech phonetically similar to a wake word yields a valid and coherent ASR transcript that the assistant wrongly executes. It introduces ASCIL, a post-ASR correction layer that re-evaluates wake-up intent before response generation by fusing acoustic embeddings, linguistic cues, device context and patterns from past misclassifications. A distinguishing feature is online adaptation to recurring errors and individual users rather than a single isolated intent decision.

entry.title: CRFCAN: A Complex-Valued Cross-Domain Residual Network for Joint Channel and Phase Noise Estimation in Sub-THz OFDM Systems

author.name: Ruilin Wang, Xiaodai Dong

entry.summary: CRFCAN is a complex-valued residual FFT convolutional attention network for joint channel and phase noise estimation in sub-THz OFDM, embedding FFT and inverse FFT modules in residual groups for end-to-end recovery. It avoids the cascaded or hybrid neural-iterative architectures used by prior deep learning schemes.

entry.title: Fast BIB simulation at a future Muon Collider with generative machine learning

author.name: Radha Mastandrea, Shiyu Peng, Benjamin Rosser, Matt LeBlanc

entry.summary: This work introduces the first machine learning models for fast generation of beam-induced background in muon collider tracking detectors, a simulation task that currently costs roughly a million HS23 hours and about 100 GB of storage for a small statistical sample. Two architecture classes are considered, including a slower higher-fidelity tabular diffusion model and a faster alternative. The goal is to make large, accurate background samples affordable so that event reconstruction algorithms can be developed and validated.

entry.title: Tight Sampling Complexity with stochastic gradient oracles in Fixed Dimensions

author.name: Weiming Ou, Xiao Wang

entry.summary: This work establishes the tight stochastic-gradient query complexity for sampling smooth strongly log-concave distributions in any fixed Euclidean dimension, with a strongly convex and smooth potential whose mode is unknown and with unbiased stochastic oracles of bounded variance. The authors prove a complexity bound in terms of condition number and variance-to-accuracy ratio that is optimal in total variation distance. It matters because matching upper and lower bounds for stochastic sampling clarify what algorithms like Langevin-type methods can and cannot achieve.

entry.title: When Ground-Truth Fidelity Matters: An Orchestrated UAS Framework for Wheat Streak Mosaic Virus Detection Using Vision Transformers and Machine Learning

author.name: Dewi Endah Kharismawati, Sandeep Dhakal, Courtney E. McCusker, Jennifer R. Wilson, Erik W. Ohlson, Sami Khanal

entry.summary: This work presents an automated plant-level pipeline for detecting wheat streak mosaic virus from UAS multispectral imagery, integrating orthomosaic reconstruction with vision transformer and classical machine learning classifiers. It targets an economically and regulatorily important pathogen where visual scouting is unreliable and ELISA testing is costly and hard to scale.

entry.title: NOVA-GS: Noise-Aware View-Consistent Gaussian Splatting for Low-Light Novel View Synthesis

author.name: Shaurya Pavan A, Vemunuri Divya Madhuri, Yash Pradeep Gawande, Kaushik Mitra

entry.summary: NOVA-GS is a unified noise-aware framework for low-light 3D Gaussian Splatting that subsumes enhancement, denoising and geometry optimization in a single process, avoiding dependence on well-lit reference data for structure-from-motion initialization and avoiding per-view enhancement that breaks cross-view consistency. It leverages feed-forward estimation to obtain robust camera initialization under degraded inputs. It matters for 3D reconstruction and view synthesis in genuinely difficult lighting conditions.

entry.title: LGFN: Lightweight Gated RGB-Polarization Fusion with Modality-Availability Conditioning for Camouflaged Object Detection

author.name: Zhuangfan Huang, Xiaosong Li, Yang Liu, Tao Ye, Haishu Tan

entry.summary: LGFN is a lightweight gated fusion framework for camouflaged object detection that explicitly handles whether polarization data is available at inference time. A deterministic modality router selects an RGB-only or polarization-assisted configuration, avoiding the fixed multimodal assumption of prior work. This matters for deploying COD systems on real sensors where polarization input may be missing.

entry.title: Input Resolution Matters: Real-Time Object Detection Latency

author.name: Qingyang Zhang, Fumio Machida, Laura Carnevali

entry.summary: The paper models end-to-end object detection latency as the convolution of preprocessing, inference, and postprocessing latency distributions, with stage parameters expressed as functions of source image resolution. Experiments use YOLOv11n on an NVIDIA Jetson Orin NX across COCO2017 images at multiple resolutions to assess the models. It matters for real-time and safety-critical deployment, where latency tail probabilities rather than mean latency determine whether deadlines are met.

entry.title: Unlabeled Echoes: Pseudo-Labels and Genus-Aware Smoothing for Bat Call Recognition

author.name: Frank Fundel, Alexandra Howard

entry.summary: This paper shows that simple model-generated pseudo-labels convert surplus unlabeled bat recordings into effective supervision, outperforming other semi-supervised methods on an 18-species European corpus using only ten percent of training labels. The approach is then transferred to South African field audio with nine bat taxa plus a nuisance class, gaining over ten points in species accuracy. It also introduces genus-aware smoothing to exploit taxonomic structure.

entry.title: Can LLMs in Draft-Verify-Revise Pipelines Resolve Deictic Ambiguity?

author.name: Obinna I. Ekekezie

entry.summary: This study examines the draft-verify-revise orchestration pattern and shows that as context cascades between stages, models can resolve context-dependent expressions such as 'previous' differently, producing a deictic shift in what the expression refers to. Using a synthetic dataset of 10 base examples rendered in three controlled conditions, it isolates whether the drafting or the verifying model resolves the reference correctly. The finding matters for reliability of multi-stage inference-time-compute pipelines.

entry.title: Robust Prototypical Networks for Few-Shot Sensor Fault Diagnosis

author.name: Mohammed Ayalew Belay, Amirshayan Haghipour, Pierluigi Salvo Rossi

entry.summary: The paper proposes Multi-Episode Prototypical Networks, which aggregate prototypes from multiple disjoint support episodes and use their mean as the final class representative to reduce prototype variance in the very-low-shot regime. Evaluation is on the DeFACTO sensor dataset with five-way fault classification under injected bias, drift, spike and noise faults. It matters for industrial monitoring where labeled fault examples are scarce.

entry.title: Hierarchical Belief Modeling for Zero-Shot Opponent Adaptation in Partially Observable Multi-Agent Navigation

author.name: Kowei Shih, Lu Cheng, Zeyu Wang, Yeyun Xu, Kejian Tong

entry.summary: HORIZON is a hierarchical agent for Lux AI Season 3 that combines symmetry-aware perception, dual-memory belief tracking, relic-centric graph attention, information-gain exploration, and an opponent-conditioned policy mixture. It separates short-horizon control from cross-match meta-reasoning and is trained with PPO in a large-scale JAX simulator, explicitly inferring hidden game parameters and opponent style. Reported gains in match win rate suggest the belief-modeling recipe is effective for partial observability and best-of-five adaptation.

entry.title: Do LLMs Trust the Accuser or the Accusation? Measuring Belief Shifts in Werewolf

author.name: Yu-Yu Yang, Ti-Rong Wu, Hung Guei, Hsing-Yu Chen, I-Chen Wu

entry.summary: The authors build a Werewolf benchmark that measures how an observing LLM's suspicion beliefs change after annotated accusation and suspicion messages, rather than judging only final game outcomes. Across 40 open-weight configurations and 1,224 annotated messages, larger models distinguish wolves from villagers better from game history, yet accusations still strongly shift beliefs, making models suspicious of the accused and less suspicious of the accuser. The result highlights a social-susceptibility bias relevant to LLM evaluation and agent trust.

entry.title: Beyond Generation and Accuracy: Diagnosing and Enhancing Visual Chain-of-Thought for Geometry Problem Solving

author.name: Zhitong Dong, Jicai Pan, Yingguo Gao, Jingting Ding, Hao Chen, Jinjie Gu

entry.summary: The paper notes that evaluations of Visual Chain-of-Thought for geometry typically score generated diagrams and final answers separately, never checking whether intermediate visual aids are geometrically valid, actually used, or causally necessary. It introduces GeoVAD-Bench, a five-dimensional trajectory diagnosis covering perception, auxiliary construction quality, utilization, deductive reasoning, and final correctness, with controlled no-auxiliary comparisons. This gives a much sharper picture of where visual reasoning fails.

entry.title: SoulAuth: An Actor-native Identity Architecture and Rust Reference Implementation for Humans and Long-lived AI Actors

author.name: Kun Yuan, Harold Wang, Echo Li, Egusi Gui, Kiki Hu, Lucas Luo, Magnus Hu

entry.summary: SoulAuth asks where the canonical continuity boundary should sit for AI systems that persist across credentials, clients, sessions, and runtime instances. It argues for an ActorIdentity that is not replaced by accounts, credentials, sessions, or bindings, treating humans and long-lived AI actors as first-class identity subjects, and ships an open-source Rust reference implementation. The work sits between security engineering, agent infrastructure, and identity architecture.

entry.title: USPLIT-VQA: U-Shaped Split Learning for Visual Question Answering with Contribution-Aware Weighted Aggregation

author.name: Md Khalid Syfullah, Alvi Ataur Khalil

entry.summary: USPLIT-VQA proposes a U-shaped split learning framework for privacy-preserving visual question answering in which each client keeps the initial layers and the classification head while the server hosts the computationally heavy intermediate layers, so raw inputs and labels stay on-device. It also introduces Contribution-Aware Weighted Aggregation, a gradient-similarity-based client scoring mechanism for weighting updates. The work targets the tension between centralized training, which needs access to all data, and federated learning, which requires each client to host the full model.

entry.title: RF-VoID: Towards Bandwidth-Efficient Exterior Tile Void Detection via Narrowband Radio-Frequency Representation Learning

author.name: Xinyan Chen, Ruiqin Ma, Shunsuke Shoda, Changyu Zhou, Ryo Natsuaki, Akira Hirose, Jianfei Yang, Li Yi

entry.summary: The paper tackles detecting hidden debonding behind exterior ceramic tiles using millimeter-wave radar, where conventional range-profile reconstruction quality is limited by the available bandwidth that also drives cost and regulatory burden. Using a 4-40 GHz stepped-frequency system across twelve wall specimens with sub-millimeter air voids, it establishes the bandwidth-resolution bound, then proposes RF-VoID to decide directly on representation learning rather than full reconstruction. The core idea is trading bandwidth for computation in RF sensing.

entry.title: ResoSeg: Resonance Tagger using Transformer and Segment Model

author.name: Chunkai Li, Junhao Yin, Ke Li, Jingde Chen

entry.summary: ResoSeg is presented as the first application of segmentation to resonance tagging at the BESIII experiment, jointly performing particle-level segmentation and event-level classification in a single pass. It targets resonance-to-anything decays, demonstrated on eta_c reconstruction in a specific decay chain. The work matters as a domain-science application of deep learning that can reduce the need for channel-specific reconstruction algorithms in high-energy physics.

entry.title: Separating Engineering Reasoning from DEXPI Serialization in LLM-Based Greenfield Surface-Process Design: A Three-Case Study for Underground Gas Storage

author.name: Qingchuan Zhu, Shuyue Tong, Pengju Ren

entry.summary: This diagnostic study asks whether separating engineering reasoning from DEXPI standards serialization changes where failures occur when an LLM performs constrained greenfield surface-process design for underground gas storage. It compares direct DEXPI generation against an intermediate lightweight engineering representation across three cases, all run with a fixed snapshot of the Qwen3.8 Max (0902) model, which was released in early September 2026 and is an existing model rather than a new release. The finding matters for how practitioners should structure LLM pipelines for standards-heavy engineering deliverables.

entry.title: A Multi-Vehicle Dataset with Camera, LiDAR, and Radar Sensors and Scanned 3D Models for Custom Auto-Annotation using RTK-GNSS

author.name: Philipp Berthold, Bianca Forkel, Mirko Maehlisch

entry.summary: The authors introduce an autonomous driving dataset that goes beyond bounding boxes and segmentation by providing scanned 3D models of all vehicles together with pose and continuous kinematics from RTK-GNSS. This makes the full dynamic surrounding of the sensor vehicle known at any point in time, enabling user-defined reference formats and deeper evaluation of sensor measurement principles. It matters for perception benchmarking that requires ground truth about object geometry and motion rather than only labels.

entry.title: LLM-Enhanced Dual-Branch Learning for Large-Scale Multi-Label Text Classification

author.name: Hui Ye, Jing Zhang, Xiulong Yang, Rajshekhar Sunderraman

entry.summary: This paper introduces DualMLC, a dual-branch framework for large-scale multi-label text classification that runs each document through both an autoregressive decoder-only language model and a bidirectional encoder, with each branch keeping its own representation pathway. The goal is to better exploit the complementarity between heterogeneous language models, which the authors argue is underexplored in existing representation-based pipelines that rely mainly on a single primary encoder.

entry.title: DynSHAP: Towards Explainable Dynamic Survival Analysis

author.name: Nastasya Anokhina, Jonas J\"ur{\ss}, Pietro Li\`o

entry.summary: DynSHAP adapts SHAP explanation methods to dynamic survival analysis, where models consume longitudinal irregular patient data and output functional survival curves. It treats time-feature pairs as players in the Shapley game and adds a Temporal DynSHAP variant that models linear feature dependencies over time with conditional sampling.

entry.title: ASTRIL-MPC: Autonomous Traversal Framework of Articulated Tracked Robots with Language-Guided Neural-Kinematic MPC

author.name: Zhenfeng Gan, Yanbo Chen, Lirong Che, Junbo Tan, Xueqian Wang

entry.summary: ASTRIL-MPC is a language-guided neural kinematic model predictive control framework for articulated tracked robots used in urban search and rescue, where robot-terrain interaction is hybrid and discontinuous. A learned kinematics model predicts short-horizon state increments from height sequences and trajectories, NMPC plans with strict feasibility constraints, and an LLM proposes bounded updates to selected cost weights.

entry.title: Fundamental Dynamical Units for Physics-Informed Structural Inference from Perturbation Time-Series in Networked Systems

author.name: Nima Nouri

entry.summary: The paper addresses recovering signed interaction structure in networked dynamical systems from perturbation time-series, a problem complicated by combinatorial architecture space, causal attribution ambiguity, and state-dependent dynamics. It introduces Fundamental Dynamical Units, signed three-node interaction patterns as composable primitives that turn the hypothesis space into a finite, tractable set for structural inference.

entry.title: QTrans: A Quantum Transformer for Sentiment Classification

author.name: Ren-Xin Zhao, Xinjie Huang, Yahong Liu, Maoyu Ye, Jinjing Shi, Shi Wang, Yaonan Wang

entry.summary: QTrans builds query, key, and value features with parameterized quantum circuits and derives attention coefficients from Gaussian distances between quantum measurements, integrating a quantum feed-forward network, residual connections, and layer normalization in an end-to-end trainable hybrid model. It targets small-scale binary sentiment classification where negation and contrastive shifts create non-linear sentiment coupling.

entry.title: Toward Reliable Railway-Bogie Response Prediction Using Multifidelity TDNN and Physics-Informed Residual Learning

author.name: Gyeolhee Lee, Moosun Kim, Taewook Kwon, Jaehun Kim, Dongjin Lee

entry.summary: The paper presents a multifidelity method for correcting railway bogie response predictions, treating multibody simulation histories as low-fidelity data and roller-rig measurements as high-fidelity evidence. It combines experiment-anchored fidelity assignment with physics-informed discrepancy learning across multichannel response histories using a time-delay neural network.

entry.title: Physics-Guided Synthetic High-Frequency Ultrasound Generation for Skin Layer Segmentation

author.name: Junkyung ju, Kyungho Yoon, Minwoo Shin

entry.summary: This work proposes a physics-guided framework for generating synthetic high-frequency ultrasound images to enable skin layer segmentation where dense annotations are scarce. It constructs multilayer acoustic skin phantoms with layer-dependent acoustic properties and uses k-Wave simulation to produce paired synthetic images, dense layer masks, and simulated data covering deeper structures such as dermis, subcutaneous tissue, fascia, and muscle.

entry.title: A Large-Scale AIS Dataset from Finnish Water

author.name: Debayan Bhattacharya, Ikram Ul Haq, Carlos Pichardo Vicencio, Sebastien Lafond

entry.summary: This paper curates and catalogs existing AIS maritime datasets and releases a new collection from Finnish waters in the Baltic Sea containing roughly 229 million data points. The dataset captures a strategically and physically distinctive region with intercontinental cargo routes, military activity, and seasonal ice. It is intended as a resource for studying vessel behavior and maritime activity.

entry.title: On Identifying Adversarial Intent Injection in AI-Native 6G Networks

author.name: Nilesh Chakraborty, Petar Djukic, Burak Kantarci

entry.summary: The paper defines a fine-grained threat model for adversarial intent injection in AI-native 6G intent-based networking, where malicious policies are disguised inside benign intent flows and may be hard to detect when adversaries operate stealthily. It investigates four injection strategies including stealth mode, random distribution, increasing frequency, and a further variant. The work matters because intent abstraction in AI-native networks expands the attack surface for policy-level manipulation.

entry.title: Same Encoder, Different Winner: A Paired-View Framework for Cell Painting Encoder Evaluation

author.name: Tim Treis, Nikita Moshkov, Johan Fredin Haslum, Shantanu Singh, Fabian J. Theis

entry.summary: The paper introduces CP-BG-Bench, a paired-view evaluation framework that fixes the central cell across four matched views, raw crop, segmented, and density-augmented variants, to test how surrounding pixels affect encoder rankings. Instantiating it on three datasets and three encoders under four community-standard protocols, the authors find that different protocols rank the same encoders systematically differently. This matters because single-protocol leaderboards for Cell Painting encoders can be misleading.

entry.title: VertexCBF: Improving Neural Control Barrier Functions via Vertex-Restricted Control Search

author.name: Bojan Deraji\'c, Sebastian Bernhard, Wolfgang H\"onig

entry.summary: VertexCBF learns neural control barrier functions in a scalable, systematic, and explainable way by approximating the stationary Hamilton-Jacobi value function with a network trained through physics-informed and sparsely supervised learning. By exploiting control-affine dynamics and a convex polytope control set, the Hamiltonian is maximized at vertices of the polytope, which restricts and simplifies the control search. The result is less conservative safe sets and better scalability than prior neural CBF design methods, which is important as autonomous robot deployments grow.

entry.title: Very Exciting: Zero-Shot Model Predictive Control of Buildings via Excitation-Based Generalized Transfer Learning Models

author.name: Fabian Raisch, Felix Koch, Zack Xuereb Conti, Christoph Goebel, Benjamin Tischler

entry.summary: This paper studies transfer learning for building energy modeling, where a model pretrained on data from multiple source buildings is reused to control a new target building without collecting building-specific data. Unlike prior work that only measures prediction accuracy, the authors embed the transferred model in a model predictive control loop and evaluate actual control performance, adding excitation-based inputs to improve zero-shot generalization.

entry.title: Quantifying Consonant Contributions to Word Intelligibility via Acoustic Masking

author.name: Eunjung Yeo, Kwanghee Choi, Krupaben Kothadia, Visar Berisha, Julie M. Liss, David R. Mortensen, David Harwath

entry.summary: The paper introduces a scalable automatic method for measuring how much each consonant contributes to word intelligibility, replacing expensive perceptual studies. It silences one consonant at a time in isolated words and measures the resulting misrecognition rate of an ASR model as a contribution score, with implications for prioritizing speech therapy targets.

entry.title: The House with a Million Windows: Interactive Fiction for Narrative Restorying

author.name: Cody Kommers, Sarah G Immel, Drew Hemment, Mina Lee

entry.summary: The authors present an LLM-based interactive fiction system, The House with a Million Windows, built on the psychological restorying intervention, in which users tell a personal story and then encounter LLM-generated windows reframing it in different literary styles. Empirical evidence indicates the system increases users' sense of narrative identity, positioning it as a counterweight to meaning-flattening AI-assisted writing.

entry.title: EgoMaize: A First-Person Maize Instance Segmentation Benchmark under Severe Field Occlusion

author.name: Jiayi Li, Zihan Zhang, Erhankang Yan, Yitian Chen, Yuze Li, Chengzhang Ding, Jianxin Cao

entry.summary: EgoMaize is a compact benchmark for first-person maize instance segmentation from close-range field images, where stems, leaves, tassels, and neighboring plants are elongated, repetitive, and heavily occluded. The authors address ownership-consistent masks and plant-owned stem/tassel cues, arguing that visible-only labels fragment plants while full-amodal labels can overreach.

entry.title: Partition-Invariant Tuning for 3D Scene Understanding

author.name: Hongqiang Lin, Tianle Wang, Shuiwang Li, Dongxu Zhang, Yiding Sun, Zihao Guo, Dongfu Yin

entry.summary: PointPiT addresses scene-level point cloud understanding with a partition-invariant parameter-efficient tuning framework, noting that existing PEFT methods are object-level and ignore serialization-induced partition variations in large scenes. A Scene-aware Structural Adapter integrates local geometry with global scene context to reduce partition-induced representation drift while tuning a pretrained 3D foundation model cheaply. It matters for scalable adaptation of 3D foundation models to large scenes.

entry.title: ChitraMiti: Benchmarking Visual Grounding and Modality Reliance in Bengali Geometric Reasoning

author.name: Khan Raiyan Ibne Reza, Sanjana Aktar Maria, Sumaiya Tabassum Nimi, Md Adnan Arefeen

entry.summary: The authors release ChitraMiti-12.8k, a synthetic benchmark of nearly 13,000 Bengali planar geometry problems with structured attribute descriptions, plus NCTB-500, 500 diagrams extracted from Bengali textbooks. Using a three-phase protocol that isolates diagram-only, diagram-plus-description and description-only inputs, they find that description-only performance matches diagram-plus-description across five VLMs, indicating models lean on text rather than genuinely reading diagrams. It matters as evidence of weak visual grounding in multimodal math reasoning for low-resource languages.

entry.title: Beyond Ambiguous Visual Cues: Studying Physiological Disruptions and Cross-Modal Inconsistencies in Deepfake Videos

author.name: Chenxi Yang, Yassine Ouzar, Larbi Boubchir

entry.summary: This work builds high-fidelity deepfake manipulations on real rPPG datasets, COHFACE and UBFC-rPPG, to study how forgeries simultaneously disrupt natural physiological signals and facial behavior, addressing the lack of physiological ground truth in existing benchmarks. It then proposes a bidirectional co-attention detector that jointly models rPPG and facial behavior tokens rather than relying on late fusion or rPPG alone. It matters for more robust and physiologically grounded deepfake detection.

entry.title: GRACE: Adaptive Concept Erasure with Geometry-Guided Retention in Diffusion Models

author.name: Qinghui Gong, Yihuai Liang, Yuanlun Xie, Deepak Kumar Jain, Vitomir \v{S}truc, Zhengchun Zhou

entry.summary: GRACE is a structured concept-erasure framework for text-to-image diffusion models that estimates a semantically weighted sensitive subspace to constrain parameter updates, enabling localized and selective intervention rather than over-intervention and semantic drift. It avoids reliance on manually crafted counterfactual supervision such as surrogate prompts, reducing data construction cost for scaling to new concepts. It matters for safety and compliance in generative image models.

entry.title: Learning Sign Language Recognition under Label Noise: A Study of Noise-Robust Losses for Isolated and Continuous Settings

author.name: Akihisa Shitara, Yoichi Ochiai

entry.summary: This study applies symmetric and generalized cross entropy, robust loss alternatives to standard cross entropy, to the single-label classifiers used in isolated and continuous sign language recognition. It addresses annotation noise from stylistic variation in isolated recognition and from pseudo-labeling in continuous recognition, testing on ASL Citizen across three backbones. It matters because label noise is a persistent, under-acknowledged problem in sign language datasets.

entry.title: Signed Sensitivity of Expected Hitting Time to Mutation Rate in the (1+1) EA: Per-State Sign Theorems and Verifiable Certificates for Non-Lumpable Families

author.name: RenKai Wang

entry.summary: This theory paper studies how the expected hitting time of the (1+1) evolutionary algorithm with standard bit mutation responds to changes in the mutation rate, arguing that the usual unsigned total-influence form of the Margulis-Russo formula is inapplicable because the improvement event is not monotone in the mutation mask; the correct quantity is a signed endpoint difference. It then constructs an exact three-dimensional separation in which two fitness functions share the same one-step success-rate curve yet have different expected hitting times, proving that simple success-rate summaries cannot determine runtime. The work offers per-state sign theorems and verifiable certificates aimed at non-lumpable families, contributing rigorous tools for runtime analysis rather than a new algorithm.

entry.title: A Physics-Based Closed-Loop Robotic Bioprinting Framework Towards Volumetric Muscle Loss Treatment

author.name: Omid Rezayof, Jerin T. Andrews, Ehsan Zobeidi, Ali Ghasemkhani, Meenakshi Kamaraj, Maryam Tilton, Johnson V. John, Farshid Alambeigi

entry.summary: The paper develops a closed-loop robotic bioprinting and Direct Ink Writing system for treating volumetric muscle loss, aiming to avoid time- and material-intensive design-of-experiments or large curated datasets. A 3D point cloud camera plus autonomous vision algorithms quantitatively evaluate printed constructs in near real time, and this evaluation feeds a controller that adapts printing parameters on the fly.

entry.title: Communication-Constrained Multi-Robot Exploration With Adaptive Communication Windows

author.name: Ben Rossano, Jaein Lim, Jonathan P. How

entry.summary: MACE is a decentralized exploration framework for multi-robot teams facing intermittent communication, where robots must weigh the benefit of information sharing against the cost of diverting from exploration to establish contact. At scheduled windows, robots estimate the cost of reaching previously identified communication locations and frame the decision as a variant of the Vehicle Orienteering Problem to evaluate routes.

entry.title: ProClosure: Hierarchical Room-Object Assignment using Progressive Boundary Closure from Monocular Video

author.name: Vinoth Kumar Muthuraj, Soumyadeep Banik, Kushal Sharma, Hardik Jain

entry.summary: ProClosure recovers the room layer of a 3D scene graph from monocular RGB video using Progressive Boundary Closure: SLAM, open-vocabulary segmentation, and object tracking supply a structural point cloud, which is rasterized into a top-down map, rooms are recovered from the map, and each object is assigned to the room containing most of its extent. The key difficulty addressed is that walls are only observed where the camera looked, so boundary gaps are ambiguous between doorways and unobserved walls. It matters for embodied agents that must fetch objects by room name.

entry.title: Improving Imitation Learning Efficiency for Manipulation through Geometric Prior Pretraining

author.name: Shogo Iwakata, Tomohiro Motoda, Ryosuke Yamada, Koshi Makihara, Ryoichi Nakajo, Keitaro Tanaka, Masaki Murooka, Roman Mykhailyshyn, Hirokatsu Kataoka, Shigeo Morishima, Yukiyasu Domae

entry.summary: This study asks what useful prior can be provided to a manipulation policy at negligible cost before task-specific data collection, and constructs an automatically generated geometric visual pretraining dataset in which each scene contains only a plane, an object, and a hand. Pretraining on these simple geometric scenes is intended to reduce the number of demonstrations and retraining cycles needed for a new task. It matters as a cheap alternative to large-scale robot-data pretraining and per-task augmentation pipelines.

entry.title: Teleoperated Humans

author.name: jefftk

entry.summary: The post argues that near-term AI impact on physical, non-computer work will come less from robots and more from software directing humans, analogous to GPS telling a driver where to go. It suggests strong economic incentives and fewer legal/social barriers make this teleoperation of people a plausible driver of rapid real-world change.

entry.title: What an odour descriptor corpus can and cannot measure: valence, attenuation, and the ceiling of the public record

author.name: Stylianos Kampakis, Fabio Rovai

entry.summary: The authors audit four public machine-olfaction descriptor corpora from the Pyrfume collection to test whether shared odour words actually measure the same thing across sources. Using molecule-conditioned McNemar tests and tetrachoric agreement, they find substantial heterogeneous disagreement across corpora, meaning simple offset correction cannot fix pooling. The work establishes a methodological ceiling for what current pooled smell datasets can and cannot support.

entry.title: Investigating Temporal Motion Features for Pose-to-Text Indian Sign Language Translation

author.name: Manav Dhamecha, Praveen Kumar Chandaliya, Pruthwik Mishra

entry.summary: This work studies the effect of pretrained T5 scale and explicit motion features on pose-to-text Indian Sign Language translation for the WSLP 2026 Shared Task. Pose sequences are projected into T5's embedding space via a lightweight pose encoder, and a motion-augmented variant adds frame-to-frame pose differences, comparing T5-small, base, and large on validation and test sets.

entry.title: HSI-Road Relabeled: Surface-Aware Road-Scene Segmentation

author.name: Imad Ali Shah, Imran Mehmood, Enda Ward, Martin Glavin, Edward Jones, Brian Deegan

entry.summary: This paper adds a manually labeled six-class surface taxonomy (background, asphalt, concrete, dirt, water, grass) plus an RGB-to-NIR registration pipeline to the HSI-Road dataset. Six semantic segmentation models are compared under four input configurations, including original and registered RGB, NIR, and stacked RGBN, quantifying resolution and modality effects per class.

entry.title: A Multimodal Explainable Deep Learning Framework for Alzheimer's Disease Diagnosis using 3D Magnetic Resonance Imaging and Clinical Data

author.name: Yusuf Brima, Marcellin Atemkeng, Lakshmana Rao Namamula, Antoine Vacavant

entry.summary: The authors build an explainable multimodal framework combining a 3D CNN over T1-weighted MRI with a feedforward network over harmonized clinical and demographic variables, evaluated on three-way and pairwise Alzheimer's diagnostic tasks across ADNI and an independent cohort. It systematically examines how explanations behave across modalities, fusion strategies and cohorts. It matters for clinical trust and deployment of multimodal diagnostics in dementia care.

entry.title: PATH: Continuous Target Sensing among Autonomous Cooperative Drones

author.name: Heegyeong Kim, Alice James, Avishkar Seth, Endrowednes Kuantama, Jane Williamson, Yimeng Feng, Richard Han

entry.summary: PATH addresses continuous target tracking by UAV teams whose flight endurance is limited, requiring the tracking responsibility to be handed off between cooperating drones. Because the receiving drone sees a different viewpoint, scale, and appearance than the sender, the framework uses platform-agnostic, geometry-assisted sensing and verification rather than relying on global localization or purely appearance-based cross-view association, with the sender reconstructing the tracked target geometry to guide handoff.

entry.title: Before the Tipping Point: Force-Guided Active Perception for Shape-Agnostic Estimation of 3D Centers of Mass

author.name: Steven M. Hyland, Jing Xiao, Cagdas D. Onal

entry.summary: The paper presents a force-based method that estimates an unknown object's center-of-mass height and mass from a single sub-critical tipping experiment, where the robot applies a quasistatic elevated push-and-retract motion and identifies parameters from force-angle measurements and the resulting object trajectory. The push-retract cycle is designed to mitigate frictional bias and enable generalized fitting. It matters for manipulation planning when grasping is infeasible, geometry is irregular, or mass distribution is uneven.

entry.title: Automated Detection and Structuring of Social Tipping Point Evidence in Climate related Documents: A Modular AI Framework

author.name: Kavindu Perera, Mohammad Abaeiani, Ekaterina Gilman, Lauri Loven, Mourad Oussalah, Tassos Kanellos, Beatrice Gobbo, Dante Adami, Nicol\`o Ferriani, Maximiliano Romero, Pierre Rossel, Marc Bonazountas, Christina Deligianni, Nikos Xyderis, Artur Bogucki, Lampros Argyriou, Prasasthy Balasubramanian

entry.summary: This paper presents an open, modular transformer-based framework that detects and structures evidence about social tipping points, the thresholds at which small changes trigger rapid self-reinforcing change in social systems, at the passage level rather than the whole-document level. It argues that climate literature is growing faster than review teams can read, and that evidence for such shifts typically occupies only one or two paragraphs, which existing topic-level or claim-level text mining misses. The framework combines five components into an end-to-end pipeline.

entry.title: Write on Paper and Get the Online Digital Trace:\newline A New Era for Handwriting

author.name: Florent Imbert, Yann Soullard, Eric Anquetil, Tanja Harbaum, Alexey Serdyuk, Fabian Kress, Tim Hamann, Peter Kampf

entry.summary: This paper describes a system that reconstructs the digital trace of ordinary pen-on-paper writing without special paper, stylus, or EMR tablet, combining a digital pen, AI trajectory-reconstruction algorithms, and adaptive AI techniques. The goal is to preserve the haptics and zero-latency feel of paper while producing an accurate online handwriting trace without any external reference system.

entry.title: Learning Interaction Kernels from Collective Steady States

author.name: Baoli Hao, Mauro Maggioni, Ming Zhong

entry.summary: The authors propose a procedure for system identification in interacting particle systems using only single-snapshot observations of collective behavior, rather than full trajectories. Because this is a fundamentally ill-posed inverse problem, they regularize using the empirical distribution of observed configurations drawn from different unobserved initial conditions. Experiments across steady-state and quasi-stationary models show stable, accurate recovery of the underlying interaction kernels.

entry.title: BRIDGE-EEG: Bridging Self-Supervised Pretraining and Efficient Deployment for Cross-Dataset EEG Classification

author.name: Meghna Roy Chowdhury, Chengwei Zhou, Haotian Yu, Gourav Datta, Shreyas Sen

entry.summary: BRIDGE-EEG is an efficient multi-task EEG classification pipeline that keeps the benefits of large-scale pretraining while shrinking model size for edge and wearable deployment. It maps heterogeneous recordings with differing channel counts, montages, and sampling rates into a device-agnostic 62-channel time-frequency representation, and pretrains an SE-ResNet18 teacher with SimCLR on unlabeled EEG from five heterogeneous datasets. The work targets transferable yet deployable EEG analysis for constrained hardware.

entry.title: Semantically Aligned Gradient-Driven Context-Preserving Image Editing

author.name: Chiranjeev Chiranjeev, Muskan Dosi, Mayank Vatsa, Richa Singh

entry.summary: IABEdit targets a blind spot in instruction-guided image editing: editors are never trained to semantically verify that outputs satisfy the instruction, since supervision stops at reconstruction and text conditioning, producing incomplete edits and spatial spillover. The method embeds differentiable semantic verification in training by having a frozen VLM extract spatially aware descriptors from the ground-truth edit and a trainable aligner reproduce them, with the residual serving as a gradient signal at no inference cost. It matters for more faithful, well-localized generative editing.

entry.title: Battery-Aware Predictive Trajectory Planning and Control for Multirotors Under Disturbances

author.name: Krishna Bhavithavya Kidambi

entry.summary: This paper presents a trajectory planning and control framework for multirotors that evaluates candidate trajectories through closed-loop vehicle, motor, and battery propagation, letting disturbances, electrical energy use, battery state evolution, and terminal-voltage-dependent actuator limits influence the plan. A reduced-order battery model is benchmarked against an independent Simscape equivalent-circuit reference with sub-one-percent power NRMSE and cumulative energy error, and the chosen trajectory reduces electrical energy in a 150-second, 640-meter mission with three disturbance regions.

entry.title: High-Fidelity Multi-Body Simulator for Autonomous Racing

author.name: Nicola Musiu, Francesco Iacovacci, Fausto Lupo, Matteo Pini, Giovanni Scapicchi, Francesco Moretti, Eugenio Mascaro, Pietro Musso, Ayoub Raji, Marko Bertogna, Vincenzo Maria Arricale, Angelo Lo Sapio, Alessandro Piccarelli, Garron Fish

entry.summary: This paper describes a custom high-fidelity vehicle dynamics simulation environment for testing autonomous racing software, with a Dymola-built multi-body digital twin, a 3D road surface using the Curved Regular Grid standard including elevation and curbs, and export as a Functional Mock-up Unit integrated into a software-in-the-loop simulator with C++ interfaces to the racing stack. Calibration against experimental data and a validation study support fidelity claims. It matters as infrastructure for safely validating limit-handling autonomous racing controllers.

entry.title: Niching Agents in The Core

author.name: Gary B. Parker, Jim O'Connor, John Asaro

entry.summary: This work extends The Core, a competitive co-evolution algorithm that evolves autonomous agent controllers through local tournament selection, crossover and mutation without a traditional fitness function. The authors niche agents to specific sub-environments of the original Xpilot test environment and compare them against agents niched to the full system and to other sub-environments. The results show niched agents succeed over their more general counterparts.

entry.title: Beyond Vector Similarity: Hierarchical Context-Aware Graph RAG vs Standard RAG in Enterprise Code Migration

author.name: Nilesh Jaiswal, Aniket Agrawal, Arjit Shukla, Divya Malhotra, Saurabh Garg, Suchit Puri, Suddhasatwa Bhaumik

entry.summary: The paper argues standard vector RAG breaks inheritance chains by retrieving isolated chunks, causing high compilation failure rates in LLM-driven legacy-to-microservice code translation. It introduces a Hierarchical Context-Resident Graph pipeline that extracts ASTs with tree-sitter, stores architectural edges in a Spanner property graph, and serializes the structure into a Gemini context cache for parent-first translation. The evaluation shift toward topological correctness rather than text similarity is the main methodological point.

entry.title: Information Specialization and Constrained Synthesis in Multi-Agent LLM Forecasting: A Prospective Live-Study of the 2026 FIFA World Cup

author.name: Julian Varghese, Lucas Bickmann, Sarah Sandmann

entry.summary: This live prospective study holds a frontier foundation model constant and assigns two specialist forecasting agents contrasting roles, one focused on structured performance statistics and one on news such as injuries, tactics, and press conferences, over the final 56 matches of the 2026 World Cup. A separate critic reviews their forecasts before a meta-agent combines them. The design probes whether role specialization produces genuinely distinct forecasts and whether synthesis improves utility.

entry.title: Assessment of Non-Institutional AI Tool Usage Among Clinicians

author.name: Sarah Pungitore, Jarrod Mosier

entry.summary: This descriptive survey of clinicians at the University of Arizona College of Medicine-Tucson and Banner University Medical Center-Tucson, fielded May 20 to June 26, 2026, examines use of generative AI tools that are not provided, managed, or governed by the healthcare institution. It documents which tool categories clinicians use and how often for work-related tasks, raising privacy, security, accuracy, and clinician-AI interaction concerns. The finding of widespread ungoverned use is the main contribution.

entry.title: MAIA: Multi-Agent Intent Articulation for Requirement Discovery in Art Commissions

author.name: Yu-Chao Wang, Yanhong Lu, Yingjie Victor Chen, Tim McGraw

entry.summary: MAIA is a multi-agent system that helps laypeople articulate visual intent during the requirement-discovery stage of bespoke art commissions, using Socratic inquiry under a verification-over-invention rule to produce a text-only brief of visual terms the user confirms. The authors frame the problem as an articulation bottleneck that precedes any artist or image generator. A within-subjects study with 16 participants evaluates full versus reduced system configurations.

entry.title: 3D Digital Twin Visualization of Multiclass GRF-Based Gait Disorder Classification

author.name: Nayoung Son, Minwoo Shin

entry.summary: The paper builds an integrated framework that classifies healthy gait versus multiple musculoskeletal impairment groups from bilateral ground reaction force and center-of-pressure signals, standardized per training statistics. Reported accuracy is 99.00 percent on validation and 90.07 percent on test under a session-level split, with class-specific epsilon-LRP identifying which signal components and stance phases drive each decision. Predictions and processed signals are synchronized in a Blender-based 3D visualization for interpretable digital-twin presentation.

entry.title: Unified CT and MRI Pancreas Segmentation for Label-Efficient Cross-Modality Subregion Transfer

author.name: Ziliang Hong, Hongyi Pan, Halil Ertugrul Aktas, Andrea Bejar, Elif Keles, Frank H. Miller, Michael B. Wallace, Rajesh N. Keswani, Gorkem Durak, Ulas Bagci

entry.summary: This work develops a unified 3D pancreas segmentation framework using domain-adversarial learning across 4,604 heterogeneous CT and MRI scans, with a shared nnU-Net encoder-decoder and a latent domain discriminator aligning CT and MRI features. The learned encoder is then transferred to pancreatic head-body-tail subregion segmentation using only limited MRI subregion annotations.

entry.title: Fed-Equilibrium Framework for Topological Pareto Control in Robust and Fair Clinical Federated Learning

author.name: Ting Xu, Henry Leung

entry.summary: Fed-Equilibrium tackles knowledge dominance in multi-center clinical federated learning, where large data hubs overwhelm minority community nodes whose distinct clinical patterns get treated as outliers. It uses a two-stage gradient control cascade, starting with cosine-similarity-based directional consistency for geometric quality assurance, to move from simple defense toward a topological equilibrium balancing robustness and fairness.

entry.title: SIFPBPNet: A Dual-Path Network for Wearable and Cuffless Blood Pressure Estimation via Individualized Steady-state Representation

author.name: Shuailong Tang, Xiaoyu Li, Donglin Xie, Wei Chen, Guangpu Zhu, Yelei Li, Yali Zheng

entry.summary: SIFPBPNet is a dual-path architecture for cuffless blood pressure estimation from photoplethysmography that separates steady-state from instantaneous features. A steady-state path uses a graph attention network to extract individual-specific long-term characteristics from multi-day data, addressing population heterogeneity and the one-to-many mapping problem where similar waveforms correspond to different blood pressures.

entry.title: Towards Sustainable Hydrogen Systems: Supply Chain Optimization with Model Predictive Control and Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Mahammad Valiyev

entry.summary: This paper examines control strategies for a renewable-powered hydrogen supply chain, a setting complicated by renewable generation variability, electricity price swings, uncertain demand, and electrolyzer and storage constraints. It compares four control approaches, including model predictive control and reinforcement learning, evaluating how well each balances economic performance, reliability, and sustainability. The goal is to guide operational strategy as hydrogen infrastructure moves toward commercial deployment.

entry.title: Direct Topology Tracking in Continuous Implicit Models

author.name: Guanqun Ma, David Lenz, Kaiyuan Tang, Hanqi Guo, Chaoli Wang, Tom Peterka, Bei Wang

entry.summary: The authors present a framework for tracking topological features directly inside continuous implicit models such as implicit neural representations and multivariate functional approximations, which represent scientific data without discrete grid resolution limits. By querying the model and its derivatives, the method follows the evolution of critical points without resampling onto a grid. This avoids discretization artifacts and enables faithful feature tracking in compact, differentiable representations.

entry.title: OphBiWSSD: Scaling Temporal Action Localization in Ophthalmic Surgeries with Bidirectional Weight-tied State Space Duality

author.name: Yang Liu, Qionghong Ma, Joongwon Chae, Lihui Luo, Yibing Shen, Yulin Zhuo, Yingting Zhu, Jiashu Chang, Xiaoyun Zhong, Dongmei Yu, Peter E. Lobie, Peiwu Qin, Chengming Yang

entry.summary: OphBiWSSD reformulates temporal action localization for high-frequency ophthalmic surgery video using a bidirectional, weight-tied selective scan that leverages state space duality to capture long-range non-causal procedural context. The design avoids aggressive temporal downsampling that hurts fine-grained action boundary detection. It matters for surgical AI and for showing state-space models can scale to fine-grained medical temporal tasks where attention is computationally prohibitive.

entry.title: One Skill Does Not Fit All: Automatic Discovery and Taxonomy-Guided Routing of Frame-Selection Skills for Long-Video Question Answering

author.name: Jian Hu, Zixu Cheng, Da Li, Wei Li, Ziquan Liu, Shaogang Gong

entry.summary: AutoSkill automatically discovers executable frame-selection skills for long-video QA, with LLM agents iteratively proposing, implementing, evaluating and refining candidate skills from a small labeled pool, then routing them by question taxonomy. The premise is that no single frame-selection strategy suits all question types, which their analysis supports across categories and benchmarks. It matters for training-free, evidence-efficient video understanding at hour scale.

entry.title: Detecting and Explaining Fake News Short Videos with Multimodal Content and Real-World Evidence

author.name: Yifeng Luo, Yupeng Li, Ming Tang, Jianxiong Guo, Liang Lan

entry.summary: NVKE-CEI is a unified system for fake news video detection and explanation that combines a chronological keyframe extraction method with a framework using both multimodal content and retrieved real-world evidence. It targets two weaknesses of prior work, frame selection that misses veracity-relevant cues and pipelines that neglect either multimodal understanding or evidence retrieval. It matters for trustworthy information ecosystems on short-video platforms.

entry.title: Uncertainty-Aware Conflict Detection Against Operator-Conditioned Weather Hazards

author.name: Balram Kandoria, Seulki Kim, Aryaman Singh Samyal

entry.summary: The paper presents a pre-flight conflict detection framework for Advanced Air Mobility that couples uncertainty-conditioned trajectory prediction with polyhedral representations of weather hazards. It derives closed-form uncertainty estimates by combining NURBS-based kinematic trajectory generation with Kalman filter covariance propagation, using a sigmoid-blended measurement noise model inspired by the Light Propagation Algorithm to capture uncertainty reduction.

entry.title: Driving Context-guided Model Predictive Planning and Control for Autonomous Car Racing at the Limit and Beyond

author.name: Ayoub Raji, Federico Sacco, Nicola Musiu, Marko Bertogna

entry.summary: This work presents a model predictive planning and control pipeline for autonomous racing that adapts to driving contexts such as overtaking, nominal driving, and countersteering, using a Cost Blending state machine to identify contexts and select predefined cost weights. Planning and control share the same formulation and model, differing in horizon, rate, tuning, and open-loop versus closed-loop operation. It is validated on the fully autonomous open-wheel racecar platform, making it relevant to high-performance vehicle control beyond normal driving envelopes.

entry.title: From Transportation to Manipulation: Enabling Grasping in Magnetic Robotics

author.name: Lara Bergmann, Noah Greis, Cedric Grothues, Lisa-Marie Weigelt, Klaus Neumann

entry.summary: The paper introduces the Gripper MagBot, a low-cost parallel 6-DoF manipulator with an integrated 1-DoF gripper that mechanically couples three magnetic levitation movers, enabling grasping and manipulation directly on MagLev systems instead of relying on separate industrial arms. Two operating configurations, a default and a single-track mode, are supported for flexible in-machine material flow. It matters for high-mix, low-volume manufacturing where reconfigurable transport and manipulation are both needed.

entry.title: Unified Agentic Video Editing Across Levels of Complexity and Creativity

author.name: Surabhi S. Nath, Kim Ferres, Milan Petrovi\'c, Lion Schulz

entry.summary: This work reports methods for agentic tooling that automates video editing across three tasks of increasing editorial ambition: scene previews, video summaries, and cinematic trailers. The authors evaluate the resulting outputs and discuss what their results imply for automation and human agency in creative production. It is a short, exploratory treatment of agentic creativity rather than a deep architecture paper.

entry.title: LettuceVisSim: A Simulator That Generates Lettuce Image Time-series for Vision-Based Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Ziye Zhu, Bert van 't Ooster, Congcong Sun, Eldert van Henten, Sjoerd Boersma

entry.summary: LettuceVisSim is a lettuce growth simulator that produces labelled time-series crop images to relieve the shortage of annotated data for vision-based reinforcement learning in controlled environment agriculture. It combines a process-based model of shoot dry weight dynamics, a canopy layout algorithm that derives canopy representations from dry weight, and a Unity rendering engine for image generation. Validation shows the process model reproduces dry weight dynamics under variable plant density with an R-squared of 0.84, among five supporting findings.

entry.title: A Differentially Private Federated Proximal Optimization Framework for Customer Churn Prediction in Heterogeneous Federated Telecom Networks

author.name: Joydeb Kumar Sana, Subrata Chakraborty, M M Manjurul Islam

entry.summary: This paper addresses telecom customer churn prediction with a differentially private federated proximal optimization framework that avoids centralizing customer data and mitigates non-IID heterogeneity across operators. It also targets privacy attacks on trained models, combining federated learning with differential privacy for regulatory-compliant collaboration.

entry.title: Parallel Training Using a CNN-DNN Architecture for Accelerated Development of Diagnostic Models

author.name: Janine Weber-Hamacher, Astha Jaiswal, Philipp Fervers, Dorotya M\'or\'e, Athanasios Giannakis, Ricarda Fischbach, Andreas Michael Bucher, Rahil Shahzad, Jonathan Kottlors, Thorsten Persigehl, Axel Klawonn

entry.summary: This retrospective study uses a hybrid CNN-DNN model based on image decomposition and localization to enable parallel and efficient training of diagnostic models on 300 CT scans from COVID-19 and non-COVID pneumonia patients across three German centers. It trains 156 models across three architectures to capture features at different levels for patient-level classification. It matters mainly as a case study in accelerating model development when data grows dynamically, such as during a pandemic.

entry.title: Trajectory Bundle Method in SE(3) for Black-Box Fixed-Wing Aircraft Trajectory Optimization

author.name: Matthew D. Osburn, Cameron K. Peterson, John L. Salmon

entry.summary: This paper formulates the Trajectory Bundle Method for motion planning implicitly on the special Euclidean group SE(3), targeting rigid-body trajectory optimization when dynamics are available only as black-box computations without derivatives.
