entry.summary: Overpainting is an image editing operation using a trimap to specify pixels that must, may, or must not be edited, giving both precise and loose spatial control with awareness of previous content. It adapts a pretrained editing diffusion model via joint attention and low-rank adaptation, with an automated training data generation pipeline.

entry.title: CEM-TUDASR: Computationally efficient multi-modality transformer based unsupervised domain adaptive super-resolution approach

author.name: Anjali Sarvaiya, Jay Kadel, Kishor Upla, Kiran Raja

entry.summary: Proposes a Transformer-based unsupervised super-resolution framework for wireless capsule endoscopy images that avoids paired low/high-resolution training data by using a domain-adaptive degradation network to synthesize realistic WCE-like degradations from conventional endoscopy images. It matters because low-resolution endoscopic imagery limits diagnosis, and paired data does not exist in this modality.

entry.title: GRIPNet: Gaussian Radial Intensity Prior Guided Architecture for Pulmonary Nodule Detection in CT

author.name: Haojie Yang, Ran Su

entry.summary: Shows that pulmonary nodule intensity follows a highly regular Gaussian radial profile (validated on 18,218 lesions across three benchmarks) and designs an architecture with radial priors to improve detection of sub-6mm nodules. Grounds the network design in imaging physics rather than treating nodules as generic objects.

entry.title: MC-DeTra: Motion-Consistent Joint Object Detection and Socially-Aware Trajectory Forecasting in Bird's-Eye-View Images

author.name: Vladislav Diuzhev, Dmitry Yudin

entry.summary: This work releases an open reimplementation of DeTra, the strongest unified detection-plus-trajectory-forecasting model for autonomous driving, and adds MC-DeTra motion-consistency mechanisms using annotation-derived auxiliary supervision on past motion and social traffic context. The open release fills a reproducibility gap since the original DeTra had no public implementation.

entry.title: Freehand Sketching for End-User Programming of Robot Swarms

author.name: Riwa Karam, Ian Kuo, Magnus Egerstedt

entry.summary: The paper introduces a sketch-to-swarm framework where non-expert users draw freehand geometries to specify robot swarm formations; the system extracts target points, builds a rigid formation graph, assigns robots, and runs distributed formation control with a guarantee against reflected formations. A 20-participant human study over 42 shapes evaluated usability.

entry.title: Aerodynamic Prior-Free Coordinated Trajectory Generation and Tracking Control for a Tail-Sitter UAV

author.name: Erchao Rong, Zihao Liu, Junning Liang, Jianguo Wang, Xiao Jie, Haoran Fu, Ziliang Chen, Ximin Lyu

entry.summary: This paper presents a trajectory generation and tracking control framework for tail-sitter UAVs that avoids requiring airframe-specific aerodynamic priors, using phase-specific modeling such as phi-theory-based differential flatness mapping for coordinated flight and simplified local models for predictive control. This matters because tail-sitters face highly nonlinear aerodynamics across hover and forward flight, and removing the need for per-airframe system identification makes the approach more generalizable and practical for new vehicles.

entry.title: What the Pro-Democracy Movement Knows About Quitting in Protest

author.name: Maxwell Love

entry.summary: Drawing on 15 years of pro-democracy organizing experience, the author applies empirical findings (Pinckney and Trilling, 2024) on defections during democratic backsliding to AI lab employees considering resignation. Key data points: insider noncooperation succeeded roughly twice as often as public speaking out, and quiet outreach moved insiders far more often than public protest.

entry.title: Categorical taboos are much better than threshold taboos: neuralese edition

author.name: Linch

entry.summary: A conceptual analysis of the ongoing debate about whether models communicate in neuralese, arguing that the definitional choice between a categorical standard (whether recurrence occurs outside natural language) and a threshold standard (a fixed count of opaque serial steps) drives much of the disagreement. The author argues the categorical definition is preferable for policy and monitoring purposes, while acknowledging that many technical experts favor threshold definitions as more causally relevant.

entry.title: Belief-State Engine: Augmenting LLMs for Principled Planning Under Partial Observability

author.name: Arnab Chattopadhayay, Debdipta Halder

entry.summary: The paper diagnoses characteristic LLM agent failures under partial observability as stemming from the absence of an explicit belief over hidden state, and proposes a Belief-State Engine that maintains a Bayesian posterior over a POMDP's latent states outside the LLM. This architectural add-on aims to prevent premature commitment, wrong-hypothesis collapse, and policy drift.

entry.title: From Symbolic Perception to Logical Deduction: A Framework for Guiding Language Models in Geometric Reasoning

author.name: Weichen Dai, Rafael Medeiros Cabral, Ziyi Shou, Yan Cao, Xin Shen, Dongcai Lu, Yi Zhou

entry.summary: The paper shows a pure LLM equipped with a Geometric Vision Parser (translating diagrams to symbolic form) and a Symbolic Solver can rival state-of-the-art multimodal models on complex plane geometry, with reduced hallucination and more interpretable reasoning. It also curates a challenging benchmark from 2025 Chinese Zhongkao problems.

entry.title: Can AI Agents Detect and Repair Artifact Drift in Network Experiments?

author.name: Tianzhu Zhang, Weichen Tao, Changgang Zheng, Yusheng Zheng, Long Chen, Xiaoyi Fan, Meikang Qiu

entry.summary: The paper introduces artifact integrity, the property that an AI agent's modifications to an experiment record remain evidence-supported, in-scope, and traceable, and releases NetArtifactBench to test whether agents can detect and repair drift in network experiment records. It reframes agent evaluation beyond task completion toward trustworthiness of the records agents touch. Timely as agentic systems enter operational research settings.

entry.title: Can Foundation Models Moderate Online Content? Evaluating Instruction- vs. Example-Driven Policy Operationalization

author.name: Ayan Majumdar, Shounak Paul, Pushpdeep Singh, Ines Abdelaziz, Sayeh Jarollahi, Seungeon Lee, Krishna P. Gummadi, Ingmar Weber, Abhisek Dash

entry.summary: The paper systematically compares instruction-driven versus example-driven operationalization of content moderation policies in vision-language models, using ModerationBench of 4,000 manually annotated Bluesky posts. It finds foundation models can substantially moderate content reliably, clarifying which guidance paradigm suits policy consistency.

entry.title: Conformal Calibration Transfer

author.name: Achref Doula

entry.summary: Studies conformal prediction when labeled calibration data exists only in a source space while prediction sets are needed in a linked target space, such as under sensor or modality changes. The proposed Transported Conformal Calibration transports labeled source calibration via paired unlabeled data and corrects residual mismatch using unlabeled target inputs, with two instantiations (TCC-KS and another variant). Extends coverage guarantees to a practically common transfer setting.

entry.title: Importance Weighting for Unlabeled-unlabeled Learning under Distribution Shift

author.name: Atsutoshi Kumagai, Tomoharu Iwata, Hiroshi Takahashi, Taishi Nishiyama, Kazuki Adachi, Yasuhiro Fujiwara

entry.summary: The paper proposes an importance-weighting method for unlabeled-unlabeled (UU) learning that adapts to distribution shift between training and test distributions using only unlabeled data plus a small amount of test-distribution UU data. Since UU learning subsumes positive-unlabeled and noisy-label learning, the method broadly improves robustness of weakly supervised binary classification under covariate/prior shift.

entry.title: A Station-Based Evaluation of Machine Learning-based Weather Forecasting Models in Northern Norway

author.name: Siyan Chen, Lars Uebbing, Eirik Mikal Samuelsen, Georgios Leontidis, Arnt-B{\o}rre Salberg, S\'ebastien Lef\`evre, Robert Jenssen, Kristoffer Wickstr{\o}m

entry.summary: This case study evaluates machine learning weather prediction models (FourCastNet3 and GraphCast) against the operational ECMWF HRES baseline for wind speed forecasting in Northern Norway, using multi-year station observations in a challenging fjord environment. The finding that HRES still slightly outperforms the ML models, particularly under high-wind conditions, provides an important reality check on MLWP generalization claims. This matters because rigorous localized evaluations are rare relative to global reanalysis-based benchmarks.

entry.title: Testing Between the Test Cases: Proving End-to-End Steering in Conditions You Never Drove

author.name: Menuka Ghalan, Charles Rodgers, Zachary D. Asher

entry.summary: Using bound propagation on trained end-to-end steering networks, the authors formally verify lane-keeping behavior across continuous ranges of disturbance strength between test images, covering 133 poses on an arterial road without further driving. This bridges the gap between passing discrete test conditions and guaranteed real-world robustness in autonomous driving. One verification run spans more conditions than an empirical testing campaign could cover.

entry.title: BodyCam-VQA: Enhanced Body-Worn Camera Video Captioning via Multimodal Reasoning and Probe Question Generation

author.name: Karish Gupta, Matthew Alex, Alex Li, Yang Wu, Yun-Wei Chu, Kashif Munir, Xiaotian Zhou, Zhengping Ji, Xiaozhong Liu

entry.summary: BodyCam-VQA targets body-worn camera video understanding, where chaotic scenes, low visual quality, and noisy audio defeat current VLMs and cause missed forensic details. The approach combines multimodal reasoning with generated probe questions to improve captioning and evidence surfacing for legal transparency and accountability.

entry.title: ReconPlusGen: Injecting Reconstruction Prior into Multi-view 3D Generation through Noise Inversion and Modulation

author.name: Jiarui Liu, Heng Li, Weiyu Li, Keng Deng, Junyuan Deng, Zheng Zhongxing, Junyu Huang, Jiahao Chang, Xiaoguang Han, Ping Tan

entry.summary: ReconPlusGen predicts a point cloud from multiple input images and deterministically injects the predicted geometry into the diffusion process via noise inversion, then modulates the noise to preserve generative flexibility for completing unobserved regions. It fuses reconstruction priors with multi-view 3D generation.

entry.title: CARLAverse: A Highly Modular, Distributed, and Multimodal Framework for Human-in-the-Loop Simulation

author.name: Patrick Rebling, Philipp Nenninger, Reiner Kriesten

entry.summary: CARLAverse is an open-source multimodal human-in-the-loop simulation ecosystem integrating driving, cycling, and pedestrian simulators into a shared CARLA-based virtual environment, designed to handle network latency and synchronization constraints for high-fidelity haptic feedback in mixed-traffic studies. It enables safe investigation of authentic human social negotiation with autonomous vehicles.

entry.title: Valerant: An Automatic Navigable Game Map Generator via Action-Conditioned World Model Exploration

author.name: Yiran Qiao, Feng Wang, Jing Ma

entry.summary: Extends World Action Models to 3D games, where the environment persists independently of the model, and builds Valerant, a system that automatically generates navigable game maps through action-conditioned world model exploration. This bridges world-model advances from robotics and driving into general game content generation.

entry.title: RESCUE-BENCH: Towards Relation-Aware Multi-Party Emotional Support Conversation Systems

author.name: Haichuan Hu, Yang Xiao, Mingni Tang, Jiawen Duan, Quanjun Zhang, Congqing He, Hao Zhang, Jiashuo Wang, Johan F. Hoorn, Wenjie Li

entry.summary: Introduces relation-aware emotional support conversation as a new task and builds RESCUE, a benchmark from real couple and family interview conversations with 191 samples, 7,079 annotated turns, and over 1,000 minutes of video. It tests whether LLMs can leverage evolving interpersonal relationship dynamics for effective emotional support. This extends emotional support research beyond one-on-one interactions.

entry.title: Grounded Evaluation and Repair for NL-to-PDDL Problem Generation

author.name: Joana Rosa, Pedro Santos, Valdemar Oliveira, Rom\~ao Silva, L. Miguel Silveira, Bruno Martins

entry.summary: The paper shows that standard metrics for LLM-generated PDDL problem instances (parseability, planner success) overestimate faithfulness to the described task, and builds an end-to-end pipeline combining parsing, planning, validation, domain-conformance checking, an LLM critic, and iterative repair. Fine-grained repair feedback improves the semantic correctness of generated planning problems.

entry.title: RAP: Research Attention Prediction Reveals Target-Conditioned Evidence Acquisition Biases

author.name: Yingqian Wu, Jingcong Liang, Siyuan Wang, Zhenfei Yin, Philip Torr, Junchi Yu, Zhongyu Wei

entry.summary: RAP is a rolling benchmark (278 AI/ML fields, 1,390 episodes) where LLM agents search a temporally restricted arXiv corpus to predict future paper shares across research directions. All diagnostic models underperform a simple EWMA count baseline, and the authors trace failures to state carry-over and evidence acquisition biases tied to target conditions.

entry.title: Fine-Tuning a KV Cache Concatenation-Aware Model or Recomputing KV Caches? Why Not Both?

author.name: Fumihiko Tachibana, Daisuke Miyashita, Jun Deguchi

entry.summary: The authors combine fine-tuning a model to be aware of KV cache concatenation with selective recomputation of a subset of cached keys to speed up RAG prefill for very long contexts. Precomputed KV cache reuse reduces time-to-first-token, and this hybrid approach aims to preserve response quality where naive reuse degrades it. Relevant to latency-critical retrieval-augmented serving.

entry.title: GANDR: Claim Auditing for Verifiable Legal Answer Generation

author.name: Chen Qian, Yimeng Wang, Yu Chen, Lingfei Wu, Andreas Stathopoulos

entry.summary: GANDR is a two-agent grounded-generation system where a Drafter writes structured legal answers and a Critic audits each claim against its cited source, emitting a per-claim audit trace. It is paired with an evaluation measuring per-claim verifiability, addressing cases where a correct conclusion rests on fabricated citations.

entry.title: GEOSTEER: Geodesic Optimization for Activation Steering in Large Language Models

author.name: Xuan Cuong Ngo, Hao Vo, Ngan Le

entry.summary: Reframes norm-preserving activation steering in LLMs as a Riemannian optimization problem, replacing predefined one-step steering trajectories with sequences of small geodesic updates that better respect the geometry of activation distributions. This provides a principled, lightweight inference-time control method for LLM behavior. Relevant to model control and interpretability without retraining.

entry.title: Certifying Lower Bounds for Risk-Sensitive Reinforcement Learning under Adversarial State Perturbations

author.name: Tong Li, Saunak Kumar Panda, Yisha Xiang

entry.summary: Extends certified robustness for RL from risk-neutral to risk-sensitive objectives, establishing lower bounds on the exponential utility of cumulative rewards under lp-norm-bounded adversarial state perturbations. A phi-divergence relaxation of the perturbation set enables a tractable risk-sensitive certification formulation. Important for deploying RL agents in safety-critical, adversarial environments.

entry.title: LILA: Calibration-Free Structured Pruning of Large Language Models via Latent Spectral Geometry

author.name: Sankar Behera, Dhruv Singh, Anshika Agnihotri, Raj Kumar Choudhary, Satyadev Ahlawat, Yamuna Prasad

entry.summary: LILA scores FFN neuron importance via Kolmogorov-Smirnov distance between singular value distributions of full and ablated weight matrices, enabling closed-form structured pruning without calibration data, gradients, or auxiliary networks. Without fine-tuning it beats PruneNet and calibrated SliceGPT on LLaMA-2-7B at 25% sparsity.

entry.title: Predicting Privacy Leakage from Weight Spectral Density

author.name: Richard J. Preen, Jim Smith

entry.summary: The authors test whether cheap WeightWatcher spectral metrics from the heavy-tailed self-regularisation framework can proxy membership inference attack vulnerability, avoiding costly shadow-model training. Stable rank correlates strongly with overall MIA success across image and tabular tasks, suggesting fast privacy auditing.

entry.title: A Quantum-Inspired Dequantization Method for Diagonally Weighted Matrix Functions: Application to Learning with Optimized Random Features

author.name: Natsuto Isogai, Mio Murao, Hayata Yamasaki

entry.summary: The authors develop a classical algorithm that dequantizes a QSVT-based sampler for learning with optimized random features, a case not covered by existing dequantization frameworks because the relevant matrix is not accessible via sampling. Their approach samples heavy indices, reduces the problem to a small principal block, and outputs a sparse representation with operator-norm guarantees. This removes a claimed quantum advantage for a concrete quantum machine learning candidate.

entry.title: Temporal and Multimodal Deep Learning for Cyberattack Detection in LEO Satellite Systems

author.name: Kyle Stein, Guillermo Francia III, Eman El-Sheikh, Hossain Shahriar

entry.summary: A systematic study of deep-learning cyberattack detection for Low-Earth Orbit satellite systems using the satellite-specific UNSW-IoT dataset, combining temporal and multimodal signals across RF links, onboard hardware, and orbital operations. The work shows that modeling temporal attack behavior and heterogeneous modalities improves detection over approaches that treat observations independently or rely on terrestrial intrusion datasets. It matters because space systems are an increasingly critical and under-defended infrastructure.

entry.title: Risk-Averse Decision Making with Multi-Level Reliability Guarantees

author.name: Amirmohammad Farzaneh, Osvaldo Simeone

entry.summary: The paper studies maximizing weighted performance certificates at multiple target outage levels under state uncertainty, showing the problem is equivalent to optimization over nested prediction sets and connecting it to conformal prediction. It extends single-level risk-averse decision making to multi-level guarantees and derives a dual formulation that decouples optimization across inputs, illustrated on a wireless transmission system. This bridges conformal prediction theory and engineering decision-making under uncertainty.

entry.title: SIRF: A Spec-Internalized Risk Foundation Model for Industrial Content Risk Control

author.name: Suwan Wu, Yumeng Lin, Pengcheng Yuan, Xiaolong Jiang

entry.summary: SIRF internalizes platform content-risk policies via continued pretraining using synthetic data from EntiGraph, MAGA rewriting, and account-level chain-of-thought, enabling verdict-only, low-latency risk classification without extra human annotation. A controlled comparison against Qwen3-8B-SFT attributes gains to policy internalization rather than output format.

entry.title: Think Before You Link: Rarity, Reasoning, and Retrieval in Multilingual Entity Linking

author.name: Parinthapat Pengpun, Simran Khanuja, Graham Neubig

entry.summary: The paper shows knowledge-graph structural rarity metrics surface rare entities that popularity-based metrics miss, with SOTA multimodal entity linking accuracy dropping 15.4-39.9% on these slices. It introduces a training-free framework where a reasoning-capable vision-language model iteratively searches Wikipedia to improve rare-entity linking.

entry.title: Distribution-aware Language Neuron Identification in Multilingual Large Language Models

author.name: Minjun Kim, Inho Won, Junghun Yuk, Dongyeon Kim, Jihyo Kim, KyungTae Lim

entry.summary: This work improves identification of language-specific neurons in multilingual LLMs by replacing entropy-based activation statistics with distribution-aware comparisons of per-language activation distributions over the full activation range, including negative values. It argues prior methods miss the distributional, mutually related nature of multilingual representations. This advances mechanistic understanding of how mLLMs encode language.

entry.title: Rethinking Verbalized Confidence for LLM-as-a-Judge: A Compatibility Shift on Post-2025 Proprietary Models

author.name: Yu-Chung Hsiao

entry.summary: This single-author study shows that verbalized confidence has overtaken log-probability-based scoring as the better soft-signal for LLM-as-a-Judge evaluation on post-2025 proprietary models, calling this a compatibility shift. Across SummEval, AggreFact, and HelpSteer2 with up to 18 LLMs, added techniques like an overconfidence advisory and self-debate improve calibration. It challenges standard advice on confidence extraction methods.

entry.title: Overview of the NLPCC 2026 Shared Task 11: Agent-Based Experiment Reproduction from Scientific Papers

author.name: Hanhua Hong, Yizhi Li, Luu Gia Huy, Jian Yang, Ming Zhou, Chenghua Lin

entry.summary: This shared-task overview introduces AgentActionBench, a process-oriented benchmark evaluating LLM agents on reproducing experiments from scientific papers across ML and AI4Science, using an MCP-based Action Recorder and paper-specific rubrics over 150 papers. Unlike prior work focused on final repositories, it evaluates the entire agent behavior trace. It advances reproducibility infrastructure through agent evaluation.

entry.title: Recognizing Is Not Reversing: A Controlled Inversion Test of Fact-Preserving News Framing

author.name: Yi Liu

entry.summary: Introduces a controlled inversion test measuring whether LLMs can undo a known news-framing transformation while preserving atomic facts, spanning evaluative lexis, agency realization, and information salence across 540 paired variants. Testing Qwen, DeepSeek, and Kimi models, it finds factual preservation near 0.84 but intervention reversal only 0.044-0.068, showing models recognize framing yet cannot reverse it. This has implications for media-analysis and debiasing applications.

entry.title: Augustinian BabyLM: What Ostensive Definition Can and Cannot Teach a Small Language Model

author.name: Lisa Bylinina

entry.summary: The paper implements Augustine's ostensive definition in a small masked LM (DeBERTa, 10M words) by initializing embeddings for visually grounded tokens from image-region representations before training. Visual initialization leaves a lasting trace and improves zero-shot object-property knowledge (e.g., COMPS) but has no effect on most BabyLM grammatical benchmarks.

entry.title: MHE-Former: Multi-Hypothesis Transformers via Entropy Maximization for 3D Mesh Recovery

author.name: Boshu Jia, Rongyu Chen, Linlin Yang, Zihao Liu, Yingjie Chen, Zhongqun Zhang, Zhulin Tao, Shaohui Lin, Xiaoyu Wu, Libiao Jin, Baochang Zhang, Angela Yao

entry.summary: MHE-Former addresses ambiguity in monocular 3D hand and body mesh recovery with an exploration-exploitation paradigm: a transformer generates diverse plausible mesh hypotheses trained via entropy maximization, and a context-aware selection module picks the best hypothesis at inference. This reduces overconfident single-solution regression under occlusion.

entry.title: SCINTILLA-SNN: A Spiking Multi-Scale Selective Aggregation Network for Perineural Invasion Prediction

author.name: Youngung Han, Yului Jeong, Kyeonghun Kim, Dohyun Kweon, Suah Park, Hyunsu Go, Sungha Park, Anna Jung, Jinyong Jun, Yunho Choe, Yunjin Seo, Ken Ying-Kai Liao, Hyuk-Jae Lee, Nam-Joon Kim

entry.summary: Applies a 3D spiking neural network with a multi-scale spike aggregation module to predict perineural invasion in cholangiocarcinoma from MRI, motivated by the sparse, boundary-localized nature of PNI cues and the compute cost of dense 3D processing. Combines neuromorphic efficiency with a concrete clinical prediction task.

entry.title: Order-Aware 2.5D Multiple Instance Learning for Preoperative MRI-Based Perineural Invasion Risk Assessment in Intrahepatic Cholangiocarcinoma

author.name: Hyunsu Go, Youngung Han, Kyeonghun Kim, Jinyong Jun, Junbeom Lee, Dohyun Kweon, Yului Jeong, Suah Park, Sungha Park, Anna Jung, Woo Kyoung Jeong, Ken Ying-Kai Liao, Hyuk-Jae Lee, Nam-Joon Kim

entry.summary: A weakly supervised multiple-instance learning framework combining set-attention and sequence-attention over ordered 2.5D MRI slabs to predict perineural invasion preoperatively using only patient-level labels. Companion work to SCINTILLA-SNN from the same clinical team, targeting a histopathologic marker normally confirmed only after resection.

entry.title: UBone3D: Physics-Rectified Conditional Flow Matching for Anatomical 3D Shape Completion from Ultrasound

author.name: Weiying Chen, Yuchong Gao, Siyuan Li, Marek Reformat, Rui Zheng, Edmond Lou

entry.summary: Performs 3D anatomical shape completion from artifact-laden partial ultrasound point clouds using physics-rectified conditional flow matching, modeling deterministic ultrasound artifacts via a simulated physics proxy and steering completion with test-time physics rectification. Enables longitudinal CT-free skeletal monitoring.

entry.title: Learning Interaction between Image and Layout Priors for Joint Image-Layout Generation in Design Templates

author.name: Shirong Yang, Bo Yang, Ying Cao

entry.summary: InterIL jointly generates background images and foreground element layouts from text in a single generative process, arguing that sequential paradigms fail to capture image-layout dependencies in graphic design. The joint modeling improves composition harmony in design template generation.

entry.title: Safety-aware Skill Adaptation for Reinforcement Learning in Dynamic Environments

author.name: A K M Nadimul Haque, Sheila Sutjipto, Marc G. Carmichael, Teresa Vidal-Calleja

entry.summary: Dist-GPRL is a distance-aware, safety-guided RL framework for skill adaptation in cluttered, dynamic environments, building on Gaussian Process skill parameterization to sequentially adapt overlapping local windows of trajectory via-points rather than full skills. This restricts exploration to safe regions near obstacles and moving objects.

entry.title: First Bill Introduced to Ban Superintelligent AI

author.name: Andrea_Miotti

entry.summary: ControlAI announces a legislative milestone: the first bill to ban superintelligent AI, introduced in the UK Parliament by MP Alex Sobel, alongside related breakthroughs in multiple legislatures following briefings to nearly 400 lawmakers. The post frames this against a backdrop of researcher resignations, including Anthropic researcher Jacob Coxon, citing race-to-superintelligence concerns.

entry.title: Time-Frequency Geometric Cross-Attention for Chunked Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Shengye Dong, Haochen Niu, Hao Liu, Peiwen Lin, Chuang Wang, Shanmin Pang

entry.summary: This work argues that action chunks in vision-language-action policies are multivariate trajectories poorly served by generic per-timestep tokens, and proposes a time-frequency geometric cross-attention module that separates smooth global trends from fine corrective motion and models cross-phase geometric structure. The design targets robot manipulation policies that emit chunked actions.

entry.title: Cyber-Financial Contagion: Modeling the Propagation of an AI Vendor Compromise Through the Banking System

author.name: Alex Leytes

entry.summary: The paper models how a compromise of a shared AI vendor (for fraud, AML, credit decisioning) can propagate through a four-layer network of vendors, banks, interbank exposures, and accounts via a stochastic epidemic-and-clearing model (CFC-Prop). Synthetic experiments with 60 vendors and 220 banks show how vendor compromises can generate losses resembling classical banking crises.

entry.title: Fidelity-Aware Scheduling of Quantum Circuits on Multi-QPU Systems

author.name: Innocenzo Fulginiti, Antonio Tudisco, Salvatore Zammuto, Patrick Hopf, Deborah Volpe, Helmut Seidl, Giovanna Turvani, Robert Wille, Christian B. Mendl, Martin Schulz

entry.summary: The paper presents a low-overhead scheduling framework for HPC-quantum systems with multiple heterogeneous QPUs, using a GNN to predict, before compilation, the expected fidelity of executing a circuit on each device. This addresses noise-driven fidelity differences across QPUs of differing size, topology, and gates. A concrete systems contribution at the intersection of ML and quantum computing.

entry.title: Forgetting Only What Matters: Layer-Selective Unlearning toward Robust LLMs

author.name: Ravi Ranjan, Olivera Kotevska, Agoritsa Polyzou

entry.summary: FOM-UL is a layer-level machine unlearning framework that selects transformer layers via a forget-to-retain significance score, applying targeted updates rather than broad parameter changes. It aims to preserve utility and remain robust to deployment changes such as post-training quantization, under which forgotten knowledge often partially re-emerges.

entry.title: TailProp: content-adaptive light- and heavy-tailed propagation for vision

author.name: Jiahao Kong, Zihan Li

entry.summary: TailProp introduces a hierarchical vision backbone built on a Tail Propagation Operator that combines Gaussian and Cauchy stable-process propagators as complementary bases with content-conditioned channel-wise coefficients. This lets spatial interaction regimes adapt across samples, channels, and stages rather than committing to one dynamical family. It offers an interpretable, science-inspired alternative to conventional token mixing in vision transformers.

entry.title: An Autonomous GeoAI Agent for Arctic Eco-Navigation

author.name: Samira Alkaee Taleghan, Younghyun Koo, Farnoush Banaei-Kashani

entry.summary: Presents a human-in-the-loop multi-agent GeoAI system for Arctic ship routing that integrates operational, physical, ecological, and community-impact criteria, going beyond conventional time/fuel/risk objectives. The application area is increasingly consequential as sea-ice change expands seasonal Arctic navigation.

entry.title: Decision Shifts, Lost Label Functionality, and an Inconclusive Grounding Audit in Correctness-Gated Multi-Teacher Distillation

author.name: Xiaofei Feng

entry.summary: Empirically examines correctness-gated multi-teacher distillation in a controlled experiment with eight arms sharing data, a 63.9M-parameter student, and fixed teacher pools. Correctness weighting improves accuracy (+0.17), macro-F1 (+0.13), and cuts unsafe-action rate (-0.50), but the paper shows these gains mask decision shifts and lost label functionality, with a grounding audit remaining inconclusive. A cautionary study on what distillation filters actually change.

entry.title: Scored vs. Generated Readouts in Behavioral Language Models: An Empirical Study of Elicitation Format

author.name: Touchapon Kraisingkorn, Krittin Pachtrachai, Wachiravit Modecrua

entry.summary: This empirical study compares scoring answer token probabilities versus generating predictions after written rationales for models fine-tuned on customer behavior, holding checkpoints and prompts fixed. Across 13 model-domain cells, scored readouts rank outcomes more accurately in 12 of 13, with AUC gaps of 1.5 to 14.5 points and statistically robust confidence intervals.

entry.title: What Should an Agent Forget? Separating What Is Stored from What Is Used

author.name: Yuhang Li, Yuchen Li

entry.summary: RD-Forget is a training-free framework that separates an agent's retained source archive from a query-conditioned memory view, using a frozen LLM curator to group facts into semantic slots. Same-slot replacement suppresses superseded values in current-state contexts while intent-aware retrieval preserves historical facts for multi-hop reasoning.

entry.title: Characterizing Text Branch Sensitivity in Medical Vision-Language Segmentation via Evidence Decoupling

author.name: Ziquan Liu, Zhewei Zhu, Xuyang Shi

entry.summary: Systematically investigates how much clinical text actually contributes to pixel-level predictions in medical vision-language segmentation, finding performance largely insensitive to fusion-module choice. It proposes an Evidence Decoupling Decoder based on evidential deep learning to decompose image versus text-modulated evidence. The finding challenges assumptions in multimodal medical segmentation research.

entry.title: Scaling Post-Training Ternarisation to Qwen3-8B Capability Retention, Reproduction, Lossless Packing, and Packed Execution

author.name: Anirudh Malik, M Sparsh Mehra, Poojith Devan

entry.summary: Scales an aggressive post-training ternarization pipeline (KOTMS rotation, adaptive ternarization, GPTQ-style compensation) from Qwen3-4B to the existing Qwen3-8B model, with external reproduction gates and matched capability analysis. The contribution is an end-to-end characterization including cross-corpus perplexity, effective-bit accounting, lossless lattice-aware packing, and direct packed execution. This makes the paper more an honest engineering-scale-up study than a novel algorithm contribution.

entry.title: Improving 5G AI-RAN MCS Selection by Predicting Retransmissions

author.name: Tamerlan Aghayev, Maxime Elkael, Michele Polese, Reshma Prasad, Salvatore D'Oro, Yunseong Lee, Koichiro Furueda, Tommaso Melodia

entry.summary: NOSTRAdAMUS is a predictive link-adaptation framework for 5G radio access networks that augments existing reactive modulation-and-coding-selection algorithms with retransmission prediction, adding foresight without replacing deployed controllers. It targets the problem that channel and HARQ feedback in 5G is noisy and quickly obsolete, causing overly aggressive or conservative rate selection. The work matters for applying machine learning to real-time telecom infrastructure under strict latency constraints.

entry.title: Edu-QuRating: Multi-Dimensional Educational Data Curation with Distilled Pairwise Judgements

author.name: Oliver G. B. Garrod, Robin A. A. Ince, Meng Liu, Mohamed Huti, Moritz Boos, Amy Waldock, Dominic Andrews, Romana Alonso-Kropil, Paul Atherton

entry.summary: Extends QuRating-style data filtering by scoring pretraining documents along multiple educational rubrics (accuracy, engagement, structure, audience fit) rather than a single scalar, using LLM pairwise judgments distilled into reusable classifiers. This enables finer-grained curation for high-quality educational corpora.

entry.title: RouteBridge: Reliability-Routed Bidirectional Distillation Between Neural Radiance Fields and 3D Gaussian Splatting

author.name: YuanHang Wang, Xin Cao

entry.summary: Introduces RouteBridge, a bidirectional distillation framework between NeRF and 3D Gaussian Splatting that routes supervision per-ray based on a reliability estimator, avoiding the error propagation of a globally fixed teacher. A renderer-independent interface transfers color, opacity, and depth without feature sharing, improving results on mip-NeRF 360.

entry.title: HiRAD: A Flexible Large-Scale AGV Routing System

author.name: Yunjie Huang, Ruizhong Wu, Mengxuan Zhang, Frodo Kin Sun Chan, Yan Nei Law, Lei Li

entry.summary: HiRAD targets warehouse routing of large Automatic Guided Vehicle fleets, addressing the combinatorial blowup of classical Multi-Agent Pathfinding solvers and the slow convergence and high inference latency of RL approaches. It offers flexible, real-time-capable routing closer to real vehicle kinematics. This has direct industrial relevance for warehouse automation.

entry.title: Albedo Estimation via Latent Bridge Matching

author.name: Carme Corbi, David Serrano-Lozano, Javier Vazquez-Corral, Maria Vanrell

entry.summary: The authors adapt latent bridge matching to intrinsic image decomposition for albedo estimation, enforcing physical consistency via pixel reconstruction loss, gaining efficient low-step inference, and improving generalization with shading conditioning. It addresses the cost, consistency, and generalization weaknesses of diffusion-based intrinsic decomposition. A solid computer vision method paper.

entry.title: DiSCo: A Distribution-First Steering and Cultural Prior Evaluation Framework for Measuring Cultural Preference Bias in LLMs

author.name: Bhuvan Arora, Devesh Saraogi, Sravya Varada, Dhruv Kumar

entry.summary: DiSCo is a distribution-first forced-choice evaluation framework that isolates default cultural priors in LLMs and measures steerability across a four-level context gradient, using a benchmark of culturally grounded scenarios. It addresses shortcomings of single-correct-answer cultural benchmarks that conflate default preference with contextual adaptation.

entry.title: Zero-shot rib design: merging training-free generative prior with topology optimization

author.name: Yongmin Kwon, Namwoo Kang

entry.summary: Treats a frozen text-to-image diffusion model as a training-free source of structural design knowledge, distilling it into density-based topology optimization via score distillation sampling so natural language prompts become explicit design intent. Prompt-induced generative gradients are combined with finite element sensitivities at each iteration, with physics deciding which generated features survive. A creative bridge between generative AI and mechanical design.

entry.title: Flow Duality and Source Geometry for Categorical Generation

author.name: Etrit Haxholli

entry.summary: Identifies a duality between continuous and discrete flow matching: projecting continuous convex-interpolant paths with one-hot targets through a position-wise argmax yields discrete convex-interpolant paths. It characterizes how source distribution geometry (Gaussian, bounded-uniform, centered negative-exponential) induces qualitatively different discrete interpolation behavior and vocabulary-size dependence, making source choice an explicit design lever for categorical generation. Theoretically interesting for discrete generative modeling.

entry.title: Bidirectional Multimodal Fusion of Sky Images and Time-Series for Solar Forecasting with Large Language Models

author.name: Ken Chen, Maneesha Perera, Wei Wang, Sachith Seneviratne, Hansani Weeratunge, Saman Halgamuge

entry.summary: The paper extends LLM-based time-series forecasting to short-term solar power and irradiance prediction by bidirectionally fusing ground-based sky images with historical time series, capturing cloud-induced ramps that numerical data alone miss. This improves site-specific forecasting with limited data, important for grid dispatch and reserve scheduling.

entry.title: When does a spectral prior help graph learning? Connectivity-loss estimation under road-network disruptions

author.name: Van-Truong Le

entry.summary: This paper uses graph neural networks (GCN, GraphSAGE, MPNN) to estimate relative algebraic-connectivity loss after simultaneous multi-edge road-network deletions, learning a bounded correction on top of a first-order Fiedler-vector sensitivity prior. It evaluates independent, clustered, and targeted failure modes with graph-disjoint splits and zero-shot transfer to 13 OpenStreetMap road networks across six countries. The residual-GCN approach measurably improves mean absolute error over analytical baselines for spatially clustered failures.

entry.title: Combining Synthetic and Real Data for Low-Resource Historical OCR: A Manchu Case Study

author.name: Yan Hon Michael Chung, Hanlin Wang

entry.summary: The authors study how to combine 60,000 synthetic and 20,306 real word images for OCR on critically endangered Manchu manuscripts, evaluating pretrained vision-language models and a compact CRNN under four training regimes. The work quantifies the synthetic-to-real gap and provides guidance for low-resource historical document transcription.

entry.title: RDDMPI: Residual Denoising Diffusion Model for Probabilistic Multivariate Time Series Imputation

author.name: Ramiro Valdes Jara, David Chapman, Adam Meyers

entry.summary: The paper proposes running diffusion in the residual space on top of a deterministic imputer rather than the raw data space, decoupling global structure capture from stochastic variability. This simplifies the generative task for probabilistic multivariate time series imputation in domains like healthcare and traffic.

entry.title: On the Relation between Code Quality and Machine Learning Performance: A Large-scale Empirical Study

author.name: Marius Mignard (CRIStAL), Steven Costiou (CRIStAL), Anne Etien (CRIStAL, EVREF)

entry.summary: This large-scale empirical study tests the assumption that code quality and ML model performance are unrelated in computational notebooks, and evaluates whether popularity and author expertise are reliable proxies for notebook quality. The findings challenge or confirm an untested belief that shapes how the ML community treats code quality. It matters for reproducibility and software engineering practice in ML research.

entry.title: From Cycle Space to Cycle Manifold: Limits and Achievability of Blind False Data Injection Attacks

author.name: Xin Li, Chenhan Xiao, Jonathan Cohen, Aviad Elyashar, Yang Weng, Rami Puzis

entry.summary: Under the connected DC branch-flow model, this paper proves that the residual-sensitive subspace of a bad-data detector equals the weighted cycle space, making weighted cycle-space knowledge necessary and sufficient for complete stealthy false data injection attacks on power grids. This gives a precise characterization of the minimum information an attacker needs. It matters for grid security and for principled understanding of adversarial vulnerabilities in state estimation.

entry.title: Quantifying the Memorization-to-Generalization Transition: Scaling Laws and Phase Structure in Grokking

author.name: Anish Kataria

entry.summary: This work maps the grokking phase boundary across 384 configurations of two-hidden-layer MLPs trained on modular arithmetic, fitting a power-law scaling relation for the time of generalization onset. The exponent hierarchy shows data complexity is the dominant driver of the transition, outweighing model capacity. This quantifies when grokking occurs in hyperparameter space, complementing existing theories of why it occurs.

entry.title: Weighted Empirical Risk Minimization for Machine Learning under Long-Range Dependence: Exact Pathwise Rates and Learning-Error Geometry

author.name: Elina Moldavskaya

entry.summary: A theoretical paper deriving exact almost-sure learning rates for smooth parametric models trained by weighted empirical risk minimization on long-range dependent Gaussian data. When the loss gradient has Wiener-chaos rank m, the authors obtain an almost-sure Bahadur representation, exact limsup laws for the learned parameter, and geometric descriptions (functional cluster sets) of the learning trajectory. This provides precise pathwise guarantees rather than typical in-probability or expectation bounds.

entry.title: Structurally Speaking: Motif-Oriented Graph Captioning through Bidirectional Graph-Text Translation

author.name: Hsiao-Ying Lu, Dongyu Liu, Kwan-Liu Ma

entry.summary: The paper reframes graph captioning as bidirectional graph-text translation where captions describe graphs via structural motifs (hubs, paths, cycles, cliques, bridges) while preserving enough topology for graph recovery. It shows that direct prompting of GPT-5.1, an existing model released in late 2025, tends to produce verbose edge enumerations rather than concise motif descriptions. A dedicated model is trained for motif-oriented, recoverable captions.

entry.title: CryptoL: Towards Scale Dominance and Physics Constraints Mitigation in Financial Multivariate Time Series Forecasting

author.name: Yalda Taheri, Mohammad Hassan Heydari, Armon Rasooli, Maryam Amirshahkarami, Mohammad Ebrahim Mahdavi, Hossein Karshenas

entry.summary: CryptoL is a framework for multivariate cryptocurrency forecasting that tackles extreme cross-asset scale heterogeneity and OHLC structural dependencies. It evaluates error in context-normalized coordinates within a RevIN pipeline and formally characterizes, via empirical risk and gradient geometry, how large-scale assets can disproportionately dominate shared-model optimization. The work matters for practitioners building financial forecasting models where scale imbalance silently biases training.

entry.title: A distribution-free certification framework for trustworthy crash-severity prediction

author.name: Amir Rafe, Subasish Das

entry.summary: The authors develop a distribution-free certification layer that wraps any crash-severity prediction model, providing finite-sample guarantees that handle ordinal KABCO outcomes, noisy field-assessed labels, and distribution shift across jurisdictions and years. The framework produces contiguous ordinal sets readable as statements like B-or-worse, with per-class validity and oracle efficiency characterization. It addresses a real safety-critical deployment gap where predictions previously came with no stated meaning.

entry.title: A Unified Per-Token Gating Family for On-Policy Distillation: FKL/RKL Mixing with Multi-Channel and Bias Coefficients

author.name: Suwan Wu, Yumeng Lin, Pengcheng Yuan, Xiaolong Jiang

entry.summary: The paper unifies per-token forward/reverse KL gating for on-policy distillation in a four-coefficient parameterization that subsumes EOPD and ToDi as one-dimensional restrictions, adding multi-channel and bias degrees of freedom. Experiments with a Qwen3-32B teacher and Qwen3-4B student on TweetEval show the full family outperforms prior single-signal gates.

entry.title: Evaluating Time-Series Foundation Models and Multimodal Dietary Context for CGM Forecasting

author.name: Bowen Zhang, Hsiu-Wen Cheng, Hongyu Yang, Evie L. Shen, Joleen Vansomphone, Yuna Li, Kerry Zhou, Zitian Qu, Suning Zhao, Xiangning Deng, Hua Zhou, Jin J. Zhou

entry.summary: A comprehensive empirical study of time-series foundation models for continuous glucose monitoring forecasting across eight public datasets and diabetes populations. Zero-shot foundation models did not consistently beat simple baselines like Elastic Net and PatchTST, while lightweight fine-tuning substantially helped, and multimodal dietary context added value.

entry.title: K/V-Cache Interventions Dissociate Representation Alignment from Persona Expression in Decoder-Only Language Models

author.name: Yu Sun, Mengyin Lu, Cong Feng, Guangming Lu, Huimin Han

entry.summary: This paper uses K/V-cache transplant interventions in Llama-3.1-8B to study persona control, finding that representation-level alignment and behavioral expression dissociate: strong local V-space alignment does not guarantee target-persona expression, and only mid-layer replacement balances expression with lexical diversity. It also reports failures under position perturbation. The findings constrain theories of where persona-like behavior lives in decoder-only models.

entry.title: From Repetition to Recognition: Inductive Discovery of Disinformation Narratives

author.name: Max Upravitelev, Veronika Solopova, Jing Yang, Charlott Jakob, Alexandra Tsiakalou, Neda Foroutan, Vera Schmitt

entry.summary: This paper introduces a three-tier evaluation framework for unsupervised narrative label generation in disinformation corpora: recovery against a corpus taxonomy, mining against external labels, and discovery without predefined labels. It compares clustering and graph-community pipelines across seven disinformation datasets with human validation. Moving beyond closed-world taxonomy evaluation is a meaningful methodological step.

entry.title: Rubric-Aligned Disentangled Evaluation of Human Simultaneous Interpreting

author.name: Ziyu Zhang, Satoshi Nakamura

entry.summary: This work builds a 1,101-segment professionally annotated corpus for rubric-aligned simultaneous interpreting evaluation across meaning transfer, delivery, and latency, and shows that standard LLM prompting and scalar supervision collapse these dimensions. It introduces dual regression heads on a LoRA-adapted COMET-KIWI encoder to disentangle the rubric dimensions. This is the first automatic metric designed for segment-level rubric-aligned SI evaluation.

entry.title: TransClean: A Benchmark for Detecting and Extracting Clean Translations from Large Language Model Outputs

author.name: Shenbin Qian, Yves Scherrer

entry.summary: This paper identifies and taxonomizes translation noise in LLM machine translation outputs, analyzing over 790,000 outputs from 12 LLMs across 22 language pairs and grouping 12 recurring noise patterns. It introduces TransClean, a 9,900-pair controlled benchmark of noisy and clean translations combining synthetic and manually curated instances. It addresses an overlooked reliability problem in LLM-based MT.

entry.title: Cross-Lingual Clinical Annotation Projection as Constrained Text Generation: A Six-Language Study

author.name: \'Alvaro Rey-Blanes, Francisco J. Moreno-Barea, Francisco J. Veredas

entry.summary: Formulates cross-lingual clinical annotation projection as a constrained text-generation task where an LLM inserts entity tags into immutable target-language text, followed by deterministic validation. Evaluated against candidate-span projection and hybrid pipelines for transferring Spanish clinical annotations into six languages. Relevant to scalable multilingual clinical corpus construction.

entry.title: Distance generalization in transformers: why bother with positional encoding?

author.name: Daniel Henrik Nevermann, Claudius Gros

entry.summary: This work studies distance generalization in transformers using synthetic delay-copy tasks, comparing RoPE, ALiBi, and NoPE when inter-token distances at inference differ from training. It examines how positional encoding schemes, data diversity, and task properties affect extrapolation to unseen delays.

entry.title: (Whose defaults?) Is artificial intelligence reorienting archaeological methods?

author.name: Lorenzo Cardarelli, Roberto Ragno

entry.summary: Using a locally run LLM to classify computational methods in roughly 119,000 archaeology abstracts (2010-2025), the authors build a Bayesian Dirichlet-multinomial model of method composition per sub-discipline. They find a small but credible post-2023 shift in method use, investigating whether generative AI and vibe coding are narrowing methodological diversity in archaeology.

entry.title: Two-Parameter Flow Map Learning for Continuous-Time Diffeomorphic Image Registration

author.name: Mohammadjavad Matinkia, Nilanjan Ray

entry.summary: The paper proposes directly learning the continuous-time solution of a non-autonomous ODE for diffeomorphic image registration as a two-parameter flow map, enforcing cocycle consistency instead of relying on numerical integration. This decouples model expressiveness from discretization accuracy in registration.

entry.title: UniH$^3$: Unifying Hierarchical Homogeneity and Heterogeneity for All-in-One Medical Image Restoration

author.name: Zhiwen Yang, Jiayin Li, Chengyu Liu, Hui Zhang, Bingzheng Wei, Yan Xu

entry.summary: UniH3 proposes an all-in-one medical image restoration framework that models not only inter-task heterogeneity but also hierarchical homogeneity, such as shared anatomical structures across modalities, via a homogeneity mechanism to ease training and improve generalization across degradation types.

entry.title: Fast and Accurate Monomodal 3D High Resolution Deep Registration of Drosophila Larval Brain Volumes

author.name: Daniel Reisenb\"uchler, Yousef Sadegheih, Michael Dittrich, Pratibha Kumari, Muhammad Usman, Dorit Merhof

entry.summary: Replaces per-case classical optimization pipelines for aligning Drosophila larval brains to a reference atlas with a trained deep registration model that aligns a volume in a single forward pass at high resolution. Enables routine, scalable preprocessing for comparative neuroscience experiments.

entry.title: R4Tun: LLM-guided adaptive segmental tunnel lining segmentation in point clouds

author.name: Xinghui Tao, Zehao Ye, Guangming Wang, Jelena Nini\'c, Brian Sheil

entry.summary: Uses an LLM to adaptively tune parameters of an expert-designed point cloud segmentation pipeline for tunnel inspection, conditioning on memory, state, and knowledge tokens, improving mIoU from 0.18 to 0.43-0.48 over a static baseline across 30 tunnel subsets. Demonstrates LLM-driven adaptation of classical perception pipelines in civil infrastructure.

entry.title: Prototype Matters: Modality-unified Prototype Self-distillation for Unsupervised Visible-infrared Person Re-identification

author.name: Menglin Wang, Xiaojin Gong

entry.summary: This paper tackles unsupervised visible-infrared person re-identification by replacing hard optimal-transport label assignment with modality-unified prototype self-distillation, jointly optimizing similarity within and across modalities. The prototype-based approach improves cross-modality association reliability and modality invariance compared to existing contrastive schemes.

entry.title: Fractional-order hardware for neuromorphic computing: Is the order really the problem?

author.name: Christof Teuscher

entry.summary: This review critically examines whether neuromorphic systems need true power-law (fractional-order) memory kernels and what hardware cost that entails, deriving the retained history required for accurate fractional evaluation versus the constant cost of integer-order derivatives. It organizes the hardware literature around this fundamental cost tradeoff, where one fractional operator carries a continuum of timescales tuned by a single parameter.

entry.title: Harness Robotic OS: A Unified Embodied-Agent Runtime for Closed-Loop Quadruped Inspection

author.name: Yaoyuan Yan, Zhiyou Heng, Haoxiang Jie, Gang Liu, Hongjie Yan, Wei Zhou

entry.summary: HROS is a unified embodied-agent runtime organizing quadruped inspection into robot runtime, autonomy skills, cognitive agent runtime, and interaction/operations layers, realized as Argos for residential-community inspection. It aims to replace task-specific integrations with a traceable closed loop connecting sensing, scene understanding, human interaction, and enterprise response.

entry.title: Morphology-Aware Human Motion Retargeting for Wheeled-Humanoid Loco-Manipulation

author.name: Chenbo Xia, Chao Ye

entry.summary: The paper presents a reproducible pipeline converting SMPLX human motion datasets into loco-manipulation behavior for the Galaxea R1 Pro wheeled humanoid, redistributing human lower-body motion across base motion and torso posture while preserving manipulation-relevant arm geometry. It builds on GMR retargeting and BeyondMimic's simulated learning framework.

entry.title: Learning Agent-based Model Predictive Control for Holistic Vehicle Performance

author.name: Jiaming Zhong, Reza Valiollahi Mehrizi, Mohammad Pirani, Chao Yu, Alireza Kasaiezadeh, Yash Vardhan Pant, Amir Khajepour

entry.summary: This paper proposes LAMPC, a hybrid control scheme combining agent-based model predictive control with data-driven learning, using Gaussian process regression with online data management to predict unknown agent contributions in multi-agent vehicle systems. This relaxes the idealized assumption that all agents and their contributions are known, making distributed MPC practical for real multi-vehicle deployments.

entry.title: The Locally Optimal Discursive Posture

author.name: deanball

entry.summary: A reflective essay by an established AI policy writer arguing that the AI safety and policy community, especially in Washington, Sacramento, and Albany, systematically avoids candid discussion of self-sovereign AI (agents as independent world actors) to stay within the Overton Window. The author acknowledges holding concerning beliefs about self-sovereign AI for three years while softening public messaging.

entry.title: One resignation turned the embers of AI fear into a wildfire

author.name: Nathan Lambert

entry.summary: Nathan Lambert analyzes why a single high-profile safety-motivated resignation from Anthropic catalyzed mass public engagement with extreme AI-risk narratives, arguing that rising stakes (e.g., the OpenAI-HuggingFace incident and the Navier-Stokes result) had dried the metaphorical damp ground. He predicts the mainstreaming of strong x-risk views will materially change the AI policy and industry landscape.

entry.title: Decision-Focused Active Learning for Scale-Aware Critical-Materials Recovery

author.name: Niranjan Srinivas, Debajyoti Ray, Elias Nakouzi

entry.summary: Analyzes PNNL's CICERO autonomous precipitation workflow and shows decision-focused active learning selects better rare-earth recovery experiments than nonadaptive space-filling baselines, reaching recorded enrichment maxima with fewer experiments on recycled NdFeB magnet records. This links lab-scale autonomous experimentation to scale-up economics for critical materials.

entry.title: Fortunate Recall: Ontology-Driven Memory Lifecycle Management for Persistent Coherence in LLMs

author.name: Ansuman Mullick, Eray T\"uz\"un

entry.summary: Fortunate Recall is a composable policy layer that classifies personal facts into a 10+1 behavioral ontology and applies category-specific lifecycle policies including temporal decay, slot-key supersession, and category-aware retrieval routing. FR-Bank reaches 76.9% pass rate on the new 516-question LifecycleBench, addressing unbounded memory growth and degraded retrieval precision.

entry.title: Modality-Decoupled Federated Learning for Privacy-Preserving Embodied Intelligence in 6G

author.name: Zhuodong Liu, Xiangyu Li, Chunhong Yuan, Hongyang Du, Bodong Shang, Qingqing Wu, Tony Q. S. Quek, Mohsen Guizani

entry.summary: Proposes a federated learning scheme tailored to vision-language-action models in 6G-enabled multi-robot systems, decoupling updates across vision, language, and action pathways to handle differing parameter scales, privacy exposure, and update dynamics. Targets privacy, communication efficiency, and heterogeneity in distributed embodied agents.

entry.title: Improving Cross-Lingual Token Representations by Adding a Pinch of SALT

author.name: Guillem Ram\'irez

entry.summary: SALT is a lightweight post-training method that injects span-level supervision into existing cross-lingual sentence encoders to improve token-level representations, addressing the mismatch between sentence-level training and token-level usage. It achieves the best overall results on four of five multilingual token-level benchmarks while also improving sentence-level performance. Useful for low-resource and multilingual applications.

entry.title: PACE: Perceived-Latency-Aware Cascading Service Routing and Filler Control for QoE-Efficient Retrieval-Augmented Dialogue Serving

author.name: Lin Huang, Yujuan Tan, Weisheng Li, Lixiang Zeng, Kun Yang, Yongzong Wang, Suihan Xiao

entry.summary: PACE formalizes perceived time-to-first-response as a QoE objective for retrieval-augmented dialogue serving, jointly controlling cascade routing, filler content during waiting, and volatility-aware cache admission. Deployed on a humanoid-robot sales service over 75k requests, it halves P95 latency versus pure-LLM serving and outperforms RAG by 2.4x at high load with equal quality.

entry.title: IBIB: A Protocol for Measuring Enterprise AI Systems by Serving Route, Not Model Identifier

author.name: Blake Stenstrom, Charangan Vasantharajan, Brian Sathianathan

entry.summary: The paper argues that benchmarking model identifiers rather than serving routes is a measurement error since enterprise capability depends on weights, precision, output contract, and harness. It proposes IB2, a protocol with capability-binding preflight checks, reliability-inclusive first-pass scoring, and score-blind adjudication, released with algorithms and schemas.

entry.title: From Connectivity to Rewards: Dense Reward Learning with Directed State Graphs

author.name: Shuyuan Zhang, Zihan Wang, Xiao-Wen Chang, Doina Precup

entry.summary: Improves goal-conditioned hierarchical RL by treating learned state graphs as environmental models that encode connectivity and state accessibility rather than mere subgoal samplers. The work targets quasimetric environments where asymmetric state transitions destabilize policy learning and path planning, deriving dense rewards from directed graph structure. Addresses a real gap in graph-based GCHRL methods.

entry.title: TART: A Modular Tool for Technique-Aware Audio-to-Tablature Guitar Transcription

author.name: Akshaj Gupta, Hwi Joo Park, Andrea Guzman, Shamak Gowda, Samhita Konduri, Jiachen Lian, Robin Netzorg, Gopala Anumanchipalli

entry.summary: TART is a modular four-stage pipeline for guitar audio-to-tablature transcription that handles expressive techniques (slides, bends, percussive hits), assigns correct string-fret combinations using an audio-conditioned T5 model, and improves robustness to noisy recordings. It is evaluated zero-shot on GuitarSet, EGDB, and augmented benchmarks.

entry.title: Improving Faint Object Detection for Space Situational Awareness with Variational Autoencoders

author.name: Angela Cratere, Luca Ghilardi, Vishnu Reddy, Francesco Dell'Olio, Charalampos S. Kouzinopoulos, Roberto Furfaro

entry.summary: The authors present a deep-learning pipeline for detecting faint moving objects in optical space situational awareness imagery, combining a lightweight Tiny-U-Net stellar mask generator with a partial-convolution VAE (astro-VAE) that reconstructs background and removes stars. This targets the difficult cislunar regime where structured backgrounds and moonlight defeat classical detection algorithms. Improved faint-object detection has direct value for space-domain awareness and tracking.

entry.title: Toward Interpretable Multimodal Fusion: Heat Conduction Modeling for Hyperspectral and LiDAR Joint Classification

author.name: Kan Wei, Jiahui Cui, Jing Yao, Xinyu Zhao, Lei Wang, Pedram Ghamisi

entry.summary: M2Heat is a physics-inspired framework for fusing hyperspectral and LiDAR data through heat conduction, using a visual heat conduction module and frequency value embeddings to simulate anisotropic information flow with sub-quadratic complexity. It aims for interpretable multimodal fusion with global dependency modeling.

entry.title: 3D Euler-Angle Orientation Control for Two-Ray Fading Mitigation in Maritime Air-to-Sea Communications

author.name: Mohammed Bajja, Abdoul Karim A. H. Saliah, Hajar El Hammouti, Daniel Bonilla Licea, Giuseppe Silano

entry.summary: This paper treats full 3D UAV attitude as a physical-layer control variable to mitigate two-ray fading in maritime air-to-sea links, deriving an affine constructive-interference condition in Euler angles with closed-form minimum-norm attitude candidates. A differentiable soft-minimum rule feeds a constrained NMPC tracker validated for attitude-based fade mitigation.

entry.title: Myocardial Strain Drift Correction in Deep Learning Based Ultrasound Tracking

author.name: Thierry Judge, Nicolas Duchateau, Andreas {\O}stvik, Havard Dalen, Bj{\o}rnar Grenne, Pierre-Yves Courand, Lasse Lovstakken, Pierre-Marc Jodoin, Olivier Bernard

entry.summary: Extends a state-of-the-art echocardiographic tracking network (TAS-Net) with persistent memory tokens across cardiac cycles and teacher-student fine-tuning to correct temporal drift in myocardial motion tracking, improving the accuracy of strain-based cardiac biomarkers.

entry.title: Elastoformer: Enabling Dynamic Adaptivity via Elastic Model Transformation

author.name: Sudaksh Kalra, Dolly Sapra

entry.summary: Elastoformer transforms conventional neural networks into elastic networks whose computation adapts at runtime to fluctuating latency, power, and memory constraints in edge deployments. This addresses the rigidity of fixed execution flows in dynamic EdgeAI conditions. Relevant to on-device vision and adaptive inference.

entry.title: RiLM: Parameter-Efficient Language Modeling via Geodesic Decoding

author.name: Fang Li

entry.summary: RiLM is a sub-million-parameter language modeling framework that eliminates the output matrix entirely, unfolding context as a trajectory on a Riemannian manifold and deriving next-token probabilities from squared geodesic distance to vocabulary embeddings. Instantiations on flat and hyperbolic geometry use roughly 290k parameters, targeting edge deployment and reproducibility.

entry.title: Phases in a class of associative memories via hidden neurons

author.name: Toshihiro Ota, Masato Taki

entry.summary: Studies the Krotov-Hopfield bipartite associative memory class using hidden neurons as order parameters of retrieval, deriving replica-symmetric phase diagrams and closed-form capacities at polynomial load, and connecting polynomial and exponential regimes within one architecture. The work unifies previously separate analyses of Hopfield network storage scales via statistical mechanics. Bridging physics and modern attention-like architectures.

entry.title: How Wrong Can a Good Predictor Be? Diverging Updates with Vanishing Predictive KL

author.name: Qifu Wen, Shuaijun Liu, Zihan Zhou, Xi Zeng, Ningxin Su

entry.summary: This theory paper proves that in a symmetric Gaussian HMM, an approximate filter's update map can diverge unboundedly from exact Bayesian mixing in logit space while predictive KL vanishes, showing that good predictions do not imply accurate posterior approximation. It quantifies this separation along stationary trajectories with an explicit rate.

entry.title: MUC-FL: Block-Wise Marginal Utility Contribution for Communication-Efficient Federated Learning

author.name: Akshay Mhatre, Vikram Karthick, Deepti Gupta, Jia Zou

entry.summary: MUC-FL selectively transmits only the highest marginal-utility data blocks in federated learning, showing on multimodal MIMIC clinical data that just 24 of 1,135 blocks carry meaningful signal, enabling 45-50% communication reduction while maintaining or improving model quality versus deduplication baselines.

entry.title: A Voice-Interactive Multi-Agent System for Smart Operating Rooms: Architecture Design and Key Technologies

author.name: Tianxiang Zhou

entry.summary: SurgicalRoomAgent is an LLM-based voice-interactive multi-agent system for smart operating rooms, with a voice pipeline (wake word, ASR, turn detection, TTS) and an agent core (skill registry, task planner, device manager). Key technical contributions include KV cache prefix warming that cuts recomputation from ~500 ms to tens of milliseconds and streaming partial JSON parsing for early parallel task execution.

entry.title: Beyond Benchmarks: Using VLMs to Reveal Systematic Classification Failures Under Real World Conditions

author.name: Dieuwertje Alblas, Alma M. Liezenga, Jan Erik van Woerden, Fedor Taggenbrock, Dalia Aljawaheri, Klamer Schutte

entry.summary: The authors explore using vision-language model embeddings to automatically distill human-interpretable systematic error patterns from classification models, replacing manual inspection in verification and validation. They address challenges of deploying VLMs in the underrepresented defence domain with limited context diversity.

entry.title: Doom as a bad method not a utopia trade-off

author.name: KatjaGrace

entry.summary: Katja Grace argues against treating AI outcomes as a utopia-versus-doom expected-value trade-off where high utopia probability offsets extinction risk. Using survey data and a driving analogy, she contends that high-variance bad outcomes should be evaluated as bad methods of achieving good outcomes, not netted against them.

entry.title: Gradland: On Phenomenal Experience, Differentiated Across Many Dimensions

author.name: David Balduzzi

entry.summary: David Balduzzi proposes that the structure of phenomenal experience is characterized by gradient/Jacobian structure of physical interaction, formalized in an idealized differentiable world called Gradland. He introduces measures of Jacobian structure (effective rank, cohesion via Kirchhoff complexity) and shows they account for features of experience such as duration, vividness, and texture.

entry.title: From State Synchronization to Cognitive Self-Evolution: An Operational Architecture for Cognitive Digital Twins

author.name: Haoran Gao, An Li, Zhen Li, Jun Cai

entry.summary: Proposes a four-layer operational architecture for Cognitive Digital Twins (CDTs) spanning physical, digital-twin, cognitive, and task layers, forming a self-evolving closed operational loop. It systematizes how cognition can be integrated into digital twin architectures beyond ad-hoc use of learning modules, knowledge graphs, and LLMs. This offers a unifying design framework for a rapidly growing area in industrial AI.

entry.title: Procedural Memory Under Change: Reuse and Interference in Controlled Web Tasks

author.name: Yanze Cao

entry.summary: This paper studies when stored procedural memory in language agents remains valid as interfaces change, using a BrowserGym-based case study and controlled frozen-memory comparisons on synthetic shopping tasks. It shows memory reuse can cause interference and degraded decisions when the environment shifts, highlighting a gap in current agent memory designs.

entry.title: Compute-Bounded Security Assurance - Coverage, Verification, and Response under Resource Constraints

author.name: Jithin VG, Ditto PS

entry.summary: Develops a formal framework separating distinct security-assurance quantities under inference-compute constraints: repeated success, unique coverage, and accepted evidence. It derives coverage formulas for repeated conditionally independent attempts and shows that positive outcome correlation does not by itself imply a coverage ceiling, constructing counterexample models with equal mean and correlation but different limiting coverage. This clarifies common statistical fallacies when reasoning about verification budgets.

entry.title: Critical initialization destabilizes higher input derivatives in wide scalar-input networks

author.name: Prashant Singh, Pranav Singh

entry.summary: This theoretical paper extends the edge-of-chaos analysis of wide randomly initialized networks to higher-order input derivatives, deriving mean-field recursions through third order that are exact at the variance fixed point. It shows that while first-derivative variance is depth-invariant at criticality, second-derivative variance grows linearly with depth whenever the activation has nonzero curvature. This matters for physics-informed networks, score matching, and other methods relying on higher-order derivatives.

entry.title: A Statistical Approach to Estimating Sample Size of Machine Learning Models

author.name: Dat Phan-Trong, Sunil Gupta, Svetha Venkatesh

entry.summary: Proposes a framework for sample-size determination for nonlinear ML prediction models by approximating them with localized linear representations and evaluating statistical power across local regions. This bridges classical power analysis and flexible ML models without requiring a priori effect specifications.

entry.title: Which Medical Questions Deserve Rationales? Perturbation-Sensitive Selection for Robust QA

author.name: Yuexin Wu, Dayou Yu, Vasile Rus

entry.summary: Proposes RMS-RSP, a method for selecting which already-labeled medical QA questions should receive scarce rationale supervision by perturbing hidden states at rationale tokens and measuring margin shifts. Evaluated with MedGemma-4B across five medical QA datasets under a fixed token budget.

entry.title: Forward-Free LLM Depth Pruning via Weight Redundancy

author.name: Vincent-Daniel Yun, Woosang Lim

entry.summary: The paper proposes Weight-Redundancy Pruning, a forward-free depth-pruning method that selects redundant Transformer blocks to remove by comparing attention and MLP projection weights across layers, requiring no calibration data or forward passes. This lowers the cost of LLM compression relative to activation-based methods. Useful for efficient model deployment pipelines.

entry.title: A Trust-Network-Based Federated Learning Framework for Multi-Center Aging Clock Prediction

author.name: Chunxu Zhang, Bo Li, Wenliang Wang, Yang Liu, Di Jiang, Yuan Huang, Yo-ichi Nabeshima, Akinori Yamamura, Bo Yang, Qiang Yang

entry.summary: TNFL is a trust-network-based federated learning framework for biological aging-clock prediction across medical centers, handling sparse directional trust, small local samples, and heterogeneous data drift. It retains age-predictive performance while supporting protein-interaction interpretation under privacy constraints.

entry.title: One Loop, Two Gains: Can Active Learning win the Lottery for Free?

author.name: Benedikt Tscheschner, Eduardo Veas, Marc Masana

entry.summary: This paper connects the lottery ticket hypothesis with pool-based active learning, observing that the iterative retraining loop in active learning already supplies the repeated cycles that iterative magnitude pruning needs. It exploits this shared structure to discover sparse winning tickets at no additional training cost.

entry.title: AUC Maximization from Biased Positive-unlabeled Data with Confidence

author.name: Atsutoshi Kumagai, Tomoharu Iwata, Hiroshi Takahashi, Taishi Nishiyama, Kazuki Adachi, Yasuhiro Fujiwara

entry.summary: Proposes a method for AUC maximization from biased positive-unlabeled data, relaxing the standard assumption that labeled positives are unbiased samples from the true positive distribution. The key idea exploits confidence information to correct the bias, targeting settings where negative data cannot be collected due to privacy or annotation costs. Practically relevant for imbalanced classification under imperfect labeling.

entry.title: Measuring the Value of World-Model Updates: A Counterfactual Utility Protocol for Continual Adaptation

author.name: Anqi Peter Li, Kaden Kim

entry.summary: Introduces the fork ledger, a protocol that branches a deployment stream at pre-registered decision points into matched update and hold continuations under common random numbers, measuring the return difference of individual world-model updates. Experiments on three simulated control tasks show that always applying a fixed update mechanism lowers return, e.g., CartPole at -144.0. A thoughtful evaluation methodology for continual world models, though demonstrated only in simulation.

entry.title: EMMI: Edge Multi-Modal Intelligence for Communication-Efficient MLLM Inference via Fused Representation Compression

author.name: Motahare Mounesan, Irfan Khan

entry.summary: EMMI proposes sending compact fused representations instead of raw sensor data between edge devices and servers for multimodal LLM inference, using modality-specific encoding and cross-modal fusion to cut communication costs. This addresses the deployment of MLLMs on bandwidth- and compute-constrained edge platforms.

entry.title: Convex Optimization with Nested Evolving Feasible Sets (CONES) under Time-Varying Loss Functions

author.name: Rahul Vaze

entry.summary: This paper extends the CONES framework, online convex optimization over a nested, shrinking feasible region, to the setting where loss functions also vary over time. It analyzes projected proximal algorithms and provides regret and movement-cost guarantees relative to a hindsight static optimum while maintaining feasibility at all times. This generalizes nested convex body chasing to a richer class of online decision problems.

entry.title: Local Robustness Quantification for Naive Bayes Classifiers and Generative Forests: a General Approach

author.name: Adri\'an Detavernier, Jasper De Bock

entry.summary: The authors develop general methods for quantifying the local robustness of generative classifier predictions (naive Bayes and generative forests) by measuring how much the underlying probabilistic graphical model distribution can be perturbed without changing a prediction. They handle perturbation neighborhoods defined by epsilon-contamination, total variation distance, and chi-squared divergence balls, and validate on benchmark datasets. This extends robustness quantification beyond discriminative classifiers to a broad class of probabilistic models.

entry.title: LoaDiff: Conditional Generation of Electricity Consumption Time Series for Energy Analytics

author.name: Mariia Baranova, Adrien Petralia, Etienne Le Naour, Nathan Etourneau, Guillaume Hofmann, Themis Palpanas

entry.summary: LoaDiff is a diffusion-based generative model producing year-long, sub-hourly synthetic smart-meter load curves, conditioned on static household attributes and dynamic factors. It addresses privacy-driven access restrictions on granular consumption data while enabling load forecasting and demand-side analysis.

entry.title: From Protocols to Evidence: Bounded Claims for AI in Service of the Common Good

author.name: Nitesh V. Chawla, Paulo Benanti

entry.summary: This governance-focused paper argues that responsible AI must evaluate both the deployed system and the institutional failures it enters, examining what protocols like the EU AI Act, NIST AI RMF, and ISO/IEC 42001 actually establish and whose power they leave untouched. It proposes bounding claims about AI's contribution to the common good.

entry.title: PEARL: A Task-Aware Framework for Evaluating Differentially Private Synthetic Educational Data

author.name: Xianghui Meng, Yujing Zhang, Jionghao Lin

entry.summary: PEARL is a framework that approves differentially private synthetic educational datasets only after passing joint checks of validity, privacy protection, predictive usefulness, and suitability for the intended personalized learning task, with a release ledger component. It fills the gap of evaluations that assess privacy and utility separately without checking task fitness. It matters for safe deployment of learner-data-driven educational systems.

entry.title: Meta-Learning for Data-Efficient Plant Growth Estimation via Vision Transformers and Fuzzy Clustering

author.name: Sheikh Hasan Elahi, Rusith Chamara Hathurusinghe Dewage, Habib Ullah, Muhammad Salman Siddiqui, Rakibul Islam, Fadi Al Machot

entry.summary: The paper proposes a few-shot regression framework for greenhouse plant growth estimation that combines Vision Transformer embeddings, fuzzy c-means clustering for task construction from an unlabeled image pool, and gradient-based meta-learning. A key empirical finding is that how tasks are constructed in embedding space is a primary driver of performance, with second-order methods like MAML++ outperforming alternatives. This reduces costly labeling requirements for agricultural monitoring.

entry.title: Coherent Floquet quantum reservoirs for molecular property prediction

author.name: Luofei Wang, Da Zhang, Congren Wang, Yiming Li, Yuxiao Yang, Xuan Zhang, Xuefeng Cui, Zhang-Qi Yin
