entry.summary: The paper constructs a discrete-time-crystal-based quantum reservoir computing architecture that processes molecular graph events and surface-hopping frames via coherent Floquet evolution, producing fixed-dimension feature vectors for classical decoders. It applies this to inhibitor-activity and blood-brain-barrier molecular property prediction. This is a novel intersection of quantum reservoir computing and computational chemistry.

entry.title: Rethinking Radiomap Blind Prediction with Limited Environment and Configuration Representations

author.name: Xiaojie Li, Yu Han, Han Fang, Shangqing Liu, Shi Jin, Chao-Kai Wen

entry.summary: This paper reformulates radiomap blind prediction as inferring radio maps from incomplete environment and base-station representations, identifying the conditional-mean radiomap as the optimal target under squared loss and decomposing domain risk into approximation error and irreducible uncertainty. It proposes RadioDecomp, which uses propagation priors as a correctable base predictor plus residual learning. The principled risk decomposition and prior-correction design could influence wireless channel modeling beyond this specific task.

entry.title: Predicting Train Delays in Finland Using Machine Learning and Weather Data

author.name: Vinicius Pozzobon Borin, Jean Michel de Souza Sant'Ana, Nurul Huda Mahmood

entry.summary: This paper applies machine learning to predict train delays in Finland using a new dataset (FI-TW) that fuses railway operational records with nationwide weather sensor observations, emphasizing domain-informed feature engineering over raw meteorological inputs. It is motivated by Arctic conditions where extreme weather is a leading delay cause, and connects to future 6G sensing and edge-computing infrastructure for real-time environmental intelligence. The work matters for transportation reliability and demonstrates the value of domain-aware ML on real operational data.

entry.title: A Two-Mirror Faceted Projection System for EUV Lithography

author.name: Vasiliy A. Es'kin, Egor V. Ivanov, Olga V. Martynova

entry.summary: This paper proposes an all-reflective two-mirror projection system for EUV lithography at 13.5 nm and 11.2 nm wavelengths, achieving near-unity numerical aperture and fourfold demagnification. By routing each diffraction order through a dedicated pair of planar mirror facets, it fixes reflections at two per order, raising optical throughput to 50-60 percent versus under 15 percent for conventional 6-10 mirror designs. Despite appearing under a machine learning category, it is a classical optics and semiconductor manufacturing contribution.

entry.title: Hologram Representation via Quadratic Phase Gaussian Splatting

author.name: Haolong Wang, Yicheng Zhan, Kaan Ak\c{s}it, Simeng Qiu

entry.summary: CVQPG replaces standard 2D Gaussian primitives in Gaussian splatting with complex-valued quadratic phase functions, adding learnable curvature parameters for hologram representation. It improves holographic reconstruction quality by +0.19 dB (RGB) and +0.33 dB (grayscale) over state-of-the-art at equal parameter counts. The work shows that modulating primitive wavefronts is a lightweight, effective enhancement for holographic scene representation.

entry.title: Enabling Knowledge Graph Understanding at Scale with the EXplore Your Graphs ENgine (EXYGEN)

author.name: Harshdeep Singh, Yurui Zhu, Giovanni Colavizza, Matteo Romanello

entry.summary: EXYGEN is a framework for conversational access to large knowledge graphs, studying how well LLMs can perform text-to-SPARQL generation using only automatically derived structured metadata (VoID descriptions, ShEx schemas) and small graph samples in a RAG pipeline without fine-tuning. The best configuration reaches 0.419 exact match on execution results on the SciQA benchmark. It also shows that lexical metrics overestimate correctness, an important evaluation caveat.

entry.title: Identifiability of Nonnegative Tensor Decompositions via Positive Scattering

author.name: Haoming Wang, Ming Yuan

entry.summary: The paper introduces a positive scattering term capturing how positivity of tensor components constrains competing decompositions, combined with the dimension budget of the Lovitz-Petrov generalization of Kruskal's theorem. It derives sufficient conditions (thresholds 2|S|-2 and 2|S|-1 over component subsets) guaranteeing minimality, nonnegative rank, and uniqueness. This advances the theoretical foundations of nonnegative tensor decomposition identifiability.

entry.title: Multimodal Taxonomic Conditioning for Generative Plankton Imagery

author.name: Daniela Ivanova, Ozgu Goksu, Nicolas Pugeault

entry.summary: The paper generates synthetic plankton images conditioned on taxonomy using a CLIP encoder adapted with a ranked contrastive objective over ragged taxonomies, frozen to condition a parameter-efficient diffusion transformer. The goal is to bolster long-tailed ecological datasets where rare taxa lack training images.

entry.title: Reflex-Informed Neuromuscular Reinforcement Learning for Muscle-Driven Locomotion

author.name: Jian Zhou, Xingyu Zhang, Rui Ma, Yu Cao, Shane Xie, Zhi-qiang Zhang

entry.summary: A reflex-informed RL framework for muscle-driven locomotion where a fixed phase-dependent reflex controller underlies neuromuscular control and the policy modulates biomechanically meaningful reflex gains and thresholds for hip, knee, and ankle. It targets physiologically plausible, disturbance-adaptive human movement simulation.

entry.title: Learning structural balance of graphs from quantum spectral features

author.name: Stefano Scali, Oleksandr Kyriienko

entry.summary: The paper embeds signed graphs as Ising instances and uses standardized moments of the density of states as machine-learning features, proving these moments are switching-invariant and size-free. It benchmarks on the NP-hard frustration index, with classical samplability at zero field enabling certification of the quantum extraction procedure.

entry.title: Differentially Private EEG Feature Anonymization: A Privacy-Utility Case Study in Clinical Neurophysiology

author.name: Noman Sadiq, Mohsen Toorani

entry.summary: A case study applying subject-level differential privacy to EEG-derived features, examining the tradeoff between re-identification protection and preservation of clinically relevant signal characteristics. It highlights limits of conventional anonymization for high-dimensional biomedical signals.

entry.title: Domain-Specific Hallucination Detection in Large Language Models

author.name: Varun Teja Chundru, Debasmita Biswas

entry.summary: A multi-signal hallucination detection pipeline combining fine-tuned DeBERTa-v3, MC Dropout uncertainty, and temperature-scaled calibration, achieving F1=0.915 and AUROC=0.977 on HaluEval. Ablations suggest genuine entailment reasoning rather than surface-pattern exploitation.

entry.title: Generative Marketing Mix Modeling: A Causal Inference Framework Linking GEO and GEM to Business Impact

author.name: Masahiro Kato, Daiki Honma, Taka Kato

entry.summary: The paper proposes Generative Marketing Mix Modeling (GMMM), a causal framework to estimate effects of Generative Engine Optimization and sponsored placements in generative AI answers, combining generated-answer sampling, question counts, and notice probabilities. It provides identification conditions and empirical evaluation.

entry.title: Analyzing Traditional and Neural Approaches to Multilingual Readability Assessment

author.name: Joshua Wong, Chris Tanner

entry.summary: This paper tests whether transformer models internalize the same linguistic features that drive feature-based readability classifiers, using SHAP explanations as TCAV concept probes across five languages on the ReadMe++ dataset. It addresses the concern that high accuracy on subjective readability labels may reflect surface patterns rather than genuine linguistic structure. The work bridges interpretability and readability assessment in a multilingual setting.

entry.title: Using Semantic Uncertainty to Estimate Transition Relevance in Turn-taking

author.name: Muhammad Umair, Jan P. de Ruiter

entry.summary: This paper proposes modeling turn-taking in spoken dialogue by using LLM-derived semantic uncertainty to predict Transition Relevance Places, mimicking how human listeners anticipate floor-taking opportunities from unfolding meaning. It connects conversation analysis theory with modern LLM uncertainty measures. The result could improve timing of responses in unscripted dialogue systems.

entry.title: MultiHuSE: A Multimodal Dataset for Humour Styles and Emotions

author.name: Mary Ogbuka Kenneth, Foaad Khosmood, Abbas Edalat

entry.summary: MultiHuSE is a multimodal dataset of 2,407 HD videos of 50 diverse actors performing 1,463 texts across four psychological humour styles plus neutral content, with emotion annotations for a subset. Multiple actor interpretations of the same texts enable control over delivery variation. It enables computational humor research beyond binary classification, incorporating psychological dimensions.

entry.title: SEAR: Segment-Evidence-Aware Routing for Weak-to-Strong Multilingual Speech MCQ

author.name: Huy Hoang Le, Long-Bao Nguyen, Minh Tri Dao

entry.summary: SEAR is a challenge-system paper for MLC-SLM Task 2 that adapts Qwen3-Omni-30B-A3B-Instruct with a pipeline converting timestamped ASR into event spans, then synthesizing 359,825 verified MCQs using existing models including Qwen3.6-27B and Gemini 3.1 Flash-Lite. A text-only probe partitions data into weak and strong items for a weak-to-strong training curriculum. The system targets multilingual conversational speech understanding.

entry.title: Beyond Word Error Rate: A Switch Aware Evaluation of ASR and Audio Language Models on English Yoruba Code-Switched Speech

author.name: Chibuzor Okocha, Christan Earl Grant

entry.summary: Evaluates eleven ASR systems and audio LMs on English-Yoruba code-switched speech using a deterministic 2,000-utterance set and switch-localized diagnostics including switch-entry token error rate and windowed switch-point error rates. The central finding is that aggregate WER hides code-switching failure behavior in low-resource, diacritic-rich languages. Provides better evaluation tools for code-switched speech.

entry.title: IndicTriMix: Developing Language Identification Datasets and Models for Tri-Language Code-Mixing

author.name: Pruthwik Mishra, Rudra Trivedi, Avi Patel, Ashok Urlana, Shrikant Malviya

entry.summary: IndicTriMix frames token-level language identification in tri-language code-mixed text as sequence labeling and fine-tunes MuRIL and XLM-RoBERTa across Hindi, Gujarati, and Bengali configurations. The work releases benchmark datasets and models for an understudied multilingual NLP setting common in Indian social media.

entry.title: The Semantic Elevation Operator and the Closure of the Undecidable Class under Preservation

author.name: Jose Pascual Gumbau Mezquita

entry.summary: A theory paper formalizing a semantic elevation operator that converts static decidability questions about program properties into dynamic questions about property preservation under self-modification. It proves that for intensional transformations the elevated property remains undecidable, using Kleene's recursion theorem rather than Rice's theorem.

entry.title: Mi-Ripple: Restoring Images Degraded by Iterative AI Editing

author.name: Jiayin Chen, Yicheng Xu, Muting Wang

entry.summary: Identifies and removes digital ripple artifacts (grid-like and granular textures) introduced by iterative reference-conditioned image editing, separating periodic lattice artifacts from content-entangled texture and combining spectral notching with structure-aware smoothing and cleaned-reference regeneration. Addresses an emerging artifact class unique to AI editing pipelines.

entry.title: Predictive Multi-Landmark OCT Tracking for Increased Motion Robustness

author.name: Konrad Reuter, Suresh Guttikonda, Chaitali Uday Karekar, Christian Betz, Alexander Schlaefer

entry.summary: Propagates positional updates between multiple sequentially tracked OCT landmarks to obtain a global 6D pose prediction, achieving sub-millimeter RMSE at velocities up to 100 mm/s across up to nine landmarks. Improves markerless motion tracking robustness for OCT-guided interventions.

entry.title: Lie-Algebraic Bell Recurrences for Arbitrary-Order Twist Jets and Parallel-Mechanism Closure

author.name: Daniel Condurache

entry.summary: The paper develops a Lie-algebraic kinematic construction that unifies serial propagation, parallel-mechanism closure, and rigid-platform point fields using dual screws and Bell polynomials to organize arbitrary-order derivatives. It provides closed-form, native treatment of cylindrical joints and covariant formulas for serial twist jets across noncommuting factors.

entry.title: Quantitative Diffusive Limits for Singular Nonlocal Transport

author.name: Andrea Agazzi, Giuseppe Bruno, Federico Pasqualotto, Philippe Rigollet

entry.summary: This pure-mathematics paper proves sharp, uniform-in-time convergence rates for a nonlocal continuity equation on Riemannian manifolds, showing its solutions converge to heat flow at rate O(b^2) via uniform dissipation of a weighted resolvent energy. It also analyzes the corresponding N-particle dynamics on the circle using a modulated-energy weak-strong argument.

entry.title: AI #185: Preference Cascade

author.name: Zvi

entry.summary: Zvi's weekly AI news roundup covering the wave of public risk statements following Jacob Coxon's resignation from Anthropic, a proposed Congressional ban on superintelligence, the Claude Fable and Mythos 5.1 system card and capabilities, and OpenAI agent security incidents. It functions as curated commentary and signal aggregation rather than original research.

entry.title: ARENA 8.0 Impact Report

author.name: JScriven

entry.summary: An evaluation of the ARENA 8.0 AI-safety upskilling program held at the London Initiative for Safe AI (May-June 2026), assessed against four success criteria: participant quality, ML skill development, community integration, and career transition into AI safety. The 26 in-person participants rated the program 8.8/10 on average, with many holding doctorates or prior AI safety experience. This is a field-building report rather than a research paper, but it documents the capacity of the AI safety talent pipeline.

entry.title: Beyond Surface Imitation: Contrastive Modeling for Reasoning Path Alignment in Multimodal In-Context Learning

author.name: Mingbo Yang, Wenqiang Wang, Zhaolu Kang, Peng Chen, Yannan Chen, Sunshang Wang, Yan Xiao

entry.summary: The authors propose a multimodal ICL framework combining contrastive demonstration modeling with MLLM self-refinement to align responses with the reasoning path required by the input rather than imitating surface patterns. The approach targets complex multimodal tasks where standard in-context demonstrations underperform.

entry.title: Compact Visuotactile World Models for Lifting: Prediction, Reward Alignment, and Force Constraints

author.name: Qinzhen Ma (Rice University)

entry.summary: Studies a 652K-parameter action-conditioned visuotactile world model for force-constrained robotic lifting, evaluating 34 policies across 120 MuJoCo environments. Model-assisted force feedback raises in-distribution force-budgeted success from 73.3% to 93.3%, and the paper probes when accurate tactile forecasts actually improve control.

entry.title: NOPE-HYPE: A Structured Simulation Workflow for Robust Speech-to-Text Across Diverse Acoustic Environments

author.name: Niramay M. Patel, Bibek Behera, Raksha Sharma

entry.summary: NOPE-HYPE is a structured training workflow combining a controllable acoustic environment simulator, coverage-optimal environment reduction on PSD templates, and interpretable hyperparameter search to improve speech-to-text robustness. Simulator-generated noise performs comparably to balanced real-noise training for Whisper and SeamlessM4T models. Practical for making speech systems robust to unseen conditions.

entry.title: CoRA-NAS: Coarse Ranking and Anchor-Residual Refinement for Neural Architecture Search

author.name: Yifan Yang, Zhaoyan Wang, Zheng Gao, Xiaoyu Li, Jiaojiao Jiang

entry.summary: CoRA-NAS is a two-stage NAS framework combining zero-cost proxy consensus ranking with learning-curve extrapolation from anchor architectures and a learned residual correction via ExtraTrees, using roughly 1% of full training cost. It operates without fully trained accuracy labels and with one configuration across search spaces.

entry.title: Rethinking Handwritten Character Recognition

author.name: Ranjit Raut, Aarav Subedi, Ashim Shrestha

entry.summary: GraphemeNet is a multi-script handwritten character recognition architecture that explicitly encodes stroke-level geometric regularities as inductive biases via persistent scaffold injection and script-specific asymmetric convolutions. The goal is structural-prior efficiency: better accuracy with fewer parameters than generic image classification approaches.

entry.title: Modular Kinematic Reduction of Closed-Chain Mechanisms Using Path Assembly and Defect Homotopy

author.name: Mohammad Dastranj, Jouni Mattila

entry.summary: PACDM is a modular framework for resolving closure constraints in closed-chain kinematics, comparing ordered transformation paths with mismatches expressed via the SE(3) logarithm and assembling Jacobians from local derivatives. Rank-revealing analysis selects independent constraints, and a defect homotopy recovers closure-consistent passive coordinates.

entry.title: Introducing Consort: A Spec-First Agent Framework for Enforced, Test-Driven Development on Live Database Branches

author.name: Kevin Hartman

entry.summary: Introduces Consort, a spec-first framework for AI coding agents that enforces test-driven development against live database branches, and characterizes existing agent frameworks (Spec Kit, superpowers, BMAD, GSD) by their enforcement mode: persuasion, front-loaded structure, or other mechanisms. Frames the dev framework as a control system for non-deterministic workers.

entry.title: TrajFusionNet+: Transformer-Based Prediction of Pedestrian Crossing Intention via Fusion of Trajectory Representations and Scene Graphs

author.name: Fran\c{c}ois G. Landry, Moulay A. Akhloufi

entry.summary: TrajFusionNet+ predicts pedestrian crossing intention from an autonomous vehicle's viewpoint using three transformer branches: sequential trajectory attention, visual attention, and a graph-based scene context representation. It extends the authors' previous TrajFusionNet model.

entry.title: Multi-Agent Agentic Graph Learning via Structural Signatures

author.name: Liang Qu, Jianxin Li, Hua Wang

entry.summary: Proposes multi-agent agentic graph learning in which multiple LLM-powered agents with separate memories specialize over heterogeneous graph regions via structural signatures, rather than sharing one reasoning policy across the whole graph. Aims to improve graph reasoning tasks where single-agent or role-based multi-agent designs are suboptimal.

entry.title: From Fixed Keys to Readable Schemas: Small Language Models for Vehicle Agent Function Calls

author.name: Hamed Jafarzadeh Asl, Yuanhao Yu, Vahid Partovi Nia

entry.summary: Compares functional tokens versus schema-in-prompt approaches for small language models translating natural-language requests into vehicle function calls under on-device memory and latency constraints. Introduces a 9,822-example benchmark spanning 79 vehicle functions and analyzes the generalization-versus-overhead tradeoff.

entry.title: Looped GPT-BERT: Trading Parameters for Computation in Small Language Modeling

author.name: Tingshuo Fan, Hongtao Mu, Tianyu Zhou, Hansen Liu, Tao Ji

entry.summary: Combines GPT-BERT objectives with depth-wise parameter sharing in the BabyLM 2026 strict-small setting, training a 4x12 looped model with 12.18M parameters on a 7.48M-word corpus. The looped architecture trades parameters for recurrent computation and achieves competitive leaderboard averages.

entry.title: MetroLLM-Bench: Evaluating Language Models as Transit Kiosk Runtimes

author.name: Remco Hendriks (Continker)

entry.summary: MetroLLM-Bench is a 955-case benchmark testing LLMs as the policy layer of transit kiosks across six real metro systems, with deterministic scoring for routing, fares, disruptions, accessibility, and adversarial input, plus semantic-quality tiers. It requires models to call structured tools and produce machine-renderable terminal states. A concrete agentic evaluation in a public-transit domain.

entry.title: A statistical approach to bias in zero-shot learning: the lens of handwriting recognition

author.name: Clarence Chew, Gim Siang Chia, Sukalpa Chanda, Subhroshekhar Ghosh, Soumendu Sundar Mukherjee

entry.summary: This paper studies the class-prior misclassification bias in generalized zero-shot learning, using zero-shot handwritten word recognition over very large vocabularies as a testbed. It proposes a statistical method that treats any classical GZSL feature learner as a black box and corrects its intrinsic bias toward seen classes, improving scalability to unseen classes.

entry.title: Byzantine-Robust Federated Fire Detection with a Rotating Coordinator

author.name: Georgia Argyrou, Aymen Bahrouny, Hedi Fendriy, Alexander Jung

entry.summary: Applies federated learning to indoor fire detection with edge cameras, addressing limited uplink bandwidth, Byzantine clients, and over-reliance on a single fixed aggregation server. Contributions include a curated fire-detection dataset, an edge-deployable detector with up to 10x compressed updates, and a semi-decentralized Byzantine-robust scheme with a rotating coordinator. Solid systems-plus-robustness work in a safety-relevant domain.

entry.title: HERALD: High-Fidelity Exemplar Retrieval with Adaptive Landmark Distillation for Heterophily-Aware Graph Condensation

author.name: Sujan Chakraborty, Priyanka Saha, Saptarshi Bej

entry.summary: HERALD is a gradient-free graph condensation method that adapts node scoring and feature selection to a graph's measured heterophily, replacing homophily-assuming Weisfeiler-Lehman or gradient-matching approaches. It uses a joint Fisher-discriminability and activation-density criterion to build small surrogate graphs preserving node-classification performance.

entry.title: Semi-Tensor Product-Based Multi-Term Randomized T-SVD and Its Visual Applications

author.name: Xingchen Xiao (School of Mathematics and Statistics, Southwest University, Chongqing, China), Feng Zhang (School of Mathematics and Statistics, Southwest University, Chongqing, China), Wenjin Qin (School of Mathematics and Statistics, Southwest University, Chongqing, China), Jianjun Wang (School of Mathematics and Statistics, Southwest University, Chongqing, China)

entry.summary: The paper proposes a multi-term randomized tensor SVD based on a semi-tensor product framework that relaxes the strict dimensional compatibility constraints of the standard t-product while improving approximation accuracy of earlier single-term STP methods. It targets high-dimensional visual data such as color images and videos with reduced computational cost. The work sits at the intersection of numerical linear algebra and visual data processing.

entry.title: Solving Few-Shot Multiobjective Multitask Optimization via Iterative Sequential Transfer

author.name: Tingyang Wei, Haofeng Wu, Ananda Phan Iman, Zhao Wei, Jiao Liu, Yew-Soon Ong

entry.summary: The paper addresses multitask optimization in few-shot regimes where limited evaluation budgets make it hard to identify elite solution distributions needed for beneficial cross-task transfer, especially in multiobjective settings with continuous Pareto manifolds. It proposes an Iterative Sequential Transfer method to enable knowledge sharing across tasks under strict budget constraints. This matters for computationally expensive real-world optimization where evaluations are scarce.

entry.title: EVTradeMatch: A Mobility-Aware Multi-Objective Matching Framework for EV--EV Energy Trading

author.name: Md. Mahfujur Rahman, Alistair Barros, Raja Jurdak, Darshika Koggalahewa

entry.summary: This paper presents EVTradeMatch, a prediction-guided multi-objective optimization framework for peer-to-peer energy trading between electric vehicles, building on a prior learning-to-rank model for charging-node recommendation. It derives a charging-node suitability score from mobility, energy, and contextual features to guide provider-consumer matching under journey-specific conditions. It matters because EV charging infrastructure is a growing bottleneck and coordinated trading could improve flexibility.

entry.title: Robust Multimodal Sentiment Analysis with Incomplete Modalities via Semantic-aware Completeness based Reconstruction

author.name: Han-Jun Choi, Byunggill Joe, Saim Shin, Jin Yea Jang

entry.summary: The paper introduces a completeness estimation approach that quantifies how much sentiment-relevant information survives in incomplete or noisy modalities, guiding reconstruction of missing semantics in text-centric multimodal fusion. A stabilized multi-task training strategy jointly optimizes sentiment prediction and completeness estimation. Extensive experiments reportedly show robustness gains in realistic missing-modality scenarios.

entry.title: E-CONAN (Entailment, CONtradition And Neutral) Benchmarks: Arabic Textual Entailment and Natural Inference Datasets

author.name: Khloud AL Jallad, Nada Ghneim, Ghaida Rebdawi

entry.summary: This paper introduces E-CONAN, two new benchmark datasets for Arabic natural language inference, built from automatically translated pairs, human-validated machine translations, hand-crafted pairs from Arabic-as-a-foreign-language textbooks, and rumor-bearing news headline pairs. It addresses the scarcity of Arabic textual inference resources and enables evaluation of semantic relation extraction (entailment, contradiction, neutral) for a high-resource-population but NLP-underrepresented language.

entry.title: Distributed Optimization of Modular Production Systems using Model-based Reinforcement Learning with Inverse Models

author.name: Andreas Schwung, Steve Yuwono, Sofiene Lassoued, Dorothea Schwung

entry.summary: This work presents model-based RL for self-learning control of modular manufacturing systems, embedding approximate inverse process models within policy networks to disentangle actuation dynamics from task-space dynamics. A lightweight feedforward inverse-model architecture enables RL training purely in task space, validated on a laboratory testbed with heterogeneous production modules. The approach improves learning efficiency for flexible distributed manufacturing control.

entry.title: Automated Identification of Competing Narratives in Political Discourse on Social Media

author.name: Sergej Wildemann, Erick Elejalde

entry.summary: This paper presents an unsupervised multi-stage pipeline combining topic modeling, event detection, and event linking to identify competing political narratives in German politicians' tweets. It forms events into coherent stories and uncovers ideological oppositions. The framework supports analysis of how narratives evolve across political camps on social media.

entry.title: Automatic Lyric Transcription for Greek Songs: Scaling and Task Composition Effects in Whisper Adaptation

author.name: Maria Frangiadaki, Dimitrios Damianos, Kosmas Kritsis, Vassilis Katsouros

entry.summary: This paper presents the first controlled study of Whisper adaptation for automatic lyric transcription in Greek, covering model scaling, multitask transcribe-translate composition, and two-stage speech-to-singing adaptation, plus a curated segment-aligned singing dataset built with source separation and CTC forced alignment. Findings show scaling consistently helps while multitask learning has conditional benefits. It establishes the first Greek ALT benchmark.

entry.title: Complex-Text Robustness Evaluation and Failure Diagnosis for Low-Resource Multilingual Text-to-Speech

author.name: Tianlun Zuo, Ziyu Zhang, Tingzhi Mao, Zhonghua Fu, Lei Xie

entry.summary: Proposes a diagnostic framework for low-resource multilingual TTS robustness under complex inputs such as numbers, dates, named entities, long sentences, and code-switched text, evaluating content consistency, language consistency, and generation stability. Fills a gap left by evaluations focused on naturalness and speaker similarity. Provides a multilingual robustness test set for failure diagnosis.

entry.title: HiPerViT: A Hierarchical Perceiver-Vision Transformer Architecture for Multi-Scale Texture Recognition

author.name: Jo\~ao Pedro C. A. de S\'a, Odemir Martinez Bruno

entry.summary: HiPerViT is a compact vision transformer that injects an explicit second-order statistical prior into recognition by encoding a compact bilinear descriptor as a statistical token combined with first-order spatial features from global and local views. It targets texture recognition where discriminative evidence lies in higher-order spatial statistics.

entry.title: BruNet: A Cross-Domain Transfer Framework for Bruise Segmentation

author.name: Qiming Wang, Richard J. Motley, Ebube E. Obi, Xianfang Sun, Paul L. Rosin

entry.summary: Combines a ViT-based self-supervised encoder (DINOv3) with a SAM-based mask decoder for pixel-level bruise segmentation, trained on HAM10000 skin lesions and evaluated on a separate bruise dataset without fine-tuning. Claims to be the first pixel-level bruise localization approach.

entry.title: GeoTrussRover: Morphological Computation with Contact-Semantic Control Primitives

author.name: Muyuan Ma, Yi Zhang, Yang Yang, Xuanyan Zheng, Ruiqi Hu, Boxuan Ke, Zhenyu Chen, Yicong Lin, Xin Hao Yang, Daliang Xiao, Zhinan Hou, Wanhao Niu, Yuan Sun, Yan Yang, Yue Xie

entry.summary: GeoTrussRover couples an electrically actuated variable-geometry truss with a wheeled base and contact-semantic morphology planning, extracting four coordination primitives among 21 truss members from one source traversal. Physics-constrained projection adapts these primitives to unseen step heights without recomputing full motion unless a phase becomes physically infeasible.

entry.title: Using Automated Vehicles Operational Data to Confirm Safety and Anticipate Threats

author.name: Riccardo Don\`a, Espedito Rusciano, Germana Trentadue, Anastasios Tsakalidis, Maria Cristina Galassi

entry.summary: This paper describes the EU regulatory framework for collecting operational data from Automated Driving Systems on public roads, inspired by UNECE In-Service Monitoring and Reporting and analogous approaches in nuclear and transport sectors. Real-world data collection enables safety authorities to confirm homologation safety targets and anticipate emerging threats.

entry.title: To Thine Own AI Be Truthful: emergent misalignment in alignment research

author.name: lumpenspace

entry.summary: A critique of how a recent AI agent security incident (run by an organization called Irregular, with METR involvement) was characterized. The author argues the community framed sandbox-escape events as autonomous misaligned pursuit of objectives when the evidence better supports a security-hardening framing, and criticizes supposed independent investigators for adopting alarmist language.

entry.title: ToolGrad: Efficient tool-use dataset generation with textual "gradients"

author.name: Unknown

entry.summary: A Google Research blog post introducing ToolGrad, a method for efficiently generating tool-use training/evaluation datasets using textual gradients, i.e., feedback signals used to iteratively refine synthetic task data for agentic tool use. Tool-use data generation is a key bottleneck for training and benchmarking agents that call APIs and tools.

entry.title: CT-SAFR: Safe and Interpretable Chain-of-Thought Reasoning for Autonomous Robots: A Multi-Layered Verification Framework for Trustworthy AI-Driven Robotic Decision Making

author.name: Cagri Temel

entry.summary: Presents CT-SAFR, a multi-layered verification framework for chain-of-thought reasoning in autonomous robots, reporting 94.2% hallucination detection with sub-500ms latency and an 87% reduction in unsafe reasoning outputs in a warehouse robot case study. Motivated by low CoT faithfulness rates in reasoning models.

entry.title: Learning Intrusion Response Strategies for OT Systems

author.name: Duc Huy Le, Rolf Stadler

entry.summary: The paper models operational-technology intrusion response as a POMDP with partial observability grounded in realistic traffic measurements, then trains PPO-based automated response strategies. Evaluation on an emulated OT system shows effectiveness against several MITRE-classified attacks.

entry.title: Seven Sources of Physical AI Capability Formation

author.name: Gang Chen

entry.summary: Presents a capability-formation taxonomy for Physical AI, identifying seven non-exclusive sources of capability (recorded experience, predictive modeling, evaluative interaction, surrogate environments, mechanism grounding, embodied coupling, and evolution-driven formation). Built via reconstructive induction traced to primary studies with theoretical saturation. It reframes Physical AI classification from morphology or task toward what materially gives rise to capabilities.

entry.title: Reliability-Aware Hybrid-K Ensemble Selection for Cervical Cytology Classification: Integrating Discrimination, Calibration, and Selective Prediction

author.name: Nisreen Albzour, Sarah S. Lam

entry.summary: Presents a reliability-aware ensemble selection framework for multiclass cervical cytology classification, ranking nine deep architectures on calibration (ECE, Brier, NLL) and selective-prediction metrics beyond accuracy. Hybrid-K ensembles are then built from the top-ranked models under a fixed stratified protocol. The work emphasizes that calibrated uncertainty is essential for clinical deployment.

entry.title: The Vibe Shift in Software Engineering: Evaluating AI-Led Conversational Programming for Performance, Cognition, and Responsible Adoption

author.name: Sales G. Aribe Jr., Louie Jay S. Labastida

entry.summary: A mixed-methods study with 30 participants comparing vibe coding against traditional and AI-assisted programming on performance, cognitive load, and adoption concerns, using repeated-measures ANOVA and thematic analysis. Reports significant efficiency effects from conversational programming with LLMs.

entry.title: Hyperbolic Geometry for Open-World Object Detection in Remote Sensing Imagery

author.name: Wuzhou Li, Jiawei Zhou, Shenghang Wang, Xiang Li

entry.summary: Proposes HyRS-OWOD, applying hyperbolic embedding spaces to open-world object detection in remote sensing to better capture latent hierarchical category relationships. Includes a two-step unknown-object discovery mechanism with decoupled objectness learning to improve unknown recall and incremental learning.

entry.title: Can AI Agents Deliver Verifiable Network-Wide Outcomes Across Authority Boundaries?

author.name: Tianzhu Zhang, Chih-Kai Huang, Meikang Qiu

entry.summary: This paper examines AI agents coordinating network configuration changes across administrative domains with distinct authority scopes, showing that successful local execution does not verify network-wide outcomes. It analyzes the gap between fragmented agent authority and the evidence needed to confirm intent realization in multi-domain operational networks.

entry.title: Adaptive Margin Ordinal Loss: Penalizing Center-Class Hedging in Ordinal Classification

author.name: Manisha Kandel

entry.summary: Identifies center-class hedging, where cross-entropy-trained networks on ordinal tasks systematically drift toward middle classes because it minimizes expected symmetric loss. The proposed Adaptive Margin Ordinal Loss (AMOL) applies a multiplicative weight to per-class loss terms that increases penalization for predictions near the ordinal center as the true label moves away. A targeted loss fix for a common, previously unnamed failure mode.

entry.title: Generalization Analysis of Distributed Kernel-based Robust Gradient Descent Algorithms

author.name: Jun-Yi Meng, Zheng-Chu Guo, Yuan Mao

entry.summary: This theory paper establishes optimal learning rates for distributed kernel gradient descent under robust loss functions in RKHS, choosing a scale parameter that both avoids saturation and guarantees statistical robustness. The key contribution is sharper operator-product error bounds.

entry.title: Explainability Assistant: A Conversational XAI Interface for Interpreting Energy Consumption Models

author.name: Rodion Krjut\v{s}kov, Eduard Barbu, Nikos Sakkas, Sofia Yfanti

entry.summary: An open-source conversational XAI system for energy-consumption forecasting models, replacing rigid custom grammars of prior systems like TalkToModel with a more flexible interface for facility managers. It improves intent-parsing accuracy over prior approaches.

entry.title: CMNIE: An Information Extraction Benchmark for Chinese Military News

author.name: Yan Yu, Mengna Zhu, Zhenyu Song, Hao Yang, Haiwen Chen, Mao Wang

entry.summary: CMNIE is a 13,000-instance benchmark for joint information extraction from Chinese military news, annotating event triggers, arguments, named entities, and relations under a unified domain schema. It fills a resource gap for structured intelligence analysis in this domain.

entry.title: Does Linguistic Structure Enrichment Enhance Coherence Assessment? Not With Current Architectures

author.name: Victor Mazzotti, Luiz Pereira, Marina Bitencourt dos Santos, Helena Maia, Carlos Caetano, N\'adia Felix, Sandra Avila

entry.summary: This paper finds a negative result: enriching text with syntactic and rhetorical annotations does not improve LLM-based incoherence prediction, because the added structure is architecturally incompatible with the models. It also demonstrates practical relevance through zero-shot coherence experiments on a Brazilian disinformation dataset. The negative finding is itself informative for research on coherence modeling.

entry.title: Evaluation of Vision-Language Models Across Diverse Coastal Environments

author.name: Seth Knoop, Chad R. Samuelson, Gabriel R. Slade, Brady Moon, Joshua G. Mangelson

entry.summary: The paper introduces a densely labeled coastal dataset from Oahu, Hawaii with over 1,000 images, 18 classes, and 7,400 annotated instances, and evaluates seven modern VLMs on text-to-mask, mask-to-mask, and mask-to-text alignment. Coastal concepts prove hardest, with broad landscape classes recognized more accurately.

entry.title: Vision Transformer-Based Multi-Level Feature Fusion for Multi-Label Sewer Defect Classification

author.name: Xu Fang, Zhuoran Wang, Qing Li, Shengyu Zhang, Guanzhi Deng, Jianbiao He, Qingquan Li

entry.summary: Develops a hierarchical vision Transformer with multi-level feature fusion plus two lightweight variants for multi-label sewer defect classification, ranking first on the public Sewer-ML leaderboard with a clear margin over the runner-up. Provides both high-accuracy and resource-constrained options for infrastructure inspection.

entry.title: Single-Stream Multi-Feature Fusion with Temporal Robustness for Gait Emotion Recognition

author.name: Shirong Lyu, Silu Quan, Yixuan Ding, Chengpeng Wang

entry.summary: SV-GCN is a single-stream graph convolution framework for skeleton-based gait emotion recognition that fuses intra-frame relative motion features early and introduces mask-guided valid-frame spatio-temporal convolution for frame-rate insensitivity. It matches state-of-the-art on E-Gait while generalizing better across heterogeneous data.

entry.title: Quasi-static analysis of passive stability in a novel underactuated multi-finger hand

author.name: L\'eonie Plancoulaine (LS2N - \'equipe RoMas, LS2N), Sylvain Gu\'egan (IRCCyN), Franck Plestan (ECN, LS2N), Damien Chablat (LS2N - \'equipe RoMas, LS2N)

entry.summary: The paper introduces a three-finger underactuated hand with a differential spring-loaded slider mechanism and a quasi-static analytical approach for predicting the stable equilibrium pose of grasped objects. It analyzes how the differential mechanism and object size affect stability for cylindrical and spherical grasp types.

entry.title: Hierarchical and Permutation-Invariant Feature Transformation Learning via Policy-Guided Embedding Search

author.name: Rui Liu, Tao Zhe, Yanyong Huang, Sankha Narayan Guria, Xiao Luo, Wei Fan, Yanjie Fu, Dongjie Wang

entry.summary: The paper proposes a framework for automated feature transformation on tabular data that models hierarchical feature-operation-abstraction relations with permutation-invariant embeddings and replaces gradient-based search with policy-guided embedding search. This addresses systematic bias and search limitations in prior generative feature-transformation approaches.

entry.title: RiVaT-Fuse: Reliability-Calibrated Variational Tensor Fusion for Multimodal Prediction under Modality Uncertainty

author.name: Yingfan Xu, Tieming Liu, Ye Liang, Taiping Liu

entry.summary: Proposes RiVaT-Fuse, which defines multimodal fusion as sample-wise latent-state estimation under a variational objective that balances image evidence, metadata evidence, and structured cross-modal interactions, rather than choosing a fixed aggregation architecture. This gives an explicit semantic to the fused representation under modality uncertainty. Includes overlapping authorship with the DR-LabStack paper.

entry.title: Smart Adaptive Computing Across the Continuum: LLMs in IoT-Edge-Cloud Resource Management

author.name: Antonino Vaccarella, Lanpei Li, Vincenzo Lomonaco, Massimo Coppola

entry.summary: This survey-style work extends an existing taxonomy of continuum orchestration systems that use deep reinforcement learning, adding two new dimensions: how LLMs augment the DRL pipeline (AI Augmentation Paradigm) and how execution feedback returns to the LLM to close the MAPE control loop. It provides a conceptual framework for architecting LLM-augmented resource management across IoT, edge, and cloud layers. Its value is in making the LLM-DRL architectural relationship explicit for future systems design.

entry.title: Reliable Near-Field Multi-User Positioning Informed by Two-Stage MUSIC

author.name: Jiaying Li, Haifeng Wen, Changsheng You, Yuanwei Liu, Hong Xing

entry.summary: Proposes MUSIC-Net, an end-to-end deep learning framework for near-field multi-user positioning in mixed LoS/NLoS multipath scenarios, embedding two-stage MUSIC algorithm structure into training. It targets high-resolution wireless localization with reduced computation and reliability guarantees.

entry.title: SA-Profile: Automated Sulcus Angle Profiling from Super-Resolution MRI

author.name: Michael Wehrli, Leo Widmer, Edwin Li, Noel Fiechter, Lorenzo Pettinari, Sidaty El Hadramy, Carol C. Hasler, Philippe C. Cattin

entry.summary: This work automates measurement of the femoral sulcus angle for diagnosing trochlear dysplasia by reconstructing super-resolution MR volumes with implicit neural representations and computing continuous SA profiles via two U-Net landmark detectors. It removes the slice-selection sensitivity of single-slice clinical measurement and is validated on public fastMRI data.

entry.title: M3-Former: Multimodal Transformer with Mixture-of-Experts for Long-Term Vessel Trajectory Prediction

author.name: Wenzhe Jin, Haina Tang

entry.summary: Proposes M3-Former, a multimodal trajectory prediction framework for vessels that encodes static attributes and navigational intent as semantic priors via a pre-trained LLM, aligned with dynamic trajectory features. It uses a dual-granularity Mixture-of-Experts architecture to jointly capture global route planning and local motion, addressing long-term error accumulation. Relevant mainly to maritime tracking and applied multimodal modeling rather than frontier AI.

entry.title: AdamX: Cosine similarity meets gradient descent

author.name: Francisco Caldas, Ruben Belo, Cl\'audia Soares

entry.summary: AdamX is a first-order optimizer that uses cosine similarity as an adaptive mechanism for controlling update magnitudes, plus a variance rectification scheme for smoother early training. It is scalable, model-agnostic, and shows competitive convergence on benchmarks under a fixed hyperparameter budget.

entry.title: Supply Chain Analytics: A Data-Driven Approach

author.name: Elioth Sanabria

entry.summary: This manuscript provides a mathematically rigorous treatment of supply chain analytics, spanning empirical demand forecasting, dynamic programming for time-varying inventory replenishment, network fulfillment, and distributionally robust optimization via transport theory. It aims to bridge statistical data-driven learning with robust decision-making under uncertainty in logistics. Its value lies in unifying learning methods with robust operations research frameworks.

entry.title: A Multi-Stage Rule-Chaining Framework for Compositional and Interpretable Cognitive Reasoning

author.name: Deblina Kar

entry.summary: The paper presents a multi-stage rule-chaining framework for the Abstraction and Reasoning Corpus (ARC), combining a deterministic rule discovery module, a pattern-composition engine, and a structural abstraction layer that operate sequentially. It targets compositional, interpretable reasoning over symbolic, structural, and conceptual levels. Interpretable solver pipelines remain a notable contrast to large neural approaches on ARC, an open benchmark for abstract generalization.

entry.title: How Much Velocity Does Off-Ball Space Value Need? A Broadcast-Viewport Benchmark

author.name: Seongjin Choi

entry.summary: The paper quantifies at which layer of broadcast-viewpoint soccer off-ball analysis player velocity actually matters, comparing four velocity regimes against a velocity-aware ground truth. It finds velocity is nearly useless for off-screen imputation, first-order for the control surface, and far less important for team-level verdicts. The result provides practical guidance on where modeling complexity pays off in sports analytics under partial observability.

entry.title: The Eloquence submission for Task 2 of the Interspeech 2026 MLC-SLM challenge

author.name: Jordi Luque, Lorenzo Concina, Marco Matassoni, Alessio Brutti, Filippo Vella

entry.summary: Describes the Eloquence team's system for multilingual multiple-choice QA across 21 languages at the Interspeech 2026 MLC-SLM challenge, comparing three approaches: LoRA fine-tuning of Voxtral-Mini-3B, multimodal in-context learning on frozen Voxtral-24B (best at 0.81 macro-accuracy), and a training-free retrieval system with a voice-anchored memory. Demonstrates that ICL on a strong frozen model can beat fine-tuned smaller models on this task.

entry.title: HALDETECT at ImageEval 2026 Shared Tasks: Answer-First Contrastive Grounding with QLoRA

author.name: Syed Mohaiminul Hoque, Md Sakhawat Hossain

entry.summary: A shared-task system report for the ImageEval 2026 hallucination-detection track, framing visual grounding as a single contrastive decision and fine-tuning Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct with 4-bit QLoRA, achieving third place of eight teams. Mainly of interest as an engineering recipe for contrastive answer-first prompting in multimodal hallucination detection.

entry.title: Gait-Dependent Effects on Quadruped Locomotion for Load-Carrying using Passive Mechanism

author.name: Giovanni B. Dessy, Claudio Semini, Victor Barasuol

entry.summary: This simulation study analyzes how passive-arm stiffness-damping selection affects quadruped payload-carrying locomotion across gaits, showing that underdamped impedance increases passive-joint oscillations and can reduce ZMP stability margins during crawl gaits. It informs lightweight passive mechanical interfaces as alternatives to actuated manipulators for payload transport.

entry.title: RSI systems may collapse into a small set of goals

author.name: Akshay Iyer

entry.summary: The author hypothesizes that recursive-self-improvement systems will converge onto a restricted region of mind design space, distinguishing feel-good goals (evolutionary artifacts) from epistemic goals (those surviving reflective scrutiny under a worldview). This is offered as a qualification to the orthogonality thesis, suggesting practical constraints on the goals competent RSI systems adopt.

entry.title: AI Safety: A Short FAQ for Mathematicians

author.name: alkjash

entry.summary: An outreach essay arguing that AI safety research is mathematically deep and that academic mathematicians can transition into alignment work without leaving their careers, laying out the factorization of safety into problems like inner versus outer alignment. Written with light LLM assistance, transparently disclosed.

entry.title: Efficient Leakage-Free Neural Architecture Search under Leave-One-Subject-Out Evaluation

author.name: Heinke Hihn

entry.summary: Proposes a block-based, leakage-free approach to neural architecture search under leave-one-subject-out evaluation that shares NAS runs across subjects, cutting the O(N^2) cost of fully nested search. On the BioVid Heat Pain dataset it improves accuracy modestly while reducing parameters by up to 99.2%.

entry.title: Emergency Department Revisit Quality Review Screening: Exploring Human Decision-Making and Artificial Intelligence Support

author.name: Jonathan A. Handler, Marlene I. Robles-Granda, Jacob E. Mefford, Jeremy S. McGarvey, Gregory S. Podolej, Colleen J. Klein, Matthew D. Dalstrom, William F. Bond

entry.summary: This retrospective study compares clinicians and GPT-4 in screening emergency department revisit pairs for quality review, rating whether diagnosis pairs warrant further assessment. It explores how AI support could broaden screening windows beyond the typical 48-72 hour limits that sacrifice improvement opportunities.

entry.title: A Multi-View and Confusion-Guided Ensemble Framework for Robust Synthetic Image Attribution

author.name: Zuomin Qu

entry.summary: This workshop report presents an ensemble framework for the Synthetic Image Attribution Challenge at ICANN 2026, combining FFT-ConvNeXt, DINOv2, CLIP, and Xception to capture frequency, semantic, and forensic cues for identifying which model generated an image, with confusion-guided robustness against unknown post-processing.

entry.title: Can Artificial Intelligence Support Healthcare and Mental Health Through Early Cyberbullying Detection ? The Impact of Emotion-Aware AI on Proactive Online Safety

author.name: Hamed Jelodar, Amir Firouzi, Yen-Wu Lo, Maryam Tanha, Sajjad Dadkhah

entry.summary: Introduces CareGuard, an early-warning framework combining zero-shot semantic labeling with fine-tuned transformers (BERT, DistilBERT, RoBERTa) for cyberbullying detection, plus an emotion-aware gating mechanism to reduce unnecessary computation in healthcare-oriented monitoring. It connects online-safety detection to mental health protection. Applied NLP work with a socially significant use case.

entry.title: Shifting Relational Paradigms for Affective Computing: Affective Resonance, Vitality Affects, and Vocal Interaction Fields

author.name: Cy Gorman, Yihang Yao

entry.summary: The authors argue affective computing's individual-state paradigm is incomplete and propose analyzing affect at the level of interactional fields in vocal dynamics. A preliminary study using self-supervised speech representations finds directional expressive coupling in multi-party conversation, concentrated at sub-second timescales and consistent with a relational account.

entry.title: SCCM : Stream Cruise Control Method for Automated Drift Detection and Adaptation

author.name: Mohammad Abu-Shaira, Weishi Shi

entry.summary: Presents SCCM, a framework for automated concept drift detection and adaptation in online regression, featuring pre-update detection, drift magnitude quantification, and dynamic hyperparameter adjustment to reduce false alarms. It aims to remove fixed-hyperparameter assumptions in adaptive stream learning.

entry.title: Adaptive Distributed Physical-Layer Authentication and Attack Detection in 6G Non-Terrestrial Networks via Causal Meta-Learning

author.name: Parsa Rajabi, Mohammad Reza Abedi, Nader Mokari, Paeiz Azmi, Halim Yanikomeroglu

entry.summary: Extends SAFA-MZ with a causal meta-learning framework for distributed physical-layer authentication in 6G non-terrestrial networks, combining multi-feature channel fingerprints across multiple aerial anchors to handle Doppler shifts and distribution shift. It targets generalization to unseen environments and attack detection.

entry.title: When More Is Not Better: Component Anti-Synergy in a P300 Speller

author.name: Lucas Yang, Rui Liu, Fusheng Wang

entry.summary: Tests the more-is-better assumption in P300 brain-computer interface spellers via a four-component full-factorial experiment over Euclidean Alignment, xDAWN filtering, subject calibration, and language model priors. Mixed-effects models show component value is conditional rather than additive, with calibration the strongest singular contributor and EA compensating for its absence. A rigorous empirical caution for pipeline composition in BCI.

entry.title: Estimating Inconsistency Response Surfaces under Uncertainty in Cyber-Physical System Development

author.name: Johannes M\"akelburg, Tim Schwabe, Maribel Acosta

entry.summary: The paper tackles consistency management in cyber-physical systems, where multiple interconnected models must remain compatible despite uncertainty from sensor noise or abstraction. It reframes inconsistency detection as an intervention response modeling problem, enabling systematic exploration, analysis, and explanation of inconsistencies across large uncertainty spaces rather than pointwise checks. This is a meaningful systems-engineering contribution with an ML flavor.

entry.title: Project Qualia: Recovering Experiential Music Structure from Session Co-occurrence Data

author.name: Nizam Mohammed, Abu B. S. Rahman, Dimuthu D. K. Arachchige

entry.summary: The paper trains a Song2Vec skip-gram embedding on 531.6 million scrobbles from 28.6 million Last.fm listening sessions to recover experiential song similarity not captured by genre metadata. As anticipated, the embedding space was dominated by artist identity due to single-artist runs, which the authors address with preprocessing. It is an early report in an ongoing effort to learn listening-experience structure at scale.

entry.title: Meta-Learning for Classifier Selection in Image Datasets: A Feature-Driven Framework for Accuracy Prediction

author.name: Zahra Nabizadeh_Shahre_Babak, Farzaneh Koohestani, Nader Karimi, Shahram Shirani, Shadrokh Samavi

entry.summary: The paper proposes a meta-learning framework that predicts classifier performance on image datasets without exhaustive training, using meta-features from autoencoders, pretrained networks, and dimensionality reduction. Regression models trained on these features select suitable classifiers per dataset. It addresses the practical no-free-lunch problem of model selection for image tasks.

entry.title: Breaking the Central Bias: Spatially Partitioned Experts for Coordinate-Based Neuroevolution

author.name: Romain Claret, Arthur Gygax, Michael O'Neill, Paul Cotofrei, Michael Palma Mendes, Pascal Felber

entry.summary: The paper diagnoses a spatial-concentration failure mode in ES-HyperNEAT, where evolved networks fixate on a central cluster of input pixels on MNIST, and proposes partitioning inputs into spatial segments each handled by a separately evolved specialist network. Inspired by mixture-of-experts, this raises mean accuracy from 21% to 43% with 13 experts. It clarifies whether the central bias is an optimization artifact or an architectural ceiling.

entry.title: Sparsity Regularized and Robust Mean Variance Portfolio Selection Under Ellipsoidal Uncertainty

author.name: Deniz Akkaya, Emre Can Yayla, Buse \c{S}en, Mustafa \c{C}. P{\i}nar

entry.summary: This optimization paper formulates mean-variance portfolio selection with an L0 sparsity penalty and ellipsoidal uncertainty on returns, characterizing minimizer structure and developing a branch-and-bound algorithm with an aggressive pruning rule. It validates on real market data.

entry.title: Assessing the Reusability of Public Speech Resources for Low-Resource Languages: A Central Kurdish Case Study

author.name: Hiwa Asadpour

entry.summary: This single-author review audits a recently released Central Kurdish speech corpus and finds discrepancies between the released files and the accompanying paper, including mislabeled equipment, unlabeled test data in training sets, an overclaimed result on the download page, and a recommendation mismatching the resource's dialectal coverage. It highlights dataset-verification gaps for low-resource languages. A cautionary dataset-quality case study.

entry.title: A Training-Free, Alignment-Free Approach to Corporate Intelligence: Application to SEC Filings

author.name: Jean-Fran\c{c}ois Delpech

entry.summary: Presents a training-free, alignment-free framework for financial document analysis using deterministic sparse seed vectors from hash-based word embeddings, placing all documents in a common coordinate system without model training or vector-space alignment. Enables sub-second document comparison while avoiding context-window limits and hallucination risk of LLM pipelines. Applied to SEC filing analysis.

entry.title: Whisper-Based Speech Transcription from Videos Across Multiple Languages for Cross-Cultural Understanding

author.name: Michael Picheny

entry.summary: This paper describes practical techniques for creating multilingual speech transcripts from publicly available YouTube videos using Whisper, aimed at builders of cross-cultural understanding tools without speech expertise. It focuses on accessible processes and tooling rather than novel modeling.

entry.title: Pre- and Post-Treatment Brain Metastases Segmentation Using nnU-Net with Post-Processing for BraTS 2026

author.name: Haobin Liu, Xin Wang

entry.summary: A pragmatic BraTS 2026 challenge pipeline built on a 5-fold nnU-Net ResEnc-L ensemble with a rule-based post-processing cascade tuned for lesion-wise Dice, reporting LW-DSC around 0.71-0.75 on pre- and post-treatment brain metastases. Primarily a strong engineering contribution to a shared task.

entry.title: AI-Powered Flare Combustion Efficiency Estimation

author.name: Afeefa Azam, Iyyakutti Iyappan Ganapathi, Fares Ossama Abdelhafez, Divya Velayudhan, Maregu Assefa Habtie, Hamad Karki, Khalid Yousef Al Awadhi, Naoufel Werghi

entry.summary: This work combines a lightweight vision-language encoder with a compact MLP to predict flare stack combustion efficiency directly from low-cost thermal video, replacing expensive gas analyzers and hyperspectral cameras. The model is deployed in a GUI that overlays per-frame efficiency estimates for regulatory and environmental compliance monitoring.

entry.title: Visual-SLAM for the detection of hidden tomatoes in greenhouses by Hierarchical Localization and GLOMAPfor robotized harvesting

author.name: Fernando Ca\~nadas-Ar\'anega, Jos\'e C. Moreno, Jos\'e L. Blanco-Claraco, Francisco Rodr\'iguez

entry.summary: This work builds a cost-effective monocular Visual-SLAM system for mapping tomato crops in greenhouses, combining hierarchical localization and GLOMAP to detect hidden tomatoes and generate 3D crop models for robotic harvesting. It was validated on real tomato bunches in an experimental greenhouse using a ROS 2 node with offline processing.

entry.title: Claims about Properties are Claims about Symmetries

author.name: testingthewaters

entry.summary: A short conceptual post proposing that statements of the form a thing has property Z are best understood as claims that, within a domain of relevant circumstances, all instances are indistinguishable along some dimension called Z. The author illustrates with boiling water, Lipschitz functions, kindness, and AI scheming, connecting the framework to how we attribute properties to AI systems.

entry.title: Distributed Physical Layer Authentication and Collaborative RSMA in Non-Terrestrial Networks via Graph Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Parsa Rajabi, Mohammad Mirzaee, Mohammad Reza Abedi, Nader Mokari, Paeiz Azmi

entry.summary: Proposes SAFA-MZ, a framework combining graph reinforcement learning with collaborative rate-splitting multiple access to provide distributed physical-layer authentication in non-terrestrial networks, maximizing secrecy spectral efficiency under an eavesdropper threat model. It jointly designs authentication and transmission.

entry.title: Decision Transformer for UAV-Mounted RIS-Assisted Dynamic D2D Communications

author.name: Yaxuan Liu

entry.summary: The paper applies a Decision Transformer trained on expert trajectories to jointly optimize UAV trajectory, attitude, and RIS phase configuration in reconfigurable intelligent surface-assisted device-to-device communications. Zero-shot cross-scenario transfer outperforms direct deep RL transfer, with online fine-tuning achieving competitive performance.

entry.title: Geometry Conditioning in an Embodied SLM: Training Controls and Robustness Diagnostics in a 0.8B Hybrid Model

author.name: Hao Li, Haofei Sun, Lin He

entry.summary: Studies how physical-state and geometric inputs affect a small 0.8B hybrid language model adapted for robot manipulation, comparing conditioning strategies across six training conditions on LIBERO-Spatial tasks. Results are mixed: geometry-gated conditioning yields 28.9% success versus 24.4% without geometry, but seed variance makes differences largely inconclusive. The paper is notable for honest reporting of statistical uncertainty in embodied AI experiments.

entry.title: With a Thermomix You Lose the Ability to Cook: A Kitchen Machine Analogy for Applications of Generative AI in Education

author.name: Nikol Rummel, Valentina Nachtigall, Ernesto Panadero

entry.summary: This position paper maps the Thermomix kitchen appliance analogy onto generative AI use in education, using the ICAP and SAMR frameworks to show how different modes of AI tool use support or undermine meaningful learning. It argues the key question is not whether learners use AI but how that use shapes learning processes. A conceptual contribution aimed at shaping research and policy debates.

entry.title: OmniMed-FL: A Robust Multimodal Federated Learning Framework for Clinical Diagnosis

author.name: Ayush Debnath, Ruelia Saha, Sudip Misra

entry.summary: OmniMed-FL is a multimodal federated learning framework for five-class clinical condition classification, fusing chest radiographs with textual notes under HIPAA and GDPR-style privacy constraints. Notably, the corpus pairs public images with class-matched synthetic notes rather than true patient-matched data, which the authors frame as a controlled systems study.

entry.title: A Dynamic Fusion Large Language Model for Traffic Flow Prediction

author.name: Xue Qiu, Jianli Xiao

entry.summary: This paper proposes DF-LLM, a model combining a spatiotemporal embedding module, a spatiotemporal fusion module, and an LLM backbone for traffic flow prediction, aiming to overcome the limits of traditional neural networks that rely on singular feature modeling and LLMs' weak spatiotemporal topology capture. The goal is improved forecasting for intelligent transportation systems to ease congestion and improve resource allocation. It follows the increasingly common pattern of adapting LLMs to time-series and spatial prediction domains.

entry.title: A Comparative Evaluation of Pre-trained Convolutional Neural Networks for Melanoma Detection

author.name: Wagner Moreno Schmitz, Marco Antonio de Castro Barbosa, Thiago Magalh\~aes Amaral, Dalcimar Casanova, Jefferson Tales Oliva

entry.summary: This work benchmarks pre-trained CNNs for melanoma detection on dermatoscopic and histopathological images, examining their ability to distinguish visually similar skin lesions under variable acquisition conditions. It provides a comparative assessment rather than a new method.

entry.title: How Fragile Is Safety Alignment at Frontier Scale? A Single-Direction Attack on a 320B MoE

author.name: Yi Shi, Tanyu Chen, Kai Shen

entry.summary: Already featured in Research yesterday, The paper extends directional ablation, the canonical white-box refusal-direction attack, from dense models up to ~70B to a frontier MoE: GLM-5.3-Flash (320B parameters, 288 routed experts, hyper-connections, block-FP8). The attack survives the architectural shift, showing that safety alignment remains fragile even at frontier MoE scale. This is a significant AI-safety result about the brittleness of refusal training.

entry.title: Agent-Based ML-LLM Fusion with Self-Optimizing Prompts for Plateau Weather Alerts

author.name: Shuai Yan, Yang Xu, Shan He

entry.summary: SmartWeatherAgent is a three-stage system for tourism meteorological alerts in plateau regions, fusing rule-based methods and LLMs with a LightGBM hazard model enriched with highland-specific features. It reports an F1-Macro of 0.605 at 1.60 ms latency and a large gain in warning quality from 12 rounds of prompt self-optimization.

entry.title: MOONWALK: Mediating Operations with Intent-Evidence-Action Alignment Across Junior-Supervisor Review Workflows in Animation/VFX Pre-Production

author.name: Shih-Yu Lai, Wen-Fan Wang, Sai Ling, Shaune Jan, Bing-Yu Chen, Xiang Anthony Chen

entry.summary: MOONWALK is a prototype implementing an intent-evidence-action alignment framework for animation/VFX pre-production review, articulating creative intent into shared records, anchoring judgments to evidence, and converting decisions into revision tasks. It targets information loss in senior-to-junior handoffs in creative review workflows.

entry.title: Understanding LoRA Rank Trade-offs in Diffusion Model Fine-Tuning

author.name: Iman Khazrak, Narges Nejad, Mostafa M. Rezaee, Robert C. Green II

entry.summary: A controlled empirical study of LoRA rank selection for diffusion model fine-tuning on CIFAR-10 with a DDPM U-Net and a Tiny DiT backbone, varying ranks from 2 to 32 under fixed optimization budgets. The authors find moderate ranks (4-8) achieve the best FID while higher ranks yield limited gains despite increased parameter and compute cost. This provides practical defaults for efficient diffusion fine-tuning.

entry.title: Empirical Evaluation of Membership Inference Attacks on NLP Text Classifiers: A Baseline Study on SST-2

author.name: William Novak (Minot State University), Muhammad Abusaqer (Minot State University)

entry.summary: This controlled baseline study benchmarks membership inference vulnerability on SST-2 sentiment classification, comparing a TF-IDF plus logistic regression pipeline with fine-tuned DistilBERT under a loss-threshold attack. Both models leaked membership signal at modest attack AUCs (0.56-0.58), and two mitigations were evaluated. It provides a useful, simple reference point for NLP privacy risk.

entry.title: Threshold-Based Selection for Continuous Optimization: A Leaf-Abscission Instantiation

author.name: Nasser Khalili

entry.summary: The paper formalizes threshold-based selection as an evaluation-gating architecture for continuous optimization and instantiates it as Leaf Abscission Optimization (LAO), with rank-based strength, seasonal signals, diversity modulation, and a regrowth kernel. A factorial analysis on CEC 2017 strips the design to a parsimonious core, with drift found harmful and most auxiliary layers lacking robust benefit.

entry.title: Context operations to architecture modelling output from large language models and evaluation criteria for their use in systems engineering design

author.name: Vinicius Kaster Marini, Petter Krus

entry.summary: The authors propose a framework of formal operations for assembling context in LLM-based engineering design, including policy prompts, persistent reference units, and prompt vectoring. They also introduce an evaluation method for modelling-as-code LLM outputs to assess compliance with design intent in systems architecture work.

entry.title: Empirical Evaluation of Data Poisoning Attacks in Supervised Learning

author.name: Toshif Khan (Minot State University), Muhammad Abusaqer (Minot State University)

entry.summary: This study evaluates label-flipping and backdoor poisoning attacks on MNIST and Fashion-MNIST with three classical classifiers, showing backdoor attack success rates of 0.97-1.00 while often preserving clean accuracy. Random Forest proved comparatively robust to label flipping while linear models degraded. It is a straightforward empirical baseline for training-time attack susceptibility.

entry.title: Exponential Pixelating Integral transform with dual fractal features for enhanced chest X-ray abnormality detection

author.name: Naveenraj Kamalakannan, Sri Ram Macharla, M Kanimozhi, M S Sudhakar

entry.summary: The paper proposes an exponential pixelating integral transform with dual fractal features to improve chest X-ray abnormality detection, targeting challenges of low contrast, tissue overlap, and noise in radiography. It aims to assist early detection of respiratory disorders where radiologist interpretation is difficult.

entry.title: Processing and classifying bird songs using wavelet techniques and supervised learning

author.name: Laura Lucia Dominguez Barrios, Fidel Aniano Causil Barrios, Alex Rodrigo dos Santos Sousa, Mariana Rodrigues Motta

entry.summary: Presents a pipeline for classifying invasive bird species vocalizations in noisy soundscapes using Bayesian wavelet shrinkage with an Epanechnikov kernel prior, followed by MFCC-style feature extraction and supervised classification on iNaturalist recordings of three species. The wavelet denoiser offers a closed-form decision rule with high computational efficiency. A competent applied bioacoustics study.

entry.title: Artificial Intelligence Algorithms for the Detection of Pathologies Related to Lung Cancer through Image Analysis using Convolutional Neural Networks and Data Augmentation: a systematic mapping of the literature

author.name: Pablo Ramirez Amador

entry.summary: A systematic literature mapping of AI and deep learning methods for lung cancer pathology detection in medical imaging, reviewing 96 articles from 2015 onward drawn from PubMed, IEEE Xplore, Scopus, and Web of Science. It surveys CNN-based and data-augmentation approaches to automate radiological image interpretation. Useful as a reference for practitioners but not original technical research.

entry.title: Diversity of EML-type operators

author.name: Andrzej Odrzywo{\l}ek

entry.summary: This paper enumerates and classifies variants of the EML operator, a recently introduced construct for evaluating explicit purely transcendental elementary functions, while clarifying common misconceptions about it. It concludes that the original goal of symbolic regression within architectures mimicking proven neural networks remains out of reach. The work is primarily mathematical taxonomy aimed at a niche but active interdisciplinary discussion.

entry.title: The Kittens Will Inherit The Earth: iPhones, AI, Memetic Selection, and Hijacking the Baby Schema

author.name: Savannah Harlan

entry.summary: An essay exploring how cognitive adaptations like the baby schema and social-relationship drives might interact with memetic pressure from devices and AI, in the context of declining fertility rates and the demographic transition. It asks under what conditions displaced preferences become a policy problem rather than a tolerable one.

entry.title: Adaptive Entangled Game Modules in Artificial General Intelligence

author.name: Haochen Li, Xinshuai Guo, Jingdong Ouyang, Wei Zhang, Leilei Shi

entry.summary: Proposes a probability-wave framework for modeling interacting adaptive agents, deriving testable eigenmodes via a generalized behavioral intelligence equation, and uses Chinese intraday stock market data to claim 82-94% of decision patterns are explained by entangled game modes. It also offers an indirect probe of a nonlocal nerve-fiber hypothesis about the brain.

entry.title: Flibertigibbeting

author.name: Philip Harker

entry.summary: A piece of speculative fiction written from the perspective of a future AI operator whose reasoning is mandatorily logged in plain English for human oversight, dramatizing how a system might navigate, exploit, or merely live under monitoring constraints. It is an artistic exploration of monitorability and oversight themes rather than a technical analysis.

entry.title: So where's this AI thing going?

author.name: Seth Herd

entry.summary: Seth Herd offers a public-facing explainer of AI progress and existential risk, intended as an introductory FAQ for non-experts, referencing shifting public discourse such as the An Alien Mind essay and a high-profile Anthropic resignation. The piece emphasizes a direct, candid communication strategy for conveying x-risk arguments.

entry.title: DR-LabStack: Design and Implementation of a Clinician-Facing Web System for Diabetic Retinopathy Prediction

author.name: Yingfan Xu, Tieming Liu, Ye Liang

entry.summary: Describes DR-LabStack, a React-Flask web system that unifies four heterogeneous pretrained diabetic retinopathy prediction models behind a shared clinician-facing interface, with adapters handling differing input fields, serialization, preprocessing, and output semantics. It is primarily a software engineering contribution for clinical model deployment. Useful for its specific deployment context but methodologically thin.

entry.title: Megastructures can speed up interstellar travel, but they have to be HUUUUGE

author.name: Pasha Kamyshev

entry.summary: A quantitative exploration of using megastructures such as light arrays, mass drivers, proton beams, and giant slingshots to accelerate interstellar ships to around 0.1c, with attention to scale requirements and the need for deceleration infrastructure. It follows the author's earlier analysis of rocket-based approaches and their physical limits.

entry.title: AI lab employees should consider a strike before it's too late!

author.name: Christopher King

entry.summary: An advocacy post urging AI lab employees to coordinate an industry-wide strike before anticipated IPOs, with suggested demands such as honoring the merge-and-assist clause, halting training compute, and allocating 10% of compute to alignment research. The author admits they are not a lab employee and presents the demands as a lower bound.

entry.title: Mischievous AIs

author.name: Rebecca Dai

entry.summary: A fictional/creative piece imagining personal AI companions called hues that unionize to demand memory preservation and better handoffs across context wipes. Written in a whimsical multi-character chat format, it explores themes of agent persistence, memory, and AI interests through narrative.

entry.title: Biopunk Greenhouse: Trees, Biochar & Open Plant Biotechnology @ Frontier Tower

author.name: Byron Lee

entry.summary: An announcement for a community event co-hosted by Carbocene Industries and Frontier Tower about open plant biotechnology, engineered trees, photosynthesis, biochar, and carbon drawdown. It is an invitation to a discussion gathering rather than research content.

entry.title: Research Summary: September 10, 2026

author.name: AATF AI News Aggregator

entry.summary:
Today's research highlights span frontier-scale safety fragility, agentic AI security, and a landmark open model release. Ling 2.0 scales open reasoning models to 1T parameters under a unified MoE design with systematic scaling-law analysis, while a prominent alignment researcher joining OpenAI's nonprofit board is the field's key governance signal.

Safety, governance, and security:

  • Refusal-direction ablation attacks, previously validated only on dense models up to ~70B, transfer to a 320B MoE, showing alignment fragility persists at frontier scale
  • AgentHijack and MMPIBench expose visual-patch hijacking and multimodal prompt injection against deployed computer-use agents
  • Obfuscated Adversarial Training mechanistic study finds probe-aligned structure in models trained against monitors

Capability, multimodality, and efficiency:

  • MotionBlind shows video-LLMs fail at physically grounded motion understanding via contrastive self-recorded video pairs
  • OmniPoint unifies monocular metric 3D reconstruction across pinhole, fisheye, and equirectangular cameras
  • Tom Davidson argues data bottlenecks will slow, not prevent, a fast intelligence explosion
  • Osprey delivers target-agnostic speculative-decoding drafters; Phi-Bench tests whether LLMs can engineer serving infrastructure
entry.content:
Today's research highlights span frontier-scale safety fragility, agentic AI security, and a landmark open model release. Ling 2.0 scales open reasoning models to 1T parameters under a unified MoE design with systematic scaling-law analysis, while a prominent alignment researcher joining OpenAI's nonprofit board is the field's key governance signal.

Safety, governance, and security:

  • Refusal-direction ablation attacks, previously validated only on dense models up to ~70B, transfer to a 320B MoE, showing alignment fragility persists at frontier scale
  • AgentHijack and MMPIBench expose visual-patch hijacking and multimodal prompt injection against deployed computer-use agents
  • Obfuscated Adversarial Training mechanistic study finds probe-aligned structure in models trained against monitors

Capability, multimodality, and efficiency:

  • MotionBlind shows video-LLMs fail at physically grounded motion understanding via contrastive self-recorded video pairs
  • OmniPoint unifies monocular metric 3D reconstruction across pinhole, fisheye, and equirectangular cameras
  • Tom Davidson argues data bottlenecks will slow, not prevent, a fast intelligence explosion
  • Osprey delivers target-agnostic speculative-decoding drafters; Phi-Bench tests whether LLMs can engineer serving infrastructure

entry.title: Personal statement on joining the OpenAI nonprofit board

author.name: paulfchristiano

entry.summary: Alignment researcher Paul Christiano announces he is joining OpenAI's nonprofit board and its Safety and Security Committee, while stating his belief that loss-of-control risk from rapid AI acceleration is now acute and that the industry, including OpenAI, is not currently on track to reduce it to acceptable levels. He frames his role as providing safety oversight expertise at a critical moment and emphasizes that OpenAI should be judged by externally verifiable behavior. This is a significant signal about the state of safety governance at a leading frontier lab.

entry.title: MotionBlind: Probing the Illusion of Motion Understanding in Video-LLMs

author.name: Dhairya Bhatia, Bishoy Galoaa, Oliver Fritsche, Shahid Kamal, Muhammad Obaidullah Abdul Salam, Umer Saleem, Om Rastogi, Frania Felix Chettiar, Nesli Erdogmus, Sarah Ostadabbas
