entry.summary: Brain2Semantics2Text reconstructs text from non-invasive MEG recordings by decoding into an intermediate semantic embedding space before inverting embeddings into natural language, motivated by the distributed and slow-evolving nature of cortical semantic representations. This semantic bottleneck sidesteps the low SNR that makes phoneme- or word-level decoding hard.

entry.title: VLX-VR: An Agentic-Aware Video Reasoning Model

author.name: Sheng Li, Peng Liu, Qianqian Zhang, Tiancheng Zhao

entry.summary: VLX-VR is an agentic video reasoning model trained with reinforcement learning within a Think-Memory-Observation loop, where at each step it decides what evidence is needed, invokes memory read/write operations, and chooses whether to continue reasoning or emit an answer. This enables adaptive evidence acquisition in real-world video understanding where observations are incomplete, ambiguous, or conflicting, moving beyond fixed-context single-pass inference pipelines.

entry.title: MLLMs Hallucinate when Information Distribution Drifts in Synergy Heads

author.name: Meng'en Qin, Junye Chen, Jucheng Liu, Youlu Xing, Song Wang, Ruize Han

entry.summary: The authors propose HEAL, a head-level method for identifying and mitigating hallucinations in multimodal LLMs. It uses causal noise intervention to filter redundant heads and counterfactual Difference-in-Differences to disentangle information distribution, categorizing heads into four types related to hallucination behavior. This offers a more direct signal than prior attention-weight-based mitigation approaches.

entry.title: Vision-language models know more about agriculture than they show and rubric-grounded verifications close the gap

author.name: Earl Ranario, Jared Smith, Lars Lundqvist, Urmil Jatin Chandarana

entry.summary: Using a 116-dataset, 834-class agriculture benchmark, the authors show VLM vision encoders already encode agricultural features nearly as well as DINOv3, and that conditioning on oracle descriptions closes most of the zero-shot gap, indicating the bottleneck is knowledge connection rather than visual features. Rubric-grounded verification then improves practical performance.

entry.title: Learning to Adapt and Calibrate: Score Distribution Alignment for Few-Shot Uncertainty Prediction in Medical VLMs

author.name: Xuan Cuong Ngo, Ngan Le

entry.summary: Addresses the breakdown of conformal prediction guarantees in few-shot medical VLM transfer, where fine-tuning on a small support set shifts nonconformity score distributions and violates exchangeability. The method aligns score distributions between adaptation and calibration to restore reliable coverage with small calibration sets.

entry.title: JEPA Policy: Diffusion-Free Imitation Learning via Paired Action and Future Representation Prediction

author.name: Jie Xu, Kangjin Yu, Ziyi Jin, Junjie Gao, Liqing Chen, Yixian Li, Shuai Tian, Zhongpu Xia

entry.summary: Proposes JEPA Policy, a diffusion-free imitation learning framework that supervises action chunks alongside their observed future representations through a shared Transformer, so future prediction shapes the action-generating representation. Ablations with dual branches and gradient routing attribute gains to the shared topology. Reports improved success over action-only and diffusion baselines across nine simulated tasks.

entry.title: SwingBot: Learning Whole-Body Brachiation for Humanoid Robots

author.name: Yujie Xiong, Peng Zhai, Taixian Hou, Quancheng Qian, Cunwang Liu, Kangmai Hu, Long Yang, Zhiyan Dong, Lihua Zhang

entry.summary: Presents a learning framework for continuous humanoid brachiation with passive wrist hooks, structuring training around biomimetic keyframes to make rare release-swing-capture events trainable, coordinating alternating contacts with whole-body momentum without direct measurements of segment-relative displacement or hook contact. Brings primate-style swinging locomotion to high-DoF humanoids. An ambitious and distinctive locomotion modality.

entry.title: ContractEval: Query-Conditioned Execution Matching for Procedural Instruction Conformance

author.name: Praphul Singh, Shanu Kumar, Akshat Agarwal, Ganesh Kumar

entry.summary: Presents ContractEval, a diagnostic framework that represents procedural instructions as query-active obligations and matches them against response or trace evidence, catching invisible failures like skipped checks, wrong branches, ordering errors, and invariant breaches that output-only evaluation misses.

entry.title: No Free Checker: A Survey of Verifiers for Robot Policies

author.name: Yang Wan, Xihang Yue, Zhirui Liu, Ziyuan Chu, Shuxun Wang, Yuhan Chen, Xiaonan Jiang, Xukun Zhu, Yubo Dong, Linchao Zhu

entry.summary: A survey of roughly 150 verifiers for robot policies, spanning success detectors, reward models, runtime monitors, safety filters, and temporal-logic specifications, organized along availability (cost, timing, density of verdicts) and credibility (how gameable the judgment is) axes. It categorizes verifiers by who supplies the judgment and links them to both evaluation and training of vision-language-action policies. This fills a real gap by unifying a fragmented literature.

entry.title: A Later Test Set Is Not a New Domain: Pretraining Familiarity Survives a Contamination-Free Hold-Out

author.name: Mahdi Naser Moghadasi (BrightMind AI), Faezeh Ghaderi (University of Texas at Arlington)

entry.summary: The authors construct a strictly contamination-free benchmark for time-series foundation models, using observations published only after the last evaluated model was released across five domains. Pretrained forecasters still win 5 of 7 groups under this protocol, indicating genuine generalization rather than pure memorization, though daily exchange rates remain indistinguishable from a seasonal naive baseline. The paper then analyzes what separates wins from losses, providing rare controlled evidence on how pretraining familiarity and domain structure interact in time-series evaluation.

entry.title: SocialRL: Refining LLMs' Social Intelligence through Multi-turn Reinforcement Learning and Reward Design

author.name: Jianing Wang, Xintao Wang, Aili Chen, Jie Shi, Hongcheng Guo, Jun Gao, Wenxuan Zhao, Chengkun Lang, Yuanli Guo, Yanghua Xiao

entry.summary: SocialRL is a multi-turn reinforcement learning framework for improving LLM social intelligence, using PPO to propagate delayed outcome rewards back to individual turns and six process reward dimensions capturing social context, intent inference, and goal-relationship management. It targets the short-sighted policies produced by single-turn, sparse-reward RL methods. The work is relevant to building trustworthy, adaptive conversational agents for sustained human-AI interaction.

entry.title: Retrofitting Code Using LLMs to Support Exceptional Behavior

author.name: Linghan Zhong, Jiyang Zhang, Jayanth Srinivasa, Junyi Jessy Li, Milos Gligoric

entry.summary: The paper defines a new task, retrofitting Exception Related Code (throw statements, guarding conditions, try/catch blocks) into existing code so that given Exceptional Behavior Tests pass. The authors implement EXCODER, a constrained LLM-based system for this, addressing the tedium of manually adding exception handling across large codebases. This is a concrete, testable contribution to LLM-driven software engineering.

entry.title: DensePol: Dense-Angle Polarization Dataset for Learning-Based Polarimetric Vision

author.name: Param Sangani, Ahmad Moori, Erik Blasch, Guna Seetharaman, Hadi Aliakbarpour

entry.summary: DensePol introduces a high-redundancy RGB-polarization dataset using Division-of-Time acquisition with 180 polarization angles per resolution element, avoiding DoFP camera interpolation and instantaneous-FOV errors. It enables better supervision for learning to predict polarization from RGB images.

entry.title: UOT-Gap: A Variational Principle for the Modality Gap in Vision-Language Models via Unbalanced Optimal Transport

author.name: Zonglin Yang, Huilan Ma, Xudan Zheng, Yuejun Xie

entry.summary: Introduces a training-free variational diagnostic that models the image-text modality gap in frozen CLIP-like embeddings using unbalanced entropic optimal transport, decomposing the gap into transport cost, coupling complexity, and marginal mass variation. Experiments on Flickr8K and COCO-1K with CLIP, OpenCLIP, and SigLIP analyze how the gap relates to retrieval performance.

entry.title: Identifying Habit, Physics, and Nuisance in Robot World Models

author.name: Jinting Hang, Zhenhui Cai

entry.summary: Formalizes a structural causal model separating teleoperation-demonstration multimodality into operator habit, shared physics, and observation nuisance, arguing that entangled next-observation predictors absorb all three factors. It validates the decomposition with interventions such as action replacement and appearance changes, and proposes habit-aware reverse scoring plus an adaptation rule of freezing state-prediction components. This offers interpretability and better behavior synthesis for robot world models.

entry.title: InstantMimic: A High Performance System for Learning Physics-based Skills in Seconds

author.name: Ikjun Choi, Geonho Leem, Jungdam Won

entry.summary: InstantMimic is a systems contribution that dramatically accelerates training of physics-based imitation learning policies (DeepMimic-style) by fixing GPU underutilization caused by fragmented kernels and CPU memory access outside the physics solver. The result is learning physics-based character skills in seconds rather than the usual hours. This has implications for both computer graphics animation and robot locomotion research.

entry.title: Which Tokens Should SFT Actually Learn? A Token-Trimming Perspective on Mathematical Reasoning

author.name: Yaning Jia, Chunhui Zhang, Wenxuan Xu, Xingjian Diao, Xiaoyuan Wang, Soroush Vosoughi

entry.summary: Proposes TrimSFT, a token-level loss reweighting for supervised fine-tuning that scales loss by the logit gap between the gold token and its strongest competitor, trimming supervision on both mastered and weakly supported tokens to improve mathematical reasoning training dynamics.

entry.title: Why Sample What You Can Enumerate? Exact Policy Optimization for Genomic Tool Selection

author.name: Haoyue Liu, Xiaoyu Ma, Ye Chen, Zhichao Wang, Xiaoying Tang

entry.summary: The paper argues that GRPO-style RL over a frozen reasoner is structurally mismatched for tool selection in scientific domains where the tool-subset space is small enough to enumerate exactly. It shows the sampled advantage estimate degrades as training succeeds — policies resample concentrated subsets, rewards collide, and group-normalized advantages vanish — and proposes exact optimization instead, demonstrated on genomic reasoning. A sharp methodological critique with practical implications for RL on discrete tool spaces.

entry.title: TRACE: Training Reasoning Agents for Causal Exploration with Synthesized Rewards

author.name: Rui Sun, Zhan Shi, Bing He

entry.summary: TRACE engineers verifiable rewards for diagnostic reasoning where ground-truth causes are normally costly to establish: it samples interventions, injects them into a controlled simulator, and uses the hidden intervention as an oracle label while the agent investigates noisy, confounded evidence. This extends the RLVR recipe beyond math and code into causal diagnosis. The simulator-based reward synthesis idea is transferable to other verification-poor domains.

entry.title: Direct Diversity Optimization for Diverse Successful Trajectories in Preference Post-Training

author.name: Junwon Ko, Dong-Jae Lee, Minchan Kwon, Sunghyun Baek, Junmo Kim

entry.summary: DDO is an offline post-training method for LLM agents aimed at successful strategy coverage: realizing multiple distinct successful trajectories from shared decision states under a fixed rollout budget. It combines Divergence-Tree Collection, which builds state-aligned branch sets, with the Reference-Relative Target-Odds Objective. Reported results show the strongest task success among compared approaches while improving diversity.

entry.title: A-JIT: Agentic Just-In-Time Software Construction

author.name: Mark Marron, Earl T. Barr

entry.summary: A-JIT proposes a paradigm shift from static software artifacts to dynamic systems composed of code, a runtime harness, and an embedded AI agent that continuously observes usage and live execution traces to specialize logic, workflows, and tool interfaces to the end-user, analogous to how JIT compilers specialize machine code. The paper argues this integrated assembly, with synthesis embedded in the ambient runtime, can perpetually evolve applications to meet changing demands. It matters as an ambitious vision for how agentic code synthesis could restructure the software delivery lifecycle.

entry.title: IBIB: A Protocol for Measuring Enterprise AI Systems by Serving Route, Not Model Identifier

author.name: Blake Stenstrom, Charangan Vasantharajan, Brian Sathianathan

entry.summary: IB2 argues that enterprises deploy serving systems rather than model checkpoints, so all 18 audited benchmarks that score advertised model identifiers commit measurement error. The protocol adds a gold-blind capability-binding preflight, reliability-inclusive first-pass scoring, and structurally score-blind adjudication, with released algorithms, schemas, and a reference implementation. This is a thoughtful critique of how AI capability should be measured in production contexts.

entry.title: Steering Diffusion Priors with Sparse Observations for High-Resolution Temperature Downscaling

author.name: Anirudh Avireddy, Manmeet Singh, Shivanshi Singh, Ayush Raj, Saptarishi Dhanuka, Parthasarathi Mukhopadhyay, Sandeep Juneja

entry.summary: This paper builds a conditional diffusion emulator for high-resolution 2-meter temperature downscaling, conditioned on static geography, climatology, ERA5 fields, and temporal features. At inference, score-based data assimilation steers the diffusion score toward sparse station observations through a differentiable Gaussian likelihood without any retraining, improving hidden-cell reconstruction on a 32-case AORC-based protocol. This is directly relevant to fine-scale heatwave hazard assessment where ground stations are sparse.

entry.title: A Block Tensor Train Burer-Monteiro Framework for Low-Rank Quantum State Tomography

author.name: Shakir Showkat Sofi, Charlotte Vermeylen, Fatemeh Mohammadi, Lieven De Lathauwer

entry.summary: This work proposes a low-rank tensor-network formulation of mixed-state quantum state tomography that represents the density matrix as the contraction of a block tensor train (Block-TT) with its Hermitian transpose, analogous to a Burer-Monteiro factorization. This parameterization guarantees Hermiticity and positive semidefiniteness by construction while taming the exponential growth of the density matrix with qubit count. It makes tomography of larger quantum systems computationally tractable.

entry.title: Differentially Private Average Treatment Effect Estimation by Propensity Score Blocking

author.name: Duncan Stewardson, Grayson W. White, Adam Groce

entry.summary: The authors present two differentially private algorithms for estimating average treatment effects on observational data: an improved inverse probability weighting method and a new propensity-score blocking (BPS) approach. Both reduce error and bias relative to prior work, with the BPS algorithm frequently cutting error by 75 percent or more, which matters for causal inference on sensitive medical and social-science data.

entry.title: MedDeID enables locally governed clinical-text de-identification from real or synthetic training data

author.name: Stig Hellemans, Tom Stroobants, Elyne Scheurwegs, Pieter Meysman, Philippe G. Jorens, Kris Laukens

entry.summary: Introduces MedDeID, an on-premises clinical-text de-identification framework combining in-house annotation, synthetic-note generation, and compact transformer training. On a Dutch hospital benchmark the hospital-trained model detects 98.9% of identifying text with minimal over-redaction, and notably a synthetic-data-only model reaches 96.1% and even outperforms on primary-care notes, showing synthetic training data alone can be effective.

entry.title: Are You Learning Biological Signal or Shortcuts? Auditing and Mitigating Bias in Protein-Protein Interaction Datasets

author.name: Judith Bernett, Anton Spannagl, Joel {\AA}s, Markus List, David B. Blumenthal

entry.summary: This paper systematically characterizes both known and previously unreported biases in protein-protein interaction datasets (HIPPIE, IntAct, STRING, and 3D-structure-derived sets) that let ML models learn shortcuts instead of biological signal. It offers an integrated audit and mitigation strategy going beyond prior work that examined these biases in isolation.

entry.title: ROAM: Robust Organization of Atomic Memories for Agents through Semantic Relations

author.name: Jianjie Zheng, Peng Lai, Sijie Cheng, Jiehui Zhao, Lei Yang, Guanhua Chen

entry.summary: ROAM is a relation-guided framework for managing long-term agent memory, classifying incoming-versus-stored atomic memory pairs as independent, equivalent, subsuming, or conflicting, and separating semantic interpretation from storage and content-generation decisions. This addresses redundancy, overlap, and conflict accumulation in atomic-memory systems, where prior LLM-manager approaches couple too many error-prone operations. The design improves retrieval precision and answer-time representations for long-lived agents.

entry.title: Why Is Video Still So Expensive? A Survey of Inference-Efficiency Mechanisms in Video and Audiovisual LLMs

author.name: Killian Steunou, Yannis Tevissen, Moun\^im A. El Yacoubi

entry.summary: This survey systematically covers inference-efficiency mechanisms for video and audiovisual LLMs, including frame sampling, modality encoding, connector design, and token reduction strategies that reduce FLOPs, latency, memory, and token counts. It maps bottlenecks across the VideoLLM pipeline, which matters as video models face compute costs scaling with frame count and context length. Useful reference for deploying video understanding in resource-constrained settings.

entry.title: TRACE: Trajectory-robust Admission with Evidence Ordering for Efficient GUI Agents

author.name: Yuhao Wang, Mu Qiao, Xindong Zhang, Yunzhi Zhuge, Lei Zhang, Huchuan Lu

entry.summary: Addresses inference cost in GUI agents where high-resolution screenshot trajectories grow memory and latency, framing training-free visual token pruning as an irreversible admission decision under cache reuse. TRACE jointly optimizes robust admission and coverage-aware evidence ordering to keep pruned tokens useful for future targets.

entry.title: ViBe: Visual Behavior Adaptation for Perceptive Humanoid Whole-Body Control

author.name: Lokesh Krishna, Sarvesh Venkatesan, An Zhang, Quan Nguyen

entry.summary: A post-training framework that grafts pre-trained visual encoders onto humanoid motion trackers via a multi-query extractor and low-rank adapters, adding task-relevant perceptive feedback with parameter-efficient fine-tuning. Avoids training geometry-only encoders from scratch and the need for task-specific teacher-student distillation. Addresses the gap between motion-tracking controllers and perception in humanoid whole-body control.

entry.title: Assembling Two Parts in One Hand

author.name: Liuao Pei, Tianyue Wu, Hui Zhang, Ping Luo, Jie Song

entry.summary: Studies in-hand assembly - mating two rigid objects within a single dexterous hand with no second arm or fixture - via reinforcement learning shaped by function-based auxiliary rewards and a human reference pose, with domain randomization and fused proprioceptive-object observations for robustness. Captures finger-level coordination that is a hallmark of human dexterity. A demanding and relatively unexplored manipulation problem.

entry.title: XAI-Arena: Can LLMs Assess the Quality of XAI Explanations?

author.name: Yanfei Hu Fleischhauer, Alona Zharova, Nadja Klein, Stefan Feuerriegel

entry.summary: Introduces XAI-Arena, an LLM-as-a-judge framework for reproducible, multidimensional evaluation of explainable-AI outputs across dimensions like clarity, faithfulness, trust calibration, and actionability. It aims to replace subjective human judgments with a scalable comparison mechanism for XAI methods.

entry.title: RobustSGPO: Search-Space Control for Agent Harness Evolution

author.name: Zibo Zhao, Jijun Shi, Mo Zhou, Zhongyuan Wang, Shifu Bie, Yunfei Zhang, Xuanting Zhou, Xiangyu Wu, Bin Liu, Ruiming Tang, Wenwu Ou, Kun Gai

entry.summary: Extends semantic-gradient prompt optimization (SGPO) for evolving agent harnesses with explicit search-space control over edit scope and operations, evaluating permission scheduling and snapshot-based search on the AgentX brainstorming workflow across 120 tasks, 95 runs, and 7,350 candidate attempts, improving held-out completion from 60% to 80%.

entry.title: Reference-Based Bias Detection in LLMs via Relative Representations of Hidden States

author.name: Marek Jeli\'nski, Jan Dubi\'nski, Maciej Chrabaszcz, Sebastian Cygert

entry.summary: The paper proposes auditing bias in hidden-state representations across related model variants, encoding sentences by similarity to fixed anchor sentences to form comparable relative representations, then measuring how target groups shift in positive/negative associations (Representational Bias Shift). This internal approach can catch bias shifts that never surface in generated text, complementing output-based audits. Relevant to model-editing and fine-tuning governance.

entry.title: ConvMem: Convolutional Memory for Long-Context Reasoning

author.name: Hongming Zhang, Zhaozhen Gu, Fengshuo Bai, Ming Hao, Qingyang Zhang, Yuanyuan Wang, Shiyang Tang, Yanna Wang, Bo Xu

entry.summary: ConvMem reformulates long-context reasoning as a hierarchical convolution, treating an LLM prompted with a specific query as a convolutional kernel over text segments, in contrast to sequential approaches like MemAgent that read segments and iteratively update fixed-size memory via costly RL training. Being training-free and highly parallelizable, it targets the latency and overfitting weaknesses of the sequential paradigm. An inventive reframing with clear efficiency motivation.

entry.title: Quantifying Logical Consistency in Transformers via Query-Key Alignment

author.name: Eduard Tulchinskii, Anastasia Voznyuk, Laida Kushnareva, Andrei Andriiainen, Irina Piontkovskaya, Evgeny Burnaev, Serguei Barannikov

entry.summary: The authors propose a lightweight probe of logical reasoning that extracts a QK-score from attention head query-key alignments in a single forward pass, separating valid from invalid inferences. This offers an internal-representation-based alternative to output-level Chain-of-Thought evaluation. The work matters because it connects mechanistic interpretability tools to reasoning-quality assessment.

entry.title: Learning with Synthetic Data via SGD in High-Dimensional Linear Regression

author.name: Jichu li, Difan Zou

entry.summary: Establishes finite-sample risk bounds for one-pass SGD in high-dimensional linear regression trained on mixed real/synthetic data under model shift, decomposing risk into bias, variance, fluctuation, persistent drift, and initialization-bias terms. The analysis sharpens the model-collapse picture, showing contrasting behavior between mixed and two-stage training. Theoretically relevant to the growing debate on synthetic data scaling.

entry.title: Subgroup Membership Inference Audits of Differentially Private Synthetic Text

author.name: Yidan Sun, Viktor Schlegel, Srinivasan Nandakumar, Siew Kei Lam, Anil Anthony Bharath

entry.summary: This paper defines a subgroup-targeted membership inference game for auditing differentially private synthetic text, where the target pool is an explicit parameter. Standard MIA audits measure average-case risk, potentially masking elevated leakage for vulnerable subgroups. Auditing 32 proxies across scenarios of differing stringency, the work exposes residual privacy risks that DP guarantees and average-case audits conceal.

entry.title: Tensor-Train Weak SINDy: Identifying High-Dimensional Nonlinear Dynamics

author.name: Will Houser, Vanja Dukic, David M. Bortz

entry.summary: TT-WSINDy combines the MANDy and WSINDy frameworks using tensor-train format to enable weak-form sparse identification of nonlinear dynamical systems in high dimensions. The method searches an exponentially growing candidate-function space while performing weak-form transformation, regression, and sparsification without incurring the curse of dimensionality. This is a meaningful scalability advance for data-driven equation discovery.

entry.title: Field-level prediction of mid-plane stress tensor fields in concrete target penetration: a cross-velocity graph neural operator surrogate

author.name: Wenpu Du, Peng Zhou, Yunlong Xia, Sinuo Xin, Congcong Zhang, Boyang Zhang, Yi Zhang, Wenzheng Xu

entry.summary: The authors build a graph neural operator surrogate predicting full six-component stress-tensor fields in concrete penetration across impact velocities, trained on 400 cases from a verified full-scale aggregate-resolved LS-DYNA simulation validated against published experiments. The work links mesoscale heterogeneity to full-field stress prediction, a previously missing capability.

entry.title: A Subsampled Davis-Kahan Bound for Large-Scale Eigenspace Estimation

author.name: Huan Qing

entry.summary: This paper extends the classical Davis-Kahan theorem to subsampled settings, proposing an independent Bernoulli sampling scheme where leading singular vectors of a subsampled matrix provably approximate the target subspace of a low-rank symmetric matrix. The main result is an explicit error bound tied directly to the sampling probability, enabling principled dimensionality reduction before eigendecomposition. This makes spectral methods more tractable for very large-scale applications.

entry.title: Encrypt What Matters: When Selective Homomorphic Inference Is Efficient

author.name: Ali Backour, Juan Reyes, Jaime Punyed, Ana Onoprishvili

entry.summary: This paper studies selective homomorphic inference, where only a sensitive region of interest of an input is encrypted under FHE while the rest is processed in plaintext, producing identical outputs to full FHE without retraining. The key finding is that efficiency hinges on how fast encrypted dependencies spread: locality-preserving architectures yield order-of-magnitude speedups for small ROIs, while architectures with early global mixing (like attention-heavy transformers) give essentially none. This gives actionable architecture-design guidance for privacy-preserving inference.

entry.title: MethaneFuse: Learning from Multi-Sensor Satellite Observations for Methane Plume Detection

author.name: Yuyao Wang, Juliana Y. Leung, Di Niu

entry.summary: Builds MethaneUnion, a temporal multi-sensor dataset pairing Carbon Mapper plume reports with Sentinel-2, Landsat 8/9, EMIT, and Sentinel-5P observations, and proposes MethaneFuse to fuse heterogeneous satellite evidence despite rarely having fully paired measurements. This addresses the limitation that most plume detectors rely on single-sensor inputs, making many reported cases unusable.

entry.title: Optimal Low-Rank Quantum State Tomography with Bounded-Sample Joint Measurements

author.name: Ashwin Nayak, Xingyu Zhou

entry.summary: The authors determine the optimal sample complexity of low-rank quantum state tomography when each measurement acts jointly on at most t samples, proving matching upper and lower bounds of order dr/eps^2 times max{1, r/sqrt(t)}. The lower bound holds even against adaptive protocols, while the matching upper bound is nonadaptive.

entry.title: SWORD: Wikidata-based Distortions Reveal Hidden Cross-Lingual Inconsistencies in LLM Factual Error Rejection

author.name: Sanghyeok Park, Minji Kang, Hosung Kwak, Jinhyuk Yun

entry.summary: SWORD is a benchmark that generates syntactically well-formed but factually incorrect statements in eight languages via controlled perturbations of Wikidata triples, evaluating whether LLMs consistently reject factual errors across languages. It surfaces cross-lingual inconsistencies in counterfactual robustness that conventional correctness-focused benchmarks obscure.

entry.title: Deep and shallow biases in language models

author.name: An Vo, Vy Tuong Dang, Khai-Nguyen Nguyen, Emilio Villa-Cueva, Thamar Solorio, Anh Totti Nguyen, Daeyoung Kim

entry.summary: The paper proposes a bias depth score that separates stable model preferences (deep biases that survive scenario reframing) from prompt-dependent ones (shallow biases), evaluated across 4,442 opinion prompts and four LLMs. Only about a quarter of concentrated preferences persist under reframing, and the authors show deep biases are more often inherited from pretraining. This refines prior work that treated answer concentration monolithically as bias.

entry.title: Less Is Personal: Learning Minimal Sufficient User Profiles for Personalized Language Models

author.name: Minghang Liu, Qiang Qiu, Yuanzhuo Wang, Huawei Shen, Xueqi Cheng

entry.summary: This paper studies minimal sufficient personalization: building the shortest effective ordered profile of user records for retrieval-augmented personalization of LLMs, instead of blindly prepending a fixed number of history records. The proposed ENOUGH method iteratively appends records or emits STOP, using bounded counterfactual search to evaluate profile prefixes. This improves cost-efficiency and avoids harm from redundant or unrelated history.

entry.title: CLFTv2: Efficient Camera-LiDAR Fusion for Semantic Segmentation via Hierarchical Feature Pyramids

author.name: Toomas Tahves, Mauro Bellone, Raivo Sell

entry.summary: CLFTv2 replaces global ViT attention with a Swin-based multi-scale encoder and lightweight FPN-style residual decoder for camera-LiDAR semantic segmentation, improving vulnerable-road-user recall across three driving datasets (e.g., 53.5 percent mIoU on ZOD, substantially improving pedestrian IoU). It avoids costly query-matching decoders.

entry.title: Beyond Similarity: Foundation Models as an Efficient Backbone for Training-Free Composed Video Retrieval

author.name: Dmitry Demidov, Muhammad Zaigham Zaheer, Omkar Thawakar, Abdelrahman Mohamed Shaker, Rao Anwer

entry.summary: Addresses the scalability-accuracy tension in composed video retrieval by assigning frozen foundation models complementary roles, adapting inference depth to query difficulty in a training-free framework. Compact embeddings enable efficient search while heavier multimodal reasoning is reserved for harder queries.

entry.title: DCReg: Decoupled Characterization for Efficient Degenerate LiDAR Registration

author.name: Xiangcheng Hu, Xieyuanli Chen, Mingkai Jia, Jin Wu, Ping Tan, Steven L. Waslander

entry.summary: Introduces DCReg, a detect-characterize-mitigate paradigm for LiDAR registration in geometrically degenerate environments such as corridors, where ill-conditioning makes solutions unstable. It uses Schur complement decomposition for reliable detection of ill-conditioned directions, physically interprets them, and mitigates instability without corrupting the optimization. This improves robustness of robotic perception and navigation in challenging scenes.

entry.title: GTA-2: A Multi-VLM Framework for Synthesizing Robot Manipulation Skills via Grounded Task Axes

author.name: M. Yunus Seker, Shobhit Aggarwal, Ruwan Wickramarachchi, Jonathan Francis, Oliver Kroemer

entry.summary: GTA-2 composes executable manipulation skills from reusable object-centric task-axis components, using multiple VLMs to produce semantic subtasks with keypoints, axes, controller compositions, and scene-dependent conditions rather than end-to-end action prediction or fixed primitives. A modular alternative to monolithic VLA policies that exposes geometric and control decisions explicitly. From a strong manipulation group including Oliver Kroemer.

entry.title: Gradland: On Phenomenal Experience, Differentiated Across Many Dimensions

author.name: David Balduzzi

entry.summary: David Balduzzi (DeepMind) proposes that the structure of phenomenal experience is characterized by first-order interaction structure, i.e. gradients and Jacobians, tested in an idealized differentiable world called Gradland. It introduces effective rank and cohesion measures of Jacobian structure and shows they account for duration, vividness, texture, and other experiential features.

entry.title: AgentAudit: An Open, Extensible Framework for Full-Lifecycle Trust Evaluation of AI Agents

author.name: Shrey Nag, Sachita, Abhishek Kumar Singh, Lipi Goel, Rajeshwar Singh Janwar

entry.summary: AgentAudit evaluates the entire agent execution trace — planning, tool selection, tool execution, memory, and reasoning — across ten capability, grounding, security, and behavioral dimensions, with failure attribution pinpointing the exact stage responsible for a failure. Unlike AgentBench or AgentDojo, which test one facet, it audits the full pipeline. This addresses a practical need for diagnosing why agents fail, not just whether they do.

entry.title: Time-Frequency Geometric Cross-Attention for Chunked Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Shengye Dong, Haochen Niu, Hao Liu, Peiwen Lin, Chuang Wang, Shanmin Pang

entry.summary: The paper observes that action chunks in vision-language-action models are short multivariate trajectories currently decoded through generic per-timestep tokens, and proposes a cross-attention mechanism that separates smooth global trends from fine corrective motion across time scales and captures near-orthogonal phase geometry (reach, contact, grasp). This is a targeted architectural improvement for robot policy decoding. If validated, it could improve manipulation precision in chunked VLA policies.

entry.title: Scaling Post-Training Ternarisation to Qwen3-8B Capability Retention, Reproduction, Lossless Packing, and Packed Execution

author.name: Anirudh Malik, M Sparsh Mehra, Poojith Devan

entry.summary: This work scales an aggressive post-training ternarisation pipeline from Qwen3-4B to Qwen3-8B, combining known techniques (KOTMS rotation, adaptive ternarisation, GPTQ-style compensation) with an end-to-end characterization: reproduction gates, cross-corpus perplexity, effective-bit accounting, lossless packing, and direct packed execution. The 8-bit-weight-free model shows strong capability retention with real memory-traffic savings. It is an engineering-heavy contribution to ultra-low-bit quantization at practical scale.

entry.title: Auditable Emergency Triage for Maternal and Newborn Care in India

author.name: Shobhit Jagga, Aman Dalmia, Niharika Priyadarshini, Neelima Devadas, Amrita K Prasen, Nikhil Nalin, Santhosh SJ, Sreeram Nurani Ramasubramanian, Muhammed Afeer K, Anubhav Arora

entry.summary: Noora Health describes replacing an opaque LLM-based emergency triage classifier for over 50,000 monthly WhatsApp medical queries with a system aligned to clinicians' decision-tree workflow, producing auditable decisions and rationales. Prompt changes previously required costly full re-evaluations to avoid regressions, motivating the structured design. It is a real-world deployment case study in high-stakes maternal and newborn health.

entry.title: High-probability guarantees for linear accessibility in feature superposition

author.name: Enrico Vompa

entry.summary: Frames linear accessibility of superposed features as a compressed sensing problem and derives high-probability bounds showing the sufficient dimension scales as O(k log m) rather than prior worst-case quadratic limits, validated with Gaussian-tail approximations. This quantifies geometric constraints underlying the linear representation hypothesis. Directly relevant to interpretability tools like sparse autoencoders.

entry.title: Distilling Image Prototypes for Guided Test-Time Adaptation

author.name: Liwen Wang, Xingbo Dong, Iman Yi Liao, Deyin Liu, Massimo Tistarelli, Lin Yuanbo Wu, Zhe Jin

entry.summary: DIPTTA introduces Distilled Image Prototypes, compact synthetic prototypes distilled from source data, to guide test-time adaptation of vision models. The approach simultaneously mitigates noisy pseudo-label error accumulation and catastrophic forgetting, avoiding overconfident uncertainty estimates and static prototype replay. This targets the two dominant failure modes of TTA under distribution shift.

entry.title: GANDR: Claim Auditing for Verifiable Legal Answer Generation

author.name: Chen Qian, Yimeng Wang, Yu Chen, Lingfei Wu, Andreas Stathopoulos

entry.summary: GANDR (Grounded ANswer DRafter) is a two-agent system for legal question answering in which a Drafter writes answers in a structured legal-reasoning format and a separate Critic, given the same view as a human verifier, audits each claim against its cited source and emits a per-claim audit trace every round. This addresses the problem that whole-answer scoring lets a correct conclusion rest on fabricated or loosely matched citations. The work matters because per-claim verifiability is essential for LLM deployment in high-stakes domains like law.

entry.title: Learning Intrusion Response Strategies for OT Systems

author.name: Duc Huy Le, Rolf Stadler

entry.summary: This paper formalizes automated intrusion response for Operational Technology (OT) systems as a POMDP, with realistic partial observability derived from network traffic measurements. The authors train PPO-based response policies and demonstrate effectiveness against several MITRE ATT&CK attack types on an emulated OT system. It matters because industrial control systems are high-stakes targets where automated, learned defenses could reduce response latency.

entry.title: Spectral origin of the topological gap exponent d + {\eta}: mechanism, kernel, decomposition, and scope

author.name: Matthew Loftus

entry.summary: This paper provides an analytical derivation of the scaling law for the topological gap, the excess H1 total persistence of a critical point cloud compared to a density-matched null. It identifies a spectral integral as the mechanism, decomposes the exponent into volume and anomalous-dimension factors, and proves the mechanism only applies under infrared dominance, restricting it to d = 2 for physical systems. This matters because it converts an empirical topological data analysis observation into a rigorous theoretical result with clearly stated scope limits.

entry.title: Positional task conditioning for scalable defect detection across product families in large product catalogs

author.name: Soham Satyadharma, Gabriel Roccabruna, Suleiman A. Khan

entry.summary: The paper tackles defect detection in large e-commerce catalogs by decomposing detection into focused sub-tasks that isolate error types, lifting F1 from 52 to 87 percent, and introduces Positional Task Conditioning (PTC) to distill the multi-task capability into a single smaller model. PTC reinforces task identity at structural prompt boundaries and outperforms rationale-based distillation across five models and two architecture families.

entry.title: ProMeta: Few-shot PROTAC-targeted degradation prediction across E3 ligases

author.name: Yuansheng Liu, Yufei Ye, Tao Tang, Jiawei Luo, Wen Tao, Xiao Luo

entry.summary: This paper addresses prediction of PROTAC-induced protein degradation across E3 ligases using few-shot meta-learning, targeting the problem that labeled data is concentrated on well-studied ligases like CRBN and VHL. By enabling cross-ligase generalization, the work could expand the computational design space for degraders against undruggable targets. It sits at the intersection of drug discovery and machine learning, where data scarcity is a core bottleneck.

entry.title: Adversarial Training for Tabular Credit Scoring: A Multi-Attack Robustness Evaluation in P2P Lending

author.name: Gijs A. F. Niewzwaag, Marijn G. S. Veth, Manuele Massei, Marcos R. Machado

entry.summary: This paper benchmarks adversarial robustness for ML-based credit scoring in P2P lending, evaluating three model families (logistic regression, feed-forward neural network, tabular transformer) against four attacks restricted to applicant-mutable features on a large Lending Club dataset. It addresses the underexplored question of how tabular-data defences generalize across attack types, unlike prior image/text-focused single attack-defence studies.

entry.title: Infra-Bench CLS: A Global, Open-Source Benchmark for Critical Infrastructure Classification with Earth Observation Foundation Models

author.name: Justin Guthrie, Edward Oughton, Konrad Wessels, Matthew Rice, Isaac Corley

entry.summary: The paper introduces Infra-Bench CLS, an open-source benchmark of 18,756 Sentinel-1 SAR and Sentinel-2 multispectral images for evaluating Earth observation foundation models on facility-scale critical infrastructure detection and classification. It addresses the global scarcity and uneven distribution of critical infrastructure location data, particularly in developing regions, and tests how well general-purpose geospatial foundation models transfer to this challenging downstream task.

entry.title: LightMedSeg-ISLES: Stroke Lesion Segmentation with 81x Fewer Parameters than nnU-Net

author.name: Giorgi Nikvashvili, Hanxue Gu, Jie Bao, Kang Wang, Yang Yang

entry.summary: Presents a 1.26M-parameter pipeline for T1-weighted stroke lesion segmentation in the ISLES 2026 challenge that achieves 0.618 Dice versus 0.634 for a 102M-parameter nnU-Net ResEnc-L, while improving lesion-wise F1 and using 4.7x fewer FLOPs with test-time augmentation. Demonstrates near-parity with much larger baselines at a fraction of the deployment cost.

entry.title: Zero-Shot Temporal Localisation of Audio Deepfakes in Multi-Speaker Conversations

author.name: Soumyadeep Roy

entry.summary: This paper formalizes Temporal Deepfake Localisation in Multi-Speaker Conversations (TDLMC), addressing voice-cloning fraud where only one or two sentences in a real conversation are synthetic. It proposes a training-free five-stage pipeline that wraps a frozen binary deepfake detector to produce segment-level localisations, using a two-threshold hysteresis finite-state-machine decoder, plus new temporal metrics for mixed real/fake files.

entry.title: BuzzASR: A Swarm of 100+ Monolingual Speech Recognition Models

author.name: Shivam Singh, Aditya Yadavalli, Catherine Arnett, Alex Warstadt

entry.summary: The authors fine-tune Whisper into over 100 language-specialized ASR models covering 102 languages from the FLEURS dataset, massively scaling a previously small-scale monolingual adaptation strategy. This addresses the well-known weakness of highly multilingual models on underrepresented languages. The release of a large swarm of specialized models is a practical resource for low-resource speech research.

entry.title: Scaling E-Commerce Attribute Extraction with Parallel Decoding

author.name: Nikhita Vedula, Dushyanta Dhyani, Bryan Wang, Shervin Malmasi

entry.summary: This paper from Amazon-affiliated researchers presents a two-stage LLM pipeline for e-commerce attribute value extraction: first discovering a compact ranked schema of purchase-discriminative attributes per product category, then extracting values with a fine-tuned compact model (Qwen3-4B) using Hyper-Parallel Decoding. It reports 85% extraction accuracy while producing attribute sets that better reflect how customers actually compare products. The work matters because it addresses the gap between messy real-world catalogs and consumer decision-relevant structure, with an efficiency focus that enables production-scale deployment.

entry.title: HyperTrace: Hypothesis-Based Preference Tracing for Online LLM Personalization

author.name: Jianzhi Shen, Keyu Mao, Minghao Shao, Chuanyang Jin, Yusong Wang, Ailiang Lin, Kotaro Funakoshi, Manabu Okumura, Tianmin Shu, Muhammad Shafique

entry.summary: HyperTrace is a training-free framework that casts online LLM personalization as latent preference tracing, maintaining interpretable natural-language hypotheses about short-term intent and long-term user preferences. It updates these hypotheses across turns and sessions using a sequential Monte Carlo-style reweighting process with an LLM-based surrogate choice model. This addresses a real weakness in existing memory/retrieval-based personalization methods that struggle to reconcile long-term preferences with topic-specific short-term needs.

entry.title: Data-Centric Post-Training for Financial Reasoning: Mining, Distillation, and Verifiable Learning

author.name: Zhirayr Hayrapetyan, Andrei Kalmykov, Denis Kokosinskii, Dmitry Stanishevskii, Dmitry Zmitrovich

entry.summary: This paper presents a data-centric pipeline for building training corpora for financial reasoning, combining mined open-source reasoning traces, distilled financial instruction data, and knowledge-graph-guided QA pairs generated from financial textbooks. Lightweight sequence classifiers filter and select finance-relevant, verifiable examples suitable for reinforcement learning after semantic deduplication. It matters because high-quality, verifiable reasoning data remains a bottleneck for domain-specific post-training, and the pipeline offers a reusable recipe for other specialized domains.

entry.title: On-Policy Distillation for Vision-Language Model Adaptation, an Effective Paradigm on Low-Quality Multimodal Data

author.name: Hongyuan Zhang, Xianda Guo, Yanlun Peng, Qianlong Yang, Yubin Guo, Pinhan Fu, Mulin Chen, Xiaozhen Qiao, Ping Luo

entry.summary: This paper proposes OnPoKD, the first on-policy distillation framework for vision-language model adaptation, treating distillation target construction as a dynamic training decision rather than a fixed teacher-prediction recipe. The approach aims to make distillation from a task-adapted VLM teacher to a compact student reliable under class and domain shifts and on low-quality multimodal data. This extends the on-policy distillation paradigm, popularized for LLMs, into multimodal adaptation.

entry.title: Do speech foundation models really learn words?

author.name: Robin Huo, Ewan Dunbar

entry.summary: This paper examines whether self-supervised speech foundation models like HuBERT and wav2vec 2.0 learn true word representations or merely encode phoneme-level word forms. Using residualization to partial out phoneme information, the authors show that apparent word discrimination in later layers can be explained by phoneme encoding rather than form-independent word identity or semantic representations. This matters for interpreting how speech models should be used as token sources for speech-aware language models.

entry.title: M2LG-DG: A Multi-modal Local-Global Domain Generalization Framework for Cross-site Major Depressive Disorder Classification

author.name: Muhammad Asif Hasan, Yanming Zhu, Xuefei Yin, Alan Wee-Chung Liew

entry.summary: This paper proposes a multi-modal local-global domain generalization framework for classifying major depressive disorder from resting-state fMRI across imaging sites. It addresses site-specific scanner and acquisition effects that cause models to fail on unseen sites, a key barrier to clinical deployment of psychiatric neuroimaging models.

entry.title: Can We Trust Video Hallucination Detectors? VidHalLoc for Evaluating the Evaluators

author.name: Xinyu Chen, Adnan Mahmood, Mark Dras

entry.summary: Introduces VidHalLoc, a benchmark of 2,000 adversarial hallucination samples for evaluating video hallucination detectors under a unified diagnostic protocol across VideoQA and captioning tasks. It also proposes VideoHALO, a multi-agent harness-engineering workflow for efficient benchmark construction. The work matters because it shifts evaluation from model hallucinations to the reliability of the detectors themselves.

entry.title: Shape-guided Gaussian Splatting for Sparse-View X-ray 3D Reconstruction

author.name: Pranav Poudel, Florence Dell'Aniello Picard, Nairouz Shehata, Fr\'ed\'eric Lavoie, Herve Lombaert

entry.summary: Incorporates statistical shape models as anatomical priors into 3D Gaussian Splatting to stabilize sparse-view X-ray reconstruction, where only a handful of projections are available and unconstrained optimization fails. The population-level bounded variation of anatomy regularizes the severely ill-posed inverse problem, relevant to reducing radiation exposure.

entry.title: Actuator Dynamics Curricula for Narrow-Viability Tasks in Legged Robot Learning

author.name: Kousheek Chakraborty, Chandan K. Rajendra, Ayham Alharbat, Abeje Y. Mersha

entry.summary: Introduces an Actuator Dynamics Curriculum that anneals joint stiffness toward the identified value as episodes lengthen, enlarging the MDP viability kernel so that hard tasks with sparse gradient signal become trainable. Demonstrated on a cart-pole representative system with theoretical motivation via natural frequency under critical damping. Addresses a real and underexplored failure mode of standard RL training in robotics.

entry.title: Learning Terrain-Adaptive Humanoid Locomotion on Granular Terrain

author.name: Junnosuke Kamohara, Feiyang Wu, Andy Ningan Zong, Daniel I. Goldman, Yashwanth Nakka, Seth Hutchinson, Ye Zhao

entry.summary: Develops a physics-grounded granular contact model based on 3D resistive force theory for efficient RL training of humanoid locomotion on granular terrain, avoiding heuristics and capturing realistic penetration dynamics. Joint work spanning Goldman lab granular mechanics expertise and robotics control. Addresses a real modeling gap for foot-terrain interaction on sand and similar media.

entry.title: Frequency-Conditioned Flow Matching for Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Haochen Niu, Shengye Dong, Hao Liu, Peiwen Lin, Wang Chuang

entry.summary: FreqFM introduces frequency-domain conditioning into flow matching for vision-language-action robot models, treating action frequency spectra as an explicit conditioning dimension rather than an implicit trajectory property. Working in DCT frequency coordinates, it constructs spectrum-matched source distributions and adaptively balances objectives across frequencies. This addresses the non-uniform energy distribution of robot motion across temporal scales.

entry.title: PRAGMA: Evaluating Personalized Guidance with Memory Alignment in Lifelong Conversations

author.name: Hyojeong Yu, Hyukhun Koh, Minsung Kim, Yunah Jang, Kyomin Jung

entry.summary: Proposes PRAGMA, a benchmark for evaluating personalized guidance (recommendations, planning, decision support) in lifelong LLM conversations where memory systems must selectively retrieve and integrate user-specific information rather than relying on full history contexts.

entry.title: Talking to Itself While Coding: What Makes Comments Help Code Generation?

author.name: Dangfeng Pan, Zhensu Sun, Cenyuan Zhang, David Lo, Xiaoning Du

entry.summary: Through observational analyses and controlled interventions on LiveCodeBench, the paper finds comment frequency and intent do not predict code-generation pass@1, but prefilling weaker models with comments from passing solutions raises recipient pass@1 by 17.2% on average. This separates comment surface form from the solution content comments convey. It offers actionable insight into self-generated context in LLM coding.

entry.title: LogiScope-VQA: Benchmarking Vision-Language Models for Logistics Hazard Identification in Industrial Scenarios

author.name: Hanjing Zhou, Mingze Yin, Ying Lian, Jun Ma, Chang-Yu Hsieh, Yanbing Zhou

entry.summary: LogiScope-VQA is a multimodal benchmark of 2,476 images and 2,918 videos from real logistics parks with 10,274 curated VQAs covering 39 subtasks over 18 object types and 20 risk types. It tests whether mainstream large multimodal models can achieve human-expert-level hazard perception and reasoning in warehouse settings. The benchmark exposes the gap between general VLM capability and industrial safety applications.

entry.title: StochBench: A Domain-Specific Benchmark for Stochastic Processes in Lean

author.name: Idan Davidovich, Debargha Ganguly, Vikash Singh, Vipin Chaudhary

entry.summary: StochBench is a Lean 4 benchmark of 450 graduate-level stochastic-processes problems paired with natural-language sources, covering Markov chains, martingales, stochastic calculus, and more, addressing the competition-math skew of existing theorem-proving benchmarks. A Claude Opus 4.8-based agent achieves a 34.9% proof rate under a 15-minute limit, with Opus 4.8 being an established frontier model released earlier in 2026.

entry.title: An Efficient and Effective Agentic Group Shilling Attack on Recommender Systems

author.name: Quoc Viet Nguyen, Trinh Pham, Viet Huynh, Hongzhi Yin, Quoc Viet Hung Nguyen, Bay Vo, Thanh Tam Nguyen

entry.summary: AGAS is a coordinated multi-agent framework for shilling attacks on recommender systems, where a central Coordinator directs role-switching worker agents to adaptively promote target items without target-specific fine-tuning or fixed templates. The work demonstrates that LLM-driven agents can conduct adaptive, harder-to-detect ranking manipulation at scale. This exposes an emerging security threat class for recommendation platforms.

entry.title: SynThermFace: Amplifying Limited Paired Data for Visible-Thermal Face Recognition via Synthetic Data Generation

author.name: Anjith George, Adam Unal, Sebastien Marcel

entry.summary: Proposes adapting diffusion models to generate synthetic paired visible-thermal face data, amplifying limited real supervision for cross-spectral face recognition useful in low-light and nighttime authentication. From an established biometrics group (Marcel et al.), the framework addresses the key bottleneck of scarce paired cross-spectral data.

entry.title: Spot-the-shift: Evaluating Grounded Image Difference Captioning of Long-term Changes

author.name: Benedetta Liberatori, Nermin Samet, Paolo Rota, Matthieu Cord, Elisa Ricci, Andrei Bursuc, Monika Wysocza\'nska

entry.summary: Introduces SPOT-THE-SHIFT, a human-verified benchmark for grounded image difference captioning of long-term structural changes in real-world driving scenes, pairing natural-language captions with spatial masks. Includes a validated evaluation protocol with applications in map maintenance and infrastructure monitoring.

entry.title: BrainTaskonomy: Learning How to Pretrain and What to Transfer in fMRI Foundation Models

author.name: Junfeng Xia, Wenhao Ye, Junxiang Zhang, Jiayu Zuo, Mo Wang, Quanying Liu

entry.summary: Studies how to organize pretraining and adaptation for fMRI foundation models using measured inter-domain and inter-task relations: a lightweight proxy estimates difficulty and facilitation across ten fMRI domains to build a curriculum, while a directed taskonomy with budgeted integer programming selects what to transfer across fifteen tasks. The approach requires no backbone modification. It brings curriculum learning and transferability theory to neuroimaging foundation models.

entry.title: CompEvo: Competition-Induced Evolution for Multi-Agent in News-Driven Time Series Forecasting

author.name: Yuxuan Zhang, Yangyang Feng, Yong Guan, Daifeng Li, Kexin Zhang, Junlan Chen, Bowen Deng, Jun Liu, Zehua Zeng

entry.summary: CompEvo tackles thought degeneration in multi-agent LLM systems for news-driven time series forecasting, where agents converge to similar evidence-seeking behaviors. It introduces an evolutionary game-theoretic formulation that guarantees equilibrium existence, using competition among agents to drive strategy diversity. Applications include market risk monitoring and resource scheduling.

entry.title: HaWMPO: Hallucination-Aware World Model-based Policy Optimization for Generalist Robot Policy

author.name: Zengjue Chen, Peidong Liu, Jiawei Li, Qi Wang

entry.summary: Proposes hallucination-aware world model rollouts for online policy improvement of generalist VLA policies, explicitly detecting and discounting biased state transitions that long-horizon imagined rollouts produce. Avoids costly and risky real-robot RL while improving long-horizon manipulation success. Tackles a recognized failure mode of world-model-based robot learning.

entry.title: httpi: the internet protocol to reduce compute from misbehaving agents

author.name: joao_abrantes

entry.summary: This LessWrong post proposes httpi, an internet protocol design that applies mechanism-design principles to AI agents, building identity, credit assignment, and deposit/staking requirements into network interactions so misbehaving agents lose compute or resources. It argues AI safety should shift from purely training-time behavioral shaping toward post-deployment incentive mechanisms analogous to fines, jail, and reputation systems for humans.

entry.title: CityPlanner: A Sandbox Agent for Executable Urban Planning

author.name: Wentao Zhang, Jingyuan Wang, Zetong Zhou, Yifan Yang, Wenrui Wang

entry.summary: Introduces CityPlanner, a sandbox-agent framework for urban planning where agents inspect task files, generate plans, run evaluators, and revise based on executable feedback, plus atomic-task reinforcement learning that decomposes long sandbox episodes to make learning tractable.

entry.title: Grounded Evaluation and Repair for NL-to-PDDL Problem Generation

author.name: Joana Rosa, Pedro Santos, Valdemar Oliveira, Rom\~ao Silva, L. Miguel Silveira, Bruno Martins

entry.summary: This work shows that standard metrics for LLM-generated PDDL planning problems (syntactic validity, planner success) overestimate faithfulness to the described task, and builds an end-to-end pipeline combining generation, parsing and validation checks, a domain-conformance checker, an LLM critic, and iterative repair with fine-grained feedback. The grounded evaluation perspective generalizes beyond PDDL to any LLM generation with hidden semantic requirements.

entry.title: OntologyAligner: Ontology-Aligned Retrieval and Hierarchy-Guided Large Language Model Reranking for Biomedical Ontology Normalization

author.name: Jie Song, Zhichuan Xu, Ziyu Lu, Meng Xiao, Cheng Bi, Yuxin Zhang, Xin Zheng, Xiaoran Li, Qiongfang Cao, Hao Yang, Bairong Shen

entry.summary: OntologyAligner is a three-stage framework combining ontology-aligned retrieval, LLM candidate reranking, and hierarchy-guided refinement for mapping free text to standardized biomedical concepts, with a new benchmark PhenoNormBench of 13,390 samples from seven Human Phenotype Ontology datasets. It achieves state-of-the-art HPO normalization at 88.78% Macro Top-1 accuracy. A solid domain contribution relevant to clinical and research data integration.

entry.title: What Should an Agent Forget? Separating What Is Stored from What Is Used

author.name: Yuhang Li, Yuchen Li

entry.summary: RD-Forget is a training-free framework that separates an agent's stored experience from what it uses per query: a retained source archive preserves observations while a query-conditioned memory view controls their influence, with same-slot replacement suppressing superseded values in current-state contexts and intent-aware retrieval preserving historical access. It addresses the key tension that a stale fact can mislead current answers yet be essential for historical queries. Conceptually clean contribution to agent memory design.

entry.title: Fortunate Recall: Ontology-Driven Memory Lifecycle Management for Persistent Coherence in LLMs

author.name: Ansuman Mullick, Eray T\"uz\"un

entry.summary: Fortunate Recall is a composable policy layer that classifies personal facts into a 10+1 behavioral ontology and applies category-specific lifecycle policies — differential temporal decay, slot-key supersession, event-time validity, category-aware retrieval routing — as deterministic functions over LLM-extracted metadata. Its implementation FR-Bank reaches 76.9% on a new 516-question LifecycleBench. Memory lifecycle management is a genuine pain point as agent memory stores grow unboundedly.

entry.title: Trust Me, I'm Your Developer: Self-Issued Authentication in Large Language Models

author.name: Syed Ghazanfar Abbas, Dongyan Xu

entry.summary: The paper probes a neglected LLM security scenario: whether models verify identity claims using tests designed by the model itself. Across staged developer-identity experiments with ChatGPT, Claude, Qwen, Mistral, and Llama, all models initially rejected an unsupported developer claim, but Qwen and Mistral went on to generate challenges and return Verified without real grounds. It highlights self-issued authentication as a novel social-engineering vector.

entry.title: VANTAGE-Bench: Evaluating the Infrastructure AI Gap in Vision-Language Models

author.name: Zaid Pervaiz Bhat, Nimra Nayyar, Arihant Jain, Lap Fung Chan, John Suchanek, Yu Wang, Varun Praveen, Tomasz Kornuta, Vidya Nariyambut Murali

entry.summary: VANTAGE-Bench targets a neglected class of Physical AI: infrastructure monitoring with fixed cameras in logistics, transportation, and smart spaces, measuring the gap between embodied-AI benchmarks and these open-loop operational tasks. It unifies image and video evaluation across semantic, spatial, temporal, and spatio-temporal capabilities with eight task formulations beyond multiple choice, including dense captioning and trajectory tracking. It quantifies a real evaluation blind spot for deployed VLMs.

entry.title: Teacher Geometry Shapes Learnability in Teacher-Student Networks

author.name: Kai J. Sandbrink, Flavio Martinelli, Alexander van Meegen, Wulfram Gerstner, Johanni Brea

entry.summary: Formalizes learnability in teacher-student setups as the convergence success rate to the global minimum as a function of overparameterization, algorithm, initialization, and teacher geometry, showing that randomly generated teacher weights hide large variation in learnability. The authors identify easy and hard teacher distributions based on node dissimilarity. A rigorous contribution to the theory of learning dynamics.

entry.title: Fine-Tuning a KV Cache Concatenation-Aware Model or Recomputing KV Caches? Why Not Both?

author.name: Fumihiko Tachibana, Daisuke Miyashita, Jun Deguchi

entry.summary: This paper tackles time-to-first-token latency in RAG systems where precomputed KV caches are reused for long concatenated contexts. The authors propose combining KV-cache-concatenation-aware fine-tuning with selective recomputation of a subset of cached KV entries. The dual approach aims to preserve response quality that degrades when caches are blindly reused on very long inputs.

entry.title: What Makes Adversarial Examples Transfer Across Deepfake Detectors?

author.name: Rafael M. Mamede, Pedro C. Neto, Ana F. Sequeira

entry.summary: The paper conducts a controlled study of black-box adversarial transferability across 60 deepfake detectors, varying six backbones, two pretraining regimes, and five training-data configurations with AutoAttack and CW-EOT. Matched comparisons disentangle architectural from training factors that drive transfer success, a dimension prior work rarely separated. Findings inform how to build deepfake detectors robust to transfer attacks.

entry.title: A Trust-Network-Based Federated Learning Framework for Multi-Center Aging Clock Prediction

author.name: Chunxu Zhang, Bo Li, Wenliang Wang, Yang Liu, Di Jiang, Yuan Huang, Yo-ichi Nabeshima, Akinori Yamamura, Bo Yang, Qiang Yang

entry.summary: The paper proposes TNFL, a trust-network-based federated learning framework for training biological aging clocks across medical centers that cannot share data due to privacy constraints. It addresses four concrete challenges: small local sample sizes, sparse and directional inter-center trust, retaining discriminative age prediction with interpretability, and model drift under heterogeneous data. This is significant because it combines a practical privacy-preserving ML solution with a biologically meaningful application (protein interaction structure in aging clocks) and involves credible federated learning researchers.

entry.title: XAI-Refine: An Automated Explanation-Knowledge Loop for Brain-Age Prediction

author.name: Yang Qiao, Junjie Wu, Deqiang Qiu, James J. Lah, Liang Zhao

entry.summary: XAI-Refine is an automated loop that consolidates post-hoc explanations across repeated training runs of brain-age prediction models on resting-state functional connectivity, converts reliable explanations into neurobiological questions, and retrieves knowledge to guide model refinement. Unlike typical explainability workflows that stop at diagnosis, it closes the loop between explanation and model improvement. This targets the important gap between predictive accuracy and neurobiologically supported mechanisms.

entry.title: Settling: Equilibrium Inference for Non-Convex Validity Sets

author.name: Lyes Saad Saoud

entry.summary: The paper formalizes conditional mean collapse, where the Bayes-optimal squared-loss predictor for a disconnected or non-convex validity set is itself invalid, and introduces Settling, an equilibrium-based inference operator that refines a mean-seeking proposal toward a locally stable valid configuration. The authors establish exact-gradient descent, local convergence, and robustness conditions for inexact gradients.

entry.title: EEGBind: Detecting Source-Level Interictal Epileptiform Discharges via EEG-Centric Multimodal Binding

author.name: Muchen Li, Anglin Liu, Xuetian Gao, Ruijian Xu, Jintai Chen

entry.summary: EEGBind is an EEG-centric multimodal binding framework for five-class source-level classification of interictal epileptiform discharges, assigning detected activity to clinically meaningful brain-region categories relevant to presurgical evaluation. It handles subtle, partial source evidence in short windows alongside subject variability, class imbalance, and imperfect multimodal context.

entry.title: Beyond Contact Sensors: Deep learning with Pseudo-Labeling for remote Photoplethysmography

author.name: Bhargav Acharya, Barbara Hammer, Hanna Drimalla

entry.summary: The study investigates when pseudo-labels from unsupervised signal-processing methods can replace expensive contact-sensor ground truth for training deep remote photoplethysmography (rPPG) models that estimate heart rate from video. This reduces dependence on labor-intensive synchronized video-sensor datasets for telemedicine applications.

entry.title: Learning to Fly: Stable Vision-Guided UAV Servoing with Compact Target-Centric Cues and Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Saurbh Singh Jamwal, Nived Chebrolu

entry.summary: This work tackles long-horizon quadrotor visual servoing by replacing raw RGB perception with a compact 12D observation built from lightweight target segmentation offsets, relative depth, velocity, and projected-gravity measurements. It compares Direct PPO against matched-budget visual and dynamic curriculum strategies for stable policy optimization. The result is a practical recipe for vision-guided UAV control that avoids the cost and instability of end-to-end visual RL.

entry.title: Mode Coverage in Normalizing Flow Boltzmann Generators via Log-Ratio Variation

author.name: Qi Feng, Rongjie Lai, Di Qi, Xuda Ye

entry.summary: The paper identifies a failure mode of forward-KL training for normalizing-flow Boltzmann generators: flows can miss target modes while inflated importance-weight effective sample sizes mask the problem. It introduces log-ratio variation and a new loss (KLXX) that augments forward KL with target-weighted and mixture-weighted log-ratio terms to improve accuracy and search for candidate modes. The authors derive Fisher-Rao-style theoretical grounding for the objective.

entry.title: TEFM: Token-Efficient Faithful Modeling for Structured Data

author.name: Zhichao Hou, Lingdao Sha, Xueyu Mao, Yang Liu, Peijie Qiu, Rui Song

entry.summary: TEFM is a framework for applying LLMs to structured data in critical domains that jointly tackles token efficiency and faithfulness: it compresses lengthy structured observations into compact Behavioral Code tokens, and uses a dual-fidelity objective optimizing code-level reconstruction and prediction-level fidelity to identify minimal sufficient feature subsets. Experiments across multiple domains show reduced token consumption with minimal information loss and grounded rationalization.

entry.title: SalamandraTA at WMT 2026 Terminology Shared Task: Hard Examples Are Better Teachers

author.name: Xixian Liao, Maite Melero

entry.summary: The paper shows that for terminology-aware translation, fine-tuning data should be filtered to keep only examples where the model's own output contradicts the glossary, since most glossary-annotated pairs teach nothing. At fixed data volume, this selection alone raises term accuracy from 78.7% to 89.9%, and the filtered data is part of the instruction-tuning mixture for the publicly released SalamandraTA-7b-instruct v3.0 model. The simple, controlled finding is a general lesson for instruction-tuning data curation.

entry.title: From Retrieval to Weights: Parametric Individualization of Small Language Models with Individual Text Corpora

author.name: Christoph Wigbels, Ali Abusaleh, Markus T. Jansen, Alexander Mehler, Markus J. Hofmann

entry.summary: This study compares retrieval-augmented generation and DoRA fine-tuning as ways to encode personal episodic and semantic memory into small language models, using web-crawled search histories of 515 participants answering knowledge questions. It shows a per-participant DoRA adapter measurably writes that individual's text corpus into model weights, fitting the participant's held-out text better than others' (effect size dz=1.27). The work is a novel cognitive-science-inspired exploration of parametric memory individualization in SLMs.

entry.title: Who Are They to Each Other? Multi-Agent Reasoning for Speaker Relationship Inference

author.name: Yaohan Guan, Yen-Ju Lu, Yuzhe Wang, Junhyeok Lee, Jesus Villalba, Laureano Moro Velazquez, Thomas Thebaud, Najim Dehak

entry.summary: This paper introduces a training-free multi-agent LLM framework for inferring relationships between speakers in conversations, where agents propose, challenge, and adjudicate relationship judgments over subtle multimodal cues. Two complementary decomposition designs instantiate the framework, avoiding costly supervised training for this underexplored socially-aware speech task. It extends structured LLM reasoning into speech-based social understanding.

entry.title: Longitudinal tracking of multiple sclerosis lesions in the spinal cord: A validation study

author.name: Pierre-Louis Benveniste, Julian McGinnis, Shannon Kolind, Larry D. Lynd, Sarah A. Morrow, Jiwon Oh, Alexandre Prat, Alice Schabas, Penelope Smyth, Roger Tam, Anthony Traboulsee, Mark M\"uhlau, Herve Lombaert, Julien Cohen-Adad

entry.summary: This validation study compares five strategies for instance-level tracking of spinal cord MS lesions across longitudinal MRI visits, addressing limitations of semantic segmentation that cannot capture lesion appearance, disappearance, splitting, or merging. It uses a multi-site clinical cohort and expert authorship.

entry.title: StreetDiff: Multi-view Street Scenes Generation via Cross-view Consistent Multi-view Stable Diffusion with Structure Prompts

author.name: Qi Zhang, Yanyifan Wang, Weiyuan Zhang, Hui Huang

entry.summary: StreetDiff is a multi-view diffusion framework for urban street scene generation that enforces cross-view alignment during denoising via a Panorama-Perspective Synergy design, decoupling global layout reasoning from local view synthesis to prevent object duplication and layout inconsistency under camera rotation.

entry.title: Putting Captions to the Test: Evaluating Video Caption Quality through Multiple-Choice Question Answering

author.name: Zizhen Wang, Bo Feng, Zhengfeng Lai, Shiyu Li, Yang Lu, Meng Cao, Ping Huang, Xiaoming Simon Wang

entry.summary: Proposes CapQuiz, a reference-free video caption evaluation benchmark that reframes caption quality as information fidelity, assessed via multiple-choice question answering rather than lexical matching to references. This avoids the one-to-many mismatch problem of traditional metrics and enables fine-grained quality analysis.

entry.title: Decoupled Self-Forcing Distillation for Streaming Talking Head Generation

author.name: Yanru An, Ruiyan Wang, Wenwu Wei, Rui Bu, Qi Wang, Hongwei Hu, Zhengxue Cheng, Rong Xie, Li Song, Wenjun Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes fusing audio and motion conditions in a low-dimensional identity-disentangled motion space rather than on every video pixel, enabling streaming talking-head generation with better fidelity-efficiency tradeoffs. The self-forcing distillation approach targets per-frame generation as audio arrives.

entry.title: RoboDrop: Curating VLA Post-Training Data via Local Gradient Compatibility

author.name: Runze Xu, Yuanfan Xu, Cuijie Xu, Shuang Dai, Yining Li, Yu Wang, Jincheng Yu

entry.summary: Introduces a data-curation framework that filters heterogeneous robot dataset errors (execution mistakes, sensor drift, timestamp misalignment) using local gradient compatibility signals, targeting the quality-sensitivity of VLA post-training. This generalizes beyond corruption-type-specific cleaning methods and reduces reliance on manual inspection. A useful data-quality tool for the growing robot post-training ecosystem.

entry.title: DiSCo: A Distribution-First Steering and Cultural Prior Evaluation Framework for Measuring Cultural Preference Bias in LLMs

author.name: Bhuvan Arora, Devesh Saraogi, Sravya Varada, Dhruv Kumar

entry.summary: DiSCo is a distribution-first, forced-choice evaluation framework that measures the default cultural priors of LLMs in culturally grounded everyday situations, separate from context-driven adaptation, using a four-level context gradient (C0-C3) to test steerability. It comes with DiSCo-Bench (over 3000 items per the abstract) and addresses the flaw that existing cultural benchmarks assume a single correct answer when multiple culturally valid responses exist. This matters for equitable global deployment of LLM assistants, where systematic favoring of some cultures affects localization and trust.

entry.title: Tensor Network Moral Graph Recovery of Discrete Probability Distributions

author.name: \'A. Troyano Olivas, Chi-Hang Fred Fung, Hans H. Brunner, Momtchil Peev, Vicente Martin

entry.summary: This paper recovers the moral graph of a causal DAG from discrete probability distributions using fully connected tensor networks with nuclear-norm-regularized low-rank bond corrections that drive unnecessary bonds to zero. Under faithfulness, positivity, and a no-implicit-rerouting condition, the authors prove that every optimal zero-error FCTN has effective graph exactly equal to the moral graph. It is a novel bridge between tensor-network representation learning and causal structure discovery.

entry.title: Decision-Focused Active Learning for Scale-Aware Critical-Materials Recovery

author.name: Niranjan Srinivas, Debajyoti Ray, Elias Nakouzi

entry.summary: Analyzes records from PNNL's CICERO autonomous precipitation workflow and shows decision-focused active learning reaches the best recorded neodymium enrichment with fewer experiments than nonadaptive space-filling designs. The work connects lab-scale results to scale-up decisions for critical-materials recovery.

entry.title: RESCUE-BENCH: Towards Relation-Aware Multi-Party Emotional Support Conversation Systems

author.name: Haichuan Hu, Yang Xiao, Mingni Tang, Jiawen Duan, Quanjun Zhang, Congqing He, Hao Zhang, Jiashuo Wang, Johan F. Hoorn, Wenjie Li

entry.summary: Introduces relation-aware emotional support conversation as a new task and RESCUE, a benchmark built from real couple and family interviews with 191 samples, 7,079 annotated turns, and over 1,000 minutes of video, evaluating whether LLMs can use evolving interpersonal dynamics for support.

entry.title: Scored vs. Generated Readouts in Behavioral Language Models: An Empirical Study of Elicitation Format

author.name: Touchapon Kraisingkorn, Krittin Pachtrachai, Wachiravit Modecrua

entry.summary: Holding checkpoints and prompts fixed, the study compares scoring answer-token probabilities versus generating predictions after a written rationale for customer-behavior prediction, finding scored readouts rank outcomes better in 12 of 13 model-domain cells by 1.5 to 14.5 AUC points with statistical significance. The result is a practical guidance point: explanation-then-prediction formats can hurt ranking accuracy. Useful for anyone deploying fine-tuned behavioral predictors.

entry.title: From Symbolic Perception to Logical Deduction: A Framework for Guiding Language Models in Geometric Reasoning

author.name: Weichen Dai, Rafael Medeiros Cabral, Ziyi Shou, Yan Cao, Xin Shen, Dongcai Lu, Yi Zhou

entry.summary: The framework shows that a pure LLM equipped with a Geometric Vision Parser translating diagrams into symbolic form and a Symbolic Solver performing formal deductions can rival state-of-the-art multimodal models on complex plane geometry, including a new benchmark from 2025 Chinese Zhongkao problems. It promotes interpretable, hallucination-resistant reasoning via modular neuro-symbolic decomposition. A solid demonstration that architecture, not raw multimodality, can win on structured visual reasoning.

entry.title: Cyber-Financial Contagion: Modeling the Propagation of an AI Vendor Compromise Through the Banking System

author.name: Alex Leytes

entry.summary: The paper builds a four-layer heterogeneous network coupling AI vendors, financial institutions, interbank exposures, and customer accounts, with CFC-Prop, a stochastic epidemic-and-clearing model, to study how a compromise in one shared AI vendor propagates into losses resembling a classical banking crisis, tested on a synthetic system of 60 vendors and 220 banks. It opens an underexplored systemic-risk dimension of AI concentration. Relevant to both financial regulation and AI supply-chain security.

entry.title: AgenticGen: Reward-Guided Agentic Video Generation for Advertising

author.name: Xingyuan Bu, Chengru Song, Hao Zhou, Tao Zhou, Dong Li, Wei Li, Shilong Li, Hao Shi, Yongxin Guo, Donghao Zhou, Qiangpeng Yang, Shilei Wen

entry.summary: AgenticGen frames advertising video generation as product-conditioned reasoning optimized against online business metrics, decomposing it into trainable strategy-selection and draft-generation stages. A performance-based reward learned from online feedback supervises the loop, building on existing video foundation models. It demonstrates closing the generation-to-business-outcome feedback loop in an industrial setting.

entry.title: DiffLUT-Net: Differentiable Training of FPGA LUT Networks with Learnable Connectivity

author.name: Jiaqi Ye, Xinrui Gong, Jingcun Wang, Olga Kondrateva, Bing Li, Grace Li Zhang
