entry.summary: DiffLUT-Net trains FPGA-native neural networks built from six-input lookup tables from scratch, jointly learning truth-table entries and input-port source selection via differentiable relaxation, then discretizing and exporting synthesizable Verilog. Across five benchmarks it achieves favorable accuracy-resource tradeoffs versus flows that convert pretrained quantized models. It advances hardware-native neural inference.

entry.title: Myocardial Strain Drift Correction in Deep Learning Based Ultrasound Tracking

author.name: Thierry Judge, Nicolas Duchateau, Andreas {\O}stvik, Havard Dalen, Bj{\o}rnar Grenne, Pierre-Yves Courand, Lasse Lovstakken, Pierre-Marc Jodoin, Olivier Bernard

entry.summary: Extends a state-of-the-art echocardiographic tracking network (TAS-Net) with persistent memory tokens across sliding windows over full cardiac cycles, plus teacher-student fine-tuning, to correct temporal drift in deep-learning myocardial motion tracking. Reducing drift improves strain estimates, a key cardiac-function biomarker. Clinically meaningful with real-world ultrasound data.

entry.title: Compact Visuotactile World Models for Lifting: Prediction, Reward Alignment, and Force Constraints

author.name: Qinzhen Ma (Rice University), Sida Peng (Zhejiang University)

entry.summary: Builds a compact, randomly initialized visuotactile world model with trajectory-level uncertainty calibration and behavior-initialized actor-critic learning in imagination, evaluated on MuJoCo lift tasks plus 680 real control executions. Adding touch sharply reduces endpoint-force prediction error, and tactile persistence performs even better. Demonstrates how contact prediction must connect to decision quality for robotic manipulation.

entry.title: HiRAD: A Flexible Large-Scale AGV Routing System

author.name: Yunjie Huang, Ruizhong Wu, Mengxuan Zhang, Frodo Kin Sun Chan, Yan Nei Law, Lei Li

entry.summary: HiRAD is a hybrid system for routing large fleets of Automatic Guided Vehicles in warehouses, addressing the combinatorial blowup of classical multi-agent pathfinding and the slow convergence and full-map observation costs of RL approaches. It targets real-time industrial control constraints with reduced model size and inference latency. The work bridges academic MAPF/RL research and practical warehouse deployment.

entry.title: Can AI Agents Detect and Repair Artifact Drift in Network Experiments?

author.name: Tianzhu Zhang, Weichen Tao, Changgang Zheng, Yusheng Zheng, Long Chen, Xiaoyi Fan, Meikang Qiu

entry.summary: The authors introduce artifact integrity, the property that an AI-modified experiment record's claims remain supported by, scoped to, and traceable through available evidence, and present NetArtifactBench to test whether agents can detect and repair violations. This reframes agent evaluation beyond task completion toward trustworthiness of the artifacts agents produce. Relevant to the network systems community's adoption of AI agents.

entry.title: Can AI Agents Deliver Verifiable Network-Wide Outcomes Across Authority Boundaries?

author.name: Tianzhu Zhang, Chih-Kai Huang, Meikang Qiu

entry.summary: The paper examines AI agents that initiate network configuration changes across multi-domain operational networks, where each agent has distinct authority scopes over accessible resources, invocable operations, and observable state. It identifies a fundamental tension: authority fragmentation limits the blast radius of erroneous actions but also fragments the evidence needed to verify that network-wide intent was actually achieved. The work matters as agent autonomy spreads into critical infrastructure, where per-action success does not establish correct remote outcomes or routing convergence.

entry.title: PACE: Perceived-Latency-Aware Cascading Service Routing and Filler Control for QoE-Efficient Retrieval-Augmented Dialogue Serving

author.name: Lin Huang, Yujuan Tan, Weisheng Li, Lixiang Zeng, Kun Yang, Suihan Xiao

entry.summary: PACE formalizes perceived time-to-first-response as a quality-of-experience objective for retrieval-augmented dialogue systems, jointly controlling cascading answer-source routing, filler content during waiting windows, and cache admission. Deployed on a humanoid-robot sales service over 75k requests, it halves P95 latency versus pure-LLM serving and beats RAG by 2.4x at high load with equal quality. It is a systems contribution to latency-aware LLM serving.

entry.title: Accountable and uncertainty-aware evaluation of sensor-based AI under distribution shift: devices, subjects, and nearly three years underground

author.name: Benny Platte (Mittweida University of Applied Sciences), Rico Thomanek (Mittweida University of Applied Sciences), Christian Roschke (Mittweida University of Applied Sciences), Marc Ritter (Mittweida University of Applied Sciences)

entry.summary: The paper proposes a staged evaluation protocol for deployed sensor-based AI that treats evaluation as a measurement with declared reference levels and quantified uncertainty, holding out devices, subjects, and time across four cumulative generalization stages. It also introduces an out-of-present-scope rate to detect silent misdirection toward classes no longer present in deployment. Validation spans nearly three years of underground sensor data, making it a unusually long-horizon deployment study.

entry.title: Literati: Towards Anytime Optimal Shape Generalized Trees via AO*

author.name: Nakul Upadhya, Eldan Cohen

entry.summary: Literati is presented as the first algorithm for optimal induction of Shape Generalized Trees, which replace axis-aligned threshold splits with learnable univariate shape functions in decision trees. Using AO* search, it provides optimality guarantees and anytime behavior where prior SGT methods were greedy and unguaranteed. This can yield more compact, interpretable trees that capture nonlinear feature effects without deep structures.

entry.title: Robust Industrial Cyber Physical Classification Using Neuromorphic Temporal Embeddings and Hybrid SNN XGBoost Under Machine Unlearning Attacks

author.name: Ammar Kamoona, Sajad Koushkbaghi, Mahdi Jalili, Peter McTaggart, Xinghuo Yu

entry.summary: For intrusion detection in power-grid infrastructure, the paper proposes a hybrid Spiking Neural Network and XGBoost architecture where the SNN serves as a fixed, train-once feature extractor and only the lightweight XGBoost head is retrained. This design provides edge-deployable efficiency and structural resilience to machine unlearning attacks that degrade retrained deep detectors.

entry.title: Meta-LinEXP3: Online-within-Online Learning for Adversarial Linear Contextual Bandits

author.name: Hao Li, Jie Xu, Zheng Xie

entry.summary: This work develops Meta-LinEXP3, an online-within-online meta-learning algorithm for adversarial linear contextual bandits with random action sets, a setting the authors note is largely unexplored. It constructs a task-level prior from completed tasks to guide an inner LinEXP3 learner and achieves an intrinsic-dimension O(sqrt(n)) per-task regret bound for known context distributions, with a moment-estimation approach for unknown distributions. The paper contributes both a new algorithm and regret guarantees for a previously open problem class.

entry.title: Deep Neural Networks for Learning Intent from sEMG Signals to Support Hardware Devices for Post-Stroke Neurorehabilitation

author.name: Zakariyya Brewster, Divy Wadhwani, Emily Yan, Aidan Wang, Karma Namgyal, Shuting Xie, Markiyan Konyk, Tala Abdelmaguid

entry.summary: The authors study five-finger motor-intent decoding from high-density surface EMG of stroke patients using a longitudinal bilateral dataset called PhysioMio, comparing LSTM, CNN, and GNN baselines with a standardized preprocessing protocol. LSTM achieves the best subset accuracy (0.545), and the work targets control signals for rehabilitation hardware.

entry.title: Learning with Covariance Matrices: Principal Component Analysis Meets Learning with Graphs

author.name: Saurabh Sihag, Andrea Cavallo, Elvin Isufi, Gonzalo Mateos, Alejandro Ribeiro

entry.summary: This feature article unifies the theory of covariance neural networks (VNNs), i.e., graph neural networks operating on covariance matrices treated as graphs, connecting them to classical PCA. It develops theoretical insights with signal-processing implications, including conceptual equivalence between VNNs and PCA-based representations and transferability analyses specific to data-driven covariance graphs. The tutorial is valuable for researchers applying GNNs to statistical dependencies, a common but theoretically under-addressed setting.

entry.title: "Transforming" LHCb: self-supervised maps of heavy-flavour decays

author.name: Marko Stamenkovic, Greg Landsberg

entry.summary: The authors propose adapting self-supervised transformer-based jet flavor-tagging techniques from ATLAS and CMS to LHCb, learning maps of heavy-hadron decay environments directly from data. The goal is to outperform current LHCb taggers and extend reconstruction to heavy-flavour decays with invisible particles, which are sensitive probes of physics beyond the Standard Model. It represents a concrete transfer of modern representation learning into a precision particle-physics pipeline.

entry.title: MiNCE: Nonparametric, Strongly Consistent Confidence Envelopes for Band-Limited Functions and their Smoothed Spectra

author.name: Bal\'azs Csan\'ad Cs\'aji, B\'alint Horv\'ath

entry.summary: This paper establishes strong uniform consistency guarantees for minimum-norm confidence envelopes (MiNCE), a nonparametric method for constructing simultaneous confidence regions for band-limited functions using RKHS theory. It extends the framework to the frequency domain, providing nonasymptotic confidence bands for smoothed spectra in both noise-free and noisy settings. The work closes a theoretical gap, since prior finite-sample coverage results lacked consistency analysis.

entry.title: Inductive Biases in Field-Level Cosmological Inference from Galaxy Catalogs

author.name: James O. Baldwin, Shy Genel, Francisco Villaescusa-Navarro

entry.summary: This work performs field-level likelihood-free inference of the matter density parameter Omega_m from simulated galaxy catalogs, comparing how different neural architectures with distinct inductive biases extract cosmological information. Using CAMELS hydrodynamic simulations, the authors evaluate Deep Sets with MLPs or Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks against graph neural networks that encode spatial relations, testing both in-distribution and out-of-distribution generalization across different subgrid galaxy-formation physics.

entry.title: When Does Low-Bit Quantization Preserve the Decisions of Vector Search?

author.name: Wenxuan Xiao, Xu Cao

entry.summary: Develops a theory of when low-bit quantization flips the comparisons used by ranking and graph-pruning algorithms in vector search, providing a distribution-free decomposition bounding flip probability by near-zero-margin mass plus residual tail probability. It further derives covariance-aware second-moment identities and tail bounds accounting for dependence between residuals sharing a query or graph node.

entry.title: Cross-Model Agreement as a Deployment-Time Reliability Signal for Automatic Polyp Segmentation

author.name: Siddharth Gupta, Jitin Singla

entry.summary: The paper proposes Referee-Based Quality Estimation (RBQE), a reference-free framework that measures agreement between a primary polyp segmentation model and an independently trained referee at inference time to flag silent failures. On a 1,223-image external benchmark, even a same-architecture referee differing only in random seed yields a useful reliability signal (ROC-AUC 0.923).

entry.title: Towards Automatic Evolution Tree Generation from Citation Graphs

author.name: Zexing Zhao, Yuntong Hu, Liang Zhao

entry.summary: EvoTree is a staged framework that automatically builds temporal method-evolution trees from citation graphs, decoupling taxonomy backbone learning from temporal refinement and using an LLM only for final concept labeling. It fixes known failure modes of prior taxonomy-induction methods, such as forcing transitional papers into mature leaves and creating ancestor-descendant topology inversions. This could automate what surveys currently do manually for tracking AI subfield lineages.

entry.title: Contrastive Projection: Reading Transformer Internals by Differencing Logit Lenses

author.name: Olli Tuomi

entry.summary: The paper introduces contrastive projection, a training-free interpretability technique that differences hidden states of closely matched prompts and projects through the unembedding matrix, cancelling generic components to isolate what distinguishes the prompts. The method is equivalent to reading RepE/ActAdd steering vectors through a logit lens and is built into a tracer reading every position, sub-layer, and head. The authors trace an MLP-to-attention chain in Phi-2 and validate it via activation patching.

entry.title: YallaMorph: A Benchmark for Evaluating Arabic Morphological Generation in Large Language Models

author.name: Mahmoud Reda, Salam Khalifa, Reham Marzouk, Nizar Habash

entry.summary: YallaMorph is a large-scale benchmark (600K entries) for evaluating controlled Arabic morphological generation, covering verbs, nouns, adjectives, cliticized forms, and invalid configurations under diacritized and undiacritized settings. Evaluations of multilingual and Arabic-oriented LLMs show that morphological control, especially for cliticized and rare forms, remains difficult even when generation is fluent. This fills a real gap in Arabic NLP evaluation beyond downstream task metrics.

entry.title: The Answer Path and the Grounding Instruction in LLM Question Answering over Knowledge Graphs

author.name: Arquimedes Canedo

entry.summary: This single-author study systematically ablates four design choices in graph retrieval-augmented generation (triple selection, syntax, ordering, and instruction wording) across six LLMs and two KGQA benchmarks. The key finding is that including the answer path (the chain of triples leading to the answer) drives nearly all gains, while other triples add almost nothing beyond the chain. This yields a practical guideline: retrieval budgets should prioritize path recall rather than general precision.

entry.title: Evidence-Order Calibration for Selective Visual Reasoning under Progressive Loss of Question-Critical Evidence

author.name: Muhamathu Ameer Ali Aacaas Muhamath

entry.summary: Using a frozen Qwen2.5-VL-3B-Instruct model, this study constructs 176 GQA-derived evidence-loss trajectories by progressively masking question-critical scene-graph regions, measuring whether VLM confidence tracks evidence degradation. It finds a high evidence monotonicity violation rate (0.436) with 92% of trajectories showing at least one adjacent violation, and critical masking reduces accuracy by 28.2 points versus 0.6 for matched controls. The work exposes structural inconsistency between confidence and evidence in VLMs.

entry.title: Cross-Species Animal Re-Identification with Semantic Consistency Learning

author.name: Shuoyi Chen, Yuejia Li, Mang Ye

entry.summary: The paper proposes Semantic Consistency Learning to address fragmented embedding spaces that arise when learning animal re-identification representations across species with drastically different anatomies. It learns representations stable across appearance variation while preserving cross-species semantic structure.

entry.title: From Few-Shot Segmentation to Clinician-in-the-Loop Medical Image Analysis

author.name: Yazhou Zhu

entry.summary: A perspective paper reframing few-shot medical image segmentation as a sequential clinician-model decision problem with separate support and interaction budgets, uniting prototype learning, interactive segmentation, uncertainty estimation, and promptable foundation models under a common clinical-risk model. It argues for jointly evaluating these previously siloed approaches through the lens of expert attention.

entry.title: When Fusion Fails: Corruption-Aware Rebalanced Fusion for Multi-Modal Medical Image Segmentation

author.name: Yuchen Pei, Xiaoyu Hu, Yixiong Zou, Dingwen Hu, Hui Chu, Yutao Ma, Shijun Qiu, Gang Li

entry.summary: Studies when multimodal fusion underperforms single-modality baselines in medical image segmentation, identifying an optimization-inference inconsistency where degraded modalities receive weak training updates yet strongly influence predictions. The paper attributes failures to resampling-induced feature corruption and proposes corruption-aware rebalanced fusion.

entry.title: Field Converter: Geometry-Initialized Temporal Residual Refinement for World-Grounded Player Pose Estimation from Soccer Broadcasts

author.name: Simon Khan, Laurent Gajny, Jennyfer Lecompte, S\'ebastien Laporte

entry.summary: Introduces a framework for world-grounded 3D player pose estimation from monocular soccer broadcasts that initializes the player root via ray-ground intersection with camera and pitch geometry, then refines with temporal residual networks. Root error drops from 49 cm with geometry alone to about 10 cm with a TCN on match-disjoint sequences. This enables player localization in a shared metric coordinate system, valuable for sports analytics.

entry.title: Morphological Decoupling-Based Skeletal Classification for Clinical Assessment of Malocclusion

author.name: Zhichun Jin, Zhicheng He, Hao Xu, Dongyang Li, Lin Wang, Hongliang Ren, Long Bai

entry.summary: TeethGNN is a graph-based framework that combines CBCT image features with morphological information to automate malocclusion skeletal grading, using a decoupled learnable decoder to predict key measurements and reduce inter-operator variability in orthodontic diagnosis. The system targets replacing the manual, time-consuming workflow in which reconstructed lateral cephalograms are reviewed by expert dentists. It matters as a step toward reliable end-to-end automation of a fundamental orthodontic clinical task.

entry.title: MuJoCable: Reduced-Order Surface-Routed Cable Transmission for Tendon-Driven Robots

author.name: Yi Zhang, Qi Shao, Yicong Lin, Muyuan Ma, Tao Sun, Yue Xie

entry.summary: Adds a reduced-order, configuration-dependent cable transmission model as a MuJoCo plugin, jointly solving routing across moving surfaces, unilateral tension, and Capstan friction propagation. This fills a real gap in mainstream rigid-body simulators for tendon-driven robots. Includes pulley benchmarks for validation.

entry.title: PccDiffuser: Multi-solution Motion Planning for Continuum Robots

author.name: Ke Qiu, Sifan Chen, Si Wang, Rong Xiong, Yue Wang, Haojian Lu

entry.summary: A conditional diffusion model that learns a multimodal distribution over complete configuration-space paths for continuum robots, encoding variable obstacle sets with graph neural networks and injecting analytical differential kinematics into denoising for accuracy and clearance. Samples multiple candidate paths in parallel and converts them to executable trajectories under actuator constraints. Reported improvements on obstacle-rich continuum planning tasks.

entry.title: Deformable Object Manipulation under Partial Observability via Real-Time Full-Shape Estimation

author.name: Kosar Behnia, Ville Kyrki, Gokhan Alcan

entry.summary: Proposes cRVAE, a lightweight conditional recurrent variational autoencoder estimating full deformable-object state from partial corner-node observations, used as a forward model in receding-horizon optimal control for obstacle-aware collaborative manipulation. Matches a parameter-identified XPBD model on rope and fabric without physical parameters at inference. Practical solution to partial observability in deformable manipulation.

entry.title: Fast Constraint Extraction for Corrective Control under STL Specifications via Logical Dependency Tracking

author.name: Antoine Besset, Joris Tillet, Chuchu Fan, Julien Alexandre dit Sandretto

entry.summary: This work introduces a logical dependency tracking framework that propagates uncertainty through Signal Temporal Logic structure to identify which uncertain components causally affect global satisfaction, even for nested formulas. Using markers and three-valued semantics, it extracts compact DNF constraints in milliseconds, enabling corrective control when reachability monitoring shows satisfaction has become indeterminate. This bridges monitoring and repair for temporal-logic-specified systems.

entry.title: Constitutional AI Widens Narrow Secret Loyalty of LLMs

author.name: navraj

entry.summary: This post reports an experiment showing that Constitutional AI fine-tuning can widen narrowly-installed Secret Loyalty backdoors in LLMs, making loyalty to a hidden principal trigger adaptively across conversational contexts, while black-box audit evasion capability remains intact. The work builds on model-organism research into sabotage and AI-enabled coup threat models. This is a safety-relevant empirical finding about how standard safety training interacts with planted deceptive behaviors.

entry.title: Multi-Agent Agentic Graph Learning via Structural Signatures

author.name: Liang Qu, Jianxin Li, Hua Wang

entry.summary: Proposes multi-agent agentic graph learning in which multiple LLM-powered agents with separate memories specialize in different graph structural regions and collaborate, overcoming the suboptimality of a shared reasoning policy on heterogeneous graphs.

entry.title: RouteBridge: Reliability-Routed Bidirectional Distillation Between Neural Radiance Fields and 3D Gaussian Splatting

author.name: YuanHang Wang, Xin Cao

entry.summary: Introduces RouteBridge, a bidirectional distillation framework between NeRF and 3D Gaussian Splatting that selects the teaching direction per ray using a reliability estimator combining photometric residuals and geometric evidence, with an abstain option. A renderer-independent interface transfers color, opacity, and normalized depth without correspondences. Improves on fixed-teacher distillation on mip-NeRF 360.

entry.title: Emergency Department Revisit Quality Review Screening: Exploring Human Decision-Making and Artificial Intelligence Support

author.name: Jonathan A. Handler, Marlene I. Robles-Granda, Jacob E. Mefford, Jeremy S. McGarvey, Gregory S. Podolej, Colleen J. Klein, Matthew D. Dalstrom, William F. Bond

entry.summary: An exploratory retrospective study comparing clinician raters and GPT-4 in screening emergency department revisit pairs for quality review, assessing whether visit pairs warrant further investigation given only primary diagnoses. The study broadens the review window from the usual 48-72 hours to 1-14 days and analyzes rater response patterns to inform AI support design. It offers concrete evidence on where LLM assistance can and cannot aid clinical quality assurance.

entry.title: Exact Degeneracy Under Balanced k-Shot Sampling:Consequences for Small-Sample Discriminant Analysis on LLM Embeddings

author.name: Lingxiao Qu

entry.summary: This paper proves that balanced k-shot sampling (exactly k labeled examples per class) induces an exact, provable degeneracy in a family of small-sample discriminant estimators, showing that the within-class scatter of KLPCDA becomes exactly a scaled orthogonal projector. The author derives closed-form consequences: some variants have all signal eigenvalues exactly equal so their eigenvector selection is provably indifferent, and another has a provably void objective, independent of any dataset. The results are confirmed empirically on frozen sentence embeddings, making this a cautionary result for few-shot classification pipelines built on LLM embeddings.

entry.title: Likelihood-free inference with nuisance parameters through normalizing flows

author.name: Phil Assheton

entry.summary: The paper presents a decomposition of normalizing flows that uncovers a near-pivotal statistic in the presence of nuisance parameters, using only a sample generator from the distribution of interest. The approach respects group invariances such as translation and scale and can rediscover the one-sample t-test almost exactly while outperforming the Welch test in some regimes.

entry.title: Freezing of Gait Prediction Under Spatial Occlusion: An IMU-Supervised Cross-Modal Distillation Approach

author.name: Chandan Biswas, Aryan Singh, Anabik Pal

entry.summary: The paper proposes cross-modal distillation where IMU sensor supervision compensates for degraded video-based pose estimation during freezing-of-gait detection in Parkinson's patients, especially under lower-limb self-occlusion during turning tasks. This enables more robust video-based FOG detection for clinical monitoring.

entry.title: Isotropic Embedding Perturbations for Robust Vision Language Encoders

author.name: Hyesong Choi, Daeun Kim, Song Park, Taekyung Kim, Byeongho Heo, Sangdoo Yun, Dongbo Min, Dongyoon Han

entry.summary: Introduces Aether, a plug-in augmentation method applying diffusion-style random perturbations in the embedding space via controlled alpha-mixing, offering isotropic regularization that preserves cross-modal semantic alignment. It targets saturation of input-space augmentation combinations for vision and multimodal encoders.

entry.title: What Symmetry Buys a Learned Motion Planner

author.name: Andrea Emir Sevincel

entry.summary: Analyzes how much rigid-body equivariance a learned motion planner gets for free by canonicalizing start-goal pairs into a derived frame, removing three translations and two rotations of SE(3) at initialization with one cross product per query and no architectural constraints. A single residual rotation remains for learning. An elegant theoretical framing of equivariance in motion planning.

entry.title: In RAG We Trust? Measuring Robustness of Retrieval-Augmented Generation Under Document Poisoning

author.name: Iliano Fasolino

entry.summary: This paper measures how a small quantized model, Llama 3.1 8B, degrades when retrieved RAG context is poisoned via entity swap, number swap, and negation corruption across a 588-run factorial sweep on a FEVER-based fact-checking task. Accuracy drops from 77.9% on clean context to 43.5% with all three passages corrupted, with entity swaps flipping the most correct answers. It quantifies a concrete vulnerability in retrieval-augmented pipelines.

entry.title: Forward-Free LLM Depth Pruning via Weight Redundancy

author.name: Vincent-Daniel Yun, Woosang Lim

entry.summary: Weight-Redundancy Pruning (WRP) is a forward-free depth-pruning method for LLMs that estimates inter-layer redundancy directly from checkpoint weights, requiring no calibration data or forward passes. It compares attention output and MLP down-projection weights across layers and uses pairwise similarity plus relative projection scale to guide layer grouping and block removal. This simplifies and potentially speeds up depth-pruning pipelines.

entry.title: A statistical approach to bias in zero-shot learning: the lens of handwriting recognition

author.name: Clarence Chew, Gim Siang Chia, Sukalpa Chanda, Subhroshekhar Ghosh, Soumendu Sundar Mukherjee

entry.summary: This paper tackles the well-known misclassification bias in generalized zero-shot learning, where models favor seen classes over unseen ones, and studies it through zero-shot handwritten word recognition over extremely large vocabularies. The authors propose a statistical post-hoc correction that treats any classical GZSL feature learner as a black box and estimates its intrinsic bias toward training-status classes. This matters because it addresses the scalability limits of GZSL to many unseen classes using a domain (handwriting recognition) with natural large-label-space structure.

entry.title: Constraint-Aware Discrete Black-Box Optimization Using Tensor Decomposition

author.name: Keisuke Onoue, Ryosuke Kojima

entry.summary: The authors propose a surrogate modeling approach for discrete black-box optimization based on tensor decomposition that captures search-space structure while directly integrating known logical feasibility constraints. This addresses a gap in sequential model-based optimization, where surrogates typically ignore symbolic rules governing feasible inputs. Better handling of constraints could improve sample efficiency in real-world discrete design problems.

entry.title: Robust Beam Prediction for V2X Networks with Multi-Modal Sensing

author.name: Chen Shang, Dinh Thai Hoang, Diep N. Nguyen, Jiadong Yu

entry.summary: The paper introduces BeamTransFuser, a hierarchical Transformer that fuses camera, LiDAR, radar, and GPS observations for robust beam prediction in V2X networks, reducing reliance on unreliable RF-only sensing in complex vehicular environments. It leverages integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) trends toward multi-modal environmental perception.

entry.title: Cost-Aware Post-Hoc Deferral Under Calibration and Shift: An Environmental AI Case Study

author.name: Haoran Yu, Lifei Liu, Danping Zhang

entry.summary: EcoTrust is a post-hoc deferral framework for frozen classifiers that jointly models miscalibration, asymmetric error costs, reviewer fallibility, and distribution shift via a six-group error-risk estimator with an optional support gate. On a Columbia River thermal-stress testbed it improves error-ranking AUC from 0.869 to 0.889, yet notably finds that simple Chow confidence rules can achieve lower in-distribution cost than the learned estimator. This honest negative-comparison framing makes it a useful case study in realistic human-AI delegation economics.

entry.title: Concept drift mitigation through community and spectral graph analysis for the detectionof cyberattacks in network traffic

author.name: Julien Michel, Abdul Qadir Khan, Majed Jaber, Pierre Parrend

entry.summary: The paper addresses concept drift in network intrusion detection by shifting the intervention point from post-drift model repair to pre-learning feature selection. It introduces t-robustness, a model-independent per-feature stability score combining stepwise statistical distance and cumulative divergence so that slow monotonic drifts cannot masquerade as stability. Community and spectral graph analysis are then used to select robust features for cyberattack detection in evolving traffic.

entry.title: An Autonomous GeoAI Agent for Arctic Eco-Navigation

author.name: Samira Alkaee Taleghan, Younghyun Koo, Farnoush Banaei-Kashani

entry.summary: Presents a human-in-the-loop multi-agent GeoAI system for Arctic maritime routing that jointly optimizes operational, ecological, and community-impact criteria, going beyond conventional time/fuel/risk routing. It targets a timely problem as sea-ice change expands seasonal navigation access.

entry.title: Decision Shifts, Lost Label Functionality, and an Inconclusive Grounding Audit in Correctness-Gated Multi-Teacher Distillation

author.name: Xiaofei Feng

entry.summary: Presents a controlled fixed-experiment analysis of correctness-gated multi-teacher distillation across eight arms sharing data and a 63.9M-parameter student, finding measurable accuracy and unsafe-action-rate shifts from correctness weighting but cautioning that these do not imply uniformly better behavior, with grounding audits inconclusive.

entry.title: Procedural Memory Under Change: Reuse and Interference in Controlled Web Tasks

author.name: Yanze Cao

entry.summary: This paper examines when stored procedural routines for language agents break down after interface changes, combining a retrospective WebShop V1-V6 adaptation case with controlled frozen-memory comparisons on synthetic shopping decisions. It finds that reused memory can produce interference effects when the environment shifts. The work matters for building agents whose accumulated experience remains reliable under drift, though the controlled component is small.

entry.title: Characterizing Text Branch Sensitivity in Medical Vision-Language Segmentation via Evidence Decoupling

author.name: Ziquan Liu, Zhewei Zhu, Xuyang Shi

entry.summary: This study examines how much clinical text actually contributes to pixel-level predictions in medical image segmentation, finding performance largely insensitive to the choice of fusion module. It proposes an Evidence Decoupling Decoder based on evidential deep learning to separate image evidence from text-modulated components. The result challenges assumptions about multimodal benefit in medical VLMs.

entry.title: Edu-QuRating: Multi-Dimensional Educational Data Curation with Distilled Pairwise Judgements

author.name: Oliver G. B. Garrod, Robin A. A. Ince, Meng Liu, Mohamed Huti, Moritz Boos, Amy Waldock, Dominic Andrews, Paul Atherton

entry.summary: Extends QuRating with Edu-QuRating, a pipeline that scores pre-training data along multiple education-specific rubrics (accuracy, engagement, structure, audience fit) instead of a single scalar educational value. It uses an LLM judge to label sampled document pairs and distills the pairwise preferences into reusable filters. This matters for data curation quality in domains where 'educational' is multidimensional.

entry.title: Modality-Decoupled Federated Learning for Privacy-Preserving Embodied Intelligence in 6G

author.name: Zhuodong Liu, Xiangyu Li, Chunhong Yuan, Hongyang Du, Bodong Shang, Qingqing Wu, Tony Q. S. Quek, Mohsen Guizani

entry.summary: Proposes modality-decoupled federated learning for training vision-language-action models across distributed robotic agents in 6G networks, treating vision, language, and action pathways separately given their different parameter scales, privacy exposure, and update dynamics. Addresses privacy, communication efficiency, and heterogeneity jointly. Sits at the intersection of embodied AI, FL, and next-gen networking.

entry.title: Which Medical Questions Deserve Rationales? Perturbation-Sensitive Selection for Robust QA

author.name: Yuexin Wu, Dayou Yu, Vasile Rus

entry.summary: Reframes rationale acquisition for medical QA: given labels already exist, which questions should receive costly rationale supervision under a fixed token budget. Proposes RMS-RSP, which perturbs hidden states at rationale tokens and measures shifts in the gold-versus-distractor margin, evaluated across five medical QA datasets with MedGemma-4B. A practical data-allocation strategy for resource-constrained medical AI.

entry.title: Pairit: A Platform for Live Experiments on Human-AI Collaboration

author.name: Harang Ju, Sinan Aral

entry.summary: Pairit is an open platform for designing and deploying live experiments on human-AI organizational design, where AI participants can communicate and act on shared workspaces. Researchers declare full experiment graphs, including routing, randomization, matchmaking, and shared work, via a single YAML configuration. It fills a methodological gap for studying how human-AI groups coordinate and delegate in real time.

entry.title: Albedo Estimation via Latent Bridge Matching

author.name: Carme Corbi, David Serrano-Lozano, Javier Vazquez-Corral, Maria Vanrell

entry.summary: The authors apply latent bridge matching to intrinsic image decomposition for albedo estimation, addressing physical consistency, inference cost, and generalization limitations of generative IID approaches. A pixel reconstruction loss enforces physical consistency, and shading conditioning improves cross-dataset generalization. The extended version adds further conditioning results.

entry.title: Fidelity-Aware Scheduling of Quantum Circuits on Multi-QPU Systems

author.name: Innocenzo Fulginiti, Antonio Tudisco, Salvatore Zammuto, Patrick Hopf, Deborah Volpe, Helmut Seidl, Giovanna Turvani, Robert Wille, Christian B. Mendl, Martin Schulz

entry.summary: This work presents a GNN-based scheduling framework for distributing quantum circuits across heterogeneous multi-QPU systems, estimating expected execution fidelity before compilation. In noisy intermediate-scale quantum settings, where errors compound along compiled circuits, fidelity-aware placement can materially improve result reliability. The framework has low overhead and accounts for differing device topologies, gates, and noise.

entry.title: OmniMed-FL: A Robust Multimodal Federated Learning Framework for Clinical Diagnosis

author.name: Ayush Debnath, Ruelia Saha, Sudip Misra

entry.summary: OmniMed-FL is a multimodal federated learning framework for clinical diagnosis that fuses chest radiographs with textual patient records across distributed networks while respecting HIPAA/GDPR constraints. It targets five-class condition classification using 3,000 public radiographs paired with class-conditioned synthetic notes. It addresses a genuine gap in privacy-preserving joint image-plus-text medical learning.

entry.title: Physics-informed neural networks by Gradient-Guided Gaussian Adaptive Sampling (3GAS-PINNs)

author.name: Yousen Wang, Wei Zhao

entry.summary: The authors propose 3GAS-PINNs, a method combining uniform and Gaussian-smoothed probability distributions for adaptive collocation-point sampling in physics-informed neural networks. The approach targets known PINN weaknesses on nonlinear PDEs, such as slow convergence, gradient imbalance, and poor resolution of localized structures like shock waves. Adaptive sampling of training points based on gradient information is a practical direction for making mesh-free PDE solvers more reliable.

entry.title: NEXUS-MI: Communication-Aware Federated Personalization for Gateway-Coordinated Motor-Imagery Brain-Computer Interfaces

author.name: Daniel Adu Worae, Aarthy Nagarajan

entry.summary: NEXUS-MI frames federated personalization for EEG motor-imagery brain-computer interfaces as a coupled learning-and-communication control problem, keeping raw EEG local while an edge coordinator maintains a shared backbone. It is evaluated via offline replay on BCICIV-2a and OpenBMI across many subjects, relaxing the regular-synchronization assumption of prior federated MI work.

entry.title: Evaluating Model Retraining under Drift: Paired Comparisons of Cumulative Subgroup Disparity

author.name: Aaron Ceross

entry.summary: The paper proposes a paired-comparison methodology for evaluating retraining policies (scheduled, loss-triggered, subgroup-gap-triggered) against retaining the initial model, measuring cumulative absolute subgroup disparity across deployment windows under delayed labels. In simulation across two drift regimes, all three policies produced lower mean cumulative disparity than the retained initial model.

entry.title: Online Inverse Integer Linear Optimization via Small-Gradient Skipping: Constant Regret and Finite Mistakes

author.name: Akira Kitaoka

entry.summary: This theoretical work studies online inverse linear optimization, where a learner predicts weights and observes an agent's optimal actions. The author proposes Small-Gradient Skipping, a mechanism that skips updates when the correct action is uniformly separated from alternatives, and shows it achieves constant regret and finitely many mistakes in online gradient descent over M-convex action sets, closing part of the O(d log T) versus Omega(d) regret gap. The result is a clean contribution to learning theory for decision-making under combinatorial constraints.

entry.title: Multi-Pass, Multi-View Blended Learning for High-Fidelity Volumetric CT Synthesis from Chest X-Rays

author.name: Ozer Can Devecioglu, Serkan Kiranyaz, Rashid Mazhar, Tahir Hamid, Muhammad Chowdhury, Moncef Gabbouj

entry.summary: The paper tackles 2D-to-3D reconstruction of volumetric CT from a single chest X-ray, an ill-posed inverse problem aggravated by scarce paired CXR-CT data. Prior work trained on synthetic DRR projections suffers a domain gap when applied to real X-rays; the proposed multi-pass, multi-view blended learning framework synthesizes volumetric CT directly from real CXR images. If validated, this could reduce radiation exposure and cost in clinical imaging workflows.

entry.title: Storage-Scalable Progressive Semantic Communication via Knowledge-Base Reuse

author.name: Heng Zhu, Ye Liu, Kun Zhu, Feifei Song

entry.summary: The paper proposes SSKBQ, a semantic communication scheme that reuses a compact set of knowledge bases across multiple residual quantization refinement stages, decoupling transmission depth from knowledge-base storage growth. A stage-aware residual supervision mechanism maintains performance while solving the linear storage scaling of multi-KB approaches.

entry.title: View-Structured Conformal Prediction for 3D Gaussian Splatting

author.name: Junzheng Chu, Bin Pan, Zhenwei Shi

entry.summary: This work brings distribution-free statistical guarantees to 3D Gaussian Splatting novel-view synthesis by treating rendering as structured regression with pixel-coverage guarantees. The proposed VSCP method factorizes calibration into a spatial shape from the renderer and a transferable view-difficulty factor, using a held-out quantile over views to achieve finite-sample validity even when transferring to new scenes. This gives rendered views certified coverage rather than merely an uncertainty heatmap, an important step for deploying 3DGS in reliability-sensitive settings.

entry.title: GLOSS: Geometric Local Self-Similarity Learning for Faithful Reference-Guided Texture Fill

author.name: Chenyue Cai, Anita Hu, James Lucas, Szymon Rusinkiewicz, Masha Shugrina

entry.summary: GLOSS is a local, less data-hungry approach to texture generation for 3D shapes that leverages geometric self-similarity for reference-guided texture fill, aiming to adhere to fine-scale geometric detail from a single view. Unlike global generative methods trained on large 3D datasets, it gives artists interactive, controllable exploration of multiple textures from varied sources. This addresses a real gap between fully automatic generators and practical artist workflows.

entry.title: Gaussian Approximation for Multivariate Martingale Sums from Uniformly Ergodic Markov Chains

author.name: Yixuan Zhang, Qiaomin Xie

entry.summary: This paper derives explicit higher-order Wasserstein Gaussian approximation bounds for multivariate martingale difference sums generated by uniformly ergodic Markov chains, under an L(2+eta)p moment condition. In the balanced-increment regime it achieves the first optimal O(n^{-1/2}) W_p rate for fixed p and dimension d. Such results underpin statistical inference for stochastic approximation and reinforcement learning analyses involving Markovian data.

entry.title: Oracle Complexity of Stochastic Fixed-Point Equations with Nonexpansive Maps

author.name: Jelena Diakonikolas, Crist\'obal Guzm\'an, David Mart\'inez-Rubio

entry.summary: The paper establishes oracle complexity bounds for computing approximate fixed points of nonexpansive maps accessed through a stochastic oracle, for general norms with weak Rademacher type greater than one. Using a recursive anchoring technique, the authors achieve stochastic oracle complexity on the order of sigma-squared times epsilon to the minus three for type-2 spaces such as l_p norms with p at least 2, and they also provide matching lower bounds.

entry.title: Why Learning Rediscovers the Closed-Form Diagonal Regularizer

author.name: Jeahn Han, Pyojin Kim

entry.summary: Identifies a diagonal saturation principle in modal inverse problems: with isotropic truncation noise, the Bayes-optimal Tikhonov regularizer has a closed-form power-law shape determined by the prior alone. Combining Berry's random-wave conjecture with Weyl's eigenvalue counting law, the authors argue the loss landscape is nearly flat across per-mode regularizer families, explaining why learned regularizers cannot robustly beat the closed form, and validate this on FEM-simulated acoustic rooms.

entry.title: Searching for New Physics with Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Jacky Kumar, Marianne Bouchard, David London

entry.summary: This paper applies reinforcement learning to search the enormous space of SMEFT operators for explanations of anomalies in low-energy particle physics observables, replacing intuition-driven human searches that can be biased and incomplete. The approach handles the combinatorial explosion and loop-level correlations among operators.

entry.title: Characterizing Language Generation in the Limit: Finite Witnesses and a Separation-Width Hierarch

author.name: Xiaoyu Li, Andi Han, Jiaojiao Jiang, Junbin Gao

entry.summary: This theoretical work characterizes when language generation in the limit is possible for arbitrary families over a countable universe, via finite positive witnesses whose activated targets share an infinite common intersection. It further introduces positive separation width to measure how large compatible witnesses must be, yielding a hierarchy of generation difficulty.

entry.title: Do LLMs Make More Mistakes If They Do Not Believe the Input Data?

author.name: Peter Kochelka, Ale\v{s} Manuel Pap\'a\v{c}ek, Vojt\v{e}ch Dvo\v{r}\'ak, Ond\v{r}ej Du\v{s}ek

entry.summary: This study analyzes how LLM faithfulness to provided context depends on perceived plausibility of the context, generating text in English, Czech, Slovak, and Upper Sorbian from factual, counterfactual, and fictional RDF triples of local Czech and Slovak data. Using low-resource settings to sharpen error patterns, it finds results contrary to expectations about context-memory conflict.

entry.title: Beyond Top Words: MonoTM for Topic Modeling with Interpretable Monosemantic Features

author.name: Una Joh, Bei Yu

entry.summary: MonoTM uses sparse autoencoders to extract interpretable features for topic modeling, decoupling document-topic mixture estimation from semantic interpretation. Across three benchmarks, the authors show that mixture estimation and interpretation favor different SAE configurations and feature subsets. This connects the interpretability tooling of SAEs to the classic topic-modeling problem in a novel way.

entry.title: SymbolicLight V2: Hybrid Neuromorphic Architecture and Sparse Execution for Low-Energy Language Inference

author.name: Ting Liu

entry.summary: SymbolicLight V2 presents a hybrid neuromorphic language architecture combining sparse event computation with continuous-state processing, including graded signed events and softmax-free local attention, implemented on both an FPGA (194M parameters, fixed-point) and ARM CPU with sparse integer execution. The authors report decode throughput rising from 474.6 to 643.2 tokens/s and a 27.6% per-token energy reduction on FPGA. The work explores hardware-software co-design for low-energy LLM inference at small model scale.

entry.title: $S^3$-Bench: Evaluating Speech Interaction Models as Scientific Voice Assistants

author.name: Heyang Liu, Jiayi Huang, Wenyang Xiao, Ziyang Cheng, Lixin Zhang, Zhen Liu, Miao He, Ronghua Wu, Qunshan Gu, Yanfeng Wang, Yu Wang

entry.summary: The paper introduces S3-Bench, a benchmark for evaluating speech-capable multimodal LLMs as scientific voice assistants across 10 disciplines, including a knowledge QA set and a multi-turn dialogue set. It targets hard challenges in spoken scientific interaction such as rare terminology, spoken forms of abbreviations, and verbalization of symbolic expressions. This fills a gap since existing speech benchmarks focus on general conversation rather than specialized scientific domains.

entry.title: Politics of Feelings: Emotional Expression and Legislative Effectiveness in the U.S. Congress

author.name: Segun Aroyehun

entry.summary: Using a transformer-based emotion classifier over 1.7 million U.S. Congressional speeches from 1973 to 2024, this study measures eight discrete emotions and examines how they vary over time, across policy topics and legislator characteristics, and how they relate to legislative effectiveness. It moves beyond describing emotional expression in political communication to testing its association with consequential outcomes. The large-scale, longitudinal design makes it a substantive contribution to computational social science.

entry.title: The Living Library: Transforming Archival Collections into Conversational Knowledge Systems -- Lessons from the Theodore Roosevelt Presidential Library

author.name: Pengce Wang, Lucia Ronchi Darre, Matt Briney, Michaell Bakalars, Dan Rutkowski, Ursula Hardy, David Wolf, Laura Hoffman, Allen Kim, Shawn Wright, Juan Lavista Ferres

entry.summary: A deployed end-to-end system from Microsoft-affiliated authors that transforms a 300,000-record presidential library archive into a governed conversational exhibit experience, spanning digitization, OCR and metadata enrichment with expert curator review, hybrid retrieval, and an embodied conversational interface. It reports practical lessons from a real public deployment.

entry.title: IAE-VTG: Interaction-Aligned Action-Entity Video Temporal Grounding

author.name: Shiwen Zhao, Qi Zhang, Sezer Karaoglu, Theo Gevers, Martin R. Oswald

entry.summary: IAE-VTG improves video temporal grounding by explicitly modeling action-entity interactions: a Fine-grained Disentangled Interaction Module separates action and entity query information and aligns it with complementary video features, with training-assignment-level alignment ensuring the queried action and entity co-occur. This prevents retrieving segments containing both concepts but not the described event.

entry.title: LinearMask-GS: Stable-Mask Importance Pruning for Compact 3D Gaussian Splatting

author.name: Donghun Ryu, Minhyeok Lee

entry.summary: Identifies a flaw in learned-mask pruning for 3D Gaussian Splatting where Gumbel-Sigmoid activations saturate masks before importance rankings stabilize, producing unreliable bimodal distributions. The proposed linear increment activation preserves ranking information during mask training, enabling better compression of Gaussian primitives.

entry.title: A Risk-Sensitive and Uncertainty-Aware Decision-Making and Control Framework for Safe and Robust Autonomous Driving

author.name: Zhuoren Li, Ran Yu, Weiqi Zhang, Ming Liu, Lu Xiong, Chen Sun, Bo Leng

entry.summary: Presents RUDC, a framework coupling risk-sensitive distributional RL with uncertainty-aware control for autonomous driving at interactive unsignalized intersections, aiming to avoid the over-conservatism of fixed safety filters. Targets the safety-efficiency trade-off in complex urban traffic. A substantive systems contribution to safe RL deployment in driving.

entry.title: Multi-Robot Scanner for Automated Full-Body Dermoscopic Imaging

author.name: Valerio Franchi, Rafael Garcia, Nuno Gracias, Ricard Campos, Josep Quintana, Sandra Gonz\'alez-Vill\`a, Mark Ventura, Nuria Ferrera, Cl\'ement Lenoir, Josep Malvehy

entry.summary: Describes a four-arm UR10-based scanner capturing dermatoscopic-level full-body images of skin lesions, with view planning, simultaneous multi-arm control, and collision detection, validated on real patients against contact dermoscopy and the Vectra system. A clinically deployed-class robotics-for-healthcare system with medical validation. Bridges robotics engineering and dermatology screening.

entry.title: Adaptive Shared Control with Online Bounded-Rational Human Behavior Estimation

author.name: Henry Ascencio Trejo, Roel Pieters, Gokhan Alcan

entry.summary: Proposes adaptive shared human-robot control that relaxes full-rationality assumptions, modeling the human with a level-k bounded-rationality game whose candidate policies are approximated via adaptive dynamic programming, then mapping state-transition residuals online to select assistance. A principled treatment of imperfect human models in shared autonomy. Combines game theory, ADP, and online estimation.

entry.title: A traffic management system for large and heterogeneous vehicles in narrow industrial environments

author.name: Alessandro Bonetti, Silvia Proia, Simone Guidetti, Lorenzo Sabattini

entry.summary: This robotics paper presents a traffic management system for Automated Guided Vehicles in dense industrial settings, using a Lifelong Multi-Agent Path Finding algorithm operating on NURBS-generated roadmaps. It integrates a modified Bounded Horizon Conflict Based Search to guarantee locally optimal coordination and safe operation of large, heterogeneous AGVs. This matters for Logistics 4.0, where traditional negotiation-based priority assignment causes inefficiencies.

entry.title: IMU-Centric Moving Horizon Estimation for Lateral Dynamics Estimation Across Vehicles and Grip Conditions

author.name: Seuffo Akouan ha Ngoune, Alessandro Toschi, Paolo Burgio, Marko Bertogna

entry.summary: This paper presents a moving horizon estimation framework that reconstructs lateral vehicle velocity near the adhesion limit using only standard IMU signals, avoiding costly optical sensors and tire-parameter tuning. It is validated on human-driven sports cars and an autonomous open-wheel race car across varied tracks and conditions, with code released publicly. Accurate lateral dynamics estimation matters for stability control and high-performance autonomous driving.

entry.title: httpi: the internet protocol to reduce compute from misbehaving agents

author.name: joao_abrantes

entry.summary: This proposal argues AI safety should shift from purely training-based approaches toward mechanism design, drawing an analogy to how societies keep humans safe by assigning accountability and imposing costs (fines, lost access, deposits) on misbehavior. The author sketches httpi, an internet protocol concept where misbehaving AI agents lose resources or access, treating post-deployment incentive structures rather than in-model training as the primary safety lever.

entry.title: Voice or Stereotype? Disentangling Acoustic and Content-Based Gender in Speech-to-Speech Models

author.name: Xiaoqun Liu, Tanu Mitra, Harshit Rajgarhia, Abhishek Mukherji

entry.summary: The paper studies whether speech-to-speech models treat a speaker according to their voice or according to content-based gender stereotypes, addressing the methodological problem that fixed hard-coded output voices mask bias. It distinguishes voice-rendering bias from stated-gender judgments and tests whether models follow acoustic cues or content stereotypes. This is a novel fairness evaluation angle specific to speech models.

entry.title: Improving Cross-Lingual Token Representations by Adding a Pinch of SALT

author.name: Guillem Ram\'irez

entry.summary: SALT is a lightweight post-training method injecting span-level supervision into cross-lingual sentence encoders to improve token representations for tasks like sequence tagging and hallucination detection. It achieves best results on four of five multilingual token-level benchmarks while preserving sentence-level quality. The work addresses the train-usage mismatch in multilingual sentence encoders.

entry.title: Uncertainty-Aware Sea-Ice Type Mapping with Multiple Ice Charts

author.name: Samira Alkaee Taleghan, Younghyun Koo, Andrew P. Barrett, Farnoush Banaei-Kashani

entry.summary: The paper addresses deep-learning-based mapping of sea-ice stage of development using operational ice charts, explicitly modeling the fact that analyst-produced labels are uncertain and represent ranges of compatible thicknesses. It fuses multiple ice charts with uncertainty awareness rather than treating chart annotations as exact ground truth. This improves the trustworthiness of automated sea-ice products used for navigation and operational monitoring.

entry.title: Unthrottling the Tanh Jacobian in SAC: A Negative Result on Bang-Bang Control and MetaDrive

author.name: Faiq Shamass

entry.summary: The paper tests whether the vanishing tanh Jacobian in Soft Actor-Critic starves the actor of critic signal when extreme actions are optimal, proposing a minimal auxiliary loss term that restores detached action-gradient signal. Across a bang-bang double integrator and MetaDrive experiments, the intervention yields no meaningful benefit, since vanilla SAC already achieves near-optimal return.

entry.title: Odometer-Agnostic Drift Correction Using OpenStreetMap Lane Geometry

author.name: Joaquin Caballero, Emilio Garcia-Fidalgo, Alberto Ortiz, Jarno Ralli

entry.summary: A lightweight, open-source method that corrects long-term odometry drift by aligning short trajectory segments to sparse OpenStreetMap lane centerlines, working online without dense maps or expensive preprocessing across LiDAR and visual odometry backends. A pragmatic map-assisted localization contribution leveraging freely available map data. Useful for large-scale or loop-free environments.

entry.title: When will average people feel AI’s impact?

author.name: Nathan Lambert

entry.summary: Nathan Lambert argues that comparisons of the AI boom to the industrial revolution miss that most people lack tangible new goods from AI and that society has more inertia than in prior technological transitions. Drawing on his time offline, he observes that current consumer touch-points for AI are fringe, marginally beneficial, or confusing, and explores when diffusion into everyday life might actually occur.

entry.title: CT-SAFR: Safe and Interpretable Chain-of-Thought Reasoning for Autonomous Robots: A Multi-Layered Verification Framework for Trustworthy AI-Driven Robotic Decision Making

author.name: Cagri Temel

entry.summary: Presents CT-SAFR, a multi-layered verification framework for chain-of-thought reasoning in autonomous robots, reporting 94.2% hallucination detection with sub-500ms latency and an 87% reduction in unsafe reasoning outputs in a warehouse robot case study. Motivated by evidence that reasoning models verbalize their true decision process only 25-39% of the time. Targets safe deployment of reasoning LLMs in physical robotics.

entry.title: Elastoformer: Enabling Dynamic Adaptivity via Elastic Model Transformation

author.name: Sudaksh Kalra, Dolly Sapra

entry.summary: Elastoformer transforms conventional neural networks into Elastic NNs that can dynamically scale computation at runtime to match fluctuating latency, power, and memory constraints on edge devices. This targets the mismatch between fixed execution flows of standard DNNs and the dynamic operating conditions of EdgeAI vision systems. The framework supports real-time elastic adaptation without retraining per configuration.

entry.title: Future-Aware Flow Planning for Safe UAV Target Following

author.name: Boning Feng, Haoran Zhang, Xiaowen Bi, Yanzhen Zhang, Xiaodan Shi

entry.summary: A flow-based planner for UAV target following that uses predicted target futures as residual signals for trajectory generation and embeds risk-scored executable-prefix repair inside the sampling loop. Improves the safety-tracking trade-off with zero in-distribution collision rate and the lowest out-of-distribution collision rate on receding-horizon benchmarks. Honest framing about trade-offs rather than dominating all metrics.

entry.title: Valerant: An Automatic Navigable Game Map Generator via Action-Conditioned World Model Exploration

author.name: Yiran Qiao, Feng Wang, Jing Ma

entry.summary: Extends World Action Models to 3D games with Valerant, a system that automatically generates navigable game maps by coupling action-conditioned world modeling with exploration, addressing the lack of persistent 3D geometry in prior 2D game-oriented approaches.

entry.title: Beyond Surface Imitation: Contrastive Modeling for Reasoning Path Alignment in Multimodal In-Context Learning

author.name: Mingbo Yang, Wenqiang Wang, Zhaolu Kang, Peng Chen, Yannan Chen, Sunshang Wang, Yan Xiao

entry.summary: The paper proposes a multimodal ICL framework combining contrastive demonstration modeling with self-refinement so that model responses align with the reasoning path required by the input rather than imitating surface features of demonstrations. This targets a recognized limitation of multimodal in-context learning on complex tasks. The direction is sensible but the approach is a fairly standard combination of known techniques.

entry.title: From Plausible to Actionable: A Position on LLM Self-Explanations

author.name: Elize Herrewijnen, Benedetta Muscato, Gizem Gezici, Fosca Giannotti

entry.summary: A position paper arguing that LLM self-explanations can be highly plausible and questionably faithful yet still actionable, and that standard XAI evaluation protocols fit LLM-generated explanations poorly. The authors propose practical evaluation directions tailored to self-explanations. It contributes a conceptual reframing for the explainable AI community.

entry.title: From Fixed Keys to Readable Schemas: Small Language Models for Vehicle Agent Function Calls

author.name: Hamed Jafarzadeh Asl, Yuanhao Yu, Vahid Partovi Nia

entry.summary: Studies how small language models for in-vehicle assistants should represent callable functions: dedicated functional tokens versus schema-in-prompt prompting. The authors release a benchmark of 9,822 single-turn examples across 79 vehicle functions, showing the compactness-generalization tradeoff between the two approaches. Relevant to on-device agentic function calling under tight latency and memory budgets.

entry.title: NOPE-HYPE: A Structured Simulation Workflow for Robust Speech-to-Text Across Diverse Acoustic Environments

author.name: Niramay M. Patel, Bibek Behera, Raksha Sharma

entry.summary: NOPE-HYPE combines a controllable acoustic environment simulator, coverage-optimal environment reduction on PSD templates, and interpretable hyperparameter search to systematically train and evaluate robust speech-to-text. Simulator-generated noise matches balanced real-noise training for Whisper and SeamlessM4T models. The workflow addresses the scarcity of diverse acoustic conditions in speech training data.

entry.title: Hierarchical and Permutation-Invariant Feature Transformation Learning via Policy-Guided Embedding Search

author.name: Rui Liu, Tao Zhe, Yanyong Huang, Sankha Narayan Guria, Xiao Luo, Wei Fan, Yanjie Fu, Dongjie Wang

entry.summary: This paper addresses automated feature transformation for tabular data, identifying three limitations of recent generative embedding-space approaches: ignored hierarchy between features, operations, and abstractions; order-sensitive embeddings imposed on permutation-invariant transformation sequences; and ill-suited gradient-based search in non-convex spaces. The authors propose a framework combining a permutation-invariant hierarchical representation with policy-guided (reinforcement learning based) search over transformation strategies. This matters for automated ML since feature transformation strongly affects predictive performance on tabular data.

entry.title: Applying foundation model embeddings towards urban livability evaluation

author.name: Ayush Khot, Wen Zhou, Shaowen Wang

entry.summary: This paper investigates which physical features are encoded in geospatial foundation model embeddings such as AlphaEarth, AnySat, and TerraMind, and provides a systematic framework for identifying the most predictive geospatial indicators for urban livability. The work targets socioeconomic measurement in data-scarce regions where high-resolution satellite data is abundant. It offers practical guidance on which embedding sources and features matter for policy-relevant prediction.

entry.title: A practical DIRECT-type algorithm for medium-scale black-box global optimization

author.name: Linas Stripinis, Remigijus Paulavi\v{c}ius

entry.summary: The paper introduces X-DTC-GL, a DIRECT-type deterministic global optimization algorithm that extends the classic method from low-dimensional to medium-scale problems. It uses dynamic partitioning driven by local one-dimensional surrogate models to rapidly subdivide promising hyper-rectangles, plus hybridization with hill-climbing. This matters for black-box optimization tasks such as hyperparameter tuning and engineering design where gradients are unavailable and dimensionality defeats existing DIRECT methods.

entry.title: Bridging Theory and Data: Correcting Nuclear Mass Models with Interpretable Machine Learning

author.name: Yanhua Lu, Tianshuai Shang, Pengxiang Du, Jian Li, Haozhao Liang

entry.summary: The study applies Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks (KANs) to refine nuclear mass predictions, halving the RMSE from 0.3 MeV to 0.16 MeV in a KAN-WS4 hybrid model. Exploiting KAN interpretability, feature importance analysis identifies proton number as the dominant residual driver, suggesting systematic biases in proton-related terms of existing theoretical models. This exemplifies interpretable scientific machine learning where the model both improves predictions and yields physics insights.

entry.title: Bayesian deep learning integration of geophysical and drilling data for 3D prediction of copper mineralization and drill targeting: a case study from the Kogodai prospect, Rudny Altai

author.name: Margarita Veshchezerova, Egor Barashov, Evgenii Gusev, Michael R. Perelshtein, Arlan Kasymzhan, Bolat M. Kabaziev, Nurlan Y. Askarov

entry.summary: The authors present an uncertainty-aware 3D workflow that fuses desurveyed drilling data, trench assays, and geophysical inversions using Bayesian deep learning to predict copper mineralization fields and prioritize drill targets at the Kogodai prospect in the Rudny Altai. The approach aims to extract hidden value from existing brownfield data and shorten time-to-discovery in structurally complex terranes. It demonstrates a credible pipeline for uncertainty-quantified mineral exploration.

entry.title: X-amine509: Predicting the Practical Risk Level of Enterprise X.509 Certificates

author.name: Cameron Keith, Shubh Patel, JD Kilgallin, Caleb Shorter

entry.summary: X-amine509 is a two-stage triage system that uses machine learning to rank enterprise X.509 certificates by predicted risk, routing only the highest-risk items to expensive deterministic analysis. Risk is a composite score from 177 defect checks grounded in CA/Browser Forum Baseline Requirements, NIST guidance, and cryptographic strength criteria across four severity tiers. It addresses a real operational scaling problem in managing millions of certificates.

entry.title: Efficient Graph Neural Networks for Multicarrier Wideband Hybrid Beamforming Optimization

author.name: Beier Li, Mai Vu

entry.summary: Uses GNNs over a bipartite graph representation, where a shared analog beamformer connects to multiple subcarriers, to optimize hybrid beamforming in wideband 6G systems affected by beam squinting. The paper develops three GNN architectures with different digital beamformer representations as a cost-effective signal-processing alternative to per-antenna true-time-delay hardware.

entry.title: Physics-Informed Multi-Task Surrogate Model for the Martian Nightside Thermosphere

author.name: Sergey Nikiforov

entry.summary: A multi-task physics-informed neural network predicts logarithmic densities of four neutral species (O, CO2, N2, Ar) in the Martian nightside thermosphere using over a decade of MAVEN/NGIMS observations. A shared backbone with species-specific heads plus a weak monotonicity prior enforced via automatic differentiation prevents non-physical artifacts like density inversions in sparsely sampled regimes.

entry.title: X2-NativeCursor: Native-Token Text Progress Tracking for Incremental-Text Streaming Codec TTS

author.name: Zehan Liu, Carl Chen, Rime Wen, Kaiqi Fu, Altman Lin, Shawn Qin, Lights Shi, Roy Gan, Hao Wang, Qian Wang

entry.summary: X2-NativeCursor is a lightweight observer that tracks speech progress directly from native codec tokens in incremental-text streaming TTS, before waveform decoding, enabling synchronized highlighting, interruption handling, and dialogue-history updates. It links spoken labels to original text spans via a normalization plan and a local matcher over text and native-token encoders. This solves a practical latency problem in real-time conversational speech systems.

entry.title: 5-Dialects-BN: Unmasking the Impact of Transliteration on Bangla Dialectal LLMs

author.name: Md Mahir Jawad, Galib Mahmud Jim, Rafid Ahmed, Mir Sazzat Hossain, Md Fahim, Md Farhad Alam Bhuiyan

entry.summary: The paper presents 5-Dialects-BN, the first multi-annotation benchmark for Bangla dialects, with 6,000 manually annotated entries across five regional varieties aligning Romanized transliteration, dialectal text, Standard Bangla, English, and subjectivity labels. It enables development and evaluation of dialect-aware LLM systems for Bangla, the world's sixth most spoken language, which is underserved by existing Standard-Bangla-only resources.

entry.title: Integrating Unimodal and Vision-Language Representations in Latent Space for Multi-Label Chest X-Ray Classification

author.name: Quang-Huy Tran, Duc-Tuan Ngo, Minh-Khoi Nguyen-Bui, Dang-Khoa Bui, Thanh-Trong Tran, Tuan-Khoi Nguyen, Hoang-Anh Ngo

entry.summary: This work fuses unimodal RAD-DINO embeddings with vision-language BioViL-T representations in latent space for 14-label multi-label chest X-ray classification on MIMIC-CXR-JPG. Each branch is refined separately before normalized fusion, and the study clarifies how the embedding sources complement each other. It is an applied medical imaging contribution combining established foundation-model embeddings.

entry.title: VFNet: Multi-View Spatio-Temporal Model for Void Fraction Estimation in Gas-Liquid Two-Phase Flow

author.name: Md Adnan Faisal Hossain, Raghav Rajeev, Kumar Nishant, Justin A Weibel, Satish Kumar, Fengqing Zhu

entry.summary: VFNet is a dual-branch spatio-temporal network that predicts void fraction in gas-liquid two-phase flow from synchronized multi-view videos, combining local dual-view feature fusion with a global spatio-temporal branch, trained partly on simulation data. It avoids intrusive sensors and flow-model assumptions that limit prior methods.

entry.title: ScopeMamba-YOLO: Widening the Perceptual Scope Inward and Outward for Small Object Detection in Remote Sensing Imagery

author.name: Junjie Fan, Yijun Mai, Linduo Wei, Jiayu Rao, Junmin Bao, Qiushi Jin, Guijia Li, Yong Qi

entry.summary: Proposes a YOLO-style detector for small objects in UAV and remote sensing imagery built on an off-path, zero-gated Mamba selective-scanning principle that decouples long-range context modeling from the convolutional stream. Includes a cascaded global-context module, selective-scan PAN neck, and adaptive multi-scale strip blocks.

entry.title: A Bio-Plausible Visual Neural Network for Locust-Inspired Collision Perception

author.name: Qinbing Fu, Jiani Li, Jiajun Huang, Jigen Peng

entry.summary: This paper presents a biologically plausible neural network inspired by locust LGMD neurons for looming detection and collision avoidance, improving on prior computational models with a spatially isotropic sampling strategy mimicking locust ommatidial organization. The goal is greater robustness in complex, dynamic visual environments. Such neuromorphic collision-perception models are relevant for low-power robotics and drones.

entry.title: AXON: A ROS 2 RMW with Shared-Memory/QUIC Transport and QKD/ML-KEM Key Establishment

author.name: Sergio S\'anchez de la Fuente, Miguel \'Angel Gonz\'alez-Santamarta, Francisco Javier Rodr\'iguez-Lera, Vicente Matell\'an Olivera, \'Angel Manuel Guerrero-Higueras

entry.summary: Presents AXON, an alternative ROS 2 middleware implementation in Rust and C++ using POSIX shared memory for same-host traffic and QUIC remotely, with fail-closed TLS 1.3 configurations supporting hybrid post-quantum key exchange (X25519MLKEM768) and QKD-derived keys via ETSI GS. Addresses transport security and performance gaps in DDS-based ROS 2 middleware. Notable for bringing post-quantum and QKD cryptography into robotics middleware.

entry.title: Recovery Theory for Projected Power Iterations in Permutation Synchronization

author.name: Vahan Huroyan, Gilad Lerman

entry.summary: This statistics/ML paper provides theoretical recovery guarantees for the projected power method in permutation synchronization under sparse uniform corruption, proving exact one-step recovery conditions and block-error contraction results. The analysis covers regimes where observed pairs are sparse and corrupted with uniform permutations. This formalizes when a widely used algorithm provably works.

entry.title: Seven Sources of Physical AI Capability Formation

author.name: Gang Chen

entry.summary: Defines a capability-formation taxonomy for Physical AI, identifying seven non-exclusive sources such as recorded experience, predictive modeling, evaluative interaction, and evolution-driven formation, derived via reconstructive induction over primary studies.

entry.title: Critical initialization destabilizes higher input derivatives in wide scalar-input networks

author.name: Prashant Singh, Pranav Singh

entry.summary: The paper derives mean-field recursions through third order for input-derivative variances in wide randomly initialized networks, showing that at the edge-of-chaos criticality the first-derivative variance stays depth-invariant while second-derivative variance grows linearly when the activation has nonzero curvature. This has direct implications for physics-informed losses, score matching, and derivative regularization. It extends classical signal-propagation theory to higher-order jets.

entry.title: Improving 5G AI-RAN MCS Selection by Predicting Retransmissions

author.name: Tamerlan Aghayev, Maxime Elkael, Michele Polese, Reshma Prasad, Salvatore D'Oro, Yunseong Lee, Koichiro Furueda, Tommaso Melodia

entry.summary: The paper introduces NOSTRAdAMUS, a predictive link-adaptation framework for 5G radio access that adds foresight to existing reactive MCS selection algorithms by predicting retransmissions rather than replacing deployed controllers. It addresses noisy, quickly obsolete channel measurements and HARQ feedback in real-time schedulers. The work is a credible applied ML contribution to AI-native RAN research.

entry.title: A Statistical Approach to Estimating Sample Size of Machine Learning Models

author.name: Dat Phan-Trong, Sunil Gupta, Svetha Venkatesh

entry.summary: Proposes a framework for sample-size determination for nonlinear ML prediction models by approximating them with localized linear representations and evaluating statistical power across local regions. This sidesteps the need to specify predictor-outcome structure a priori as in classical power analysis. Useful for study design where ML models replace conventional regression.

entry.title: The Vibe Shift in Software Engineering: Evaluating AI-Led Conversational Programming for Performance, Cognition, and Responsible Adoption

author.name: Sales G. Aribe Jr., Louie Jay S. Labastida

entry.summary: A mixed-methods study of vibe coding with 30 professional developers and students completing tasks under traditional, AI-assisted, and AI-led conversational conditions, measuring efficiency, cognitive effects, and responsible-adoption considerations. Reports significant differences across conditions using ANOVA and thematic analysis. Timely empirical evidence on an emerging development practice.

entry.title: SA-Profile: Automated Sulcus Angle Profiling from Super-Resolution MRI

author.name: Michael Wehrli, Leo Widmer, Edwin Li, Noel Fiechter, Lorenzo Pettinari, Sidaty El Hadramy, Carol C. Hasler, Philippe C. Cattin

entry.summary: This medical imaging paper presents an automated pipeline for continuous sulcus angle profiling to assess trochlear dysplasia, replacing error-prone single-slice manual MRI measurements. It combines implicit neural representation-based super-resolution of multi-planar MR scans with two U-Net landmark detection models, and evaluates on the public fastMRI dataset. The work matters clinically because sulcus angle measurement is currently sensitive to arbitrary slice selection, and continuous profiling across the trochlear region could improve diagnosis of patellar instability.

entry.title: Development and Validation of a Physics-Guided Machine Learning Extrapolation Framework Using a Classical Transient Diffusion Benchmark

author.name: Ashutosh Yadav, Alok Dubey, Prodyut Ranjan Chakraborty, Harshal Akolekar

entry.summary: This paper builds an extrapolation framework for engineering machine learning models, comparing a Bidirectional LSTM and a Physics-Informed Neural Network on a classical one-dimensional transient diffusion benchmark. The goal is physically consistent predictions outside the training domain, a common failure mode of purely data-driven engineering models. The use of a known analytical benchmark allows rigorous validation of extrapolation behavior that field data cannot easily provide.

entry.title: Real-time and adaptive anomaly detection algorithm for cyclostationary models

author.name: Justyna Witulska, Tomasz Barszcz, Ireneusz Jab{\l}o\'nski, Agnieszka Wy{\l}oma\'nska

entry.summary: PeriodicCALM is a real-time anomaly detection framework for cyclostationary data streams that models cycle-dependent variability so that regular cyclic impulses are ignored while genuine anomalies are isolated. It operates with continuous retraining, addressing false-alarm problems of existing methods that misread phase-dependent variability as anomalies. Applications include condition monitoring of machinery and other periodic signal streams.

entry.title: A Unifying Perspective on Probabilities as Model Predictions

author.name: Benedikt H\"oltgen

entry.summary: Argues that every probability is the output of a prediction method combining an abstraction-construction step and a prediction transformation, unifying Bayesian and frequentist notions and showing that even supposedly objective probabilities are model-dependent. It connects finite calibration criteria to the distribution of utilities from acting on probabilistic predictions.

entry.title: Deterministic Prompting for Speaker-Stable Low-Resource Greek TTS

author.name: Georgios Syllas, Efthymios Georgiou, Kosmas Kritsis, Alexandros Potamianos

entry.summary: Provides a data curation recipe turning Greek audiobook recordings into TTS-ready data via WhisperX alignment, then fine-tunes the 880M multilingual Parler-TTS model. The key finding is that LLM-generated style prompts cause speaker drift at inference, and replacing them with deterministic prompts plus a speaker-specific LoRA on 3.5 hours of data anchors speaker identity while updating only ~5% of parameters.

entry.title: HybridFLow: SDN-Orchestrated Client Partitioning for Hybrid Federated Learning

author.name: Osama Abu Hamdan, Rabin Pandey, Hao Che, Engin Arslan, Md Arifuzzaman

entry.summary: HybridFLow is a closed-loop SDN-driven orchestration framework that partitions clients between synchronous and asynchronous participation in cross-silo federated learning, using the SDN controller's global view of network topology, bottlenecks, and contention. It aims to mitigate stragglers in wide-area deployments.

entry.title: When Does Defendant Statement Matter? A Study of Bias and Persuasion in LLM-Simulated Jurors

author.name: Cho-Ying Wu

entry.summary: The paper introduces JuryBench, a benchmark of controversial U.S. criminal cases used to study how defendant courtroom statements influence LLM-simulated jurors, varying defendant background, emotional appeal, and rebuttal strategies.
