entry.summary: NSFlow combines CNN feature extraction with a differentiable classical Lucas-Kanade-style optimization layer to produce sparse optical flow that is robust to large motions and illumination changes yet efficient for visual odometry front-ends. The neuro-symbolic hybrid aims to get the geometric consistency of classical methods with the robustness of learned ones. This is relevant to lightweight SLAM/VO systems on constrained hardware.

entry.title: Unified Multi-Layer Subspace Modeling for Cross-Domain OOD Detection

author.name: Gerhard Krumpl, Henning Avenhaus, Horst Possegger

entry.summary: PRISM is a model-agnostic post-hoc out-of-distribution detection method that models a unified subspace across intermediate representation layers, addressing the brittleness of fixed-layer or OOD-calibrated aggregation when OOD shifts vary across types and domains. It argues no single layer is reliably informative, so the method spans multiple layers simultaneously. This matters for safer deployment of classifiers that are overconfident on shifted inputs.

entry.title: GIFT: Goal-Injected Fine-Tuning for Efficient Manipulation Policy Adaptation

author.name: Xiaoyuan Fang, Shuo Feng, Yuxuan Wang, Enhua Cheng, Peng Zhou, Piji Li

entry.summary: GIFT is a lightweight fine-tuning framework that integrates generated goal images as high-level visual guidance into multiple pretrained vision-language-action models, injecting goal features via a zero-initialized convolution that grows parameters from zero to prevent destabilization. This enables goal-image conditioning that foundation VLA models have lacked due to high training costs. The work matters for improving robustness of robot manipulation policies without full retraining.

entry.title: KODAMA: Multimodal Digital Twin Reconstruction for Urban RF Propagation Modelling

author.name: Maximiliano Wardle, A. Ryo Koblitz

entry.summary: KODAMA is an automated pipeline that builds ray tracing-ready radio frequency digital twins at city scale from off-the-shelf geospatial data (aerial imagery, LiDAR, photogrammetry, street-level imagery), avoiding weeks of manual per-site model construction. The twins are judged by whether communication channels behave realistically, enabling site-specific RF channel prediction.

entry.title: TRAIL: Trajectory-Aware Visual Place Recognition against Unordered Databases

author.name: Dominik A. Kloepfer, Patrick Wenzel

entry.summary: TRAIL formalizes a task combining trajectory context with visual place recognition: localizing the final image of a query sequence against an unordered reference database, without requiring sequential structure in the database. The method uses Conditional Random Fields to fuse learned visual similarity and camera-motion consistency, refining candidate distributions as queries arrive. This addresses brittleness of standard VPR in feature-poor environments.

entry.title: From Glance to Scrutiny: Progressive Distortion Reasoning for Fine-Grained Image Quality Assessment

author.name: Aoting Zhang, Mingze Gao, Dongbao Yang, Longyi Chen, Daoxin Zhang, Yi Wu, Yao Hu, Yu Zhou

entry.summary: GS-IQA reformulates image quality assessment with multimodal LLMs as a progressive Where-What-How diagnosis that mimics human perception moving from a glance to close scrutiny, localizing distortions, identifying them, and judging severity in an ordered pipeline. This addresses the black-box limitation of holistic IQA approaches that give little insight into localized degradations. The work matters for interpretable quality assessment relevant to generative media evaluation.

entry.title: STSG-VQA: Evidence-Grounded Temporal Question Answering from Surgical Spatio-Temporal Scene Graphs

author.name: Jing Li, Duygu Sarikaya

entry.summary: STSG-VQA introduces multi-level structured temporal supervision over surgical scene graphs, adding object-level continuity, event-level interaction continuity, and procedure-level connectivity to frame-centric representations. It executes temporal queries over spatio-temporal scene graphs to generate evidence-grounded question-answer pairs, addressing the limited temporal reasoning of current surgical vision-language models. This supports workflow understanding and surgical assistance.

entry.title: AURORA: Active Uncertainty-Driven Re-Orientation for In-Hand Reconstruction

author.name: Feiyu Zhao, Yuetong Li, Chenxi Xiao

entry.summary: AURORA closes the loop between online object-centric 3D reconstruction and in-hand reorientation, using Ray-GPIS to estimate directional reconstruction uncertainty along viewing rays and select next-best views via an uncertainty-novelty objective realized with an axis-conditioned rotation policy. RGB-D observations are fused incrementally to reconstruct occluded object surfaces. This targets a real perception challenge in dexterous manipulation.

entry.title: Rethinking Learned Occupancy in Autonomous Active Mapping with Observation-Gated Filtering

author.name: Jiahui Zhang, Bonian Han, Gongbo Liang, Yu Zhang

entry.summary: This companion work to a diagnostic study examines how learned occupancy completion serves dual roles in active mapping, scoring expected surface gain while constraining collision-free motion, and shows improving occupancy accuracy does not monotonically improve mapping outcomes. It proposes observation-gated filtering to decouple planner-facing occupancy roles in a controlled closed-loop benchmark. The findings challenge assumptions about simply improving world-model accuracy.

entry.title: Geometric Distributional Control: Learning Progress with Partial Structural Knowledge

author.name: Tong Wu

entry.summary: Geometric Distributional Control (GDC) targets the middle regime between fully specified model-based control and exploration-heavy RL, where partial geometry, physics, or constraints are known but the local direction of task progress is uncertain. It uses known structure to accelerate progress estimation without long-horizon value inference. This addresses a real gap relevant to autonomous driving, warehouse robotics, and drones.

entry.title: OCTN: Neural OCT Representations for Robot-Guided Precision Intervention

author.name: Ravi Prakash, Ryan P. McNabb, Patrick J. Codd, Shan Lin

entry.summary: OCTN is an implicit neural representation framework that converts volumetric OCT scans into continuous, differentiable tissue-intensity fields for robot-guided surgical intervention. A two-stage hybrid training strategy combines voxel supervision with inter-slice interpolation, preserving B-scan fidelity while enabling fast volumetric reasoning and robot integration. It bridges medical imaging and surgical robotics with micron-scale contactless intraoperative guidance.

entry.title: Nonparametric Hypothesis Testing of High-dimensional Clustering With Application to Single-cell RNA Data

author.name: Yifan Dai, Di Wu, Yufeng Liu

entry.summary: The paper proposes SigClust-LCP, a nonparametric extension of clustering significance testing that models a single cluster under a log-concave distribution instead of the unreliable Gaussian null, with computational tricks for moderate-to-high dimensions. Applied to single-cell RNA-seq, it helps distinguish genuine cell-type heterogeneity from sampling variability. This addresses a real methodological gap in genomics workflows.

entry.title: Beyond "AI Helps Humans": Decision-Targeted Evaluation Design for Human-Agent Teams in the Agentic Era

author.name: Hamed Khosravi, Xiaoming Huo

entry.summary: This position/methodology paper argues that human-AI workflow evaluations should target the actual deployment decision: keep the combined workflow versus human-only or agent-only alternatives. It formalizes the replay-budget problem of choosing which counterfactual baseline to estimate and proposes decision-targeted evaluation design.

entry.title: LayerRoute: Action-Conditioned Mixture-of-Layers Routing for Vision-Language-Action Policies

author.name: Zheng Lu, Haoran Liao, Wanqi Zhong, Yunhe Ni, Lijie Wang, Xingjie Fan, Zhisheng Chen, Yantang Qu, Meijia Chen, Tianyu Xin, Zirui Song, Yiming Li

entry.summary: LayerRoute introduces an action-conditioned mixture-of-layers routing mechanism for vision-language-action (VLA) robot policies, allowing each action computation step to dynamically draw on different layers of the underlying vision-language model rather than fixed layer assignments. This exploits the hierarchy from local visual geometry to abstract language-aligned semantics across layers.

entry.title: VST: Verifiable Structured Transport for Auditable Agent-to-Agent Alpha Discovery

author.name: Yuqi Li, Siyuan Liu, Bingjun Liu

entry.summary: Restructures communication between mining and evaluation agents in multi-agent alpha discovery as typed, causally addressable, unicast records forming a replayable causal trajectory, then adds a predictor that forecasts multi-cycle guidance and a transactional verify-leap controller that commits speculative multi-cycle outcomes only when a four-level gate passes. Replacing free-form natural-language hand-offs with verifiable contracts improves auditability and cuts feedback cycles.

entry.title: World Models Under Asynchronous Sensor Observations

author.name: Akash Anand, Abhay Anand, Yash Vishe

entry.summary: This paper addresses the unrealistic synchronous-observation assumption in learned world models, studying transformer world models under heterogeneous, asynchronous sensor rates using staleness and time-to-refresh features rather than interpolation or downsampling. It evaluates across three regimes of increasing causal coupling, including open-loop rollouts. The work matters for deploying world models in real robotics and sensing settings where channels are frequently stale.

entry.title: FinCUABuild: Can Agents Build Reliable Benchmarks for Dynamic Financial Computer Use?

author.name: Jingpu Yang, Fengxian Ji, Jinri Guo, Tianhao Li, Qian Jiang, Fan Zhang, Min Peng, Qianqian Xie, Preslav Nakov, Zhuohan Xie

entry.summary: Introduces FinCUABuildBench, a benchmark evaluating whether computer-using agents can autonomously construct diverse, reliable CUA evaluation tasks for financial scenarios, with 576 construction requests across 24 financial workflows. Addresses scenario coverage, fair method comparison, and generated-task quality assessment.

entry.title: SE-GoS: Self-Evolving Graph-of-Skills for Skill Library at Scale

author.name: Dawei Fu, Cheng Jiang, Sitian Qian, Huainan Wang, Zhongkai Hao

entry.summary: Presents SE-GoS, a training-free framework that evolves an existing Graph-of-Skills retrieval structure by distilling historical execution traces into a better dependency-aware skill graph, preserving the original retrieval pipeline. It targets the bottleneck of skill retrieval as agent skill libraries scale to thousands of entries.

entry.title: SkillAdam: Stable and Efficient Skill Evolution for Agents

author.name: Gaoyuan Li, Meihao Fan, Yizhe Liu, Shaolei Zhang, Ju Fan, Siyi Wang, Jiaheng Hou, Xudong Weng, Honghan Tian, Zang Li

entry.summary: SkillAdam addresses instability in LLM agent skill self-evolution, where iterative loops revise reusable skill documents using execution feedback. The paper identifies two desiderata, Direction Stability (corrections should accumulate rather than be overwritten) and Update Adaptivity (revision scope should reflect feedback consistency), and proposes an optimizer-style update rule analogous to Adam for skill evolution. This matters because reusable skills are an increasingly popular way to extend frozen LLM agents, and current heuristic update loops are inefficient.

entry.title: STAR-Pro: Stage-Wise Token Adaptive Reduction with Progressive Refinement for Efficient Large Vision-Language Models

author.name: Yichen Guo, Tinghao Wang, Qizhe Zhang, Lingbei Meng, Yuan Zhang, Jiajun Cao, Hao Jiang, Chenwei Wu, Jixian Wu, Sixiang Chen, Tao Luo, Hongyang Cheng, Kai Tang, Chenxi Li, Renyuan Li, Xiande Huang, Wenya Wang, Shanghang Zhang

entry.summary: STAR-Pro is a training-free visual token pruning method for large vision-language models grounded in two analyses: aggressive pruning discards substantial pre-fusion visual information, and text-to-visual attention patterns shift substantially across decoder layers, making one-shot pruning unreliable. It therefore applies stage-wise, progressive token reduction with refinement instead of a single pruning decision.

entry.title: AVSplat: Dense-View Feed-Forward 3D Gaussian Splatting with Assist-View Preconditioning

author.name: Muyu Xu, Fangneng Zhan, Yu Wei, Hanspeter Pfister, Shijian Lu

entry.summary: AVSplat addresses pose-free feed-forward 3D Gaussian Splatting, where more input views often degrade performance due to attention dilution and over-smoothed voxel fusion. It introduces assist-view preconditioning (lightweight relevance- and diversity-based interactions before global attention) and adaptive representation fusion to convert dense views into reliable signals for novel view synthesis.

entry.title: Memory in Deep Time-Series Models

author.name: Minh Hoang Nguyen, Huu Hiep Nguyen, Manh Nguyen, Van Dai Do, Dung Nguyen, Hung Le

entry.summary: A perspective/survey paper arguing that diverse time-series architectures, from recurrent networks and transformers to state-space models, retrieval-augmented predictors, foundation models, and tool-using agents, should be unified under the question of how a model retains and accesses information beyond its input window. It frames memory as the central organizing principle of the field.

entry.title: Programmable Cellular Automata

author.name: Ahmed Khalifa, Muhammad Umair Nasir, Matthew Siper, Steve James, Julian Togelius

entry.summary: Introduces programmable cellular automata, representing CA systems as modularized Python code with local and decision functions to make rule design more intuitive and interpretable than evolved or hand-written local rules. Relevant to games, simulation, and procedural content generation.

entry.title: From Splats to Silicon: Rethinking Computational Efficiency of 3DGS

author.name: Minnan Pei, Qiwei Dong, Yihan Zhou, Gang Li, Yuchen Zhu, Wenju Zhao, Zhongtian Long, Siting Wang, Peisong Wang, Jian Cheng

entry.summary: A workload-centric systems analysis connecting 3D Gaussian splatting efficiency research across representation design, GPU runtime optimization, and hardware support, tracing how each optimization affects Gaussian selection, screen-space work, data movement, and frame time to relate reported gains to end-to-end system benefit.

entry.title: Scratchy: Visual-Scratchpad Multimodal Reasoning for Cryptographic Proof Generation in EasyCrypt

author.name: Yupeng Ren, Zhaoxuan Li, Rui Zhang

entry.summary: Scratchy is a visual-scratchpad method that exposes implicit proof-theoretic dependencies in cryptographic security proofs for multimodal LLMs, enabling generation of machine-checked proofs in the EasyCrypt framework. It targets a genuinely hard reasoning domain where coordinating probabilities, adversarial games, and assumptions stumps current LLMs. The visual scratchpad idea is a novel mechanism for making distributed context tractable.

entry.title: Collision Snapshot Guided Time-Reversed Safety-Critical Scenario Generation

author.name: Taehyung Kim, Jongeun Choi

entry.summary: COSTER generates safety-critical traffic scenarios for autonomous vehicle testing by first computing a collision snapshot and then using time-reversed planning with learned traffic dynamics to find plausible trajectories leading to it. This avoids the implausibility and diversity limits of trajectory-perturbation approaches.

entry.title: Power Mean Estimation in Stochastic Continuous Monte Carlo Tree Search

author.name: Tuan Dam

entry.summary: The paper proposes a novel MCTS algorithm for stochastic MDPs with continuous state-action spaces, using power mean estimation to obtain convergence guarantees where prior methods like HOOT and POLY-HOOT lacked theory. It extends MCTS convergence results to the stochastic continuous setting.

entry.title: Certifying cooperation: a novel approach to cooperative multi-agent task generation

author.name: Yannick Molinghen, Hugo Charels, Tom Lenaerts

entry.summary: Introduces temporal cooperation graphs and six provably complete cooperation profiles for the Laser Learning Environment, then encodes dynamics and profile predicates as propositional formulae to certify which multi-agent tasks admit cooperative solutions. This enables principled generation of cooperative tasks rather than ad hoc environment design.

entry.title: Constrained Online Learning with Noisy Constraint Values

author.name: Vaneet Aggarwal

entry.summary: Studies constrained online convex optimization with adversarial constraints under noisy feedback, proving a lower bound showing joint sublinear regret and violation is impossible with value noise. The authors propose LEDGER, an algorithm tracking net consumption in a nonnegative balance and setting constraint weights, which achieves guarantees in terms of budget violation over any window.

entry.title: LoGAN: Multilingual Font Localization with Generative Agents

author.name: Zhuoning Yuan, Ta-Ying Cheng, Benjamin Klein

entry.summary: LoGAN is a VLM-based agentic framework that localizes fonts and logos into new languages from only a few source glyphs, combining glyph-level diffusion, style finetuning, spacing/kerning transfer, and texture expansion. It moves beyond single-glyph generation to complete multilingual character sets, a task critical for typography and brand localization. The decomposition into coordinated generative components is the main technical contribution.

entry.title: Staying on the Attack Path: Structured State for Long-Horizon Automated Penetration Testing

author.name: Weizhe Wang, Yitong Zhang, Yao Zhang, Xiaoqiang Di, Zhigang Li, Bin Wu, Guangquan Xu

entry.summary: Intentest is an LLM agent for automated penetration testing that externalizes long-horizon state into a persistent fact-intent directed acyclic graph (DAG), countering context forgetting and intent drift during extended security tasks. On web application pentesting benchmarks it substantially reduces invalid transitions and aimless, repetitive exploration. This addresses a real limitation of LLM agents in multi-step cybersecurity workflows.

entry.title: Federated Binary Gating with Server-Side Vision-Language Inference for Surveillance Anomaly Classification

author.name: C\^ome-Alexis Puech, S\'ebastien Thuau, Amira Gran, Arthur Mennessier, Siba Haidar, Rachid Chelouah

entry.summary: This work proposes a hybrid two-stage architecture where a lightweight federated CNN gate performs local anomaly screening on privacy-sensitive surveillance video, forwarding only flagged clips to a server-side Qwen3-VL-8B for zero-shot classification into anomaly metaclasses. This addresses non-IID federated data instability for rare categories while limiting raw video transmission.

entry.title: We're Cooked! - Probing LLM Political Alignment Via Conflict-Framed Recipe Translation

author.name: Svetlana Gorovaia, Angelica Henestrosa, Ivan P. Yamshchikov

entry.summary: A fully crossed factorial study of 15,680 responses across 17 languages, four conflict-framing conditions, and eight LLMs from Western, Chinese, and European origins, testing whether politically charged framing terms like aggressor or coloniser trigger implicit political alignment in an otherwise neutral translation task. The authors find models resolve ambiguity by adopting implicit political positions rather than declining or clarifying.

entry.title: Quantifying the Engagement Trap: Impact of Short-form Video Recommender Systems on Users with ADHD

author.name: Vedad Misirlic, Gregor Mayr, Elisabeth Lex

entry.summary: A stratified study of 302 participants showing that short-form video recommenders disproportionately trap users with ADHD: recommendations feel similarly relevant across groups, but ADHD participants report significantly higher disengagement costs. Introduces and operationalizes the Engagement Trap concept for recommender-system harm analysis.

entry.title: AVCG: A Generalized Variational Framework for Counterfactual Generation under Hypothesis Distributions

author.name: Jamie Duell, Alejandro Jimenez Rodriguez, Mahault Albarracin

entry.summary: Proposes the Amortized Variational Counterfactual Generator, which formulates counterfactual explanation as optimization over a distribution of plausible model hypotheses rather than a single point-estimate predictor. This produces robust explanations that remain valid when the underlying model is retrained or updated.

entry.title: FPicker: Topology-Guided Evolution for Filament Tracing in Low-SNR Microscopy

author.name: Tingyin Zhao, Mingtao Huang, Yuan Shen

entry.summary: FPicker is a topology-guided framework for tracing filaments in cryo-electron microscopy at extremely low signal-to-noise ratios, unifying perception via a center-endpoint representation and an open-curve evolution module. It avoids failure modes of pixel-wise segmentation, box detection, sequential tracking, and active contours. Accurate tracing enables 3D helical reconstruction of biomolecules.

entry.title: Capsule Lens: Locating and Tracking Concept Geometry in Model Representations

author.name: Yiming Tang, Harshvardhan Saini, Samyak Jha, Huaming Chen, Xufeng Duan, Dianbo Liu

entry.summary: Introduces Capsule Lens, an interpretability framework that matches the region a concept occupies in representation space with a trackable capsule geometry defined by interpretable parameters, enabling direct characterization and dynamic tracking of concepts rather than static projection to interpretable spaces. Addresses a core mechanistic interpretability problem with rigorous geometric validation.

entry.title: LoGIC: Budgeted Context Construction for Node-Level Graph In-Context Learning with Tabular Foundation Models

author.name: Mingqi Yang, Zidong Guo, Jihui Yang, Wenming Zuo

entry.summary: LoGIC addresses scaling bottlenecks in tabular foundation models used as graph learners (e.g., G2T-FM, GraphPFN) by studying which labeled and unlabeled nodes should form the in-context prompt under budget constraints, avoiding quadratic attention scaling with the labeled pool. It formulates context construction as an allocation problem over labeled-context and unlabeled-halo budgets. This improves efficiency of a promising new paradigm for node-level prediction.

entry.title: Rethinking One-Shot Federated Graph Learning: Training-Free Statistical Estimation

author.name: Shutong Zheng, Sijia Chen

entry.summary: SPEAR reformulates one-shot federated graph learning as a statistical estimation problem, showing that local GNN training under extreme non-IID conditions causes cross-client representation misalignment. The training-free framework directly computes topology-smoothed client prototypes with adaptive reliability instead of training local models. The reframing is the notable contribution, replacing optimization with estimation in a single-round federated setting.

entry.title: EgoNeMo: Transferable Map of Pedestrian Dynamics via Egocentric LiDAR Scan

author.name: Azusa Sawada, Allan Wang, Hideo Saito, Aaron Steinfeld

entry.summary: EgoNeMo trains a continuous, LiDAR-based Map of Dynamics estimator that generalizes to unknown environments, removing the need to accumulate site-specific pedestrian trajectories at each new location. It uses neural implicit modeling with position-balanced sampling to handle sparse, temporally biased real-world trajectory data. Relevant to robot navigation and pedestrian trajectory prediction in deployment settings.

entry.title: Learning Adaptive SED for heterogeneous load balancing

author.name: Sanne van Kempen, Jaron Sanders, Fiona Sloothaak, Maarten G. Wolf

entry.summary: Proposes an online learning algorithm for routing in a two-server load balancing system with unknown heterogeneous service rates, combining empirical Shortest-Expected-Delay routing with forced exploration phases. Proves finite regret, contrasting with classic bandit results that imply infinite regret in this setting.

entry.title: Fine-grained Distributed Backdoor Attacks in Federated Learning

author.name: Jian Wang, Hong Shen, Wei Ke, Xue Hua Liu

entry.summary: Proposes FDBA, a fine-grained distributed backdoor attack framework for federated learning that uses dynamic trigger generation based on image edge structures and embedding vector optimization. This reduces the number of poisoned samples needed and evades robust aggregation defenses that detect fixed trigger patterns.

entry.title: Attributing Cohen's d: Training Data Attribution for Disease-Related Effects in Normative Age Biomarkers

author.name: Jakob Snel, Marc-Andre Schulz

entry.summary: The paper develops a closed-form influence function that attributes disease-related effect sizes in brain/biomarker age-gap models directly to individual training samples, validated against leave-one-out retraining on UK Biobank data across four diseases. Removing the most influential samples materially changes held-out case-control separation. This bridges training data attribution and epidemiological biomarker analysis in a clinically meaningful way.

entry.title: Geometry-Aware Bayesian Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning on the Stiefel Manifold via Stein Variational Gradient Descent

author.name: Quang-Duy Tran, Trung Le, Bao Duong, Phuoc Nguyen, Thin Nguyen

entry.summary: The paper develops a Bayesian treatment of geometry-aware low-rank adapters, transporting SVD-factorized adapter matrices over the Stiefel manifold using Stein variational gradient descent. This targets the overconfidence problem observed in deterministic orthogonality-constrained PEFT methods by producing posterior samples rather than point estimates. It matters because combining parameter-efficient fine-tuning with calibrated uncertainty is increasingly important for deployed large models.

entry.title: Physics-Informed Deep Learning for False Ventricular Tachycardia Alarm Reduction in the ICU

author.name: Athanasios Papastathopoulos-Katsaros, Alexandra Stavrianidi, Zhandong Liu

entry.summary: Combines a 1D SE-ResNet with ICU-realistic augmentations and a physics-informed auxiliary task based on the Windkessel hemodynamic model to suppress false ventricular tachycardia alarms. Under a strict real-time protocol on the VTaC benchmark, it improves the Challenge Score by roughly 5 points over prior state of the art.

entry.title: A Nuclear-Norm Lower Bound for Dithered Scalar Quantization of Matrix Products

author.name: Piyush Sao, Narasinga Miniskar, Pedro Valero-Lara, Keita Teranishi, Sudip Seal

entry.summary: Proves a lower bound on the expected leading squared error of quantized matrix multiplication under product-preserving basis changes and subtractive dither, showing error scales with the nuclear norm of the product. This gives a fundamental limit relevant to efficient low-precision linear algebra used in large-model serving.

entry.title: Physical policy gradient theorem for in situ stochastic-adjoint training

author.name: William Tuxbury, Zin Lin

entry.summary: Introduces a physical analogue of the policy gradient theorem: a stochastic-adjoint gradient estimator enabling in situ training of nonlinear photonic resonator systems beyond reciprocal constraints, using gradients extracted from measured stochastic trajectories alone. Demonstrated by training a resonator network against adversarial temporal modulations without finite differences.

entry.title: From Narrative to Auditable Forecasts: A Structured Scaffold for Agentic Forecasting

author.name: Yuanpu Cao, Yongkang Du, Yurui Chang, Lu Lin, Jinghui Chen

entry.summary: Proposes AuditForecast, an agentic scaffold replacing implicit narrative probability aggregation with a structured path: a quantitative baseline anchors a base probability, model-guided retrieval supplies evidence, and mechanistic situational updates are applied outside the model scope. Aims to improve both accuracy and auditability of LLM live forecasting.

entry.title: Causal DAG Identification for Count Data via Poisson Thinning Structural Equation Models

author.name: Penggang Gao, Ming Cai, Hisayuki Hara

entry.summary: This paper proposes the Poisson thinning structural equation model (PT-SEM), extending the Poisson branching structural causal model for count-valued data by replacing binomial thinning with Poisson thinning and allowing diverse count-distribution families for exogenous variables. Under node-wise regularity conditions, the authors establish full identifiability of the causal DAG from observational data, going beyond the partial identifiability of prior work. This is a meaningful theoretical advance for causal discovery on count data common in epidemiology, traffic, and network applications.

entry.title: Detect Anything in Graphic Design: Element-Level Rewards for Autoregressive Detection

author.name: Jiangning Zhu, Bowen Li, Shenyu Qiao, Yima Gu, Zhao Zhang, Yuhui Yuan, Shixia Liu

entry.summary: Presents DAD, a model that formulates graphic design element detection as compositional deconstruction, decoding elements in compositional order and using amodal detection to predict full bounding boxes of occluded elements. It exploits layered element order that standard object detectors ignore.

entry.title: The OCUDU dApp Platform: An Open Runtime and E3 Interface for Real-Time AI-RAN

author.name: Timothy O'Shea, Matthew Pennybacker, Andriy Kharchenko

entry.summary: Introduces an open runtime and E3 interface that lets independently built AI applications execute inside a production 5G distributed unit under strict timing contracts, moving beyond prior frameworks that only observed exported streams. This enables ML in the sub-10 ms control band for link adaptation, scheduling, and receiver processing.

entry.title: CoVeR: Coverage-Based Token Pruning for Multi-View 3D Reasoning in VLMs

author.name: Nhat-Tan Bui, Varshini Elangovan, Arun Reddy Anugu, Sreyas Mohan, Wei Ye, Dilin Wang, JQ Huang, Rakesh Ranjan, Aviral Chharia, Fernando De la Torre

entry.summary: CoVeR is a token-pruning method for multi-view 3D reasoning with vision-language models that enforces spatial coverage while respecting an exact token budget, overcoming the redundancy limits of learned-importance pruners and the budget saturation of voxelization approaches. This substantially reduces the visual token cost of multi-view VLM reasoning.

entry.title: Correction as Annotation: Bootstrapping a Dependency Parser for Documentary Medieval Latin

author.name: Gabriel H. Pizzorno (Harvard University)

entry.summary: Shows that all five available Latin treebank models perform poorly on 160 medieval Marseille inventories (best labeled attachment score 0.62, best morphology-aware score 0.24), then builds in-domain training data iteratively: a model pre-annotates sentences, an expert corrects them, and corrections train the next model across nine rounds. The approach turns necessary human correction work into reusable annotation, yielding a usable parser for an underserved historical language.

entry.title: TurEngMix: A Text Corpus and Benchmark for Turkish-English Code-Mixed Language Identification and Named Entity Recognition

author.name: Ilayda Dogan, Phuong-Anh Nguyen-Le, Julia Mendelsohn

entry.summary: TurEngMix introduces a 5.5K-post social media corpus (about 487K tokens) of naturally occurring Turkish-English code-mixing, with 15K expert-annotated tokens for language identification and NER benchmarks. Baselines including decoder LLMs and fine-tuned encoders handle monolingual tokens reliably but fail on mixed-language tokens, a distinctive challenge given Turkish suffixation of English stems. The resource exposes a concrete weakness of current multilingual NLP on code-mixed text.

entry.title: Marginal Fidelity Does Not Establish User Simulation in Demographic Synthetic Survey Panels: Response Contracts, Support Collapse and Conditioning Failure

author.name: Alexander Doudkin

entry.summary: Critically examines the common validation practice of matching aggregate answer marginals when using LLM-based synthetic survey panels, testing across multiselect batteries from four survey organisations in three countries. It finds the response contract dominates measured fidelity: committed answer sets leave 66 of 128 option slots empty even in panels of 500 respondents, versus 0 under per-option probability elicitation. This is a cautionary result for anyone using synthetic respondents to stand in for human survey data.

entry.title: SentryLine: Evidence-Grounded Question Answering over Evolving Documents in Oncology Care

author.name: Tampu Ravi Kumar, Gaurav Najpande, Muhammad Ali Khan, Kaneez Zahra Rubab Khakwani, Karan Kathuria, Shorya Azriel Moses, Yuvraj Kalia, M Bassam Sonbol, Irbaz Bin Riaz, Vivek Gupta

entry.summary: Presents a living-guideline-aware clinical QA system for oncology that retrieves passages via a vectorless hierarchical RAG pipeline and returns role-specific answers with inline citations, temporal verification, and guideline drift detection. It also contributes ASCOBENCH, a benchmark of 405 three-turn conversations grounded in versioned ASCO guideline documents.

entry.title: ReCite: Agentic Reasoning for Faithful Citation

author.name: Yuyang Huang, Bobo Li, Jiajia Song, Yuzhe Ding, Chong Teng, Fei Li, Donghong Ji

entry.summary: ReCite reframes citation recommendation from semantic-similarity retrieval to active, claim-level agentic reasoning, decoupling the process so the system verifies that candidate papers logically support an author's claim rather than merely resembling it. This addresses misattribution of real papers, a failure mode that retrieval-augmented systems still exhibit. It is relevant to trustworthy AI-assisted scientific writing.

entry.title: Do Depressive Facial Patterns Transfer Across Cultures and Contexts? Evidence from a German RCT and E-DAIC

author.name: Misha Sadeghi, Robert Richer, Lydia Helene Rupp, Lena Schindler-Gmelch, Marie Keinert, Farnaz Rahimi, Malin Hager, Bernhard Egger, Matthias Berking, Bjoern M. Eskofier

entry.summary: This systematic bidirectional transfer study tests whether facial behavioral markers of depression generalize between a German RCT (N=256, SCID-5-CV diagnoses) and the E-DAIC interview corpus (N=275), predicting severity and diagnostic status from action units, head pose, and gaze. Cross-corpus binary classification is more robust than continuous severity regression, with transfer governed by functional context.

entry.title: UniFusion: Sparse-View 4D Reconstruction via Unified Spatio-temporal Depth Alignment

author.name: Yongzhe Lyu, Shaofei Wang, Yixin Chen, Siyuan Huang

entry.summary: UniFusion addresses 4D reconstruction from sparse-view videos by jointly resolving cross-view and cross-time inconsistencies in monocular depth priors within a unified spatial-temporal alignment framework, rather than separate stages. It avoids dependence on foreground segmentation masks and leverages temporal cues for cross-view alignment.

entry.title: Efficient and Robust Camera-independent Multiview 3D Geometric Reconstruction from Noisy Monocular Depth Estimation and Multiple Point Matching

author.name: Marius Leordeanu

entry.summary: The author presents a 3D reconstruction method based on camera-independent linear relationships among points, learned as an auto-regression matrix W from cross-frame correspondences. The matrix is intrinsic to the point set and independent of camera pose, with principal eigenvectors providing a homogeneous representation. This offers a theoretically grounded, robust alternative to conventional multiview geometry pipelines.

entry.title: DualPathOcc: Dual-Resolution BEV Encoder for 3D Occupancy Prediction

author.name: Lihao Qiu, Jian Chen, Ruihao Wang, Ramu Gautam, Mei Yang, Yingtao Jiang

entry.summary: Introduces DualPathOcc, a camera-based 3D occupancy prediction framework with a spatial enhancer for high-resolution pre-compression features, a SENet-augmented dual-path BEV encoder, and height-aware weighted cross-entropy, reaching 37.37 mIoU on single-frame Occ3D-nuScenes. It also analyzes how surface-centered depth targets interact with volumetric occupancy learning.

entry.title: GAN-Blot: A Controllable Structure-Style Synthesis Benchmark for Western Blot Forensics

author.name: Hao-Chiang Shao, Fong-Yi Lin, Te-An Chien, TianYu Chen, Da-Jhong Chen

entry.summary: Presents GAN-Blot, a controllable synthesis framework and benchmark for Western blot images that decomposes images into structure and style factors, enabling realistic synthetic WB generation to advance forensic detection of fabricated biomedical imagery, an area motivated by rising research-integrity misconduct cases.

entry.title: AnomalyCraft-700K: Component-Level Controllable and Verifiable Synthetic Anomalies for Fine-Grained Video Anomaly Understanding

author.name: Yuzhou Long, Haodong Zhang, Yunpeng Yang, Peng Wu, Guansong Pang

entry.summary: AnomalyCraft-700K is a component-controllable synthetic anomaly dataset for fine-grained video anomaly understanding, containing over 40K videos and 700K task-level textual annotations generated through a progressive three-stage pipeline. It addresses limitations of real-world anomaly videos, which are hard to collect and hard to control, by providing component-level verification of video-text consistency and hard normal samples near the normal-anomaly boundary. This fills an important data gap for training and evaluating video anomaly models.

entry.title: Zero-Shot 3D Plant Organ Segmentation with SAM3 and Semantic NeRFs

author.name: Andreas Gilson, Laura Hennig, Peter Pietrzyk

entry.summary: The paper presents an annotation-free pipeline for 3D plant organ segmentation combining text-prompted SAM3 segmentation with semantic neural radiance fields, producing labeled 3D point clouds from multi-view RGB images and class names alone. NeRF multi-view fusion acts as an implicit consensus mechanism lifting imperfect per-frame masks, reaching 92.6% on a Begonia testbed.

entry.title: SynthGait-19K: A Physically Grounded Synthetic Video Dataset for Gait Parameter Estimation

author.name: Soroush Mehraban, Xin Lei Lin, Vida Adeli, Majid Mirmehdi, Amirhossein Dadashzadeh, Clint Hansen, Andrea Iaboni, Babak Taati

entry.summary: SynthGait-19K provides 19,272 synthetic walking videos derived from 6,427 MoCap sequences of 437 subjects via Gait2Vid, a pipeline unifying heterogeneous MoCap through SMPL with controllable viewpoints and scene appearances, annotated with six clinically meaningful gait parameters. It targets scalable monocular gait assessment for mobility monitoring in clinical settings.

entry.title: ReMoMask-2: Latent Retrieval-Augmented Masked Motion Generation

author.name: Yiran Wang, Zeyu Zhang, Ling Shao, Hao Tang

entry.summary: ReMoMask-2 improves retrieval-augmented text-to-motion generation by addressing coarse-grained retrieval and the representation gap between retrieved evidence and the generator latent space, using hierarchical bidirectional momentum contrastive learning and structure-aware alignment. Text-to-motion generation supports gaming, VR, and robotics applications. The paper targets the hierarchical spatio-temporal topology of human motion specifically.

entry.title: SeGDeP: Semantic- and Geometric-Aware Decoupled Prompts for Reasoning Segmentation

author.name: Linnan Zhao, Xu Liu, Lingling Li, Licheng Jiao, Fang Liu, Wenping Ma

entry.summary: SeGDeP introduces an explicit what-where interface for reasoning segmentation, decoupling a semantic prompt branch from an independent geometric projection path that jointly condition a SAM-class mask decoder, with training that first aligns the interface then applies group reward-decoupled post-training. This separation makes failures attributable to either target interpretation or spatial localization.

entry.title: Diagnosing and Dynamically Filtering Occupancy World Models for Active Mapping

author.name: Jiahui Zhang, Gongbo Liang, Yu Zhang

entry.summary: This paper diagnoses how errors in learned occupancy world models affect active mapping by holding the planner fixed and varying only the occupancy representation, comparing no completion, learned, oracle-corrected, and ground-truth conditions. It finds occupancy errors can distort both exploration targets and feasible motion. The analysis motivates dynamic filtering of predicted occupancy before planning.

entry.title: \textbf{PLATO}: \emph{Preintegration Learning from Accurate Trajectory Observations} for Neural Inertial Odometry

author.name: Haoying Li, Qihang Liu, Yifan Peng, Keyan Miao, Junfeng Wu

entry.summary: PLATO is a likelihood-based framework for neural inertial odometry that jointly learns IMU bias dynamics via a neural ODE and gyroscope/accelerometer noise covariances from accurate trajectory observations. It exploits sparse negative log-likelihood structure with forward differentiation and a tailored double-adjoint scheme coupling invariant-error adjoint methods. This targets the sensitivity of inertial-only preintegration to bias and uncertainty in challenging environments.

entry.title: EquiGQNet: Fast Grasp Quality Evaluation via Shared Equivariant Point Cloud Encoding

author.name: Sungwon Seo, Jaeseog Won, Jiyou Shin, Youngjin Seo, Hyunjun Kim, Seokmin Yoon, Tuan Luong, Hyungpil Moon

entry.summary: EquiGQNet is a 6-DoF grasp quality evaluator that encodes a cluttered scene once with an SO(3)-equivariant encoder and then rotates the shared representation per grasp candidate, combining the local geometric sensitivity of early fusion with the efficiency of late fusion. This enables fast, accurate grasp evaluation for unseen objects from a single-view depth image. The encode-once-then-rotate scheme is a clean use of equivariance for computational efficiency.

entry.title: SPOT: Spatial Perception-Oriented Long-Horizon Humanoid Teleoperation

author.name: Lixing Fang, Ziyan Xiong, Sunli Chen, Zhiyang Dou, Chuang Gan

entry.summary: SPOT is a humanoid teleoperation system that maintains the operator's perceptual horizon during long-horizon loco-manipulation, addressing failures like narrow views, unstable robot-mounted cameras, and coupled head-view control. It lets operators preserve spatial awareness of objects, environment, and robot pose over time, improving demonstration data quality for humanoid training. High-quality demonstration data is framed as the central bottleneck for general-purpose humanoids.

entry.title: Bridging Language and Physics: Automated Design of Continuum Robots with Large Language Models

author.name: Jingyi Chen, Mohan Zhang, Laura Yao, Yingtai Ni, Jianmin Ji, Jie Peng, Song Wang, Tianlong Chen

entry.summary: AID-SR is a multi-layered framework for LLM-driven design of continuum robots that closes the loop between language-based reasoning and physical consequences by translating simulator-observed states into structured feedback for the LLM designer. It combines semantic critique, human feedback, and iterative refinement to produce physically feasible, functionally meaningful designs. The work targets low physical validity in LLM-based robot design.

entry.title: Graph-Based Safe Reinforcement Learning for Multi-Agent Systems with Time-Varying Topology

author.name: Xiao Sizhe, Dong Lijing, Bai Rui, Tan Xin

entry.summary: The paper presents a graph-based safe multi-agent RL framework for cooperative navigation with a Control Barrier-Like Function action screening layer that guarantees physical safety regardless of learning progress. It combines an attention-based actor with a GAT centralized critic under time-varying communication topology. Bridging discrete LiDAR perception and continuous safety constraints is the key technical contribution.

entry.title: Avoiding steering awareness by optimizing steering parameters

author.name: Tomás Gimenez Molina

entry.summary: Motivated by evidence that models can detect when activation steering is applied to them, this post presents a prototype tool for optimizing steering parameters (e.g., vector strength) to find operating windows where steering remains effective while detection frequency is minimized. The author argues detection-awareness threatens the validity of safety evaluations that use steering, and that the effectiveness-detection tradeoff is heavily model- and concept-dependent. A GitHub repository accompanies the work.

entry.title: FastE: Readout-Triggered Token Compression for LLM Embedding Inference

author.name: Jinsong Shu, Jinyong Wen, Baokun Wang, Zhongle Xie, Lidan Shou, Weiqiang Wang, Gang Chen

entry.summary: Identifies depth-dependent prefix redundancy in final-readout LLM embedding models such as Qwen3-Embedding and Qwen3-VL-Embedding, showing prefix states become increasingly compressible at greater depth. It introduces FastE, a training-free, plug-and-play method that uses readout-prefix attention alignment to decide when to compress and which prefix tokens to drop during embedding inference.

entry.title: Solving versus Verifying: Catching Contradictions in Tax Reasoning Systems

author.name: Albert Sadowski, Jaros{\l}aw A. Chudziak

entry.summary: This paper studies LLM behavior on defective tax-law inputs - missing or contradictory facts - where clean-benchmark accuracy above 90% says little. It asks whether models asked to solve a case abstain on defective inputs, and whether the same model can catch defects when asked to verify instead, probing the solve-versus-verify gap in a legally consequential domain.

entry.title: Parser-Free VLM Verification for Federated Weakly Supervised Video Anomaly Detection

author.name: S\'ebastien Thuau, Amira Gran, Siba Haidar, Rachid Chelouah

entry.summary: This paper presents a lightweight federated MIL-VLM cascade in which only a compact MIL scorer is trained across clients, while a frozen VLM verifies high-scoring suspect segments post hoc for weakly supervised video anomaly detection. It compares parsed text-generation decisions against a logit-based interface extracting continuous anomaly scores from next-token Yes/No probabilities, using InternVL3.5-2B and Qwen3-VL-2B on UCF-Crime.

entry.title: Accuracy is Not Enough: A Divergence-Based Approach to Evaluate Fidelity Loss in Quantized LLMs

author.name: Shahzeb Qamar, Lorenz Sparrenberg, Christian Bauckhage, Baha Rababah, Carson Leung, Murat Kantarcioglu, Cuneyt Gurcan Akcora, Rafet Sifa

entry.summary: The paper shows that zero-shot accuracy is an unstable, non-monotonic and potentially misleading metric for post-training quantization of LLMs, masking substantial fidelity loss relative to BF16 baselines. It introduces a distribution-sensitive evaluation framework measuring divergence between full-vocabulary predictive distributions at the token level.

entry.title: Dual-Layer Semantic-Spatial Belief Mapping for Aerial Object Goal Navigation

author.name: Jianqiang Xiao, Xiang Deng, Yuexuan Sun, Yanjin Wu, Wenbiao Yan, Liqiang Nie

entry.summary: Proposes AeroBelief, a framework converting noisy, transient VLM observations into persistent spatial guidance for UAV object-goal navigation via a dual-layer belief map separating contextual plausibility from target-specific evidence. Addresses real limitations of frame-level VLM outputs in outdoor aerial navigation.

entry.title: Learning Length-Extrapolatable Recurrent Models

author.name: Hanwen Jiang

entry.summary: Studies why BPTT-trained recurrent models fail beyond their training horizon, arguing the key issue is state credit rather than gradient decay alone. It proposes Credit Stabilization through Time (CST), a backward-pass rescaling of the state-credit signal that stabilizes training and improves length extrapolation of recurrent models.

entry.title: The Exact Time-Uniform Rate Frontier for Stochastic Gradient Descent on Smooth Convex Objectives

author.name: Ruijie Li, Kang Chen, Tianyu Wang

entry.summary: The authors characterize the exact time-uniform convergence rate of raw SGD iterates on smooth convex objectives, showing the rate approaches but never reaches sqrt(log n / n). They give a necessary-and-sufficient condition on achievable bound sequences via a dyadic horizon-free schedule and a lower-bound argument.

entry.title: SPARROW: Scalable Taxonomy Induction via Structure-Preserving Partitioning and Constraint-Guided Merging

author.name: Yirui Zhang, Yixuan Tang, Yandong Sun, Mong-Li Lee, Anthony Kum Hoe Tung

entry.summary: Addresses the degradation of LLM-based taxonomy induction as concept sets grow by adopting a divide-and-merge paradigm that partitions concepts, induces local taxonomies, and merges them into a global hierarchy. It identifies two structural failure modes of this paradigm, Structural Fragmentation and Parent Displacement, and proposes structure-preserving partitioning with constraint-guided merging to counter them. This improves scalability of a task relevant to knowledge organization.

entry.title: MolParser-Mobile: Ultrafast OCSR System for Large-Scale Chemical Literature Mining

author.name: Xi Fang, Haocheng Lu, Han Lyu, Chengxiang Luo, Linfeng Zhang, Guolin Ke

entry.summary: MolParser-Mobile is an AutoML-optimized, end-to-end optical chemical structure recognition system with only about 10 million parameters that achieves a throughput of 1,520 molecules per second on a single RTX 4090D while maintaining competitive or superior recognition accuracy on several benchmarks. It targets web-scale chemical literature mining where inference throughput is the bottleneck.

entry.title: BEFORE THE FLIP: Measuring Hidden Score Shifts In Quantized Vision Language Models Before The Answer Changes for Visual Question Answering

author.name: Sourajit Saha, Shubhashis Roy Dipta, Shaswati Saha, Nobin Sarwar, Yuxuan Jiang

entry.summary: BEFORE THE FLIP measures hidden degradation in quantized VLMs where VQA answers remain unchanged but underlying score margins shrink, comparing compression-induced score changes against those from replacing image tokens with a fixed average token. By selectively increasing the precision of one weight group at a time, the method identifies where extra bits help most. This provides a finer-grained reliability lens than answer-match evaluation for efficient VLM deployment.

entry.title: SupGRPO: Enhancing GRPO with Matching-based Online SFT for Text Spotting

author.name: Xudong Xie, Yuzhe Li, Jing Shi, Zhifei Zhang, Curtis Wigington, Zhaowen Wang

entry.summary: The paper studies MLLM-based fine-tuning for text spotting, finding that SFT is more effective than GRPO for localization while GRPO is more effective than SFT for recognition, and proposes SupGRPO, which augments GRPO with matching-based online supervised fine-tuning to get the best of both. The work equips text spotters with strong MLLM recognition while maximizing localization precision, including on complex or artistic text. The complementary finding about SFT versus RL is itself informative for the broader vision community.

entry.title: PGP-Clinical-TimeKAN: Prior-Guided Joint Probabilistic Forecasting of Clinical Trajectories

author.name: Weizhi Nie, Rihao Chang, Weijie Wang, Yuting Su

entry.summary: This paper presents a trajectory-first framework for joint probabilistic forecasting of multivariate physiological signals, combining missingness-aware encoders, organ-system priors, Kolmogorov-Arnold message passing, and a low-rank Student-t head. On a frozen MIMIC-IV-derived cohort of 6,882 patients, it achieves the second-lowest normalized MAE and lowest RMSE across five seeds and 13 comparison models for six-hour deterioration forecasts.

entry.title: Deep belief networks are exact

author.name: Gleb Smirnov

entry.summary: A theory paper proving that every strictly positive probability distribution on binary vectors is represented exactly by a sigmoid belief network with finite parameters, resolving a question posed by Sutskever and Hinton. The proof upgrades prior probability-sharing approximation results to exact representation using Brouwer's fixed-point theorem.

entry.title: Distilling Vision-Language Models for On-Device Fire Understanding

author.name: Mohammad Kazzazi, Zixuan Liu, Siavash Khajavi

entry.summary: The authors present a teacher-student knowledge distillation framework that compresses large, fire-fine-tuned vision-language models into lightweight students capable of running fully on embedded fire sensors while preserving safety-critical understanding. Experiments across multiple VLM families and scales show compact students retain most of the teachers' fire-understanding capability.

entry.title: Evidence-Aligned Local Composition of Discrete Experts for Sequence Restoration

author.name: Mohammad Panahazari, Usman A. Khan, Shuchin Aeron

entry.summary: The paper introduces a test-time method for restoring corrupted documents composed of multiple domains (e.g., prose, code, config) using frozen domain experts without a trained router or region labels. It infers position-wise soft weights over experts from the marginal evidence of the corrupted observation under a corruption model, estimated from experts' denoising losses. This is relevant to modular AI systems where routing must happen without extra training.

entry.title: Beyond Final Decisions: A Process-Centric Benchmark for Transparent AI-Assisted Peer Review

author.name: Siming Yuan, Xueyi Zhang, Wangze Ni, Tianfang Xiao, Shimin Di, Jia Zhu, Zhuoren Jiang, Rong Tan, Lei Chen, Kui Ren

entry.summary: This work introduces a process-centric diagnostic benchmark for AI-assisted peer review that evaluates whether model decisions are supported by intermediate summaries, critiques, and suggestions rather than only final accept/reject accuracy. It converts heterogeneous review records from PeerRead, NLPeer ARR-22, and OpenReview-ICLR into process-aligned data with decision prediction as the baseline.

entry.title: MVFA: A Multi-View Text-Guided Multimodal Fusion LLM Adapter for Sentiment Analysis and Emotion Recognition

author.name: Pengfei Shao, Jisheng Dang, Jiawen Fang, Ning Liu, Wencan Zhang, Bimei Wang, Jingwen Zhao, Jianhuang Lai, Qi Tian, Tat-Seng Chua

entry.summary: Introduces MVFA, a parameter-efficient adapter that augments frozen LLMs for multimodal sentiment analysis and emotion recognition by constructing complementary text views and preserving textual cues during cross-modal fusion of text, audio, and video. Addresses the cost of full fine-tuning while retaining rich language information. Includes strong co-authorship from senior multimodal researchers.

entry.title: Beyond One-Shot Expansion: Contrastive Evidence Exploration for Multi-Hop Retrieval

author.name: JungMin Yun, YoungBin Kim

entry.summary: A training-free multi-hop retrieval framework for RAG that replaces single-intent, one-shot query expansion with iterative evidence-conditioned exploration, passage-specific contrastive refinement, and coverage-aware selection, adapting to newly retrieved evidence at each hop. Multi-hop question answering is a known failure mode of standard RAG pipelines.

entry.title: A Hierarchical Consistency Framework for Auditing Retrieval-Augmented Generation Systems

author.name: Ramon Gonzalez, Antonio Diaz

entry.summary: Introduces the Hierarchical Consistency Framework, a post-hoc, model-agnostic audit that checks consistency at three levels of a RAG pipeline: the knowledge corpus, the retrieved context, and the generated answer. By representing corpus conflicts as source-linked atomic facts and producing an Answer Consistency Score with explanations, it surfaces contradictions that answer-only review and relevance scores miss.

entry.title: CIT-CAD: Constraint Intent Tree-based CAD Code Generation and Verification

author.name: Yali Du, Hui Sun, San-Zhuo Xi, Ming Li

entry.summary: Proposes CI... a Constraint Intent Tree representation for LLM-based CAD code generation that makes design intent explicit, enabling verification of construction processes (part decomposition, Boolean operations, sketch structure) rather than only final geometry via IoU. This addresses a real gap where geometric match metrics miss structural errors in generated parametric programs.

entry.title: Understanding the Impact of Model Pruning on Long-Tail Forgetting and Explanation Reliability in Medical Imaging

author.name: Nazish Khalid, Tausifa Jan Saleem, Amal Saqib, Donald C. Wunsch II, Mohammad Yaqub

entry.summary: A systematic study of how pruning affects long-tail forgetting and explanation reliability in medical imaging, spanning two datasets, two CNN architectures, four pruning methods, and sparsity up to 95 percent. It evaluates rare-condition performance and explanation stability, both clinically critical but usually ignored in compression work.

entry.title: Support Topology and Gradient Mixing in Sinkhorn Layers

author.name: Dylan Forde

entry.summary: Develops a theoretical calculus for how the fixed support graph in sparse Sinkhorn (optimal transport) layers controls gradient propagation through the scaling iterations. The paper derives operators for reverse-mode cotangent propagation, uses Dobrushin contraction to bound tail gradients, and characterizes when the support graph causes gradient mixing. Relevant for training sparsified attention or transport-based layers in transformer-style models.

entry.title: A Better Spur Should Start From Each Objective

author.name: Shanwen Mao, Hao Zhang, Guangtao nie, Zhiheng Li, Huimu Wang, Sulong Xu, Gu Simiu

entry.summary: Introduces Multi-Marginal Preference Optimization (MMPO), a multi-objective RL framework that intervenes at the data, gradient, and constraint levels to handle sparse rewards, reward conflicts, and late-stage metric oscillation that plague linear scalarization. Techniques include exposure debiasing, priority-aware orthogonal gradient projection, and self-prompted gradient constraints, apparently targeting industrial recommendation/ranking settings.

entry.title: MemForest: Efficient Agent Memory Management via EventTree Partitioning and Progressive Merging

author.name: Junxi Wang, Te Sun, Jiayi Zhu, Chen Zhang, Siyuan Li, Xuyang Liu, Zichen Wen, Xiaobing Tu, Jinkui Ren, Xiantao Zhang, Ziqi Yuan, Linfeng Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes MemForest, a general memory compression framework for agent memory systems that partitions history into event-centric units using semantic similarity and temporal continuity, builds maximum spanning trees (EventTrees) per unit, and progressively merges redundant nodes to reduce storage and retrieval cost. It is designed to be adaptable across existing agent memory systems.

entry.title: Answer-Distribution Trajectories: A Stochastic-Dynamics View of LLM Reasoning

author.name: Mar Gonz\`alez I Catal\`a, Haitz S\'aez de Oc\'ariz Borde, Davide Murari, Carola-Bibiane Sch\"onlieb, Pietro Li\`o, George Monta\~nez

entry.summary: This paper introduces answer-distribution trajectories, a representation that tracks the model's full predictive distribution over candidate answers as chain-of-thought reasoning unfolds, going beyond endpoint accuracy and entropy profiles by revealing which competing hypotheses account for uncertainty over time. This finer-grained view enables characterizing reasoning traces through a stochastic-dynamics lens. It matters for reasoning interpretability and for diagnostics that go beyond right-or-wrong answer evaluation.

entry.title: MeClear: Cooperative Game-Theoretic Attribution and Risk-Aware Memory Clearance for Long-Horizon LLM Agents

author.name: Boyu Yang, Jiazheng Sun, Zilong Lu, Zhi Qiu, Xin Peng, Jun Zheng

entry.summary: MeClear is a task-conditioned framework for clearing harmful memories from long-horizon LLM agents, using Leave-One-Out screening combined with sampled cooperative Shapley attribution to identify evidence with negative downstream utility. It selectively suppresses outdated, misleading, or conflicting memories from agent context. The approach addresses the problem that semantic retrieval optimizes compatibility rather than utility.

entry.title: TamilEOT: A Dataset and Model for Semantic End-of-Turn Detection in Tamil Telephone Speech

author.name: Santhoshkumar V

entry.summary: The authors release TamilEOT, a dataset of 18,485 labeled turn boundaries from 116 real Tamil telephone conversations, plus two compact audio-only end-of-turn detectors fine-tuned from Smart Turn v3. Accuracy improves from 70.3 percent zero-shot to 86.1 percent, with both models running under 150 ms on a laptop CPU. This fills a notable gap in conversational voice-agent research for South Indian languages.

entry.title: Versioned Transitive Dependency-Closure Binding and Operation-Time Effect Governance for Agent Skills: ClosureBound

author.name: Genliang Zhu (Accentrust, Georgia Institute of Technology), Chu Wang (Accentrust, University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign)

entry.summary: ClosureBound is a reference monitor for agent skills that prevents authorization transfer across material changes to a skill's heterogeneous dependency closure (files, packages, tools, models, services). It commits typed graph nodes and topology, binds grants to exact closure roots with effect ceilings and provenance, and re-resolves the closure at operation time, admitting external effects only when a joint witness satisfies every bound.

entry.title: What Does Animal Re-Identification Learn? Linear Biological Concepts and Their Origins in Visual Representations

author.name: Robert Nolting, Alexandra Schild, Moritz Weckbecker, Maximilian Schall, Gerard de Melo

entry.summary: Investigates whether ViT-based animal re-identification models organize representations along biologically meaningful axes, finding that sex and age emerge as linear directions in a DINOv3 backbone fine-tuned for gorilla Re-ID, with strong generalization to held-out individuals. This has implications for understanding and auditing conservation models.

entry.title: Linear Algebra Foundations of Efficient Attention: A Phase Reversal in Rank Collapse Under SVD Compression

author.name: Anjaneya Teja Sarma Kalvakolanu

entry.summary: This paper unifies fourteen peer-reviewed works on the linear-algebraic properties of transformer attention, covering rank collapse of attention outputs, SVD-based compression exploiting that phenomenon, and the duality between low-rank KV cache projection, linear attention, and state-space models. A synthesis of this kind is valuable for researchers navigating the fast-growing efficient-attention literature. The claim of identifying a phase reversal in rank collapse under compression adds an original analytical thread.

entry.title: Parameterized and Streaming Algorithms for Euclidean Fair $k$-Center Clustering

author.name: Zeyu Lin, Chaoqi Jia, Longkun Guo, Chao Chen

entry.summary: This theoretical work develops a parameterized 2.732-approximation algorithm for fair k-center clustering in Euclidean spaces, where centers are constrained across demographic groups, and integrates it into a one-pass streaming algorithm. It advances the algorithmic foundations of fairness-aware clustering.

entry.title: Reading Decoder Trajectories: Training-Free Counterfactual Query-Trajectory Reliability for Small-Object Detection

author.name: Zhaoning Shi, Bo Ma

entry.summary: Proposes CQTR, a training-free framework for small-object detection that hypothesizes small-object knowledge already exists in frozen detectors and elicits it via counterfactual scale interventions while interpreting query trajectories for candidate reliability. This challenges the dominant assumption that frozen models require architecture changes or finetuning to handle small objects.

entry.title: Characterizing Contention-Induced Reliability Collapse in KV-Cache Timing Side Channels for Multi-Tenant LLM Serving

author.name: Rana Abu Bakar

entry.summary: This work empirically studies how reliable KV-cache timing side-channel attacks remain under realistic multi-tenant contention in shared LLM serving systems. Through seven experiments on live vLLM deployments, it shows that attack effect sizes (Cohen's d) collapse sharply with even a small number of concurrent workers, tempering prior feasibility claims. The findings are important for realistic threat modeling of LLM infrastructure security.

entry.title: Train Overcomplete, Deploy Compact: Scaling Recovery Capacity for Structured LLM Pruning

author.name: Seungmin Oh, Donggeon Lee, Jongbin Ryu

entry.summary: Identifies a capacity-knowledge asymmetry bottleneck in structured LLM pruning recovery and proposes OverRep, which temporarily overparameterizes the recovery module during training to absorb distilled knowledge, then collapses it for a compact deployment artifact. This follows a train-overcomplete, deploy-compact principle.

entry.title: ARNAI: Artifact Removal Network based on Autoencoding and Inpainting for Robust Spinal Image Segmentation and Measurement

author.name: Sang-Jin Park, Jinyoung Choi, Seokwon Kim, Seungeon Song, Insu Park, Dougho Park, Taeyeon Kim, Youjin Lee, Donghoon Yang, Jaeman Cho, Joongwon Yang, Mansu Kim, Heumdai Kwon, Hong Gyu Baek, Dae Chul Cho, Injung Kim

entry.summary: ARNAI presents a Restore-Segment-Measure framework that removes spinal implant artifacts from postoperative radiographs via an autoencoding-and-inpainting network, enabling automated spinopelvic parameter measurement. Validated retrospectively on radiographs from two institutions spanning 2017-2025, it addresses a real clinical gap since postoperative images are usually excluded from automated analysis. This could extend AI-assisted spinal assessment to surgical follow-up care.

entry.title: Tensor network representations of discrete maximum entropy distributions via mean polytopes

author.name: Alex Goessmann, Martin Eigel

entry.summary: The paper introduces Computation-Activation Networks, a tensor network architecture subsuming exponential families, and proves that any discrete maximum entropy distribution under expectation constraints admits a representation in this architecture by exploiting the geometry of the mean polytope. It connects polytope faces to support boundaries of exponential families and proposes tensor ranks as complexity measures. This is a substantive theoretical bridge between information geometry and tensor networks.

entry.title: Mathematical Programming in Machine Learning and Artificial Intelligence: A Unified Taxonomy of Models and Applications

author.name: Chaosheng Dong

entry.summary: A survey that unifies fragmented applications of mathematical programming across ML and AI - retrieval selection, token routing, inference compute allocation, structured prediction, robustness - under common optimization paradigms (linear, mixed-integer, conic, bilevel, submodular, min-max, etc.). It serves as a reference taxonomy connecting optimization, IR, NLP, and vision literatures.

entry.title: D3ARC: Time-Critical Distributed Disaster Detection for Asynchronous Cooperative Multi-Robot Systems

author.name: Nikolaos Koursioumpas, Lina Magoula, Nancy Alonistioti, Ramin Khalili

entry.summary: This paper proposes D3ARC, an asynchronous distributed hierarchical framework in which multiple robotic agents cooperate to detect wildfires under uncertainty. A remote controller asynchronously directs robot motion while each agent senses the environment and coordinates detection actions, addressing coverage, cost, and personnel-risk limitations of traditional disaster monitoring.

entry.title: Topology Obstructs Pure Foundation Neural Quantum States

author.name: Timothy Heightman, Elena Orlova, Philip Mantrov, Aleksei Ustimenko

entry.summary: The paper proves a fundamental limitation for pure-state foundation models of quantum ground states: for any gapped Hamiltonian family with a non-trivial ground-state bundle, every continuous normalized state-vector model has zero fidelity with the true ground state at some parameter value, incurring an O(gap) energy error. This is a topological no-go result for a growing class of neural-network approaches to quantum many-body problems.

entry.title: Your Agent Says Yes: Interpreting Adversarial Market Behavior Beyond Individual Transactions

author.name: Zelin Li, Yiyun Su, Matt White, Zhipeng Wang, Xiao-Yang Liu, Tianyu Shi

entry.summary: The study populates a virtual exchange with ten role-conditioned language-model agents that communicate, trade, launch tokens, and manage liquidity pools under adversarial roles, then analyzes eight 72-cycle trajectories to interpret market-level behavior beyond individual transaction controls. A focal reconstruction shows a launch-promotion-exit scenario, illustrating how per-transaction compliance misses distributed manipulative behavior.

entry.title: Climate-ModernBERT: Revisiting Corpus Composition for Domain-Adaptive Continued Pretraining

author.name: Yongan Yu, Shantam Raj, Jingwei Ni, Ario Saeid Vaghefi, Dominik Stammbach, Markus Leippold

entry.summary: Presents a family of climate-adapted encoder models via continued pretraining of ModernBERT-Base on academic, web-filtered, and synthetic climate corpora, systematically comparing corpus mixtures against parameter-space merging of specialized checkpoints. Best models improve across nine climate NLP benchmarks.

entry.title: DISEIL: Demonstration Distillation for Sample-Efficient Imitation Learning

author.name: Suyog Khanal, Arun Kumar A V, Santu Rana

entry.summary: Proposes DISEIL for interactive imitation learning, making two previously incidental decisions deliberate: which failure to correct and where a requested demonstration should start, by detecting the step where the policy first becomes unreliable. Aims to reduce the number of expert queries a robot needs to learn new tasks.

entry.title: A Measurement Study of LLM Inference Trade-offs Across Edge Continuum Hardware

author.name: Maysam Khatib, Moysis Symeonides, Demetris Trihinas, George Pallis, Marios D. Dikaiakos

entry.summary: This measurement study benchmarks self-hosted LLM inference on edge hardware (Jetson AGX Orin, CPU-only and GPU near-edge server) versus GPT-4o as a cloud reference, across multiple open-weight models and quantization variants on a fixed QA workload. It reports accuracy, footprint, per-token latency, prefill latency, and energy. The results guide deployment choices for LLM-backed services at the edge.

entry.title: Adaptive Anisotropic Attention for Axis-Structured Signals

author.name: Mahir Jain, Parshva Runwal, Aditya Ray Mishra, Arvasu Kulkarni, Sandeep Singh, Siddharth Panwar

entry.summary: The paper proposes Adaptive Anisotropic Attention (AAA), an attention variant that replaces the uniform isotropic prior of dense self-attention with two structured paths for axis-organized signals: a temporal path attending within an electrode across time and a spatial path attending across electrodes at the same time step, combined via a learned per-token gate. It targets low-SNR structured data such as EEG, where standard attention wastes capacity on irrelevant token interactions. The contribution is an architecture-level efficiency and inductive-bias improvement for structured signals rather than language models.

entry.title: ThinkPrior: Zero-Rollout Difficulty Priors for Cold-Start Prompt Selection in RLVR

author.name: Tommy Sha, Skylar Zhai, Siqi Zhao

entry.summary: Targets wasted rollouts in RLVR training with GRPO, where uniform prompt sampling spends about 39% of rollouts on zero-advantage groups that provide no gradient. ThinkPrior builds a zero-rollout difficulty prior from an external verifier-scored anchor in one offline pass, eliminating the cold-start cost of history-based prompt selection. A focused efficiency improvement for reasoning-model RL training.

entry.title: A Multi-Source Ensemble Approach to Candidate Generation for Alternative Vacation Rental Property Recommendations

author.name: Syed Mohammed Arshad Zaidi, Eric Rincon, Shayan Hassantabar

entry.summary: This paper studies candidate generation for alternative vacation rental recommendations at scale, comparing collaborative filtering, shallow embeddings, and graph neural networks on a platform with over 2M active properties. It shows a hybrid of item-based CF with GNN retrieval performs best under challenges like heterogeneous inventory and rapid availability changes. It matters as a practical, large-scale recommender systems case study from industry researchers.

entry.title: CALM: Class-wise Agreement and Label-gated Disagreement Modulation for Decentralized Federated Learning

author.name: Yifan Ying, Qing Tian

entry.summary: CALM improves decentralized federated distillation under severe non-IID data by replacing hard all-or-nothing trust decisions about teacher predictions with soft, class-wise agreement modulation and label-gated disagreement handling. This avoids discarding outlier teachers wholesale and better weights aggregated teacher targets. It is relevant to serverless, privacy-conscious distributed learning without shared architectures.

entry.title: Interpretable and Fair Generalized Additive Neural Networks via Multi-objective Learning

author.name: Ziming Wang, Changwu Huang, Ke Tang, Yew-Soon Ong, Xin Yao

entry.summary: The paper introduces explicit quantitative metrics for interpretability of neural-network-based generalized additive models (GAMs) and jointly optimizes interpretability alongside fairness and accuracy via multi-objective learning. This addresses an underexplored gap, as most NN-GAM research has focused on accuracy. The work contributes to trustworthy AI by making interpretability measurable and optimizable.

entry.title: Learning to Price and Stock Under Contextual and Censored Demand

author.name: Zean Han, Zezhen Ding, Jiheng Zhang

entry.summary: This paper tackles joint pricing and inventory control when demand depends on contextual factors and is censored by lost sales, meaning true demand is unobserved when stock runs out. The authors model demand as a linear combination of basis functions and propose an algorithm with sublinear regret bounds for adaptive decisions. It matters for retail operations research where lost-sales censoring has historically forced practitioners to choose between contextual awareness and demand observability.

entry.title: Spectral Prioritized Sweeping in Nonstationary Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Hung Pham, Tuan Dam

entry.summary: The paper improves Prioritized Sweeping for nonstationary reward settings by augmenting Bellman-residual priorities with graph-topology information via the graph resolvent, so that updates propagate to topologically distant or bottlenecked states even under limited replanning budgets. GTA-PS/SPS is presented as a drop-in enhancement to model-based RL planning. It addresses a real shortsightedness of canonical priority scores after localized reward shifts.

entry.title: Structural Entropy-Driven Graph Diffusion Generation for One-Shot Federated Graph Learning

author.name: Shutong Zheng, Lele Fu, Sheng Huang, Wei Yang Bryan Lim, Chuan Chen

entry.summary: SPIRE introduces topology-aware client weighting into one-shot federated graph learning using first-order degree-distribution structural entropy, capturing how client connectivity is organized beyond raw data volume, combined with a server-side graph diffusion model for generation. It addresses the problem of estimating client contributions from highly compressed information in a single round. Note it shares first author and topic with SPEAR (item 7), indicating a research line on one-shot FGL.

entry.title: Train Smarter, Not Harder: Switching Signal-Guided Training in Active Learning

author.name: Nagham Omar, Maya Rozenshtein, Evgeny Mishlyakov, Avigdor Gal

entry.summary: Shows that the choice between retraining from scratch and fine-tuning in active learning has exploitable structure and proposes HybridAL, which monitors an online stabilization signal (spectral exponent or accuracy change) to switch from retraining to fine-tuning. Reduces training cost without sacrificing accuracy.

entry.title: Conditioned Initialization for Attention

author.name: Hemanth Saratchandran, Simon Lucey

entry.summary: Examines an underexplored factor in transformer training: initialization of the query, key, and value matrices. The authors show that naive random initialization can introduce optimization pathologies and propose a conditioned initialization scheme that improves training dynamics relative to random and mimetic initialization.

entry.title: Inferring Urban Mobility Interactions from Aggregated Dynamics

author.name: Yi Wang, Jing Li, Jinliang Deng, Zhenghong Wang, Yizhi Zhang, Fan Zhang, Ivor W. Tsang, Yu Liu

entry.summary: Shows that origin-destination flow matrices, normally requiring privacy-invasive individual tracking, can be reconstructed from aggregated area-level counts using an uncertainty-aware physics-informed framework. Validated across twelve mobility datasets from US and Chinese cities with accuracy comparable to trajectory-based models.

entry.title: MetaKV: Adaptive KV Cache Compression for Constrained LLM Inference

author.name: Michael Wang, Keith Li, Roozbeh Bostandoost

entry.summary: MetaKV adaptively selects a KV cache compression configuration per prompt under user-specified latency and memory budgets, using lightweight predictors of end-to-end latency, peak memory, and correctness probability. It addresses the fact that no single compression setting works across prompts and constraints. Directly relevant to efficient long-context LLM serving.

entry.title: SIM: Subspace Interaction-based Method for Token-Level Text Anomaly Detection

author.name: Kehan Yan, Yue Tan, Qingfeng Chen, Shiyuan Li, Yu Zheng, Yixin Liu

entry.summary: Presents SIM, a method for token-level text anomaly detection that uses subspace interaction instead of global distance calculations, avoiding dilution of local anomaly signals by redundant normal feature dimensions. It also addresses the smoothing of surface anomalies caused by pre-trained language model representations. Applications include spam filtering and fake news detection.

entry.title: Chimaera: A Mixture-of-Graph-Experts Architecture for Cross-Task and Cross-Dataset Graph Learning

author.name: Jonathan Frank, David Richerby, Ansgar Scherp

entry.summary: Combines mixture-of-experts with graph foundation models, integrating heterogeneous GFM architectures such as graph prompts and linear GNNs with LLM-generated embeddings. It extends linear GNNs to link- and graph-level tasks and evaluates cross-task, cross-dataset transfer on six text-attributed graph benchmarks.

entry.title: Do Reasoning Representations Help Humans Evaluate LLM Outputs?

author.name: Jaewoo Lim, Sungbok Shin, Sanghyun Hong

entry.summary: Runs a controlled human study of six reasoning explanation formats to test whether reasoning representations actually help people evaluate LLM outputs, measuring structural understanding, error detection, and trust calibration. Results indicate mixed effects, challenging model-centric evaluation of reasoning explanations.

entry.title: Asymptotically-informed neural networks for Black-Scholes implied volatility computation

author.name: Samira Amiriyan, Youness Boutaib
